text_original: In English Webbarkiv Rosenberg: Riksbanken och penningpolitiken Datum 2007-05-31 Frste vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade under torsdagen p Nordea i Kpenhamn. Rosenberg brjade med att tala om hur Riksbanken arbetar idag och redogjorde drefter fr sin syn p det ekonomiska lget i samband med det penningpolitiska mtet i maj. I februari i r presenterade vi fr frsta gngen vr egen prognos fr reporntan. Sklet till att vi tog det steget var att vi vill bli nnu mer ppna och tydliga mot allmnheten om hur Riksbanken ser bde p den framtida utvecklingen i svensk ekonomi och p konsekvenserna fr penningpolitiken. Samtidigt vill jag understryka att vr egen prognos fr rntans utveckling inte r ngot lfte frn Riksbankens sida, utan den r just en prognos och omprvas hela tiden. Precis som tidigare kommer den ekonomiska utvecklingen att avgra hur vi kommer att frndra reporntan i framtiden. Vr prognos kan ocks skilja sig ngot frn de lngsiktiga rntefrvntningarna p de finansiella marknaderna. Detta behver inte vara ngot konstigt d vi kanske bedmer den framtida ekonomiska utvecklingen lite olika. Dremot pverkas givetvis de kortsiktiga marknadsfrvntningarna tydligare av vr prognos. Det r helt naturligt eftersom reporntan framfrallt pverkar den korta rntan, inledde Rosenberg. Genom att vi publicerar vr egen rntebana r vi i princip s tydliga som vi kan vara. Det nya sttet att arbeta minskar drfr behovet att fre de penningpolitiska mtena signalera hur direktionen ser p rntans niv. Det rcker i normalfallet med att signalera tydligt i samband med de penningpolitiska mtena. Endast i undantagsfall finns det anledning att ge ytterligare signaler nr man nrmar sig nsta mte och rntebeslut. Naturligtvis ska enskilda ledamter, precis som tidigare, i fortsttningen ocks kunna uttrycka sin egen uppfattning offentligt. Men det handlar d framfr allt om att i efterskott klargra sina personliga vervganden vid de penningpolitiska mtena. Genom att vi nu ocks kommer att namnge ledamterna i protokollen blir det nnu tydligare vilken stllning var och en tar. Drmed blir det ocks lttare att granska motiven bakom besluten, fortsatte Rosenberg. Jag tnkte nu g ver till att sga ngra ord om hur jag sg p den ekonomiska utvecklingen i samband med det senaste penningpolitiska mtet. Den nya informationen som kommit de senaste mnaderna tyder p att inflationstrycket har blivit ngot hgre n vad vi vntade i den penningpolitiska rapporten i februari och vid det penningpolitiska mtet i mars. Det beror bland annat p att regeringens vrbudget ser ut att vara mer efterfrgestimulerande, i vart fall under nsta r, n vi tidigare trott. En annan anledning till den ndrade bilden r att verenskommelserna i avtalsfrhandlingarna s hr lngt tyder p att lnerna kommer att ka snabbare n vad vi tidigare rknade med. Hur hga lnekningarna kan vntas bli beror bland annat p hur arbetsmarknaden fungerar. Viktiga frgor r om arbetsutbudet kommer att ka i den utstrckning vi rknade med, om utvecklingen mellan efterfrgan och utbud av arbetskraft fljs t och vilken hnsyn till arbetsmarknadslget som tas i lnefrhandlingarna. Idag har vi ett starkt arbetsmarknadslge och d r det rimligt att rkna med ngot hgre lnekningar n under de senaste ren. Men utfallet i lnefrhandlingarna har nd blivit hgre n vi tyckte det fanns anledning att rkna med, mot bakgrund av att den outnyttjade kapaciteten p arbetsmarknaden fortfarande r ganska stor, konstaterade Rosenberg. Vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet i brjan av maj var min uppfattning att den ekonomiska bilden inte hade frndrats s mycket att det var brttom att hja reporntan. Inflationen var fortfarande lg och bedmningen var att den kommer att stiga endast lngsamt framver. Det berodde p att det fortfarande fanns flera faktorer som hllit tillbaka inflationstrycket. Prispressen frn omvrlden vntades fortstta och produktiviteten frbttrades fortfarande i god takt. Fretagens vinster var goda och mycket tydde p att lnsamheten i nringslivet hade fortsatt att frbttras. Drfr var min uppfattning att det inte var ndvndigt att hja rntan vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet. Dremot talade utvecklingen fr att reporntan behvde hjas mer under prognosperioden n i februarirapporten fr att inflationen ska vara i linje med mlet och att den reala ekonomin ska utvecklas balanserat, sa Rosenberg. Takten i rntehjningarna mste nu avvgas s att inflationen inte tar fart snabbare n vntat, men tillvxten i produktion och sysselsttning fr inte heller bromsas in alltfr tidigt. Hur snabbt och hur mycket rntan ska hjas framver r ngot vi fr terkomma till vid nsta penningpolitiska mte i juni. D har vi mer information om avtalsrrelsen och hur produktionen utvecklats i r, fortsatte Rosenberg. Jag tnkte avsluta med ngra ord om konsekvenserna av att fastighetsskatten avskaffas och erstts med en lgre kommunal avgift. Skattefrndringen pverkar inflationen genom att boendekostnaderna i KPI frndras. Denna frndring ger en relativt stor direkt, men tillfllig effekt p inflationen. Det finns normalt sett ingen anledning att motverka sdana skatteeffekter med penningpolitiken. Nr det gller indirekta effekter p inflationen via den allmnna efterfrgan kan man notera att snkningen av fastighetsskatten enligt regeringens frslag r fullt finansierad i bostadssektorn. Det innebr att de disponibla inkomsterna inte pverkas totalt sett. Dremot kan skattefrndringarna pverka fastighetspriserna. Om fastighetspriserna stiger av fundamentala skl, ssom en frndring av fastighetsskatten, r det normalt sett inte ett problem fr penningpolitiken. Men om hushllens efterfrgan kar till fljd av detta, mste naturligtvis penningpolitiken ta hnsyn till vilka effekter det kan f p inflationen och BNP-tillvxten, avslutade Rosenberg. Title: Current monetary policy
text: In English Webbarkiv Current monetary policy Date: 1997-05-26 Speakers: Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom Location: Penningpolitiskt Forum Once again, the Riksbank, in cooperation with SNS, arranges the Monetary Policy Forum. It is the fifth year in a row and now I can state that together we have created a tradition. We are also in the fifth year of a floating exchange rate regime. The importance of credibility Persistently low inflation is not an end goal of economic policy, but a means to achieve key objectives such as sustainable growth and increased employment. However, bringing down high inflation so that it stays at a low level for a year or so is not the hard part. On the other hand, ensuring that inflation is persistently at a low level and establishing a low-inflation regime is often a more protracted process. I have discussed many times over the past few years and in this forum the importance of confidence in economic policy. This refers to the degree of confidence of the various actors in the economy in the will and ability of economic policy to sustain price developments in line with the price stability objective. It is therefore a question of the expectations of future inflation, i.e. what inflation do the actors of the economy expect - not only for the near future - but for the 2, 5 or 10 year term, and how these expectations relate to the price stability objective. It is not done in a jiffy to convince everyone in a country that inflation will not be 8% in the long term, as the average was for the 1970s and 1980s in our country, but instead 2% for a considerable time to come. The extensive economic problems of the early 1990s, the large imbalances and our inflationary history made it difficult to establish credibility quickly. The road has thus been lined with some hesitation and doubt. We remember the widespread currency turmoil in the autumn of 1992, the dramatic rise in long-term interest rates in the spring and summer of 1994 and the failure of the wage round in the spring of 1995. These examples were likely signs that the long-term credibility of the low-inflation regime had not been consolidated. If inflation expectations linger at a high level, they will gradually become self-fulfilling even if the current inflation rate is currently at a low level. The economic players expect a higher rate of price rises going forward - and that characterizes their actions and they enter into contracts with that perception. This applies, for example, to the social partners, shopkeepers, savers and investors. Wages, prices, long-term interest rates and the krona exchange rate will therefore sooner or later develop as in the old inflationary economy unless the expectation picture changes. All experience shows that proud declarations are not enough to change expectations, especially as such declarations were issued in the past without success. That is why a sustained and consistent economic policy is required that demonstrates in action a determination to bring down inflation in a sustained manner. Then, but only then, does the formation of expectation give way. This will also bring confidence in the new direction of the policy, which will gradually have an impact both on the financial markets and on the real economy. Interest rates fall, the currency stabilizes, contracts in the supply and labor markets are concluded at new and permanently lower levels, etc. Lengthy process of breaking inflation expectations We have also seen in other countries that it takes time and perseverance to gain credibility for the low-inflation line. The long-term interest rate can, at least in a slightly longer perspective, be seen as a gauge of confidence in low-inflation policy. It was not until the early 1990s that the US long-term interest rate came into line with the German one, i.e. only almost ten years after the Federal Reserve decided to fight inflation. Many today have forgotten that the US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate to almost 20 percent in the early 1980s. It also took upwards of 10 years before European countries such as France, Belgium and Denmark came close to the German long-term interest rate. For the Netherlands, however, things moved faster, probably as a result of very consistent economic policies and less of the setbacks from the inflationary years. The difficulty of breaking expectations and creating confidence in the new low-inflation regime has also from time to time created debate around monetary policy - even at the Monetary Policy Forum - and contributed to controversy in the general discussion about the benefits of economic development without inflation. However, I now seem to be able to trace a more balanced discussion of monetary policy in Swedish society. Something obviously seems to have happened. Support for the low-inflation regime has increased. Understanding of the possibilities and conditions of monetary policy also appears to have improved. Credibility has increased Most indicators suggest that inflation expectations have come down. Not only in surveys, but also in the form of concrete actions of economic actors. The work to safeguard persistently low inflation never ends, but the Swedish economy has come a long way towards a low inflation regime. There are several explanations for the increased confidence. Monetary policy has played a role. However, I would particularly like to emphasise the determination of the political system in the form of extensive budgetary consolidation. From a budget deficit of at most just over 12 percent of GDP, public finances appear to be heading for balance and surplus. It reduces the risk of inconsistencies in economic policy and creates a basis for the ability to sustainably establish a low-inflation regime. The desire to change economic policy and bring inflation down from a high to a low level has characterised economic policy since 1990. The Riksbank's inflation target has received support from the political system. The five-party agreement last week on new legislation for the Riksbank clearly marks this will. A statutory delegation of monetary policy to an independent central bank clearly shows the policy that the state authorities want to pursue. It also shows that it will be conducted. But the increased independence places demands on responsibility. The political system and the public must be given clear justifications for the monetary policy pursued and they will want to follow up the decisions made by the Riksbank. This requires that the process towards greater transparency continues. This is also something that the Riksbank will work ambitiously on. No contradiction between inflation and growth As the various actors in the economy have confidence in the will and ability of economic policy to sustain price developments in line with the price stability objective, the propensity for inflation in the economy also decreases. This, in turn, leads to the fact that inflationary developments will be more dependent on economic activity in the economy. With increased credibility, resource utilisation is becoming an increasingly important factor in the inflation process and thus in monetary policy. A weak economy normally leads to falling inflation and thus to easing of monetary policy. Conversely, too strong economic development, which risks leading to overheating and accelerating inflation, means the need for tighter policies. A monetary policy geared towards low inflation thus means that the economy can grow in line with the expansion of the growth potential of the economy. The development of this long-term growth potential does not depend on monetary policy but on real economic factors. In several areas, structural changes have been implemented that stimulate the potential growth rate of the Swedish economy, but we have problems with the functioning of the labor market. There is a risk that a great deal of unemployment is structural. As a result, it risks remaining at a high level even in the event of a better economy. Low inflation will be a prerequisite for growth to continue and not be broken by accelerating inflation and is thus not opposed to growth. In this way, the discussion about the Riksbank's goals can hopefully be de-dramatized. However, let me underline what I said at the beginning of this line of reasoning; a prerequisite is that long-term inflation expectations have been broken and this confidence will continue to hold up in the future. Monetary policy ahead Let me conclude by saying a few words about the current situation. The Riksbank's assessment is that growth in 1997 and 1998 will be around 2 and 3 per cent, respectively. The question then arises as to how fast the economy can grow without inflation accelerating. It is not possible to say exactly how fast the Swedish economy has the ability to grow in the long term in the new low-inflation regime and after the various structural changes that the economy has undergone since the late 1980s. However, most evidence suggests that production potential has increased slightly compared to the 1970s and 1980s. Nor do we know today for sure how much spare capacity there is in the economy and which can meet an increasing demand. In various inflation reports, we have presented different measures of the so-called output gap. In the next inflation report, which will be presented on 5 June, more analyses will be presented. By all accounts, output growth of 5% overall in 1997 and 1998 should not close the output gap. Thus, that analysis tells us that the economy does not need to experience tensions that could cause inflation to accelerate. Consequently, underlying inflation should be stable around 1.5 to 2% this year and next and perhaps well into 1999. To complement the assessment of production capacity and the output gap, as everyone knows, we are also following other indicators of whether possible tensions in the economy are developing and that could lead to inflationary pressures. The reverse may also happen that the economy works better than we think and can cope with higher growth. We must also pay attention to this. Of course, the picture can also change if the economy grows faster or slower than we assumed, but today there is no indication of that. But, of course, such deviations are always something that must be included in the monetary policy trade-offs. As is well known, monetary policy is about weighing risks and opportunities, not about precise precision in forecasts. It is also important to follow up on the possible stimulus or contractual effect that monetary conditions have, i.e. the short-term interest rate and the krona's combined. This analysis also leads us to the conclusion that monetary policy is well balanced. The stimulus now being given to the economy does not currently pose a threat to the price stability objective. The conclusion is thus that there is no need to change the repo rate. Title: Monetary policy
text: In English Webbarkiv Monetary policy Date: 1997-10-22 Speakers: Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Location: SNS conference on the economic situation Let me begin by thanking you for being able to come here and talk about monetary policy. The business cycle conferences are a good tradition and in the Riksbank we value the opportunity to participate in a discussion on monetary policy in this forum. Today I intend to dwell on four subject areas. Initially, I intend to talk about the principled framework that guides the Riksbank when we work with inflation targets. Next, I intend to follow last year's approach and make some comments on what has happened in the area of monetary policy since we met here a year ago. The third point is a discussion of the inflation outlook going forward, which is based on the latest Inflation Report. Finally, I wanted to touch on two factors that are important for the assessment of inflation; fiscal policy and wage formation. 1. The principled framework of inflation targeting policies In order to understand how the Riksbank works, it is important to have the basic features of the thinking framework that guides monetary policy clear. Such a framework is necessarily schematic and simplified, but it is nevertheless a support for the idea. The aim of monetary policy is to safeguard the value of money. Behind this goal formulation lies the realization that it is by ensuring low and stable inflation that monetary policy can best contribute to creating long-term favorable conditions for growth, employment and prosperity. In Sweden, as in a number of other countries, monetary policy is now conducted with direct guidance from an inflation target. In other words, there is no intermediate goal between the instrument, the policy rate, and the ultimate goal, low inflation. Inflationsprognosen central The lag between a monetary policy measure and the impact on demand and inflationary pressures make forecasting future inflation a key tool for policy implementation. Inflation assessments, like most other economic forecasts, are, of course, fraught with uncertainty. Therefore, the Riksbank does not work with individual point estimates of future inflation. In practice, the forecast is a probability distribution with a number of more or less likely outcomes. Based on both model calculations and business cycle forecasts of a more traditional type, scenarios for the whole economy and especially for inflation are developed. Typically, a main scenario is identified. An analysis of specific uncertain "key factors" in the assessment analyses, discusses and assesses the likelihood of alternative inflation scenarios. These are scenarios that in the current assessment are considered somewhat less likely than the main scenario, but where the factors that call for special vigilance are highlighted. Demand situation and inflation expectations In its inflation assessment, the Riksbank uses a wide range of indicators. These can naturally be divided into two groups; those that provide a picture of the evolution of supply and demand conditions in the economy and those that help capture expectations about the future rate of inflation. Inflation expectations are important as a measure of confidence in the Riksbank's success in achieving its inflation target. They play a central role in the inflation assessment, for example, because expectations of future inflation affect price and wage formation. As for the supply and demand conditions in the economy, the starting point of the reasoning is that demand cannot in the long run grow faster than production capacity - the potential level of production. A level of demand that means that the economy's resources are used more than is sustainable in the long term eventually results in bottlenecks and other shortage phenomena, which in turn lead to price increases. It is easy to illustrate this line of thinking by seeing how capacity utilisation across the economy as measured by the so-called output gap has developed in relation to inflation. (Figure 1) The connection is apparently clear. In order to achieve the inflation target, it is important that monetary policy is balanced so that demand in the economy does not grow too fast or too slowly, but at the pace that the economy can cope with with, among other things, new investments, improved efficiency and a good supply of labour. If future demand is expected to be too high, monetary policy needs to be tightened and vice versa. In this way, monetary policy geared towards an inflation target can help to reduce fluctuations in the economy. Alignment with the inflation target The principles of how monetary policy is designed can be formulated as a simple rule of thumb: If the inflation forecast (or rather the probability distribution over different possible outcomes) - assuming an unchanged policy rate suggests that inflation will be in line with the target over one to two years' time, monetary policy is properly balanced. If the assessment shows that inflation risks exceeding (below) the inflation target, monetary policy is too expansionary (tight), and the policy rate should then be raised (lowered). An important question in such situations is over what time horizon this assessment should be made and thus how fast and vigorous a diversion should be. There are many indications that the reorientation should be gradual and that the time horizon over which monetary policy aims to reach the inflation target should not be too short. This is one of the reasons why we usually talk about the inflation target being seen in a slightly longer, annual perspective. First, there is unavoidable uncertainty about the impact of monetary policy changes on inflation and demand, both in terms of size and delay. Under such conditions, it seems intuitively reasonable to proceed cautiously and carefully evaluate the monetary policy pursued using all new incoming information. Second, sharp shifts in monetary policy risk creating unnecessary instability in real variables such as output and employment. Cautious and gradual changes in interest rates, which may instead operate for a slightly longer period of time, are therefore preferable. A longer horizon, above which the inflation target is to be reached, and a gradual adjustment of monetary policy, make it possible to achieve the inflation target while stabilising real variables to some extent. From this also follows something that has a bearing on today's situation; it is important that monetary policy is refocused in time. By countering rising inflationary pressures in good time, the measures do not need to be so forceful. The risk of inflationary tensions arising in the economic upturn will be less. The same applies to the risk of inflation expectations rising. As a result, fluctuations in interest rates may be smaller and the impact on the real economy more subdued. Us monetary policy can serve as an illustrative example of how a central bank with small changes in interest rates, both upwards and downwards, appears in recent years to have succeeded in keeping inflation low while the economy has shown stable and good growth. However, two reservations are in order: one should not overestimate the ability of monetary policy to smooth out cyclical fluctuations in the economy through "fine calibration". Experience shows that this is difficult, among other things, because the necessary knowledge is lacking and development is more or less regularly disturbed by factors that cannot be predicted. In practice, account must be taken of the confidence of the policies pursued. For example, if there is uncertainty about the long-term viability of economic policy to meet the inflation target, a strategy aimed at gradually bringing inflation down towards the target may lead to problems by further amplifying uncertainty. It may be worth underlining that, in this context, it is not only monetary policy that matters. Historical experience, not least in Sweden, shows that fiscal policy must also be designed in a way that is in line with price stability in the long term in order for inflation policy to enjoy full confidence. 2. Developments over the past year From imbalance to credibility When we saw each other here about a year ago, the Riksbank had gradually lowered interest rates since the beginning of 1996. The rate cuts lasted until December, when the repo rate came down to just over 4 percent. In total, the interest rate had then been reduced by almost 5 percentage points. The Finance Minister usually prides himself on being the world champion in budget consolidation. Without taking a position on this assertion, it is clear that confidence in economic policy - as expressed, inter alia, in the exchange rate and in market developments - increased markedly in 1995. This, in turn, made it possible for the Riksbank to cut interest rates radically. However, Sweden is not unique. A similar development, with rapid interest rate cuts in the wake of fiscal consolidation, has also occurred in, for example, Canada. When the Riksbank initiated interest rate cuts at the beginning of 1996, the background was a clear improvement in the inflation picture during the summer and autumn of 1995. The positive development was largely due to the strengthening of the krona after several years of severe undervaluation. The stronger krona opened the way for a better balance in monetary stimulus from interest rates and exchange rates, respectively. Thanks to the lower level of interest rates, domestic demand received much-needed support at the beginning of 1996. Inflation expectations among both households and firms had gradually crept down, showing that economic actors were increasingly beginning to adjust to the persistence of the low inflation rate. In many respects, the fall in interest rates in 1996 was about adjusting interest rates from an economy with major imbalances and credibility problems to an economy with a better balance and growing confidence in the direction of economic policy towards price stability. Penningpolititisk incentive The Inflation Report of last December said that the signs of a recovery in the domestic economy were clear. At the same time, the Riksbank considered the risk of overheating to be small, as the recovery started from a low level. The overall assessment was that there could be some additional scope for monetary policy easing. That the market shared this assessment is evident from the implied forward rates at this time. (Figure 2) The inflation assessment was based, among other things, on an assumption that the krona would strengthen slightly. This reinforcement failed; instead, the krona weakened by 6 percent from November 1996 until June 1997. In this situation, the Riksbank chose not to cut interest rates further. The weakening appeared to be of a lasting nature and affected demand to such an extent that no further reduction in interest rates was deemed necessary. In its Inflation Report in March, the Riksbank stated that monetary policy was well balanced and that the large repo rate cuts needed to be evaluated. The same assessment was made in June. This year, the economy appears to have developed mainly according to the Riksbank's assessment. With the benefit of hindsight, it appears that the recovery got underway a little later than expected. On the other hand, it seems - at least in the second quarter - to have accelerated so much that the average figure for the year should be in line with the forecast. For the first time since the Riksbank began working on an inflation target, the Swedish economy is now heading into a boom. An important explanation for this is the support the economy has received in recent years from monetary policy. Market expectations now show that the discussion among economic players is no longer about whether but when a rate hike will take place. 3. The economic situation Broad rise In the September inflation report, the Riksbank drew a relatively bright picture of economic development in Sweden, although it was not a picture without reservations. The recovery appears to be continuing. Since the economy bottomed out in the summer of 1993, the Swedish economy has grown by more than 2.5 percent on average, which is more than in the 80s. The upturn in the first half of this year also shows a more balanced development where domestic demand is increasingly contributing to growth (Figure 3). The industrial economy is now strengthening further and various barometer data show that new orders from both exports and the domestic market continue to increase (Figure 4). Several factors indicate that profitability is good in large parts of the business community. The exchange rate of the krona has favoured the profitability of export companies, while productivity growth is good (Figure 5). Productivity in manufacturing grew by nearly 7 per cent in the first half of this year compared with the same period last year. Overall in the economy, including the public sector, productivity increased by close to 4 percent. Against the background of the rapid growth of the industry, it is not surprising that capacity utilization is rising. The share of enterprises that reported that the availability of factors of production limits production rose between the first and second quarters and the shortage rates for some skilled workers are approaching the levels prevailing during the temporary peak of the economic cycle in 1995. Private consumption also now appears to be growing at a faster pace. For example, retail sales rose by around 4% in the first half of 1997 compared with the same period last year. (Figure 6) The upturn in private consumption is taking place despite the fact that household income is being held back by the tax increases and spending cuts decided in recent years. The tightening of fiscal policies has led to a decline in households' real disposable income in 1995 and 1996, despite an increase in the number of hours worked and the fact that average hourly wages have grown significantly more than consumer prices. (Figure 7) Fiscal consolidation will continue over the next few years, albeit at a slower pace. Households' real disposable income is likely to grow slightly in 1997. A more noticeable upturn is expected in 1998 and 1999. Households' expectations about their own and the country's economy improved significantly in September after a slight decline in August. This is also reflected in the clear rise in house prices and even more so in stocks. The HIP survey for September shows that households are more optimistic about the outlook in the labour market. For the first time since 1995, the proportion of households believing that unemployment will fall is clearly higher than the proportion who believe in increased unemployment. There are also signs that the demand situation in the labour market is improving. The number of newly registered vacancies increased by 15 per cent year-on-year during the period June-August and a slight improvement in employment can be discerned. In summary, most of the evidence suggests a good demand trend in the coming years. Exports should be able to continue to grow at a relatively fast pace. At the same time, the Riksbank expects private consumption growth to accelerate and that public consumption will in any case not decrease. In the inflation report's main scenario, GDP growth is around 2% this year and around 3% in 1998. In 1999, growth is expected to pick up slightly further. Produktionsgapet sluts The Riksbank thus expects the economy to strengthen in the coming years. In the Inflation Report, we made it clear that the risk of weaker-than-main scenario developments has diminished since last spring. The information that has come later underlines this. The difficulty in assessing inflation currently lies mainly in uncertainty about the supply side of the economy. It is therefore particularly important to follow various indicators of the state of the economy that provide a picture of how the strengthening of demand affects developments in the labour market and in different commodity markets. How do different measures of e.g. capacity utilisation develop and what picture does one get from following price developments in the economy? Inflation as measured by the change in the consumer price index has risen rapidly in 1997. The twelve-month figure was down to 0 percent for a couple of months this spring and has since moved up to 1.9 percent for the month of September at a fairly fast pace. The main features of this development are no surprise. One reason why the CPI has risen is increased indirect taxes on tobacco, among other things, and an increase in several different administratively set prices. Another factor is that the fall in interest rates in 1996-1997 has a decreasing impact on consumer prices. All in all, this means that the CPI is approaching the various measures of underlying inflation that the Riksbank is working on.) However, the outcome of the CPI for September was slightly larger than the Riksbank and many other analysts expected. Although one should not draw any big gears on a single figure, both the development of the CPI and the development of a couple of the different measures of underlying inflation underline the importance of a sharpened attention. The growth the Riksbank expects in the inflation report's main scenario is higher than the growth we believe the economy will tolerate in the long term without shortage phenomena occurring and inflation accelerating (potential growth). This means that the excess capacity that exists today will gradually disappear. So what is the overcapacity? The Riksbank appreciates what is known as the "Riksbank". the output gap with several different methods. (Figure 9.) When we weighed up the results of the various estimates - and taken into account all the other information on capacity utilisation - we have made the assessment that there is a surplus capacity in the economy as a whole amounting to about 2% of GDP. Thus, with the growth rates we expect - and with potential growth of just over 2% over the next few years - the output gap will close sometime in 1999. The Inflation Report also presents other information that gives a picture of when inflation may start to accelerate. Calculations of structural unemployment - and thus indirectly of unemployment, which can be reconciled with stable and low inflation - suggest that there are risks to inflation even in the shorter term. The rate at which capacity utilisation rises may also have an impact on inflation rates. If slack decreases at a rapid pace, the result could be increased inflationary impulses, although there is still excess capacity overall in the economy. 4. Fiscal policy Two effects In any assessment of the inflation outlook, the fiscal stance is essential. Fiscal policy affects the conditions of monetary policy in two different ways. - First, the degree of austerity or expansion in fiscal policy affects the demand situation in the economy. This is the traditional impact of fiscal policy on the economic situation. - Secondly, confidence in the long-term sustainability of fiscal policy is important for the monetary policy climate. If the government deficit appears to be increasing in an uncontrolled manner, uncertainty may arise as to whether the problems can be sorted out at all. In this situation, the risk of abandoning low-inflation policy and choosing to inflate out blame can be perceived as real regardless of the messages given from official sources. The ongoing fiscal consolidation is dampening demand in the economy. Tax increases and reduced transfers have reduced household income by the equivalent of 3-4 per cent per year. The burden on household income was probably at its highest in 1996, but fiscal policy measured in this way is also tight this year and next year. In addition, there is the pressure to save money that the budget consolidation has led to for public activities. Against this background, there is no doubt that fiscal policy in recent years has contributed to reducing inflationary pressures and that it has thus also enabled monetary policy to ease. For a long time, however, the large deficits - despite the fact that extensive savings programs were presented - meant that there was a more fundamental, long-term concern about the Swedish political system's ability to sort out the fiscal problems. These concerns were a key factor behind the recurrent interest rate and currency turmoil during 1990 to 1995. The situation in this regard has changed. Fiscal consolidation is an important explanation for the strengthening of the krona since the crisis years and for the sharp decline in long-term interest rates. Fiscal policy has thus also opened the way for a more expansionary monetary policy. At the same time, fiscal consolidation has led to increased optimism, which, together with the fall in interest rates, has contributed to rising share prices and to the recovery in the housing market. This has increased household wealth values and created a space for consumption. To that extent, the tight fiscal policy has all contributed to a stimulus for the economy. This is nothing unique. Academic studies have shown that measures to restructure a state's finances can have an expansionary effect on economic development, especially in situations when there is concern about the long-term sustainability of public finances. At the same time, when the krona has strengthened, which has dampened growth in the competitive parts of the economy somewhat, Sweden has gained a better balance in the economy's growth. Reducing government debt How should the established fiscal policy be valued in this light? Clearly, fiscal policy in the next few years seems to be less tight. In 1998 and 1999, however, it still appears to mean that the state is taking away part of their income growth from households. Even from an international perspective, the policy is tight. In no country is the so-called structural deficit (as calculated by the OECD) improving as rapidly between 1997 and 1998. The concern one may have is more long-term. Swedish government finances are highly sensitive to economic cycles, according to a number of different studies. There are arguments that this sensitivity may have decreased, but no one knows for sure what the situation is. In-depth work needs to be done here. Cyclical sensitivity is linked to the extent of public expenditure and taxes, but also to the construction of different systems. Added to this is a factor neglected in the debate; the policies actually pursued in recent business cycles. The experience here is not entirely positive. Fiscal policy has not been designed in such a way that the cumulative effect has been stabilising on the economy. It is against this background that the Riksbank has argued that an ambition for fiscal policy in the coming years should be to reduce government debt. From a monetary policy point of view, this would be good because it reduces the risk that a situation would arise at some point in the future, when the long-term sustainability of the state's finances would again be called into question. A policy that reduces cyclical sensitivity and contributes to a reduction in government debt also creates better conditions for stable production and employment development by reducing the risk of severe austerity in the next economic downturn. It is something of a paradox - and difficult to understand when you consider what happened in the early 1990s - that there are those in the debate who today, in the midst of the economic upturn for reasons of unemployment, want to weaken the state's finances. Now if ever it's time to "gather in the barns". 5. Wage formation Prerequisites for better outcomes One factor that is critical to the current inflation assessment is future wage developments. Preliminary data on wage developments so far this year indicate that the pace of wage growth has slowed down. It is now just under 4% for the whole economy. This may indicate that wage formation is adjusting to an economy with low inflation. The 1998 wage round will be an important indicator of whether such optimism is justified. Large parts of the current agreements are then renegotiated. At the last major round of agreements in 1995, the agreements resulted in excessive wage increases. This is despite the fact that around twelve per cent of the labour force was then openly unemployed or in labour market measures. This time, the conditions for wage outcomes that are compatible with balanced economic development seem in some respects more favourable; we have a price trend that has come down to levels around the inflation target while profit levels in the export industry are lower. On the other hand, the economic upturn is broader than in 1994-1995. Inflation expectations among the social partners suggest that they envisage a continued inflation rate in line with the inflation target. (Figure 10) That's important. The debate around the wage movement also shows that there has been an increased realization that an inflation rate around two percent should be the starting point for nominal wage requirements. Several important players in the labour market have stated that they have the inflation target as a starting point for their actions. In this way, we in Sweden are once again approaching a world of the type we were in during the first post-war decades, with firm rules of the game for the social partners. At the time, it was a fixed exchange rate regime (the so-called Betton Woods system). Now we have a variable exchange rate with inflation targets. Productivity of various kinds The real problem with wage increases that create inflationary pressures today lies in the effects on employment not on inflation. If the rate of wage growth is pushed up so high that the inflation target is threatened, it is the Riksbank's obligation to raise its key interest rate. As a result, inflation will at least be in line with the target in any one year's time. There are important links between wage formation and productivity developments. It is improvements in productivity that create room for real wage increases. But also the opposite may actually apply; wage increases can drive productivity growth. It is therefore important to make a distinction between different types of productivity growth. Normally, high productivity is assumed to be the result of investments, new, more efficient working methods and technological developments. For example, better technology increases the value of the work effort. Productivity improvements of this kind create scope for real wage increases. Developments over the past century show that a dramatic increase in productivity has been able to go hand in hand both with growth in real wages and with a rapid rise in employment. (Figure 11) In addition, there are productivity improvements resulting from a strengthening of the economy. When demand and thus production increases, it can often happen at the beginning of an economic upturn without the need to deploy new resources. However, high measured productivity can also be caused by high real wage increases , driven by wage earners. In this case, wage increases create pressure on companies to reduce wage costs in production through rationalisation. In the statistics, this will also be recorded as increased labor productivity. In practice, it is not easy to distinguish between different kinds of productivity; the high productivity growth in recent years has probably had features of all three. What is important to underline is that it is not historical productivity growth that can be used as a basis for wage increases, but estimates of how the productivity of the first mentioned - more fundamental - variety develops. Taking into account also productivity growth of the latter kind risks driving the exclusion of jobs. 6. Conclusion Let me conclude by coming back to the monetary policy framework and monetary policy going forward. The task of monetary policy is to safeguard the value of money. Policy needs to be refocused when inflation forecasts are not in line with the target. Monetary policy is conducted in an environment where there is uncertainty about the functioning of the economy, uncertainty in the interpretation of new information and about the effects of policy rate changes. In order to avoid sharp shifts in output and employment and to provide stability, monetary policy should be adjusted gradually and with good foresight. For the first time since the fixed exchange rate was abandoned and the Riksbank formulated the current inflation target, the Swedish economy is heading into a boom with both strong domestic demand and strong export growth. In its September inflation report, the Riksbank made it clear that the risk of a weaker development has decreased since the June report. Later information supports this image. The uncertainty in the assessment now revolves mainly around the supply side of the economy. Sweden has not yet undergone a broad economic upturn since the low-inflation regime was established in the early 1990s. Most indications are that the level of activity and resource utilisation has risen further during the autumn. However, according to the Riksbank's assessment, there is still spare capacity to meet an upturn. Our assessment is therefore that monetary policy is currently well balanced. As activity in the economy strengthens and the outlook for monetary policy moves forward in time, monetary policy must gradually adjust from providing an expansionary effect to providing a more neutral effect on the economy. The timing and pace of this adjustment must be continually tested against the new information that is coming. text_original: In English Webbarkiv Penningpolitiken Datum: 1997-10-22 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Lars Heikensten Plats: SNS konferens om konjunkturlget Lt mig brja med att tacka fr att jag ftt komma hit och tala om penningpolitiken. Konjunkturkonferenserna r en god tradition och i Riksbanken vrdestter vi mjligheten att i detta forum f medverka i en diskussion om penningpolitiken. Idag har jag tnkt uppehlla mig vid fyra mnesomrden. Inledningsvis tnker jag tala om den principiella ram som vgleder Riksbanken nr vi arbetar med inflationsml. Drefter tnker jag flja fjolrets upplggning och ngot kommentera vad som hnt p penningpolitikens omrde sedan vi sgs hr fr ett r sedan. Den tredje punkten r en diskussion om inflationsutsikterna framver, som tar avstamp i den senaste inflationsrapporten. Till slut tnkte jag berra tv faktorer som r viktiga fr bedmningen av inflationen; finanspolitiken och lnebildningen. 1. Den principiella ramen fr inflationsmlspolitiken Fr att frst hur Riksbanken arbetar r det viktigt att ha grunddragen i den tankeram som vgleder penningpolitiken klar fr sig. En sdan ram r med ndvndighet schematisk och frenklad, men den r likvl ett std fr tanken. Mlet fr penningpolitiken r att vrna penningvrdet. Bakom denna mlformulering ligger insikten att det r genom att skra en lg och stabil inflation som penningpolitiken bst kan bidra till att skapa lngsiktigt gynnsamma frutsttningar fr tillvxt, sysselsttning och vlstnd. I Sverige, liksom i en rad andra lnder, bedrivs numera penningpolitiken med direkt ledning av ett inflationsml. Med andra ord finns det inget mellanliggande ml mellan instrumentet, styrrntan, och det slutliga mlet, lg inflation. Inflationsprognosen central Efterslpningar mellan en penningpolitisk tgrd och effekterna p efterfrgan och inflationstryck gr att prognoser ver framtida inflation r ett centralt medel nr det gller genomfrandet av politiken. Inflationsbedmningar, i likhet med de flesta andra ekonomiska prognoser, r naturligtvis behftade med oskerhet. Drfr arbetar Riksbanken inte med enskilda punktskattningar av den framtida inflationen. I praktiken r prognosen en sannolikhetsfrdelning med ett antal mer eller mindre troliga utfall. Med ledning av svl modellberkningar som konjunkturprognoser av mer traditionell typ tas scenarier fr hela ekonomin och speciellt fr inflationen fram. Normalt identifieras ett huvudscenario. Med hjlp av en analys av srskilda oskra "nyckelfaktorer" i bedmningen analyseras, diskuteras och sannolikhetsbedms alternativa inflationsscenarier. Det r scenarier som i den aktuella bedmningen anses som ngot mindre troliga n huvudscenariet, men dr de faktorer som pkallar srskild vaksamhet lyfts fram. Efterfrgelget och inflationsfrvntningarna I inflationsbedmningen anvnder sig Riksbanken av ett brett spektrum av indikatorer. Dessa kan naturligen delas in i tv grupper; de som ger en bild av utvecklingen av utbuds- och efterfrgefrhllandena i ekonomin och de som hjlper till att fnga frvntningarna om den framtida inflationstakten. Inflationsfrvntningarna r viktiga som mtt p frtroendet fr att Riksbanken ska lyckas uppn inflationsmlet. De spelar en central roll i inflationsbedmningen bl.a. genom att frvntningar om framtida inflation pverkar pris- och lnebildningen. Nr det gller utbuds- och efterfrgefrhllandena i ekonomin r utgngspunkten fr resonemanget att efterfrgan inte i lngden kan vxa snabbare n produktionskapaciteten - den potentiella produktionsnivn. En efterfrgeniv som innebr att ekonomins resurser utnyttjas mer n vad som r lngsiktigt hllbart resulterar s smningom i flaskhalsar och andra bristfenomen, som i sin tur leder till priskningar. Det r ltt att skdliggra denna tankegng genom att se hur kapacitetsutnyttjandet i hela ekonomin mtt med det s.k. produktionsgapet har utvecklats i relation till inflationen. (Diagram 1) Sambandet r som synes tydligt. Fr att uppn inflationsmlet r det viktigt att penningpolitiken avvgs s att efterfrgan i ekonomin varken vxer fr snabbt eller fr lngsamt utan i den takt som ekonomin kan klara med hjlp av bl.a. nya investeringar, frbttrad effektivitet och god tillgng p arbetskraft. Om den framtida efterfrgan bedms bli fr hg behver penningpolitiken stramas t och tvrtom. P s stt kan en penningpolitik som inriktas mot ett inflationsml bidra till att minska svngningarna i ekonomin. Anpassning till inflationsmlet Principerna fr hur penningpolitiken utformas kan formuleras som en enkel tumregel: Om inflationsprognosen (eller snarare sannolikhetsfrdelningen ver olika mjliga utfall) - under antagande om en ofrndrad styrrnta talar fr att inflationen kommer att vara i linje med mlet p ett  tv rs sikt r penningpolitiken rtt avvgd. Om bedmningen visar att inflationen riskerar att verstiga (understiga) inflationsmlet r penningpolitiken fr expansiv (stram), och styrrntan br d hjas (snkas). En viktig frga i sdana situationer r ver vilken tidshorisont denna bedmning br gras och drmed hur snabb och kraftig en omlggning br vara. Mycket talar fr att omlggningen br ske gradvis och att den tidshorisont, ver vilken penningpolitiken syftar till att n inflationsmlet, inte br vara alltfr kort. Det r bl.a. drfr vi brukar tala om att inflationsmlet ska ses i ett lite lngre, rligt perspektiv. Fr det frsta finns en oundviklig oskerhet om effekterna av penningpolitiska frndringar p inflation och efterfrgan, bde vad gller storlek och frdrjning. Under sdana frhllandena verkar det intuitivt rimligt att g frsiktigt fram och noga utvrdera den frda penningpolitiken med hjlp av all ny inkommande information. Fr det andra riskerar kraftiga omslag i penningpolitiken att skapa ondig instabilitet i reala variabler som produktion och sysselsttning. Frsiktiga och gradvisa rntefrndringar, som istllet fr verka under ngot lngre tid, r drfr att fredra. En lngre horisont, ver vilken inflationsmlet ska ns, och en gradvis anpassning av penningpolitiken, gr det mjligt att uppn inflationsmlet och samtidigt i viss utstrckning stabilisera reala variabler. Av det hr fljer ocks ngot som har en bring p dagens situation; det r viktigt att penningpolitiken lggs om i tid. Genom att i god tid motverka ett stigande inflationstryck behver inte tgrderna vara s kraftfulla. Risken fr att inflationsdrivande spnningar ska uppst i konjunkturuppgngen blir mindre. Detsamma gller risken fr att inflationsfrvntningarna ska stiga. Drmed kan svngningarna i rntelget komma att bli mindre och inverkan p den reala ekonomin mer dmpad. Den amerikanska penningpolitiken kan tjna som illustrativt exempel p hur en centralbank med sm rntefrndringar, svl uppt som nedt, under de senaste ren frefaller ha lyckats med att hlla inflationen lg samtidigt som ekonomin uppvisat en stabil och god tillvxt. Tv reservationer r emellertid p sin plats: Man br inte verskatta penningpolitikens mjligheter att genom "finkalibrering" utjmna konjunkturella svngningar i ekonomin. Erfarenheten visar att detta r svrt bl.a. drfr att den ndvndiga kunskapen saknas och utvecklingen mer eller mindre regelbundet strs av faktorer som man inte kan frutsga. I praktiken mste hnsyn tas till vilket frtroende den frda politiken tnjuter. Om det rder oskerhet kring den ekonomiska politikens mjligheter att lngsiktigt klara inflationsmlet kan t.ex. en strategi som syftar till att gradvis f ned inflationen mot mlet leda till problem genom att frstrka oskerheten ytterligare. Det kan vara vrt att understryka att det i detta sammanhang inte endast r penningpolitiken som r av betydelse. Historiska erfarenheter, inte minst i Sverige, visar att ven finanspolitiken mste utformas p ett stt som lngsiktigt r i verensstmmelse med prisstabilitet fr att inflationspolitiken ska tnjuta fullt frtroende. 2. Utvecklingen under det senaste ret Frn obalans till trovrdighet Nr vi sgs hr fr ungefr ett r sedan hade Riksbanken successivt snkt rntan sedan brjan av 1996. Rntesnkningarna pgick till december, d reporntan kommit ner till strax ver 4 procent. Sammanlagt hade rntan d snkts med nra 5 procentenheter. Finansministern brukar bermma sig av att vara vrldsmstare i budgetsanering. Utan att ta stllning till detta pstende str det klart att frtroendet fr den ekonomiska politiken - som detta kommer till uttryck i bl.a. vxelkursen och i rnteutvecklingen p marknaden - kade markant under 1995. Detta gjorde det i sin tur mjligt fr Riksbanken att snka rntan radikalt. Dock r Sverige inte unikt. En snarlik utveckling, med snabba rntesnkningar i klvattnet av en statsfinansiell konsolidering, har ocks skett i t.ex. Kanada. Nr Riksbanken inledde rntesnkningarna i brjan av 1996 var bakgrunden en tydlig frbttring av inflationsbilden under sommaren och hsten 1995. Den positiva utvecklingen hngde i hg grad samman med att kronan frstrkts efter flera r med en kraftig undervrdering. Den starkare kronan ppnade fr en bttre balans i den monetra stimulansen frn rnta respektive vxelkurs. Tack vare den lgre rntenivn fick den inhemska efterfrgan i brjan av 1996 ett vlbehvligt std. Inflationsfrvntningarna hos svl hushll som fretag hade gradvis krupit ner, vilket visade att ekonomins aktrer i allt strre utstrckning brjade stlla in sig p att den lga inflationstakten skulle bli bestende. I mycket handlade rntenedgngen under 1996 om en anpassning av rntelget frn en ekonomi med stora obalanser och trovrdighetsproblem till en ekonomi med bttre balans och vxande frtroende fr den ekonomiska politikens inriktning mot prisstabilitet. Penningpolititisk stimulans I inflationsrapporten frn december i fjol sades att tecknen p en terhmtning i den inhemska ekonomin var tydliga. Samtidigt ansg Riksbanken att risken fr verhettning var liten, eftersom terhmtningen startade frn en lg niv. Den samlade bedmningen var att det kunde finnas ytterligare ngot utrymme fr penningpolitiska lttnader. Att marknaden delade denna bedmning framgr av de implicita terminsrntorna vid denna tid. (Diagram 2) Inflationsbedmningen byggde bl.a. p ett antagande om att kronan skulle strkas ngot. Denna frstrkning uteblev; kronan frsvagades istllet med 6 procent frn november 1996 fram till juni 1997. I detta lge valde Riksbanken att inte snka rntorna ytterligare. Frsvagningen frefll vara av varaktig karaktr och pverkade efterfrgan i sdan omfattning att ngon ytterligare snkning av rntorna inte bedmdes vara pkallad. I inflationsrapporten i mars konstaterade Riksbanken att penningpolitiken var vl avvgd och att de stora snkningarna av reporntan behvde utvrderas. Samma bedmning gjordes i juni. Konjunkturen frefaller i r i huvudsak ha utvecklats enligt Riksbankens bedmning. Med facit i hand frefaller det som om terhmtningen kom igng lite senare n frvntat.  andra sidan tycks den - i varje fall under andra kvartalet - ha accelererat s mycket att genomsnittssiffran fr ret br bli i linje med prognosen. Fr frsta gngen sedan Riksbanken brjade arbeta med ett inflationsml r nu svensk ekonomi p vg in i en hgkonjunktur. En viktig frklaring till detta r det std ekonomin har ftt under de senaste ren frn penningpolitiken. Marknadens frvntningar visar nu att diskussionen bland ekonomins aktrer inte lngre handlar om utan nr en rntehjning kommer att ske. 3. Det ekonomiska lget Bred uppgng I inflationsrapporten i september tecknade Riksbanken en relativt ljus bild av den ekonomiska utvecklingen i Sverige, ven om det inte var en bild utan reservationer. terhmtningen frefaller fortstta. Sedan konjunkturen bottnade under sommaren 1993 har svensk ekonomi vuxit med mer n 2,5 procent i genomsnitt, vilket r mer n under 80-talet. Uppgngen under frsta halvret i r visar ocks en mer balanserad utveckling dr, den inhemska efterfrgan i kad utstrckning bidrar till tillvxten (Diagram 3). Industrikonjunkturen frstrks nu ytterligare och olika barometerdata visar att orderingngen frn bde export - och hemmamarknaden fortstter att ka (Diagram 4). Flera faktorer talar fr att lnsamheten r god i stora delar av nringslivet. Kronans vxelkurs har gynnat exportfretagens lnsamhet samtidigt som produktivitetsutvecklingen r god (Diagram 5). Produktiviteten inom industrin kade med nstan mer n 7 procent under frsta halvret i r jmfrt med samma period i fjol. Totalt i ekonomin, inklusive offentlig sektor, kade produktiviteten med nra 4 procent. Mot bakgrund av den snabba tillvxten i industrin r det inte frvnande att kapacitetsutnyttjandet stiger. Andelen fretag som uppgav att tillgngen p produktionsfaktorer begrnsar produktionen steg mellan frsta och andra kvartalet och bristtalen fr vissa yrkesarbetare nrmar sig de niver som rdde under den tillflliga konjunkturtoppen 1995. ven den privata konsumtionen frefaller nu ka i en snabbare takt. Exempelvis steg omsttningen i detaljhandeln med omkring 4 procent under frsta halvret 1997 jmfrt med samma period i fjol. (Diagram 6) Uppgngen i den privata konsumtionen sker trots att hushllens inkomster hlls tillbaka av de skattehjningar och utgiftsneddragningar som beslutats under senare r. Den strama finanspolitiken har medfrt att hushllens reala disponibla inkomster minskat under 1995 och 1996, trots att antalet arbetade timmar kat och trots att de genomsnittliga timlnerna vxt betydligt mer n konsumentpriserna. (Diagram 7) Budgetsaneringen fortstter under de nrmaste ren om n i lngsammare takt. Hushllens reala disponibla inkomster kommer troligen att ka svagt under 1997. En mer mrkbar uppgng vntas 1998 och 1999. Hushllens frvntningar om den egna och om landets ekonomi frbttrades rejlt i september efter en mindre tillbakagng i augusti. Detta avspeglas ocks i den tydliga uppgngen i villapriser och nnu mer i aktier. HIPunderskningen fr september visar att hushllen r mer optimistiska om utsikterna p arbetsmarknaden. Fr frsta gngen sedan 1995 r andelen hushll som tror att arbetslsheten skall minska klart strre n andelen som tror p kad arbetslshet. Det finns ocks tecken p att efterfrgelget p arbetsmarknaden frbttras. Antalet nyanmlda lediga platser kade under perioden juni-augusti med 15 procent p rsbasis och en viss frbttring i sysselsttningen kan sknjas. Sammanfattningsvis talar det mesta fr en god efterfrgeutveckling de nrmaste ren. Exporten br kunna fortstta vxa i relativt snabb takt. Samtidigt rknar Riksbanken med att tillvxten i den privat konsumtionen tilltar och att den offentliga konsumtionen i varje fall inte minskar. I inflationsrapportens huvudscenario r BNP-kningen runt 2 procent i r och omkring 3 procent 1998. Under 1999 bedms tillvxten stiga ytterligare ngot. Produktionsgapet sluts Riksbanken rknar allts med att konjunkturen frstrks under de nrmaste ren. I inflationsrapporten gjorde vi klart att risken fr en utveckling som r svagare n i huvudscenariot har minskat sedan i vras. Den information som kommit senare understryker detta. Svrigheten i att bedma inflationen ligger fr nrvarande frmst i oskerhet om ekonomins utbudssida. Det r drfr srskilt centralt att flja olika indikatorer p tillstndet i ekonomin som ger en bild av hur den frstrkta efterfrgan pverkar utvecklingen p arbetsmarknaden och p olika varumarknader. Hur utvecklas olika mtt p t.ex. kapacitetsutnyttjandet och vilken bild fr man genom att flja prisutvecklingen i ekonomin? Inflationen mtt som frndringen av konsumentprisindex har stigit snabbt under 1997. Tolvmnaderstalet var nere p 0 procent under ett par mnader i vras och har sedan dess i ganska snabb takt rrt sig uppt till 1,9 procent fr september mnad. Huvuddragen i denna utveckling r inte ngon verraskning. En orsak till att KPI stigit r hjda indirekta skatter p bl.a. tobak och en uppgng i flera olika administrativt satta priser. En annan faktor r att rntenedgngen 1996-1997 har en avtagande inverkan p konsumentpriserna. Sammantaget innebr detta att KPI nrmar sig de olika mtt p underliggande inflation som Riksbanken arbetar med. (Diagram 8.) Utfallet av KPI fr september blev emellertid ngot strre n Riksbanken och mnga andra bedmare rknat med. ven om man inte ska dra ngra stora vxlar p en enskild siffra understryker bde KPI:s utveckling och utvecklingen av ett par av de olika mtten p underliggande inflation att det r viktigt med en skrpt uppmrksamhet. Den tillvxt Riksbanken rknar med i inflationsrapportens huvudscenario r hgre n den tillvxt vi bedmer att ekonomin tl lngsiktigt utan att bristfenomen upptrder och att inflationen skjuter fart (den potentiella tillvxten). Detta innebr att den verskottskapacitet som finns idag gradvis kommer att frsvinna. Hur stor r d verkapaciteten? Riksbanken uppskattar det sk. produktionsgapet med flera olika metoder. (Diagram 9.) Nr vi vgt ihop resultatet av de olika skattningarna - och tagit hnsyn till all vrig information om kapacitetsutnyttjandet - har vi gjort bedmningen att det finns en verskottskapacitet i ekonomin som helhet som uppgr till ca 2 procent av BNP. Med de tillvxttakter vi rknar med - och med en potentiell tillvxt p drygt 2 procent under de nrmaste ren - kommer allts produktionsgapet att slutas ngon gng under 1999. I inflationsrapporten redovisas ocks annan information som ger en bild av nr inflationen kan tnkas brja accelerera. Berkningar av den strukturella arbetslsheten - och drmed indirekt av den arbetslshet som gr att frena med en stabil och lg inflation - antyder att det finns risker fr inflationen ocks p kortare sikt. Den takt med vilken kapacitetsutnyttjandet stiger kan ocks ha betydelse fr inflationstakten. Om de lediga resurserna minskar i snabb takt kan resultatet bli kade inflationsimpulser ven om det fortfarande finns verskottskapacitet totalt sett i ekonomin. 4. Finanspolitiken Tv effekter I varje bedmning av inflationsutsikterna r den finanspolitiska inriktningen vsentlig. Finanspolitiken pverkar villkoren fr penningpolitiken p tv olika stt. - Fr det frsta pverkar graden av stramhet eller expansion i finanspolitiken efterfrgelget i ekonomin. Detta r finanspolitikens traditionella inverkan p konjunkturlget. - Fr det andra r frtroendet fr den lngsiktiga hllbarheten i finanspolitiken av betydelse fr det penningpolitiska klimatet. Om statens underskott frefaller ka p ett okontrollerat stt kan oskerhet uppst om problemen ver huvud ska kunna redas ut. Risken fr att lginflationspolitiken ska verges och statsmakterna vlja att inflatera bort skulden kan i denna situation upplevas som ptaglig oberoende av vilka budskap som ges frn officiellt hll. Den pgende budgetsaneringen dmpar efterfrgan i ekonomin. Skattehjningar och minskade transfereringar har dragit ned hushllens inkomster med motsvarande 3 - 4 procent per r. Belastningen p hushllens inkomster var sannolikt som strst 1996, men ven i r och nsta r r finanspolitiken mtt p detta stt stram. Till detta kommer det besparingstryck som budgetsaneringen lett till fr den offentliga verksamheten. Mot den hr bakgrunden rder det ingen tvekan om att finanspolitiken under senare r bidragit till att minska inflationstrycket och att den drmed ocks mjliggjort en lttnad i penningpolitiken. Lnge medfrde dock de stora underskotten - trots att omfattande besparingsprogram presenterades - att det fanns en mer fundamental, lngsiktig oro kring det svenska politiska systemets frmga att reda upp de statsfinansiella problemen. Denna oro var en central faktor bakom den under 1990 till 1995 terkommande rnte- och valutaoron. Situationen har i detta avseende frndrats. Budgetsaneringen r en viktig frklaring till att kronan strkts sedan krisren och till den kraftiga nedgngen i de lnga rntorna. Finanspolitiken har allts ocks p detta stt ppnat fr en mer expansiv penningpolitik. Samtidigt har budgetsaneringen medfrt en kad optimism, som tillsammans med rntefallet, har bidragit till stigande aktiekurser och till terhmtningen p bostadsmarknaden. Detta har kat hushllens frmgenhetsvrden och skapat ett utrymme fr konsumtion. I s mtto har allts den strama finanspolitiken sammantaget bidragit till en stimulans fr ekonomin. Detta r inget unikt. Akademiska studier har visat att tgrder fr att sanera en stats finanser kan ha en expansiv effekt p den ekonomiska utvecklingen srskilt i situationer nr det finns en oro fr den lngsiktiga hllbarheten i statsfinanserna. Nr kronan samtidigt strkts, vilket dmpat tillvxten i de konkurrensutsatta delarna av ekonomin ngot, har Sverige ftt en bttre balans i ekonomins tillvxt. Minska statens skuld Hur ska den fastlagda finanspolitiken vrderas i detta ljus? Klart r att finanspolitiken de nrmaste ren verkar bli mindre stram. Under 1998 och 1999 frefaller den dock fortfarande innebra att staten tar ifrn hushllen en del av deras inkomstkningar. Ocks i ett internationellt perspektiv r politiken stram. Inte i ngot land frbttras det s.k. strukturella underskottet (som det berknas av OECD) lika snabbt mellan 1997 och 1998. Den oro man kan ha r mer lngsiktig. De svenska statsfinanserna r starkt konjunkturknsliga, det visar ett antal olika studier. Det finns argument fr att denna knslighet kan ha minskat, men ingen vet med skerhet hur det frhller sig. Hr behver ett frdjupat arbete gras. Konjunkturknsligheten hnger samman med de offentliga utgifternas och skatternas omfattning, men ocks med olika systems konstruktion. Till detta kommer en i debatten frsummad faktor; den politik som faktiskt bedrivits under de senaste konjunkturcyklerna. Erfarenheten hr r inte helt igenom positiv. Finanspolitiken har inte utformats s att den samlade effekten varit stabiliserande p ekonomin. Det r mot denna bakgrund som Riksbanken argumenterat fr att en ambitionen fr finanspolitiken under de nrmaste ren br vara att reducera statsskulden. Ur penningpolitisk synpunkt skulle detta vara bra eftersom det minskar risken fr att en situation skulle uppkomma ngon gng i framtiden, nr den lngsiktiga hllbarheten i statens finanser ter skulle ifrgasttas. En politik som reducerar konjunkturknsligheten och bidrar till att statens skuld krymper skapar ocks bttre frutsttningar fr en stabil produktionsoch sysselsttningsutveckling genom att minska risken fr kraftiga tstramningar i nsta konjunkturnedgng.
