Title: Current monetary policy
text: In English Webbarkiv Current monetary policy Date: 1998-03-12 Speakers: Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom Location: Finance Committee Thank you for the invitation to come to the Finance Committee and discuss the Swedish economy and monetary policy. I will initially touch on the evaluation of the price stability objective that we have made within the Riksbank and then make a brief comment in connection with the Riksdag's initial decision on new legislation for the Riksbank, which was taken last week. Next, I come to the monetary policy pursued, what assessments we make today about future developments and what it means for monetary policy in the future. The price stability objective has worked well It has now been just over five years since the price stability target was decided in January 1993 by the then Riksbank Council. The decision was made under quite a lot of time pressure. The possibility of deeper analysis was therefore limited. In recent months, we at the Riksbank have spent time studying in more detail various aspects related to the goal formulation and how monetary policy should be conducted to achieve the goal. Now there is more experience and it is possible to look back on the past. The conclusion we have drawn in discussions in the Riksbank's council is that the goal has worked well so far and that there is no reason to rephrase it in any respect. Since the target came into effect, consumer prices have increased by an average of 1.5% per year. This means that the average outcome is below but relatively close to the target of 2 percent and well within the tolerance range. Underlying inflation has been close to 2 per cent over the corresponding period. Thus, the temporary effects that lower inflation have been greater on average than those that raise it. During certain periods, the temporary effects have been particularly noticeable. From July 1996 to July 1997, the 12-month figure in the CPI was below the lower tolerance limit. This was mainly due to the effects that the general decline in interest rates had on the CPI through lower interest costs for own homes. Temporary effects refer to temporary price movements that may result from, for example, changes in indirect taxes or subsidies, changes in international commodity prices, changes in the policy rate, etc. Such effects raise or lower the general price level and thus have a temporary impact on the measured inflation rate over the current 12-month period. If inflation expectations are not affected, such temporary effects are not part of the long-term and trend inflation process. As the 12-month figures in the CPI fell below the lower tolerance limit for a period of time, a discussion arose about why the Riksbank, so to speak, missed the target. Here it is important to note that the reason was temporary effects on inflation and that these became unusually large during this period - not least as a result of the Riksbank's own interest rate cuts. It is not reasonable for monetary policy to seek to counteract the direct impact of the policy rate on consumer prices. In that case, it would mean that monetary policy would, so to speak, chase its own tail. Normally, interest rate effects cancel each other out over an entire business cycle. This raises the wider question of how the Riksbank should view temporary price effects in general. Is it reasonable for monetary policy to seek to counteract the effects of, for example, changes in indirect taxes and subsidies or major international commodity price disruptions? In that case, it would require more drastic monetary policy measures, which would risk destabilising output and employment, which is obviously undesirable. The Riksbank has therefore come to the conclusion that temporary effects should play a subordinate role in monetary policy design to the extent that they do not affect inflation expectations and thus have more lasting effects on inflation. Is it not reasonable, then, to allow this view to be explicitly expressed in the choice of target variable? After all, the CPI measure has the disadvantage that it contains information about both the long-term and trend inflation process and about temporary price movements. If, instead, some measure of underlying inflation were chosen as the target variable, we would of course avoid the discussion we had. The problem is, among other things, that the public would probably not recognize themselves in such a measure. We have therefore come to the conclusion that the benefits of CPI still outweigh and therefore the CPI should be retained as the target variable. On the other hand, it is important to analyse different measures of underlying inflation in the inflation reports, and in other contexts, in order to take into account the information they provide on long-term and trend inflation developments and on temporary price movements. Gradually, the understanding and understanding of these factors will also continue to increase. Independence a support The price stability objective was originally a self-imposed commitment by the Riksbank. However, the Government and the Riksdag have supported both the monetary policy stance towards price stability and the Riksbank's specification of the price stability objective, as formulated five years ago. Last week, the Riksdag took a first decision on the way to new legislation for the Riksbank, which is supposed to enter into force on 1 January 1999. The monetary policy stance towards low inflation is thus consolidated even more strongly. In the five years since the price stability objective was decided, the primary task of monetary policy has been to establish credibility for the objective and the new regime. It has been a long and arduous process. The degree of credibility of the price stability objective depends on the extent to which the public trusts that inflation rates will remain around the target on a lasting basis. A lack of credibility means that monetary policy must be tighter than would otherwise be necessary, and resource utilisation in the economy consequently lower, in order to counteract the inflationary impulses caused by excessive inflation expectations. As a lack of credibility has real economic costs, it is essential that inflation expectations are brought into line with the target as quickly as possible. The new legislation on the Riksbank will be a good support in the work of getting the public to trust that inflation will be around the target of 2 percent in the long term. This, in turn, creates better conditions for, among other things, the wage movements and also enables market interest rates to fluctuate around a lower level in the long term. The legislation also provides the conditions for a stable development of the krona exchange rate. At the same time, we know that the development of public finances also plays an important role in confidence in low-inflation policy and thus in the conditions for monetary policy. This has become clear both when deficits increased and now that we are on the road to balance or even surplus. It underlines that the whole of economic policy must be sustainable in the long term and focused on low inflation. This is a direction that must be nurtured - not least when Sweden will now be outside EMU. In this situation, the demands on economic policy are particularly high  not least in light of the discussion that has taken place about the future development of the krona. In recent years, the credibility of the new low inflation regime and of the price stability target of 2% has increased significantly. This enabled a sharp reduction in the key interest rate in 1996. It has also meant better conditions for, for example, the negotiations that are now being conducted. Even in the rental area, it has left its mark in the form of small rent increases. Furthermore, long-term interest rates are at historically low levels. The margin on long-term interest rates vis-a-vis other countries has also fallen to low levels, although there is room for further improvement as confidence in policy becomes even more consolidated. The demands for transparency are increasing The first decision now taken by the Riksdag on the new legislation for the Riksbank marks for us the start of the work of preparing for the new organisation of the Council and the Executive Board. This includes the need for further steps towards greater transparency. The responsibility given to the Riksbank places natural demands on increased transparency and control of what guides monetary policy decisions. Transparency makes it clear how policies work, which facilitates public efforts to agree with the price stability objective. Market participants can get a clear picture of what governs the Riksbank's actions. The price stability objective is a means of stabilising expectations of the conduct of monetary policy. Therefore, transparency is important in order to make monetary policy work effectively. A lack of transparency and clarity makes it more difficult for inflation expectations to set theirs on target. This, in turn, can make it more difficult to achieve high and stable growth. It is gratifying that the Riksbank's work towards increased transparency has yielded results. The implementation of monetary policy has worked well in recent years. It has also led to a deeper understanding of the opportunities and limitations of monetary policy among a wider public. The surveys that the Riksbank continuously commissions show, gratifyingly, that the Swedish people's support for the price stability objective is very good. As many as 63 percent of the Swedish people support the goal of 2 percent. Only 13 percent are negative. Widespread support is important because monetary policy as a whole must be perceived as legitimate. The new legislation increases the requirements for transparency. This means that this process should continue as far as it is reasonable and possible. For example, the Riksbank's council has already stressed in the past that voluntary publication of the minutes of the Executive Board should be possible within the framework of the current confidentiality legislation and that this issue should be examined when the new Executive Board has found its role. Repo rate has been raised Let me now turn to the current monetary policy. Since I was last in the Finance Committee at the end of October last year to discuss monetary policy, the repo rate has been raised from 4.10 to 4.35 percent, i.e. by 0.25 percentage points. More specifically, it took place in December 1997. The decision provided for the consistent application of the following rule to monetary policy: Assuming an unchanged policy rate, the headline inflation projection suggests that inflation will be in line with the price stability objective of 2%, over a two-year horizon, monetary policy is well balanced. If the assessment instead shows that inflation risks exceeding the target, the monetary policy stance is too expansionary, and the repo rate should then be raised. Conversely, if the target is at risk of being undercut, the policy is too contractive and the repo rate should be lowered. In some quarters, the decision met with some criticism. I believe that it would be of value for the monetary policy discussion if those who have views on the Riksbank's actions more clearly specify the arguments. Is it advocating a different target, which is higher than 2%? Or is the criticism about making a different inflation assessment than the Riksbank? In the general discussion, the distinction between these two is not always clear. The Riksbank's view is that monetary policy must be consistently focused on the target. Otherwise, ambiguities may arise, which in turn may drive up inflation expectations. This, as I have said before, is something that must be avoided. Higher than target inflation expectations lead to unnecessary real economic costs. The reason for choosing such a long horizon for monetary policy as one of two years, with the difficulties it entails in making reliable forecasts, is that it allows for a softer and more gradual adjustment of interest rate policy than otherwise. If, instead, a shorter time horizon is chosen, which in itself could mean greater accuracy in the assessments, the monetary policy rulings must be greater in order for the target to be met. Then there would be greater fluctuations in production and employment, a risk that should be taken into account when choosing the time horizon. In this election, therefore, consideration of real factors such as production and employment comes into play. The Riksbank has therefore, among other things, stopped at the fact that the so-called. the steering horizon normally should be one of two years. In connection with the previous discussion here in committee, I stressed that monetary policy cannot be allowed to be too expansionary for too long in a rising economy. In such a situation, it should be rescheduled in good time so that actual growth is in line with the long-term growth trajectory of the economy. Otherwise, the economy risks expanding too quickly in the short term and various types of bottleneck problems arise in the labour market or on the real capital side. It is in such a situation that inflation can increase. Sooner or later, this leads to a halt in the growth phase, a slowdown in production and a fall in employment. A change in monetary policy in good time is thus not done to break off the expansion of the economy, but to make growth more lasting and balanced. That is the meaning of a policy geared towards price stability and perceived as credible. It is therefore not, at least to begin with, a question of a real tightening of monetary policy, but of a movement that gives a less expansionary direction. The December 1997 Inflation Report estimated that overall growth would be around 3% in 1998 and 1999. The rising demand would gradually increase capacity utilisation in the economy and gradually create pressure on available production resources. This was expected to lead to some increased inflationary pressures. With monetary policy unchanged, inflation, as measured by the CPI, was expected to rise gradually to 2.5 percent. Underlying inflation was projected to be slightly higher. In order to avoid sharper interest rate hikes at a later stage, it was estimated that the time had come for a shift in a less expansionary direction. A first step was taken when the repo rate was raised by 25 basis points in December. Latest Inflation Report Since the increase in the repo rate in December, the GDP outcome for the fourth quarter has been presented. Between the fourth quarters of 1996 and 1997, GDP grew by 3.3%. Thus, activity in the Swedish economy rose significantly towards the end of the year. At the same time, the Asian crisis has worsened. Although the starting point is still that the economy is still rising both in Europe and in Sweden, the assessment is now made that the Asian crisis will probably have a more dampening effect on economic and inflation development than previously predicted. In addition, there is a somewhat more favourable start to the wage round than previously estimated, as well as the fact that renegotiations on rents result in lower increases than expected. In the Riksbank's latest inflation report, which was presented in early March, we present an assessment that usually extends two years ahead. This means that inflation, as measured by an annual change in the CPI, is projected to be broadly in line with the 1998 and 1999 headlines at unchanged monetary policy. The underlying pace is expected to be slightly higher towards the end of the period, reflecting a still rising economy, despite the Asian crisis, and gradually rising resource utilisation in the economy. The Asian crisis is thus expected to dampen the upturn in the economy somewhat, but not to interrupt growth. The inflation outlook is based on growth this year being just over 2.5 per cent and about. 3 percent next year. In light of the expansionary monetary policy prevailing and on which the forecast conditions are based, and provided that the crisis in Asia does not have too long-lasting effects on international development, growth is expected to be good also in 2000. Employment is expected to increase as demand strengthens. Signs of this are also visible in the statistics. This, together with various educational initiatives, means that unemployment is expected to continue to decrease to some extent. If this main scenario is realized, it means that we have to look forward to a fairly favorable development for the Swedish economy in the coming years. Good growth and slightly rising employment, while inflationary pressures are moderate. It can be said that the Asian crisis, as assessed in this main scenario, means that the continued monetary policy shift is being pushed forward somewhat. The future of monetary policy Overall, the information received since the end of 1997 suggests that the inflation outlook will be somewhat more subdued. The comprehensive inflation assessment is normally based not only on a single scenario, but different types of risk assessments, which are taken into account in the final assessment, of future inflation developments, are at least as important. The changing risk picture, which we see ahead of us, is therefore also important for the design of monetary policy. There is still a risk that the Asian crisis will worsen and that inflation will be lower than can now be estimated. The repercussions on the international economy and on Sweden can then be more extensive and protracted. At the same time, the risk of higher inflation driven by high wage growth and weak productivity growth has diminished. In addition, the development of the krona plays a role in the Riksbank's assessments. There has been a tendency to weaken the krona in recent months. If such a weakening is permanent, it could affect the inflation outlook and thus also the structure of monetary policy. In summary, the Riksbank's assessment in the latest inflation report shows that the inflation outlook appears to be more subdued compared with the end of the year. However, in our main scenario, an economic upturn is expected, with slowly rising capacity utilisation and thus slightly increasing inflationary pressures. This suggests a certain cautious tightening of monetary policy in the coming year. At the same time, the Asian crisis means that inflation may be lower. In addition, the krona's development has led to increased uncertainty about future inflation. Overall, the Riksbank concluded in the Inflation Report that the repo rate should not be changed at this time. However, the uncertainty in the assessment means that there are strong reasons to continuously test the structure of monetary policy in the light of new incoming information. Since the presentation of the Inflation Report, some new statistics have been received. It does not justify any other conclusion on monetary policy. Title: Monetary policy
text: In English Webbarkiv Monetary policy Date: 1998-10-14 Speakers: Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Location: SNS conference on the economic situation Let me start by thanking you for allowing me to come here. SNS business conference is a fine tradition that it is nice to be able to contribute to. In previous years, I have used this opportunity to look back at the past year and discuss the Riksbank's actions and the monetary policy structure. But I have also tried to look ahead and point out some issues that are important for monetary policy in the long run. I intend to broadly follow this approach. Thus, I begin by looking back at developments from last autumn and commenting on how the Riksbank's assessment of inflation has developed during the year. I will also, as in the past, raise the issue of how we have communicated policy and how it has been perceived in the financial markets. This year we are in the midst of an international financial crisis, with great uncertainty about what the real economic effects may be. The crisis has gradually proved to have ever greater spill-over effects. Looking back, it is clear how most analysts' forecasts of economic development have swung during the year from a stage of concern about rising inflationary pressures in the long run to a stage where there is strong concern that the world economy will be hit by recession. Against this background, I discuss the current monetary policy assessment of the Swedish economy and some factors that will be important in the trade-offs. First of all, however, I will give a brief description of the framework of thought for monetary policy. Forecasts and probability assessments The overall objective of Swedish monetary policy is to safeguard the value of money. Annual inflation, as measured by the change in the consumer price index, shall be limited to 2%. However, the Riksbank's monetary policy measures will only have a full impact after a certain period of time. Our action must therefore be based primarily on an assessment of inflation developments in the future. The policy horizon - the time after which monetary policy has most of its impact - is around one to two years. The Riksbank's assessment of future inflation is presented on an ongoing basis in our inflation reports. These have gradually developed since the first report was published in October 1993 and the Riksbank has, among other things, become increasingly explicit in its assessments. Until 1995, the reports included a more general review of developments in inflation indicators and inflationary pressures in the economy. From November 1995 onwards, the Riksbank began to put figures on the inflation assessment presented. The June 1996 report supported the inflation assessment for the first time with an overall picture of the economic situation. The inflation assessment developed further in September 1997, when it was supplemented by a path of inflation over the projection horizon. In the following report, we presented uncertainty ranges around our main inflation trajectory. The likelihood that developments will follow different alternative paths is taken into account when monetary policy decisions are taken. How, then, are the uncertainty intervals calculated? In practice, those involved in the forecasting work make assessments for a number of variables - both about how uncertain they are and how great this uncertainty is compared to what is normal. This information is then used in a smaller macro model, with the help of which inflation can be calculated. Of course, the probability distributions we obtain in this way are highly subjective, but they at least give a coherent picture of how the Riksbank values different risks. One thing is particularly important to remember when it comes to the inflation projections; they are based on keeping the repo rate unchanged during the period. A forecast of inflationary developments that deviate from the target  or the large deviations that the uncertainty intervals indicate as possible events  constitutes a diagnosis that may require treatment. If necessary, changes in the repo rate are used to bring inflation back to target. One consequence of this is that the uncertainty about future inflation is in reality not as great as the uncertainty ranges may give the impression, another that our inflation forecasts are out of date as soon as the Riksbank changes interest rates. Last year's assessments A lot has happened over the past year in terms of economic development and the conditions for monetary policy. Both the Riksbank, other public analysts and market forecasters have changed their assessments as the international crisis has had increasing spillover effects. "Last autumn, most analysts believed in strong economic development, both in Sweden and in the rest of the world. The crisis that had flared up in Southeast Asia was seen as leading mostly to a much-needed dampening of international price pressures. In Sweden, some indicators last autumn pointed to increasing inflationary pressures in the Swedish economy. Above all, capacity utilisation in the economy gradually increased and this process was eventually expected to lead to inflation above the Riksbank's target. Inflation expectations also rose slightly after previously falling for several years in a row and subsequently stabilising. In the Riksbank's December inflation report, inflation was assumed to be above target in 1999. The Riksbank raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage points. At the same time, the Riksbank pointed to the uncertainty in its assessment, which could lead to a different development than in the main scenario. On the one hand, a worsening crisis in Asia could lead to weaker inflationary pressures. On the other hand, there were risks that high wage growth and weak productivity growth would fuel inflation rates. The two alternative scenarios were assessed as equally plausible. "During the spring, the inflation picture gradually changed. The worsening crisis in Asia and low import prices slightly changed the inflation outlook in the March report. Subdued inflation expectations and wage moderation pointed in the same direction. As a result of the weak international economic development, Sweden was not expected to reach full capacity utilisation until the end of the forecast period and inflation was assumed to exceed the target marginally. This suggested a readiness for some cautious tightening of monetary policy later in the year. At the same time, the risk picture had shifted. Risks of higher than expected inflation had diminished, while there were still risks of weaker developments than the main scenario indicated. The uncertainty meant that the Riksbank chose to wait for further developments. "At the beginning of the summer, we found that inflation developments were more subdued than we had assumed in the main scenario in March. This was due to weaker import prices, but also to other factors. Temporary effects  weaker interest rates and changes in indirect taxes and subsidies  were particularly important. Longer-term inflation was also expected to be slightly lower than previously forecast by the Riksbank as a result of lower wage increases and stronger than expected productivity growth. The productivity development meant that some overcapacity was expected to remain in Sweden throughout the period. Overall, the one- to two-year inflation outlook thus appeared to be more subdued than in the past and the forecast remained below target throughout the projection horizon. In addition, risks were assessed to be high for inflation to be lower than in the main scenario. Against this background, the repo rate was lowered by 0.25 percentage points. Despite the changes, however, the economic picture for the near future has remained broadly the same over the past year, with expectations of good economic growth in 1998, increasingly due to rising domestic demand. This development has also been confirmed. However, uncertainty about the longer growth perspective has increased during the year and increased significantly in late summer and autumn. Temporary effects and lower import prices The picture is that inflation in 1998, although the economic forecast has proved to be fairly correct, has fallen markedly lower, mainly as a result of large changes in temporary effects and import prices. At the beginning of the year, the temporary effects were expected to cancel each other out and have no impact on inflation developments at all in 1998. However, decisions on, among other things, reduced tobacco tax and property tax in the spring meant that the temporary effects were assumed to have a sharply restraining effect on inflation. The June report expected the temporary effects to contain inflation by as much as 1.2 percentage points in 1998. In the September report, this figure was revised up to 1.3 percent. The temporary effects on inflation for 1999 and 2000 were assumed to be marginal. Import prices have also developed weaker than expected. In its assessment made in December, the Riksbank assumed that import prices would increase inflation by around half a percentage point per year throughout our forecast period. Some downward revision was made in March and in June a further adjustment was made. Import prices were then no longer considered to make a major contribution to the CPI. Behind the lower outcomes and the lower forecasts is mainly a fall in the price of raw materials, but also the international price development of processed goods that has been lower than expected, which is probably partly a result of the Asian crisis. Rents are another item in the CPI basket that performed weaker than expected in the spring. Since the turn of the year, rent growth has fallen to historically low levels. This development can to some extent be attributed to lower interest costs as well as lower wage and inflation expectations, but is also due to lower property taxes and lower heating costs. Wages appear to have developed largely as the Riksbank expected. We currently expect them to increase by 3.5-4 percent per year during the period 19982000. This is only slightly lower than what we expected in December before the conclusion of the contract negotiations. What effect the Riksbank's own actions have had on the wage movement is debatable; about this there are different opinions. I myself live by the contacts I have had with the social partners in the notion that monetary policy has influenced the outcome of the wage movement in a positive direction. However, many other factors also came into play. The fact that wage formation this time took place both centrally, with attempts to keep wage formation together if not in the entire labor market, then at least in large parts, and decentralized in individual companies, seems to have contributed to the low outcome. Another question is whether this model can be repeated. Temporary effects, import prices and rents account for 2 percentage points of the significant downward revision of inflation for 1998 totalling 2.2 percentage points between the December and September Inflation Reports. The same factors account for about half of the adjustment for 1999 and 2000 between the March and June forecasts. Increased understanding of monetary policy, but problems this spring For a few years now, the Riksbank has worked hard to communicate the thinking framework that forms the basis for the decisions to both the public and market players. The intention of this is, on the one hand, to increase the general understanding of the role and possibilities of monetary policy and, on the other hand, to avoid , as far as possible, market disturbances due to uncertainty. The clearer the thinking model for market participants, the smoother the adjustment of short-term interest rates should be able to take place as new information on inflation perspectives comes in. When market expectations, as expressed in the implicit forward rates, are compared with the actual repo rate, one gets a kind of measure of the market's forecast error for the repo rate. These forecasting errors have, on the whole, become less and less. With the reservation that this measure is also affected by various interest rate premiums in the market, which can vary from time to time, it suggests that the understanding of our policies has increased. Naturally, the forecast errors are greater in a year's time. In this time perspective, they do not normally reflect so much communication problems or a lack of understanding of how politics works. Rather, it is probably a question of shifting the whole picture of the economy and inflation. In the three-month perspective, the picture is probably a little different, as the forecast errors are probably also due to misinterpretations of the signals sent out by the Riksbank. Over the past year, there has been both an increase and a reduction in interest rates. This has placed great demands on the Riksbank's ability to communicate its policy to the outside world and explain what lies behind the measures taken. A study of market prices as well as forecasts and statements on the market shows that the increase in interest rates in December 1997 was largely expected. An important part of the signalling, incidentally, took place at this very conference last year. In the run-up to the interest rate cut in June, on the other hand, the expectations picture in the market changed at a relatively late stage. The implicit forward rate curves three months before the change in interest rates show that market participants did not foresee a reduction in the repo rate in June. Expectations were focused on a reduction mainly in the context of an interview I gave a few weeks before the decision. The Riksbank's handling of the information about the interest rate cut was subjected to criticism from market participants. It was felt that we had been unclear and too quickly pivoted in our assessment of the inflation outlook. Some stakeholders took big words, saying that the lack of clarity had damaged confidence in the policy and would make it difficult to conduct effective policies in the future. I think that was a good thing. However, this does not prevent the Riksbank from being able to better prepare the market for what could possibly happen. At the same time, it is important to emphasize that the development during the spring was difficult to assess. Of course, we changed our minds, but not so quickly, and there was great uncertainty for a long time about what the next step might be. In such a situation, where uncertainty is perceived as great, it is difficult to communicate. One reason why we were not so attentive to the fact that market expectations were wrong was that market participants' own forecasts were in line with ours. The problem was not that we had different views on inflation perspectives, but that market pricing did not reflect that the Riksbank would lower interest rates even though inflation was below target. Somewhat drastically, it can be said that market players seemed to share lo's view that the Riksbank had a "bias" in its actions. In any case, a clear lesson from the events of the spring is the value for market assessors of making independent forecasts of inflation and, on the basis of these, making forecasts for the repo rate. For the Riksbank, what happened has meant that we are working even more to continuously monitor how market perceptions develop in order to be able to react in good time if deviations seem to arise between market participants' and our own assessments. Baseline and balanced risks Let me now look ahead and look at the current inflation assessment. The Riksbank's latest inflation report, published at the end of September, stressed that uncertainty about the inflation outlook was high. The picture of economic development was somewhat different from June, as growth was expected to be strongest this year and then slow down somewhat. Nevertheless, we expected a decent economic development with growth of just under 3 percent per year in the coming years. Inflation  measured as twelve-month figures in the CPI  was assumed to be below 2% in 1998 and 1999, but to be around 2% at the end of the period. The composition of demand was expected to be slightly different than before. The international crisis was expected to result in a weaker development of net exports than previously assumed, while domestic demand was expected to develop somewhat stronger than in the June forecast. The assessment was based on an assumption of a strengthening of the krona from the then prevailing level of 124, measured by the so-called TCW index, to 120 in the coming year and just over 117 in the following year. Inflation impulses from the rest of the world were expected to be low during the period. The increase in domestic demand was not expected to lead to a worrying increase in inflationary pressures. Investment growth and labour supply were considered sufficient to avoid general capacity problems during the forecast period. Wage and productivity developments were expected to be favourable to developments of moderate, but rising, inflation. Inflation expectations remained low among market participants, firms and households. In the short term, inflation was expected to fall below the target, but in the longer term inflation was expected on a par with the inflation target. The fundamentally positive picture of the Swedish economy with good growth and inflation gradually returning to the target level during the forecast period meant that the Riksbank left the repo rate unchanged. However, the increased uncertainty compared to previous assessments meant that the uncertainty ranges around our main trajectory were wider. However, the risk picture was symmetrical, i.e. there were estimated to be as high a risk that inflation would be higher as that it would be lower than in the main scenario. The international economic climate may lead to even weaker inflation developments than in our main scenario, while a permanently weaker krona, which was not due to deteriorating economic fundamentals, could lead to upward pressure on prices. Increased financial turmoil Financial turmoil has intensified since the report was published. How great the real economic impact will be on the industrialized countries in the Western world of the crisis that started in Thailand barely a year and a half ago is difficult to predict. After all, the direct real economic effects via foreign trade are likely to be relatively small. For the Swedish economy and inflation perspectives, the effects that may arise from reduced general confidence in the economy are more important. The Swedish stock market has fallen further since the inflation report was presented and it is now not only the upturn in 1998 that has been erased but also part of the upturn last year. Since peaking in July, the stock market has fallen by just under 30 percent , which means a fall of close to 8 percent since the turn of the year 1997/98. Since the publication of the Inflation Report, prices have fallen by just under 6 percent. If the turmoil continues and wealth values fall, it will have an impact on consumer and corporate behavior. The level of activity in the economy will be lower if households and enterprises delay consumption and investment decisions. Some signs of this exist. Households' expectations of the Swedish economy have taken a minor hit, judging by the latest figures. However, this has not yet affected expectations about one's own economy. The growth rate of loans to enterprises has also slowed down slightly. Another channel through which the economy can be influenced is through the banking system. Increased caution on the part of banks to provide credit may dampen economic activity. Here, the international picture is a cause for concern. The movement noted in the late summer when investors fled to assets that were considered generally safe - flight to quality - has developed into a general reluctance to hold risk and investors are instead fleeing to more liquid assets. The economic fundamentals of individual countries do not currently play a major role in the investment decisions taken. Some third world countries have been hit very hard by this development. The Riksbank is closely monitoring developments in the financial system in Sweden. From what can be deduced from the statistics, Swedish banks are in a better position than many of the international banks with a lower exposure to crisis-hit countries. Even when it comes to exposure to so-called hedge funds, the picture seems to be relatively good. Behind this low exposure is probably the Swedish banking crisis at the beginning of the decade. Thus, the risk of a domestically generated "credit crunch" should be small. Weak crown However, developments since the inflation report was written have not only led to increased uncertainty and greater risks of a weaker economy. It has also put pressure on the Swedish krona. Since September 28, the krona, as measured by the TCW index, has weakened by just under 2 percent and since the krona weakening began in May this year, the krona's share price has fallen by about 9 percent. As on previous occasions, the Swedish krona has been hit by financial turmoil as investors take the safe before the uncertain and seek out larger and more stable currencies. However, this time the concern seems to be to a lesser extent due to uncertainty about the development of the economic basic conditions in Sweden. Instead, it seems to be due to a general aversion to risk on the part of investors. Support for this view can be obtained, among other things, by looking at what is written in market letters (both Swedish and foreign). This should suggest a strengthening in the next stage, when the general unrest has subsided and the assessment of the economic fundamentals will again be decisive for the interest of investors. Market participants also seem to take this into account in their assessments, judging, among other things, by the surveys Prospera has conducted for the Riksbank. The recent sharp weakening of the Swedish krona reminds us of both the advantages and disadvantages of variable exchange rates. The weaker exchange rate may provide an adjustment mechanism at a time when the international economy is weakening. This can prove valuable if the crisis is deep. At the same time, recent events show that our vulnerability is significant with a variable exchange rate. Despite a fundamentally stability-oriented economic policy, the krona has swung. The same experience has been gained in other countries with variable exchange rates and inflation targets such as Canada, Australia and New Zealand. This not only makes it more difficult to assess future developments, but is also likely to entail costs in the form of poorer real economic developments. Conclusion Sweden has been pursuing monetary policy with inflation targets and variable exchange rates since January 1993. The result has in many ways been good. Growth in the Swedish economy has since the economy started to turn up in the summer of 1993, compared with, for example, the boom in the late 1980s. Unlike then, however, inflation has been low. It is also important to note the good real wage development. The low price increases have led to an average increase in real wages of 2.5% per year since 1994, which is more than in the 1980s, for example, when nominal wages increased rapidly while the amounts that households were really allowed to retain from wage increases were very modest. Understanding of monetary policy also appears to have increased. This is probably mainly due to the relatively good economic development in recent years. We can see the changed attitudes by studying measurements of how Swedes view the Riksbank and monetary policy. You get the same picture if you look at how the bank and monetary policy are treated in the Swedish press. The basic framework of thought has largely gained acceptance, although of course (and sometimes perhaps even fairly) from time to time there is criticism of our actions. It is also worth noting that a large majority of the new Riksdag has now supported a deal with, among other things, a statutory goal of maintaining a fixed monetary value and greater independence for the Riksbank. The previous discussion also shows that the understanding of the Riksbank's actions seems to have increased among market players, which does not prevent this from being improved. In recent weeks, there have been some cuts in key interest rates in the rest of the world. This is, of course, an expression of the increased concern that exists about a deepening crisis that will lead to lower inflation. However, there is reason to be a little cautious about taking other central banks' interest rate cuts as revenue because the Riksbank should do the same. This often happens in the debate. In comparison with the US, for example, it is important to remember that interest rates there are 1.15 percentage points higher in the initial situation. According to most analysts, the US is also in a different economic phase. When making comparisons with continental Europe, it is particularly important to consider the exchange rate. The weakening of the exchange rate that has occurred means that the economy has received a tangible stimulus. If the current TCW index were to persist for the next two years, it would mean an expansionary effect on the economy equivalent to one or a few percentage points of interest rate cuts. The weeks since the Riksbank presented the Inflation Report have been dramatic in the financial markets. Our baseline scenario is still a relatively good Swedish economy in the coming years, with inflationary pressures gradually rising from a low level. On the other hand, uncertainty about developments has been further strengthened in connection with the financial turbulence. The risk of weak international development has increased. In addition, the continued stock market turmoil has made domestic demand more difficult to assess than before. At the same time, the krona has weakened and thus moved in a different direction than the one that formed the basis for the main assessment in the Inflation Report. From the Riksbank's side, we are following developments closely. It is an obvious part of our work to promote financial stability in the economy. It is also a necessary part of monetary policy work. At present, there is no reason to change the direction of interest rate policy. Lne- och produktivitetsutvecklingen frvntades bli gynnsam fr en utveckling med mttlig, men stigande, inflation. Inflationsfrvntningarna var fortsatt lga bland marknadsaktrer, fretag och hushll. P kort sikt frvntades inflationen komma att understiga mlet, men p lngre sikt frvntades en inflation i paritet med inflationsmlet. Den grundlggande positiva bilden av den svenska ekonomin med god tillvxt och en inflation som successivt terfrs till den mlsatta nivn under prognosperioden innebar att Riksbanken lmnade reporntan ofrndrad. Den kade oskerheten jmfrt med tidigare bedmningar innebar dock att oskerhetsintervallen kring vr huvudbana var bredare. Riskbilden var emellertid symmetrisk, d.v.s. det bedmdes finnas lika stora risker att inflationen skulle bli hgre som att den skulle bli lgre n i huvudscenariot. Den internationella konjunkturen kan komma att leda till en nnu svagare inflationsutveckling n i vrt huvudscenario, medan en varaktigt svagare krona som inte berodde p frsmrade ekonomiska grundfrutsttningar skulle kunna leda till en press uppt p priserna. kad finansiell oro Den finansiella oron har tilltagit sedan rapporten publicerades. Hur stora de realekonomiska effekterna blir fr industrilnderna i vstvrlden av den kris som startade i Thailand fr knappt ett och ett halvt r sedan r svrt att frutsga. De direkta realekonomiska effekterna via utrikeshandeln blir sannolikt trots allt relativt sm. Fr den svenska konjunkturen och inflationsperspektiven r de effekter som kan uppst via minskat allmnt frtroende i ekonomin viktigare. Den svenska brsen har fallit ytterligare sedan inflationsrapporten presenterades och det r nu inte enbart uppgngen under 1998 som har raderats utan ven en del av uppgngen under frra ret. Sedan toppnoteringen i juli har brsen fallit med knappt 30 procent , vilket innebr ett fall med nra 8 procent sedan rsskiftet 1997/98. Sedan inflationsrapporten publicerades har kurserna fallit med knappt 6 procent. Om oron fortstter och frmgenhetsvrdena faller fr det effekter p konsumenters och fretags beteende. Aktivitetsnivn i ekonomin blir lgre om hushll och fretag avvaktar med konsumtions- och investeringsbeslut. Vissa tecken p detta finns. Hushllens frvntningar om den svenska ekonomin har ftt sig en mindre trn att dma av de senaste siffrorna. En del lnder i tredje vrlden har drabbats mycket hrt av denna utveckling. Riksbanken fljer noga utvecklingen i det finansiella systemet i Sverige. Av vad som kan utlsas ur statistiken har de svenska bankerna en bttre position n mnga av de internationella bankerna med en lgre exponering gentemot krisdrabbade lnder. Svag krona Utvecklingen sedan inflationsrapporten skrevs har emellertid inte enbart inneburit en kad oskerhet och strre risker fr en svagare konjunktur. Den har ocks pressat den svenska kronan. I huvudsak verkar det i stllet bero p allmn motvilja mot risk hos placerarna. Std fr denna uppfattning kan man bl.a. f genom att titta p vad som skrivs i marknadsbrev (bde svenska och utlndska). Detta borde tala fr en frstrkning i nsta skede, d den allmnna oron lagt sig och bedmningen av de ekonomiska grundfrutsttningarna ter blir det avgrande fr placerarnas intresse. Detta frefaller ocks marknadsaktrerna ta med i sina bedmningar att dma bl.a. av de enkter Prospera gjort t Riksbanken. Den kraftiga frsvagningen i den svenska kronan under den senaste tiden pminner oss om svl frdelarna som nackdelarna med rrlig vxelkurs. Den svagare vxelkursen kan utgra en anpassningsmekanism i ett skede d den internationella konjunkturen frsvagas. Detta kan visa sig vrdefullt om krisen r djup. Samtidigt visar den senaste tidens hndelser att vr utsatthet r betydande med en rrlig vxelkurs. Trots en i grunden stabilitetsinriktad ekonomisk politik har kronan svngt. Avslutning Sverige har bedrivit penningpolitik med inflationsml och rrlig vxelkurs sedan januari 1993. Resultatet har p mnga vis varit gott. Den tidigare diskussionen visar ocks att frstelsen fr Riksbankens agerande verkar har kat hos marknadens aktrer, vilket inte hindrar att detta kan frbttras. Under de senaste veckorna har det skett en del snkningar av styrrntorna i omvrlden. Detta r naturligtvis ett uttryck fr den kade oro som finns fr en frdjupad kris som medfr en lgre inflation. Title: Sweden and EMU
text: In English Webbarkiv Sweden and EMU Date: 1998-03-16 Speakers: Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom Location: Central Union of Industry and Employers, Helsinki Mr President, I would like to begin by thanking you for the invitation to speak about Sweden and EMU. Listening to the debate on economic development in Sweden and Finland, one can see that relations between the countries are described with parables taken from both the world of family life and sports. Should big or little brother decide? Who will win the international match in economic development when the countries go in different directions? By the way, who is big and little brother, respectively? I think it is wrong to use such terms. Instead, we can state that the two brothers choose to go their separate ways in the near future. For various reasons, Finland has chosen to participate in the currency union from the start, while Sweden has chosen to remain outside when EMU is formed. However, we are still on the same financial playing field with the same rules and the same referees. In my speech, I wanted to give my picture of what this might mean for the Swedish economy. I will begin by briefly showing the similar experiences Finland and Sweden had during the 80s and 90s. Next, I would like to address the preparations and frameworks that have been created for economic policy within Sweden and that will apply to our action in an exclusion. Similar experiences The development of the Swedish economy during the 80s and 90s is very similar to that of Finland. Like Finland, the Swedish economy experienced overheating in the late eighties, mainly due to excessive domestic demand as a result of rapid credit expansion. Overheating was reversed in a sharp setback during the early 90s. Between 1991 and 1993, GDP fell markedly, unemployment rose, state finances deteriorated significantly and the banking system went through a crisis. The pressure against the currency became strong and the fixed exchange rate was abandoned in the autumn of 1992. Sveriges Riksbank was in the same difficult situation as the Bank of Finland did after the currency crisis. Decisions on a new monetary policy strategy would be taken in an environment where confidence in monetary and exchange rate policy was low. Previous actions in economic policy  with great eagerness to resort to the weapon of devaluation in the event of the cost crises that have arisen  together with the loss in the battle for the fixed rate, were some reasons for the weak confidence. Alternative strategies were investigated and the Riksbank looked at solutions in other countries. As in the case of Finland, we in Sweden were not familiar with an environment of variable exchange rates. The general view, both among politicians and economists, had been that a fixed exchange rate is the only solution for a small, open economy with a high foreign dependence. This perception has since changed. The two central banks chose largely the same path. Monetary policy focused on direct inflation targets and the quantified target was published in early 1993. However, the Swedish target formulation was somewhat more detailed, as we established that inflation, measured as CPI, is limited to 2 percent, with a permissible deviation of /- 1 percentage point. Finland chose to formulate its inflation target as a sustained stable underlying inflation rate of 2 per cent. As in Finland, the Swedish price stability objective was initially a self-imposed commitment on the part of the central bank, but gradually received explicit support from the Riksdag and the government. The target of an inflation rate of 2% applied from 1995 onwards. During the transition period, inflation and expectations would be dampened from the high levels prevailing in the 80s. Confidence would thus be restored. In order to achieve an understanding of our policy and create a broad knowledge of the decision-making bases for policy, the Riksbank chose to publish inflation reports on an ongoing basis. Inflation reports are now published four times a year and describe clearly and in detail actual inflation developments, present the Bank's assessment of future inflation and draw conclusions on the direction of monetary policy. Parted ways In October 1996, Finland's choice of strategy was changed. While maintaining the price stability objective, an exchange rate target was also set within the exchange rate cooperation (ERM). Reconnaissance at a fixed rate would be seen as a preparatory step for Finland's participation in monetary union from January 1999. Sweden, for its part, has opted for a wait-and-see attitude towards monetary union and does not intend to participate from the outset. The Riksdag noted that Sweden's economy had recovered and that the convergence criteria are likely to be achieved, but that popular support is too weak for participation from 1999. A later participation is not excluded if the situation changes. As far as the Riksbank is concerned, we have the ambition to make the necessary preparations so that we can participate in monetary union with one year's notice. Technical preparations are already underway in many areas, partly to be able to meet the requirements set for participation in the future and partly for the requirements that are simply imposed due to the fact that a new currency is introduced in Europe and must be met regardless of whether Sweden chooses to remain outside. Sweden must also prepare itself economically and politically. What does exclusion mean for Swedish economic policy? What are the requirements? The debate in Finland often reflects concern that Sweden, by staying out of the currency union, will allow the krona to depreciate and thus create a competitive advantage over Finnish industry. I am very surprised by these statements, especially the indignation that is sometimes suspected. I am perhaps most surprised by the fact that they often reflect an outdated economic policy environment and do not take into account the framework for policy that currently exists both in Finland and in Sweden in the area of monetary policy. The requirements for the economic policy of an individual country do not depend on participation in monetary union, but are the result of the world in which we live today. There is simply less room to pursue a national policy that deviates sharply from that of the world around us. Let me continue with a discussion about what the framework is for Swedish policy and what priorities have guided us to these. Implications for economic policy going forward Sweden will thus remain outside the currency union initially, which means that monetary policy decisions will continue to be made by the Riksbank. Swedish monetary policy will continue to be designed based on developments in the Swedish economy Just as today, Swedish policy will be designed both on the basis of the frameworks set up within Sweden for economic policy based on our domestic priorities and the frameworks provided by our membership of the EU. The priorities within Sweden and the EU are to a large extent the same. They are to pursue an economic policy geared towards stability and low inflation. The requirements for balanced economic policy are independent of participation in monetary union. Conditions for monetary policy The Riksdag's statement on the ERM in connection with the decision on EMU means that Swedish monetary policy will continue to be conducted in the same way as today. The Riksdag stated that membership of the ERM should be seen as a preparatory step before entering the monetary union and that there is therefore much to suggest that participation in the ERM will only be relevant in connection with decisions on participation in EMU. Monetary policy will thus continue to focus on floating exchange rates with an explicit price stability objective. As from 1 January 1999, the objective of price stability will be enshrined in law. The Riksbank will become more independent and thus have the opportunity to ensure that the goal assigned to it by the Riksdag is achieved. A majority of the Swedish Parliament supports these changes. These changes respond to the demands of the EU on monetary policy and the role of the central bank. Regardless of participation in the currency union, Sweden is committed to having an independent central bank and therein lies a far-reaching delegation of decision-making power over monetary policy based on an operational goal. Conditions for fiscal policy Similarly, Swedish fiscal policy will also continue to be covered by the targets set in Sweden, but also by those established within the EU. In 1997, the government declared that it was setting a long-term target for Swedish public finances. The Swedish Parliament supported the objective. In the medium term, the budget should show a surplus of 2% of GDP on average over a business cycle. By achieving a surplus, public debt can be reduced so that the challenges that may meet the Swedish economy in the future can be assumed without creating fiscal problems. The Riksbank considers this to be a reasonable target in light of the relatively high cyclical sensitivity of Swedish public finances. In addition to an increased awareness of the importance of stable finances, institutional changes in the budget process have also improved the conditions for achieving the Swedish budget target. Sweden has now got a budget process that in itself creates more discipline and can thus contribute to healthier finances. Sweden's objective of consolidating public finances is in line with the ambitions of the EU; to achieve, in a medium-term perspective, a balance or surplus in the state budget. However, the Swedish Government's objective is somewhat more ambitious. In the fiscal area, too, we are covered by the agreements made within the Community, even though we are holding off on participation in EMU. Sweden is committed to pursuing this objective as part of the Stability and Growth Pact, but our exclusion means that we cannot be fined if we do not achieve the objective. More generally, we in Sweden, through membership of the EU, have also committed ourselves to seeing our economic policy as an issue of interest to all EU countries. We will thus participate in discussions on economic policy and be subject to assessments and evaluations. We are involved in the formulation of the broad economic policy guidelines. These guidelines can be described as the Community's financial plan and are intended to inform the formulation of economic policies in the EU countries. What does this mean for the crown development? Let me mention something about the role of the crown in exclusion. The Swedish monetary policy strategy in exclusion means that the krona is variable and that policy is focused on price stability. The Riksbank has no explicit target for the exchange rate and given the Swedish attitude towards the ERM, the rate will remain variable until we have decided to participate in the currency union. This is consistent with what has been agreed within the EU, as participation in the ERM should be voluntary. However, the Treaty states that we should regard our monetary policy as a matter of common interest even if we have a variable rate. With this strategy, exchange rate developments will be included as an important indicator guiding policy. If the exchange rate weakens for too long, it could lead to higher inflationary pressures in the long run. In such a situation, the Riksbank will react to defend its price stability objective. If the riksbank's reaction pattern is clear, i.e. always putting the price stability objective first, the adjustment will probably take place more quickly. The deviations can thus be short-lived. Overall, the conditions for stable exchange rate developments between the krona and the single currency should be good. There are many indications that the ECB will define a price stability objective similar to the Swedish one. Similar developments in inflation rates, together with confidence in economic policy in general, provide stability in nominal and real exchange rates between the euro and the krona. It may be worth noting that the Swedish krona has been reasonably stable against the Deutschmark, even though we have not participated in the exchange rate cooperation ERM. Results of the policy pursued If you weigh up the factors I have mentioned  changing objectives and institutional arrangements and economic cooperation within Europe  you can see that a consensus has emerged. There is a consensus among politicians and central bank governors that the previous devaluation policy created problems and cost more than it tasted. The repeated devaluations resulted only in changes in nominal quantities and produced no real effects in the long run. Inflation rose and eroded the effects achieved in the short term. The adjustments back to more sustainable inflation were painful. In Sweden, we can state that developments are moving in the right direction in terms of the results of economic policy. After the monetary policy shift, Sweden has experienced price increases in line with the EU in general or lower. Inflation as measured by the CPI has increased by an average of 2.3% per annum since the inflation target was announced in January 1993. Since the target came into force in January 1995, the CPI has increased by an average of 1.5%. As far as fiscal policy is concerned, the budget deficit has been significantly reduced from a peak of just over 12% of GDP to the current deficit of just 0.8%. This is less than the EU average. Five years after the price stability objective was set, we note that confidence in monetary policy has returned from the low levels prevailing after the abandonment of the fixed exchange rate for the krona. The monetary policy strategy has proven to work and the Riksbank's framework for its actions seems to have been perceived by the actors in the Swedish economy. Inflation has moderated and inflation expectations indicate that the Riksbank's inflation target is expected to be achieved also in the future. Confidence in the future Finland will participate in EMU. Sweden is initially outside the monetary union with a variable exchange rate and price stability objective. From having previously had a similar approach to monetary policy, countries are now choosing different paths, but are striving to achieve the same objective  price stability. We have come a long way in terms of Swedish economic policy and the conditions are good for stable economic development. I am confident about Sweden's opportunities to conduct a well-balanced policy in the future, both in terms of the design of the policy and the institutional framework. Nr man lyssnar p debatten om den ekonomiska utvecklingen i Sverige och Finland kan man konstatera att relationerna lnderna emellan beskrivs med liknelser hmtade svl frn familjelivets som sportens vrld. Ska store- eller lillebror bestmma? Vem ska vinna landskampen i ekonomisk utveckling d lnderna gr t skilda hll? Vem r frresten store- respektive lillebror? Av olika skl har Finland valt att delta i valutaunionen frn start medan Sverige valt att st utanfr nr EMU bildas. Vi befinner oss dock fortfarande p samma ekonomiska spelplan med samma regler och samma domare. I mitt anfrande tnkte jag ge min bild av vad detta kan innebra fr svensk ekonomi. Jag tnker inleda med att kort visa p de liknande erfarenheter Finland och Sverige haft under 80- och 90-talen. Drefter tnkte jag ta upp de frberedelser och de ramar som skapats fr den ekonomiska politiken inom Sverige och som kommer att glla fr vrt agerande i ett utanfrskap. Liknande erfarenheter Utvecklingen i den svenska ekonomin under 80-och 90-talen pminner i hg grad om den finlndska utvecklingen. I likhet med Finland genomlevde den svenska ekonomin verhettning under slutet av ttiotalet som frmst berodde p en alltfr stark inhemsk efterfrgan till fljd av en snabb kreditexpansion. verhettningen vndes i ett kraftigt bakslag under 90-talets brjan. Mellan 1991 och 1993 fll BNP markant, arbetslsheten steg, de statliga finanserna frsmrades betydligt och banksystemet genomlevde en kris. Pressen mot valutan blev stark och den fasta vxelkursen vergavs under hsten 1992. Sveriges riksbank befann sig i samma svra situation som Finlands bank gjorde efter valutakrisen. Beslut om en ny penningpolitisk strategi skulle fattas i en milj dr frtroendet fr penning- och valutapolitiken var lgt. Tidigare agerande i den ekonomiska politiken  med stor iver att ta till devalveringsvapnet vid de kostnadskriser som uppsttt  var tillsammans med frlusten i kampen om den fasta kursen ngra orsaker till det svaga frtroendet. Alternativa strategier undersktes och Riksbanken sneglade p lsningar i andra lnder. Precis som i Finlands fall var vi i Sverige inte bekanta med en milj med rrlig vxelkurs. Den allmnna uppfattningen, bde bland politiker och ekonomer, hade varit att en fast vxelkurs r den enda lsningen fr en liten, ppen ekonomi med stort utlandsberoende. Denna uppfattning har senare kommit att frndras. De bda centralbankerna valde i stort samma vg. Penningpolitiken inriktades p direkta inflationsml och den kvantifierade mlsttningen publicerades i brjan av 1993. Den svenska mlformuleringen var emellertid ngot mer utfrlig, d vi slog fast att inflationen, mtt som KPI, begrnsas till 2 procent, med en tillten avvikelse p +/- 1 procentenhet. Finland valde att formulera sitt inflationsml som en varaktigt stabil underliggande inflationstakt p 2 procent. Precis som i Finland var det svenska prisstabilitetsmlet inledningsvis ett sjlvptaget tagande frn centralbankens sida, men fick efterhand uttalat std frn riksdag och regering. Mlsttningen om en inflationstakt p 2 procent gllde frn 1995 och framt. Under vergngsperioden skulle inflation och frvntningar dmpas frn de hga niver som rtt under 80-talet. Frtroendet skulle allts terskapas. Fr att stadkomma frstelse fr vr politik och skapa en bred kunskap om beslutsgrunderna fr politiken valde Riksbanken att lpande publicera inflationsrapporter. Inflationsrapporter publiceras nu fyra gnger per r och beskriver tydligt och detaljerat den faktiska inflationsutvecklingen, redogr fr bankens bedmning av den framtida inflationen samt drar slutsatser fr penningpolitikens inriktning. Skilda vgar I oktober 1996 ndrades Finlands val av strategi. Med bibehllet prisstabilitetsml sattes ven ett ml upp fr vxelkursen inom vxelkurssamarbetet ERM. Att terigen knyta marken till en fast kurs skulle ses som ett frberedande steg fr Finlands deltagande i valutaunionen frn och med januari 1999. Sverige har  sin sida valt en avvaktande attityd till valutaunionen och avser inte att delta frn starten. Riksdagen konstaterade att Sveriges ekonomi terhmtat sig och att konvergenskraven sannolikt kommer att uppns, men att det folkliga stdet r fr svagt fr ett deltagande frn 1999. Ett senare deltagande utesluts inte om situationen frndras. Frn Riksbankens sida har vi ambitionen att genomfra de frberedelser som krvs s att vi kan delta i valutaunionen med ett rs varsel. Tekniska frberedelser pgr redan inom mnga omrden, dels fr att kunna uppfylla de krav som stlls fr att delta framver, dels fr de krav som helt enkelt stlls p grund av att en ny valuta infrs i Europa och mste uppfyllas oberoende av om Sverige vljer att st utanfr. Sverige mste ocks frbereda sig ekonomisk-politiskt. Vad innebr utanfrskapet fr den svenska ekonomiska politiken? Vilka krav stlls? Debatten i Finland speglar ofta oro fr att Sverige, genom att stanna utanfr valutaunionen, ska lta kronan deprecieras och drmed skapa konkurrensfrdelar gentemot den finlndska industrin. Mycket frvnar mig i dessa uttalanden, srskilt den indignation man ibland anar. Jag frvnas kanske mest av det faktum att de ofta speglar en frlegad ekonomisk-politisk milj och inte tar hnsyn till de ramar fr politiken som idag finns svl i Finland som i Sverige p det penningpolitiska omrdet. Kraven p den ekonomiska politiken i ett enskilt land beror inte p deltagande i valutaunionen, utan r ett resultat av den vrld vi lever i idag. Det finns helt enkelt mindre utrymme att fra en nationell politik som kraftigt avviker frn den som frs i vr omvrld. Lt mig fortstta med en diskussion om vilka ramarna r fr den svenska politiken och vilka prioriteringar som styrt oss fram till dessa. Implikationer fr den ekonomiska politiken framver Sverige kommer sledes att st utanfr valutaunionen inledningsvis, vilket innebr att penningpolitiska beslut ven fortsttningsvis fattas av Riksbanken. Den svenska penningpolitiken kommer fortsatt att utformas utifrn utvecklingen i den svenska ekonomin Precis som idag kommer den svenska politiken att utformas svl utifrn de ramar som satts upp inom Sverige fr den ekonomiska politiken utifrn vra inhemska prioriteringarna som de ramar som ges av vrt medlemskap i EU. Prioriteringarna inom Sverige respektive EU r i stor utstrckning desamma. De r att fra en ekonomisk politik inriktad p stabilitet och lg inflation. Kraven som stlls p vl avvgd ekonomisk politik r oberoende av deltagande i valutaunionen. Villkor fr penningpolitiken Riksdagens uttalande om ERM i samband med beslutet om EMU innebr att den svenska penningpolitiken kommer att drivas p samma stt som idag ven framver. Riksdagen konstaterade att medlemskap i ERM ska ses som ett frberedande steg fre ett intrde i valutaunionen och att mycket drfr talar fr att deltagande i ERM blir aktuellt frst i samband med beslut om deltagande i EMU. Penningpolitiken kommer drmed fortsatt att inriktas p rrlig vxelkurs med ett uttalat prisstabilitetsml. Frn och med den 1 januari 1999 kommer mlet om stabila priser att lagfstas. Riksbanken blir mer sjlvstndig och fr drmed mjlighet att se till att det ml som riksdagen har tilldelat den uppns. Dessa frndringar stller sig en majoritet av den svenska riksdagen bakom. Dessa frndringar svarar mot de krav som stlls inom EU p penningpolitiken och centralbankens roll. Oavsett deltagande i valutaunionen har Sverige frbundit sig att ha en sjlvstndig centralbank och dri ligger en lngtgende delegering av beslutandertten ver penningpolitiken utifrn ett operationellt ml. Villkor fr finanspolitiken P motsvarande stt kommer ocks den svenska finanspolitiken fortsttningsvis att omfattas av de ml som satts upp i Sverige, men ocks av de som etablerats inom EU. Under 1997 deklarerade regeringen att man stter upp ett lngsiktigt ml fr de svenska offentliga finanserna. Den svenska riksdagen stllde sig bakom mlsttningen. P medellng sikt ska budgeten visa verskott med 2 procent av BNP i genomsnitt ver en konjunkturcykel. Genom att stadkomma ett verskott kan den offentliga skulden reduceras s att de utmaningar som kan komma att mta den svenska ekonomin framver kan antas utan att skapa statsfinansiella problem. Riksbanken anser att detta r en rimlig mlsttning mot bakgrund av den relativt hga konjunkturknsligheten i de svenska offentliga finanserna. Frutom en kad medvetenhet om vikten av stabila finanser har ocks institutionella frndringar vad gller budgetprocessen frbttrat frutsttningarna fr att det svenska budgetmlet ska uppns. Sverige har nu ftt en budgetprocess som i sig skapar mer disciplin och drmed kan bidra till sundare finanser. Sveriges mlsttning att konsolidera de offentliga finanserna verensstmmer med ambitionerna inom EU; att i ett medelfristigt perspektiv n balans eller verskott i statsbudgeten. Den svenska regeringens mlsttning r emellertid ngot mer ambitis. ven inom det finanspolitiska omrdet omfattas vi av de verenskommelser som gjorts inom gemenskapen trots att vi avvaktar med deltagande i EMU. Sverige har frbundit sig att efterstrva detta ml som en del av stabilitets- och tillvxtpakten, men vrt utanfrskap gr att vi inte kan drabbas av bter om vi inte skulle n mlet. Mer allmnt har vi ocks i Sverige, genom medlemskapet i EU, frbundit oss att se vr ekonomiska politik som en frga av intresse fr alla EU-lnder. Vi kommer drmed att delta i diskussioner om den ekonomiska politiken och bli freml fr bedmningar och utvrderingar. Vi deltar i utformningen av de allmnna riktlinjerna fr den ekonomiska politiken. Dessa riktlinjer kan beskrivas som gemenskapens finansplan och ska genomsyra utformningen av den ekonomiska politiken i EU-lnderna. Vad innebr detta fr kronutvecklingen? Lt mig nmna ngot om kronans roll vid ett utanfrskap. Den svenska penningpolitiska strategin i utanfrskapet innebr att kronan r rrlig och att politiken inriktas p prisstabilitet. Riksbanken har inget explicit ml fr vxelkursen och givet den svenska instllningen till ERM kommer kursen att frbli rrlig till dess att vi beslutat att delta i valutaunionen. Detta r frenligt med vad man kommit verens om inom EU, d deltagande i ERM ska vara frivilligt. Frdraget sger dock att vi ska betrakta vr valutapolitik som en frga av gemensamt intresse ven om vi har en rrlig kurs. Med denna strategi kommer vxelkursens utveckling att ing som en viktig indikatorer som vgleder politiken. Om vxelkursen frsvagas under alltfr lng tid kan det leda till ett hgre inflationstryck p sikt. I ett sdant lge kommer Riksbanken att reagera fr att frsvara prisstabilitetsmlet. Om reaktionsmnstret frn Riksbankens sida r tydligt, d.v.s. att alltid stta prisstabilitetsmlet frmst, kommer anpassningen troligen att ske snabbare. Avvikelserna kan drmed bli kortvariga. Sammantaget br frutsttningarna fr en stabil vxelkursutveckling mellan kronan och den gemensamma valutan vara goda. Mycket talar fr att ECB kommer att definiera ett prisstabilitetsml som liknar det svenska. Liknande utveckling i inflationstakt, tillsammans med frtroende fr den ekonomiska politiken i allmnhet, ger stabilitet i nominella och reala vxelkurser mellan euron och kronan. Det kan vara vrt att notera att den svenska kronan varit ngorlunda stabil gentemot D-marken ven om vi inte deltagit i vxelkurssamarbetet ERM. Resultat av den frda politiken Vger man samman de faktorer som jag nmnt  ndrade mlsttningar och institutionella arrangemang samt ekonomiskt samarbete inom Europa  kan man konstatera att en samsyn vxt fram. Det rder enighet bland politiker och centralbankschefer att den tidigare devalveringspolitiken skapade problem och kostade mer n den smakade. De upprepade devalveringarna resulterade enbart i frndringar i de nominella storheterna och gav inga reala effekter p sikt. Inflationen steg och urholkade de effekter som uppntts p kort sikt. Anpassningarna tillbaka till en mer lngsiktigt hllbar inflation blev smrtsamma. I Sverige kan vi konstatera att utvecklingen gr i rtt riktning vad gller resultaten av den ekonomiska politiken. Efter den penningpolitiska omlggningen har Sverige haft priskningar i takt med EU i vrigt eller lgre. Inflationen mtt som KPI har sedan inflationsmlet annonserades i januari 1993 kat med i genomsnitt 2,3 procent per r. Sedan mlet trdde i kraft i januari 1995 har KPI kat med 1,5 procent i genomsnitt. Vad gller finanspolitiken har budgetunderskottet reducerats avsevrt frn som mest strax ver 12 procent av BNP till dagens underskott p enbart 0,8 procent. Detta r mindre n genomsnittet inom EU. Fem r efter att prisstabilitetsmlet utformades kan vi konstatera att frtroendet fr penningpolitiken har tervnt frn de lga niver som rdde efter att den fasta kursen fr kronan vergavs. Den penningpolitiska strategin har visat sig fungera och Riksbankens tankeram fr sitt agerande verkar ha uppfattats av aktrerna i den svenska ekonomin. Inflationen har dmpats och inflationsfrvntningarna visar p att Riksbankens inflationsml frvntas uppns ven i framtiden. Tillfrsikt infr framtiden Finland kommer att delta i EMU. Sverige str inledningsvis utanfr valutaunionen med rrlig vxelkurs och prisstabilitetsml. Frn att tidigare ha haft liknande strategi fr penningpolitiken vljer nu lnderna olika vgar, men strvar efter att n samma ml  prisstabilitet. Vi har kommit lng vg vad gller den svenska ekonomiska politiken och frutsttningarna r bra fr en stabil ekonomisk utveckling. Jag hyser tillfrsikt om Sveriges mjligheter att fra en vl avvgd politik framver, bde vad avser utformningen av politiken och den institutionella ramen.
