Detta innebr bl.a. att centralkurser skall upprttas gentemot euron och inte som idag gentemot samtliga deltagande valutor. De deltagande valutorna tillts fluktuera med +/- 15% kring centralkurserna. Beslutet om centralkurserna kommer att involvera ECB och eurolndernas finansministrar samt centralbankscheferna och ministrarna i de lnder som deltar i ERM II. Betalningssystemet En annan viktig byggsten i EMU-huset r en skert fungerande infrastruktur fr betalningar och penningpolitiska transaktioner inom euroomrdet. Rnteniverna mste kunna pverkas i alla lnder samtidigt. Detta kommer att kunna ske genom det nya europeiska gemensamma betalningssystemet, TARGET. De nationella banksystemen fr stora betalningar kommer att vara sammanlnkade i detta gemensamma ntverk. Alla deltagare i de nationella systemen - i Sveriges fall RIXsystemet- kommer att ing. TARGET kommer ocks att kunna anvndas fr kommersiella betalningar vilket dock inte innebr att centralbanken fr monopol p betalningar inom EMU. Det str bankerna fritt att anvnda andra vgar, t.ex. korrespondentbanker. Kostnaden fr att anvnda systemet samt snabbheten och skerheten kommer att styra hur mycket banker och fretag kommer att anvnda systemet. TARGET:s policy fr prissttning kommer att grundas p principen full kostnadstckning. Systemet blir tillgngligt fr alla EU-lnders centralbanker oavsett om lnderna r med i unionen eller inte. Det r dock fortfarande oskert om lnder som str utanfr unionen kommer att f delta p samma villkor som de andra. Det kan t.ex. handla om begrnsningar i att lna i euro under dagen i syfte att parera svngningar i betalningsfldena. Motiveringen fr sdana begrnsningar r risken fr att intradagskrediter skulle kunna verg i "over-night"-utlning och drmed pverka den samlade eurolikviditeten och rntelget. Frn svensk sida menar vi dock att denna risk inte r ett faktiskt problem. Denna frga kommer inte avgras slutgiltigt frrn den europeiska centralbanken r p plats. Skerheter Ett gemensamt betalningssystem och en gemensam penningpolitik frutstter att det r mjligt att genomfra penningpolitiska operationer i vrdepapper som emitterats i olika lnder. Dessa vrdepapper mste ocks kunna utnyttjas som skerhet fr ln i centralbanker i andra lnder n dr papperet r emitterat eller deponerat i. Det kommer att finnas tv kategorier av skerheter som fr anvndas vid penningpolitiska operationer, Tier one och Tier two. Tier one listan innehller skerheter som uppfyller fr hela den monetra unionen enhetliga acceptanskrav (eligibility criteria). Tier two listan bestr av skerheter som r av speciell vikt fr de nationella finansmarknaderna och dr kraven faststlls av den nationella centralbanken. Bda typerna av tillgngar kan anvndas som skerheter i penningpolitiska operationer med undantag fr direkta kp, "outright" transaktioner. Fr dessa transaktioner godknds normalt endast Tier one papper. Bde Tier one och two papper kan anvndas som skerheter vid transaktioner ver grnserna inom den monetra unionen. Papper dr emittenten r etablerad utanfr euroomrdet och som inkluderas i en Tier two lista kan dock bli undantagna frn denna mjlighet. Det frekommer en diskussion inom EU om bostadsobligationer ska godknnas som Tier one papper. Sverige driver linjen att s ska vara fallet. Frgan r nnu inte avgjord. "Juridiska systemet" Om jag fortstter min liknelse mellan EMU och en byggnad, skulle man kunna jmfra EMU:s juridiska detaljstruktur med byggnadens VVS-system: ngot som lper genom alla delar i en byggnad och som r ndvndigt fr dess funktionalitet. Man tnker inte s mycket p det tills den dagen det brjar krngla. Valutaunionen skulle inte kunna fungera utan en juridisk struktur, vilket mste vara ett "vattenttt system". I annat fall uppstr kaos fr dem som bor i huset. Det mste finnas en legal ram fr att euron skall kunna anvndas. Detta regleras bl.a. i de tv eurofrordningarna. I den frsta av dessa frordningar sls fast att euron i legal mening skall vara unionens valuta frn frsta dagen och drmed erstta de nationella valutorna redan frn den 1 januari 1999. Vidare ingr att bytet av valutan till euro inte skall vara uppsgningsgrund fr kontrakt, dvs kontraktskontinuitet skall glla. I den andra frordningen regleras frgor om framfrallt vergngsfrgor fr perioden 1999-2002, fr att mjliggra ett snabbt infrande av euron. I detta ingr t.ex. att ingen skall hindras att anvnda euron, men ingen heller skall tvingas att gra det under denna vergngsperiod. Vidare r det tnkt att de lnder som gr med i valutaunionen skall genomfra alla nyemissioner i statspapper i euro. Om ett medlemsland ven vill konvertera sin utestende skuldstock till euro s fr landet sjlv vidta lmpliga tgrder. Alla privata ekonomiska aktrer skall kunna vlja nr de vill g ver till euro under vergngsperioden eller vid dess slut. Det frbereds dessutom juridiska regler om bl.a. skerheter, vrdepapperssystem, betalningssystem och penning- och valutapolitiska operationer. Vad hnder 1/1 1999 inom ECB och centralbankerna? Det frsta som hnder r att vxelkurserna lses och euron blir en sjlvstndig valuta. De nationella valutorna blir frn denna tidpunkt endast nationella uttryck av euron. Den gemensamma penningpolitiken i euro brjar bedrivas genom TARGET. De nationella centralbankerna kommer att fungera som ECB:s "frlngda armar" vid genomfrandet av penningpolitiken. Fr de banker och finansinstitut som idag deltar i centralbankernas penningpolitiska operationer kommer frndringarna inte att bli speciellt stora. Dagslnemarknaden kommer dock att bli betydligt strre och de potentiella motparterna kommer att finnas ver hela Europa. Den fusionsprocess som jag nmnde tidigare skall genomfras. De nationella centralbankerna har frt ver valutareservsmedel till ECB s att den kan bedriva valutapolitiken gentemot tredje land p valutataunionens frsta dag Hur valutainterventionerna skall g till vet vi inte ngot om idag. Antingen kan det ske decentraliserat genom de nationella centralbankerna p ECB:s uppdrag eller centraliserat i Frankfurt. De nationella centralbankerna skall lpande frse ECBS med statistiskt och analytiskt material fr att skerstlla att ECB skall kunna utfra sina uppgifter. ...och centralbanker vars lnder som str utanfr? De nationella centralbankerna kommer att behlla ansvaret fr den nationella penning- och valutapolitiken. Om landet r med i ERM II kommer valutan att vara knuten direkt mot euron och inte som i det nuvarande systemet med ett ntverk av vxelkurser mellan de ingende valutorna. Risken fr spnningar blir frmodligen ngot mindre n i det nuvarande systemet eftersom konvergensen r bttre mellan lnderna nu n tidigare under 90-talet. Lnder som str utanfr valutaunionen och inte deltar i vxelkursmekanismen ERM II fr nd inte bedriva en helt sjlvstndig valutapolitik. Den mste fra en valutapolitik i EU:s gemensamma intresse, eftersom detta r nmnt i Maastrichtfrdraget. Skillnaden mot hur Riksbanken i praktiken arbetar idag kommer formellt inte att bli s stor. RIX-systemet kommer fortsatt att arbeta i kronor, men det kommer ocks att finnas ett parallellt system i euro. Den svenska finansiella sektorn kommer att f mjlighet att genomfra snabba och skra betalningar genom TARGET. Rapporteringskrav fr den finansiella sektorn fr statistikbehov kommer att kvarst, i princip i den omfattning som om Sverige vore medlem frn 1999. Vad fr EMU fr konsekvenser fr den finansiella sektorn och vrdepappersmarknaderna i Europa? Stora strukturfrndringar pgr inom det finansiella systemet i Europa. Dessa beror bl.a. p tekniska innovationer, frndrade statliga regelverk samt globaliseringen. Bildandet av EMU intensifierar och pskyndar denna ombildningsprocess. Valutaunionen kommer sannolikt att leda till att rnteniverna mellan lnderna i Europa kommer att nrma sig varandra. Detta beror p att det kommer rda ekonomisk konvergens mellan lnderna och att det bedrivs en gemensam inflationsbekmpande penningpolitik. Den gemensamma penningpolitiken och det faktum att valutariskerna frsvinner kommer att gra att de terstende rnteskillnaderna mellan olika statspapper frmst kommer att avspegla andra typer av marknadsbedmningar. Det kan ocks tnkas att det kommer att finnas ett kat utrymme fr andra lntagare n staten och bostadsinstituten. Troligtvis kommer ett mer differentierat utbud av vrdepapper. De finansiella produkterna kommer att frndras, vissa kommer att frsvinna t.ex. valuta, termins- och optionsprodukter i de valutor som vergr i euro. I och med att EMU bildas kommer det att skapas en gemensam europeisk penningoch kapitalmarknad som blir bde strre och mer likvid n ngon av de idag existerande nationella marknaderna. Detta kommer sannolikt att innebra en kande konkurrens mellan de institut som r aktiva p penning- och kapitalmarknaderna. Lntagare kommer att ha lttare att f tag p en attraktiv finansiering via bl.a. obligationsmarknaden. Konkurrensen mellan instituten i EMU-lnder kommer bl.a. att ka eftersom de mister frdelen av egna hemlandsvalutor. Instituten fr istllet dela sin nya "hemmavaluta" med ett stort antal europeiska konkurrenter. Det kommer drfr att vara viktigt fr de finansiella instituten att redan p ett tidigt stadium finnas p plats p de gemensamma marknaderna fr att inte riskera att frlora kunder. Detta frhllande kommer ocks glla fr svenska finansiella fretag om Sverige str utanfr. En del av fretagens verksamheter kan d komma att flytta utomlands till dotterbolag och filialer som redan finns i de blivande EMU-lnderna. Hr spelar bl a den kommande utformningen av TARGET-systemet en roll. Det kan komma att uppst vl utvecklade europeiska marknader ver landgrnserna fr olika typer av obligationer t.ex. fretags- bostads- och kommunobligationer. Detta kan delvis frklaras av att placerare nskar sprida sina risker genom att diversifiera sina portfljer till flera lnder. P detta stt kan frlustriskerna begrnsas om asymmetriska chocker uppstr i ngot land. Den svenska marknaden kommer att pverkas ven om Sverige inte r med i EMU frn brjan. EMU kommer att innebra frre restriktioner fr placerare nr det gller grnsverskridande handel och detta kommer att glla ven fr Sverige oavsett medlemskap. Bostadsobligationerna dominerar tillsammans med statsobligationerna den svenska obligationsmarknaden. Inom Europa ligger Sverige runt 4:e plats beloppsmssigt ifrga om utestende bostadsobligationsln. Placeringarna i svenska bostadsobligationer r starkt koncentrerade till Sverige. Utlndska lngivare har dock i kad omfattning riktat sig mot den svenska obligationsmarknaden under det senaste ret. Hur man n vrider och vnder p siffrorna r den svenska finansiella sektorn ganska liten i ett europeiskt perspektiv. Den finansiella sektorns kunder kan komma att efterfrga eurotjnster som t.ex. eurosparkonton och europensionskonton. Det kan ocks komma att bli aktuellt med kunder som nskar lna i euro. De svenska finansinstituten har uttryckt en oro ver att de kan hamna i ett smre konkurrenslge jmfrt med de europeiska banker som kommer att ha sin inlningsbas i euro. Vrdepappersmarknad Brserna i Europa har meddelat att vrdepappershandeln kommer att verg till euro, i de lnder som r med frn brjan. vergngen kommer ocks att ske genom en sk Big Bang , d.v.s. att i princip all handel i ett slag vergr frn nationell valuta till euro, den 1/1 1999. Bedmningen r att aktiemarknaden kommer att bli strre och att det kommer bildas en eller ett ftal dominerande marknader fr de mest omsatta europeiska aktierna. Om Sverige str utanfr r det troligt att handeln i vissa aktier p Stockholms fondbrs kommer att verg till euro i alla fall. Denna frndring r frmodligen ndvndig fr att kunna erbjuda en fortsatt konkurrenskraftig marknadsplats. Utlndska kunder str fr en tredjedel av handeln p Stockholms brsen och svenska placerare handlar p utlndska brser i samma storleksordning. Vrdepappersbranschen bedmer drfr att det kommer finnas en stor efterfrgan i euro i de mest handlade aktierna redan frn starten, ven om Sverige inte gr med frn 1999. Sammanfattning Slutspurten i EMU-arbetet har inletts. Sverige r en kvalificerad kandidat om vi skulle nska g med 1999, vilket i dagslget dock frefaller hgst oskert. Valutaunionen kommer att f stora konsekvenser fr alla EU-lnder oavsett om landet r med i valutaunionen eller inte. Vad kan ett utanfrskap innebra fr Sverige som land? Behovet av inflationsbekmpning och budgetstramhet kvarstr, frihetsgraderna kar inte. Vi frlorar i inflytande genom att inte f vara med och utforma EMU:s operationer i det inledande, formande, skedet. Det finns ocks risk fr inflytandefrlust ven i andra europeiska frhandlingar, eftersom vi inte ingr i "inre kretsen". Konsekvenser fr det finansiella systemet  ena sidan mste svenska banker, brsen, VPC etc. och fretag vara beredda att infra eurotjnster och euroredovisning om marknaden s krver. Dubbelarbetet med kronor/euro ger extra kostnader och konkurrensnackdelar gentemot EMU-banker. Svenska finansiella institut str infr en utmaning fr att inte hamna p efterklken i strukturomvandlingen om denna koncentreras till EMUEuropa. Sklet r att de arbetar p en mindre marknad (Sverige) n andra, som arbetar p den breda euro-marknaden och som kommer att delta i den gemensamma penningpolitiken etc. Svenska banker deltar i TARGET liksom andra, men det kan bli vissa nackdelar beroende p utformningen.  andra sidan kommer svenska banker sannolikt att ha mer valutahandel n om Sverige r med i EMU, samt Svenska finansiella institut och marknader kan genomfra eurofrndringarna i lugnare takt och drmed dra nytta av andras erfarenheter. Detta gller ven Riksbanken och statliga myndigheter, t.ex. Riksglden, Riksskatteverket. Det finns en viss risk att svenska finansiella institut kan komma att marginaliseras och hamna utanfr frndringarnas fokus. Det krvs starka tgrder fr att motverka detta - aktiva strategier frn finansinstitutens sida och en ekonomisk politik som innebr att Sverige r ett attraktivt land fr utlndska investeringar. Hursomhelst mste myndigheterna, det finansiella systemet och Riksbanken hela tiden betrakta EMU som en realitet som pverkar oss ven om vi str utanfr. Riksbankens aktiviteter inom EMU-arbetet kommer drfr inte att avta ven om Riksdagen i hst beslutar att Sverige skall st utanfr. Ett fortsatt EMU-arbete r ytterst en konsekvens av EU-medlemskapet och det kommer drfr fortsatt att vara viktigt att flja EMU-projektets utveckling. Sverige kommer annars att missa mjligheterna att kunna delta i diskussionerna infr besluten som kommer att styra mycket av de europeiska lndernas ekonomiska framtid. Fr Riksbanken r det vsentligt att Sveriges intressen bevakas, ven vid ett utanfrskap. Det r viktigt att vi, s lngt mjligt, r delaktiga i den fredliga revolution som Europas ekonomi r p vg in i. Title: EMU, monetary policy and financial markets
text: EMU, monetary policy and financial markets Date: 1996-10-25 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Location: Bond promotion EMU seminar Let me begin by thanking you for being able to come here and talk about how EMU may affect both monetary policy and the financial markets. Interest in what EMU may mean for Sweden in general and for the financial markets in particular has increased recently. That's not surprising. We are fast approaching the time point when EMU is supposed to start working. In line with this, political determination in Europe has become increasingly clear. This has resulted in more and more people - not least in the financial markets - expecting EMU to start on time and for a large part of the EU's countries to be involved from the start. My impression is that we here in Sweden are lagging behind. An inevitable reason for this is that a decision on whether or not we want to participate in EMU will not be taken until next autumn. But whether we will be involved from the beginning, later or not at all, EMU will affect us in many ways that require analysis and preparation. Today I intend to dwell on three different themes; monetary policy within EMU, how EMU may affect the financial sector (both institutions and markets) and the Riksbank's role if we join EMU. Time is limited. I will therefore more hint at issues for further discussion than deliver final answers that may not even exist today. The high demand for EMU information has meant that the Riksbank's management has given several speeches in recent times on themes similar to today's. Those of you who want an in-depth picture of how we view the consequences for the financial markets and for the Riksbank can read Urban Backstrom's and Stefan Ingve's speeches from 17 October. 1. Monetary policy Once EMU has started, monetary policy will be decided by the Governing Council in Frankfurt. The cornerstone of monetary union is the single monetary policy. For Sweden, it will of course play a big role whether we are involved then or not. If we are involved from the outset, we will be able to influence not only what policy is being pursued, but also how the ECB chooses to work, how the policy is set up, etc. Today, within the framework of the EMI, a number of issues of importance for policy in the future are being discussed. However, how the policy will be conducted is formally determined only by those who join EMU. Already today, there are tendencies for those belonging to the "intended" core to have greater influence over the process. Current affairs Let me briefly mention something about the current monetary policy issues. Several of them also have consequences for market development. 1. Institutional affairs. The Governing Board of the Single Central Bank comprises the governors of the central banks whose home countries are members of EMU and the Executive Board of the ECB. Day-to-day monetary policy is managed by the Executive Board, whose members are appointed by the Heads of State or Government of the EU for 8 years. All national central banks (NCBs) will be part of the ECB system and are required to be independent regardless of whether the country participates in monetary union or not. For Sweden, the Maastricht Treaty means, among other things, that the position of the Governor of the Riksbank must be made clearer. He or she should only be able to be replaced if there are explicit reasons such as gross misconduct, etc., for this. For Sweden, the composition of the Riksbank's council could also be a problem. Active members of parliament in the council are completely opposed to the traditions that exist in Central Europe. 2. Strategy. As the media has shown, there is an ongoing discussion on the strategy to be taken by the ECB to achieve the ultimate objective of price stability. Should there be an explicit inflation target of the type the Riksbank is working on, or should the ECB tackle inflation indirectly, by steering monetary policy towards an intermediate target such as money supply growth? From the Swedish side, we have argued for inflation targets. It seems to us to have worked well. It is educational, because the policy is directly focused on what is the real end goal. It also facilitates an open and constructive evaluation of the work of the Central Bank, which we see as an advantage when building confidence in a new European institution. This issue is not yet settled. In any case, the ECB will opt for a strategy in which price stability is the primary objective. This means that the contradiction between inflation targeting and money governance should not be exaggerated. Experience shows that most central banks in the EU work with many indicators in practice, in a way that does not deviate much from ours. 3. Control system. The instruments of monetary policy will also be harmonised. There is agreement that an entry and lending step should exist for investment and lending in the European System of Central Banks, and that repos and other open market operations should be used in a similar way as with us today. The debate has focused, among other things, on the need for loan facilities with a maturity of more than a week and for reserve requirements. For our part, we have advocated a market-conforming system without, for example, reserve requirements. What has been decided so far is that preparations for reserve requirements will be made. The decision on whether or not to impose minimum reserves is ultimately taken by the ECB. One issue that has led to much debate is which securities should be allowed to provide collateral for loans within the payment system and for the money-policy transactions. Some central banks recommend that only securities denominated in euro and issued by issuers in the euro area should be allowed to be used. We believe that the system would work better if the credit risk in the security is decisive, not the issuer's country of establishment. 4. Implementation of monetary policy. The monetary policy instruments will essentially be handled in a decentralised manner by ncb in the different countries. In Sweden, like some other countries, we have for a couple of years worked with a small circle of counterparts in monetary policy, so-called primary dealers. Most central banks in the EU incl. The Bundesbank has involved a much wider range of counterparties. What will happen to the ECB system is not yet clear, but there are many indications that a larger circle than in Sweden today will be able to act as a counterparty in monetary policy operations. 5. Foreign exchange reserve management. A further issue relating to monetary policy is the composition and size of the single foreign exchange reserves. It is clear that the Union's need for foreign exchange reserves is less than the total reserves of the constituent countries. In all likelihood, the Union will have a variable exchange rate vis-a-vis the other major currency blocs and there will therefore be little need to defend a certain rate by means of intervention. Admittedly, it is likely that the ECB will have intervention obligations at the margins with other EU countries in the context of a future ERM 2. However, as the euro is predicted to be the anchor currency, the interventions will mainly involve the purchase of weaker currencies. Central banks from countries participating in EMU will transfer part of their reserves to the ECB. There are many indications that the ECB will decide that the management of the reserve will be decentralised at least for a transitional period. Foreign exchange reserves will be restructured towards non-European currencies. This could have an impact on foreign exchange markets during the transition phase. However, the studies carried out suggest that the "portfolio effects" of the diversion are limited. "Ins and outs" Before I leave the section on monetary policy, let me also say something about what could happen if Sweden were to end up outside EMU. Some of the issues I have mentioned are not affected that much. This applies, among other things, to institutional issues. For example, Sweden has already committed itself to amending legislation to strengthen the position of governor of the Riksbank. It is different in terms of strategy, governance system, foreign exchange reserve management, etc. In these respects, too, we will be affected, but ultimately we decide for ourselves how we want to design our system. Monetary policy will be able to operate both with inflation targets and with a fixed exchange rate against the euro. If Sweden has not joined the ERM, there will be strong pressure on us to join the ERM's successor and there is a risk that a period of membership of the exchange rate mechanism will prove to be a requirement for EU membership. In any case, we have committed ourselves to conducting exchange rate policy as 'a matter of common interest', which of course limits monetary policy freedom of action. In the debate, it is sometimes even claimed that monetary policy will completely lose its importance even if we are outside EMU. The ECB will decide everything, just like the Bundesbank today, it is claimed. However, that is an exaggeration. Certainly, there is room for manoeuvre outside EMU and certainly disturbances in the economy, such as an upturn in inflation, can be countered by monetary policy measures. Against this, however, is that Sweden, as a member of EMU, will perhaps find it easier to avoid some of the mistakes we have made in the past, and it is perhaps precisely these mistakes that would otherwise have had to be corrected in retrospect with the help of monetary policy. Fiscal policy will also be tied up whether Sweden is outside EMU or is involved. If we are outside, we have to strive to meet the Maastricht conditions and our policy will also be continuously evaluated, among other things, from this point of view. For example, the Commission proposes to make convergence programmes compulsory and to serve as a basis for continuous monitoring of policies. If we are in, the Maastricht conditions will be replaced by the so-called Stability Pact. This has evolved a lot since the German Finance Minister, Mr Waigel, made his proposal almost a year ago. But the basic idea remains  to tie up emu's member countries to continue to have strong public finances even after EMU started and to punish those who mismanage their public affairs. We in Sweden have supported this idea. Not least for small countries, there could be problems if a major player in EMU were to mismanage its business and thus jeopardise the Union's budgetary policy and interest rates. The problem has been finding models that "punish" those who misbehave without taking away a desirable flexibility. This may be necessary to create room for national differences in views on the size, design, etc. of the public sector. It must also be possible to counter, through fiscal policy, disturbances that occur in one part of the Union as a result of major differences in economic cycles or structural changes. The relationship between the countries that join EMU  ins in the EU jargon  and those that are outside  outs  raises many questions. Work is well advanced in terms of both monetary and exchange rate policy and fiscal policy and the Stability Pact. But little by little, the discussion raises new questions: If the "ins" central banks join forces and monetary policy becomes one, shouldn't the "ins" finance ministers also coordinate their actions to a greater extent? If that is the case, will it not soon become an internal and an outer circle within the EU in the field of economic policy? It is difficult to know for sure how strong coordination of fiscal policy between "ins" will result, but "outs" can in any case risk losing influence by not being part of the club. 2. The financial sector The impact of EMU on the financial sector will be significant. Most important are probably the overall consequences of a number of countries coming closer together in economic terms, strengthening the single internal market and facilitating competition and specialisation by the fact that there will be only one currency in EMU. Added to this are the effects of institutional and legal arrangements of the type I have previously discussed in terms of monetary policy, but which are also likely to emerge in other areas (government borrowing, surveillance, etc.). Current trends are extended The overall impact is driven by factors that have relatively little to do with EMU per se. To a large extent, this is a development in the extension of trends we are already seeing. Examples of factors that are likely to affect the future are deregulation, information technology, the new financial theory, the institutionalization of savings, the continued internationalization of entrepreneurship, etc. Of course, it is not possible to give a clear picture of how the development will take shape. Current trends suggest the continued rapid development of the financial markets, with new instruments, industry slippage, concentration of certain specialist functions, clearing in new forms, etc. Competitive pressures in traditional banking are likely to continue to intensify at the same time as long-term demand for financial services increases and customers - whether we are talking about companies or households - are becoming increasingly demanding. It seems likely that the number of "full-service" banks is decreasing while their size is increasing. It is also likely with a continued growth of so-called niche banks or financial companies focused on just a few services or distribution channels. The trend of traditional bank deposits and lending decreases while supply and demand for market-based instruments increases should also continue. However, how great the importance of EMU will prove to be for this development is debatable; rather, it has to do primarily with integration globally and in the EU's internal market. Specialization in the capital market Today's European capital markets are fragmented. Domestic banks and insurance companies dominate in most countries and Sweden is no exception. The basis for this is not only that there are different currencies in Europe, but probably even more the tendency of customers to stick to banks they know in combination with the banks' long-acquired knowledge of credit risks and local markets. (church tower principle). With the exception of the disappearance of the various currencies, the arguments for nationally based activities remain even after EMU has been formed. In combination with language difficulties, etc., suggest that the development of the retail function will be driven by essentially factors other than EMU. In the long term, however, the constituent countries can be expected to grow ever closer together. As uncertainty decreases, then, economies of scale of various kinds (in the development of computer systems, etc.) may become more significant for the development of the industry structure. In specialist functions such as "corporate finance", rapid internationalization is already underway. This is likely to continue and possibly the interesting question here will be, in which centres, the activities will be conducted. Emu may be of greater importance for the growing fund activity. When currency risks disappear, it becomes more natural to buy into foreign funds. Similarly, the regulations for pension foundations, etc. may be subject to change. The result of both changes will be more of financial integration and tougher competition. Perhaps these developments may further reinforce the importance of analytical activities. In this context, specialization is conceivable; Swedish banks have a lot of knowledge about e.g. forest industry, Norwegian about oil, etc. Credit risk is increasing in importance A first question regarding developments in the markets for interest-bearing instruments is how a new risk-free euro rate might be established. Unlike in the US, for example, there is not a single easily identified government bond rate to start from. Thus, the players in the market have to decide which rate should be the risk-free one. In this context, credit assessments of different countries become central. When currency risk disappears, the difference in the valuation of different instruments will be about credit and liquidity risks. But credit risks for government securities may also converge. For this to happen - especially for papers with short maturities - the demands for good public finances speak in the wake of the Stability Pact. But there are also factors that pull in the opposite direction. Current currency risks include embedded assessments of the ability of different countries to manage their national economies as well as their public finances. Some of this will now instead be captured in credit risks. In addition, the possibility of getting out of fiscal problems via a lighter monetary policy disappears. The conclusion seems to be that differences in interest rates on government securities from different countries are entirely possible. Another conclusion is that banks and other financial institutions may want to diversify their portfolios for country risk. Such a development could increase European financial integration. Thus, there are differences between EMU and the UNITED STATES when it comes to government securities. In some other respects, parallels could possibly be more rewarding. For example, a European corporate bond market is likely. Today, these markets are small and not very liquid in most countries. Perhaps they can be given life when it is credit risk rather than currency risk to be traded. In the long run, a stronger link can be seen between trading in fixed income corporate instruments and equities. Perhaps investors may also spread risks, etc., more according to industry considerations than with regard to national borders. In that case, credit assessments and industry know-how could become important means of competition. Another likely effect of a euro market free of foreign exchange risk will be the consolidation of the rapidly growing derivatives markets. Previous national experience suggests that there is only a need for a few different contracts in each currency, where investors can play on the yield curve. Judging by what has happened in the US, it is also not profitable to enter this market once someone has established themselves. Whoever first succeeds in creating liquidity seems to be the winner. Localization effects not obvious Before I leave the question of the effects of EMU on the financial sector, there may also be grounds for briefly touching on possible consequences for the location of financial activities. Historically, it does not appear to be the case that trade is automatically drawn to the cities where central banks, etc. are located. New York, Milan and indeed also Frankfurt are example of this. Against this background, it is not obvious that Frankfurt will gain much from, for example, the lack of transparency. London's expense as a result of the formation of EMU and the location of the ECB in Frankfurt. Most important for where financial activities will be conducted is the environment at large, incl. regulations, access to various specialists, etc. A potential threat to London - and, incidentally, also to Stockholm if Sweden ends up outside EMU - constitutes protectionist measures. An example of this, in our view, is the idea of restricting access to the European payment system Target for countries outside EMU. At the same time, Target in particular shows that it is difficult to make this type of discrimination. There are ways to circumvent the rules. However, such manoeuvres will mean that one cannot take advantage of the increased security of the payment system that Target entails. There is often a risk that those who set up the regulations will ultimately suffer themselves, that the markets will be drawn to places where they can develop reasonably freely and rationally. A good example of this is the emergence of a Euromarket for bonds outside the issuing country during the 1970s. There are many good arguments against the notion that all financial activities will be concentrated in one or a few centers: The monetary policy implementation is likely to take place in the different countries. There is a continued need here for "primary dealers", as counterparties and as donors of information. The majority of investors in a particular country's bonds today are concentrated in that country. Increased diversification is certainly likely in the long run, but it will come in time. Local knowledge can prove particularly valuable for the assessment of less liquid papers with greater credit risk (ranging from mortgage securities to industrial bonds and stocks). The banks will need continued local anchoring for credit assessment and customer relationships. Technological developments can also favour decentralisation. The opportunities to work remotely with "remote access" have increased. Moreover, this is a development facilitated by the fact that the importance of merchant floors is decreasing and being replaced by electronic commerce. The conclusion could be that a network of exchanges and clearing houses is emerging linked to each other electronically. In this context, the Stockholm Stock Exchange has high ambitions, which I assume Bengt Ryden will return to. In summary, there is much to be said for London being able to maintain its dominant position in Europe by virtue of a good environment even if the UK does not join EMU. For a country like Sweden, EMU offers good opportunities. Financial activities can develop if only a good environment is offered. 3. The role of the Riksbank Finally, I will say a few words about the Riksbank's role if Sweden joins EMU. Change of emphasis Monetary policy decisions will be taken in Frankfurt. But monetary policy decisions require a basis and policy must be implemented. When it comes to the data, I see strong arguments for continued operations in Sweden. We have an analytical tradition that there are good reasons to defend, if not for nationalistic reasons, then because it has something to add to the work that is being done in the other EU countries. Inspiration is offered by the division of labor that exists in the United States between different banks within the Federal Reserve system. International coordination of statistics at the Riksbank area is ongoing but production and processing will essentially be national. Parts of the implementation of monetary policy can be decentralized. The national central banks have experience worth taking advantage of. Centralization can also be difficult to manage if the counterparties are many. In general, we think that implementation should take place nationally to the extent that it is rational, but in this area, as in the case of, for example, foreign exchange reserve management, there may be efficiency arguments that speak in the opposite direction. Similar arguments also apply to other areas, such as the payment system. Here, there is a case for distinguishing between the wholesale function via electronic systems such as RIX etc. and retail. In the first area, the main line is that national systems are interconnected. As regards the distribution and other handling (quality control, etc.) of banknotes and coins, the possibility of centralisation is naturally limited. In the long run, however, the development of technology (smartcards, etc.) may become of great importance in this area. Finally, there is the Riksbank's role as overseer of the functioning of the financial system, security, etc. This is a rapidly changing job, but in which the basic needs will certainly be at least as great after the formation of EMU as before. With increased specialization and financial integration come new problems and issues. At the same time, economic development in the euro area should be able to be relatively stable, at least compared with what we in Sweden have experienced over the past decade. This should facilitate monitoring. An important aspect of the Riksbank's role in this area has to do with how we can contribute to a good environment for financial activity and thus increase Sweden's attractiveness. Swedish profile Finally, let me stress that we think we have a profile in European cooperation, a profile that we are not alone in but that we would still like to protect. It has to do with openness and transparency on the part of its own citizens. We want to be comprehensible as far as possible and strive to create an understanding of our work. This characterises our argumentation about the ECB's monetary policy strategy and guides us in discussions about what should and should not be published. It also has to do with a reliance on market-conforming solutions. This applies in the view of how monetary policy should be conducted (control system, etc.) but also in the view we have of how the markets should work, regulations should be set up, etc. We believe that this is the best way to create financial markets that contribute to prosperity and we also believe that it is Europe's chance to become competitive with the rest of the world in the financial field. Finally, we defend free trade as far as possible. Here, too, there are concrete examples. We believe that securities of many kinds should be allowed to provide collateral for monetary policy operations. We are also opposed to the idea of restricting access to the common payment system that is now being built up between the central banks. If Sweden does not join EMU, our opportunities to assert these perspectives on European development will be limited. Styrsystem. ven instrumenten fr penningpolitiken kommer att harmoniseras. Valutareservsfrvaltning. Ytterligare en frga som har med penningpolitiken att gra r sammansttningen av och storleken p den gemensamma valutareserven. De studier som gjorts tyder dock p att "portfljeffekterna" av omlggningen r begrnsade. Det gller bl.a. de institutionella frgorna. Sverige har t.ex. redan frbundit sig att ndra lagstiftningen s att riksbankschefens stllning strks. Det r emellertid en verdrift. Visst finns ett manverutrymme utanfr EMU och visst kan strningar i ekonomin, t.ex en inflationsuppgng, motverkas med penningpolitiska tgrder. Str vi utanfr har vi att strva efter att uppfylla Maastricht-villkoren och vr politik kommer ocks lpande att utvrderas bl.a. frn denna utgngspunkt. Kommissionen freslr t.ex. att konvergensprogrammen skall bli obligatoriska och lggas till grund fr en fortlpande vervakning av politiken. r vi med erstts Maastricht-villkoren med den s.k. stabilitetspakten. Frhllandet mellan de lnder som blir med i EMU  ins i EU-jargongen  och de som r utanfr - outs - vcker mnga frgor. Om s r fallet blir det d inte snart en inre och en yttre cirkel inom EU p det ekonomisk-politiska omrdet? Det r svrt att bestmt veta hur stark samordning av finanspolitiken mellan "ins" som kommer att bli fljden, men "outs" kan hur som helst riskera att frlora i inflytande genom att inte ing i klubben. 2. Den finansiella sektorn EMU:s effekter p den finansiella sektorn kommer att vara betydande. Viktigast r sannolikt de vergripande konsekvenserna av att ett antal lnder i ekonomiskt hnseende kommer nrmare varandra, att den gemensamma inre marknaden strks och att konkurrens och specialisering underlttas av att det inom EMU bara kommer att finnas en valuta. Nuvarande tendenser frlngs De vergripande effekterna drivs av faktorer som har relativt lite med EMU i sig att gra. I hg grad r det frga om en utveckling i frlngningen av tendenser vi redan ser. Det verkar troligt att antalet "full-service" banker minskar samtidigt som deras storlek kar. Troligt r det ocks med en fortsatt tillvxt av s.k. nischbanker eller finansiella fretag inriktade p bara ngra tjnster eller distributionskanaler. Tendensen att traditionell inlning och utlning i bank minskar samtidigt som utbudet och efterfrgan av marknadsbaserade instrument kar torde ocks fortstta. Hur stor just EMU:s betydelse kommer visa sig vara fr denna utveckling kan dock diskuteras; den har snarare frmst med integrationen globalt och p EU:s inre marknad att gra. Specialisering p kapitalmarknaden Dagens europeiska kapitalmarknader r fragmenterade. Inhemska banker och frskringsbolag dominerar i de flesta lnder och Sverige r inget undantag. Grunden fr detta r inte bara att det r olika valutor i Europa utan antagligen n mer kundernas tendens att hlla sig till banker de knner i kombination med bankernas sedan lnge frvrvade kunskaper om kreditrisker och lokala marknader. (kyrktornsprincipen). Med undantag fr att de olika valutorna frsvinner kvarstr argumenten fr nationellt baserade verksamheter ven sedan EMU bildats. I kombination med sprksvrigheter etc. talar det fr att utvecklingen av detaljistfunktionen kommer att styras av i huvudsak andra faktorer n EMU. P sikt kan dock de ingende lnderna frvntas vxa allt nrmare varandra. I takt med att oskerheten minskar kan d skalfrdelar av olika slag (vid utveckling av datorsystem mm.) komma att bli mer betydelsefulla fr branschstrukturens utveckling. Inom specialistfunktioner som "corporate finance" pgr redan en snabb internationalisering. Denna lr fortstta och mjligen blir den intressanta frgan hr var, i vilka centra, verksamheten kommer att bedrivas. Fr den vxande fondverksamheten kan EMU eventuellt f strre betydelse. Nr valutariskerna frsvinner blir det naturligare att kpa in sig i utlndska fonder. P samma stt kan reglementen fr pensionstiftelser etc. komma att ndras. Resultatet av bda frndringarna blir mer av finansiell integration och hrdare konkurrens. Kanske kan utvecklingen komma att ytterligare frstrka analysverksamhetens betydelse. I detta sammanhang r specialisering tnkbar; svenska banker har mycket kunskaper om t.ex. skogsindustri, norska om olja etc. Kreditrisken kar i betydelse En frsta frga nr det gller utvecklingen p marknaderna fr rntebrande instrument r hur en ny riskfri rnta i euro kan tnkas etableras. Till skillnad frn i t.ex. USA finns det inte en enda lttidentifierad statspappersrnta att utg ifrn. Aktrerna p marknaden mste allts bestmma sig fr vilken rnta som ska vara den riskfria. I detta sammanhang blir kreditbedmningar av olika lnder centrala. Nr valutarisken frsvinner kommer skillnaden i vrdering av olika instrument att handla om kredit- och likviditetsrisker. Men ven kreditriskerna fr statspapper kan komma att konvergera. Fr att s ska komma att ske - srskilt fr papper med korta lptider - talar kraven p goda statsfinanser i stabilitetspaktens klvatten. Men det finns ocks faktorer som drar i motsatt riktning. I de nuvarande valutariskerna ligger inbddade bedmningar av olika lnders frmga att hantera svl sina nationella ekonomier som sina statsfinanser. En del av detta kommer nu i stllet att fngas upp i kreditriskerna. Till detta kommer att mjligheten att ta sig ur statsfinansiella problem via en lttare penningpolitik frsvinner. Slutsatsen frefaller vara att skillnader i rnta p statspapper frn olika lnder r fullt mjliga. En annan slutsats r att banker och andra finansiella institutioner kan komma att vilja diversifiera sina portfljer fr lnderrisk. En sdan utveckling skulle kunna komma att ka den europeiska finansiella integrationen. Skillnader finns allts mellan EMU och USA nr det gller statspapper. I en del andra avseenden kan mjligen paralleller vara mer givande. En europeisk marknad fr fretagsobligationer r t.ex. sannolik. Idag r dessa marknader sm och inte srskilt likvida i flertalet lnder. Kanske kan de f liv nr det r kreditrisk snarare n valutarisk som ska handlas. I frlngningen kan man se en starkare koppling mellan handel med rntebrande fretagsinstrument och aktier. Kanske kan ocks investerare komma att sprida risker etc. mer efter branschmssiga vervganden n med hnsyn till nations-grnser. Kreditbedmningar och branschkunnande skulle i s fall kunna bli viktiga konkurrensmedel. En annan trolig effekt av en euromarknad fri frn valutarisk blir en konsolidering av de snabbt vxande derivatmarknaderna. Hittillsvarande nationella erfarenheter tyder p att det bara finns behov fr ngra f olika kontrakt i varje valuta, dr placerare kan spela p avkastningskurvan. Att dma av vad som hnt i USA r det inte heller lnsamt att sl sig in p denna marknad nr ngon vl etablerat sig. Den som frst lyckas skapa likviditet frefaller vara vinnare. Historiskt sett frefaller det inte vara s att handel automatiskt dras till de stder dr centralbanker etc. finns. New York, Milano och faktiskt ocks Frankfurt r exempel p detta.
