Den nya vrlden Det r mnga och viktiga saker som har hnt p finansmarknaderna de senaste femton ren. Vi har p ganska kort tid gtt frn en hrt reglerad och utprglat nationell marknad till en avreglerad marknad med snabbt vxande internationell konkurrens. Detta har dessutom gtt hand i hand med en snabb teknisk utveckling. Under de hr ren har jag sjlv varit med om att se de frsta terminsaffrerna i statsobligationer genomfras, sett optionsmarknaden introduceras och vxa, sett aktiebreven avskaffas och golvhandeln p brsen frsvinna. Vidare har stora delar av det finansiella regelverket ndrats radikalt. Eftersom avregleringarna i Sverige kom relativt sent i ett internationellt perspektiv har det under det gngna decenniet ganska mycket handlat om att komma ikapp. Det har vi ocks gjort, men ingenting varar fr evigt. Dagens diskussion handlar om hur vi ska klara en god utveckling ven i fortsttningen. Idag har vi frihandel p det finansiella omrdet, av i grunden samma slag som vi lnge haft fr tillverkningsindustrin. Frdelarna r ocks i grunden desamma - mer av specialisering, kad effektivitet och i slutndan kat vlstnd. Detsamma gller priset fr detta - stora och snabba frndringar som ibland kan vara smrtsamma eller tminstone frvirrande fr mnga. I det sammanhanget kanske det kan vara vrt att ppeka att den finansiella sektorn r en "nrande" och inte "trande" sektor av samhllsekonomin, ven om jag mycket vl vet att det kan finnas en och annan som tycker annorlunda, i varje fall utanfr den hr lokalen. I varje ekonomi dr man vergett byteshandeln som dominerande form fr ekonomiskt utbyte spelar det finansiella systemet en central roll. Man kan sga att det finansiella systemet har tre huvuduppgifter: att tillhandahlla betalningstjnster, att omvandla sparkapital till investeringar, samt att mjliggra fr hushll och fretag att hantera ekonomisk oskerhet och risk. Det finansiella systemet fungerar som ett smrjmedel fr hela ekonomin. Med ett vl fungerande finansiellt system fr vi lgre kostnader och mindre risker i produktionen av varor och tjnster. Detta frmjar tillvxt och sysselsttning. P motsvarande stt kan en strning i det finansiella systemets funktioner f negativa konsekvenser fr hela samhllsekonomin. Kriser i det finansiella systemet kan medverka till att den samhllsekonomiska utvecklingen kommer in i en ond cirkel av fallande produktion, stigande arbetslshet och deflation. Jag tycker det r viktigt att konstatera och kommunicera detta - det senare har vi vl, om vi ska vara sjlvkritiska, inte alltid varit s bra p inom den finansiella sektorn, och uppgiften blev naturligtvis inte lttare under finanskrisen och dess efterdyningar. Den bristande insikten om finanssektorns roll och betydelse r hur som helst ett problem och vi har sjlva ett ansvar hr. Allt r inte okomplicerat och allt gr inte att frklara p tio sekunder, men det mesta gr trots allt att beskriva p ett begripligt stt om man anstrnger sig lite, och det r viktigt att vi alla gr detta i skilda sammanhang. Min tes r att den mest grundlggande frndringen som hnt p de finansiella marknaderna r att frihandeln nu ntt ven denna del av ekonomin. Hur hanterar vi d en sdan situation? Sverige r ett litet land och en liten ekonomi och vi kan inte vara bst p allt. Hr p samma stt som inom industrin mste vi se vad vi r bra p och utveckla detta. Nsta frga - och dr vi p myndighetssidan kommer in i bilden r om det finns hinder fr en sn utveckling som vi kan avlgsna eller i varje fall minska. Annorlunda uttryckt: Hur ska vi p bsta stt kratta manegen ? Finansiella marknader har historiskt i huvudsak varit nationellt definierade och knutna till storleken p den egna ekonomin. Givet storleken p den svenska ekonomin ligger vi ngonstans i mitten i en EU-rangordning men i de flesta fall lngt under de stora lnderna - brsomsttningen r cirka tta gnger strre i London n i Stockholm, emissionerna av rntebrande vrdepapper r fyra gnger strre i Tyskland n i Sverige, fr att ta tv exempel. Ett undantag frn mnstret r derivatmarknaden, dr vi ligger p en fjrdeplats i EU, vilket visar att produktutveckling kan lna sig. I ett Europa med fria kapitalrrelser och fri etableringsrtt innebr det hr att det alltid kommer att finnas konkurrenter eller potentiella konkurrenter som agerar p en marknad som r strre n vr egen. Med det hr synsttet blir ocks slutsatsen att konkurrensbilden och synen p konkurrensfrgor blir helt olika beroende p om man anlgger ett nationellt eller ett europeiskt perspektiv. Givet de utvecklingstendenser som jag antytt r det enligt min mening ett europeiskt eller i frlngningen ett globalt perspektiv som man br ha nr man diskuterar utvecklingen inom den svenska finansiella sektorn. Det hr synsttet utesluter p intet stt egna svenska lsningar, men man mste vara medveten om att verksamhetsfrutsttningarna i framtiden kommer att vara helt annorlunda n i den slutna och "hemsnickrade" vrld som vi levt i tidigare. 2. Se ver infrastrukturen! En frsta frga man kan stlla r frsts om det spelar ngon roll var den finansiella aktiviteten sker. r det bra om transaktionerna sker i just Sverige, kan de inte lika grna ske utomlands ? I en teknisk mening kan ju numera finansiella transaktioner ske snart sagt var som helst i vrlden. Hur definierar man t ex var en transaktion sker p Internet och spelar det ngon roll ? Finansiella transaktioner handlar inte bara om teknologi. Det handlar ocks om information, kontakter mnniskor emellan och uppbyggnad av kunskap om den finansiella tekonologin. Jag tror det r vrdefullt fr ett land att s a s ha dessa funktioner hemma, ven om de konkreta operationerna i teknisk mening kan utfras ngon annanstans. Jag tror att ett land med en likvid inhemsk riskkapitalmarknad har ett bttre utgngslge nr det gller kapitalfrsrjningen till nringslivet n lnder i avsaknad av en sdan, fr att ta ett exempel. En livskraftig finansmarknad ger dessutom spin-offeffekter p sysselsttning och produktion inom relaterade nringar t ex inom IT- branschen. Sverige ligger lngt framme i den tekniska utvecklingen, och har en utvecklad tradition och en god utbildningsniv inom det finansiella omrdet. Detta ger oss ocks en plattform fr framtiden. Kort sagt: att bibehlla och utveckla kompetens inom det finansiella omrdet r enligt min mening vrdefullt fr landets ekonomiska utveckling. Hur ska vi d ta tillvara den potential vi har ? Fr att en relativt liten marknad som den svenska skall kunna hvda sig mste den framst som attraktiv i jmfrelse med konkurrenterna. Marknaden skall ha en hg likviditet och en vl fungerande infrastruktur. Fr att vrdepappersmarknaden skall kunna fungera mste det finnas en en infrastruktur som p ett enkelt stt gr det mjligt fr kpare och sljare att mtas. Denna infrastruktur omfattar ett antal sammanlnkade delar som p olika stt r beroende av varandra. De metoder, regelverk och den kapitalstock som krvs fr att hantera information, matchning av affrer, ganderttsvergng och registrering och betalning utgr i vid mening vad man kan kalla fr den finansiella infrastrukturen. Med dagens tekniska utveckling bestr denna infrastruktur i stor utstrckning av datasystem av olika slag. Utvecklingen av den finansiella infrastrukturen handlar drfr idag mycket om datasystem, vem som har tilltrde till systemen, hur de kommunicerar med varandra, hur tjnsterna prisstts och vem som ger systemen. Datasystemen kombineras sedan ihop med de juridiska regelverken fr att definiera de finansiella produkterna och transaktionskedjan. Nr man i denna vrld skapar finansiella produkter r fyra faktorer av avgrande betydelse. Kostnaderna fr att utfra finansiella transaktioner fr inte verstiga kostnaderna p konkurrerande marknadsplatser. Det fr inte freligga ngra hinder eller s f hinder som mjligt fr att en aktr skall kunna f tilltrde till marknadsplatsen. Det gller svl olika typer av aktrer som mellan lnder. Valet av transaktionsteknologi i hela transaktionskedjan mste hlla hg internationell klass och bygga p internationell standard. Kunskapen om finansiella produkter, produktutveckling och finansiella regelverk mste hlla hg internationell niv. Den svenska marknaden mste helt enkelt framst som lttillgnglig och effektiv. Om det r tekniskt besvrligt och dyrt att utnyttja den svenska marknaden r det tmligen enkelt fr svl utlndska som svenska aktrer att hitta en alternativ marknad eller fr utlndska placerare att hitta substitut fr svenska placeringar i sina portfljer. Bedmda var fr sig i ett internationellt perspektiv ligger de fyra centrala infrastruktursystemen p den svenska marknaden, Fondbrsen, OM, VPC och RIX, relativt vl framme. Med hnsyn till den internationella utvecklingen r det, enligt min mening, ndvndigt att se ver den tekniska integrationen mellan systemen fr att skra en positiv utveckling av den svenska finansmarknaden. En integration av hela transaktionskedjan - avslut, clearing, avveckling och kontofring - skulle frenkla tillgngen till den svenska marknaden och drmed strka dess konkurrenskraft samt ocks bidra till en vlkommen riskreducering i det finansiella systemet. Hg skerhet bde operationellt och riskmssigt r en konkurrensfaktor i sig. Utvecklingen gr allt mer mot transaktioner i realtid vilket r ngot som pverkar hela transaktionskedjan. Det i sin tur krver ett tekniskt samarbete fr att kunna frverkligas. P det tekniska planet tycker jag ocks att det r angelget att finna former fr att fullflja dematerialiseringen p vrdepapperssidan s att vi inte lngre behver den manuella vrdepappershanteringen (mvps). En lyckosam integration handlar givetvis inte bara om att "koppla ihop" ngra tekniska system. Det handlar ocks om regelsystem, tilltrdesfrgor och tillsynsaspekter dr det grundlggande syftet r att skerstlla en god och transparent riskhantering. Detta r lngifrn okomplicerat, men det r angelget att diskussionen frs - sjlva diskuterar vi den hr typen av frgor bl.a. nr det gller hur vi nrmare ska integrera vrt RIX-system med VPC. Finansdepartementet kom fr ngra mnader sen med en rad frslag inom brsomrdet, bl.a. fresls att det skall vara mjligt med direktaccess p en brs, dvs fyller man vissa krav behver man inte vara vrdepappersinstitut fr att handla p brsen i egen rkning. Det r en frga som har vckt en del starka knslor, men icke desto mindre tycker jag det r bra att vi nu ftt diskussionen p bordet. Med dagens teknologi och den utveckling som pgr frefaller direktacces enligt min mening vara rimligt. Dessutom tror jag det kan bidra till en bttre och tydligare prisbildning fr den hr typen av finansiella tjnster. Om man inte absolut mste handla via mellanhnder skapar man ett system som tydliggr det mervrde som mellanhnderna mste skapa fr att den transaktionskanalen skall vljas. 3. Frmja frihandeln! Inte minst som ett litet land r det viktigt att vi aktivt arbetar fr frihandel. Det r en god svensk handelpolitisk tradition som vi br tillmpa ocks hr. Jag ska nmna tv, delvis sammanhngade omrden, dr vi frn Riksbankens sida varit aktiva. Det ena gller centralbankernas kreditgivning mot skerhet i utlndska vrdepapper och det andra berr det kommande EU-betalningsystemet Target. Frgan om "utlndska skerheter" har diskuterats bde i ett nordiskt sammanhang och i EU-kretsen; i det senare fallet r det ju i ett EMU-perspektiv uppenbart ndvndigt att kunna anvnda papper som finns i en del av unionen, sg Tyskland, fr att f kredit i exempelvis den franska centralbanken. Frnsett de rent tekniska problemen med en sdan hantering, som naturligtvis finns i betydande mtt, r det enligt min uppfattning svrt att se ngra grundlggande principiella problem med sdana arrangemang - med eller utan valutaunion. Likvl har detta ansetts vldigt problematiskt p vissa hll. Nr det gller arrangemangen inom EMU ska exempelvis glla att papperen som ett absolut minimikrav mste vara emitterade inom EES-omrdet. Den frga man d kan stlla r vad som r intressant nr man tar skerhet fr ett ln. Rimligen mste vl detta vara emittentens kreditvrdighet, snarare n i vilket land vederbrande rkar ha sina boplar eller var han valt att genomfra en emission. Men ett sdant synstt mter, har vi mrkt, ofta p ett intensivt motstnd. Nr det gller Target-systemet har EMIs rd beslutat att bankerna i de EU-lnder som str utanfr EMU visserligen skall f delta i systemet, men att man skall frbereda sig p att tillgngen till s.k. intradagskedit i systemet kan komma att begrnsas eller helt utebli. Eftersom intradagskredit frn centralbankerna r "smrjmedlet" fr betalningsfldena i den hr typen av system, kommer detta i s fall att frsvra och frdyra de svenska bankernas utnyttjande av systemet. Det officiella argumentet fr detta r att intrdagskredit till "outs" i vissa lgen skulle kunna frsvra penningpolitiken inom EMU. Fr vr del tycker vi oss ha kunnat visa att detta argument inte r hllbart - sdana penningpolitiska effekter r fr det frsta osannolika, fr det andra r de fullt mjliga att hantera om de trots allt skulle uppst. Men likafullt har man hllit fast vi detta, och verlmnat till det kommande ECB att slutgiltigt besluta. Hur som helst: gr man p restriktionslinjen innebr detta en de-facto protektionism som det finns all anledning att beklaga. Om vr analys av de penningpolitiska aspekterna nr det gller intradagskrediter hller, finns egentligen ur denna aspekt inga principiella skl att begrnsa utlndskt deltagande i ett nationellt betalningssystem. Som jag nmnde tidigare ser jag heller inga principiella problem med att anvnda vrdepapper frn olika lnder och i olika valutor som skerhet fr sdana krediter. Lgger vi samman detta r det svrt att se ngra principiella hinder fr att lnka samman betalningsystemen vrlden ver och dr betalningar i vilken valuta som helst i princip ocks skulle kunna avvecklas var som helst. Lt mig redan hr sga att detta frvisso kan tyckas vara en vl lngtgende slutsats utifrn en skissartad analys, men det r nd frgor som br resas och analyseras framver. Fick vi ngot sdant till stnd skulle det naturligtvis innebra en frbttring av skerhet och effektivitet fr det globala finansiella systemet. Sjlvklart skulle det ocks innefatta stora tekniska och juridiska svrigheter att genomfra ngot sdant att bygga Target inom EU-kretsen har ju varit nog s komplicerat. Med andra ord r detta definitivt inget som grs p en kafferast, men jag tycker nd det r vrt att hlla fram som en vision, en frsta frutsttning fr att brja vandra i den riktningen r att man vet vart man vill, och det kan krva att man gr sig av med en del tidigare barlast. 4. Effekter av EMU Den avreglerings- och internationaliseringsprocess vi varit uppe i det senaste decenniet r ett globalt fenomen snarare n ett europeiskt. nd r det uppenbart att integrationen inom EU i allmnhet och EMU i synnerhet lagt ytterligare kol p brasan. Tendenserna pekar mot en fortsatt snabb utveckling av de finansiella marknaderna, med nya instrument, branschglidning och koncentration av vissa specialistfunktioner. Konkurrenstrycket inom den traditionella bankverksamheten lr fortstta att skrpas samtidigt som den lngsiktiga efterfrgan p finansiella tjnster kar och kunderna vare sig vi talar om fretag, kommuner eller hushll - blir alltmer krvande. Antalet "full-service" banker har redan minskat samtidigt som deras storlek kar. Troligt r ocks en fortsatt tillvxt av s k nischbanker eller finansiella fretag inriktade p bara ngra tjnster eller distributionskanaler. Tendensen att traditionell inlning och utlning i bank minskar, samtidigt som utbudet och efterfrgan p marknadsbaserade instrument kar frvntas fortstta. Vissa andra sannolika utvecklingsdrag r dock mer direkt kopplade till EMU. Strre marknader och nya instrument Fr det frsta handlar det om bildandet av ett strre och enhetligare marknadsomrde. Idag har vi i Sverige ca 9 miljoner potentiella placerare. Inom EU finns totalt drygt 370 miljoner. Drutver kan man rkna med att investerare frn andra lnder i Europa och frn resten av vrlden sker sig till denna nya stora marknad. En strre marknad leder normalt, genom stigande konkurrens, till lgre kostnader och kad likviditet. I och med valutaunionen fr allts lntagare en strre marknad att verka p. Placerarna kommer ocks att bli flera och d valutarisken frsvinner blir det billigare fr dessa att diversifiera sina portfljer. Kort sagt fr vi i ett slag en mycket strre och mycket mer likvid europeisk kapitalmarknad, som bde till storlek och karaktr efterhand alltmer kan komma att likna den amerikanska. Fr det andra finns anledning att anta att vissa produkter p de finansiella marknaderna kommer att frsvinna medan nya kommer till. Exempel p produkter som kan komma att frsvinna r t.ex. intra-europeiska valutaterminer och intraeuropeiska "currency swaps". Samtidigt kan nya produkter skapas t.ex. eurooptioner, euro-terminer, aktieindex fr euroomrdet etc. I detalj kan vi givetvis inte veta vad som kommer att hnda hr. Sprksvrigheter, kulturskillnader och skillnader i marknadsstruktur och marknadskonventioner gr dock att argumenten fr nationellt baserade verksamheter kommer att kvarst ven ganska lngt efter att EMU bildats. Detta gller i synnerhet den finansiella "detaljhandeln" visavi hushllen. I det lnga perspektivet kommer dock de ingende lnderna och marknaderna att vxa allt nrmare varandra ven hr. Ser vi till den institutionella strukturen r det tydligt att EMU-effekterna redan brjat verka - vi ser brssammanslagningar lite varstans i Europa, hr hemma frndras bankstrukturen. Delvis r detta att se som en positionering infr det som komma skall, och det har ju ocks i flertalet fall bekrftats av de involverade fretagen. Kreditrisken kar i betydelse Valutaunionen kommer generellt sett - genom att en inflationbekmpande penningpolitik r det gemensamma fundamentet - att leda till att rnteniverna i hgrntelnderna och lgrntelnderna konvergerar. Fr detta talar ven att valutariskpremien helt frsvinner eftersom det i EMU endast finns en valuta. Det som kommer att finnas kvar, ven efter vergngsprocessen r helt genomfrd, r framfr allt likviditets- och kreditrisker. I och med att valutarisken frsvinner och placeringsbesluten mera kommer att handla om kreditrisker talar mycket fr att det kan komma att bildas vl utvecklade europeiska marknader ver landgrnserna fr olika typer av obligationer som exempelvis fretags-, bostads- och kommunobligationer. Till detta bidrar sannolikt ett intresse frn placerarnas sida att sprida sina risker genom att diversifiera sina portfljer till flera lnder fr att begrnsa frlustriskerna i hndelse av asymmetriska chocker i ngot land. Konsekvenser fr den svenska vrdepappersmarknaden Vad blir d det troliga konsekvenserna fr den svenska marknaden, i synnerhet i beaktade av att Sverige tminstone inledningsvis kommer att st utanfr EMU? Detta kan vi givetvis inte veta med ngon skerhet. Troligt r vl dock att svenska investerare i rtt hg grad kommer att vnda sig mot den likvida euromarknaden. Allt annat lika skulle det innebra att placeringarna i Sverige d skulle minska. Samma effekt kan uppst ven frn utlndska investerares sida - hr finns en risk att svenska fretag inte kommer att f del av en sannolik "diversifieringsvg" mot sdana tillgngar dr valutarisken tidigare utgjort en restriktion. Om Sverige senare gr in finns en risk att portfljanpassningen i huvudsak redan genomfrts - och dessutom p ett "ensidigt" stt. Utmaningen fr oss i Sverige kommer mot den bakgrunden att vara att fra en ekonomisk politik som behller och strker frtroendet fr svensk ekonomi och som gr att placeringar i svenska tillgngar inte framstr som riskabla utan som attraktiva. I s fall kan vi nd f del av denna process, trots en "ute-position". Detta bekrftar n en gng att ett utanfrskap inte ger utrymme fr inflationistisk politik. Rntemarknaden Den svenska penning- och obligationsmarknaden r redan starkt internationaliserad. Om man ser p hur Riksbankens s.k. Primary dealers och i vilken grad dessa bedriver handel med utlndska motparter, kan man konstatera att detta kat snabbt under de senaste ren. De utlndska motparternas andel kade frn 5% till 25% mellan 1992 och brjan p 1997. Samtidigt som internationaliseringsgraden r hg och vxande r det uppenbart att svenska fretag fortfarande har en betydande konkurrensfrdel p den svenska marknaden. Man har upparbetade kanaler mellan ett brett spektrum av aktrer och grundlig kunskap om marknaden och om den svenska ekonomin. Detta frsteg skulle naturligtvis gradvis frsvinna vid ett intrde i EMU. Idag bedrivs den mest likvida delen av den europeiska rntehandeln i tjugotalet future-kontrakt, och huvudsakligen i London. P den amerikanska marknaden r det tre kontrakt som br upp motsvarande marknad. P sikt r det rimligt att vi kommer att nrma oss den amerikanska situationen. Hr r det ocks troligt att vi fr se en koncentration av de institutioner som dominerar marknaden. Hr har svenska institutioner en generell nackdel storleksmssigt.  andra sidan kommer mjligheten att gra goda lokala/nationella kreditbedmningar och vrderingar att f stor betydelse i ljuset av de sannolikt framvxande europeiska marknaderna fr fretags, kommunobligationer och liknande. Aktiemarknaden ven den svenska aktiemarknaden r redan i hg grad internationaliserad - idag str utlndska aktrer fr omkring en tredjedel av handeln. Det faktum att Sverige r 1993 var det frsta landet i vrlden som tillt fjrrdeltagande har naturligtvis bidragit till detta. Visserligen drjde det ett tag innan den frste utlndske deltagaren kom med, men idag r tolv av fyrtiofem brsmedlemmar sdana fjrrmedlemmar. De egenskaper en framgngsrik svensk brs mste ha - i eller utanfr EMU - r god transparens, lga transaktionskostnader, kompetenta medlemmar och en allmnt hg professionalism. Enligt min bedmning r Stockholmsbrsen konkurrenskraftig hrvidlag. Fr att vara konkurrenskraftig i ett "out"-scenario kommer det att vara ndvndigt fr brsen att stta priser i flera olika valutor, varav euron kommer att vara en. Tillsammans med VPC arbetar man ocks p lsningar fr att hantera clearing och avveckling i svl kronor som euro, liksom kanske ocks andra valutor. "Flervalutamiljn" kommer givetvis att pverka alla aktrer p marknaden i strre eller mindre grad. Som jag sa tidigare kommer detta att innebra kostnader som vissa av vra konkurrenter slipper, men samtidigt kan det ocks finnas en positiv sida i detta, nmligen att det stter fokus p betydelsen av att skapa rationella infrastukturella lsningar. 5. Slutsatser Sammanfattningvis vill jag sga fljande: Omvandlingen av finansmarknaderna frn en reglerad och sluten milj till en milj prglad av marknadsstyrning och internationell konkurrens har varit av godo inte bara fr finansmarknaden sjlv, utan ocks fr samhllsekonomin i stort. Det innebr sjlvklart inte att den varit problemfri, men strukturomvandlingsprocesser r aldrig problemfria. Fr svensk del r det viktigt att i internationella sammanhang frsvara och flytta fram frihandelns positioner p finansmarknadsomrdet, p samma stt som vi gr nr det gller den tillverkande industin. Sverige r inte och kan sannolikt inte bli en globalt ledande marknadsplats. Men vi behver fr den skull inte lta oss marginaliseras, n mindre sls ut. Det krver att vi tar fasta p och utvecklar det vi r bra p. Till detta hr inte minst att erbjuda en infrastruktur av hgsta klass bde nr det gller effektivitet och stabilitet. Frverkligandet av EMU kommer att ytterligare frstrka flera av de utvecklingsdrag som prglat de finansiella marknaderna under de senaste ren. Nr det gller infrastruktursidan kompliceras tillvaron en del fr oss i Sverige, eftersom vi tminstone inledningsvis kommer att st utanfr EMU. Det innebr att vi i stor utstrckning mste bygga upp dubbla infrastrukturer. Detta kommer att kosta. Dock kan det frhoppningsvis nd vndas till ngot positivt i den meningen att det hjlper till att stta fokus p den finansiella infrastrukturens uppbyggnad. Lt oss hoppas att detta kan frigra en hel del av kreativt tnkande som resulterar i att lsningarna bde blir bttre och kommer till stnd snabbare n vad som annars blivit fallet ! text: Good conditions for growth Date: 1999-06-08 Speaker: Deputy Governor Villy Bergstrom Location: FFO Thank you for giving me the opportunity to come here and talk about the economic situation. First, I would like to mention a few words about how the Riksbank assesses economic development in the coming years. However, I intend to begin by giving a brief description of the guidelines for the Riksbank's work. Next, I intend to touch on some of the factors that we believe are important for a stable economic expansion in the longer term. In this context, I shall also talk a little about the Swedish business climate. The new monetary policy and economic developments in the short term The role of the Riksbank The Riksbank's main task is to safeguard the value of Swedish money. The Riksbank itself has specified the law's requirements for stable monetary value. The annual rate of price increase - expressed as the change in the consumer price index, CPI - shall be 2 percent. Since assessments of the future economic cycle, inflationary pressures and the effects of monetary policy measures can never hit exactly right, there is a tolerance range of /- 1 percentage point. The actual inflation outcome will, of course, still sometimes fall outside the range. The Riksbank's task will then be to explain what factors have been behind this deviation. The steering instrument for monetary policy is the so-called repo rate. Following a decision by the Riksbank's Executive Board on a change in interest rates, the banks' short-term borrowing or lending costs will change accordingly. Other interest rates in the money market follow suit. With some delay, interest rates to households and firms are also affected. As a result, economic conditions for all domestic sectors are changing, which has an effect on general economic activity and Swedish price developments. However, there are a number of other factors that can influence inflation in the short term as well. Examples of such factors are taxes, import prices and wage developments. The exchange rate, capacity utilisation and the public's inflation expectations are important facts behind the Riksbank's inflation forecasts. The exchange rate, on the other hand, is not a target for the Riksbank's monetary policy. The exchange rate is included in the basis for the analyses of the economic situation that the Riksbank is working on, but only if the exchange rate is expected to affect future price developments can it affect monetary policy. Capacity utilisation and unemployment, on the other hand, play an important direct role  in addition to being behind the inflation forecast  in that the Riksbank's target achievement be pursued gradually, over a two-year period. It is the time horizon on which the inflation forecasts are made. If the Riksbank were to inexorably try to keep inflation at two per cent, drastic changes in interest rates would sometimes have to be made with major real economic effects. Inflation rates would stabilise at prices of real economic instability. I think this briefly sums up the monetary policy that Sweden has been pursuing since 1993. At the turn of the year, the Riksbank was formally made independent. The Bank is now governed by a six-member Executive Board. It's really just a formal confirmation of the relationship that prevailed in the 1990s. The new monetary policy in the rearview mirror From being a country with high inflation, forcing several devaluations of the fixed exchange rate of that time, we have managed in a short time to establish a credible low-inflation regime to promote economic stability and high growth. Thus, there are good conditions for achieving a long-term stable labor market situation with low unemployment and high employment. I believe that there are two main factors that have contributed to the fact that the new monetary policy stance has been implemented in a short time in Sweden. The first factor is that the international political establishment has achieved consensus on monetary policy objectives, not only within the EU but also in a number of overseas countries. One example is New Zealand, which introduced price stability as the explicit objective of monetary policy back in 1990, and which was shortly thereafter followed by similar decisions in many other OECD countries. The second factor has to do with our own failures with stabilisation policies. An example can illustrate. Between 1975 and 1994, that is, over two decades, the hourly wages of industrial workers rose by 6.9 percent per year. But the salary was SEK 12 lower per hour in 1994 in that year's prices than it had been in 1975! With almost 7 percent annual nominal salary increase for 20 years, a reduction in salary by SEK 12 / hour was achieved. It was not a brilliant result of union wage policy. Economic development in Sweden in the short term In the inflation report published by the Riksbank last week (3/6), the Riksbank expects economic growth of 2.5 per cent this year and 3.0 per cent next year. Inflation  measured by CPI  is expected to fall below 2 per cent over the next two years, but this is due, among other things, to temporary effects, namely the direct effects of the Riksbank's own policy on raising inflation, which I have just mentioned. The first thing that happens when you lower interest rates is that inflation falls, because the cost of living in one's own homes falls. But underlying inflation, which is cleared of temporary interest rate effects and temporary effects of indirect tax changes and subsidies, is projected to be 1.9 and 2.0 percent over one to two years' time. In the autumn of 1998, the export sector was expected to lose momentum and be replaced by a stronger domestic market. The current picture seems to be a continued expansion for exports, while domestic demand is expected to develop better than many previously dared to believe. A contributing factor to the changed picture may be that the financial situation in Asia, which last autumn once again looked so threatening, now seems to have reached a turning point. The present forecasts therefore reflect a more positive picture of the next two years, with annual growth of between 2.5% and 3%. The risk picture is judged to be symmetrical. Oil prices may rise and the international economy may pick up considerably, as could the Swedish economy. On the other hand, quarter-year risks of a price correction on the US stock market and a general weakening of US demand. The US has palpable imbalances with current account deficits of 4% of GDP and negative savings in private sector -- 6 percent of GDP -- which is only partially offset by public savings. Longer-term economic development In order for low-inflation policy to remain successful and win general support, long-term economic development must be stable and rapid with a return to full employment in Sweden. How, then, is it to be judged that the development in the slightly longer term is to be assessed? What conditions does our country have for long-term economic expansion? Mentality, history and traditions are characteristics that are often overshadowed by variables such as savings, inflation and public debt. That is not to say that the need for economic policy measures has been exaggerated in recent years. The recent change With the measures taken in Sweden after the 1992/1993 financial crisis with a vigorous clean-up of the financial sector, fiscal austerity and the focus on price stability, we have managed to avoid a long and protracted financial crisis similar to that in which the Japanese economy has been mired since the early 1990s. The state's budget points to a surplus in the coming years, the banking sector has emerged from its deepest slump in decades and inflation has reached record lows. Can we then finally exhale? This has not been free of charge. The price has been mass unemployment, which we are finally getting out of. In the early and mid-1990s, the debate was very much about the importance of sound public finances and stability in the financial system. When the worst of the crisis was over, the focus was on the labour market situation and economic growth. It was feared that the Swedish model, of being able to combine growth and employment with income equalisation and social welfare, was no longer viable. Sweden slipped for a quarter of a century far down from the fourth place our country held in the OECD's prosperity league. When, in the latter part of the 1990s, we have seen an annual average growth of 2.5 to 3% and - for the first time in 10 years - a certain improvement in the number of employed and registered unemployed, another issue is at the centre; the Swedish corporate structure and foreign ownership. The Swedish industrial structure has undergone an extensive transformation during the 1980s and 1990s. The importance of traditional Swedish basic industry has decreased in favor of private service production, which today employs almost half of the workforce. This transformation has had a noticeable impact on employment. Friction in the labour market increased, as traditional worker occupations were replaced by jobs in the service sector and in high-tech industry. Knowledge-intensive companies have gained increased dominance, which leads to a greater need for skilled workers. The knowledge sectors are experiencing rapid growth in the Swedish economy. Since the business is no longer physically anchored to Sweden in the same way as steel and the forest, the industry has also become more agile. However, when ownership changes and ends up in foreign hands, this does not necessarily mean that operations move out of the country. National treasures such as Volvo, Astra and Stora have been merged with or acquired by large foreign groups, but this does not in itself have negative consequences for Swedish business and the national economy. In parallel with this, Swedish companies have flagged the relocation of the parent companies' headquarters out of the country. This can be a sign of a bad business climate in this country and it can become a problem if production and investments are also steered away from Sweden. This could have serious consequences for Swedish research, for Swedish influence in international organizations such as the WTO, the EU and the G10, and for the training of future business leaders and so-called spin-offs. Good conditions for entrepreneurship in Sweden Despite the fact that we are currently moving away from the old industrial society, we in Sweden still have the advantage of having these natural resources at our disposal. We are a large country relative to population with a lot of forest between the villages. International competition in the pulp, paper and steel industries has certainly intensified, which requires high productivity development and a degree of innovation. It is far too early to fully figure out our traditional but advanced basic industries. However, the focus has shifted to companies in telecommunications, pharmaceuticals and IT. R&D, design and customization have become the watchwords for continued success and survival in these areas while rationalizations have been necessary for the survival of the traditional basic industry. It has become important for economic analysts to know the latest trends in the shape and colour of mobile phones as well as to have an idea of the evolution of commodity prices. There are several reasons why the new industries have grown so strong in Sweden. We have a well-developed university and college system, which has contributed to a high level of education. The workforce is homogeneous and industrious. Swedish research is prominent. Possibly the non-hierarchical management of Swedish companies and institutions has also been an advantage, and contributed to the rapid growth of the new areas of business. We are also likely to be open to new technologies; together with the Finns, we are known to have the most mobile phones and Internet subscriptions per capita in the world. It is probably also of the utmost importance that we have a long history of invention and entrepreneurship in the country. Key figures show that we are at the top in terms of R&D efforts and IT investments among OECD countries. This points to good conditions for favourable development for these new industries. The current debate on the Swedish business environment Despite this, the recent newspaper headlines have been very much about the Swedish business climate. The mergers and acquisitions of large companies have filled up the front pages and debate articles. In this context, I think it is important to distinguish between two different phenomena. Mergers on the one hand and acquisitions of Swedish companies and the relocation of head offices on the other. The former can have several causes. During the 1970s and 1980s, diversification was the buzzword among business leaders. In downturn phases for the main business, companies could fall back on less cyclical or countercyclical activities. During the 1990s, it has instead been about concentration on the core business. Ironically, the motives in both cases have been increased chances of survival and a focus on shareholder value. Of course, there can also be trends in business management and many of the messages are driven by developments in management skills in the United States. But there are also more fundamental reasons for this reversal. International competition and over-establishment in certain industries have led to an increased need for large-scale production, especially in the most capital-intensive sectors of activity. An example of this is the Swedish car industry. The latest passenger car model from Volvo (S80) is estimated to have cost SEK 30 billion to develop. Shortly after it was presented, the entire passenger car business was sold to Ford for SEK 50 billion. The development cost of new car models requires production volumes and capital inputs that fewer and fewer individual car companies can handle. A large part of the large deals carried out in recent times have not been pure takeovers from abroad, but mutual mergers of various nature. This applies, for example, to Merita-Nordbanken, Pharmacia-Upjohn, Autoliv-Morton and others. These need not have a negative impact on employment or growth in the country. Sweden's assets in the form of foreign companies still far exceed foreign assets in Sweden. The balance between initial and outgoing direct investments, marketed, shows a plus of SEK 620 billion in 1998. If you also include portfolio shares, you end up with 500 billion SEK. We can also see that the current account no longer gives rise to any structural financing need. Since 1995, we have had a current account surplus of between SEK 40 and 50 billion annually, or a total of approximately SEK 200 billion during the period. This savings surplus must be invested abroad. Nevertheless, foreign acquisitions of Swedish companies have increased recently. Allow me to speculate on the reasons: Sweden still has a net debt to the rest of the world. Net debt is a result of historical overconsumption and write-downs of the krona. Going forward, a current account surplus is required if we are to be able to amortize the debt. One hypothesis in this reasoning is that in this situation the krona must be undervalued in relation to its long-term equilibrium exchange rate in order for current account surpluses to occur. This in turn means that Swedish companies, and in particular companies with a large export share, could be perceived as undervalued by foreign investors. It is natural to assume that the adjustment mechanism has been even more delayed regarding foreign direct investment ownership in Sweden, as this often involves a more long-term and sluggish commitment. I will try to summarise the views on this matter: The motives for mergers of Swedish and foreign companies may partly have macroeconomic or political background. But it is likely that increased international competition, over-establishment in certain industries and free movement of capital are the most significant drivers of mergers in recent years. But the actual situation is that Sweden still has net assets in the form of direct investments abroad. The foundations have already been laid, Sweden today has an interest rate level that is on par with other parts of the Western world, a well-established monetary policy that has led to persistently low inflation and a well-functioning financial market. The risk of a financial and socio-economic crisis such as the one we experienced in the early 1990s being repeated should therefore be minimised. Pharmaceuticals, telecommunications and IT are now fast-growing sectors, areas in which Sweden had good conditions early on through prominent research and early business establishments. Perhaps our country is facing a period of successes. Not only the new, fast-growing industrial sectors speak for it. After a quarter of a century, inflation seems to be finally giving way and productivity is growing on a broad front. In addition, some indicators suggest that business investment now has more of an expansion focus than before. It is no longer just a question of rationalising labour.

Title: Has the inflation process changed?
text: Has the inflationary process changed? Date: 1997-05-26 Speaker: Claes Berg Place: Monetary Policy Forum Introduction During the 1970s and 1980s, inflation as measured by the CPI increased by an average of 8 percent per year. Between 1992 and 1996, inflation has increased by about 2.5% per year. Does this also mean that the inflation process has changed more permanently and that the propensity for inflation in the broad sense in the Swedish economy has decreased? My ambition is to contribute to an analysis of these issues. I shall first discuss the relationship between inflation and demand in macroeconomic models. It then analyses whether the inflation process in the Swedish economy changed during the 1990s. I will also say a few words about how deregulation, internationalisation and increased competition may have affected price formation in various areas. In short, the conclusions I will draw are as follows: there is much to suggest that the propensity for inflation has decreased in the broadest sense. Since inflation expectations have decreased quite a bit since the 1980s, the credibility for us to continue to have low inflation has increased. However, it is difficult to measure how much the inflation process has shifted down. The difficulty is due to the fact that there are several different ways to measure the economic situation. It is also clear that price formation in the food sector, import-dependent trade and some service sectors have been positively affected by deregulation and increased competition. Inflationsprocessen Inflation developments are due, for example, to inflation expectations and cyclical changes in output and employment. Inflation is therefore affected by both confidence in the ability of monetary policy to safeguard monetary value and cyclical developments. A simple inflation equation can be written: * *e b*GAP c**u e where *is actual domestic inflation, *e is the expected inflation, GAP is a measure of the cyclical situation (output gap or unemployment), *u is foreign inflation (or other supply shocks), and e is a random disruption term. b and c are parameters that determine how much changes in the state of the economy or foreign prices and supply shocks pass through in inflation. A lasting change in the inflationary process may be due to a few different factors. On the one hand, the process that generates inflation expectations may have changed. For example, a change in expectation may be a result of the credibility of inflation target increased, all other things being equal. A change in the inflationary process may also be related to a different exchange between demand and supply and inflation. (This means that the parametric values relating demand mode and supply shocks to inflation change.) Neo-Keynesian theory The interpretation of the coefficient over the measure of the cyclical situation is partly influenced by the analysis used to derive the inflation equation. In Neo-Keynesian theory, it is related to how price and wage formation works. The starting point is that wages and/or prices are inertial, i.e. do not change directly when supply or demand conditions change. For example, it is possible to derive the neo-Keynesian inflation equation by assuming that companies face adjustment costs when adjusting prices. Price rigidity can occur if companies strike a balance between setting a price appropriate from a demand point of view and the cost of changing the price. Rigidities in the labour market can also give rise to sluggish prices. For example, companies' prices can be assumed to be given by a surcharge on wage costs. This mark-up depends on productivity developments and foreign prices, while wage developments are influenced by both output gaps and inflation expectations. If the level of production is above the potential level and the prices of companies can be raised, then the pressure to raise wages will also rise. How much wages rise depends on inflation expectations and labour shortages. When the economy turns down, the level of output will be below the potential level. Unemployment then rises above its potential level. Companies' prices need to decrease to contribute to increased sales. Then wages also need to be reduced. However, if wages are sluggish downwards, average wages will decline more slowly than is necessary to restore full employment. This may be due, for example, to the fact that only a certain proportion of wage contracts are renegotiated in each period of time. Lower inflation propensity in this analysis may be associated with, for example, improved wage formation, better matching between those who have become unemployed and new vacancies, and lower levels of unemployment benefits. A shift in the inflation process can also come about through decisions to abandon different types of wage indexation and compliance clauses. Flexible wage formation and information uncertainty It is also possible to analyze changes in the inflation process without an assumption of sluggish prices and wages. Although prices and wages are fully flexible, the inflation process may change as a result of a change in the ability of wage earners to discern what influences wage developments. In an analysis based on rational expectations and flexible price and wage formation, the coefficient over the output gap is related to the ability of wage earners to see why wages and prices are rising. Since wage formation includes elements of information uncertainty, wages and prices in a particular industry can rise for two reasons, with completely different consequences for production and employment. In the first case, the demand for the products of the specific market has increased. Then there are opportunities for increased relative prices and relative wages compared to other industries. An increase in wages and prices leads to increased labour inputs and increased production. This means that a certain positive difference between actual prices and expected prices leads to a relatively large change in the volume of production. This is matched in the inflation equation at the aggregate level by the fact that a certain difference between actual production volume and potential output -- an output gap -- correspond to a minor change in inflation. In the second case, the increase in wages and prices noted in a local market is due to a monetary policy expansion that will primarily raise the general price level in the economy. Then the opportunities for relative price improvements and relative wage improvements are not as good. Therefore, a wage and price increase in this case will lead to a limited increase in labor inputs and production. This means that a large difference between actual prices and expected prices leads to a small change in the volume of production. This is matched in the inflation equation at the aggregate level by the fact that a certain difference between actual output volume and potential output -- an output gap -- produces a larger change in inflation. Processes that reduce inflation propensity In summary, the theoretical analysis leads to the following interpretation of what can contribute to a sustained shift in the inflation process. Long-term inflation expectations may fall and the credibility of the central bank's inflation control may increase. This credibility may increase, inter alia, as a result of institutional changes. In addition, there are two different types of explanations: The inflationary process may change: if wage formation and/or matching between the unemployed and new vacancies improves. if the correlation between relative prices at the industry level and general price variations decreases. Has the inflationary process changed in the 1990s? A clear sign of increased credibility for the inflation target is that household inflation expectations have fallen sharply in the 1990s. During the 1980s, household inflation expectations for the next twelve months averaged 6-7 percent. Since the beginning of 1992, the corresponding average has been just over 2%. Although this period coincides with a cyclical shift from a consumption boom to weak domestic demand, the lower inflation expectations of households from the early 1990s onwards appear to be signs of a change in the inflation process. Of even greater interest is the fact that the longer-term inflation expectations (over a five-year horizon) of investors in the bond market have gradually decreased since 1991. However, they have only fallen below three per cent in 1996. The inflation process may have shifted down in the Swedish economy for several reasons. The credibility of the fight against inflation may have increased. Factors that should have contributed to this are the krona defense in the autumn of 1992, the introduction of the Riksbank's inflation target in January 1993, the cautious interest rate reduction policy in 1993, the interest rate hikes in 1994-1995, swedish EU entry and the consolidation of government finances. It is difficult to coat structural shifts using econometric methods. This is due, among other things, to the fact that the period since the inflation target was declared is rather short. Below are results from two different Riksbank studies. In the first, a simple inflation equation has been estimated for the period from the second quarter of 1972 to the second quarter of 1996. Inflation in the current period is explained by inflation in the previous period, demand in the current period, the change in foreign prices in the previous period and an average of historical changes in foreign consumer prices. In addition, a number of dummy variables are included that intend to capture the VAT changes that occurred during the period. From the third quarter of 1994 onwards, a forecasting characteristic for three different demand measures is evaluated. As a measure of demand, the output gap calculated with whittaker-henderson filters is used, the production function approach as well as the actual unemployment rate. The econometric results are presented in the table. They show that the simple inflation equation tends to overestimate inflation after 1993 if either of the two measures of output gap is included as a measure of the demand situation. However, the forecasting capacity of the inflation equation increases if a so-called regime dummy is introduced from the first quarter of 1993. This is especially true if the output gap measured by the WH filter is used. With such a dummy variable, inflation will shift down from the beginning of 1993 by about 0.6 percent per quarter, i.e. by about 2.4 percent per year. The relationship between output gaps - as specified here - and inflation suggests that the path of inflation has shifted down to a lower level. If unemployment is instead included as a measure of the demand situation, the inflation equation no longer overestimates inflation in the post-1993 period. In the second study, the relationship between growth and unemployment, inflation and the economic situation is analyzed in a broader way in the so-called UC model. The UC model confirms that when unemployment is used to derive the demand situation, a different picture of the inflation process is obtained than if production is used. In the UC model, the so-called equilibrium unemployment rate is allowed to vary over time. With cyclical unemployment (the difference between actual unemployment and equilibrium unemployment) as a demand variable, an estimate without a regime change dummy provides about as good an adjustment to inflation developments as an estimate with this dummy. The results confirm that it is difficult to draw firm conclusions about the magnitude of a structural change in the inflationary process. Estimates of an inflation equation are sensitive to the measure of cyclical situation used. It is therefore too early to draw conclusions about how much the propensity for inflation in the Swedish economy has decreased, in addition to the effects of the weak economic situation. However, it seems clear that the credibility of the inflation target has increased. This is shown both by the fact that inflation expectations for several different groups as well as bond yields have fallen in recent years. Structural change and price formation The structural changes that the Swedish economy has undergone, in the form of deregulation, internationalization and increased competition, may also have contributed to this development through improved price formation. Since the early 1980s, almost all industrialised countries have carried out more or less far-reaching liberalisations of various markets. In addition, public activities have also been privatised and opened up to competition. There is also a pressure for transformation due to the fact that technological development enables new forms of production, distribution and consumption. In particular, developments in communication and information technology have had a major impact on the organisation of production and distribution. Increasing foreign trade and internationalisation, in the form of foreign-owned enterprises and free movement of capital, also have an impact on the structural environment through increased competition. In part, internationalisation is due to technological developments, but it is also due, for example, to the EU process, the GATT and WTO agreements, the upheavals in Eastern Europe and the economic progress of several Asian countries. In Sweden, several areas have been subject to deregulation over the past ten years. Some deregulation can be seen as part of internationalization, but in other cases Sweden has been among the first in the world to deregulate, especially in the field of transport and communication. One of the more significant changes is the deregulation of the Swedish credit and foreign exchange market. Other important events are the tax reform and the new competition law. EU membership has also had positive effects on the competitive situation in Sweden. Changes in the regulatory systems for different markets that have led to improved price formation have taken place in, for example, the food sector, telecommunications and various transport. The food market has been liberalised somewhat, but to a large extent it is still characterised by low competition. Agricultural policy was partially liberalised in the 1990 food policy reform; the role of price support would be reduced and export subsidies would be phased out. EU membership has entailed some re-regulation, but imports of food have increased somewhat with some price pressure as a result. International competition has been further promoted by the WTO agreements signed by EU countries, which reduce export subsidies on agricultural products to non-EU countries. In the grocery trade, competitive pressures have increased as a result of the loosening of the link between wholesale and retail trade in favour of direct deliveries from manufacturers. The number of discount stores has increased. During the 1990s, food prices have fallen. Even adjusted for vat changes, food prices have risen significantly less than the general price level. The charter aviation and taxi market are examples in the field of transport where increased competition has had positive effects on price development. Furthermore, the telecommunications monopoly has been abolished. Competitive products, such as international telephony and mobile telephony, have fallen sharply in price, while prices in more protected markets have risen. Products on markets that have been deregulated for a long time and/or where import competition is high have prices that have risen to a lesser extent than the CPI has. This applies to the prices of clothes and shoes and other imported goods. Given the weakening of the krona since 1992, price pressures have been significant. Competition from foreign producers has probably increased further as a result of EU membership. Areas of the CPI that have risen more than average are primarily administratively set prices. Rents, which are also affected to a very small extent by market forces, have also risen more than the CPI has. Conclusions The analysis of the decline in inflation expectations suggests that the credibility of the inflation target has increased. There are many indications that the inflation process has slowed down. However, it is difficult to draw conclusions about the magnitude of this decrease. This is because actual inflation is influenced by both the cyclical situation and the structural parameters that determine the propensity to inflation. The specification of the demand situation plays a major role in the empirical results concerning these parameters. Price formation in a number of areas has changed towards lower price increases and higher flexibility in consumer prices in the 1990s compared to the 1980s. In many commodity areas, the rate of price increase appears to have slowed down. For administratively priced products, however, an upward trend can be discerned in the rate of price increase. The fiscal situation partly explains this upturn as fiscal consolidation has led to reduced subsidies and an increasing degree of fee financing. In particular, price formation in the food sector, import-dependent trade and some service sectors appear to have been positively affected.

En nedskiftning av inflationsprocessen kan ocks komma till stnd genom beslut att verge olika typer av lneindexering och fljsamhetsklausuler. Flexibel lnebildning och informationsoskerhet Det r ocks mjligt att analysera frndringar i inflationsprocessen utan ett antagande om trgrrliga priser och lner. ven om priser och lner r fullstndigt flexibla kan inflationsprocessen frndras till fljd av en frndring av lntagarnas mjligheter att urskilja vad som pverkar lneutvecklingen. Det r drfr fr tidigt att dra slutsatser om hur mycket inflationsbengenheten i svensk ekonomi minskat, utver effekterna av det svaga konjunkturlget. Det frefaller dock klart att trovrdigheten fr inflationsmlet kat. Detta visas bde av att inflationsfrvntningarna fr flera olika grupper liksom obligationsrntorna fallit under de senaste ren. Strukturomvandlingen och prisbildningen De strukturella frndringar som den svenska ekonomin genomgtt, i form av avregleringar, internationalisering och kad konkurrens, kan ocks ha bidragit till denna utveckling genom en frbttrad prisbildning. Sedan brjan av 1980-talet har s gott som samtliga industrilnder genomfrt mer eller mindre lngtgende avregleringar av olika marknader. Dessutom har ven offentliga verksamheter privatiserats och konkurrensutsatts. Det finns ven ett omvandlingstryck som beror p att den teknologiska utvecklingen mjliggr nya former fr produktion, distribution och konsumtion. Framfr allt har utvecklingen inom kommunikations- och informationsteknologi haft stor inverkan p hur produktion och distribution organiseras. Den kande utrikeshandeln och internationaliseringen, i form av utlandsgda fretag och fria kapitalrrelser, har ocks en inverkan p den strukturella omgivningen genom kad konkurrens. Delvis r internationaliseringen betingad av den tekniska utvecklingen men den beror ocks p exempelvis EU-processen, GATT - och WTO -avtalen, omvlvningarna i steuropa och de ekonomiska framstegen i flera asiatiska lnder. I Sverige har flera omrden varit freml fr avregleringar de senaste tio ren. En del avregleringar kan ses som ett led i internationaliseringen, men i andra fall har Sverige varit bland de frsta i vrlden att avreglera, framfr allt inom transport- och kommunikationsomrdet. En av de mer betydelsefulla frndringarna r avregleringen av den svenska kredit- och valutamarknaden. Andra viktiga hndelser r skattereformen och den nya konkurrenslagen. ven EU-medlemskapet har haft positiva effekter p konkurrenssituationen i Sverige. ndringar i regelsystemen fr olika marknader som medfrt en frbttrad prisbildning har skett i bl.a. livsmedelssektorn, telekommunikation och olika transporter. Marknaden fr livsmedel har avreglerats ngot men till stora delar knnetecknas den fortfarande av lg konkurrens. Jordbrukspolitiken avreglerades delvis i 1990 rs livsmedelspolitiska reform; prisstdets roll skulle minska och exportstdet skulle avvecklas. EU-medlemskapet har medfrt en viss terreglering men importen av livsmedel har kat ngot med viss prispress som fljd. Den internationella konkurrensen har frmjats ytterligare av de WTO-avtal som EU-lnderna undertecknat och som medfr att exportsubventioner p jordbruksprodukter till lnder utanfr EU trappas ned. Inom dagligvaruhandeln har konkurrenstrycket kat till fljd av uppluckringen av kopplingen mellan parti- och detaljhandel till frmn fr direktleveranser frn tillverkare. Antal lgprisbutiker har kat. Under 1990-talet har livsmedelspriserna sjunkit. ven rensat fr momsfrndringarna har livsmedelspriserna stigit betydligt mindre n den allmnna prisnivn. Charterflyg- och taximarknaden r exempel inom transportomrdet dr kad konkurrens har medfrt positiva effekter p prisutvecklingen. Vidare har telemonopolet avskaffats. Konkurrensutsatta produkter, som utlandstelefoni och mobiltelefoni har sjunkit kraftigt i pris, medan priserna p mer skyddade marknader stigit. Produkter p markader som under en lngre tid varit avreglerade och/eller dr importkonkurrensen r hg har priser som stigit i mindre omfattning n vad KPI har gjort. Detta gller priserna p klder och skor och andra importerade varor. Med tanke p kronans frsvagning sedan 1992 har prispressen varit betydande. Konkurrensen frn utlndska producenter har frmodligen kat ytterligare som en fljd av EU-medlemskapet. Omrden i KPI som stigit mer n genomsnittet r i frsta hand administrativt satta priser. Hyrorna, som ocks pverkas i mycket liten utstrckning av marknadskrafterna, har ocks stigit mer n vad KPI har gjort. Slutsatser Analysen av de minskade inflationsfrvntningarna tyder p att trovrdigheten fr inflationsmlet har kat. Mycket talar fr att inflationsprocessen skiftat ned. Det r dock svrt att dra slutsatser om storleken p denna minskning. Det beror p att den faktiska inflationen pverkas svl av konjunkturlge som de strukturella parametrar som avgr inflationsbengenheten. Specifikationen av efterfrgelget spelar en stor roll fr de empiriska resultaten rrande dessa parametrar. Prisbildningen inom ett antal omrden har frndrats mot lgre priskningar och en hgre flexibilitet i konsumentpriserna under 1990-talet jmfrt med 1980-talet. Inom mnga varuomrden frefaller priskningstakten ha vxlats ned. Fr administrativt prissatta produkter kan man dock sknja en upptgende trend i priskningstakten. Den statsfinansiella situationen frklarar delvis denna uppgng d budgetsaneringen medfrt minskade subventioner och kande grad av avgiftsfinansiering. Framfr allt verkar prisbildningen inom livsmedelssektorn, importberoende handel och en del servicesektorer ha pverkats positivt. Title: The assessment of the economy and inflation stands up
text: Heikensten: The assessment of the economy and inflation stands Date 2004-05-17 Riksbank Governor Lars Heikensten spoke about economic development on Monday at a seminar in Tanum arranged by the municipalities in northern Bohuslan. "The performance of the financial markets in recent weeks has been unusually eventful. Since employment in the United States began to rise significantly, there has been a shift in views on US monetary policy. Now interest rate hikes are expected and some expect them to come fairly quickly. This, in turn, has led to quite significant revaluations in other markets as well. In particular, long-term interest rates have risen rapidly in the United States, just over 1 percentage point since the end of March. But there has been an uptick elsewhere as well. In riskier developing countries, there have been increases of between 2 and 3 percentage points, while the increase in, for example, The Netherlands has increased. Japan has not been greater than 0.1 percentage points. The fact that the development has not followed the same trajectory on all sides is a sign of health; long-term interest rates should reasonably reflect differences in risk and future expected inflation. For the euro area, it is also good that the rise in interest rates has been limited, as this should facilitate the recovery. In Sweden, the rise in the 10-year yield has so far stopped at 0.5 percentage points. It's not something that gives us reason to be worried or gives us reasons to change our assessments of future developments," Heikensten said. "Crucial to monetary policy is, of course, as usual, our assessment of inflation going forward. If we look at the economy and price pressures, recent developments have been significantly less dramatic than the development in the financial markets might suggest. Incoming data have essentially confirmed the picture most analysts, including the Riksbank, have had. This means that growth in the United States appears to be strong. The same is also true in, for example, the United States. Asia and Eastern Europe and there the development may even be slightly better than many expected. In the euro area, too, the recovery appears to be proceeding gradually, but the signals are still mixed in the words of the ECB. In light of this picture, we in the Riksbank made some minor changes in our view of international growth at the last monetary policy meeting on 28 April. There is nothing today to suggest that we have reasons to change this picture significantly. The fact that the economy is gaining momentum internationally will of course also have an impact on international price pressures, which are expected to rise gradually and relatively cautiously over the next few years in approximately the way we previously indicated," Heikensten continued. "As growth in the rest of the world has risen, Swedish exports have also increased. It now seems likely that export growth will be somewhat more marked than in the assessment we made in March. In addition, there are positive effects on domestic demand from the repurchase rate reduction that was implemented and from some expansionary measures in the spring budget. All in all, this meant that we already revised up our view of growth for the Swedish economy somewhat in connection with our last meeting. I don't see any reason today to make any further crucial revisions," Heikensten said. "So what are we to believe about Swedish inflation going forward? Here, too, there has been no any major scene change. In March, we expected inflation to rise cautiously in line with the economy and resource utilisation. That's still the picture. However, the slightly higher growth that is now in our assessment suggests that inflation can be expected to rise somewhat faster than we expected in the previous inflation report. In addition, there are a couple of things to consider: One is oil prices, which have risen more than expected. Exactly what is behind the price surge is not obvious. The increasing international growth has probably affected the price, but at the same time one might ask why this would have affected the price so strongly only now. Other factors that have affected the price recently are probably related to the supply of oil, not least an increased concern in the Middle East. There are probably reasons to expect slightly higher oil prices during the forecast period, at least in the short term. How to look at oil prices in the longer term is more uncertain. Still, most indications are that they will fall back from current high-powered levels, which is also what futures markets seem to be counting on. Moreover, when it comes to shaping monetary policy, we must decide to what extent the rise in oil prices should be allowed to influence interest rate decisions. This, in turn, depends both on how durable price changes are expected to be and on how they may affect inflation expectations. Another is the technical change that has taken place in Statistics Sweden's way of calculating inflation according to CPI. It will affect the forecasts of inflation for 2005 and beyond and dampen it by a couple of tenths. When all these factors have been taken into account, it seems likely that the conclusion that the Riksbank drew on inflation at its last meeting at the end of April will stand. We said at the time that inflation is expected to be in line with the target by the end of the forecast period. That's still my assessment," Heikensten concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Heikensten: Bedmningen av konjunkturen och inflationen str sig Datum 2004-05-17 Riksbankschef Lars Heikensten talade om den ekonomiska utvecklingen under mndagen p ett seminarium i Tanum arrangerat av kommunerna i norra Bohusln. "De senaste veckornas utveckling p de finansiella marknaderna har varit ovanligt hndelserika. Sedan sysselsttningen i Frenta Staterna brjat stiga ptagligt har en omsvngning skett i synen p den amerikanska penningpolitiken. Nu vntas rntehjningar och en del rknar med att de kommer ganska snabbt. Det har i sin tur medfrt ganska betydande omvrderingar ocks p andra marknader. Framfrallt har de lnga rntorna stigit snabbt i Frenta Staterna, drygt 1 procentenhet sedan i slutet av mars. Men en uppgng har skett ocks p andra hll. I mer riskfyllda utvecklingslnder har det handlat om uppgngar p mellan 2 och 3 procentenheter medan uppgngen i t.ex. Japan inte har varit strre n 0,1 procentenheter. Att utvecklingen inte fljt samma banor p alla hll r ett hlsotecken; de lnga rntorna br ju rimligen avspegla skillnader i risk och framtida frvntad inflation. Fr euroomrdet r det ocks bra att rnteuppgngen varit begrnsad eftersom det br underltta terhmtningen. I Sverige har uppgngen fr 10-rsrntan hittills stannat vid 0,5 procentenheter. Det r inget som ger oss anledning att vara oroliga eller ger oss skl att ndra vra bedmningar av den framtida utvecklingen, "sa Heikensten. "Avgrande fr penningpolitiken r frsts som vanligt vr bedmning av inflationen framver. Ser vi till konjunkturen och pristrycket har utvecklingen p senare tid varit betydligt mindre dramatisk n vad utvecklingen p de finansiella marknaderna kan ge sken av. Inkommande data har i allt vsentligt bekrftat den bild de flesta bedmare inklusive Riksbanken har haft. Det innebr att tillvxten i Frenta Staterna frefaller bli stark. Detsamma gller ocks i t.ex. Asien och steuropa och dr kan utvecklingen kanske t.o.m. bli ngot bttre n mnga rknat med. ven i euroomrdet frefaller terhmtningen fortstta gradvis, men signalerna r dr med ECB:s ord nnu blandade. Mot bakgrund av den hr bilden gjorde vi i Riksbanken ngra mindre frndringar i synen p den internationella tillvxten vid det senaste penningpolitiska sammantrdet den 28 april. Inget talar idag fr att vi har skl att ndra denna bild ptagligt. Att konjunkturen internationellt tar fart kommer naturligtvis ocks att f effekter p det internationella pristrycket, som vntas stiga gradvis och relativt frsiktigt de nrmaste ren p ungefr det vis vi tidigare indikerat," fortsatte Heikensten. "I takt med att tillvxten i omvrlden har stigit har ocks den svenska exporten kat. Det verkar nu sannolikt att exporttillvxten blir ngot mer markerad n i den bedmning vi gjorde i mars. Till detta kommer positiva effekter p den inhemska efterfrgan av den reporntesnkning som genomfrdes och av en del expansiva tgrder i vrbudgeten. Sammantaget medfrde detta att vi redan i samband med vrt senaste sammantrde reviderade upp vr syn p tillvxten fr den svenska ekonomin ngot. Jag ser idag inte skl att gra ngra ytterligare avgrande revideringar," sa Heikensten. "Vad ska vi d tro om den svenska inflationen framver? Inte heller hr har det skett ngon strre scenfrndring. Vi rknade i mars med en inflation som skulle stiga frsiktigt i takt med konjunktur och resursutnyttjande. Det r fortfarande bilden. Den aningen hgre tillvxt som nu ligger i vr bedmning talar dock fr att inflationen kan vntas stiga ngot snabbare n vi rknade med i frra inflationsrapporten. Till detta kommer ett par saker att ta stllning till: En r oljepriserna, som stigit mer n vntat. Exakt vad som ligger bakom prisuppgngen r inte uppenbart. Den allt starkare internationella tillvxten har troligen pverkat priset, men samtidigt kan man frga sig varfr detta skulle ha pverkat priset s kraftigt frst nu. Andra faktorer som pverkat priset den allra senaste tiden r troligtvis relaterade till utbudet p olja, inte minst en kad oro i Mellersta stern. Antagligen finns det skl att rkna med ngot hgre oljepris under prognosperioden, i varje fall i det korta perspektivet. Hur man ska se p oljepriserna p lngre sikt r mer oskert. Det mesta talar nd fr att de kommer att falla tillbaka frn nuvarande hgt uppdrivna niver, vilket ocks r vad terminsmarknaderna synes rkna med. Nr vi ska utforma penningpolitiken mste vi dessutom bestmma oss fr i vilken utstrckning uppgngen i oljepriserna ska tilltas pverka rntebesluten. Det beror i sin tur bde p hur varaktiga prisfrndringarna vntas bli och p hur de kan tnkas pverka inflationsfrvntningarna. En annan r den tekniska frndring som skett i SCB:s stt att berkna inflationen enligt KPI. Den kommer att pverka prognoserna av inflationen fr 2005 och framt och dmpa den med ett par tiondelar. Nr alla dessa faktorer beaktats frefaller det troligt att den slutsats som Riksbanken drog om inflationen vid frra sammantrdet i slutet av april str sig. Vi sa d att inflationen vntas vara i linje med mlet vid slutet av prognosperioden. Det r fortfarande min bedmning," avslutade Heikensten.
