Title: Socio-economic conditions for wage formation
text: Heikensten: The socio-economic conditions for wage formation Date: 1999-10-26 Speaker: First Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Place: Seminar arranged by the National Institute for Working Life Mr President, I would like to begin by thanking the organisers who have given me this good opportunity to discuss the issue of wage formation. Wage formation is a constantly topical and important issue in the discussion about the development of the Swedish economy. Excessively high nominal wage increases have for several decades contributed to creating problems for the Swedish economy. The issue of wage formation has also gained increased topicality at present, as Sweden is facing a broad economic upturn at the same time as agreements in a large part of the labor market are to be renegotiated. According to the Riksbank's assessment in the latest inflation report, perhaps the biggest threat to continued low inflation is that wage formation will work poorly. The discussion about wage formation also seems to have been given extra impetus, in that the Riksbank assumed in the Inflation Report that nominal wages in 2000 and 2001 will rise by 4-4.5 percent at the same time as inflation rises relatively moderately. In some press comments, this has been interpreted as the Riksbank giving "carte blanche" to salary increases of this magnitude. Against this background, let me comment on something about how the Riksbank views the situation today and in the coming years. My starting point, then, is the Inflation Report. Next, I intend to say something about why, in the report, we did not expect a higher rate of price increase despite the relatively high wage increases. Finally, I will talk about the framework that I believe should apply to wage formation in an inflation targeting regime. Increased resource utilisation and rising price pressures In the inflation report published by the Riksbank at the beginning of this month, we estimated that growth would increase by 3.6, 3.8 and 3.0 per cent respectively during the current year and the two following years. This is a higher growth than we have been used to in recent decades and certainly higher than what the Swedish economy can handle in the long run with unchanged low inflation. With the high growth, the current available resources in the Swedish economy are expected to be gradually utilized. In the Inflation Report, the Riksbank estimates that the capacity gap will close over the next two years and that some capacity shortages will occur at the end of this period. Gradually increasing tensions and the lack of resources in the economy lead to the fact that prices and wages tend to rise. As I mentioned earlier, the Riksbank expects a wage growth rate of 4-4.5 percent per year for the next two years. At the same time, productivity growth is expected to be just over 1.5% per annum, which is slightly weaker than in recent years, largely due to the fact that employment growth is mainly in low-productive sectors. Overall, in the Inflation Report, we expect inflation to rise below the next few years. CPI inflation is expected to rise from 0.9% at present to 2.0% in September 2001. If we weed out interest costs and changes in indirect taxes and subsidies - effects that monetary policy should not normally take into account - then inflation is currently 1.8% and is expected to reach 2.1% by the end of 2001. If we also add the risk picture that the Riksbank painted in the Inflation Report and try to put figures on the various outcomes, it gives underlying inflation in two years of just over 2.2 percent. Why aren't prices rising more right now? In the long term, of course, real wage developments must reflect the ability of the labour force to produce goods and services. In order for real wages to be possible, productivity must rise. Wage increases in addition to productivity developments contribute over time to an increase in inflation. A simple rule for wage space at national level in nominal terms will thus be that wages can increase by the sum of inflation according to the target - i.e. 2 percent - and productivity growth. However, this applies under certain conditions, to which I shall return in a moment. In the shorter term, however, the relationship between nominal wage growth and prices is also influenced by factors other than productivity growth. One reason why the correlation may change is that companies choose, or perhaps are forced to choose, to let an increase in wage costs have an impact on reduced profit margins rather than charging higher prices. Another reason is that developments in other price components are simultaneously acting in the opposite direction, holding back inflation. In the Riksbank's latest inflation assessment, a couple of factors of the latter type are expected to hold back inflation in the coming years: (1) Whereas import prices are expected to increase slowly; This, in turn, depends on several factors. In the Inflation Report, we have expected a slight fall in oil prices. The price development of processed goods is also rising slowly despite an international recovery, partly because the initial situation is estimated to have available resources in the world economy. In addition, there is  and it is probably the most important factor that the krona is assumed to strengthen in the future. The fact that our assumptions about import prices are holding back inflation is clear if we study what happens without this effect. The Riksbank reports an inflation measure, UNDINHX, which is adjusted for the impact of import prices. With the same assumptions, inflation is otherwise expected to be 2.7% in September 2001. Perhaps, just in case, I should add that this measure should normally be above broader measures of inflation such as the CPI, etc., because it has a higher content of services for which prices tend to rise faster than for goods. 2. The inflation picture in the coming years will also be favourably affected by a number of liberalisations, including in the electricity and telecommunications markets, but also within the framework of the EU's agricultural policy. On average, in the years in question, this is a few tenths of a percentage point. How big can the salary increases be? Price developments may thus be more or less favourable for some time than the underlying wage and productivity developments suggest. In the long term, however, it is crucial for inflation that wages develop in line with trend productivity. The stronger the productivity growth, the greater the scope for wage increases and vice versa. Labour productivity may increase as a result of investment and/or as a result of technological progress. Such improvements create room for higher real wages. However, recorded labour productivity can also be influenced by other, more temporary factors, which means that the measured productivity figures do not always show the productive and wage-paying capacity of the economy. During the 80s, productivity in Sweden - measured by the hour - grew by just over 1 percent per year. Now there are some signs that productivity growth has improved and since the early 90s the rate of increase has been just under two percent per year. It is possible that the fact that a number of structural reforms have been implemented and that Sweden has established a stabilization policy regime with low inflation may have contributed to this. However, there are strong reasons to be cautious about allowing the relatively high measured productivity of recent years to form the basis for wage increases in the future. After all, productivity increased strongly precisely in connection with the economic downturn of the early 1990s. This was probably largely due to the fact that it was mainly low-productive companies that were knocked out when demand fell. One possible reason for the high rate of productivity thereafter could be that real capital has been better utilized in existing plants, as the economic situation has gradually improved. If productivity at national level had increased for these latter reasons, it would not allow for a real wage increase, at least not if the ambition is to bring down unemployment quickly. Another way to approach the question of what can be a reasonable rate of productivity growth is to study what has happened in other countries. It is a reasonable approach if one does not believe that production conditions differ significantly between, for example, different European countries. During the 70s and 80s, the rate of productivity in the EU has exceeded that in Sweden, but this has changed during the 90s when the Swedish productivity rate has been higher. Note that this applies to productivity measured per person employed. Obviously, an analysis of this kind does not give a clear picture of long-term productivity developments going forward. However, productivity growth between 1% and 2% seems reasonable. This, in turn, could make it possible to reconcile an inflation target of 2% with nominal wage increases of between 3% and 4% at national level. It is important to note that wage increases relate to both contracts and wage slippage. Another thing is that the salary space naturally varies between different sectors, something I will return to in a moment. This is a rate of wage growth that clearly undercuts the Riksbank's wage forecast in the Inflation Report. The reasoning illustrates that the wage growth figures that the Riksbank states in the Inflation Report are only forecasts and not assessments of what rate is the best for the economy in the long run. Some limitations of the analysis I noted that the expected inflation rate of 2%, together with the projected productivity developments, constitute a natural starting point for assessing the wage space at national level. However, this reasoning has its clear limitations. The economy must be in external and internal balance, which in practice means that there should be full employment and that payments with foreign countries should not pose a problem. Profit levels in the economy must also be compatible with long-term good growth. If this does not apply and if, as is currently the case, there is unemployment, the average wage increases must be lower than implied by the simple rule in order for employment to increase. Countries in the EU that have managed to contain nominal wage increases have also succeeded well in creating new jobs. Developments in Denmark and the Netherlands are good examples of this. Let me also underline that I have so far fully pursued my reasoning from an overall national perspective. This perspective has its clear flaws. Productivity improvements are achieved by individuals out in various companies and production units. Thus, this is where the salary space is created. Against this background, there is a risk of focusing too much on the average rate of wage growth in the economy. Actual wage growth in different sectors of the economy - i.e. what the structure of wages looks like - is central to the impact on employment and inflation. An example: Suppose that a given average overall wage growth rate  which is inherently consistent with the inflation target  is essentially due to wage increases for relatively unskilled and inexperienced labor. It has quite different, and more negative, consequences for overall unemployment than if the same average wage increase is due to wage increases that take into account differences in productivity in different occupational groups. Or let us assume that behind an average wage increase figure, wage increases are hidden mainly in sectors where competition is relatively low. This should have an impact on increased prices to a greater extent than if the corresponding wage increase were more evenly distributed. Let me conclude by saying that it is gratifying that in recent years the social partners seem to be increasingly endorsing inflation targeting policies. In many ways, I find it natural. Low and stable inflation creates good conditions for growth and employment. It is certainly also very much precisely the members of your trade unions who would suffer if inflation were to be allowed to pick up again. In addition, a policy aimed at a clear inflation target over time should be able to provide a stable basis for wage formation and thus facilitate, not least, for the contracting parties. At the same time, I think it is important that we have an ongoing discussion about the current assessment and policy. Today - like most other analysts - we expect inflation to rise in the coming years. Estimates of how much inflation is rising can, of course, vary. However, when underlying inflation is 1.8 per cent, it is clear that an increase in the repo rate should not take very long, given that nothing unforeseen affects the economic picture. By acting in good time, the best conditions are created for stable development with a longer economic upturn.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Heikensten: De samhllsekonomiska frutsttningarna fr lnebildningen Datum: 1999-10-26 Talare: Frste vice riksbankschef Lars Heikensten Plats: Seminarium arrangerat av Arbetslivsinstitutet Jag vill brja med att rikta ett tack till arrangrerna som givit mig det hr goda tillfllet att diskutera lnebildningsfrgan. Lnebildningen r en stndigt aktuell och viktig frga i diskussionen om den svenska ekonomins utveckling. Alltfr hga nominella lnekningar har under flera decennier bidragit till att skapa problem fr den svenska ekonomin. Lnebildningsfrgan har dessutom ftt kad aktualitet i dagslget, d Sverige str infr en bred konjunkturuppgng samtidigt som avtal p en stor del av arbetsmarknaden ska omfrhandlas. Enligt Riksbankens bedmning i den senaste inflationsrapporten r det kanske strsta hotet mot en fortsatt lg inflation att lnebildningen ska fungera dligt. Diskussionen kring lnebildningen frefaller ocks ha ftt extra nring, genom att Riksbanken i inflationsrapporten utgick frn att de nominella lnerna under 2000 och 2001 kommer att stiga med 4-4,5 procent samtidigt som inflationen stiger frhllandevis mttligt. I en del presskommentarer har detta tolkats som att Riksbanken givit "carte blanche" till lnehjningar i denna storleksordning. Lt mig, mot den hr bakgrunden, kommentera ngot om hur Riksbanken ser p situationen idag och de nrmaste ren. Min utgngspunkt r d inflationsrapporten. Drefter avser jag sga ngot om varfr vi i rapporten inte rknade med en hgre priskningstakt trots de relativt hga lnekningarna. Avslutningsvis tnker jag tala om de ramar som jag anser br glla fr lnebildningen i en inflationsmlsregim. kat resursutnyttjande och stigande pristryck I den inflationsrapport som Riksbanken publicerade i brjan av den hr mnaden bedmde vi att tillvxten skulle ka med 3,6, 3,8 respektive 3,0 procent under innevarande r och de tv drp fljande ren. Det r en hgre tillvxt n vad vi varit vana vid under de senaste decennierna och med all skerhet hgre n vad svensk ekonomi i lngden klarar av med ofrndrat lg inflation. Med den hga tillvxten vntas de nuvarande lediga resurserna i den svenska ekonomin gradvis tas i ansprk. I inflationsrapporten berknar Riksbanken att kapacitetsgapet sluts under de kommande tv ren och att viss kapacitetsbrist uppstr i slutet av denna period. Gradvis kande spnningar och bristen p resurser i ekonomin leder till att priser och lner tenderar att stiga. Som jag tidigare nmnde rknar Riksbanken med en lnekningstakt p 4-4,5 procent per r de kommande tv ren. Samtidigt frvntas produktivitetstillvxten uppg till drygt 1,5 procent per r, vilket r ngot svagare n under senare r, till strsta delen p grund av att sysselsttningskningen frmst sker i lgproduktiva sektorer. Sammantaget rknar vi i inflationsrapporten med att inflationen stiger under de nrmaste ren. KPI-inflationen bedms stiga frn 0,9 procent fr nrvarande till 2,0 procent i september 2001. Om vi rensar bort rntekostnader och frndringar i indirekta skatter och subventioner - effekter som penningpolitiken normalt inte ska beakta - s r inflationen fr nrvarande 1,8 procent och frvntas vid slutet av 2001 uppg till 2,1 procent. Lgger vi ven till den riskbild som Riksbanken mlade upp i inflationsrapporten och frsker att stta siffror p de olika utfallen s ger det en underliggande inflation om tv r p drygt 2,2 procent. Varfr stiger inte priserna mer just nu? P lng sikt r det naturligtvis s att reallneutvecklingen mste avspegla arbetskraftens frmga att producera varor och tjnster. Fr att det ska vara mjligt att hja de reala lnerna krvs att produktiviteten stiger. Lnekningar utver produktivitetsutvecklingen bidrar ver tiden till att inflationen kar. En enkel regel fr lneutrymmet p nationell niv i nominella termer blir drmed att lnerna kan ka med summan av inflationen enligt mlet - d.v.s. 2 procent - och produktivitetstillvxten. Det gller dock under vissa frutsttningar som jag strax ska terkomma till. P kortare sikt pverkas emellertid sambandet mellan nominella lnekningar och priserna ven av andra faktorer n produktivitetstillvxten. Ett skl till att sambandet kan frndras r att fretagen vljer, eller kanske tvingas vlja, att lta en lnekostnadskning sl igenom i minskade vinstmarginaler snarare n att ta ut hgre priser. En annat skl r att utvecklingen i andra priskomponenter samtidigt verkar i motsatt riktning och hller tillbaka inflationen. I Riksbankens senaste inflationsbedmning r det framfrallt ett par faktorer av den senare typen som bedms hlla tillbaka inflationen under de kommande ren: 1. Importpriserna bedms ka lngsamt. Detta beror i sin tur p flera faktorer. I inflationsrapporten har vi rknat med ett visst oljeprisfall. Prisutvecklingen p bearbetade varor stiger ocks lngsamt trots en internationell terhmtning bl.a. drfr att det i utgngslget bedms finnas lediga resurser i vrldsekonomin. Till detta kommer  och det r nog den viktigaste faktorn att kronan antas frstrkas framver. Att vra antaganden om importpriserna hller tillbaka inflationen mrks tydligt om vi studerar vad som hnder utan denna effekt. Riksbanken redovisar ett inflationsmtt, UNDINHX, som r rensat fr importprisernas inverkan. Med samma antaganden i vrigt bedms inflationen enligt detta mtt bli 2,7 procent i september 2001. Kanske ska jag fr skerhets skull lgga till att detta mtt normalt sett br ligga ver bredare inflationsmtt som KPI etc. eftersom det har ett hgre innehll av tjnster fr vilka priserna tenderar att stiga snabbare n fr varor. 2. Inflationsbilden de nrmaste ren pverkas ocks gynnsamt av ett antal avregleringar bl.a. p el och telemarknaderna men ocks inom ramen fr EU:s jordbrukspolitik. I genomsnitt under de aktuella ren rr det sig om ngra tiondels procentenheter. Hur stora kan lnekningarna vara? Prisutvecklingen kan sledes under en tid vara mer eller mindre frmnlig n vad den underliggande lne- och produktivitetsutvecklingen talar fr. P lng sikt r det emellertid avgrande fr inflationen att lnerna utvecklas i linje med den trendmssiga produktiviteten. Ju starkare produktivitetstillvxt, desto strre utrymme fr lnekningar och tvrtom. Arbetsproduktiviteten kan ka som ett resultat av investeringar och/eller till fljd av tekniska framsteg. Sdana frbttringar skapar utrymme fr hgre reallner. Men den registrerade arbetsproduktiviteten kan pverkas ven av andra, mer tillflliga faktorer, vilket gr att de uppmtta produktivitetssiffrorna inte alltid visar produktionsoch lnebetalningsfrmgan i ekonomin. Under 80-talet vxte produktiviteten i Sverige - mtt per timme - med strax ver 1 procent per r. Nu finns det en del tecken p att produktivitetsutvecklingen har frbttrats och sedan brjan av 90-talet har kningstakten varit knappt tv procent per r. Det r mjligt att det faktum att det genomfrts ett antal strukturreformer och att Sverige etablerat en stabiliseringspolitisk regim med lg inflation kan ha bidragit till detta. Det finns dock starka skl att vara frsiktig med att lta de senaste rens relativt hga uppmtta produktivitet ligga till grund fr lnekningar framver. Produktiviteten kade trots allt starkt just i samband med konjunkturnedgngen i brjan av 1990talet. Sannolikt berodde det i hg grad p att det frmst var lgproduktiva fretag som slogs ut d efterfrgan fll. En tnkbar orsak till att produktivitetstakten varit hg drefter kan vara att realkapital har utnyttjats bttre i befintliga anlggningar, d konjunkturlget successivt frbttrats. Skulle produktiviteten p nationell niv ha kat av dessa senare skl ger det inte utrymme fr reallnelyft, i varje fall inte om ambitionen r att snabbt f ned arbetslsheten. Ytterligare ett stt att nrma sig frgan om vad som kan vara en rimlig produktivitetskningstakt r att studera vad som hnt i andra lnder. Det r en rimlig ansats om man inte tror att produktionsfrhllandena skiljer sig t ptagligt mellan t.ex. olika europeiska lnder. Produktivitetstakten i EU har under 70- och 80-talen verstigit den i Sverige, men detta har frndrats under 90-talet d den svenska produktivitetstakten varit hgre. Observera att detta gller produktivitet mtt per sysselsatt. Uppenbarligen ger en analys av det hr slaget inte en entydig bild av den lngsiktiga produktivitetsutvecklingen framver. En produktivitetstillvxt mellan 1 och 2 procent verkar dock rimlig. Det skulle i sin tur kunna gra det mjligt att frena ett inflationsml p 2 procent med nominella lnekningar p mellan 3 och 4 procent p nationell niv. Det r viktigt att observera att lnekningarna avser svl avtal som lneglidning. En annan sak r sedan att lneutrymmet naturligtvis varierar mellan olika sektorer, ngot jag strax terkommer till. Det hr r en lnekningstakt som tydligt underskrider Riksbankens lneprognos i inflationsrapporten. Resonemanget skdliggr att de lnekningstal som Riksbanken anger i inflationsrapporten enbart r prognoser och inte bedmningar av vilken takt som r den bsta fr ekonomin p sikt. Ngra begrnsningar i analysen Jag konstaterade att den vntade inflationstakten p 2 procent tillsammans med den berknade produktivitetsutvecklingen utgr en naturlig startpunkt fr bedmningen av lneutrymmet p nationell niv. Det hr resonemanget har dock sina tydliga begrnsningar. Ekonomin mste befinna sig i extern och intern balans, vilket i praktiken innebr att det ska rda full sysselsttning och att betalningarna med utlandet inte ska utgra ngot problem. Vinstniverna i ekonomin mste ocks vara frenliga med en lngsiktigt god tillvxt. Om inte detta gller och om det, som idag, rder arbetslshet mste de genomsnittliga lnekningarna vara lgre n vad som antyds av den enkla regeln fr att sysselsttningen ska kunna ka. Lnder inom EU som lyckats hlla tillbaka nominella lnekningar har ocks lyckats bra med att skapa nya jobb. Utvecklingen i Danmark och Holland r goda exempel p detta. Lt mig ocks understryka att jag hittills helt har frt mitt resonemang utifrn ett vergripande nationellt perspektiv. Detta perspektiv har sina tydliga brister. Produktivitetsfrbttringar stadkoms av individer ute i olika fretag och produktionsenheter. Det r allts dr lneutrymmet skapas. Mot denna bakgrund ligger det en risk i att alltfr mycket fokusera p den genomsnittliga lnekningstakten i ekonomin. Den faktiska lnekningen i olika sektorer i ekonomin - d.v.s. hur lnestrukturen ser ut - r centralt fr hur sysselsttningen och inflationen pverkas. Ett exempel: Antag att en given genomsnittlig total lnekningstakt - som i sig r frenlig med inflationsmlet - i huvudsak beror p lnekningar fr relativt outbildad och oerfaren arbetskraft. Det fr helt andra, och mer negativa konsekvenser fr den totala arbetslsheten n om samma genomsnittliga lnekning beror p lnekningar som tagit hnsyn till skillnader i produktivitet i olika yrkesgrupper. Eller lt oss anta att det bakom en genomsnittlig lnekningssiffra dljer sig lnekningar frmst inom sektorer dr konkurrensen r frhllandevis lg. Detta br sl igenom i kade priser i hgre grad, n om motsvarande lnekning vore mer jmnt frdelad. Lt mig avslutningsvis konstatera att det r gldjande att arbetsmarknadens parter under senare r i allt hgre grad verkar stlla sig bakom inflationsmlspolitiken. P mnga vis finner jag det naturligt. Med en lg och stabil inflation skapas goda frutsttningar fr tillvxt och sysselsttning. Det r med all skerhet ocks i hg grad just medlemmarna i era fackfreningar som skulle drabbas om inflationen ter skulle tilltas ta fart. Till detta kommer att en politik inriktad p ett tydligt inflationsml ver tiden br kunna ge en stabil grund fr lnebildningen och drmed underltta inte minst fr de avtalsslutande parterna. Samtidigt tycker jag att det r viktigt att vi fr en lpande diskussion om den aktuella bedmningen och politiken. Vi rknar idag - i likhet med flertalet andra bedmare med att inflationen ska stiga de nrmaste ren. Bedmningarna om hur mycket inflationen stiger kan frsts variera. Nr den underliggande inflationen r 1,8 procent r det emellertid uppenbart att en hjning av reporntan inte br drja srskilt lnge, givet att inget ofrutsett pverkar konjunkturbilden. Title: Effects on the growth of the new stabilisation policy regime
text: Heikensten: Effects on the growth of the new stabilization policy regime Date: 2002-04-02 Speaker: First Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Place: Seminar on growth, SACO, Stockholm Let me begin by thanking you for the invitation to speak here today. The question I will try to highlight is how the choice of stabilization policy regime may affect the conditions for achieving good and long-term sustainable growth in the economy. I will focus on three different issues. Initially, I will take a historical look back to try to find out the answer to the question of what the relationship between inflation and growth looks like. I illustrate this with data from the 1900s. In this context, I also comment on what economic research has to say about the links between inflation and growth. Next, I turn the question around and highlight how economic growth affects monetary policy in an inflation targeting regime. Finally, I will make some reflections on how the new stabilization policy regime we obtained in Sweden during the 1990s, with low inflation and stable macroeconomic conditions, has affected the prospects for economic growth. Inflation and growth in a longer perspective Since the introduction of the inflation targeting regime in Sweden in 1993, the annual average inflation measured by the consumer price index (CPI) has been approximately 1.8 percent. Over the same period, GDP has grown by about 2.5 per cent per year. This development represents a marked shift compared to the latter part of the 1980s. It is also a rather different development compared to the rest of the world, as illustrated by Chart 1. In the latter part of the period, we have had both higher growth and lower inflation than the euro area and Germany, while the opposite was true in the second half of the 1980s. At the same time, of course, we must not forget that the good development in recent times is partly due to the fact that capacity utilisation has long been rather low, after the crisis in the early 1990s. It is a considerable reduction in inflation and increase in growth that has occurred. However, there have been periods of high growth and low inflation in the past, as shown in Chart 2. For example, inflation averaged about 1 percent per year and growth almost 3.5 percent per year from the beginning of the century until the outbreak of The First World War (1900-1914). Figure 2 also shows that periods of low inflation and high growth can be found, as well as vice versa. But to conclude with certainty on this basis that there is a stable causal relationship, i.e. that low inflation causes higher growth, is not possible. Figure 3 shows the relationship between inflation and growth, with each point in the chart corresponding to the inflation and growth rate in Sweden over a five-year period. There is a correlation, but it is not so strong. Low inflation could conceivably lead to higher growth, but it could just as easily be the case that some omitted variable affects both inflation and growth so that the above correlation arises. An example could be oil price rises, which both drive up the inflation rate and, via various mechanisms, push back growth. The fact that the link between inflation and growth is not so strong is perhaps also not so surprising. According to the theory of rational expectations, it is not actual inflation so much as the unexpected one that could conceivably have an impact on household and corporate behavior. There are some studies that suggest that low inflation can be beneficial for growth, especially when it comes to comparing very high inflation levels of over 10% with levels close to our current target. A number of studies along these lines have been carried out, for example, within the framework of the work of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. But many of these studies suffer from what statisticians usually call identification problems. It has often been the case that inflation fluctuated most in periods of high inflation, while periods of low inflation have usually been associated with more stable inflation. It is therefore difficult to determine what role average inflation actually plays. After all, it is indistinguishable from the effects of fluctuations in inflation. It is easy to see that large fluctuations in inflation can be detrimental to real economic development. They naturally entail significant uncertainty for households and businesses that risk having a negative impact, not least on the willingness to invest. Chart 4 shows that growth in Sweden has fluctuated most during decades when inflation has varied widely. Stabilising inflation at a low level can thus be a way of reducing the risk of fluctuations in inflation and thus also in the real economy. It should thus also be able to contribute to a slightly higher growth in the long run. Exactly at what level inflation should stabilise, on the other hand, is a more difficult question, and there is an extensive literature that I will not go into in this context. I myself have sympathy for a definition usually attributed to Alan Greenspan; that inflation should be so low that it does not significantly affect the actions of households and businesses. Then I think you end up pretty close to the 2 percent we currently work with in Sweden. It is worth noting that inflation targets in a number of other countries are also around this level. The role of growth in the inflation targeting regime Although it is difficult to demonstrate a clear causal link between inflation and growth, economic growth plays a central role in monetary policy in an inflation targeting regime. I will now go on to briefly explain how we view growth when we make inflation forecasts and touch on some of the problems we then face in practice. According to traditional Keynesian reasoning, actual output developments - measured as e.g. GDP - fluctuate around a long-term growth trend due to demand in the economy fluctuating over time, see Chart 5. When GDP exceeds its trend level, demand pressures normally arise, which in turn are often associated with inflation. The Riksbank's role is to counteract such inflationary impulses. Similarly, we can normally act if actual growth is about to be lower than the long-term, potential growth. Thus, when we try to achieve our inflation target, we can also help to smooth out the fluctuations in the economy. The trend in GDP is usually assumed to be exogenous, i.e. pre-given, and not possible to influence with monetary policy. What we can influence by changing the repo rate in the first place is the fluctuations in general demand and thus inflationary pressures. It is a common belief that monetary policy affects demand with a certain lag. Therefore, the Riksbank must make forecasts on inflation a number of years in the future and let these forecasts guide decisions on the repo rate. If a forecast made under the assumption that the repo rate is unchanged results in the assessment that inflation during the forecast period will exceed the target, there are normally reasons to increase the repo rate. Similarly, there are normally reasons to lower interest rates if the forecast suggests below-target inflation. Growth plays a central role in the inflation assessment. An assessment must be made of the development of demand. This is then set against a valuation of what growth may be possible without resource utilisation being so high that inflation risks picking up. One problem with concepts such as potential growth and resource utilization in the economy as a whole is that they cannot be directly observed, but must be estimated using various econometric and statistical methods. That the reality is not simple is shown in Figure 6. Different ways of measuring potential growth obviously produce quite different results. Potential growth can also vary over time, which often cannot be substantiated until there are outcome figures for growth and inflation. For these reasons, among others, the Riksbank works in parallel with many different methodological approaches. For example, with regard to potential growth over the next few years, we also base our work on relatively detailed assessments of the evolution of labour supply, combined with different forecasts of productivity, taking into account, inter alia, cyclical patterns. Of course, as the estimate of the productive capacity of the economy has changed over time, the estimates of resource utilisation at a given point in time have also changed, as shown in Figure 7. A good example is the assessments for 1995-1996. In November 1995, the economic slack - calculated by the so-called output gap - was projected to run out in the following year. Subsequently, the output gap was projected to be positive. The corresponding assessment in last autumn's inflation reports was that the output gap between 1995 and 1996 was sharply negative, around 5-6 per cent. To some extent, the changed view is due to the fact that the way of measuring the output gap has evolved over time. In addition, the data is revised, even back in time, which can also affect the estimates. Another contributing factor to the fact that the view of the economy's spare resources changes over time is that new information comes in. Our current view of the size of the output gap is thus also likely to change as new methods are developed and new statistics are introduced. Let me emphasise, just in case, that the Riksbank does not rely solely on econometric estimates when it comes to resource utilisation either. In parallel, we use other types of information about bottlenecks, etc. that we can get e.g. from barometer surveys. An unusually good example of this, incidentally, is precisely the winter and spring of 1996, when little weight was in practice given to the calculations that were available on the use of resources. Instead, account was taken of barometer surveys and information on the situation in the labour market, among other things. There are also many good examples from recent years of the difficulties in assessing the size of potential growth and resource utilisation. Going back a few years, the discussion was very much about what the so-called new economy could possibly mean. Productivity development surprised positively for a couple of years, not only in the US but also to some extent in Sweden. In addition, inflation year after year, despite high growth, was significantly lower than expected. Against this background, there were arguments that potential growth could have increased slightly. This was also the subject of some of the reforms carried out in the areas of taxation, social security and deregulation in the first part of the 1990s. If this were the case, there might also be room for lower interest rates. However, the problems of assessment and decision-making are not limited to this. The demand side of the economy can also be affected by fundamental changes in supply conditions. If growth conditions improve, profit expectations will be positively affected. That, in turn, affects stock prices, which rise. This favours investment, but also consumption among households that own shares. Rising product viability can also be a signal to households that the scope for wage increases has become larger, which can also benefit consumption. A process of this kind could just as easily end up with higher as lower interest rates. The difficulty in assessing the strength of the various mechanisms and even more so the dynamics over time is obviously significant. The higher inflation outcome of the past year raises some similar questions, but now with the opposite sign, as inflation has come out higher than expected despite lower aggregate demand. In several inflation reports over the past year, this has led us to discuss whether we have been too optimistic in assessing how much the economy can withstand without inflation rising. Let me draw two conclusions on this issue before moving on to the last question: "In practice, a central bank can probably only act in a way that gradually absorbs new information about resource utilisation and potential growth and includes this in its assessments. You will then be criticised both for being too pessimistic and too optimistic. Only in arrears does it turn out what was right. I myself described the Riksbank's stance on the new economy as "hesitant but not dismissive". That's also what we were in our forecasts. We looked a little more optimistically than before at the potential growth and resource utilization. But it was only about a few tenths. "The second conclusion concerns the view of how great the accuracy of inflation targeting policy can be. We probably have to reckon with inflation fluctuating a bit. Achieving exactly 2% inflation every year is practically not possible. However, it should do well on average over time. In fact, it is not even desirable to seek exactly 2% in all situations. This could mean unnecessarily large fluctuations in interest rates and economic growth. With the knowledge gaps we and other central banks have illustrated, for example, with the difficulties in specifying resource utilisation - there are also good reasons to be sceptical about the ambition to conduct a fine-tuning monetary policy. We know too little to cope with this. Finally, let me turn to the question of what the transition to a low-inflation environment, with stable rules of the game for economic policy, may have meant for growth. In any case, I intended to do this partly on the basis of my own experiences from what has happened in Sweden over the past 10-15 years. Sometimes there is support in the research for the reasoning I bring up, sometimes not. I will address four areas where I see clear changes in the direction of growth promotion compared to the 1970s and 80s. Productivity An important explanation for the acute economic crisis of the early 1990s was the weak productivity development in the 1970s and 80s. A change for the better appears to have taken place in terms of productivity, although it is too early to evaluate its permanentity, see Figure 8. I believe that the improvement we have seen is partly due to the fact that the inflation targeting regime has created a clearer framework for companies' actions. Today, there are no shortcuts to profitability, as there were in the 1970s and 80s, when competition problems were repeatedly solved with devaluations. Both the motives and the acceptance for continuously rationalizing and streamlining production have been strengthened. Investeringsmonstret During the 1980s, we invested a lot in housing and real estate in Sweden. Over the past ten years, the picture has been different, now it is machines and other investments that have taken over, see chart 9. The sectoral distribution is also partly different, with significantly more investment in high technology. These differences, of course, have many explanations; the structure of the tax system, the presence of new technologies, etc. But I also believe that an important factor has been the new, more stable macroeconomic environment. Many of the investment decisions of the 1980s, not least concerning real estate, were taken on the wrong premises. Industrial investment was also hit by the high cost situation that followed in the wake of inflation. Furthermore, the difficulty of assessing profitability and economic development in general was likely to have a dampening effect. For this approach, it is also possible to find support in the academic literature. When inflation is high and volatile, the price mechanism works worse. It becomes difficult to distinguish profitable from less profitable investments. Wage Wage formation has also seen tangible improvements. Carling et al. point to five significant changes that occurred in this area during the 1990s. Of these, at least two are associated with the monetary policy regime: Firstly, lower inflation means better conditions for expecting rising real wages in the event of low nominal wage increases. The development of real wages in this way is confirmed by Chart 10. The nominal rate of wage growth has fallen in the 1990s compared with the 1970s and 80s. At the same time, real wage growth has been relatively good. In the 1970s and 80s, the picture was different. When fiscal policy could not ensure low inflation, and devaluations succeeded each other, wage formation more or less broke down. Wages and prices chased each other upwards in a spiral. Secondly, high wage increases do not detour through higher prices and weakened competitiveness, but have a direct impact on lower production, investment and employment. Nowadays, the social partners can start from a clear inflation target, which, although it will sometimes be undercut and sometimes exceeded, nevertheless provides a useful and clear benchmark. Strukturpolitiken The new environment, with a precise inflation target, has also improved the conditions for bringing about changes that intensify competition and increase the efficiency of the Swedish economy. The main argument in favor of such measures is, of course, that they contribute to raising prosperity. This is also how we argued in the Ministry of Finance in the latter part of the 1980s, when we worked for, for example, deregulation of agriculture and the housing sector. But it wasn't always an argument that bit strong producer interests. Now there is one more argument; increased competition can help keep inflationary pressures down. That, in turn - at least for some time - could open the door to slightly lower interest rates and therefore higher growth. Final words The reorientation of stabilization policy has thus, in my opinion, played an important role in improving the conditions for economic growth in Sweden. The new stabilization policy environment is in several ways better from a growth point of view than the previously prevailing one. The role of monetary policy in this context is to secure a fixed monetary value, operationalised by the Riksbank at 2 per cent inflation. This, in turn, provides a good basis for growth and employment. But at the same time, it should be remembered that achieving high economic growth requires more than just low inflation; a good education system, a good business and investment climate, a well-functioning tax and social security system, etc. The demands on economic policy are further heightened by competition from a rapidly changing world where ambitions to increase prosperity are high. Significantly more attention both in the media and in discussions among economists should be given to issues of this kind. They are much more important for long-term prosperity development than if the repo rate is a quarter of a percentage point higher or lower. text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Heikensten: Effekter p tillvxten av den nya stabiliseringspolitiska regimen Datum: 2002-04-02 Talare: Frsta vice riksbankschef Lars Heikensten Plats: Seminarium om tillvxt, SACO, Stockholm Lt mig brja med att tacka fr inbjudan att tala hr idag. Den frga jag ska frska belysa r hur valet av stabiliseringspolitisk regim kan tnkas pverka frutsttningarna fr att f till stnd en god och lngsiktigt hllbar tillvxt i ekonomin. Jag kommer att fokusera p tre olika frgestllningar. Inledningsvis kommer jag att gra en historisk tillbakablick fr att frska utrna svaret p frgan hur relationen mellan inflation och tillvxt ser ut. Detta skdliggr jag med data frn 1900-talet. I detta sammanhang kommenterar jag ocks ngot vad nationalekonomisk forskning har att sga om sambanden mellan inflation och tillvxt. Drefter vnder jag p frgan och belyser hur den ekonomiska tillvxten inverkar p penningpolitiken i en inflationsmlsregim. Avslutningsvis ska jag gra ngra reflektioner kring hur den nya stabiliseringspolitiska regim vi ftt i Sverige under 1990-talet, med lg inflation och stabila makroekonomiska frutsttningar, har pverkat utsikterna fr ekonomisk tillvxt. Inflation och tillvxt i ett lngre perspektiv Sedan inflationsmlsregimen introducerades i Sverige 1993 har den rliga genomsnittliga inflationen mtt med konsumentprisindex (KPI) varit ungefr 1,8 procent. BNP har under samma period vxt med ungefr 2,5 procent per r. Den hr utvecklingen innebr ett markant skift jmfrt med senare delen av 1980-talet. Det r ocks en ganska annorlunda utveckling jmfrt med omvrlden, vilket skdliggrs av diagram 1. Under den senare delen av perioden har vi haft bde en hgre tillvxt och en lgre inflation n euroomrdet och Tyskland, medan motsatsen gllde under andra hlften av 1980-talet. Samtidigt fr vi frsts inte glmma bort att den goda utvecklingen under senare tid delvis hnger samman med att kapacitetsutnyttjandet lnge varit ganska lgt, efter krisen i brjan p 1990-talet. Det r en avsevrd snkning av inflationen och kning av tillvxten som intrffat. Det har dock funnits perioder med hg tillvxt och lg inflation tidigare, det framgr tydligt av diagram 2. Exempelvis var inflationen i genomsnitt cirka 1 procent per r och tillvxten nstan 3,5 procent per r frn seklets brjan till frsta vrldskrigets utbrott (1900-1914). Av diagram 2 framgr ocks att man kan hitta svl perioder med lg inflation och hg tillvxt som vice versa. Men att p basis av detta med skerhet dra slutsatsen att det finns ett stabilt orsakssamband, dvs. att den lga inflationen orsakar en hgre tillvxt, r inte mjligt. I diagram 3 visas sambandet mellan inflation och tillvxt, dr varje punkt i diagrammet motsvarar inflations- och tillvxttakten i Sverige under en femrsperiod. Det finns en korrelation, men den r inte s stark. Den lga inflationen skulle kunna tnkas leda till en hgre tillvxt, men det skulle lika grna kunna vara s att ngon utelmnad variabel pverkar bde inflationen och tillvxten s att sambandet ovan uppstr. Ett exempel skulle kunna vara oljeprisstegringar, som bde driver upp inflationstakten och via olika mekanismer pressar tillbaka tillvxten. Att sambandet mellan inflation och tillvxt inte r s starkt r kanske heller inte r s frvnande. Enligt teorin om rationella frvntningar r det inte den faktiska inflationen s mycket som den ovntade som kan tnkas f effekter p hushlls och fretags beteende. Det finns en del studier som tyder p att lg inflation kan vara gynnsamt fr tillvxten, srskilt nr det handlar om att jmfra mycket hga inflationsniver p ver 10 procent med niver nra vrt nuvarande ml. Ett antal studier med den hr inriktningen har t.ex. gjorts inom ramen fr Internationella valutafondens och Vrldsbankens arbete. Men mnga av dessa studier lider av vad statistikerna brukar kalla identifikationsproblem. Oftast har det varit s att inflationen fluktuerat som mest i perioder med hg inflation, medan perioder med lg inflation vanligen varit frknippade med mer stabil inflation. Det r drmed svrt att avgra vilken roll den genomsnittliga inflationen egentligen spelar. Den gr ju inte skilja frn effekterna av fluktuationerna i inflationen. Att stora fluktuationer i inflationen kan vara skadligt fr den realekonomiska utvecklingen r ltt att inse. De medfr naturligt nog en betydande oskerhet fr hushll och fretag som riskerar att ha en negativ inverkan, inte minst p viljan att investera. Diagram 4 visar att tillvxten i Sverige fluktuerat som mest under decennier d inflationen varierat kraftigt. Att stabilisera inflationen p en lg niv kan allts vara ett stt att minska risken fr svngningar i inflationen och drmed ocks i den reala ekonomin. Det br drmed ocks kunna bidra till att tillvxten i det lnga loppet blir ngot hgre. Exakt vid vilken niv inflationen br stabiliseras r dremot en svrare frga, och det finns en omfattande litteratur som jag inte ska g in p i detta sammanhang. Sjlv har jag sympati fr en definition som brukar tillskrivas Alan Greenspan; att inflationen ska var s lg att den inte ptagligt pverkar hushlls och fretags agerande. D tror jag att man hamnar ganska nra de 2 procent vi idag arbetar med i Sverige. Vrt att notera r att inflationsml i en rad andra lnder ocks ligger kring denna niv. Tillvxtens roll i inflationsmlsregimen ven om det r svrt att pvisa ett tydligt orsakssamband mellan inflation och tillvxt s spelar den ekonomiska tillvxten en central roll fr penningpolitiken i en inflationsmlsregim. Jag tnker nu g vidare och kort redogra fr hur vi ser p tillvxten nr vi gr inflationsprognoser och berra en del av de problem vi d i praktiken stlls infr. Enligt traditionella keynesianska resonemang fluktuerar den faktiska produktionsutvecklingen - mtt som t.ex. BNP - kring en lngsiktig tillvxttrend p.g.a. att efterfrgan i ekonomin varierar ver tiden, se diagram 5. Nr BNP verstiger sin trendmssiga niv uppkommer normalt sett ett efterfrgetryck, som i sin tur ofta r frknippat med inflation. Riksbankens roll r att motverka sdana inflationsimpulser. P motsvarande stt kan vi normalt agera om den faktiska tillvxten r p vg att bli lgre n den lngsiktiga, potentiella tillvxten. Nr vi frsker uppn vrt inflationsml kan vi allts ocks bidra till att jmna ut svngningarna i konjunkturen. Trenden i BNP antas vanligtvis vara exogen, dvs. p frhand given, och inte mjlig att pverka med penningpolitiken. Vad vi kan pverka genom att ndra i frsta hand reporntan r fluktuationerna i den allmnna efterfrgan och drmed inflationstrycket. Det r en vanlig uppfattning att penningpolitiken pverkar efterfrgan med en viss efterslpning. Drfr mste Riksbanken gra prognoser p inflationen ett antal r fram i tiden och lta dessa prognoser vgleda besluten om reporntan. Om en prognos som grs under antagandet att reporntan r ofrndrad resulterar i bedmningen att inflationen under prognosperioden kommer att verstiga mlet finns det normalt sett skl att hja reporntan. P motsvarande stt finns det normalt sett skl att snka rntan om prognosen tyder p en inflation under mlet. Tillvxten spelar en central roll nr inflationsbedmningen grs. En bedmning mste gras av efterfrgans utveckling. Denna stlls sedan mot en vrdering av vilken tillvxt som kan tnkas vara mjlig utan att resursutnyttjandet blir s hgt att inflationen riskerar att skjuta fart. Ett problem med begrepp som potentiell tillvxt och resursutnyttjande i ekonomin som helhet r att de inte direkt kan observeras utan mste skattas med hjlp av olika ekonometriska och statistiska metoder. Att verkligheten inte r enkel framgr av diagram 6. Olika stt att mta potentiell tillvxt ger uppenbarligen ganska olika resultat. Den potentiella tillvxten kan ocks variera ver tiden, ngot som ofta inte kan belggas innan det finns utfallssiffror fr tillvxt och inflation. Av bl.a. dessa skl arbetar Riksbanken parallellt med mnga olika metodologiska ansatser. Nr det gller den potentiella tillvxten under de nrmaste ren utgr vi t.ex. ocks frn relativt detaljerade bedmningar av arbetskraftsutbudets utveckling i kombination med olika prognoser fr produktiviteten, dr hnsyn tas bl.a. till det cykliska mnstret. Eftersom uppskattningen av ekonomins produktionskapacitet har ndrats ver tiden har frsts ocks bedmningarna av resursutnyttjandet vid en viss tidpunkt ndrats, vilket framgr av diagram 7. Ett bra exempel r bedmningarna fr 1995-1996. I november 1995 berknades de lediga resurserna i ekonomin - berknade med det s.k. produktionsgapet - komma att ta slut under det fljande ret. Drefter berknades produktionsgapet bli positivt. Motsvarande bedmning i frra hstens inflationsrapporter var att produktionsgapet 1995-1996 var kraftigt negativt, cirka 5-6 procent. Till en viss del beror den ndrade synen p att sttet att mta produktionsgapet utvecklats ver tiden. Till detta kommer att data revideras, ven bakt i tiden, vilket ocks kan pverka skattningarna. Ytterligare en bidragande faktor till att synen p ekonomins lediga resurser ndras ver tiden r att ny information kommer in. Vr nuvarande syn p produktionsgapets storlek kommer allts ocks antagligen att frndras efterhand som nya metoder utvecklas och ny statistisk inkommer. Lt mig fr skerhets skull understryka att Riksbanken inte heller nr det gller resursutnyttjandet enbart utgr ifrn ekonometriska skattningar. Vi anvnder oss parallellt av andra typer av information om flaskhalsar etc. som vi kan f t.ex. frn barometerunderskningar. Ett ovanligt bra exempel p detta r fr vrigt just vintern och vren 1996, d liten vikt i praktiken tillmttes de berkningar som fanns p resursutnyttjandet. Hnsyn togs i stllet bl.a. till barometerunderskningar och information om situationen p arbetsmarkanden. Det finns mnga goda exempel ocks frn senare r p svrigheterna med att bedma storleken p den potentiella tillvxten och resursutnyttjandet. Gr vi tillbaka ngra r handlade diskussionen mycket om vad den s.k. nya ekonomin skulle kunna tnkas innebra. Produktivitetsutvecklingen verraskade positivt under ett par r, inte bara i USA utan ocks i ngon mn i Sverige. Dessutom blev inflationen r efter r, trots en hg tillvxt, vsentligt lgre n berknat. Mot den hr bakgrunden fanns det allts argument fr att den potentiella tillvxten skulle kunna ha kat ngot. Fr det talade ocks en del av de reformer som genomfrts nr det gller skatter, socialfrskringar och avregleringar under frsta delen av 1990-talet. Om det frhll sig p detta stt skulle det mjligen ocks finnas utrymme fr lgre rntor. Bedmnings- och beslutsproblemen inskrnker sig emellertid inte till detta. Ocks ekonomins efterfrgesida kan pverkas av fundamentala frndringar rrande utbudsfrhllandena. Om tillvxtfrutsttningarna frbttras pverkas vinstfrvntningarna positivt. Det pverkar i sin tur aktiepriserna, som stiger. Det gynnar investeringar, men ven konsumtion bland hushll som ger aktier. Stigande produktvitet kan ven vara en signal till hushllen att utrymmet fr lnekningar blivit strre, vilket ven det kan gynna konsumtionen. Ett frlopp av det hr slaget skulle lika grna kunna sluta med hgre som lgre rntor. Svrigheten att bedma styrkan i de olika mekanismerna och n mer dynamiken ver tiden r sjlvfallet betydande. Det senaste rets hgre inflationsutfall reser en del liknande frgor, men nu med motsatt frtecken, eftersom inflationen kommit ut hgre n vntat trots en lgre aggregerad efterfrgan. I flera inflationsrapporter det senaste ret har detta franlett oss att diskutera om vi varit fr optimistiska i bedmningen av hur mycket ekonomin tl utan att inflationen kar. Lt mig dra tv slutsatser rrande den hr problematiken innan jag gr ver till den sista frgestllningen:  I praktiken kan en centralbank antagligen inte agera p annat vis n att gradvis ta till sig ny information om resursutnyttjandet och den potentiella tillvxten och inkludera detta i sina bedmningar. Man kommer d att f kritik bde fr att man r fr pessimistisk och fr optimistisk. Frst i efterskott visar det sig vad som var rtt. Riksbankens hllning till den nya ekonomin beskrev jag sjlv som "avvaktande men inte avvisande". Det var ocks vad vi var i vra prognoser. Vi sg lite mer optimistiskt n tidigare p den potentiella tillvxten och resursutnyttjandet. Men det handlade bara om ngra tiondelar.  Den andra slutsatsen rr synen p hur stor trffskerheten i inflationsmlspolitiken kan vara. Vi mste antagligen rkna med att inflationen varierar en del. Att uppn exakt 2 procents inflation varje r r i praktiken inte mjligt. Dremot br det g bra i genomsnitt ver tiden. Det r faktiskt inte ens nskvrt att efterstrva exakt 2 procent i alla lgen. Det skulle kunna innebra ondigt stora svngningar i rntor och ekonomisk tillvxt. Med de kunskapsluckor vi och andra centralbanker har skdliggjorda t.ex. med svrigheterna att precisera resursutnyttjandet - finns det ocks goda skl att stlla sig skeptisk till ambitionen att bedriva en finjusterande penningpolitik. Vi vet fr lite fr att klara av detta. Inflationsmlsregimens effekter p tillvxten Lt mig nu avslutningsvis ta upp frgan om vad vergngen till en lginflationsmilj, med stabila spelregler fr den ekonomiska politiken, kan ha betytt fr tillvxten. Det tnkte jag i varje fall delvis gra p basis av egna erfarenheter frn vad som hnt i Sverige under de senaste 10-15 ren. Ibland finns det std i forskningen fr de resonemang jag tar upp, ibland inte. Jag ska ta upp fyra omrden dr jag ser tydliga frndringar i tillvxtbefrmjande riktning jmfrt med 1970- och 80-talen. Produktiviteten En viktig frklaring till den akuta ekonomiska krisen i brjan av 1990-talet var den svaga produktivitetsutvecklingen under 1970- och 80-talen. En frndring till det bttre frefaller ha skett nr det gller produktiviteten, ven om det r fr tidigt att vrdera hur permanent den r, se diagram 8. Jag tror att den frbttring som vi sett delvis sammanhnger med att inflationsmlsregimen skapat en tydligare ram fr fretagens agerande. Det finns idag inte ngra genvgar till lnsamhet, som det gjorde under 1970- och 80-talen, nr konkurrensproblemen gng efter annan lstes med devalveringar. Bde motiven och acceptansen fr att lpande rationalisera och effektivisera produktionen har strkts. Investeringsmnstret Under 1980-talet investerade vi i Sverige mycket i bostder och fastigheter. De senaste tio ren har bilden varit en annan, nu r det maskiner och vriga investeringar som tagit ver, se diagram 9. Sektorfrdelningen r ocks delvis en annan, med betydligt mer investeringar i hgteknologi. De hr skillnaderna har frsts mnga frklaringar; skattesystemets upplggning, frekomsten av ny teknik etc. Men jag tror ocks att en viktig faktor varit den nya stabilare makroekonomiska miljn. Mnga av 1980-talets investeringsbeslut, inte minst rrande fastigheter, togs p felaktiga premisser. Industriinvesteringarna drabbades ocks av det hga kostnadslge som fljde i inflationens klvatten. Vidare hade svrigheten att bedma lnsamheten och den ekonomiska utvecklingen i stort troligtvis en dmpande effekt. Fr detta synstt gr det ocks att finna std i den akademiska litteraturen. Nr inflationen r hg och volatil fungerar prismekanismen smre. Det blir svrt att urskilja lnsamma frn mindre lnsamma investeringar. Lnebildningen Ocks nr det gller lnebildningen har det skett ptagliga frbttringar. Carling m.fl. pekar p fem betydelsefulla frndringar som skett p detta omrde under 1990talet. Av dessa r tminstone tv frknippade med den penningpolitiska regimen: Fr det frsta innebr den lgre inflationen bttre frutsttningar att vid lga nominella lnelyft frvnta sig stigande reallner. Att reallnerna utvecklats p detta stt bekrftas av diagram 10. Den nominella lnekningstakten har under 1990-talet sjunkit jmfrt med 1970- och 80talen. Samtidigt har reallnekningarna blivit frhllandevis goda. Under 1970- och 80-talen var bilden en annan. Nr finanspolitiken inte kunde skra en lg inflation, och devalveringarna avlste varandra, brt lnebildningen mer eller mindre samman. Lner och priser jagade varandra uppt i en spiral. Fr det andra gr inte hga lnekningar omvgen via hgre priser och frsvagad konkurrenskraft utan ger direkt utslag i lgre produktion, investeringar och sysselsttning. Numera kan arbetsmarknadens parter utg ifrn ett tydligt inflationsml, som visserligen ibland kommer att underskridas och ibland verskridas, men som nd ger ett anvndbart och tydligt riktmrke. Strukturpolitiken Den nya miljn, med ett precist inflationsml, har ocks frbttrat frutsttningarna fr att f till stnd frndringar som skrper konkurrensen och kar effektiviteten i den svenska ekonomin. Det viktigaste argumentet fr sdana tgrder r frsts att de bidrar till att hja vlstndet. Det var ocks s vi argumenterade i finansdepartementet under senare delen av 1980-talet, nr vi arbetade fr t.ex. avregleringar av jordbruket och bostadssektorn. Men det var inte alltid ett argument som bet p starka producentintressen. Nu finns ytterligare ett argument; kad konkurrens kan bidra till att hlla inflationstrycket nere. Det kan i sin tur - i varje fall en tid - ppna fr ngot lgre rntor och drmed hgre tillvxt. Slutord Omlggningen av stabiliseringspolitiken har allts enligt min mening spelat en viktig roll fr att frbttra villkoren fr ekonomisk tillvxt i Sverige. Den nya stabiliseringspolitiska miljn r p flera stt bttre ur tillvxtsynpunkt n den tidigare rdande. Penningpolitikens roll i det hr sammanhanget r att skra ett fast penningvrde, av Riksbanken operationaliserat till 2 procents inflation. Det utgr i sin tur en god grund fr tillvxt och sysselsttning. Men samtidigt ska man komma ihg att det krvs mer n bara lg inflationen fr att uppn en hg ekonomisk tillvxt; ett bra utbildningssystem, ett gott fretags- och investeringsklimat, ett vl fungerande skatte- och socialfrskringssystem osv. Kraven p den ekonomiska politiken skrps ytterligare av konkurrens frn en omvrld som snabbt frndras och dr ambitionerna att hja vlstndet r hga. Betydligt mer uppmrksamhet bde i media och i diskussioner bland ekonomer borde gnas t frgestllningar av det hr slaget. De r mycket viktigare fr den lngsiktiga vlstndsutvecklingen n om reporntan r en kvarts procentenhet hgre eller lgre. Title: The inflation picture stands out mainly
text: Heikensten: The inflation picture stands the test of time Date 2004-08-16 Riksbank Governor Lars Heikensten spoke about economic development and the inflation outlook on Monday at a lunch seminar in Falun arranged by the County Administrative Board of Dalarna. "In the previous inflation report from the beginning of June, the Riksbank's assessment was that the international economy would continue to strengthen this year and over the next two years. At the subsequent monetary policy meeting at the end of June, we concluded that there was possibly reason to be somewhat more optimistic about economic growth this year. Recent statistics confirm this picture and suggest that the upturn in the next few years may be somewhat stronger. Admittedly, there have been some less positive signals from the US recently, but this is offset by the fact that growth elsewhere, including in Asia, has been surprisingly strong," Heikensten said. "In June, we expected international inflation to increase during the year as a result primarily of rising global resource utilisation. Developments since the beginning of June indicate that the international price increase has been somewhat stronger than expected. A slight upward revision of the forecast for oil prices in the near future seems justified today, partly in the light of the prevailing futures prices. However, most estimates still assume that oil prices will fall back in the coming years, which is also what futures markets reflect. Since monetary policy focuses on the development of inflation over a couple of years, the high oil price today does not need to have much monetary policy significance. Crucially, however, the rise in oil prices does not perpetuate, spread further in the economy or lead to higher inflation expectations," Heikensten continued. "The international financial markets have recently been characterized by uncertainty about the strength of the US economic upturn and the impact of high oil prices on global growth. Long-term interest rates have fallen since the end of May, as have international stock prices. The krona has weakened slightly in TCW terms. As I see it today, however, there is no reason to change the view from early summer on future financial conditions; long-term interest rates can be expected to rise with the increased global resource utilisation, while the krona should strengthen, taking into account, among other things, the continued very large trade surpluses," Heikensten said. "Compared with other analysts, the Riksbank has been relatively optimistic about the Swedish economy over the past year. Nevertheless, we have had to revise up our forecasts for GDP growth gradually. Last year and this year, exports have risen unexpectedly fast. This is due both to the fact that international demand has generally grown faster than expected and that the relative price of Swedish exports has become unexpectedly low. Newly emerged data since the previous monetary policy meeting suggests that exports have once again surprised. Another positive signal is that an upturn in investment, which we and other observers have long been waiting for, seems to have begun. At the same time, consumption continues to grow stably. All in all, this suggests that there is reason to be more optimistic about growth in the Swedish economy," Heikensten continued. "The labour market has so far performed relatively weakly and there are no clear signs of a turnaround yet. However, the recovery in the economy suggests that there will be an improvement. The mirror image of good growth and a subdued labour market is continued high productivity growth and low cost pressures in the Swedish economy," Heikensten noted. "Inflation in Sweden has developed in line with the assessment made in the previous inflation report and remains low. However, as I have already pointed out, the decisive factor for monetary policy is not inflation at present, but how we view inflationary pressures over a couple of years' time. In June, the Riksbank's assessment was that inflation in the coming year would be relatively stable and then gradually increase as a result of rising international and domestic resource utilisation. Taking into account the risks we saw ahead of us  mainly a slightly stronger economic upturn, inflation was judged to be in line with the Riksbank's inflation target over two years. This was the reason why the repo rate was left unchanged at the last two monetary policy meetings," Heikensten said. "How, then, will the view of inflation in the coming years be affected by the new information received in July and August? My own assessment is that the conclusion that the Riksbank drew on inflation at its last meeting at the end of June essentially stands. Some minor revisions in views on economic developments and inflation may be justified. In addition, the economic upturn has now lasted another couple of months. Nevertheless, inflation in a couple of years' time still looks to be in line with the target," Heikensten concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Heikensten: Inflationsbilden str sig i huvudsak Datum 2004-08-16 Riksbankschef Lars Heikensten talade om den ekonomiska utvecklingen och inflationsutsikterna under mndagen p ett lunchseminarium i Falun arrangerat av Lnsstyrelsen i Dalarna. "I fregende inflationsrapport frn brjan av juni var Riksbankens bedmning att den internationella konjunkturen skulle fortstta att frstrkas i r och under de kommande tv ren. Vid det pfljande penningpolitiska mtet i slutet av juni konstaterade vi att det mjligtvis fanns anledning att vara ngot mer optimistisk om den ekonomiska tillvxten i r. Nyinkommen statistik bekrftar denna bild och talar fr att uppgngen de nrmaste ren kan bli ngot starkare. Visserligen har det kommit en del mindre positiva signaler frn USA p senare tid, men detta uppvgs av att tillvxten p andra hll, bland annat i Asien, varit verraskande stark," sa Heikensten. "I juni rknade vi med att den internationella inflationen skulle ka under ret till fljd i frsta hand av ett stigande globalt resursutnyttjande. Utvecklingen sedan i brjan av juni tyder p att den internationella prisuppgngen blivit ngot starkare n vntat. En viss upprevidering av prognosen fr oljepriset under den nrmaste tiden frefaller idag motiverad bland annat mot bakgrund av de rdande terminspriserna. Title: Incoming data important
text: Heikensten: Incoming data important Date 2005-05-31 At a meeting organized by Sodra Smaland's municipalities and county councils in connection with Tylosand Week, Riksbank Governor Lars Heikensten spoke on Tuesday about the current economic situation and monetary policy. "Let me start with the assessment of Swedish economic and inflation developments that we made in our latest inflation report in March. We then found that the recovery in Sweden's economy, which began in 2003, continued last year. Strong international demand for Swedish exports was an important driver. Global GDP growth was estimated to have peaked in 2004, but would remain good in the coming years. Growth in the euro area, which remained surprisingly weak, was also expected to pick up moderately in the coming years," Heikensten began. "The Swedish economic upturn was expected to continue and gradually spread to the domestic parts of the economy. Business investment, construction and household consumption were expected to account for most of the growth in demand in 2005. Although employment had developed surprisingly weakly last year, continued good GDP growth suggested that employment would turn upwards in the coming years. Despite gradually rising resource utilisation, we expected inflation to remain low at least over the next year. In the long term, however, inflation was expected to rise as the economic upturn continued," Heikensten noted. "When we checked our assessment in the Inflation Report since April, we highlighted that the outlook for the economy has become somewhat more uncertain as weaker data were received from the euro area. At the same time, the picture was divided as to whether the slowdown in growth in the United States was temporary or not. In addition, there were signs from Sweden that goods exports and industrial production increased less than expected and that the labour market has not yet turned upwards in a clear way. Against this background, we stressed that we intended to closely monitor whether the observed trends in the economy were temporary or more permanent," Heikensten said. "Both in connection with the inflation report and at our last monetary policy meeting in April, the Riksbank chose, as you know, to leave the repo rate unchanged at 2 percent. The decisions were not obvious, even though we were unanimous in the Riksbank's management. Although inflation at the end of the two-year period we reviewed was expected to be in line with the target, we expected it to be consistently lower than the Riksbank's target of 2 per cent before that, partly due to the effects of various types of so-called supply factors. At the same time, however, we expected  incidentally, like virtually all other analysts  that growth in the next few years would be higher than the economy could be expected to manage in the long term without inflation picking up. The question was thus how meaningful it would be to further increase demand, especially as we were well into the economic upturn. The picture also included the high growth in household borrowing combined with rising house prices. While none of these arguments were individually sufficient to refrain from cutting interest rates, all in all, as we saw it, they spoke for a degree of caution," Heikensten said. "Perhaps there is a case for somewhat developing in this context the discussion that has been brought about the rapid expansion of credit and the evolution of house prices. The Riksbank is not worried about house prices per se. Nor do we worry about the banking system as a whole, even though debt levels have increased and some 80s-like elements have begun to appear. I am thinking, for example, of the headlines of the tabloids and the increasingly escalating campaigns to get households to borrow more. What we cannot completely ignore is what could happen to general demand and employment in the future if conditions change and households want to reduce their indebtedness. The risk is that this will force an abrupt adjustment of demand. The fact that this is not only a matter of theoretical speculation is illustrated by developments in the Netherlands in recent years, but also by the concerns that exist today also in, for example, the United States, Great Britain and Australia," Heikensten continued. "When inflation is as low as it has been in Sweden recently, it is easy to forget what the connections between the economy and inflation normally look like. What has happened in the United States and, more recently, in The United Kingdom, can then serve as a reminder that the usual connection still seems to apply. Over the past year, the US inflation rate has risen gradually and this seems to be largely explained in the traditional way by the fact that companies' labour costs have increased faster and faster as productivity growth has slowed and resource utilisation has increased," Heikensten recalled. "So how should you look at economic development and inflation in the coming years? The world economy continues to grow relatively stable and few analysts expect anything other than this trend to continue, although there are of course risks, not least as a result of the savings imbalances that have built up. A fundamental driving force behind the upturn is the economic policy that is stimulating in many places. After a few years of low interest rates, corporate balance sheets are now generally strong, while the profit situation is good. In Sweden, too, there are many factors that suggest continued good growth. Both fiscal and monetary policy are expansionary and will probably remain so for some time to come. With nominal wage increases around 3.5 percent and today's low inflation, real wage growth will be good. All in all, this contributes to households being expected to have a good income development. The situation of companies is also good, with strong balance sheets and good profits. Further support for demand provides the currently relatively low-valued exchange rate. The risks of a weaker development for Sweden are probably mainly related to the continued weak labor market," Heikensten said. "Compared to the assessment we made in March, there are reasons to look somewhat less optimistically at the international development. This is mainly due to the fact that developments in the euro area appear to be somewhat weaker than we expected in the Inflation Report. As far as Sweden is concerned, growth apparently continues to be relatively good. A twist now appears to be taking place against domestic demand as expected. However, new labour market figures have continued to be somewhat weaker than expected, although there are signs of stabilisation. It cannot be ruled out that the major changes that are taking place and the concerns that exist about the continued decline in employment will hold back households' willingness to consume compared to what we have expected. Together with the somewhat weaker international picture, this today seems to justify more subdued Swedish output growth, mainly during the current year, than we expected in the inflation report," Heikensten said. "Let me round off with a couple of reflections on the current state of decision-making in monetary policy. As usual, it is important for us in the Riksbank's management to take a position on the information we have and to try to make as good an assessment as possible. All in all, as I mentioned earlier, the statistics received so far seem to me to suggest that the economy may be somewhat weaker than we expected in March. In addition, in my opinion, there has been a slight increase in uncertainty about the economy both in Sweden and abroad. But it's not about a dramatic change," Heikensten said. "For my part, I have repeatedly stressed during the spring the importance of not to lock oneself into any position. It is important to keep all doors open in the future as well. I am now closely following the information that comes in and takes part in the discussion. I am not yet prepared to lay down a line for the next monetary policy meeting for my own part," Heikensten concluded.

Vi konstaterade d att terhmtningen i Sveriges ekonomi, som inleddes 2003, fortsatte i fjol. En stark internationell efterfrgan p svensk export var en viktig drivkraft. Fretagens investeringar, byggandet och hushllens konsumtion vntades svara fr merparten av kningen av efterfrgan under 2005. ven om sysselsttningen hade utvecklats verraskande svagt i fjol, talade en fortsatt god BNP-tillvxt fr att sysselsttningen skulle vnda uppt kommande r. "Nr vi sedan i april gjorde en avstmning av vr bedmning i inflationsrapporten framhll vi att utsikterna fr konjunkturen blivit ngot mer oskra d svagare statistik inkommit frn euroomrdet.
