Title: The Riksbank's work on financial stability
text: SPEECH DATE: SPEAKER: LOCATION: 2003-11-25 Riksbank Governor Lars Heikensten University of Gothenburg SVERIGES RIKSBANK SE-103 37 Stockholm (Brunkebergstorg 11) Phone 46 8 787 00 00 Fax 46 8 21 05 31 registratorn@riksbank.se The Riksbank's work on financial stability Let me begin by thanking you for the invitation to come here and speak today. It feels like a privilege to speak at a Felix Neubergh lecture. In the autumn of 1992, the Swedish Government and the Riksdag were faced with a choice: to take a very quick decision on aid to the Swedish banks without really knowing how extensive this support would ultimately be or to be hit by a financial crisis with unforeseeable consequences for the Swedish economy. All the Swedish banks had made extensive credit losses. Confidence in the Swedish banking system in the international credit market was low regardless of how much loss each of the banks had made. The banks faced difficult financing problems that could ultimately have led to bankruptcy and in the shorter term could have led to difficulties for Swedish companies in obtaining the necessary financing. The decision was the only reasonable one  to save the Swedish banks. The government issued a general guarantee for the debts of banks and established a special authority, the Bank Support Board, which dealt with those banks that had serious problems. The government  with the opposition's stated support  acted just as forcefully and quickly as the situation demanded. However, they were forced, on the basis of insufficient information about the depth and causes of the crisis, to take a decision that could have cost the state budget 100 billion kronor or more. We do not want to experience this again. Sweden came out of the crisis well at that time and our way of solving it has often been a model for other countries' actions. The crisis also focused on financial stability work. The increased complexity of the payment system and the expansion of the financial sector have contributed to financial stability becoming an increasingly important issue both for the Riksbank and for other central banks in the world. A look back After the banking crisis, there were reasons for a certain amount of self-criticism, not least for the Riksbank. The mission of promoting a secure and efficient payment system had in practice 1 [10] not backed up with any systematic analysis work within the bank. Like many others, the Riksbank had been caught off guard by the problems that came to light. The Riksbank therefore began to build up knowledge and analytical capacity on stability issues. The work began on a small scale with only a handful of people involved. The focus of the work was narrow  to detect vulnerabilities in the banking system at an early stage that could lead to a new banking crisis. The Riksbank also decided to issue a report in which the stability situation in the banking sector would be discussed. Internal reports already existed, but in the autumn of 1997 the Riksbank published the first report with a more coherent analysis of financial stability. The idea was that the report would give a signal of how important the Riksbank considered the stability work to be, but it was also a way to focus and develop the work internally. The experience gained from the work on the Inflation Report was good and it therefore seemed natural to build up the work and communication on stability issues in the same way. Through the Stability Report, or financial market report as it was initially called, the Riksbank became the first central bank to publicly present its view on the stability of the financial system. Today, about thirty other countries have followed suit. Recurring financial crises have made it clear that there will always be problems that the authorities must somehow relate to and that they can therefore be helped by a structured, clearly accounted for way of looking at financial stability. Against this background, the International Monetary Fund, among others, has paid more attention to these issues. From 1999 onwards, the Monetary Fund and the World Bank jointly evaluate the financial systems of different countries in something called the Financial Sector Assessment Program. Stability issues are now also on the agenda on almost every occasion when I meet my foreign colleagues. Principles of supervision of the financial system Let me start by sorting out what the financial system actually does. It will provide payment services, convert savings into financing investment and consumption, and provide risk management services. The system thus fulfils a number of important functions in society. If any of these functions were to cease to function, the costs to society could be very great. The damage caused by a disruption would likely be particularly great if it were to affect any vital part of the payment system. It is easy to understand this if you consider the huge amount of payments flowing through the system. The Swedish payment system has a turnover of approximately SEK 500 billion per day. Thus, in less than a week, the entire annual gross domestic product of the Swedish economy is traded! There are also studies showing that more than a dozen crises over the past 15 years have cost the affected countries 10 percent or more of GDP. 2 [10] Thus, the state has good reason to engage in monitoring the financial system. The Riksbank has a role in this work, as the Riksdag has given us the task of promoting a secure and efficient payment system. An important reason why we should ensure efficiency and stability is that the Riksbank, together with the banks, are the central players in the payment system and provide means of payment. Banks distribute banknotes and coins, keep transaction accounts linked to giro systems and operate payment card systems. The Riksbank, for its part, provides accounts in the RIX payment system that banks can use to make large payments among themselves. The work on financial stability is mainly done in three ways. Firstly, there is a specific regulatory framework that sets the framework within which financial firms can operate. Secondly, the system is continuously monitored by both the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Riksbank. Thirdly, the state must be able to deal with crises should they arise after all. The stability work is based on the fact that the Ministry of Finance, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Riksbank have a well-developed cooperation. Parliament makes the laws that apply to financial activities. In this work, the Ministry of Finance is an important player. Finansinspektionen issues more detailed regulations and ensures that the rules are complied with. The Riksbank's contribution to work with the regulations is primarily about responding to referrals, but also about participating in the international work to develop the regulations further. The Riksbank has a central role to play in its surveillance work. The Riksbank concentrates its work on how the financial system as a whole works and what risks may arise. However, in order to identify risks in the system as a whole, the individual institutions and the financial infrastructure must also be monitored. Primarily the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority, but to some extent also the Riksbank, needs to continuously monitor developments in the individual banks. The central role of banks means that a crisis in the banking system could quickly hit both the payment system and credit provision in a serious way. However, it is not only the importance of banks in the payment system or as creditors that makes them worth monitoring. The Economist magazine described banks in an article last spring as the riskiest economic institutions known to man. It may sound drastic, but is in some sense true. The fact that they are risky, however, is not because bankers as a generation are irresponsible and daring, but because banks must inevitably function in such a way in order to fulfil the function so badly needed in the economy. Their main task is to take risks. Banks' financing  deposits or loans from other banks  can quickly disappear, while their assets take longer to materialise. Problems in one bank can also spread to the other banks, something that is usually called systemic risk. This may either be because they have debts among themselves due to loans or trading in securities, or because they participate in the payment system. They also have similar activities and can therefore suffer from the same problems if they arise in the outside world. Spillovers can also arise only as a result of other actors having suspicions that there are links between banks. 3 [10] The monitoring of system stability also increasingly requires the supervision of the financial infrastructure. By infrastructure is meant the systems needed to be able to pay and to trade and deliver financial products. One example is Bankgirocentralen. The proper functioning of these systems reduces the risk of problems spreading from the financial markets, between participants or arising from disruptions caused by the systems themselves. The third part of the monitoring work  crisis management  comes from the fact that the state may need to act to avoid a crisis that threatens system stability. In order to deal with the crisis, the state must be able to assess the consequences of an institution with problems going bankrupt and, if these appear to be serious, take measures to reduce the consequences. In some cases, it may be a question of contributing to the orderly winding-up of the enterprise, in other cases of providing financial support. The general bank guarantee issued by the state during the banking crisis is an example of the latter. In some cases, it may be the Riksbank's responsibility to provide liquidity support. If any bank should have such serious problems that stability is threatened - and the bank has long-term survivability - the Riksbank can give the bank credit on special terms and act as what is normally called lender of last resort. Ongoing monitoring and crisis management are closely linked. Monitoring is a prerequisite for the Riksbank to be able to assess whether financial stability is threatened in the event of a crisis. Without an ongoing analysis of banks, it is difficult to assess in a crisis situation whether and how possible support should be provided. Work on surveillance and crisis management The Riksbank's analysis of system stability is presented twice a year in a report, Financial Stability. A basic purpose of the report is to provide a picture of the resilience of Swedish banks to possible disruptions. The intention is to identify possible risks and influence the players in the market with good analysis. The Riksbank's task can perhaps be seen as keeping a cool head and holding back excessive optimism in an upturn phase when everything seems problem-free or, if there are reasons for it, nuance the picture in a downward phase and allay concerns about serious credit losses. The analysis concentrates on the four large Swedish banking groups, as they are so large that they are probably important for the stability of the system. A default in any of these could threaten stability, although it is by no means self-evident. The evolution of banks' resilience depends on several factors. The Riksbank analyses the banks' most important borrower categories, developments in banking groups and the financial infrastructure. The Riksbank's analysis of borrowers focuses on how companies and households as a whole develop, especially debt levels and future ability to pay. The real estate sector is studied separately, as this sector accounts for a third of 4 [10] bank lending to companies. The prices of commercial real estate and single-family houses are also analysed, as they affect the value of collateral provided for loans in banks and in residential institutions. As Swedish banks have expanded in the Nordic and Baltic sea region, developments in these countries have become increasingly important for the major Swedish banks. About half of their lending goes to foreign borrowers. The borrower analysis has therefore been broadened beyond the country's borders. The large banking groups are analyzed from various aspects. Profitability developments show the ability of banks to create a buffer for future unexpected losses. In addition, there is always the risk that banks with weak profitability will be lured into bold new strategies with the aim of getting a better return on equity  the banks' strategic risk. The analysis of banks' credit portfolios can give an indication of how credit losses will develop over the next one to two years. The liabilities side of banks' balance sheets are also analysed. Traditionally, banks have taken deposits and used these funds to lend. As an increasing proportion of the public's savings have turned to forms of savings other than bank accounts, banks have had to finance increasing lending with borrowing on the capital market. How banks choose to finance themselves gives a picture of the liquidity risks they take. This is perhaps the most difficult part to follow, as the liquidity situation can change very quickly. If problems in an individual banking group spread to other players in the system via commitments the banks have to each other, this can have immediate effects on the payment system. The Riksbank is therefore also looking at what exposures the banks have among themselves. The monitoring of the infrastructure focuses on the systems that are central to the functioning of the Swedish financial market. This mainly concerns VPC, the Stockholm Stock Exchange and BGC, as well as the system for large payments, RIX, which the Riksbank provides. The Riksbank has also chosen to work with issues related to practical crisis management. These have always been complicated issues. Financial crises can develop very quickly, not least as a result of the large flows of payments and the banks' often short-term financing. The increased integration may mean that it is possibly even more difficult now. The Riksbank has therefore built up an internal crisis organization with clear documentation of who does what if a crisis occurs, who should be contacted and informed, how the press should be informed and what legal consequences different measures have. An important element of the preparatory work is regular crisis exercises. Crisis management has also become an important international profile issue for Sweden. One reason is our experience, another is our basic view of the importance of transparency. The Riksbank leads Nordic and European working groups in this area. In the stability report published yesterday, we presented an article about the Riksbank's role as lender of last resort. It discusses the principles in which situations and under what conditions the Riksbank may provide support to troubled banks. 5 [10] Ker. Many other countries are not happy to talk openly about these issues for fear that it will lead to banks taking greater risks. The Riksbank, on the other hand, sees openness as a way to reduce increased risk-taking. With clear rules of the game, banks know better what applies. Future stability work A lot has happened to the Riksbank's stability work over the past seven years. Still, it's easy to identify areas we can get better at. The analysis of foreign borrowers will be improved. The Riksbank must gain a better understanding of how the banks manage their liquidity; their choice of funding sources and how it affects their resilience. The stability analysis must also be complemented by methods for sensitivity analyses, known as stress tests, of banks' resilience. In order to get further inspiration in the work to improve our analysis, the Riksbank has commissioned three external persons to evaluate the work on financial stability. The three people represent the international research front, the central bank world and the Swedish banking sector. The intention is that they, with joint efforts and from their respective perspectives, will evaluate quality and focus on the work we have built up. It is our intention to publish their report and then to invite a broad discussion on the further direction of our work. Finally, without prejudging their work, I would like to say a few words about the issues that I myself believe will have an increased weight in the future. A natural way to start such a discussion is to identify different drivers that affect financial development going forward. Three of the most important are: - increasing cross-border integration within Europe, - increasing banks' risk management, - increasing the focus on efficiency aspects. Consequences of European integration Perhaps what concerns us most clearly is the increased international dependence. Banking systems in Europe are still largely national. In some regions, however, integrated banking systems have begun to emerge. This development has perhaps been the furthest in the Nordic-Baltic region, but there are reasons to believe that integration will increase elsewhere as well. As a result, dependence between the countries' banking systems will also increase. For the Riksbank's stability work, it has several dimensions. Part of our work consists of promoting integration by influencing the design of the regulatory framework. Behind this lies the conviction that integration itself benefits growth. 6 [10] The current regulatory framework is not designed for an integrated European banking market that transcends national borders. Common legislation has taken only minor account of integration. In order to achieve a single market for financial services, the EU is working to put in place a regulatory framework for financial firms that is as common as possible within the Union. In this way, banks can compete on a level playing field and a common market with the most competitive companies can emerge. This is a well-intentioned ambition that the Riksbank supports. At the same time, it is important to avoid possible pitfalls that may hamper development. One danger is that the regulatory framework will become too detailed; that the strictest existing regulatory framework should be the starting point for harmonisation, instead of an open-ended discussion taking place. Integration also has an impact on day-to-day supervision and monitoring. At present, the principle of home country supervision applies, i.e. that the banks' legal home countries are responsible for the supervision of a bank branch. In the case of a subsidiary, the country established by the subsidiary is the country established by the subsidiary and is therefore responsible for supervision. However, it is still the legal home country of the parent company that is responsible for the supervision of the entire banking group. This is a solution that should be able to work, as long as the activities of banks outside their own country are rather modest. But what happens the day banks' branches in other countries become systemically important? What responsibility are the home countries willing to take for the financial stability of the countries where there are branches? And are the authorities of these latter countries prepared to entrust responsibility for a substantial part of the financial system to the home country of the parent bank? The fact that these are not completely abstract issues can be illustrated by the fact that Nordea, based in Sweden, is Finland's largest bank or that Swedish banks own most of the banking systems in the Baltics. The supervision of international groups thus appears to lead to coordination problems and duplication of effort. Overall, there does not appear to be a lack of incentives for the supervision of cross-border banks. Rather, the problem is that, in some cases, the regulatory framework prevents the most pressing countries from exercising supervision and that monitoring can therefore fall through the cracks. On the other hand, excessive generosity in who should be allowed to carry out supervision can lead to individual banks being subject to excessively burdensome supervision. This can result in integration and efficiency. Crisis management is more difficult to formalise than the other parts of the stability work. It can be perceived as sensitive and difficult to discuss in advance, as it is partly about the state's willingness to provide liquidity support to the financial sector. Often the dividing line is between the different views on whether this should be discussed openly between the countries that have experienced or not experienced a financial crisis. Those who have experience of a crisis are generally in favor of clarity in the process. It can therefore be difficult to draw up a clear template for how crises are to be handled in advance. How these problems will be handled is difficult to say today. There are two fundamentally different ways to go. One is to continue with cooperation through agreement. 7 [10] regulations, common principles and framework regulations. The second possible path is towards more supranational management. It is likely that a combination of these two paths will be needed. The important thing at this stage, however, is that the debate on these difficult issues gets under way, before we find ourselves in a situation where they must instead be resolved urgently. More advanced risk management Another factor likely to influence the supervisory and stability monitoring process going forward is the increased ability of banks to manage risks. One of the traditional tasks of banks is to be able to assess risks. Since the mid-1990s, there has been a marked change. The methods and possibilities for measuring credit risks have been refined in line with technological advances and new financial theory. At the same time, it has become possible to trade risks with more financial instruments in increasingly internationalized markets. All this has improved banks' ability to manage their risks. Banks  and not just the largest international banks  have invested in new risk management systems. The new capital adequacy framework, Basel II, which is currently being drafted, has further accelerated the process that had already begun. In Sweden, all the major banks are actively working on these issues, partly because it is expected to give rise to reduced capital needs. For the Riksbank, it is of course not the reduced need for capital per se that is interesting, but rather that the new rules better take into account the actual risk of different credits. The Financial Supervisory Authority has a central role here in ensuring that financial companies comply with the intentions of the Basel rules and not just their letter. This, in turn, should lead to better pricing of risk and thus a more efficient financial system. One problem that has come to be discussed in connection with the newer risk management methods and Basel II is whether these can reinforce fluctuations in the economy. Since the basic idea of Basel II is that the credit risk in lending should control how much capital a bank should hold, the banks' need for capital and thus the cost of credit can co-vary with the business cycle. As credit risk increases in a recession, banks need to hold more capital. The concern is that this could lead to credit crunches in downturns and credit expansions in upturns, which amplify the fluctuations of the business cycle. There is something to that criticism. Experience from previous business cycles tells us that it is when we approach the peak of a boom that the major credit risks are taken. However, the solution to these problems is not to oppose the new risk management methods or Basel II. They will contribute to greater financial stability. However, there is reason for banks to try to find ways of dealing with the possible effects of strengthening cyclical fluctuations. 8 [10] For economic development, it is important that credit and venture capital are available even in a recession  and perhaps to a somewhat lesser extent at the peak of a boom. The more advanced risk management methods have not only influenced banks' capital management, but also led to the creation of new financial instruments. Some examples of this are securitisation and credit derivatives. Banks can thus relinquish the credit risk that arises when they lend money by hedging themselves in the credit derivatives market or by simply selling the risk by securitising the loans. The credit risks in the economy can then be spread across more actors. This is fundamentally a positive development for financial stability and market efficiency. At the same time, authorities must closely monitor developments to understand where these credit risks are going. They do not disappear from the economy as they leave the banking sector, but arise in another form elsewhere, for example in insurance companies or mutual funds. Does the new ability to trade in risks also mean that banks will have a different focus on their operations? In doing so, will they try to reduce their large illiquid balance sheets by selling their loans or securitising their assets? And does this mean that they will thus no longer be able to be described as the riskiest economic institutions known to man? The US is already further ahead in this development, where market financing is significantly more important than in Sweden and Europe. What would a similar development, where today's more relationship-based lending is replaced by market financing, mean for the supply of credit over a business cycle in Sweden? Increased focus on efficiency aspects A third driver that most clearly affects the financial system is the increased focus on efficiency aspects. Let me touch briefly on this. The financial infrastructure has undergone improvements in recent years and thus in various ways become more secure and robust. Both BGC and VPC, for example, today have significantly safer settlement routines than before. All parts of the infrastructure have improved their continuity solutions, so that operations can be ensured even in more extreme events. As the most serious shortcomings have now been fixed, the focus has shifted towards how to increase efficiency within given security frameworks. There are significant socio-economic gains to be made from streamlining infrastructure. This applies not only to the central settlement systems, but perhaps even more so to different payment instruments. Increased automation and higher rates of electronic payments over payments with paper-based instruments and cash can lead to major savings for society at large. Even if it is only a few dollars or barely that per transaction, the total amount of the 9 [10] the sparing big because a modern economy generates a huge amount of payments. In recent years, the banks' operations have been very much about savings and efficiency improvements. From a government perspective, it is always important to see what the competitive conditions look like and balance these against efficiency drivers, such as economies of scale. It is also important to follow developments to ensure that risk levels do not increase again. In addition, the Riksbank has been and is an important player in the payment system. We must also continuously test this activity so that our way of working does not contribute to a less efficient development for the national economy as a whole. From what I have now said about the future work, it is hopefully clear that the financial markets are changing at a rapid pace and that the development is in many ways exciting. The Riksbank will continue to be a key player in this work in the future. It has felt natural to talk about these types of issues at a university. I hope that I may have even succeeded in inspiring some of you to get involved in this type of issue and contribute to further development. Thanks! 10 [10]

Title: Henry Ohlsson in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy
text: Henry Ohlsson in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2015-11-12 Speaker: Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament On Thursday, Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson will participate in this year's third hearing on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. Ingves: Sweden must relate to developments in the outside world Stefan Ingves begins the hearing by presenting the latest monetary policy decision from the end of October, when the Riksbank's Executive Board decided to expand purchases of government bonds, leave the repo rate unchanged at -0.35 percent and postpone a first rate hike six months ahead. Ingves points out how dependent the Swedish economy is on developments in the outside world. There is continued uncertainty about the strength of the global economy and monetary policy in the rest of the world. The low interest rate situation in Sweden has contributed to a relatively strong economy with stable GDP growth, falling unemployment and inflation rising since last year. Ingves points out that it is important to maintain the positive trend with low interest rates so that inflation continues to rise towards the target. At the same time, he stresses that the low interest rate environment can increase the risks associated with the housing market and high household indebtedness, and therefore underlines the importance of other policy areas addressing these risks in different ways. Ohlsson: Opportunities and challenges with increased immigration In his introduction, Henry Ohlsson focuses on the opportunities and challenges that increased immigration to Sweden entails. He believes that since a country's growth in the long term largely depends on how its population changes, the increased immigration is a positive and much-needed addition to the Swedish, aging population. But Ohlsson also points to the challenges that increased immigration entails: that it is difficult for vulnerable groups to enter the labor market and that housing construction needs to increase in order to meet the need for housing.

Title: The inflation target, the economic situation and the new economy
text: Hessius: Inflation target, cyclical situation and the new economy Date: 1999-12-01 Speaker: Deputy Governor Kerstin Hessius Location: NationalEkonomiska foreningen, Stockholm I would like to begin by thanking you for the invitation to come and speak at the meeting of the Economic Association and look forward to tonight's discussion. Sweden is still in its seventh year of inflation targeting since it was announced in early 1993. Several OECD countries have also been pursuing inflation targeting policies for several years. This means that today there is a rich source of experience to draw from. Tonight I was going to address challenges for monetary policy in an inflation targeting regime, mainly in view of Sweden's situation. How active should an independent central bank be in stabilising the economy? What kind of interaction between monetary and fiscal policy leads to favourable economic developments when monetary policy is geared towards an inflation target? This is, of course, a big issue, so I will confine myself to a few key aspects. Finally, I intend to say something about the 'new economy'. Stable conditions rather than stabilisation policies Stable conditions in the form of less variability in the real economy mean higher welfare for society as a whole. A key question is whether short-term stabilisation policies should be pursued more generally in order to seek to contribute to long-term high real growth. It is worth pointing out here that monetary and fiscal policy reacts with different rapidity to changing economic conditions. In principle, the Riksbank can change its key interest rate at any time to stimulate or tighten demand. At the same time, however, the greatest effect is expected to occur only in 1-2 years' time. This means that the design of monetary policy should primarily be long-term. Fiscal policy, on the other hand, can have major direct effects on the economy but, in its most important parts, can only be changed with some inertia. There is an administrative cost associated with, for example, changing tax rates and changing rules taking time to implement. This means that fiscal policy is difficult to adapt quickly to changing economic prospects. The conclusion is that although monetary policy can react immediately to a changed economic situation, neither monetary nor fiscal policy should aim to influence the economic situation in the short term, i.e. stabilization policies of a "fine-tuning nature". Instead, both monetary and fiscal policies should be designed in such a way as to create long-term stable conditions. The contribution of monetary policy to welfare is precisely to create as stable conditions as possible in the economy with inflation targeting policies. In the Riksbank Act, this is formulated so that the goal of the Riksbank's operations shall be to maintain a fixed monetary value and to promote a secure and efficient payment system. The role of fiscal policy should be, among other things, to design the tax system so that the best conditions for as high a potential output as possible are created. Both the changes in the government budget process such as the requirement for the surplus target in public savings over a business cycle work to create greater confidence in fiscal policy. The orientation of budgetary policy, like that of monetary policy, is of great importance for economic development. If the basic rules of the game are stable, the players in an economy dare to make long-term decisions. It would also be desirable for monetary and fiscal policy to interact in such a way as to dampen large variations in employment and growth, i.e. in order to reduce cyclical fluctuations around potential growth. As this can be difficult to achieve in practice, one question is how best to interact between fiscal and monetary policy within the framework of the inflation targeting regime. What happens in an inflation-targeting economy if fiscal policy takes no account whatsoever of the economic situation? What happens, for example, in a boom if fiscal policy is conducted in an overly expansionary direction? Should there not be a credible nominal anchor in the economy, e.g. in the form of an inflation target, demand increases further. This, in turn, leads to companies, especially in a situation where production is limited by bottlenecks, tending to raise their prices; in addition, workers would demand higher wages, which taken together would create a spiral of rising inflationary pressures, such as we experienced in the 1980s. The adjustment towards a higher price level may take place over a longer period, but will gradually set in motion processes that slow down growth. This is an expression of the time-honoured theory that it is not possible in the long term to increase the economy's productive capacity via short-term stimulus policies. What happens in this process if the central bank has an inflation target? With increased inflationary pressures in the economy, the central bank will tighten monetary policy so that the inflation target is not exceeded. The result of such a process would be an unfavourable policy mix. The fiscal stimulus is counterbalanced by monetary policy, which means that even the short-term positive effects of the stimulus will be smaller or even negative. In addition, if the fiscal stimulus is very strong, this could contribute to expectations of an increased risk that the inflation target cannot be maintained, which in that case leads to rising inflation expectations and higher risk premia on Swedish interest-bearing securities. This can also lead to increased uncertainty among households and businesses about both the evolution of government revenues and expenditure and the design of monetary policy. This can be costly for the economy if it means that investments are not carried out and that decisions on resource allocation become unnecessarily cautious. All in all, it will thus be costly to conduct an overly expansionary fiscal policy even when monetary policy is governed by an explicit inflation target. A good policy mix provides better conditions A better policy mix will arise if the stance of fiscal policy does not contribute to increasing inflation risk premia, which it can do by appearing sustainable in the long term. The surplus target in government savings is an exemplary example. Public confidence in economic policy can be read, among other things, in inflation expectations, which should not deviate significantly from the Riksbank's inflation target. When inflation expectations deviate from the longer-term target  up or down  this implies that monetary policy should be reoriented to steer expectations back towards the target. In this context, it is important to mention that a central bank with a high credibility for its inflation target often has more room for manoeuvre than one with a low credibility. For example, suppose that an economy where the credibility of the inflation target is high is subject to a positive cyclical disruption that leads to higher demand. Because inflation risk premia are low, workers do not need to demand extra high nominal pay to insure against unexpectedly high inflation. That's because it's expected that the central bank will tighten monetary policy. This, in turn, means that the the tightening required is likely to be less than that of a central bank that has not yet established its credibility. To discuss the Swedish situation more concretely, it can be said that macroeconomic conditions today are favorable: inflation is low, budget deficits have been turned into surpluses and growth prospects are good. However, economic policy is a continuous learning process and the successes of recent years should not be taken as a reason for structural problems to be solved. In the labour market, for example, structural rigidities remain; the tax burden remains high, which inevitably distorts incentives to work and save. As far as monetary policy is concerned, the credibility of the inflation targeting regime has hardly yet been tested in an economic upturn. What does this mean for how much and how often monetary policy should react to changing economic outlooks? This is, of course, an issue that the Executive Board continuously takes a position on and communicates its views on via inflation reports, minutes and speeches. What can be said more generally is that the need for action should depend on the outlook for domestic demand, on the rigour of fiscal policy and on external developments. In addition, inflation expectations play a central role as an overall indicator of inflationary pressures. In a situation of low inflation risk premia, an independent central bank with price stability objectives can also help to stabilise the cyclical cycle around potential growth. How far does this responsibility extend? The Riksbank's clarification on the target means that annual inflation measured by the CPI should normally be limited to 2 per cent with a tolerance range of 1 percentage point. In the event of a deviation from the target, inflation should normally be returned to the target over a 1-2 year horizon. However, in the event of a major deviation, caused, for example, by a significant external disturbance, there may be grounds for extending the target horizon in order to limit fluctuations in output and employment. In other words, in such circumstances, it may be too difficult or costly for monetary policy to quickly return inflation to its target. The "new economy" Let me now turn to another issue that is hotly debated in both the media and academic circles: the existence of a so-called 'new economy'. It is mainly to the American economy that the eyes are on this. Much seems to be accommodated within the concept. In this context, I define 'new economy' as an increase in the growth potential of the economy. In recent years, growth in the U.S. economy has surpassed most forecasts. Not only has the growth rate been historically high during this economic upturn, around 3.5% per annum on average since the end of 1991, but it has also been very stable and exceptionally long-lasting. At the same time, unemployment has fallen to 4 percent. Such low levels have not been seen since the 1960s. However, unlike previous booms, there has been no increase in inflation rates and the underlying inflation rate has more than halved since 1991, from over 4% to 2%. Public finances have improved sharply, from a deficit of 5% of GDP in 1991 to an expected surplus of around 1% this year. If you look at productivity per hour worked in the American economy, which is perhaps the best measure of how good a country's growth potential is in the short term, this has increased sharply, just over 2.5 percent on average since 1997. This compares with average productivity growth of around 1.5% over the period 1974-96. A large part of the improved labour productivity can be attributed to very high investments, so-called "capital deepening". Not least, large investments in computer equipment have been made. Although unemployment has continued to fall over the period, productivity growth has been impressively high. This is noteworthy given that new jobs have been created mainly in the services sector, which usually has a relatively lower increase in productivity than industry. Three main groups of reasons for the good American development can be distinguished: A major reason behind the upturn appears to be good economic policy. Since the early 1990s, fiscal policy has been set on achieving budgetary balance, and for some years now the budget has been balanced. To achieve this, taxes have been raised, spending has been reduced and the budget process tightened up. Monetary policy has focused on keeping inflation low and stable and has succeeded in averting both destabilising inflation and deflationary pressures early on. The policy mix of monetary and fiscal policy thus appears to have been favourable. A number of structural factors appear to have been important. Deregulation in many sectors and increased globalisation have intensified already fierce competition and increased pressure on the social partners, making the labour market more flexible and the workforce more mobile. Increased and more efficient use of new technology (IT) has increased productivity and the use of JIT (Just in Time Inventory Management) has improved the matching of supply and demand in the economy. The increased openness of the economy, including as a result of NAFTA and the GATT agreements, has meant that foreign trade has acted as a "shock absorber" for fluctuations in domestic demand. Finally, fortunate circumstances seem to have done their thing. With the end of the Cold War in the early 1990s, resources were freed up, mainly from the military sector, that could be used more productively in the private sector. Furthermore, both the Mexico crisis and the Asian crisis have been shocks from outside that have dampened some overheating tendencies and thus inflation, without leading the economy into recession. During crises, a "flight to quality" seems to have led to falling long-term interest rates, which has benefited stock prices and strengthened the dollar. Foreign investors have been willing to finance the U.S. current account deficits, which currently amount to about 4 percent of GDP. All in all, it seems likely that some increase in growth potential occurred in the US during the 1990s and that the propensity for inflation has decreased. However, how much is an open question. For example, the OECD has raised its estimate for potential growth rates to just over 3 percent. However, over the past three years, growth has averaged over 4%, which means that some of the factors discussed above are perceived to be temporary in nature and that growth is expected to slow down as these slow down. At the same time, during the very strong upturn in the US economy, significant imbalances have built up. For example, the current account deficit has never been as large as it is now, and consumption has recently grown faster than household income, which has brought the saving rate to a record low. Sooner or later, these imbalances will need to be corrected. However, a discussion of how this might happen is beyond what I've been meaning to talk about tonight. Are there traces of a "new economy" in Sweden? "Since Sweden switched from a fixed exchange rate to an inflation target, monetary policy has been designed to achieve the target and thereby create credibility. Monetary policy has succeeded in stabilising prices and long-term inflation expectations are currently close to the Riksbank's target of 2 per cent. The effects of a change in fiscal policy, which has meant, among other things, reforming the budget process and introducing a ceiling on central government expenditure, have been good. This is manifested, among other things, by the budget surpluses that are now being displayed. All in all, we have come a long way towards achieving macroeconomic stability and therefore appear to meet the requirement of a 'good economic policy', even if we have fulfilled this for a significantly shorter period of time than the UNITED STATES. "If you look at structural factors, on the other hand, perhaps our problems were also worse in the initial situation. The Swedish economy is less competitive than the American economy. For example, the Swedish price level, also adjusted for VAT differences, is between 15-20 percent higher on average than in the United States. A number of deregulations, which have long since been carried out in the United States, such as the liberalisation of the transport sector, have more recently been carried out in Sweden and there is much to suggest that we have not seen the full impact of this. However, competition in many markets is expected to increase in Sweden in the future as a result of, among other things, increased globalization and European integration. One area where very little has been done is the labour market, which, in comparison with the American one, is rigid and regulated. As far as the introduction of new technology is concerned, Sweden has embraced this to a greater extent than many other OECD countries. For example, we have the highest number of internet users per capita in the whole world. "The Swedish economy, like the American economy, is very open to the outside world and Sweden has a long tradition of free trade. This counteracts to some extent the trends towards restricting competition on the Swedish market. "On the other hand, we have not seen any clear signs of the impact of the new economy so far in the statistics. For example, Sweden does not show at all the strong investment development that has been in the US over the past four to six years. Furthermore, there are also no signs that labour productivity has increased particularly sharply, which seems to have been an important part of the strong US development. According to the Executive Board's assessment, which was reported in the Inflation Report 1999:3, the exchange between inflation and growth has improved somewhat, although uncertainty prevails over the order of magnitude. All in all, the Swedish economy appears to have undergone only partially the structural changes made by the US economy. It remains to be seen whether the "new economy" can have a further impact in Sweden.

Detta innebr att det idag finns en rik klla av erfarenheter att sa ur. Jag tnkte ikvll ta upp utmaningar fr penningpolitiken i en inflationsmlsregim, frmst med tanke p Sveriges situation. Hur aktiv br en sjlvstndig centralbank vara vad gller att stabilisera konjunkturen? Vilken form av samspel mellan penningoch finanspolitik leder till en gynnsam ekonomisk utveckling nr penningpolitiken inriktas mot ett inflationsml? Detta r givetvis en stor frga s jag tnker avgrnsa mig till ngra f centrala aspekter. Avslutningsvis har jag tnkt att sga ngot om den "nya ekonomin". Stabila frutsttningar snarare n stabiliseringspolitik Stabila frutsttningar i form av mindre variabilitet i den reala ekonomin innebr hgre vlfrd fr samhllet som helhet. En central frga r om kortsiktig stabiliseringspolitik mer allmnt br bedrivas fr att ska bidra till en lngsiktigt hg real tillvxt. Det r hr vrt att pongtera att penning- och finanspolitiken reagerar med olika snabbhet p frndrade ekonomiska frhllanden. Riksbanken kan i princip nr som helst ndra sin styrrnta fr att stimulera eller strama t efterfrgan. Samtidigt vntas dock den strsta effekten uppst frst p 1-2 rs sikt. Det innebr att penningpolitikens utformning frmst br vara lngsiktig. Finanspolitiken kan dremot f stora direkta effekter p ekonomin men kan i sina viktigaste delar endast ndras med viss trghet. Det finns en administrativ kostnad frknippad med att t.ex. ndra skattesatser och ndrade regler tar tid att genomfra. Detta innebr att finanspolitiken r svr att snabbt anpassa till ndrade ekonomiska utsikter. Slutsatsen r att ven om penningpolitiken omedelbart kan reagera p ett frndrat ekonomiskt lge br varken penning- eller finanspolitiken syfta till att kortsiktigt pverka konjunkturlget d.v.s. stabiliseringspolitik av "fine-tuningkaraktr". I stllet br svl penning- som finanspolitik utformas s att lngsiktiga stabila frutsttningar skapas. Penningpolitikens bidrag till vlfrden r just att med inflationsmlspolitik skapa s stabila frutsttningar som mjligt i ekonomin. I Riksbankslagen r detta formulerat s att mlet fr Riksbankens verksamhet ska vara att upprtthlla ett fast penningvrde och att frmja ett skert och effektivt betalningsvsende. Finanspolitikens roll borde bl. a. vara att utforma skattesystemet s att bsta frutsttningar fr en s hg potentiell produktion som mjligt skapas. Svl frndringarna i den statliga budgetprocessen som kravet p verskottsmlet i det offentliga sparandet ver en konjunkturcykel verkar fr att skapa ett strre frtroende fr finanspolitiken. Budgetpolitikens inriktning r, i likhet med penningpolitikens, av stor betydelse fr den ekonomiska utvecklingen. r de grundlggande spelreglerna stabila vgar aktrerna i en ekonomi fatta lngsiktiga beslut. Det vore i och fr sig ocks nskvrt att penningpolitiken och finanspolitiken samverkar p ett sdant stt att stora variationer i sysselsttning och tillvxt dmpas, d.v.s. i syfte att minska konjunktursvngningarna runt den potentiella tillvxten. Eftersom detta i praktiken kan vara svrt att stadkomma r en frga hur samspelet mellan finanspolitiken och penningpolitiken kan ske p bsta stt inom ramen fr inflationsmlsregimen. Vad hnder i en inflationsmlsekonomi om finanspolitiken inte tar ngra som helst hnsyn till konjunkturlget? Vad hnder t.ex. i en hgkonjunktur om finanspolitiken frs i en alltfr expansiv riktning? Skulle det inte finnas ett trovrdigt nominellt ankare i ekonomin, t.ex. i form av ett inflationsml, kar efterfrgan ytterligare. Detta leder i sin tur till att fretag, srskilt i ett lge dr produktionen begrnsas av flaskhalsar, tenderar att hja sina priser; drtill skulle arbetstagare krva hgre lner, vilket sammantaget skulle skapa en spiral med stigande inflationstryck, t.ex. som vi upplevde p 1980-talet. Anpassningen mot en hgre prisniv kan ske under en lngre period, men kommer gradvis att stta igng processer som bromsar tillvxten. Detta r ett uttryck fr den hvdvunna teorin att det inte p lng sikt gr att hja ekonomins produktionsfrmga via kortsiktig stimulanspolitik. Vad hnder i detta frlopp om centralbanken har ett inflationsml? Med ett kat inflationstryck i ekonomin kommer centralbanken strama t penningpolitiken fr att inte inflationsmlet ska verskridas. Resultatet av ett sdant frlopp skulle bli en ofrdelaktig policy-mix. Den finanspolitiska stimulansen motverkas av penningpolitiken, vilket leder till att ven de kortsiktigt positiva effekterna av stimulansen blir mindre eller rentav negativa. Om dessutom den finanspolitiska stimulansen r mycket kraftig skulle detta kunna bidra till frvntningar om kad risk fr att inflationsmlet inte kan upprtthllas, vilket i s fall leder till stigande inflationsfrvntningar och hgre riskpremier p svenska rntebrande papper. Detta kan ocks leda till kad oskerhet bland hushll och fretag om svl utvecklingen fr statliga intkter och utgifter som penningpolitikens utformning. Detta kan vara kostsamt fr ekonomin om det medfr att investeringar inte genomfrs och att beslut om resursallokering blir ondigt frsiktiga. Sammantaget blir det allts kostsamt att bedriva en alltfr expansiv finanspolitik ven nr penningpolitiken styrs av ett explicit inflationsml. En god policy-mix ger bttre frutsttningar En bttre policy-mix uppstr om finanspolitikens inriktning inte bidrar till att ka inflationsriskpremierna, vilket den kan gra genom att framst som lngsiktigt hllbar. verskottsmlet i det offentliga sparandet r ett fredmligt exempel. Allmnhetens frtroende fr den ekonomiska politiken kan bl. a. avlsas i inflationsfrvntningarna, som inte vsentligt br avvika frn Riksbankens inflationsml. Nr inflationsfrvntningarna avviker frn mlet p lngre sikt  uppt eller nedt  implicerar detta att penningpolitiken br lggas om fr att styra frvntningarna tillbaka mot mlet. I detta sammanhang r det viktigt att nmna att en centralbank med hg trovrdighet fr sitt inflationsml ofta har strre handlingsutrymme n en med lg trovrdighet. Anta t.ex. att en ekonomi dr trovrdigheten fr inflationsmlet r hg utstts fr en positiv konjunkturstrning som leder till hgre efterfrgan. Eftersom inflationsriskpremierna r lga behver inte arbetstagare krva extra hg nominell ln fr att frskra sig mot ovntat hg inflation. Det beror p att det frvntas att centralbanken kommer att strama t penningpolitiken. Detta innebr i sin tur att den tstramning som krvs sannolikt kan bli mindre n fr en centralbank som nnu inte etablerat sin trovrdighet. Fr att mer konkret diskutera den svenska situationen kan man sga att de makroekonomiska frutsttningarna idag r gynnsamma: inflationen r lg, budgetunderskott har vnts till verskott och tillvxtutsikterna r goda. Ekonomisk politik r dock en kontinuerlig lrprocess och de senaste rens framgngar ska inte tas som intkt fr att strukturproblemen r lsta. P arbetsmarknaden kvarstr t.ex. strukturella stelheter; skattetrycket r fortfarande hgt vilket oundvikligen snedvrider incitament till arbete och sparande. Vad gller penningpolitiken har trovrdigheten hos inflationsmlsregimen knappast nnu testats i en konjunkturuppgng. Vad innebr detta fr hur mycket och hur ofta penningpolitiken br reagera p ndrade ekonomiska utsikter? Detta r frsts en frga som direktionen lpande tar stllning till och kommunicerar sin syn p via inflationsrapporter, protokoll och tal. Vad man kan sga mer allmnt r att behovet av tgrder br bero p utsikterna fr den inhemska efterfrgan, p hur stram finanspolitiken r samt p omvrldsutvecklingen. Drtill har inflationsfrvntningar en central roll som en vergripande indikator p inflationstrycket. I en situation med lga inflationsriskpremier kan ven en sjlvstndig centralbank med prisstabilitetsml bidra till att stabilisera konjunkturen runt den potentiella tillvxten. Hur lngt strcker sig detta ansvar? Riksbankens frtydligande om mlet innebr att den rliga inflationen mtt med KPI normalt ska begrnsas till 2 procent med en toleransintervall om  1 procentenhet. Vid en avvikelse frn mlet ska inflationen normalt terfras till mlet p 1-2 rs sikt. Vid en strre avvikelse, som exempelvis orsakats av en betydande extern strning, kan det dock finnas skl att frlnga mlhorisonten fr att begrnsa fluktuationerna i produktion och sysselsttning. Med andra ord kan det under sdana omstndigheter vara alltfr svrt eller kostsamt fr penningpolitiken att snabbt terfra inflationen till mlet. Den "nya ekonomin" Lt mig nu ta upp en annan frga som diskuteras livligt i bde media och akademiska kretsar: frekomsten av en s.k. "ny ekonomi". Det r frmst mot den amerikanska ekonomin som blickarna riktas nr man talar om detta. Mycket frefaller kunna rymmas inom begreppet. I detta sammanhang definierar jag "ny ekonomi" som en kning av ekonomins tillvxtpotential. Under de senaste ren har tillvxten i amerikansk ekonomi vertrffat de flesta prognoser. Tillvxttakten har inte bara varit historiskt sett hg under denna konjunkturuppgng, omkring 3,5 procent per r i genomsnitt sedan i slutet av 1991, den har dessutom varit mycket stabil och osedvanligt lngvarig. Samtidigt har arbetslsheten fallit ned mot 4 procent. S lga niver har inte skdats sedan 1960talet. Till skillnad frn tidigare hgkonjunkturer har emellertid ingen kning av inflationstakten skett och den underliggande inflationstakten har mer n halverats sedan 1991, frn ver 4 till 2 procent. Statsfinanserna har kraftigt frbttrats, frn ett underskott p 5 procent av BNP 1991 till ett frvntat verskott p omkring 1 procent i r. Ser man till produktivitet per arbetad timme i det amerikanska nringslivet, som kanske r det bsta mttet fr hur god ett lands tillvxtpotential r p lite sikt, har denna kat kraftigt, drygt 2,5 procent i genomsnitt sedan 1997. Detta kan jmfras med en genomsnittlig produktivitetstillvxt p omkring 1,5 procent under perioden 1974-96. En stor del av den frbttrade arbetsproduktiviteten kan hnfras till mycket hga investeringar s.k. "capital deepening". Inte minst stora investeringar i datorutrustning har gjorts. Trots att arbetslsheten under perioden fortsatt att falla har produktivitetstillvxten varit imponerande hg. Detta r anmrkningsvrt med tanke p att nya arbetstillfllen frmst skapats inom tjnstesektorn, vilken vanligtvis har en relativt lgre produktivitetskning n industrin. Tre huvudgrupper av orsaker till den goda amerikanska utvecklingen kan urskiljas: En viktig orsak bakom uppgngen frefaller vara god ekonomisk politik. Finanspolitiken har sedan i brjan av 1990-talet varit instlld p att uppn budgetbalans, och sedan ngot r tillbaka r budgeten balanserad. Fr att n detta har skatter hjts, utgifter minskats och budgetprocessen stramats upp. Penningpolitiken har inriktats p att hlla inflationen lg och stabil och har lyckats med att avvrja bde destabiliserande inflations- och deflationstryck tidigt. Policymixen av penning- och finanspolitik framstr allts som om den varit gynnsam. En mngd strukturella faktorer frefaller ha varit viktiga. Avregleringar inom mnga sektorer och den kade globaliseringen har skrpt en redan hrd konkurrens och kat trycket p arbetsmarknadens parter, vilket gjort arbetsmarknaden mer flexibel och arbetskraften mer lttrrlig. kad och mer effektiv anvndning av ny teknologi (IT) har hjt produktiviteten och anvndandet av JIT (Just in Time Inventory Management) har gjort att matchningen av utbud och efterfrgan i ekonomin har blivit bttre. Den kade ppenheten i ekonomin, bl.a. som en fljd av NAFTA och GATT-avtalen, har gjort att utrikeshandeln har fungerat som en "chockabsorberare" fr fluktuationer i inhemsk efterfrgan. Slutligen verkar lyckosamma omstndigheter gjort sitt. Med det kalla krigets slut i brjan av 1990-talet frigjordes resurser, frmst frn militrsektorn, som kunde anvndas mer produktivt i den privata sektorn. Vidare har svl Mexikokrisen som Asienkrisen varit chocker utifrn som dmpat vissa verhettningstendenser och drmed inflationen, utan att fr den skull leda in ekonomin i recession. Under kriser tycks en "flykt till kvalit" ha lett till fallande lngrntor vilket gynnat brskurserna och strkt dollarn. Utlndska investerare har varit villiga att finansiera de amerikanska bytesbalansunderskotten, som fr nrvarande uppgr till ca 4 procent av BNP. Sammantaget verkar det troligt att en viss hjning av tillvxtpotentialen skett i USA under 1990-talet och att inflationsbengenheten har minskat. Hur mycket r emellertid en ppen frga. OECD har exempelvis hjt sitt estimat fr potentiell tillvxttakt till strax ver 3 procent. Tillvxten har dock under de tre senaste ren uppgtt till ver 4 procent i genomsnitt, vilket innebr att vissa av de faktorer som diskuterats ovan uppfattas vara av temporr karaktr och att tillvxten frvntas att mattas i takt med att dessa klingar av. Under den mycket starka uppgngen i amerikansk ekonomi har det samtidigt byggts upp betydande obalanser. Bl.a. har underskottet i bytesbalansen aldrig varit s stort som nu och konsumtionen har under den senaste tiden kat snabbare n hushllens inkomster vilket gjort att sparkvoten blivit rekordlg. Frr eller senare kommer dessa obalanser att behva korrigeras. En diskussion kring hur detta kan komma att ske ligger emellertid utanfr vad jag har tnkt att prata om ikvll. Finns det spr av en "ny ekonomi" i Sverige? - Sedan Sverige vergick frn fast vxelkurs till ett inflationsml, har penningpolitiken utformats fr att n mlet och drigenom skapa trovrdighet. Penningpolitiken har lyckats att stabilisera priserna och de lngsiktiga inflationsfrvntningarna ligger i dagslget nra Riksbankens ml p 2 procent. Effekterna av att finanspolitiken har lagts om, vilket bl.a. inneburit att budgetprocessen reformerats och att ett tak fr statens utgifter har infrts, har varit goda. Detta manifesteras bl.a. av de budgetverskott som nu uppvisas. Sammantaget har vi kommit en god bit p vg att uppn makroekonomisk stabilitet och frefaller drfr uppfylla kravet p en "god ekonomisk politik" ven om vi uppfyllt detta under en vsentlig kortare tid n USA. - Ser man  andra sidan till strukturella faktorer var kanske vra problem ocks vrre i utgngslget. Den svenska ekonomin r mindre konkurrensutsatt n den amerikanska. Exempelvis r den svenska prisnivn, ven rensad fr momsskillnader, mellan 15-20 procent hgre i genomsnitt n i USA. En mngd avregleringar, som fr lnge sedan genomfrts i USA, ssom exempelvis avregleringen av transportsektorn, har mer nyligen genomfrts i Sverige och mycket talar fr att vi inte sett det fulla genomslaget av detta. Konkurrensen p mnga marknader frvntas dock framgent ka i Sverige som en fljd av bl.a. den kade globaliseringen och Europaintegrationen. Ett omrde dr mycket lite gjorts r arbetsmarknaden som i jmfrelse med den amerikanska r stel och reglerad. - Vad betrffar infrande av ny teknologi har Sverige tagit till sig denna i hgre utstrckning n mnga andra OECD-lnder. Exempelvis har vi flest antal internetanvndare per capita i hela vrlden. - Den svenska ekonomin r, liksom den amerikanska, mycket ppen mot omvrlden och Sverige har en lng tradition av frihandel. Detta motverkar i viss mn tendenserna till begrnsning av konkurrensen p den svenska marknaden. - Vi har  andra sidan inte hittills i statistiken sett ngra tydliga tecken p den nya ekonomins genomslag. Exempelvis uppvisar inte Sverige alls den starka investeringsutveckling som varit i USA under de senaste fyra till sex ren. Vidare finns inte heller tecken p att arbetsproduktiviteten kat speciellt kraftigt, vilket frefaller ha varit en viktig del i den starka amerikanska utvecklingen. Enligt Direktionens bedmning, som redovisades i inflationsrapport 1999:3, har utvxlingen mellan inflation och tillvxt frbttrats ngot ven om oskerhet rder ver storleksordningen. Sammantaget frefaller den svenska ekonomin endast delvis genomgtt de strukturella frndringar som den amerikanska ekonomin gjort. Det terstr att se om den "nya ekonomin" kan f ytterligare genomslag i Sverige. Title: More balanced risk picture in inflationary pressures
text: Hessius: More balanced risk picture in inflationary pressures Date: 2000-03-14 Speaker: Deputy Governor Kerstin Hessius Location: Controller Congress 2000 In light of the 0.5 percentage point rate hike by the Riksbank in February, which aimed to create a good basis for continued favourable economic development with stable prices, high growth and increased employment, I currently believe that the risk picture with regard to inflationary pressures is more balanced." Kerstin Hessius said this on Tuesday in connection with a debate on growth at Controller Congress 2000. She further pointed out, among other things, that: "At present, the growth outlook in Sweden is robust and during an economic upturn, monetary policy must gradually be conducted in a less expansionary direction, but it is far from obvious at what pace we must move forward." "There is reason to wonder if we still do not see certain signs of the so-called new economy in Sweden, at least this is indicated by the fact that both productivity and investment picked up in the latter part of last year," kerstin Hessius said. "The recent economic data for Sweden confirms the picture that growth is stronger than we assessed in the December inflation report. Last year, GDP rose by as much as 3.8 per cent, while the pace of price growth has been subdued." "Growth is generated when the players in an economy dare to invest and consume. It occurs when the risks decrease in relation to the expected return. The most important long-term contribution of monetary policy to growth is to lower inflation risks in the economy by maintaining stable prices," said Kerstin Hessius.

Det sade Kerstin Hessius p tisdagen i samband med en debatt om tillvxt p Controller Congress 2000. Hon framhll vidare bland annat att: "I nulget r tillvxtutsikterna i Sverige robusta och under en konjunkturuppgng mste penningpolitiken gradvis fras i mindre expansiv riktning, men det r lngt ifrn sjlvklart i vilken takt vi mste g fram." "Det finns anledning att fundera ver om vi nd inte ser vissa tecken p den s.k. nya ekonomin i Sverige, tminstone indikeras detta genom att svl produktiviteten som investeringarna tog fart under senare delen av frra ret", sade Kerstin Hessius. "Den senaste tidens ekonomiska data fr Sverige bekrftar bilden av att tillvxten r starkare n vad vi bedmde i inflationsrapporten i december. Under frra ret steg BNP med hela 3,8 procent, samtidigt som priskningstakten har varit dmpad." "Tillvxt genereras nr aktrerna i en ekonomi vgar investera och konsumera. Det intrffar nr riskerna minskar i frhllande till den frvntade avkastningen. Penningpolitikens viktigaste lngsiktiga bidrag till tillvxten r att snka inflationsriskerna i ekonomin genom att upprtthlla stabila priser", sade Kerstin Hessius.
