Title: How does Sweden best prepare for EMU?
text: How does Sweden best prepare for EMU? Date: 1999-04-21 Speaker: Second Deputy Governor Eva Srejber Location: Finansforum A short answer to the question posed by the organizers for today's discussion is from my starting point: firstly, by keeping the economy in order and, secondly, maintaining a good readiness to act for the legal and practical possibilities of changing currency units in Sweden. I will be happy to elaborate on the answer, but I would like to emphasise at the outset that there is, of course, a big difference between these two kinds of conditions; the requirement for order in the economy applies regardless of whether Sweden participates in EMU or not, while the other preparations depend on the timetable that will apply for a possible Swedish entry into EMU. Today we do not know anything definite about this timetable. Certainly, the continued political discussion about Sweden and EMU will also be affected by what is happening in the other EU countries that are now outside the currency union. The direct influence on Swedish public opinion from Greek entry into EMU may not be so great, but Greece may be first in line for an enlargement of monetary union by seeking to participate from 1 January 2001. More closely, it can be noted that various opinion polls from Denmark have for a number of months indicated that there has been a shift in favour of a reassessment of the Danish opt-out. In the United Kingdom, the government has taken a clearer position and even put forward a transitional plan for the introduction of the euro, albeit without setting a date for when it can be put into effect. It is not my role to evaluate political developments, but I would mostly like to remind you of what is happening in other countries and that it may quite soon make the issue hotter in Sweden as well. So let me quickly go to how I see the Swedish conditions. At the start of emu preparations, there was a clear focus on the entry conditions set out in the Treaty on macroeconomic stability for a country to participate in monetary union. In the debate, however, the underlying idea that sound public finances and stable prices are a prerequisite for sustainable economic growth was often lost. Instead, it was often portrayed as EMU's "fault" that public subsidies had to be cut and taxes raised, in order to meet the 3% limit for the general government deficit. When the Stability and Growth Pact was subsequently decided, it became clearer to everyone that it would not be enough to have public finances in order at a given moment, but that this is a requirement that applies permanently. The most important element of the Pact is not, in principle, the ban on exceeding the 3% limit in any single year, but the requirement for public finances to be in balance or to lead to surpluses in the medium term. If public debt can be kept under control in a more sustainable perspective, credibility will also be strengthened to enable monetary policy to deliver price stability at low interest rates. The full potential for balanced economic growth can then be further developed if macroeconomic stability is followed up with reforms that improve the functioning of European economies. The rules of the Stability Pact therefore apply to all EU countries, both those participating in EMU and those outside. The Stability Pact's requirement for a balance or surplus over a business cycle has also another point, namely that individual countries are given a space to let the automatic stabilisers work to meet normal weakenings in the economy. In order for this to be exploited, countries must ensure that they are in a good starting position when growth is good. However, despite fairly decent economic growth in recent years, deficits in several EU countries have remained embarrassingly large, increasing vulnerability. Fiscal policy may have to be tightened at a time when growth is slowing down, which is both economically and politically costly to implement. Thus, in several countries, efforts to consolidate public finances remain to be stepped up. However, it should be said shortly that this does not primarily apply to Sweden at present. The Swedish Government's stated objective of a budget surplus of 2% of GDP in the medium term is among the more ambitious in the EU and also enjoys credibility in that there is actually now a surplus. In the financial markets, however, there is always some uncertainty about where the political decision-making process is heading and whether the objective will also be achieved in the long term. Sweden's history of sound government finances has not yet been so long, and it is difficult to assess whether the Swedish state budget has become less sensitive to economic cycles than in the past. Reassuring safety margins are therefore of value, especially in view of the fact that public debt remains relatively high. In addition, with the large share that the public sector has in Sweden, future pension and health care expenses may be more difficult to manage with us than in many other countries. Although the demographic development in Sweden is rather less unfavorable than in other countries, we therefore have a greater "burden of proof" in the initial situation. The objectives for fiscal development are thus the same regardless of whether Sweden participates in the currency union or not. The same applies to monetary policy, which in both cases should have price stability over the medium term as its overarching objective. The European Central Bank (ECB) has chosen a slightly different concept from the Riksbank for its quantification of what it means by price stability, but in all material respects the objectives are consistent. While, as is well known, the Riksbank aims to try to keep the increase in the consumer price index at 2% per annum, the ECB draws on the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) for the euro area and sets a target of keeping the annual rate of increase below 2%. Although the ECB has not set a lower limit on the rate of price increase, it is intended to be positive, i.e. to avoid deflation or falling consumer prices. If one looks at the historical development of the two index series HICP and CPI in Sweden, one finds that the annual deviations are small and that in the long run there is no systematic difference. The Riksbank is studying these technicalities carefully and may consider switching to the HICP once the Swedish CPI investigation is complete and when the HICP is fully developed within the EU, which is not yet the case. The Riksbank's target level is thus consistent with what the ECB has set as the highest rate of price rise. The extent to which systematic divergences may arise in the future will depend mainly on what the ECB will focus on in practice and where expectations of price rise rates in the euro area will actually end up. Should it turn out that the ECB aims to keep inflation well below 2 percent per year, the Riksbank will probably have to take this into account in its future monetary policy. And if Sweden enters monetary union, we will of course be covered by the ECB's objectives, but I do not foresee that there will be any decisive differences in terms of monetary policy. The fact that the objectives of monetary policy in Sweden and the euro area are equivalent does not, of course, mean that monetary policy must at all times be identical, as long as Sweden is outside the currency union. The ECB is responsible for price stability in the euro area as a whole, the Riksbank for it in Sweden. Depending on differences in the cyclical situation and other factors relevant to inflationary pressures, both the level and changes in interest rates may differ. We got an illustration of this at the end of March when the Riksbank lowered the repo rate to 2.90 percent while the ECB remained at 3.0 percent, and when the ECB then lowered to 2.5 percent, the Riksbank did not follow suit. The Riksbank takes its decisions independently and does not need to consult the ECB before: such decisions; the consultation mechanism in place between the ECB and the outside central banks takes into account the long-term objectives and the assessments of the general requirements this imposes on actual policies. However, the need to be able to conduct a different monetary policy in Sweden for economic reasons should not be exaggerated, because we are not fundamentally out of step with economic developments in the euro area today. On those occasions in the past when we have had a deviant economic development in Sweden, it has largely been due to what today often appears to be mistakes through no fault of our own in economic policy rather than on fundamental differences in the structure of business compared to most other European countries. Although similar requirements are thus imposed on economic policy whether Sweden participates in EMU or not, the Riksbank believes that there is added value for the country in actually participating. The Riksbank developed its view on this point in its response to the so-called 'Green Paper'. The Calmfors investigation in the spring of 1997. According to the Riksbank's assessment, this brings benefits primarily in terms of welfare development and the Swedish influence on development within the EU. Waiting and seeing does not diminish the demands for stabilisation policies and the need for structural reforms. If Sweden applies to participate in monetary union, the Commission and the ECB will examine to what extent we meet the Treaty convergence criteria for the final decision taken at the highest political level, by the EU Heads of State or Government. If the development and direction of economic policy that I have described stands, there is no reason to fear that the outcome of that review will be negative for Sweden. With regard to the budgetary position or the convergence of inflation rates and long-term interest rates, we currently clearly meet the set criteria. The last criterion, which has to do with exchange rate stability, was, of course, invoked a year ago as the main formal justification for Sweden not being found to meet the necessary conditions for participating in monetary union from the outset. However, the Treaty is not easy to interpret on this point. The explanatory statement formulated on the exchange rate criterion in spring 1998 is characterised, in eu terms, by a 'constructive ambiguity', which leaves several possibilities open for the future. Countries that had not participated in the ERM for two years were accepted as participants in the monetary union, and currencies with greater volatility than the Swedish krona were accepted. Moreover, since then, the ERM has been replaced by ERM2, which is constructed differently from the multilateral network of central rates in the old ERM and which is not mentioned at all in the Treaty. The decision as to whether a country qualifies for participation in monetary union is thus the result of a political balance. The central banks' contribution to this decision consists of a basis that reports on actual developments. Without interfering in the political test that is finally to take place, I dare to believe that if sweden has the political will to participate in monetary union, if economic policy continues to be geared towards stability and if the krona's exchange rate against the euro is at a reasonable level, the other EU countries will also want us involved. Let me now mention something about more practical preparations for a possible Swedish accession to the euro area. The Riksdag decision of November 1997 includes that the door should be kept open for later Swedish EMU entry. The greatest possible freedom of action shall be maintained on the basis of a preserved position of economic strength. The Government Offices have an organisation to monitor how readiness to act is maintained in different parts of society. For its part, the Riksbank maintains such preparedness that we expect a maximum of one year from the time the Riksdag possibly decides on Swedish participation until we have the necessary functions in place to be able to participate in the common monetary policy and other parts of central bank cooperation. However, this also requires some further adaptations to the legislation that we do not control ourselves. Among the more time-consuming preparations is the capacity to produce euro banknotes and coins with the high security standards to be applied; Therefore, the Riksbank has participated in the development work carried out by the ECB and, among other things, commissioned limited-scale test printing of the banknotes. The Riksbank also has a special responsibility for coordinating the financial sector's EMU preparations, and we have described in several reports in recent years the consequences of the introduction of the euro for Sweden outside the currency union and started taking stock of what changes would be required if we are to participate fully. As I stated at the beginning, the preparatory work regarding the necessary changes in various sectors in Sweden is still taking place under great uncertainty about what the timetable for possible Swedish participation in monetary union looks like. This is a cost that is inevitable for us to live up to the Riksdag decision on freedom of action. The Riksbank's one-year preparatory ambition needs to be put into context in terms of the political process, and without being unnecessarily speculative, I think one can have a hypothesis about how the signals that have emerged so far can be translated into a scenario. On the basis that there will be an extraordinary Social Democratic party congress in about a year's time, and then additional time is required for the broader popular support and for the political and legal preparation of the issue within Sweden and within the EU, I believe that Swedish participation from 1 January 2002 is a possibility. But of course, it could be later - or maybe not at all for the foreseeable future. In any case, 1 January 2002 is the time when the eleven countries of the first wave of EMU take the final step in the transition process, exchanging the notes and coins of the respective national currency units for euro notes and coins. Swedish financial firms and institutions have so far done considerable work to adapt to the introduction of the euro. This has meant that a number of financial and payment intermediation services are now offered in euros on the Swedish market as well. But the euro has of course remained a foreign currency for Swedish players, and the new handling procedures have been introduced in parallel with those for other foreign currencies. There is also a need to be able to deal for some time still with the eleven national currency units that have been absorbed into the euro, even though they have disappeared from some types of transactions. Each financial company determines based on its commercial considerations what types of services it wants to offer its customers. However, entry into monetary union would mean a completely different organisational environment for financial firms, both in that the exchange rate between the krona and the euro would then be irrevocably fixed and in that there would then be a timetable for replacing the krona with the euro in a legal and practical sense. Investment decisions regarding systems and strategies could then be made with a much higher degree of certainty than before. Today, it cannot be judged for sure whether Sweden could also exchange banknotes and coins at the same time and thus carry out the entire currency reform as a 'big bang', but so much can be said that the administrative consequences in that case would be significantly more extensive by affecting the entire cash management system in society. To summarize: The best way for Sweden to prepare for EMU is to ensure sound public finances, good price stability and structural reforms. It is, in fact, a good way of preparing for life outside EMU as well, but participation in monetary union can increase the return on such a policy. The greatest possible freedom of action in the face of a political position on the emu issue also presupposes that we continue the practical preparations for the introduction of the euro.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Hur frbereder Sverige sig bst fr EMU? Datum: 1999-04-21 Talare: Andre vice riksbankschef Eva Srejber Plats: Finansforum Ett kort svar p den frga som arrangrerna stller fr dagens diskussion r frn min utgngspunkt: genom att fr det frsta hlla ekonomin i ordning och fr det andra upprtthlla en god handlingsberedskap fr de legala och praktiska mjligheterna att byta valutaenhet i Sverige. Jag ska grna utveckla svaret, men vill redan frn brjan understryka att det naturligtvis r en stor skillnad mellan dessa bda slags villkor; kravet p ordning i ekonomin gller oavsett om Sverige deltar i EMU eller inte, medan de andra frberedelserna beror p vilken tidtabell som kommer att glla fr ett eventuellt svenskt intrde i EMU. Om denna tidtabell vet vi idag inte ngot bestmt. Skert kommer den fortsatta politiska diskussionen om Sverige och EMU ocks att pverkas av vad som sker i de andra EU-lnder som nu str utanfr valutaunionen. Det direkta inflytandet p den svenska opinionen frn ett grekiskt intrde i EMU r kanske inte s stort, men Grekland kan komma frst i kn fr en utvidgning av valutaunionen i och med att man efterstrvar att kunna delta frn den 1 januari 2001. Mera nraliggande kan man notera att olika opinionsunderskningar frn Danmark sedan ett antal mnader tyder p att det skett en frskjutning till frmn fr en omprvning av det danska undantaget. I Storbritannien har regeringen tagit tydligare stllning och t.o.m. lagt fram en vergngsplan fr att infra euron, om n utan att ange datum fr nr den kan sttas i verket. Det r inte min roll att vrdera den politiska utvecklingen, utan jag vill mest erinra om vad som sker i andra lnder och att det ganska snart kan gra frgan hetare ocks i Sverige. S lt mig raskt g till hur jag ser p de svenska frutsttningarna. Nr EMU-frberedelserna brjade skedde en tydlig fokusering p de intrdesvillkor som frdraget anger om den makroekonomiska stabiliteten fr att ett land skulle f delta i valutaunionen. I debatten frsvann dock ofta den bakomliggande tanken att sunda offentliga finanser och stabila priser r en frutsttning fr en hllbar ekonomisk tillvxt. I stllet framstlldes det ofta som EMU:s "fel" att offentliga bidrag mste skras ned och skatter hjas, fr att klara 3-procentsgrnsen fr underskottet i den offentliga sektorns finanser. Nr stabilitets- och tillvxtpakten sedermera beslutades blev det tydligare fr envar att det inte skulle rcka med att ha ordning i de offentliga finanserna i ett givet gonblick utan att detta r ett krav som gller varaktigt. Det viktigaste inslaget i pakten r nmligen inte frbudet, i princip, mot att verskrida 3-procentsgrnsen ngot enskilt r utan kravet p att de offentliga finanserna ska vara i balans eller leda till verskott p medellng sikt. Om den offentliga skuldsttningen kan hllas under kontroll i ett mera varaktigt perspektiv, strks trovrdigheten ocks till att penningpolitiken kan leverera prisstabilitet till lg rnta. Den fulla potentialen fr en balanserad ekonomisk tillvxt kan sedan vidareutvecklas om den makroekonomiska stabiliteten fljs upp med reformer som frbttrar de europeiska ekonomiernas funktionsstt. Stabilitetspaktens regler gller drfr alla EU-lnder, bde de som deltar i EMU och de som str utanfr. Stabilitetspaktens krav p balans eller verskott ver en konjunkturcykel har ocks en annan pong, nmligen att enskilda lnder fr ett utrymme att lta de automatiska stabilisatorerna verka fr att mta normala frsvagningar i konjunkturen. Fr att detta ska kunna utnyttjas mste lnderna se till att skaffa sig ett gott utgngslge nr tillvxten r god. Trots en ganska hygglig ekonomisk tillvxt de senaste ren har underskotten i flera EU-lnder dock frblivit besvrande stora, vilket kar srbarheten. Finanspolitiken mste kanske stramas t i ett lge nr tillvxten viker, vilket bde r samhllsekonomiskt och politiskt kostsamt att genomfra. I flera lnder terstr det allts att intensifiera anstrngningarna att konsolidera de offentliga finanserna. Dock ska strax sgas att detta i nulget inte i frsta hand gller Sverige. Den svenska regeringens fastlagda mlsttning om ett budgetverskott p 2 procent av BNP p medellng sikt tillhr de mer ambitisa inom EU och tnjuter ocks en trovrdighet genom att det faktiskt nu freligger ett verskott. P de finansiella marknaderna finns det dock alltid en viss oskerhet om vart den politiska beslutsprocessen r p vg och om mlet ocks kommer att infrias p sikt. Sveriges historia med sunda statsfinanser har ju nnu inte hunnit bli s lng, och det r svrt att bedma om den svenska statsbudgeten blivit mindre konjunkturknslig n i det frflutna. Betryggande skerhetsmarginaler r drfr av vrde, srskilt mot bakgrund av att statsskulden fortfarande r relativt stor. Med den stora andel som den offentliga sektorn har i Sverige kan dessutom framtida pensions- och hlsovrdsutgifter bli svrare att hantera hos oss n i mnga andra lnder. ven om den demografiska utvecklingen i Sverige snarast r mindre ogynnsam n i andra lnder har vi drfr en strre "bevisbrda" i utgngslget. Mlen fr den finanspolitiska utvecklingen r allts desamma oavsett om Sverige deltar i valutaunionen eller inte. Detsamma gller penningpolitiken som i bda fallen ska ha prisstabilitet p medellng sikt som vergripande ml. Europeiska centralbanken (ECB) har valt ett ngot annat begrepp n Riksbanken fr sin kvantifiering av vad man menar med prisstabilitet, men i allt vsentligt r mlen verensstmmande. Medan Riksbanken som bekant har som ml att ska hlla kningen i konsumentprisindex p 2 procent per r, utgr ECB frn det harmoniserade konsumentprisindexet HIKP fr euroomrdet och anger som ml att den rliga kningstakten ska hlla sig under 2 procent. ven om ECB inte angivit ngon undre grns fr priskningstakten, r avsikten att den ska vara positiv, dvs. att deflation eller fallande konsumentpriser ska undvikas. Om man ser till den historiska utvecklingen av de bda indexserierna HIKP och KPI i Sverige, finner man att de rliga avvikelserna r sm och att det p sikt inte freligger ngon systematisk skillnad. Riksbanken studerar dessa teknikaliteter noga och kan komma att vervga att g ver till HIKP nr vl den svenska KPI-utredningen r klar och nr HIKP utvecklats frdigt inom EU, vilket nnu inte r fallet. Riksbankens mlniv r allts frenlig med vad ECB angivit som hgsta prisstegringstakt. I vad mn det kan uppkomma systematiska skillnader framver beror frmst p vad ECB kommer att inrikta sig p i praktiken och var frvntningarna om prisstegringstakten inom euroomrdet faktiskt kommer att hamna. Skulle det visa sig att ECB siktar p att hlla inflationen klart under 2 procent per r, mste Riksbanken sannolikt beakta det i sin framtida penningpolitik. Och om Sverige gr in i valutaunionen, kommer vi naturligtvis att omfattas av ECB:s ml, men jag frutser allts inte att det kommer att innebra ngra avgrande skillnader nr det gller penningpolitiken. Att mlen fr penningpolitiken i Sverige och euroomrdet r likvrdiga, betyder naturligtvis inte att penningpolitiken i varje gonblick mste vara identisk, s lnge som Sverige str utanfr valutaunionen. ECB har ansvar fr prisstabiliteten i euroomrdet som helhet, Riksbanken fr den i Sverige. Beroende p skillnader i konjunkturlge och andra faktorer av betydelse fr inflationstrycket kan bde nivn och frndringarna i rntelget avvika. Vi fick en illustration till det i slutet av mars nr Riksbanken snkte reporntan till 2,90 procent medan ECB lg kvar p 3,0 procent, och nr ECB sedan snkte till 2,5 procent fljde Riksbanken inte efter. Riksbanken fattar sina beslut sjlvstndigt och behver inte samrda med ECB infr sdana beslut; den samrdsmekanism som finns mellan ECB och de utanfrstende centralbankerna tar fasta p de lngsiktiga mlen och bedmningarna av vilka krav detta allmnt sett stller p den faktiska politiken. Behovet av att av konjunkturskl kunna fra en annorlunda penningpolitik i Sverige ska emellertid inte verdrivas, ty vi r inte fundamentalt ur fas med konjunkturutvecklingen i euroomrdet idag. Vid de tillfllen i det frflutna d vi haft en avvikande ekonomisk utveckling i Sverige har det i stor utstrckning berott p vad som idag mnga gnger framstr som misstag av egen frskyllan i den ekonomiska politiken snarare n p grundlggande skillnader i nringslivets struktur jmfrt med flertalet vriga europeiska lnder. ven om det slunda stlls likartade krav p den ekonomiska politiken om Sverige deltar i EMU eller inte, anser Riksbanken att det finns ett mervrde fr landet av att faktiskt delta. Riksbanken utvecklade sin uppfattning p den punkten i sitt remissvar p den s.k. Calmfors-utredningen vren 1997. Enligt Riksbankens bedmning medfr det frdelar frmst vad gller vlfrdsutvecklingen och det svenska inflytandet p utvecklingen inom EU. Att vnta och se minskar inte kraven p stabiliseringspolitiken och behoven av strukturella reformer. Om Sverige ansker om att f delta i valutaunionen, ska kommissionen och ECB granska i vad mn vi uppfyller frdragets konvergenskriterier infr det slutliga beslutet som tas p hgsta politiska niv, av EU:s stats- och regeringschefer. Om den utveckling och inriktning av den ekonomiska politiken som jag beskrivit str sig, finns det inte anledning att befara att utfallet av den granskningen blir negativt fr Sveriges del. Nr det gller lget i de offentliga finanserna eller konvergensen i inflationstakt och lnga rntor uppfyller vi f.n. klart de uppsatta kriterierna. Det sista kriteriet, som har med vxelkursstabiliteten att gra beropades ju fr ett r sedan som den frmsta formella motiveringen till att Sverige inte befanns uppfylla de ndvndiga villkoren fr att delta i valutaunionen frn starten. Frdraget r dock inte alldeles ltt att tolka p denna punkt. Den motivering som formulerades om vxelkurskriteriet vren 1998 knnetecknas p EU-manr av en "konstruktiv tvetydighet", som lmnar flera mjligheter ppna fr framtiden. Lnder som inte deltagit i vxelkursmekanismen ERM i tv r godtogs som deltagare i valutaunionen, och valutor med strre volatilitet n den svenska kronan accepterades. Sedan dess har ERM dessutom avlsts av ERM2, som r konstruerat p ett annat stt n det multilaterala ntverket av centralkurser i det gamla ERM och som ver huvud taget inte nmns i frdraget. Beslutet om huruvida ett land kvalificerar fr deltagande i valutaunionen blir allts resultatet av en politisk avvgning. Centralbankernas bidrag infr detta beslut bestr av ett underlag som redovisar den faktiska utvecklingen. Utan att jag blandar mig i den politiska prvning som slutligen ska till, vgar jag tro att om den politiska viljan finns i Sverige av att delta i valutaunionen, om den ekonomiska politiken fortsatt inriktas mot stabilitet och om kronans kurs mot euron befinner sig p en rimlig niv kommer ocks de vriga EU-lnderna att vilja ha oss med. Lt mig s nmna ngot om mera praktiska frberedelser fr en eventuell svensk anslutning till euroomrdet. I riksdagsbeslutet frn november 1997 ingr ju att drren ska hllas ppen fr ett senare svenskt EMU-intrde. Strsta mjliga handlingsfrihet ska upprtthllas utifrn en bevarad ekonomisk styrkeposition. Regeringskansliet har en organisation fr att flja upp hur handlingsberedskapen upprtthlls i olika delar av samhllet. Riksbanken upprtthller fr egen del en sdan beredskap att vi rknar med att det ska behvas hgst ett r frn det att riksdagen eventuellt fattar beslut om ett svenskt deltagande till dess att vi har de ndvndiga funktionerna p plats fr att kunna delta i den gemensamma penningpolitiken och andra delar av centralbankssamarbetet. Detta krver dock ven en del ytterligare anpassningar av lagstiftningen som vi inte rder ver sjlva. Bland de mera tidskrvande frberedelserna ingr kapaciteten att framstlla sedlar och mynt i euro med den hga skerhetsstandard som ska glla; drfr har Riksbanken deltagit i det utvecklingsarbete som ECB drivit och bl.a. ltit gra provtryckningar i begrnsad skala av sedlarna. Riksbanken har vidare ett srskilt ansvar fr att samordna den finansiella sektorns EMU-frberedelser, och vi har i flera rapporter de senaste ren beskrivit konsekvenserna av eurons infrande fr Sverige utanfr valutaunionen och brjat inventera vilka frndringar som skulle krvas om vi ska delta fullt ut. Som jag konstaterade inledningsvis sker frberedelsearbetet vad gller ndvndiga frndringar i olika sektorer i Sverige fortfarande under stor oskerhet om hur tidtabellen fr ett eventuellt svenskt deltagande i valutaunionen ser ut. Detta r en kostnad som r oundviklig fr att vi ska leva upp till riksdagsbeslutet om handlingsfriheten. Riksbankens ettriga frberedelseambition behver sttas in i ett sammanhang vad gller den politiska processen, och utan att vara ondigt spekulativ tycker jag att man kan ha en hypotes om hur de signaler som hittills framkommit kan omsttas i ett scenario. Med utgngspunkt frn att det blir en extra socialdemokratisk partikongress om ungefr ett r, och det sedan krvs ytterligare tid fr den bredare folkliga frankringen och fr den politiska och legala beredningen av frgan inom Sverige respektive inom EU, tror jag att ett svenskt deltagande frn den 1 januari 2002 r en mjlighet. Men det kan frsts bli senare - eller kanske inte alls under verskdlig tid. Den 1 januari 2002 r under alla omstndigheter den tidpunkt d de elva lnderna i den frsta EMU-vgen tar det sista steget i vergngsprocessen och byter ut sedlarna och mynten i de respektive nationella valutaenheterna mot sedlar och mynt i euro. Svenska finansiella fretag och institutioner har hittills lagt ner ett betydande arbete fr att anpassa sig till eurons infrande. Det har inneburit att ett antal finansiella tjnster och betalningsfrmedlingstjnster nu erbjuds i euro ven p den svenska marknaden. Men euron har naturligtvis frblivit en utlndsk valuta fr svenska aktrer, och de nya hanteringsrutinerna har infrts parallellt med dem fr andra utlndska valutor. Det finns ocks behov av att nnu ett tag kunna hantera de elva nationella valutaenheter som uppgtt i euron, ven om de har frsvunnit ur en del typer av transaktioner. Varje finansiellt fretag avgr utifrn sina kommersiella vervganden vilka typer av tjnster som det vill erbjuda sina kunder. Ett intrde i valutaunionen skulle dock innebra en helt annan organisatorisk milj fr de finansiella fretagen, bde i och med att det vxelkursen mellan kronan och euron d oterkalleligen skulle lsas och i och med att det d skulle finnas en tidsplan fr att erstta kronan med euron i legal och praktisk mening. Investeringsbeslut betrffande system och strategier skulle d kunna fattas med en betydligt hgre grad av skerhet n tidigare. Det kan idag inte skert bedmas om Sverige ocks skulle kunna byta ut sedlar och mynt vid samma tidpunkt och sledes genomfra hela valutareformen som en 'big bang', men s mycket kan sgas som att de administrativa konsekvenserna i s fall skulle bli betydligt mer omfattande genom att de berr hela kontanthanteringssystemet i samhllet. Fr att sammanfatta: Det bsta sttet fr Sverige att frbereda sig fr EMU r att skra sunda statsfinanser, god prisstabilitet och strukturella reformer. Det r faktiskt ett bra stt att frbereda sig ven fr ett liv utanfr EMU, men ett deltagande i valutaunionen kan ka avkastningen p en sdan politik. Strsta mjliga handlingsfrihet infr ett politiskt stllningstagande i EMU-frgan frutstter ocks att vi fortstter de praktiska frberedelserna fr infrandet av euron. Title: How is the Riksbank affected by EMU? (1/2)
text: How is the Riksbank affected by EMU? (1/2) Date: 1996-10-17 Speaker: Governor Urban Backstrom Location: Speech at the School of Business, Economics and Law seminar In Sweden, the discussion is currently underway about our country's future relationship with the European Monetary Union (EMU). The question is whether Sweden will be part of the first group of countries to form EMU or whether the political process will lead to us waiting. It will not be until next autumn that the Riksdag will take a position. In the meantime, the Riksbank is actively participating in the preparations that must be made for the Riksdag to have a real choice. At European level, the Riksbank participates in the work of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) in Frankfurt, which is the forerunner of the new European Central Bank. We are also represented in the Monetary Committee. The Riksbank has also initiated practical preparatory work within Sweden by forming an overall consultation group for the financial sector. In the coming winter, a detailed so-called. masterplan is prepared for the financial sector in Sweden. We are also developing a detailed plan for the Riksbank's inner workings. The timetable is getting tight. Nevertheless, preparations are progressing according to plan. Most of the evidence also points to EMU coming into being at the beginning of 1999. The timetable means that the Heads of State or Government of the EU countries will decide as early as spring 1998 which countries are involved from the start. Soon after, the European Central Bank (ECB) is formed. Emu will start on 1 January 1999. Exchange rates are fixed and monetary policy is taken over by the ECB. By January 2002 at the latest, euro notes and coins will be issued. The topic of today's seminar is not so much the question of whether Sweden should join EMU or not. Let us put it aside for a moment and simply assume for the sake of the continued discus-sion here today that Sweden will be in the first group of EMU countries. What will be the consequences? It has fallen on my lot to discuss how the Riksbank is affected by EMU. I will first deal very specifically with the various areas of work for the Riksbank. These include monetary policy, the payment system and banknotes and coins. Next, I will discuss how the EMU process might affect the financial system in a more strategic perspective and how this transformation may affect our work. The introduction of a single currency in Europe Monetary policy will be centrally controlled by the ECB in Frankfurt. A single monetary policy is a cornerstone of monetary union. There is currently a discussion going on about what strategy should be applied in order for monetary policy to lead to the ultimate objective of price stability. Will there be an explicit inflation target, similar to the one the Riksbank is currently applying, or should inflation be tackled indirectly by using monetary aggregates as a so-called intermediate target? From Swedish sia, we believe that the difference is not as great as sometimes may seem. The goal in both cases is to secure a stable monetary value. To achieve this, central banks analyse a wide range of indicators of inflationary pressures, including various measures of money supply. If it turns out that monetary aggregates within EMU are reliably linked to inflation, this indicator may take on a special position. It is likely that more indicators will need to be taken into account in the inflation assessment. The instruments of monetary policy also need to be harmonised between countries. In addition to repos and other direct market operations by central banks, as well as standing loan facilities, reserve requirements are also used in some countries. Although it is still possible to determine exactly which instruments will be used, there is agreement on a system that shows great similarities with what we already have in Sweden. In order to be able to implement a single monetary policy throughout EMU, it must be possible to operate in euros quickly throughout the area. This requires the interconnection of national payment systems as well as the ability to handle securities transactions across borders. In practice, this means that the national systems for large payments, in Sweden the Riksbank's so-called RIX system, are partly harmonized so that they can work together and partly that linking arrangements are created. All countries' systems must work according to the RTGS principle - which the Swedish RIX system has been doing for several years. RTGS stands for "Real Time Gross Settlement" and means that the payment orders that enter the system are settled one by one, and continuously throughout the entire time the system is open. This network of national RTGS systems, named TARGET, will make it possible to initiate and settle payments in euro across land borders within seconds. Everyone realises that this European financial highway will mean a major change in the possibilities for making payments in Europe compared to the current system where it can take several days and often up to even a week to make payments from one country to another. Now that the decision on the design of TARGET has been taken, it has become the task of central banks, banks and clearing houses to rebuild their systems so that they can handle the euro and otherwise meet the requirements for participating in TARGET. The Euro function is necessary to be able to make and receive payments via RIX, which becomes the Riksbank's TARGET connection. TARGET is complemented by existing systems for the management of securities as collateral for the provision of credit in the payment system and for the implementation of monetary policy. In several EU countries, the central bank owns the settlement systems in whole or in part. As is well known, this is not the case in Sweden, but since the Riksbank and VPC have a close exchange of information, the preparatory work works well. A concrete sub-question is how payments and accounting are to be made during the period when we still have kronor, but when the euro is increasingly being used as a unit of valuation for the central bank, the state, companies and other parties. The banks must then be prepared, for example, to receive payments in sek but to make the corresponding payment in euros. Somewhere in the system there must be a conversion mechanism where the crowns are converted into euros at the fixed rate. Of course, a euro payment before 2002 can only be made by crediting an account, since physical notes and coins are still missing. It is planned that the public authorities will gradually start using the euro as a valuation unit from 1999. For example, all monetary policy operations are to be carried out and expressed in euro and new government loans are issued in this new currency unit. Among other things, it aims to show that the authorities are behind the new currency. Private sector operators may switch to using the euro as a valuation unit whenever they see fit (but no later than the end of 2001). However, central banks will create incentives for such an early transition, inter alia, by using the euro in transactions with banks and in the foreign exchange market. For the Riksbank, this transition will take place as early as 1 January 1999. From that point on, the Riksbank's accounts will be made in euros. It takes quite a long time from the time from the first planning of a new banknote until the first copies are printed and issued. Work on euro banknotes has already been going on for some time, although they may not be issued until around 2002. There has been a design competition this year. A number of companies in Europe have drawn up sketches of the appearance of banknotes. Later this autumn, it will be decided which proposals will be chosen. The competition covers different subject areas: one is different cultural styles in European history, in the form of architecture, art or otherwise. The second subject area--it is purely abstract patterns. As the banknotes will be widely distributed, it is likely that the banknotes will also be distributed outside the EMU area, the designers will take the opportunity to introduce the latest in protection against counterfeiting. This applies to traditional watermarks, security wires and other things, but also to advanced optical protection mechanisms. The notes and coins will be introduced at the beginning of 2002 and the idea is that the national currencies will cease to be valid means of payment by the middle of this year at the latest. Needless to say, I would hardly like to add that at that time there will be a very large amount of work involved in transporting and exchanging the national notes and coins for the new euro. The stores will also have to work with double price lists during a transitional period, one for the krona and one for the euro. The exchange of banknotes and coins will take place according to a timetable set by each country, and for the Riksbank we see strong reasons to manage it in a significantly shorter period than six months. Talking about expanded statistical reporting usually does not provoke much cheer from representatives of the financial sector who are the ones who bear the burden of reporting. Emu will unfortunately mean changed and also increased reporting requirements. The basic purpose of banking statistics is to provide a basis for the single monetary policy. In order to measure liquidity in the financial sector, the ECB needs to be aware of developments in account balances and other financial dealings in the different countries. Furthermore, the ECB must have access to other balance sheet data that indicate the overall stability of the payment system or whether there are tensions. If the data collected are to be summed up within EMU and form the basis for monetary policy, the statistics must be harmonised so that each country reports the same things and according to the same principles. Extensive harmonisation work is currently under way. Preparatory work within the European Monetary Institute covers a very large number of sub-areas. Within each sub-project there are also legal issues to be resolved. An important ju-ridic issue is the so-called contract continuity. Contracts which currently stipulate that payments or other transactions are to be carried out in national currency will, from 2002, only be able to be executed in euro, since the national currency has ceased to be a means of payment. The Commission has just presented a proposal for a regulation which will make it easier for the courts to regard payments in euro as the fulfilment of the contractual obligation for payments in national currency. Another legal issue has a much less fundamental importance but is of great practical importance to all of us is what rounding rules should be applied when moving from national currency to euro. Since conversions are to be made at fixed rates, it is of the utmost importance that the rounding rules are uniform and precise when there are conversions between different currencies used for a given transaction. The stability of the pay system An important mission of the Riksbank is to safeguard the stability and efficiency of the payment system. A well-functioning payment system is a basic prerequisite for the development of the market system. What comes to mind first and foremost is the system that businesses and households use to effect payments in connection with various economic transactions. These are banknotes and coins, where the Riksbank is the direct guarantor through their monopoly, and the whole flora of giro systems, in which banks play a central role through the special position they have been given in offering account-based deposits. This can be said to describe the retail function of the payment system, but as with most businesses that are of a retail nature, there is also a wholesale function that is a prerequisite for the smooth functioning of the retail trade. In Sweden, the Riksbank has direct responsibility for this wholesale function through the so-called RIX system. This is a system in which the banks' positions vis-a-vis each other are cleared daily with the Riksbank as coordinator. Any over-respected and shortfalls in payments for the banking system as a whole are regulated through borrowing and borrowing in the Riksbank. It can be said that the Riksbank is ultimately responsible for ensuring that banks can fulfill their role in the payment system without disruption. Normally, lending to banks for the purpose of bridging liquidity deficits should be provided against collateral in the form of, for example, government securities. However, in special situations, the Riksbank can assist a bank that has encountered serious payment difficulties with loans. However, the prerequisite is that the bank can be considered to be fundamentally solvent and capable of surviving on commercial terms in the long run. The idea is thus that the Riksbank will prevent illiquid but fundamentally solvent banks from failing with the risks of spillover effects in the payment system that this would entail. Through the banks' special construction of highly liquid deposits and fairly illiquid lending, the stability of the banking system can be threatened by the mere reputation of defaults leading to a bank run. Against this background, it is important for the central bank to have a preparedness in the form of knowledge of the various actors who play an essential role in the payment system, i.e. primarily the banks, and how they interact with each other. On the one hand, the central bank must be able to make reasonable assessments of the banks' financial situation when a crisis is about to emerge, and on the other hand, it should be able to reduce the risks of such crises arising through its ongoing monitoring of the banks' economic development and activities. Here it is important to point out that the Riksbank does not have sole responsibility for the banks acting in such a way that their strategic role in the financial system is not compromised. In Sweden, as in many other countries, the direct supervision of banks and other financial institutions has been entrusted to a special government agency, namely the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority. The inspection shall ensure that the regulatory framework applicable in particular to banking is complied with by the institutions concerned. It will also supplement this acquis with various regulations, as the basic regulatory framework is often of a framework law nature and explicitly instructs the inspectorate to take care of the practical design. Finally, the Inspectorate shall handle the registration, information gathering, etc. necessary for the practical supervision to be carried out. However, the inspection has no means of providing the banks with liquidity, but this is, as noted, the Riksbank's role. It goes without saying that the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Riksbank, especially when it comes to building knowledge about the banking sector, have great common interests. It is, of course, desirable from the point of view of resources to have as little duplication as possible with regard to this information activity. In practice, however, the Riksbank must have its own expertise in processing and analysing the economic development of the banking sector. Of course, this activity should take place in as good collaboration with the Inspectorate as possible, not least because the problems in question are so complicated that analysis from several angles is particularly valuable. What, then, will the formation of EMU mean in terms of the Swedish payment system and the Riksbank's role in this area? As far as the payment system is concerned from a more technical point of view, the retail system is unlikely to change much. Swedish companies and households will make extensive use of banks and giro systems based in Sweden for their payments. The Riksbank will still play a central role in terms of the wholesale trading function of the payment system. However, the RIX system will be more definitively incorporated into the EMI's payment system. The construction of the so-called TARGET is an example of how this process is already under way. Another is the Riksbank's own efforts to broaden the RIX system's clientele by accepting collateral in other countries' government securities. With exchange rate risk eliminated, this process is, of course, facilitated. Finally, emu coordination must take place, because monetary policy in monetary union requires, for its operation, that banks can freely and on the same day transfer liquidity across national borders so that changes in interest rates have a rapid and uniform impact throughout the Union. The RIX system becomes a component of this whole. What is perhaps more interesting to consider is how the institutions and markets on which the payment system is structured will be affected by EMU and how this may affect the Riksbank's work in this area.

(1/2) Datum: 1996-10-17 Talare: Riksbankschef Urban Bckstrm Plats: Anfrande vid Handelshgskolans seminarium I Sverige pgr som bst diskussionen om vrt lands framtida frhllande till den Europeiska Monetra Unionen (EMU). Lt oss fr en stund lgga den t sidan och helt enkelt fr den fortsatta diskus-sionens skull hr idag anta att Sverige kommer att vara med i den frsta gruppen av EMU-lnder. Vad kommer det att f fr konsekvenser? P min lott har fallit att diskutera hur Riksbanken pverkas av EMU. Jag tnker frst mycket konkret behandla de olika arbetsomrdena fr Riksbanken. Infrandet av en enda valuta i Europa Penningpolitiken kommer att styras centralt frn ECB i Frankfurt. En gemensam penningpolitik r en grundbult i en monetr union. Det pgr just nu en diskussion om vilken strategi som br tillmpas fr att penningpolitiken skall leda till det slutliga mlet som r prisstabilitet. Kommer det att finnas ett explicit inflationsml, likt det som Riksbanken nu tillmpar, eller skall man angripa inflationen indirekt genom att anvnda monetra aggregat som s.k. intermedirt ml? Frn svensk sia anser vi att skillnaden inte r s stor som ibland kan tyckas. Mlet i bda fallen r att skra ett stabilt penningvrde. Fr att n dit analyserar centralbankerna ett stort antal indikatorer p inflationstrycket, dribland olika mtt p penningmngden. Om det visar sig att monetra aggregat inom EMU har ett plitligt samband med inflationen kan denna indikator komma att inta en srstllning. Sannolikt mste fler indikatorer vgas in i inflationsbedmningen. ven instrumenten fr penningpolitiken behver harmoniseras mellan lnderna. Utver repor och andra direkta marknadsoperationer frn centralbankernas sida samt stende lnefaciliteter anvnds i vissa lnder ven kassakrav. ven om det nnu terstr att exakt faststlla vilka instrument som kommer att anvndas finns samstmmighet om ett system som visar stora likheter med det vi redan har i Sverige. Fr att kunna genomfra en gemensam penningpolitik inom hela EMU mste operationer i euro kunna gras snabbt i hela omrdet. Detta krver att de nationella betalningssystemen sammanlnkas liksom mjligheten att hantera vrdepapperstransaktioner ver grnserna. I praktiken innebr det att de nationella systemen fr stora betalningar, i Sverige Riksbankens s.k. RIX-system, dels harmoniseras s att de kan fungera tillsammans, dels att lnkningsarrangemang skapas. Samtliga lnders system skall arbeta enligt RTGS-principen - vilket det svenska RIX-systemet gr sedan flera r. RTGS str fr "Real Time Gross Settlement" och innebr att de betalningsuppdrag som gr in i systemet avvecklas ett och ett, och lpande under hela tiden systemet r ppet. Detta ntverk av nationella RTGS-system, som getts namnet TARGET, skall gra det mjligt att initiera och avveckla betalningar i euro ver landgrnserna inom loppet av ngra sekunder. Var och en inser att denna europeiska finansiella motorvg kommer att innebra en stor frndring av mjligheterna att genomfra betalningar i Europa jmfrt med dagens system dr det kan g flera dagar och ofta upp till t.o.m. en vecka fr att gra betalningar frn ett land till ett annat. Efter det att beslut om utformning av TARGET nu har fattats har det blivit centralbankernas, bankernas och clearinginstitutens uppgift att bygga om sina system s att de kan hantera euro samt i vrigt uppfylla de krav som stlls fr att delta i TARGET. Euro-funktionen r ndvndig fr att kunna utfra och motta betalningar via RIX som blir Riksbankens TARGET-anslutning. TARGET kompletteras med existerande system fr hantering av vrdepapper som skerhet fr kreditgivning i betalningssystemet och fr genomfrandet av penningpolitiken. I flera EU-lnder ger centralbanken avvecklingssystemen helt eller delvis. Det r som bekant inte fallet i Sverige, men genom att Riksbanken och VPC har ett nra informationsutbyte s fungerar frberedelsearbetet bra. En konkret delfrga r hur betalningar och redovisning skall g till under den period d vi alltjmt har kronor, men d euro brjar anvndas alltmer som en vrderingsenhet fr centralbanken, staten, fretagen och andra parter. Bankerna mste d vara beredda att exempelvis motta inbetalningar i kronor men att gra motsvarande utbetalning i euro. Ngonstans i systemet mste det finnas en konverteringsmekanism dr kronorna rknas om till euro enligt den fasta kursen. En euro-betalning kan fre 2002 givetvis endast ske genom att kreditera ett konto eftersom fysiska sedlar och mynt nnu saknas. Enligt planerna kommer de offentliga myndigheterna gradvis att brja anvnda sig av euro som vrderingsenhet alltifrn 1999. Exempelvis skall alla penningpolitiska transaktioner genomfras och uttryckas i euro och nya statsln emitteras i denna nya valutaenhet. Det syftar bl.a. till att visa att myndigheterna str bakom den nya valutan. Aktrer inom den privata sektorn fr verg till att anvnda euro som vrderingsenhet nr de s finner lmpligt (dock senast vid utgngen av 2001). Centralbankerna kommer dock att skapa incitament fr en tidig sdan vergng bl.a. genom att anvnda euro i transaktioner med bankerna samt p valutamarknaden. Denna vergng kommer fr Riksbankens del att ske redan den 1 januari 1999. Fr.o.m. den tidpunkten kommer Riksbankens redovisning att ske i euro. Det tar ganska lng tid frn tidpunkten frn den frsta planeringen av en ny sedel till dess att de frsta exemplaren r tryckta och utgivna. Arbetet med euro sedlar har redan pgtt en tid trots att de mjligen inte kommer att ges ut frrn kring r 2002. Det har i r gt rum en designtvling. Ett antal fretag i Europa har gjort skisser p sedlarnas utseende. Senare i hst beslutas vilka frslag som skall vljas. Tvlingen gller olika motivomrden: det ena r olika kulturstilar i Europas historia, i form av arkitektur, konst eller annat. Det andra motivomr-det r rent abstrakta mnster. Eftersom sedlarna kommer att f en stor spridning sannolikt ven utanfr EMUomrdet tar konstruktrerna tillfllet i akt och infr det senaste i skydd mot frfalskningar. Det gller traditionella vattenstmplar, skerhetstrdar och annat men ven avancerade optiska skyddsmekanismer. Sedlarna och mynten kommer att introduceras i brjan av 2002 och tanken r att de nationella valutorna skall upphra att vara giltiga betalningsmedel senast vid halvrsskiftet detta r. Jag behver vl knappast tillgga att det vid den tidpunkten kommer att rra sig om ett mycket omfattande arbete med att transportera och byta ut de nationella sedlarna och mynten mot den nya euron. I butikerna kommer man ocks att f arbeta med dubbla prislistor under en vergngsperiod, en fr kronan och en fr euron. Utbytet av sedlar och mynt kommer att ske enligt en tidtabell som varje land faststller, och fr Riksbankens del ser vi starka skl att klara av det p vsentligt kortare tid n sex mnader. Att bertta om utkad statistisk rapportering brukar vanligen inte vcka ngot strre jubel hos fretrdare fr den finansiella sektorn som r de som fr bra brdan av att rapportera. EMU kommer dessvrre att innebra ndrade och ven utkade rapporteringskrav. Det grundlggande syftet med statistiken p bankomrdet r att den skall utgra underlag fr den gemensamma penningpolitiken. Fr att mta likviditeten i den finansiella sektorn mste ECB knna till utvecklingen i kontotillgodohavanden och andra finansiella mellanhavanden i de olika lnderna. Vidare mste ECB ha tillgng till andra balansdata som visar p den generella stabiliteten i betalningsvsendet eller om dr finns spnningar. Om de data som insamlas skall kunna summeras inom EMU och ligga till grund fr penningpolitiken mste statistiken vara harmoniserad s att varje land rapporterar samma saker och enligt samma principer. Ett omfattande harmoniseringsarbete pgr just nu. Frberedelsearbete inom det Europeiska Monetra Institutet omfattar ett mycket stort antal delomrden. Inom varje delprojekt finns ocks juridiska frgor att lsa. En viktig ju-ridisk frga r den s.k. kontraktskontinuiteten. Kontrakt som i dag anger att betalningar eller andra transaktioner skall fullgras i nationell valuta kommer frn r 2002 endast att kunna fullgras i euro eftersom den nationella valutan upphrt att glla som betalningsmedel. Eftersom vxlingarna skall ske till fasta kurser r det av strsta vikt att avrundningsreglerna r enhetliga och precisa nr det sker konverteringar mellan olika valutor som man anvnder fr en viss transaktion. Stabiliteten i betalningssystemet Ett viktigt uppdrag som Riksbanken har r att vrna stabiliteten och effektiviteten i betalningsvsendet. Ett vl fungerande betalningssystem r en grundfrutsttning fr att marknadssystemet skall kunna utvecklas. Det man vl i frsta hand tnker p r det system som fretag och hushll utnyttjar sig av fr att effektuera betalningar i samband med olika ekonomiska transaktioner. Detta kan sgas beskriva betalningssystemets detaljhandelsfunktion, men liksom med de flesta verksamheter som r av detaljhandelskaraktr finns det ocks en grosshandelsfunktion som r en frutsttning fr att detaljhandeln skall fungera smidigt. Denna grosshandelsfunktion har i Sverige Riksbanken ett direkt ansvar fr genom det s.k. RIX-systemet. Detta r ett system, dr bankernas positioner gentemot varandra dagligen clearas med Riksbanken som samordnare. Eventuella verrespektive underskott i betalningarna fr banksystemet som helhet regleras genom in- respektive upplning i Riksbanken. Man kan sga att Riksbanken ytterst ansvarar fr att bankerna kan fullgra sin roll i betalningssystemet utan strningar. Normalt skall utlningen till banker i syfte att verbrygga likviditetsunderskott ske mot betryggande skerheter i form av t.ex. statspapper. Riksbanken kan i speciella situationer emellertid bist en bank som rkat i allvarliga betalningssvrigheter med ln. Frutsttningen r dock att banken kan anses vara i grunden solvent och frmgen att p sikt verleva p affrsmssiga villkor. Tanken r sledes att Riksbanken skall frhindra att illikvida men i grunden solventa banker gr omkull med de risker fr spridningseffekter i betalningssystemet som detta skulle innebra. Genom bankernas speciella konstruktion med hglikvid inlning och tmligen illikvid utlning kan stabiliteten i banksystemet hotas genom att blotta ryktet om betalningsinstllelser leder till uttagsanstormning. Det r mot denna bakgrund viktigt fr centralbanken att ha en beredskap i form av kunskap om de olika aktrer, som spelar en vsentlig roll i betalningssystemet, dvs. frmst bankerna, och hur dessa interagerar med varandra. Dels mste centralbanken kunna gra rimliga bedmningar av bankernas ekonomiska situation nr en kris r p vg att segla upp, dels br den genom sin lpande bevakning av bankernas ekonomiska utveckling och verksamheter kunna minska riskerna fr att sdana kriser skall uppkomma. Hr r det viktigt att ppeka att Riksbanken inte har ensamt ansvar fr att bankerna agerar p ett sdant stt att deras strategiska roll i det finansiella systemet inte ventyras. I Sverige liksom i mnga andra lnder har den direkta tillsynen av banker och andra finansiella institutioner uppdragits t en srskild statlig myndighet, nmligen Finansinspektionen. Inspektionen skall se till att det regelverk, som gller speciellt p bankomrdet, fljs av de berrda instituten. Den skall ocks komplettera detta regelverk med olika frordningar, eftersom det grundlggande regelverket ofta r av ramlagskaraktr och explicit ger inspektionen i uppdrag att svara fr den praktiska utformningen. Slutligen skall Inspektionen handha den registrering, informationsinsamling etc som r ndvndig fr att tillsynen praktiskt skall kunna bedrivas. Dremot har inspektionen inga mjligheter att frse bankerna med likviditet, utan detta r som noterats Riksbankens roll. Det sger sig sjlvt att Finansinspektionen och Riksbanken framfr allt nr det gller uppbyggnad av kunskap om banksektorn har stora gemensamma intressen. Det r naturligtvis frn resurssynpunkt nskvrt med s lite dubbelarbete som mjligt vad gller denna informationsverksamhet. I praktiken mste dock Riksbanken ha en egen kompetens fr bearbetning och analys av banksektorns ekonomiska utveckling. Sjlvklart br denna verksamhet ske i s god samverkan med Inspektionen som mjligt, inte minst drfr att de problem det hr r frga om r s komplicerade att genomlysning frn flera vinklar r srskilt vrdefull. Vad kommer d bildandet av EMU att innebra vad gller det svenska betalningssystemet och Riksbankens roll p detta omrde? Vad gller betalningssystemet frn mera teknisk synvinkel kommer detaljhandelssystemet knappast att frndras s mycket. Svenska fretag och hushll kommer i stor utstrckning att utnyttja i Sverige baserade banker och girosystem fr sina betalningar. Riksbanken kommer fortfarande att spela en central roll nr det gller betalningssystemets grosshandelsfunktion. RIX-systemet kommer emellertid att p ett mera definitivt stt infogas i EMUs betalningssystem. Uppbyggnaden av det s.k. TARGET r exempel p att denna process redan r igng. Ett annat r Riksbankens egna strvanden att vidga RIX-systemets kundkrets genom att acceptera skerheter i andra lnders statspapper. Med vxelkursrisken eliminerad underlttas givetvis denna process. Slutligen mste en EMU-samordning ske, drfr att penningpolitiken i den monetra unionen fr sitt bedrivande krver att bankerna fritt och under samma dag kan fra likviditet ver nationsgrnserna s att rntefrndringar fr ett snabbt och enhetligt genomslag i hela unionen. RIX-systemet blir en komponent i denna helhet. Det som kanske r mer intressant att fundera ver r hur de institutioner och marknader, p vilka betalningssystemet r uppbyggt, kommer att pverkas av EMU och hur detta kan pverka Riksbankens arbete inom detta omrde. Title: How is the Riksbank affected by EMU? (2/2)
text: How is the Riksbank affected by EMU? (2/2) Date: 1996-10-17 Speaker: Governor Urban Backstrom Location: School of Business, Economics and Law seminar The ""financial revolution""" It can probably be said without exaggeration that the financial system in Sweden, as in most industrialized countries, has undergone a revolutionary transformation process over the past decade, the consequences of which we have still probably only seen part of. It is important to remember that the financial system is not a new creation, nor has it been developed for its own sake. Its structure has come into being over the centuries as a means of facilitating the production and trade of goods and services. This is true in the transition in the old days from the barter economy to trade that was facilitated with precious metals. Similarly, the first banknotes were a success when they replaced the old coins. Although the financial system has roots that go far back in time, development took off in connection with the breakthrough of industrialism in the middle of the last century. However, since the mid-1980s, financial development has accelerated significantly. Turnover in trading in the financial markets has only in a decade increased very rapidly. The same applies to cross-border movements of capital. New financial instruments have come into being. The new stage of development has probably only just begun. Most indications are that in the next century we will see a much more developed financial system than today's. Through deregulation, globalization, advanced information technology and new methods of valuation and risk management, a dynamic process has been initiated, where financial markets, institutions and instruments work in interaction. There are several similarities with the expansion of the last hundred years in the real economy, with constantly new and more efficient production processes and new communication opportunities that led to a growing global trade exchange. Financial development and its internationalisation are fundamentally natural. It is a logical consequence of continued expansion of global trade, transformation of production and globalised investment and savings opportunities. The new derivative instruments will facilitate the continued specialisation and streamlining of output in the real economy. In this way, financial developments will contribute to the continued emergence of prosperity. Neither developments in the real economy nor in the financial field have always been painless over the years. More or less difficult changes are well documented in historical reflections. Even in our time, development does not take place without problems and difficulties. We have seen banking crises unfold and many times abrupt corrections and large fluctuations in interest rate, stock and exchange rates. This is especially true in our own country, but also to varying degrees in the world around us. The globalisation of the financial sector has created a new and more difficult environment for various authorities at both national and international level. The creation of EMU, with a single currency, will create more stable conditions within Europe. The focus on low inflation and sound public finances also means that the overall economic environment will promote more stable development. However, this does not prevent the review and supervision of the financial sector from continuing to be developed and refined. In addition, international cooperation between different authorities must be increased, especially as problems in one country can now spread to other countries even more than before. The problems in Mexico last spring are an example of that. What, then, can the formation of EMU mean for the development of the financial sector? As has just been pointed out, it is basically a question of studying a process that has been going on for more than a decade at a partly accelerating pace. This development would probably have been similar even if the EMU project had not existed, as it can be seen as a natural consequence of the general efforts to integrate Europe. However, a common currency for the countries of Europe will of course have interesting consequences for the Swedish financial system and thus for the Riksbank and the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority. Let me discuss some such possible consequences. Financial development trends In addition to EMU, there are several development trends affecting the financial system. The adjustment following the liberalisations of the 1980s has not yet been completed. The development of the new information technologies will continue to have an impact. The demographic trend suggests an increased need for pension savings. The EU, NAFTA, GATT, the emerging new economies and the high growth in South-East Asia tend to drive the globalisation of entrepreneurship. Of course, it is difficult to point out unequivocally what the development will look like. But most of it points to a continued rapid development of the financial markets, with new instruments and the need for clearing and settlement. Competitive pressures in the traditional banking sector continue to increase, while long-term demand for financial services is expanding rapidly, but investors and capital users are becoming more and more sophisticated. If this is a reasonable assessment of the future, the need for restructuring of the financial sector will increase, at the same time there is a need for consolidation in order to be able to cope with the pressures of a transformation process. What this will lead to in more detail is difficult to say. But it seems reasonable to assume that the number of institutions is decreasing while their average size is increasing. But we will also have different types of specialized banks, so-called. niche banks. In addition, the relative size of traditional bank deposits and lending should decrease and the supply and demand for market-based instruments increase its relative importance. This in and of itself is nothing new. This process has already begun. These are forces that are already at work today. Added to this is the EMU process. Swedish membership of EMU could mean that the market for Swedish government securities would be more or less fully integrated with the large market for interest-bearing securities issued by the Member States of the monetary union. It is difficult to see that investors will in the long run make much distinction between securities issued by the Swedish state and securities issued by, for example, the German or Dutch state, at least if the indebtedness (and thus credit risk) is offset over time by bringing public finances under permanent control. The conclusion could be that we will have a single yield curve for government interest-bearing euro securities within EMU or at least a situation where different countries' government bonds will be close substitutes. This means that the conditions for the national markets for fixed income securities and their derivatives, which today, along with the foreign exchange market, are the largest markets in terms of volume, radically subject to change. Some believe that in such a situation it is hardly likely that the spot and futures markets for Swedish government securities will remain in Sweden, but the trading of these papers will take place in a large European market, in some financial center, with Swedish paper as a component of a larger euro-dominated market. Since, as I said, the spot markets for Swedish treasury bills and so-called bench-mark bonds are today very extensive and the standardized futures on these instruments constitute the largest Swedish derivatives market, this development means a loss of financial markets in Sweden. On the other hand, others believe that there are factors that suggest that the Swedish spot and futures markets will remain even in the event of Swedish membership of EMU. Proximity to a local market may remain important as market participants may spend more resources on assessing different risks that are specifically national. The two approaches mean that today it is not possible to point to an unambiguous direction of development. A loss of financial markets in Sweden can - and should - of course be seen as a problem, but you can also see it in a positive perspective. This may give rise to a new development. Although there are markets for mortgage instruments in Sweden, they are significantly less active and effective than their counterparts on the government securities side. This applies even more to the market for industrial bonds - or "corporate bonds" for which the term corporate bonds would be more adequate where the Swedish market is completely undeveloped except possibly when it comes to the shortest side with the so-called commercial paper. It is not unreasonable to think that the possible disappearance of national sovereign debt markets and their derivatives stimulates the development of the mortgage market, including derivatives within EMU. Whether Swedish actors will be the initiators of this process is difficult to speculate on and is not really that interesting from the Riksbank's perspective. What is essential is that Swedish banks and mortgage institutions have access to a significantly broadened market for mortgage securities and their derivatives issued throughout the monetary union. This means both more liquid futures and options instruments for risk management and the possibility of better diversified residential paper portfolios. It would also mean a significantly increased demand for the knowledge needed to properly analyze and price different forms of credit risk in the mortgage market. Furthermore, such a development could stimulate the industrial bond market, where the assessment of credit risks and the pricing of risk premia impose additional requirements for qualified analysis. The larger the volume of the market, the more it can pay off for large investment banks to invest in building up competence in this area. This valuation and risk management technology can then become a valuable component of another possible and particularly interesting development for the banking system. It is the case that awareness and knowledge among various financial companies in Sweden as well as in Western Europe about risk exposure and risk control has increased rapidly in recent times. With some simplification, it can be argued that the methods for measuring and controlling so-called market risks, such as interest rate and currency risks, are quite well developed and known by financial firms. The problems can often be of a management and governance nature. It is important to minimize the risk of abuse and incompetent handling of type Barings. Credit risk, on the other hand, is a notoriously unwieldy matter, where so far little of sophisticated risk management methods have been developed in Europe. However, judging by recent developments, innovations in this area can be expected. In US banks, there is currently an intensive development of methods for measuring, valuing and controlling credit risks, whether they are associated with the issuance of corporate bonds or with lending portfolios. Also the rapid development of so-called. credit derivatives for the purpose of managing and allocating credit risks should be mentioned. One consequence of this development is the so-called "loan sales". These mean that a bank sells off part of its loan portfolios to one or more other banks and possibly correspondingly replenishes its balance sheet with purchases of loans granted by other banks. As for the individual loans included in these "loan sales", it is of course the case that the bank that originally granted the loan retains at least part of it in its portfolio. The reason is that in this way banks can more clearly indicate that these are not bad loans the banks sell off and that they do not lose the incentives to continue to monitor and possibly influence the financial position of borrowers. The consequences will be similar to those we have with a widening corporate bond market. Conditions are created for a more efficient valuation of credit risks and thus increased diversification and risk diversification. Even if such a development in the management of credit risks were nevertheless to come over time, the formation of monetary union, in which all currency risk is eliminated between the constituent countries, could stimulate development. Other development trends are that payment intermediation is becoming an increasing source of revenue for banks, e.g. through the introduction of so-called smart cards. Furthermore, wealth management should be a growing business, given the demographic developments in Europe that I have spoken about earlier. My analysis has mostly focused on instruments and risks. It could also go deeper and analyse more institutional aspects. By that I mean how the EMU process affects certain types of banks, such as large or small banks and whether they are located in large or small countries. One might also ask whether financial institutions other than banks will gain or lose market share. I also haven't gotten into industry slippage aspects. However, time does not allow me to get any further. My point has probably nevertheless emerged, i.e. that the formation of EMU can have rather far-reaching consequences for financial markets and institutions in Sweden and the rest of Europe. It will be a development that will take place in addition to the forces of change that are already underway. This type of transformation and development of the financial system will place great demands on the authorities with supervisory and supervisory tasks. These are tasks that the Riksbank will work ambitiously on in the coming years. Conclusion Although monetary policy will be decided in Frankfurt, we in the Swedish central bank will not be without tasks. Let me give some examples. The Governor of the Swedish Riksbank will need an analysis function to support the line he or she will pursue in Frankfurt. Furthermore, it is conceivable that different national central banks in Europe specialize in different areas of analysis, in the same way as happens at different local Federal Reserve banks in the United States. In addition, there is currently a debate on whether the single foreign exchange reserve should be managed centrally in Frankfurt or whether it should be decentralised at the respective national central banks. There is also much to suggest that the actual execution of monetary policy operations will, at least initially, take place on a decentralised basis at each central bank of the various participating countries. As a result, we will remain responsible for the national payment system. To this can also be added responsibility for the distribution of banknotes and coins. It is today a very large part of our business to ensure that there are means of payment throughout the country. This will also be the case in the future, although the notes and coins will say euros and not crowns. These tasks will closely monitor the future development of the financial sector with a view to promoting a secure and efficient payment system. This means that it will thus be possible to make great demands also in the future on: The Riksbank's work, even though we, like many others, will change and adapt resources and tasks to the new requirements that the formation of EMU will give rise to.
