(2/2) Datum: 1996-10-17 Talare: Riksbankschef Urban Bckstrm Plats: Handelshgskolans seminarium Den """finansiella revolutionen""" Man kan nog utan verdrift pst att det finansiella systemet i Sverige liksom i flertalet industrilnder under det senaste rtiondet har genomgtt en revolutionerande omvandlingsprocess, vars konsekvenser vi nnu sannolikt endast sett en del av. Det r viktigt att komma ihg att det finansiella systemet inte r ngon ny skapelse, inte heller har det utvecklats fr sin egen skull. Dess struktur har kommit till under rhundradenas lopp som ett medel fr att underltta fr produktion och handel med varor och tjnster. Det gller vid vergngen i gamla tider frn bytesekonomin till handel som underlttades med delmetaller. Likas blev de frsta sedlarna en succ nr de ersatte de gamla vrdemynten. ven om det finansiella systemet har rtter som gr lngt tillbaka i tiden tog utvecklingen fart i samband med industrialismens genombrott i mitten av frra seklet. Sedan mitten av 1980-talet har dock den finansiella utvecklingen accelererat ptagligt. Omsttningen i handeln p de finansiella marknaderna har bara p ett decennium kat mycket snabbt. Detsamma gller kapitalrrelser ver nationsgrnserna. Nya finansiella instrument har kommit till. Det nya steget i utvecklingen har frmodligen bara brjat. Det mesta tyder p att vi under nsta sekel kommer att f se ett vsentligt mer utbyggt finansiellt system n dagens. Genom avreglering, globalisering, avancerad informationsteknologi samt nya metoder fr vrdering och riskhantering har en dynamisk process initierats, dr finansiella marknader, institutioner och instrument fungerar i samspel. Det finns flera likheter med de senaste hundra rens expansion i den reala ekonomin, med stndigt nya och mer effektiva produktionsprocesser och nya kommunikationsmjligheter som ledde till ett vxande globalt handelsutbyte. Den finansiella utvecklingen och dess internationalisering r i grunden naturlig. Den r en logisk konsekvens av ett fortsatt expanderande globalt handelsutbyte, omvandling av produktionen samt globaliserade investerings- och sparmjligheter. De nya derivatinstrumenten kommer att underltta en fortsatt specialisering och effektivisering av produktionen i den reala ekonomin. P s stt kommer den finansiella utvecklingen att bidra till det fortsatt framvxande vlstndet. Vare sig utvecklingen inom den reala ekonomin eller p det finansiella omrdet har under rens lopp alltid skett p ett smrtfritt stt. Mer eller mindre svra omstllningar finns vl dokumenterade i historiska betraktelser. Inte heller i vrt tid sker utvecklingen utan problem och svrigheter. Vi har sett bankkriser utvecklas och mnga gnger abrupta korrigeringar och stora svngningar av rnte- aktie- och valutakurser. Det gller inte minst i vrt eget land, men ocks i varierande utstrckning i vr omvrld. Globaliseringen av den finansiella sektorn har skapat en ny och svrare milj fr olika myndigheter svl p nationell som p internationell niv. Bildandet av EMU, med en enda valuta, kommer att skapa stabilare frhllanden inom Europa. Inriktningen p lg inflation och sunda statsfinanser gr ocks att den vergripande ekonomiska miljn kommer att befrmja en stabilare utveckling. Det hindrar emellertid inte att versynen och tillsynen av den finansiella sektorn mste fortstta att utvecklas och frfinas. Dessutom mste det internationella samarbetet ka mellan olika myndigheter, srskilt som problem i ett land numera i n hgre grad n tidigare kan spridas till andra lnder. Problemen i Mexiko frra vren r ett exempel p det. Vad kan d bildandet av EMU innebra fr utvecklingen av finanssektorn? Som just ppekats r det i grunden frga om att studera en process som pgtt i drygt ett decennium i ett delvis accelererande tempo. Denna utveckling skulle sannolikt ha varit likartad ven om EMU-projektet inte hade funnits, eftersom den kan ses som en naturlig fljd av de allmnna europeiska integrationsstrvandena. Dock kommer sjlvklart en gemensam valuta fr Europas lnder att kunna f intressanta konsekvenser fr det svenska finansiella systemet och drmed fr Riksbanken och Finansinspektionen. Lt mig diskutera ngra sdana tnkbara konsekvenser. Finansiella utvecklingstrender Frutom EMU r det flera utvecklingstrender som pverkar det finansiella systemet. Anpassningen efter avregleringarna p 1980-talet r nnu inte avslutad. Utvecklingen av den nya informationsteknologin kommer att fortstta pverka. Den demografiska trenden talar fr ett kat behov av pensionssparande. EU, NAFTA, GATT, de framvxande nya ekonomierna och den hga tillvxten i sydostasien tenderar att driva fram en globalisering av fretagandet. Det r naturligtvis svrt att entydigt peka p hur utvecklingen kommer att se ut. Men det mesta pekar p en fortsatt snabb utveckling av de finansiella marknaderna, med nya instrument och behov av clearing och avveckling. Konkurrenstrycket inom den traditionella banksektorn fortstter att ka, samtidigt som den lngsiktiga efterfrgan p finansiella tjnster expanderar kraftigt, men investerare och kapitalanvndare blir mer och mer sofistikerade. Om detta r en rimligt bedmning av framtiden kommer behovet av omstrukturering av det finansiella sektorn att ka, samtidigt finns behov av konsolidering fr att kunna klara de pfrestningar som en omvandlingsprocess fr med sig. Vad detta mer i detalj kommer att leda till r svrt att sga. Men det frefaller rimligt att anta att antalet institutioner minskar samtidigt som deras genomsnittliga storlek kar. Men vi kommer ocks att ha olika typer av specialiserade banker, sk. nischbanker. Dessutom torde den relativa storleken av traditionell bankinlning och utlning minskar och utbudet och efterfrgan p marknadsbaserade instrument kar sin relativa betydelse. Detta r i och fr sig ingenting nytt. Denna process har redan inletts. Det hr r krafter som redan i dag verkar. Till detta kommer EMU-processen. Ett svenskt medlemskap i EMU skulle kunna innebra att marknaden fr svenska statspapper blir mer eller mindre helt integrerad med den stora marknaden fr rntebrande papper emitterade av medlemsstaterna i den monetra unionen. Det r svrt att se att placerarna i lngden kommer att gra ngon strre tskillnad mellan vrdepapper emitterade av den svenska staten och vrdepapper emitterade av t.ex. den tyska eller nederlndska staten, i vart fall om skuldsttningen (och drmed kreditrisken) utjmnas ver tiden av att statsfinanserna bringas under varaktig kontroll. Slutsatsen skulle kunna bli att vi fr en enda avkastningskurva fr statliga rntebrande euro-papper inom EMU eller vart fall en situation dr olika lnders statsobligationer kommer att vara nra substitut. Detta betyder att frutsttningarna fr de nationella marknaderna fr rntepapper och deras derivat, som i dag, jmte valutamarknaden, r de volymmssigt strsta marknaderna, radikalt kan komma att ndras. En del menar att det i en sdan situation knappast r troligt att avista- och terminsmarknaderna fr svenska statspapper kommer att finnas kvar i Sverige, utan handeln med dessa papper kommer att ske p en stor europeisk marknad, i ngot finansiellt centrum, med svenska papper som en komponent i en strre eurodominerad marknad. Eftersom, som sagt, avistamarknaderna fr svenska statsskuldvxlar och s.k. bench-markobligationer i dag r mycket omfattande och de standardiserade terminerna p dessa instrument utgr den strsta svenska derivatmarknaden, innebr denna utveckling ett bortfall av finansiella marknader i Sverige.  andra sidan menar andra att det finns faktorer som talar fr att den svenska avistaoch terminsmarknaden kommer att finnas kvar ven vid ett svenskt medlemskap i EMU. Nrheten till en lokal marknad kan vara av fortsatt vikt eftersom marknadsaktrerna kan tnkas lgga ner mer resurser p bedmning av olika risker som r specifikt nationella. De bda synstten gr att man idag inte kan peka p en entydig utvecklingsriktning. Ett bortfall av finansiella marknader i Sverige kan - och br - naturligtvis ses som ett problem, men man kan ocks se det i positivt perspektiv. Det kan ge upphov till en ny utveckling. I Sverige finns visserligen marknader fr hypoteksinstrument, men de r vsentligt mindre aktiva och effektiva n sina motsvarigheter p statspapperssidan. Detta gller i nnu hgre grad marknaden fr industriobligationer - eller "corporate bonds" fr vilka beteckningen fretagsobligationer vore mera adekvat dr den svenska marknaden r helt outvecklad utom mjligen nr det gller den kortaste sidan med de s.k. fretagscertifikaten. Det r ingen orimlig tanke att ett eventuellt bortfall av nationella marknader fr statspapper och deras derivat stimulerar till en utveckling av hypoteksmarknaden inklusive derivat inom EMU. Huruvida svenska aktrer kommer att vara initiativtagare i denna process r svrt att spekulera i och r egentligen inte s intressant ur Riksbankens perspektiv. Det vsentliga r att svenska banker och hypoteksinstitut fr tillgng till en vsentligt breddad marknad fr hypotekspapper och deras derivat emitterade ver hela den monetra unionen. Det innebr bde mera likvida terminsoch optionsinstrument fr riskhantering och mjlighet till bttre diversifierade bostadspappersportfljer. Det skulle ocks innebra en vsentligt kad efterfrgan p den kunskap som behvs fr att rtt analysera och prisstta olika former av kreditrisk p hypoteksmarknaden. En sdan utveckling skulle vidare kunna stimulera industriobligationsmarknaden, dr bedmningen av kreditrisker och prissttningen av riskpremier stller ytterligare krav p kvalificerad analys. Ju strre volym marknaden fr, desto mer kan det lna sig fr stora investmentbanker att satsa p att bygga upp kompetens p detta omrde. Denna vrderings- och riskhanteringsteknologi kan sedan bli en vrdefull komponent i en annan mjlig och fr banksystemet synnerligen intressant utveckling. Det r ju s att medvetenheten och kunskapen hos olika finansfretag i Sverige svl som i Vsteuropa om riskexponering och riskkontroll har kat snabbt under senare tid. Med ngon frenkling kan man hvda att metoderna fr att mta och kontrollera s.k. marknadsrisker, t.ex. rnte- och valutarisker, r ganska vlutvecklade och knda av finansfretagen. Problemen kan ofta vara av lednings- och styrningskaraktr. Det gller att minimera risken fr missbruk och inkompetent hantering av typ Barings. Kreditrisk r dremot en notoriskt svrhanterlig materia, dr n s lnge fga av sofistikerade riskhanteringsmetoder utvecklats i Europa. Att dma av den senaste utvecklingen kan man emellertid vnta sig innovationer p detta omrde. I amerikanska banker pgr f.n. en intensiv utveckling av metoder fr att mta, vrdera och kontrollera kreditrisker vare sig de r frknippade med emissioner av "corporate bonds" eller med utlningsportfljer. ven den snabba utvecklingen av sk. kreditderivat i syfte att hantera och frdela kreditrisker br nmnas. En fljd av denna utveckling r de s.k. "loan sales". Dessa innebr att en bank sljer av delar av sina lnestockar till en eller flera andra banker och eventuellt i motsvarande grad fyller p sin balansrkning med inkp av ln beviljade av andra banker. Nr det gller de enskilda ln som ingr i dessa "loan sales" r det naturligtvis s att den bank som ursprungligen beviljade lnet behller tminstone en del av det i sin portflj. Anledningen r att banker p detta stt tydligare kan markera dels att det inte r dliga ln bankerna sljer av, dels att den inte frlorar incitamenten att fortsatt vervaka och eventuellt pverka lntagarnas ekonomiska stllning. Konsekvenserna blir likartade dem vi erhller med en vidgad marknad fr fretagsobligationer. Frutsttningar skapas fr en effektivare vrdering av kreditrisker och drmed kad diversifiering och riskspridning. ven om en sdan utveckling vad gller hanteringen av kreditrisker nd skulle komma med tiden, kan bildandet av den monetra unionen, dr all valutarisk r eliminerad mellan de ingende lnderna, stimulera utvecklingen. Andra utvecklingstrender r att betalningsfrmedling blir en kande intktsklla fr banker, t.ex. genom infrande av sk smart-cards. Vidare torde frmgenhetsfrvaltning kunna bli en vxande verksamhet, med tanke p den demografiska utvecklingen i Europa som jag tidigare talat om. Min analys har mest inriktats p instrument och risker. Man skulle ocks kunna g djupare och analysera mer institutionella aspekter. Med det menar jag hur EMUprocessen pverkar vissa typer av banker, t.ex stora eller sm banker och om de ligger i stora eller sm lnder. Man kan ocks frga sig om andra finansiella institut n banker kommer att vinna eller frlora marknadsandelar. Jag har heller inte kommit in p branschglidningsaspekter. Tiden medger emellertid inte att jag kommer lngre. Min pong har nog nd framkommit, dvs att bildandet av EMU kan f tmligen vittgende konsekvenser fr finansiella marknader och institutioner i Sverige och vriga Europa. Det blir en utveckling som kommer att ske utver de frndringskrafter som redan r igng. Denna typ av omvandling och utveckling av det finansiella systemet kommer att stlla stora krav p de myndigheter som har tillsyns- och vervakningsuppgifter. Det r uppgifter som Riksbanken kommer att arbeta ambitist med under kommande r. Avslutning ven om penningpolitiken kommer att beslutas i Frankfurt kommer vi i den svenska centralbanken inte att bli utan arbetsuppgifter. Lt mig ge ngra exempel. Den svenske riksbankschefen kommer att behva en analysfunktion som std fr den linje han eller hon skall driva i Frankfurt. Vidare kan man tnka sig att olika nationella centralbanker i Europa specialiserar sig p olika analysomrden, p samma stt som sker vid olika lokala Federal Reserve banker i USA. Dessutom diskuteras fr nrvarande om den gemensamma valutareserven skall frvaltas centralt i Frankfurt eller om det skall ske decentraliserat hos respektive nationell centralbank. Mycket talar ocks fr att sjlva utfrandet av de penningpolitiska operationerna, i vart fall till en brjan, kommer att ske decentraliserat hos varje centralbank i de olika deltagande lnderna. Drmed kommer vi alltjmt att ha ansvaret fr det nationella betalningssystemet. Till detta kan ven fogas ansvaret fr distributionen av sedlar och mynt. Det r idag en mycket stor del av vr verksamhet att se till att det finns betalningsmedel i hela landet. S kommer det att vara ocks i framtiden, ven om det p sedlarna och mynten kommer att st euro och inte krona. Till dessa arbetsuppgifter kommer att noga flja den finansiella sektorns utveckling i framtiden i syfte att frmja ett skert och effektivt betalningsvsende. Detta innebr sledes att stora krav kommer att kunna stllas ocks i framtiden p Riksbankens arbete, ven om vi precis som mnga andra kommer att frndra oss och anpassa resurser och arbetsuppgifter till de nya krav som bildandet av EMU kommer att ge upphov till. Title: Inflation and monetary policy
text: Inflation and monetary policy Date: 1998-03-21 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Location: Stora Aktiedagen in Trelleborg Thank you for the invitation to come here and discuss the Swedish economy and monetary policy. I will begin by briefly touching on the principles of monetary policy with an inflation target. Next, I will get into what assessments the Riksbank is making today about future inflation developments and what this means for monetary policy in the future. Before concluding with some conclusions for monetary policy, I discuss, in the light, among other things, of the large rise in share prices in recent years, what asset prices mean for monetary policy. 1. Monetary policy with inflation targeting The Riksbank's task is to shape Swedish monetary policy. The goal of the policy is stable prices in the Swedish economy. More precisely, this means that the change in CPI over the course of a year should be limited to 2 percent. However, deviations of /- 1% from this target are acceptable. By ensuring that the general price level does not change at too rapid a pace, monetary policy can contribute to the proper functioning of the economy. Different actors in the economy  consumers, savers and investors  can more easily make decisions about both consumption and investment if the general price level is stable. A rise in the price of a single product then reflects a shortage of this commodity and is not a sign of general inflation. Stable prices thus create good conditions for a reasonable allocation of resources and good growth in the economy. In addition, it reduces the risk of arbitrary income and wealth redistributions. Consumer price developments are thus the target variable of monetary policy. However, it takes time for a monetary policy change to have an impact on the economy and affect this variable. This delayed effect of monetary policy is usually estimated at around one to two years. Thus, it is not the latest, current inflation figure that is decisive for decisions on monetary policy, but the Riksbank must instead try to look ahead and estimate how inflation may develop over the next one to two years. The Riksbank's assessment of inflation developments in the economy is made continuously and presented in quarterly inflation reports. Many different indicators provide guidance on what inflationary pressures look like in the Swedish economy and how monetary policy should thus be designed. The Riksbank also carries out risk assessments of future inflation developments. Although the assessment remains unchanged with regard to inflation developments, heightened uncertainty may lead to greater caution in monetary policy. The Riksbank will then wait with interest rate changes until the situation has become further clearer. In this way, the changes in market interest rates will be smaller. This is also good for the general economic development. 2. The Riksbank's inflation assessment Let me then turn to the Riksbank's current assessment of inflation developments in the future. Is the objective of price stability achieved over one to two years' time without the need to change the repo rate? The assessment I am presenting here is based primarily on the inflation report published three weeks ago. Our estimates in this report relate to the period from the second quarter of 1999 to the first quarter of 2000. Inflation is roughly influenced by developments in the following areas; developments in the world around us and their impact on the Swedish economy via, among other things, the exchange rate, the demand and supply situation in Sweden, other cost shocks and temporary effects, as well as expectations about future inflation. I would like to set out here our views on developments in these areas. International business cycle and inflation Swedish price developments are affected by developments in the rest of the world via import prices and by the impact on the general demand situation in the Swedish economy. The impact of foreign prices on prices expressed in sek depends on how the exchange rate develops and on the extent to which import companies choose to allow price increases to take effect on prices expressed in sek. Developments in world market prices may also affect the competitive position of the export industry and thus have an impact on domestic wage growth and other production costs. The international discussion at the moment is, of course, very much influenced by developments in Asia. The impact of the Asian crisis and its repercussions on the world economy are difficult to assess. However, we assume that the economies of Asia will gradually recover after very weak growth this year. Provided that our assumption is correct, international development should be relatively good in the coming years, partly because the economy in Western Europe is increasingly strong. Nevertheless, inflationary pressures from abroad are expected to be moderate. To this contribute price-depressing effects of, among other things, the following: The Asian crisis in the commodity markets, but also in other areas of production. The development of the crown The development of the krona plays an important role in the Riksbank's assessments of price stability. There has been a tendency to weaken the krona over the past six months, although the trend has been in the opposite direction since mid-February. If a weakening becomes permanent, it will affect the inflation outlook and thus also the structure of monetary policy. In this context, let me digress about the Riksbank's view of the Swedish krona. Recently, in the debate, there have been interpretations about our monetary policy; that we would have a target for the Swedish krona exchange rate. This is a misconception. The Riksbank does not have a target for the Swedish krona exchange rate. The krona is one of the factors affecting inflation Therefore, the exchange rate is important for monetary policy during the variable exchange rate. If the exchange rate were to weaken for too long, the inflation forecast could end up above the target and then the Riksbank would have to react to defend the inflation target. Similarly, the Riksbank would react with appropriate measures if the krona strengthens in the long term. At the same time, of course, a stable exchange rate is fundamentally desirable. It makes it easier for everyone in the economy to make economic decisions and should thus  all other things being equal  lead to higher growth. In addition, Sweden is in a European context. As members of the European Union, we have a duty to regard our monetary policy as a matter of common interest. Nor can it be ruled out that Sweden will join EMU and the Riksdag made it clear in its decision on EMU last year that, as part of this, it could also be relevant to join the Krona to the European exchange rate system, the ERM. From this perspective, it is an advantage if the Swedish krona is reasonably stable. Today, most of the evidence suggests that EMU will in practice have a target for monetary policy that is very close to Swedish inflation, i.e. 2 percent inflation. In such a situation, the chances are good that the exchange rate between the krona and the euro will be stable. Demand and supply situation If demand is greater than can be produced and offered on the market in the long term, inflationary pressures arise. Monetary policy must therefore prevent the emergence of such imbalances. The Riksbank is looking at several different indicators to get an overall picture of how the relationship between demand and supply may affect inflation in the future. Overall, the Riksbank estimated in the Inflation Report that growth in the Swedish economy will be slightly lower than previously assumed. However, the course remains unchanged with an upturn in the economy in which domestic demand is gradually making an increasing contribution to the upturn. GDP is expected to grow by just over 2.5% in 1998 and by around 3% in 1999. If our forecast of a relatively good international economic development is correct, growth is expected to be good also in 2000. The stronger growth in domestic demand can be attributed to increased private consumption and increased investment in industry. Several factors suggest a continued upturn in private consumption in both 1998 and 1999. Household wealth has increased sharply as a result of rising share prices in recent years and more recently also as a result of rising property prices. I will come back to that later. In addition, fiscal policy will gradually become less tightening in 1998 and 1999. Therefore, for the first time since 1994, household disposable income is likely to increase appreciably in 1998. Households also have positive expectations about their own economy, even if these have slowed down somewhat. The bifurcation of the Swedish economy  with a strong export sector and a weak domestic sector  is thus expected to continue to decline. Since the presentation of the Inflation Report, some new statistics highlighting cyclical developments have been published, including national accounts for the last quarter of 1997. All in all, these statistics support the riksbank's assessment in the inflation report; the economy is strengthening, but the trend is not dramatic. Other cost disruptions and temporary effects Inflation impulses can also come from specific cost increases stemming neither from an international increase in inflation nor from a high domestic demand situation. Examples of such cost increases are temporarily rising commodity prices. Similar inflation impulses can also come from fiscal policy in the form of changes in indirect taxes and subsidies. Inflationary impulses of this nature are normally temporary. However, they can also affect inflation expectations and thus have an impact on the long-term inflation process. In order to get an idea of trend inflation (adjusted for temporary inflation impulses) and thus reach a deeper understanding of the inflation process, the Riksbank works with various measures of underlying inflation, among other things. In recent years, the temporary effects have played a major role in the development of the CPI. The fall in interest rates has led to significantly lower CPI inflation than otherwise. At the same time, for example, tobacco tax in 1997 pushed up inflation as measured by the CPI. Over the next two-year period, the Inflation Report assessed the tax and interest rate changes to largely cancel each other out; temporary effects would thus not affect the CPI to any great extent. The fall in commodity prices during the winter is interesting in this context. Presumably it is, at least in part, temporary. Inflation expectations A high demand situation in the economy leads producers to raise their prices and wage earners to demand increased wages. But expectations of high inflation in the future can also in themselves lead to inflationary price and wage increases, as economic actors strive to maintain or increase their incomes in real terms. Inflation expectations thus risk becoming self-fulfilling and therefore play a central role in the price formation process. The clearest example for us Swedes of how it can work is the wage price spiral of the 70s and 80s. The overall picture is that inflation expectations are low and relatively well in line with the inflation target. Most of the measurements, both implicit futures rates and surveys and forecasts, have shown that inflation expectations have fallen slightly recently. The low-inflation regime is about to be established. Inflationsprognos Economic activity is expected to increase over the next two years. This led us to the assessment in our latest Inflation Report that inflation will rise slightly from today's levels in 1998 and 1999. However, the upturn was expected to be cautious, partly due to good productivity growth. Inflation calculated as an annual average measured by CPI was estimated in the report to be 1.6 percent this year and 2.1 percent next year. In the light of the inflation figures received for February and oil price developments, it cannot be ruled out that inflation, as measured by the CPI, in 1998 will be slightly lower than forecast in the Inflation Report. So far, we have seen a limited impact at the consumer level of the fall in oil prices. At the same time, it is uncertain at what level the price of oil will stabilize. Moreover, underlying domestic inflation has not been affected by lower inflation as measured by the CPI. Although the lower outcome for the CPI in February seems to be mainly a consequence of temporary factors, it is a fact that the rate of price increase both in Sweden and abroad has become lower than expected in recent years. There are many explanations for this, of which in Sweden one of the most important is certainly the transition from a low-inflation regime with all that this entails in the form of changed pricing behavior, lower inflation expectations, etc. Structural reforms and increased competition have certainly also played a role. 3. Monetary policy and asset prices As I mentioned, developments in supply prices are expected to lead to an increase in domestic demand. Lately, this uptick has been glaring. While consumer prices have remained low and stable in most western countries, asset prices have risen sharply. During the 90s, Swedish consumer prices have risen by about 30 percent, while share prices during the same period increased by about 170 percent. The rise in share prices presupposes very good economic development in parallel with continued low interest rates. This is a development that raises questions for monetary policy. Do rising asset prices mean that inflationary pressures are manifesting themselves in a different guise than in rising consumer prices or are there other risks with rising asset prices? How should monetary policy respond to these changes? The wealth effects of rising asset prices and the effects this in turn can have on demand and inflation are one reason that has been highlighted why monetary policy should take greater account of developments in asset prices. Another reason is the financial instability that excessive price rises can cause. I will now explain in a little more detail what these connections look like. Effects on the demand situation Higher asset prices can affect consumption prices both through increased consumption and through increased investments. As households' assets rise in value, their wealth also rises. This can lead to increased consumption. Rising share prices also make it cheaper for companies to obtain capital for investments, which is why investment activity may also be accelerated by rising asset prices. Experience shows that household behaviour is more affected than firms by rising asset prices. This applies at least to household behavior in the long term of rising stock prices. Over a longer period of time, it seems natural that households regard rising share prices as a real addition to wealth, thereby increasing life income and thus gives greater scope for consumption. In the short term, however, the correlation appears to be weaker for several reasons. One of these is that a large percentage of the households that own shares have relatively high income and large wealth. These households have a relatively low propensity to consume. They place long-term and are likely to place less emphasis on short-term price fluctuations. Another reason is that a large proportion of the shareholding consists of pension savings. Thus, the long-term nature of savings is also found in groups other than just high-income groups. Effects on financial stability Another reason that has been highlighted for a more prominent role in the formulation of monetary policy is the possible impact of these prices on the stability of the financial system. The Asian crisis and the Swedish banking crisis in the early 90s are clear examples of the effects that a bursting financial bubble can have on the banking system, although in these cases it is mainly a matter of large exposure to the real estate market. The consequences of crises of this kind can be major costs for the national economy. This would suggest that central banks are trying to prevent such excessive price movements from taking place at an early stage. However, there are reasons against a central bank trying to counteract the rise in asset prices at an early stage via monetary policy. The main reason, of course, is the difficulty of being able to discern what is really excessive price development and thus can be termed as a price bubble. It is usually possible to point to some fundamental factors that can seemingly explain the rise in prices. In such a situation, determining how much of a price increase is justified is a very difficult task. Moreover, the arguments for an early reaction to price bubbles in the stock market are weaker compared to those for the real estate market. This is because, as I have said before, banks in most countries are more exposed to risks in the real estate market than to risks in the stock market. A crash in the stock market should thus have less impact on the stability of the financial system and thus on activity in the economy in the medium term. Asset prices and monetary policy The question of how monetary policy should manage and respond to changes in asset prices is a complex one. The Riksbank's target of stable prices does not currently include prices for financial and real assets such as shares and real estate. This type of pricing is not included in the target variable, CPI. The Riksbank is certainly closely monitoring developments in asset prices both to make a general assessment of inflationary pressures and to evaluate whether there are risks to financial stability. However, Swedish monetary policy does not react directly to rising asset prices to the same extent as, for example, to rising goods and services prices. An important reason why the Riksbank does not react immediately is that these prices are not always an indication of future inflation developments and that it will thus be difficult for central banks to identify which occasions require an adjustment of policy. However, one possibility that always exists is to contribute to a broader discussion of asset prices and to highlight the risks arising from a valuation in the stock or real estate markets that presupposes a very favorable economic development going forward. 4. Conclusion and conclusions In assessing how monetary policy should be designed, the Riksbank looks ahead in time to estimate how inflation will develop over the next two years. Our goal is stable prices in the economy. In our latest inflation report, we estimated that inflation will rise slightly over the next two years, albeit at a slightly slower pace than we previously expected. The uncertainty in the assessment led us to the conclusion that the Riksbank should be vigilant about developments going forward. Developments suggested a cautious tightening of monetary policy over the next year. Since the presentation of the Inflation Report, new statistics have been published. However, this does not bring about any major changes in our view of developments. Information received on inflation expectations and wage agreements confirms our previous assessment. The exchange rate development  with a slightly stronger krona  is also more in line with our forecast in the Inflation Report. The same applies to the information received on cyclical developments. However, some figures have turned out to be weaker than expected. International inflation is low and Swedish inflation measured by the CPI was weaker in February than we previously assumed. The reason for the latter was mainly lower prices for clothes and shoes and a certain decline in long-term interest rates. Added to this is a fall in commodity prices that could have a slight impact on the CPI figures for the next few months. However, these developments are likely to be mostly temporary and so far have had little impact on underlying domestic inflation. Overall, inflationary pressures in the short term could be marginally lower than we thought in the Inflation Report. However, the statistics mainly support the forecast in the slightly longer term. The conclusion of the latest Inflation Report was that the repo rate should not change at this time, but that some cautious tightening was likely to occur in the coming year. The information received after the publication of the Inflation Report does not alter this conclusion.

Samtidigt som konsumentpriserna frblivit lga och stabila i merparten av lnderna i vstvrlden, har tillgngspriserna stigit kraftigt. Under 90-talet har de svenska konsumentpriserna stigit med ca 30 procent, medan aktiekurserna under samma period kat med ca 170 procent. Aktieprisuppgngen frutstter en mycket god ekonomisk utveckling parallellt med fortsatt lga rntor. Det hr r en utveckling som reser frgor fr penningpolitiken. Innebr de stigande tillgngspriserna att inflationstrycket visar sig i en annan skepnad n i stigande konsumentpriser eller finns det andra risker med stigande tillgngspriser? Hur ska penningpolitiken reagera p dessa frndringar? De frmgenhetseffekter som stigande tillgngspriser ger upphov till och de effekter detta i sin tur kan f p efterfrgan och inflation r ett skl som framhllits till att penningpolitiken i hgre grad br ta hnsyn till tillgngsprisernas utveckling. Ett annat skl r den finansiella instabilitet som verdrivna prisuppgngar kan orsaka. Jag ska nu redogra lite nrmare fr hur dessa samband ser ut. Effekter p efterfrgelget Hgre tillgngspriser kan pverka konsumtionspriserna svl via kad konsumtion som via kade investeringar. D hushllens tillgngar stiger i vrde stiger ven deras frmgenhet. Detta kan leda till kad konsumtion. Stigande aktiepriser leder ven till att det blir billigare fr fretagen att erhlla kapital till investeringar, varfr ven investeringsaktiviteten kan tillta av stigande tillgngspriser. Erfarenheten visar att hushllens beteende pverkas mer n fretagen av stigande tillgngspriser. Detta gller tminstone hushllens beteende p lng sikt av stigande aktiepriser. ver en lngre tidsperiod verkar det naturligt att hushllen betraktar stigande aktiekurser som ett reellt tillskott till frmgenheten som drmed kar livsinkomsten och sledes ger strre utrymme fr konsumtion. P kort sikt frefaller emellertid sambandet vara svagare av flera skl. Ett av dessa r att en stor andel av de hushll som ger aktier har relativt hg inkomst och stor frmgenhet. Dessa hushll har en relativt lg bengenhet att konsumera. De placerar lngsiktigt och lgger sannolikt mindre vikt vid kortsiktiga prisfluktuationer. Ett annat skl r att en stor andel av aktieinnehavet utgrs av pensionssparande. Lngsiktigheten i sparandet terfinns sledes ven i andra grupper n enbart hginkomstgrupperna. Effekter p finansiell stabilitet Ett annat skl som framhllits till att tillgngspriserna br f en mer framtrdande roll i utformningen av penningpolitiken r dessa prisers mjliga pverkan p stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet. Den asiatiska krisen och den svenska bankkrisen i brjan av 90-talet r tydliga exempel p vilka effekter en sprucken finansiell bubbla kan f fr banksystemet ven om det i dessa fall frmst handlar om en stor exponering mot fastighetsmarknaden. Konsekvenserna av kriser av det hr slaget kan bli stora kostnader fr samhllsekonomin. Det frmsta sklet r givetvis svrigheten att kunna urskilja vad som r verkligen r verdriven prisutveckling och drmed kan betecknas som en prisbubbla. Det r oftast mjligt att peka p ngra fundamentala faktorer som till synes kan frklara prisuppgngen. Att i ett sdant lge bestmma hur stor del av en prisuppgng som r berttigad r en mycket svr uppgift. Argumenten fr en tidig reaktion p prisbubblor i aktiemarknaden r dessutom svagare jmfrt med de fr fastighetsmarknaden. Detta beror p att banker i de flesta lnder som jag tidigare sagt r mer exponerade fr risker i fastighetsmarknaden n fr risker i aktiemarknaden. En krasch p aktiemarknaden borde drmed f mindre effekter p stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet och drmed p aktiviteten i ekonomin p medellng sikt. Tillgngspriser och penningpolitiken Frgan hur penningpolitiken br hantera och reagera p frndringar i tillgngspriserna r komplicerad. Riksbankens ml om stabila priser inkluderar i dagslget inte priser p finansiella och reala tillgngar ssom aktier och fastigheter. Denna typ av priser ingr inte i mlvariabeln, KPI. Riksbanken fljer frvisso noga utvecklingen i tillgngspriserna bde fr att gra en allmn bedmning av inflationstrycket och fr att vrdera om det finns risker fr den finansiella stabiliteten. Den svenska penningpolitiken reagerar dock inte direkt p stigande tillgngspriser i samma utstrckning som t.ex. p stigande varu- och tjnstepriser. Ett viktigt skl till att Riksbanken inte reagerar direkt r att dessa priser inte alltid r en indikation p framtida inflationsutveckling och att det drmed blir svrt fr centralbankerna att identifiera vilka tillfllen som krver en anpassning av politiken. Vr mlsttning r stabila priser i ekonomin. I vr senaste inflationsrapport gjorde vi bedmningen att inflationen stiger ngot de kommande tv ren om n i ngot lngsammare takt n vad vi tidigare frvntat oss. Oskerheten i bedmningen ledde oss till slutsatsen att Riksbanken br vara vaksam p utvecklingen framver. Utvecklingen talade fr en frsiktig tstramning av penningpolitiken under det nrmaste ret. Sedan inflationsrapporten presenterades har ny statistik publicerats. Dennaa medfr emellertid inte ngra stora frndringar i vr syn p utvecklingen. Denna utveckling r dock sannolikt till strsta delen tillfllig och hittills har den i liten utstrckning pverkat den underliggande inhemska inflationen. Sammantaget kan inflationstrycket p kort sikt bli marginellt lgre n vad vi trodde i inflationsrapporten. Statistiken ger emellertid i huvudsak std fr prognosen p ngot lngre sikt. Title: BcBS prioritises risk-weighted assets in the finalisation of the Basel III framework
text: Ingves: Basel Committee prioritises risk-weighted assets in finalising basel III framework Date: 2015-10-12 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Lima Much of the work on Basel III has been completed. However, the outstanding regulations need to be finalised. The different regulations must also be calibrated and analyzed together to gain an even better understanding of their weighted effect. A central part of this work is to reduce unjustified differences in the calculations of risk-weighted assets. Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves talked about this when, in his role as chair of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), he attended a conference organised by the Institute of International Finance (IIF) on the occasion of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in Lima, Peru, on 9 October 2015. The Basel Committee's work plan now focuses on finalising outstanding reforms and striking a good balance between simplicity, risk sensitivity and the comparability of capital adequacy rules. Work in the coming year will include: work to increase the comparability of the calculations of risk-weighted assets in banks' internal models, make proposals for the final design of the standard credit risk and operational risk methodologies, and, finalise the market risk standard He also noted that some regulatory adjustments may remain as the Basel Committee is required to take into account both external views on the major policy proposals and the results of the quantitative impact assessments. Furthermore, the calibration consists of a number of important elements, such as the leverage ratio requirement. "Although I have not touched on it today in my comments, by the end of the year the Basel Committee will also be able to present the results of its strategic review of the capital framework. This will provide further clarity on how the Committee intends to address the issue of unwanted variability in the risk-weighted assets," Ingves concluded.

Title: Changing payment market and the Riksbank's control system
text: Ingves: Changing payment market and the Riksbank's control system The Riksbank is working in progress to review how the interest rate management system can be developed in order to continue to be an effective tool for achieving the goal of price stability. "We are currently thinking about how we can design a robust, transparent and automated interest rate management system that can also effectively control market interest rates in the future," Ingves said today when speaking at a conference at the International Capital Markets Association in Stockholm. Date: 2019-05-16 12:45 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: ICMA  International Capital Market Association One of the Riksbank's main tasks is price stability, i.e. low and stable inflation. By raising or lowering the Riksbank's key interest rate, the repo rate, the Riksbank affects other interest rates in Sweden, which affects demand in the Swedish economy and thus inflation. In order for short-term market interest rates to be close to the Riksbank's key interest rate, the Riksbank has an interest rate management system. The Riksbank's interest rate management system has a strong connection to the Riksbank's payment system, RIX. Today, the demand for instant payments around the clock is increasing and the Riksbank's payment system needs to be modernized to meet the demands placed on speed and availability. Since the Riksbank's control system is interconnected with the payment system, the Riksbank also needs to think about how interest rate management systems can be changed to be sufficiently robust and flexible to be able to meet the challenges that follow a changing payment market. "We intend to get back to you with more details on how our concerns are going within the next few months," Ingves said. Title: Central banks' activities  post-crisis direction of travel
text: Ingves: Central bank operations  the direction of travel after the crisis Date: 2013-10-04 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Royal Bank of Scotland, Stockholm The most important conclusion of the financial crisis is that greater account must be taken of debt developments in the economy in the future. Different countries are now choosing slightly different paths to do this. Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves said this on Friday in a speech at royal bank of scotland in Stockholm. Stefan Ingves sums up his speech. The Riksbank was one of the central banks that first and most clearly raised risks of financial imbalances, such as the development of household debt and house prices, on its monetary policy agenda, and has also pursued policies that have tried to take these risks into account. The policy has been well in line with the international discussion after the crisis and also well compatible with the task of keeping the macroeconomy in balance, the Governor of the Riksbank said. But stabilising the economy and reaching the inflation target while taking into account risks associated with debt with only one instrument, the repo rate, is a difficult task, Ingves noted. The post-crisis international discussion has therefore largely revolved around how the new policy area macroprudential policy area should be designed in order to best prevent and manage financial crises. Many countries have already come a long way in designing a macroprudential framework. In Sweden, it was unclear for a long time what the political side intended this to look like, but a few weeks ago the government decided. Much of the exact details remain to be specified, but it is clear that the Financial Supervisory Authority will have the main responsibility for macroprudential tools. It is good that the division of responsibilities has now been clarified and that the responsibility has ended up in an authority, the Governor of the Riksbank pointed out. Other countries have certainly chosen other solutions, but which ones turn out to work best in the end, the future will tell, Ingves noted. Nevertheless, there are questions that may need to be considered further. Among other things, it is important to clarify what the relationship between macroprudential policy and monetary policy should look like and whether there may be situations where macroprudential policy needs the support of monetary policy. "I am confident that we will succeed in this, with joint efforts and as knowledge increases about how the upcoming new macroprudential framework works in practice," the Governor concluded. Title: Current and future payment systems
text: Ingves: Today's and the future's payment systems "The public should be able to pay digitally with money issued by the state," riksbank governor Stefan Ingves said in his speech today at the conference DI Framtidens payments. Date: 2019-11-05 15:20 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Place: Conference DI Future Payments In the wake of the increasing digitalization, there are now rapid changes in the payment market and central banks around the world therefore need to think new. The Riksbank also needs to review what services we offer and what new technologies we can adopt in order to continue to be able to pay in a safe and efficient way. "An e-krona is similar to cash government money, but in digital form. As cash is now rapidly decreasing in importance, it is urgent to investigate the future of the e-krona and make decisions about what the role of the state and the Riksbank should look like in the payment systems of the future," Ingves continued. The question of the future of the e-krona is something the Riksdag needs to decide on. Ingves ended his speech with four ambitions for the Swedish payments market: There must be sufficient cash in case the electronic systems fail. There will be digital government money as legal tender, an e-krona, issued by the Riksbank. It should be possible to make instant payments in Swedish kronor, with state money, around the clock. There should be the possibility of making instant payments between currencies around the clock. Ingves today also published a debate article with the headline "How we secure the Swedish krona" where he presents his vision of money. He notes that government money is still needed and that the Riksbank is working to ensure that it is quick, safe and cheap to pay within and between countries, around the clock. Title: The monetary policy toolbox when the policy rate is close to its lower bound
text: Ingves: The monetary policy toolbox as the policy rate is close to its lower limit Date: 2015-03-06 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Location: SNS/SIFR Finanspanel, Stockholm What complementary monetary policy measures can be used in a situation where the policy rate is close to its lower limit? Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves discusses this issue when he participates in the SNS/SIFR financial panel on Friday morning. "Inflation in Sweden is currently low. In order for inflation to rise towards the target, the repo rate has been lowered to a very low level. In addition, the Riksbank has initiated purchases of government bonds," explains Ingves. "But there are several ways to make monetary policy more expansionary. We can and will do more if necessary," he notes. In other countries, too, a number of accompanying measures have been used. The choice has been made, among other things, of how well the transmission mechanism has worked in the countries concerned. Common to complementary monetary policy measures, however, is that they lower the general interest rate situation and increase the amount of money in society, thus affecting the economy. Ingves points out that the Riksbank is prepared to make monetary policy even more expansionary if necessary for inflation to rise towards its target. "We can lower the repo rate further and push rate hikes into the future, buy more government bonds or provide loans to companies through the banks. We also don't want to rule out currency interventions," says Ingves. The link contains the pictures that Ingves shows during his presentation at SNS/SIFR's financial panel.

Title: The economic situation  Starting point for current monetary policy
text: Ingves: The economic situation - Starting point for current monetary policy Date: 2016-03-15 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Affe4rsve4rlden, Bank & Finans 2016, Nalen, Stockholm Inflation is very low in many countries in the world around us. Several central banks are therefore pursuing a very expansionary monetary policy. The situation with low inflation and low interest rates is thus not unique to Sweden. This is emphasized by Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves when he speaks at Affe4rsve4rlden's event Bank & Finans 2016 on Tuesday. Small, open economies such as Sweden are highly dependent on the world around us and cannot ignore developments in other countries and the level of international interest rates, as this affects Swedish growth and employment - and thus inflation. The external situation and low energy prices are now contributing to a longer period of low inflation in Sweden. This increases the risk of weakening confidence in the inflation target. Therefore, the Executive Board lowered the repo rate on 10 February. The low interest rate environment has contributed to a strengthening of the Swedish economy, a fall in unemployment and an increase in inflation and inflation expectations. At the same time, the low interest rate environment contributes to inflated balance sheets and rising household debt. This must be addressed in order to avoid poor socio-economic development later on. So there is a very unusual situation with many considerations. But the inflation target is a common benchmark that has helped create stable rules of the game in the economy for over 20 years - and that is important to defend. Title: Structural reforms in the housing market are needed
text: Ingves: Structural reforms are needed in the housing market Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves today gave a speech at DI's banking conference in Stockholm. He stated that high household indebtedness is the biggest risk in the Swedish economy. Housing policy has led to a skewed system in which certain groups can pursue housing careers. Date: 2019-05-14 10:40 Speaker: Stefan Ingves Place: DI's banking conference, Stockholm Ingves began his presentation by justifying the Executive Board's latest monetary policy decision at the end of April. Activity in the Swedish economy is high and the economic outlook looks good, even when the economy enters a phase of slightly lower growth than before. Inflation has been at target for some time, but inflationary pressures are a little weaker than expected. The Riksbank's forecast is that interest rates will be raised again towards the end of the year or early next year. Ingves also highlighted the challenges that exist in the housing market. "We have been living with problems in the housing market for a long time. Rising house prices have led to an unsustainable increase in household debt. But, among other things, the macroprudential measures that FI has introduced seem to have ultimately contributed to the price development being somewhat dampened. But high household indebtedness remains the biggest risk in the Swedish economy." Ingves continued to talk about housing policy favoring certain groups that can make housing careers. "Those who are in the housing market, so-called "insiders", benefit from good opportunities to make money on their housing, they can make various deductions on their accommodation such as interest deductions, RUT and ROT deductions. But several other groups are outside the housing market, so-called "outsiders", they have no opportunity to take part in this development and few have the opportunity to save up for a cash contribution with only their salary. This has led to a skewed system that is now being patched and mended with various macroprudential measures instead of structural reforms. In order to address the fundamental problems in the housing market, it is urgent that measures are taken in housing and tax policy". Title: Efficient payment systems and the Riksbank's approach to cash distribution
text: Ingves: Efficient payment systems and the Riksbank's approach to cash distribution Datum: 2016-09-20 Talare: Riksbankschef Stefan Ingves Plats: Money and Banking Conference, Central Bank of Argentina, Buenos Aires, Argentina On Tuesday, Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves will talk about the use of cash in Sweden and the Riksbank's role in promoting an efficient payment system at a conference arranged by Argentina's central bank. He describes Sweden's path towards a society with less and less use of cash. The Swedish payment market began to form almost 100 years ago, when Postgirot (now Plusgirot) was created. This led to the banks together creating Bankgirot as a counterweight. "This was the beginning of a series of collaborations between the Swedish banks that are still ongoing today. This contributes to Swedish households and companies having access to appropriate payment services with which they can reach all payees," says Ingves. Other examples of such collaborations are the decision not to create a national bank card; without using the global card brands, Swish and ATM. He also believes that tech-savvy households and companies together with a well-developed telecommunications and broadband network are important reasons for the large use of electronic payment services in Sweden. The Riksbank's role in cash distribution after 2005 has given banks and cash carriers incentives to streamline the distribution and circulation of cash. This was because the costs of handling cash became visible. "Together, all these factors have contributed to a long-term trend of falling cash use and where Sweden is one of the countries that uses the least cash in the world. Whether this trend continues unabated and how we will pay tomorrow is an open question," said Ingves.

Title: Flexibility crucial for the Riksbank at a time of change
text: Ingves: Flexibility crucial for the Riksbank at a time of change "Our economic environment is constantly changing and as a central bank we must then have mandates and instruments that can be used flexibly both in normal times and in crisis." This is what Stefan Ingves said when he spoke today at the Swedish Economic Association about how the financial environment has changed in recent decades and how the Riksbank is meeting the challenges that this entails. Date: 2021-05-31 12:30 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Nationalekonomiska foreningen (Digital) Changes create new challenges Over the past 10-20 years, technological developments, globalisation and various reforms have changed the financial environment. The financial sector has become an increasingly important part of the economy. We have new players, new services and new financial innovations. "The changes are fundamentally positive and contribute to favourable economic development. But they also bring new risks and challenges for society," Ingves pointed out. E-kronor  new cash? Ingves gave several examples of changes that affect the Riksbank's operations. Firstly, we Swedes no longer pay in the same way. Electronic payments are knocking out cash. "In order for the public to have access to central bank money also in the future, we at the Riksbank are investigating the possibility of introducing an e-krona that would then exist in parallel with physical cash," Ingves explained. The financial system has become more integrated and risky Secondly, the integration of international financial markets means that national financial market policies have been given less room for manoeuvre and more difficult to maintain financial stability. "This calls for more cooperation at the supranational level. I therefore believe that Sweden, which has large cross-border banks, should consider membership of the banking union," Ingves said. Monetary policy must be flexible Thirdly, monetary policy instruments need to be fit for purpose and flexible in order for the Riksbank to be able to carry out its tasks and deal with the challenges posed by the changes in the financial system. This means that large bond purchases will probably play a bigger role than before when we want to influence interest rates and contribute to financial stability. The Government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act is problematic However, in its proposal for a new Riksbank Act, the Government has restricted the Riksbank's ability to use its instruments in a flexible way. What is particularly problematic is the artificial division between the Riksbank's core tasks: price stability and safeguarding the financial system. The split means that the Riksbank cannot act as quickly and forcefully in the next crisis as we could have done during the pandemic. Namely, the new law requires us to first determine what is the main purpose of each action and conditions and procedures differ depending on the purpose. Another problem with the bill that Ingves mentioned is that the new legislation does not comply with EU law and that it is not clear how the Riksbank should handle issues where national legislation conflicts with EU law. "The government's proposal will thus make it more difficult for the Riksbank in the future to quickly, flexibly and efficiently implement measures when needed - thereby increasing the risks for the Swedish economy. In my opinion, this is the wrong way to go if politicians and citizens still want an independent central bank that can act with vigour to stabilize the economy with its entire balance sheet", concluded Stefan Ingves. Det betyder att stora obligationskp frmodligen kommer att spela en strre roll n tidigare nr vi vill pverka rntorna och bidra till finansiell stabilitet. Regeringens frslag till ny riksbankslag r problematisk Regeringen har dock i sitt frslag till ny riksbankslag inskrnkt Riksbankens mjligheter att anvnda sina instrument p ett flexibelt stt. Det som framfr allt r problematiskt r den konstlade uppdelningen mellan Riksbankens krnuppgifter: prisstabilitet och att vrna det finansiella systemet. Uppdelningen innebr att Riksbanken inte kan agera lika snabbt och kraftfullt i nsta kris som vi kunnat gra under pandemin. Den nya lagen krver nmligen att vi frst bestmmer vad som r det huvudsakliga syftet med varje tgrd och villkor och procedurer skiljer sig t beroende p syftet. Ett annat problem med lagfrslaget som Ingves nmnde r att den nya lagstiftningen inte verensstmmer med EU-rtten och att det inte framgr hur Riksbanken ska hantera frgor dr nationell lagstiftning str i konflikt med EU-rtten. Regeringens frslag kommer allts att gra det svrare fr Riksbanken att i framtiden snabbt, flexibelt och effektivt stta in tgrder nr det behvs - och drmed kar riskerna fr svensk ekonomi. Enligt min mening r detta fel vg att g om politiker och medborgare fortfarande vill ha en sjlvstndig centralbank som med kraft kan agera fr att stabilisera ekonomin med hela sin balansrkning, avslutade Stefan Ingves. Title: From the Vasa to the Basel framework: The dangers of instability
text: Ingves: From the Vasa to the Basel framework: The dangers of instability Date: 2015-11-02 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Madrid In his role as chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves spoke on Monday about the future work of the Basel Committee, at a conference organized by the Asociacion de Mercados Financieros in Madrid. He took his starting point in the historical event of 1628, when the Vasa ship went to the bottom. The Basel Committee's work on Basel III aims to address the shortcomings in the global regulatory framework that were highlighted in the context of the financial crisis. The completion of the reform package that makes up Basel III is within clear reach, Ingves noted. He explained that further work now focuses on finalising the remaining reforms and finding a good balance between simplicity, comparability and risk sensitivity in the capital adequacy rules. The reforms that remain can be divided into three broad categories: increase the risk sensitivity and robustness of the standardised approaches to credit, market and operational risk, review the role of internal models in the capital framework, and complete the design and calibration of leverage ratio requirements and risk weight floors. "In my speech today, I have touched on a historical event that many have already forgotten  I am of course referring to the recent financial crisis rather than the Vasa ship. The Basel Committee will remain attentive to the lessons learned from the crisis to help create a stable regulatory framework. This lays the foundation for a sustainable financial system, which in turn supports the real economy," Ingves concluded.

Han frklarade att det fortsatta arbetet nu fokuserar p att frdigstlla terstende reformer och hitta en bra balans mellan enkelhet, jmfrbarhet och riskknslighet i kapitaltckningsreglerna. "I mitt anfrande idag har jag berrt en historisk hndelse som mnga redan har glmt  jag syftar naturligtvis till den senaste finanskrisen snarare n Vasaskeppet. Baselkommittn kommer vara fortsatt uppmrksam p lrdomarna frn krisen fr att bidra till att skapa ett stabilt regelverk. Detta lgger grunden fr ett hllbart finansiellt system, som i sin tur stdjer den reala ekonomin", avslutade Ingves. Title: Hearing on financial stability
text: Ingves in the Finance Committee: Hearing on financial stability Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves today visited the Riksdag's Finance Committee for a hearing on the Riksbank's work on financial stability. Date: 2019-02-05 09:00 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Place: Second Chamber Hall, Riksdagen, Stockholm "Structural problems in the housing market and the design of the tax system have contributed to Swedish households being highly indebted". This is what Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves said when he began his report on the current situation at the Riksdag's Finance Committee by highlighting household debt as the biggest risk to financial stability. Ingves advocated a holistic approach combining measures in several policy areas to address the structural problems of the housing market and reduce the risks of household indebtedness. Ingves went on to address the vulnerability of the Swedish banking system, which is large, concentrated and linked to small equity. These vulnerabilities require banks to strengthen their resilience  both in terms of capital and liquidity. In the discussions under the heading "Ten years after the financial crisis  are the regulations effective?" highlighted the lesson that financial crises are very costly for the national economy and robust regulations are required to avoid them. Much has been done to strengthen the regulatory framework since the crisis, but more needs to be done. The Riksbank believes, among other things, that the banks' capital in relation to total assets should increase and that it is important that the banks themselves insure themselves against liquidity risks in different currencies. In addition, the size of foreign exchange reserves must be sufficient in the event of the next financial crisis. Minister of Finance and Housing Per Bolund, Director General of the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority, Erik Thedeen, and Director General of the Swedish National Debt Office Hans Lindblad also participated in the committee's hearing. Ingves fortsatte med att ta upp srbarheten i det svenska banksystemet som r stort, koncentrerat och sammanlnkat med litet eget kapital. Dessa srbarheter gr att bankerna behver strka sin motstndskraft  bde vad gller kapital och likviditet. I diskussionerna under rubriken "Tio r efter finanskrisen  r regelverken effektiva?" framhvde Ingves lrdomen att finanskriser r vldigt kostsamma fr samhllsekonomin och det krvs robusta regelverk fr undvika dem. Mycket har gjorts fr att strka upp regelverken sedan krisen men mer behver gras. On the other hand, both Floden and Ingves are concerned about developments in the housing market and household indebtedness. Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Ingves in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2016-09-27 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament Monetary policy has contributed to strengthening Sweden's economy. This is what Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Per Jansson say when they participate today in this year's second hearing on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. Stefan Ingves begins the hearing by stating that monetary policy works well and provides support for the Swedish economy. The economy is strengthening and inflation is rising. At the same time, he points out the Swedish economy's great dependence on the world around us. The global economic recovery remains fraught with uncertainty, while monetary policy is generally very expansionary. "The low interest rate situation in the rest of the world spills over onto us and is something that Swedish monetary policy must relate to," says Ingves, mentioning in this context the importance of the exchange rate for inflation developments. As before, Ingves also highlights the problems in the Swedish housing market in his introduction. "Interest rates now need to be low to defend the inflation target. At the same time, household debt continues to increase and this is not sustainable in the long run. In this respect, we in Sweden live dangerously", says Ingves. In order for us to have stable economic development also in the longer term, measures from other policy areas are therefore needed that limit the growth in household debt, Ingves concludes. In his introduction, Per Jansson recalls the situation at the beginning of 2015. The low inflation then left a mark on inflation expectations, which fell further and further from the target. At the same time, there was a risk that the low interest rates in the rest of the world would mean that the krona would strengthen sharply, which would not only have weakened the chances of raising inflation but also weakened the competitiveness of Swedish exports. "The risks in the spring of 2015 when the ECB started its major asset purchases are underestimated by many, it was a dangerous situation," says Jansson. The Riksbank's monetary policy, with a negative repo rate and purchases of government bonds, has contributed to the situation now looking better. But the inflation picture needs to be even better for us to feel safe, he concludes.

Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Ingves in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2016-11-15 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Place: First Chamber Hall, Riksdagen, Stockholm Today, Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and First Deputy Governor Kerstin af Jochnick will participate in this year's third hearing on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. "It is a challenge in Sweden to keep both inflation and growth higher than in Europe on average. But so far we are well on our way to making it," Ingves said in his introduction to the hearing. The expansionary monetary policy in Sweden and in other countries is necessary to stimulate economic growth and counteract the risks of too low inflation, according to Ingves. But at the same time, he points out that the generally low interest rate environment contributes to increased risk-taking in the economy, highly valued assets and increased debt. "It is highly important to have targeted measures in macroprudential policy, housing policy and tax policy so that the stability of the Swedish economy is not compromised," Ingves emphasizes. "We must not forget the central role that the inflation target plays for the national economy," says af Jochnick. In her presentation, she points out not only that inflation has become lower and more stable since the inflation target was introduced, but also that Swedes have gained greater purchasing power and more stable wage growth. "The inflation target is a cornerstone of economic policy worth defending." She shows how the Riksbank's monetary policy, with a negative repo rate and purchases of government bonds, has had the intended effect. Inflation expectations have risen and the strong economic development in Sweden suggests that inflation will rise in the future.
