Title: The Riksbank does not track any wage shocks
text: Jansson: Riksbank predicts no wage shocks Date: 2015-09-15 Speaker: Deputy Governor Per Jansson Location: LO, Stockholm "The Riksbank is not predicting any wage shocks in the coming round of collective bargaining. What we see in front of us is a normal wage trend that does not threaten Sweden's competitiveness." This is what Deputy Governor Per Jansson said when he today gives a presentation at lo. Sweden has had stable wage formation since the 90s when the industrial agreement was concluded and the inflation target was created. Although inflation has at times deviated from the 2% inflation target, it has nevertheless served as a common starting point for the social partners in their wage negotiations. Jansson points out that this in itself has benefited the general economic development in Sweden. Among other things, this has contributed to greater purchasing power and more stable wage formation. Large fluctuations in prices and wages make it more difficult for all actors and create socio-economic costs. Instead, stable rules of the game and predictability reduce uncertainty and create stability in the economy. But in recent years, inflation has been too low. The Riksbank has therefore taken strong measures to bring inflation closer to its target. The repo rate has been significantly reduced and is now  0.35 percent. In addition, extensive purchases of Swedish government bonds are carried out. This has contributed to inflation clearly rising since last year. It is important that inflation continues to rise and establishes itself at a level around 2 percent. Such a development contributes to long-term inflation expectations that are consistent with the inflation target and stable developments in the Swedish labour market. "We expect fairly normal developments in the economy, productivity and inflation in the coming years. This suggests that wages are increasing in line with a historical average of 3.23.5 percent," jansson concludes.

Title: Monetary policy supports the recovery and inflation
text: Jansson hearing in the Finance Committee: Monetary policy supports recovery and inflation The Swedish economy has withstood the second wave of the spread of infection relatively well, supported by extensive economic policy measures. This is what Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves said in his introduction when he and Deputy Governor Per Jansson today participated in the first hearing of the year on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. Date: 2021-03-16 10:00 Speaker: Deputy Governor per Jansson Location: Finance Committee, Swedish Parliament In his introduction, Jansson focused on inflation. It is expected to rise quite clearly in the future, but this is mainly due to temporary effects, such as rising energy prices. Underlying inflation remains moderate. The Riksbank's forecast is that inflation will fall back, but that it will then rise gradually after the summer in line with the recovery in the economy. Jansson also noted that the debate around inflation has changed recently. Now the risks of inflation that are too high have begun to be discussed, especially in the United States. "For my part, I think the risk of higher inflation is about as great as the risk of a lower one," Jansson said. "But after a long period of too low inflation, it would do nothing if inflation in Sweden shoots above the target for some time. Then I would see no need to make monetary policy less expansionary. On the other hand, inflation that is too low could have to be met with a more expansionary monetary policy, at least if confidence problems arise in our inflation target. In that case, there may also be a need for a lower repo rate," Jansson said. Title: It is important that the upward trend in inflation continues
text: Jansson: It is important that the upward trend in inflation continues Date: 2016-02-18 Speaker: Deputy Governor Per Jansson Location: Me4lardalen Chamber of Commerce, d6rebro On Thursday, Deputy Governor Per Jansson will visit d6rebro where he talks about the latest interest rate decision. At the same time, growth in the Swedish economy is high and the situation on the labour market has improved. Expansionary monetary policy has contributed to this positive development. "To use the strong economic situation in Sweden as an argument against the Riksbank's expansionary monetary policy will be strange. The fact that Sweden is doing well depends a lot on the monetary policy that is being pursued," says Jansson. Jansson emphasizes that we are not on solid ground yet as inflation in 2016 will be lower than the Riksbank previously expected. This increases the risk that confidence in the inflation target will weaken again and thus also that inflation will not rise towards the target as expected. "You can't expect the upturn in inflation to be straight forward and without setbacks. But the upward trend must continue and confidence in the inflation target must be safeguarded. This is the important thing and therefore we need to maintain a high level of preparedness to take further measures in monetary policy," jansson concludes. Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Kerstin af Jochnick in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2015-03-05 Speaker: First Deputy Governor of the Riksbank Kerstin af Jochnick Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament Why do we have negative interest rates? How is the Swedish economy developing? These are some of the questions that Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and First Deputy Governor Kerstin af Jochnick will answer when they begin the first hearing of the year on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee on Thursday. Stefan Ingves presents the background to the decision to lower the repo rate to a historically low -0.10 percent and to buy government bonds for SEK 10 billion. He talks about the fact that the Swedish economy has developed relatively well and that there are signs that low inflation has bottomed out. But he also points out that uncertainty in the world around us has increased. "The measures we have taken, which can be scaled up if necessary, can be seen as insurance against the risk of lower inflation and inflation expectations. We show in action that we are defending the inflation target", says Ingves. Ingves also highlights the problems in the housing market. The fact that both house prices and lending for home purchases are increasing is a side effect of the low interest rate. "It is urgent that other policy areas address these risks," Ingves stresses. Kerstin af Jochnick also points out how important it is for inflation to rise towards the target and gives her perspective on the debate on monetary policy in recent years. The criticism has now clearly changed character, says af Jochnick. From having previously been about the Riksbank stimulating more, that debt does not pose a risk and that the inflation target must be prioritized, the criticism now boils down to the fact that the Riksbank should stimulate less, that debt is a significant risk and that the inflation target is less important. af Jochnick believes that the previous criticism took too lightly the risks of high household indebtedness, while the new criticism underestimates the importance of the inflation target for stable economic development. "The policy we pursue is not a new type of policy, it is a reaction to a change in the conditions for monetary policy", says af Jochnick, pointing out that inflation in recent years has become lower than expected and that inflation expectations have fallen. The Governor of the Riksbank and one of the Deputy Governors of the Riksbank are questioned about monetary policy by the Parliamentary Finance Committee three times a year.

Title: The consequences for Sweden if we join the EMU
text: The consequences for Sweden if we join EMU Date: 1997-04-17 Speaker: Deputy Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Sparbankens Bofinanssymposium in Copenhagen First of all, I would like to thank you for allowing me to come here and talk about EMU and about the effects EMU can have on the Swedish financial market. These are issues that interest and engage more and more people - quite naturally, both because we are approaching the stipulated start of EMU and because it seems increasingly likely that the whole thing will actually happen. The last meeting between the finance ministers and the central bank governors in the Netherlands gave a further confirmation of this. What I will talk about here today is partly to recapitulate what the timetable looks like for EMU, what changes we already know will occur today and what practical preparations the Riksbank is making for EMU. I will also discuss what the consequences may be for the financial sector in Sweden - both in the case where we participate and in the event that we do not participate. No one today can accurately assess how great and how rapid the effects of the introduction of a single European currency will be. The EMU project is actually something unique - there is nothing to compare with and just no experiences to lean on, at least not in modern times. Therefore, I think it may be appropriate to have a certain humility when trying to assess effects and evaluate different pros and cons. Moreover, it is indeed a question of economics - but far from being just about the economy. This does not prevent one from nevertheless having a fairly well-founded idea of in what direction and approximately with what force various effects will act. On that basis, I believe, it is also possible to take a stand. Why EMU and why should Sweden be involved? Monetary union or not ? There is a high probability that monetary union will be realised as planned - the political will is great and it is manifested time and time again when contradictions and doubts appear to threaten the process. Discussing whether the project is in principle and in the greatest generality good or less good has therefore lost some of its timeliness. What the question is now, in practice, is whether we want to be on the train that is likely to leave on the platform on 1 January 1999, whether we should wait for the next departure or whether we should go home again. Sweden should participate from the start The basic idea of EMU is quite simple. A single currency brings efficiency gains, and increased efficiency means growing resources and increased prosperity. Transaction costs decrease as exchange costs disappear. The absence of exchange rate fluctuations facilitates trade and investment. Price comparisons and financial calculations will be easier, not least for households and smaller companies. When the price picture becomes transparent across the euro area, competition will be intensified and prices will be squeezed for the benefit of consumers. As for the Riksbank's view of whether Sweden should participate in the currency union, our full- mighty concluded that we should be involved, and be involved from the start in 1999. We believe that the economic and political benefits of joining the Union have been underestimated, particularly in the so-called 'Green Paper'. Calm research the investigation, while exaggerating the stabilization policy costs. Let me explain in more detail. One of the most common arguments against monetary union is that it is believed that we must retain the possibility of devaluation in order to cope with so-called asymmetric shocks, i.e. disruptions in the economy that unilaterally affect Sweden. In the event of such a disturbance in the economy, there is a great risk of an increase in unemployment, and in order to prevent this, we must be able to adjust the exchange rate. This argument is also commonly referred to as the insurance argument. In a monetary union with fixed exchange rates, we do not have this 'insurance' : in EMU, Sweden cannot devalue itself from economic problems. Here our views on economic policy differ from those who say 'no' to the Union. We cannot use monetary and exchange rate policy to solve problems that in practice have often been due to economic policies pursued and to lingering structural problems that we ourselves have created, rather than to any asymmetric shocks. The problems highlighted by the EMU investigation, such as the risk of increased unemployment, naturally deserve to be taken very seriously. But the solution to the problems of unemployment does not lie in monetary or exchange rate policy, but mainly in changes in the functioning of the labour market. The political consequences The economic effects of EMU are, of course, important to discuss. What also matters is the political effects of being involved or being left out. Here we share the view of the EMU inquiry - to remain outside the Union entails political costs. We will be outside the inner circle of countries that will take Europe into the future. Our ability to influence important decisions is probably also reduced in areas other than monetary policy. Should Sweden stand outside the currency zone for good, there is a risk that we will be marginalized as an "outdoor country". We should also be aware that the countries that join EMU from the outset will have a greater say in how the new European Central Bank, the ECB, will develop during the first important years when it comes to finding the forms of its work. What we should do is ask what kind of Europe do we want to develop, and how can we participate and contribute to that process. We can, of course, also choose to stand by and watch as the other countries move forward in this cooperation. But in that case, we should be aware that it is a choice we are making. I find it difficult to see that Sweden would like to remain outside a functioning EMU in the long run. Europe's economies and countries will grow together. The question is thus not if but when Sweden should join. This was also the conclusion of the EMU study. When the question is formulated, the debate is somewhat de-dramatized. Let me now turn to the more practical aspects of this project. What will happen ? Sweden and convergence conditions As far as the convergence conditions are concerned, these do not imply a new direction of economic policy in Sweden. Three of the criteria directly concern the Riksbank's area, namely the inflation criterion, the long-term interest rate criterion and the exchange rate criterion. At the moment, Sweden has europe's lowest inflation and we expect Sweden to meet the inflation criterion in 1997 as well. We are also likely to meet the interest rate criterion. There has been a lot of discussion about the exchange rate criterion. Some consider that a country must participate in exchange rate cooperation within the ERM for at least two years before the pre-EMU test in order to qualify, while others argue that it is the stability of the currency in practice that is essential. From the Swedish side, we subscribe to the latter view. With regard to the remaining criteria, the forecast is that the budget deficit will remain close to 3% for 1997. The government has stated that it is prepared to take action if the deficit develops in an unfavourable direction. On the other hand, we will probably not be able to reduce the government debt/GDP ratio, which is currently located around 80%, to the stated 60% already by 1997. However, the Maastricht Treaty allows for a flexible interpretation on this point. For example, it is acceptable for a country to be above 60% in debt ratio if it shows a satisfactoryly fast and stable rate of reduction. All in all, therefore, the situation looks as if we will actually meet the convergence conditions. This, of course, makes it even more interesting to start preparations even for those who were previously hesitant. So what happens in the future? The "driving schedule" for EMU is in brief: In almost exactly one year' s time, during a weekend at the end of April or the beginning of May 1998, the Council of Ministers will decide which countries will participate in the Union. The decision is based on which countries have fulfilled the convergence conditions on the basis of the 1997 statis- tion. On the first of January 1999, exchange rates will be fixed and the European Central Bank, the ECB, will take over monetary policy. The euro is introduced as its own currency and all monetary policy operations are conducted in euros. Until 1 January 2002 at the latest, both euros and crowns will exist in parallel. However, in a legal sense, it will be a currency. It is no stranger than that Swedish kronor can be printed both as pennies and crowns. However, we will not have euros in our wallets during this time, but only by 1 January 2002 will euros be available as notes and coins. When euro banknotes and cents are put into circulation, a large exchange of notes and coins begins over six months. No later than 1 July 2002, kronor will lose the status of legal tender, but the Riksbank will of course also exchange sek for euros after this date. Preparations in Sweden It is the Riksdag that decides on Sweden's membership of EMU. The Riksbank's task is to contribute to Sweden really being able to join if the Riksdag's majority so wishes. That is why preparations are needed now. Both the Ministry of Finance and the Riksbank have their own organisations for the practical introduction of the euro. A fundamental principle of this work is that voluntarism should prevail. It is therefore up to each organization to decide for itself what changes it wants to make. All parties involved must also resolve for themselves the possible problems they face as a result of EMU. One result of the work so far is the report "The euro in the Swedish financial sector a progress report", which was published in early February. The report has been prepared together with representatives from the financial sector and therefore reflects both our view of the transition issues and the views of another 12 organisations via attached opinions. It is the first report where a review and compilation has been made of the EMU preparations in the Swedish financial system. In the report, we conclude that the preparatory work in the Swedish financial sector has come a long way. Timetables and appropriate solutions have been developed in most areas. The Riksbank's assessment is therefore that the financial sector will be able to cope with a changeover to the euro on 1 January 1999. We also see that a later membership can in some cases facilitate and in other cases complicate the preparatory work. The worst option is a long period of uncertainty as to whether or not we should participate, what we usually call a 'soft no'. Double costly systems will then become a reality in several areas. We have also seen concern in the financial sector about increased costs, competitive disadvantages and the risk of various forms of discrimination outside EMU. This is pointed out both in our progress report and in our response to the EU inquiry. Our work on the preparations will continue in the spring. What will change? How will we feel about EMU? What changes will be of greatest importance to the financial system? What will we as citizens notice? I will briefly review some of the changes we know will occur for a number of important areas. 1. Monetary and exchange rate policy A single currency presupposes a single monetary policy. In EMU, this will: be determined by the ECB. The riksbank and the other national central banks will have the role of implementing this monetary policy. For Swedish banks and financial institutions, the practical difference is unlikely to be so great. It is likely that the Riksbank will continue to be the financial sector's counterparty. The biggest difference compared to today for Swedish banks is that the overnight market will be significantly larger and that counterparties will be located throughout Europe. How monetary policy in all details will be conducted is not yet clear. It was not until 1998, when the ECB was formed, that the final decisions were taken. It will therefore be the countries that join from the outset that will be able to influence the policies pursued and the organisation of the work of the new European Bank. There are tendencies that those who belong to the "intended" core of member states have more influence over the process already today. 2. Betalningssystem In order to be able to conduct a single monetary policy, a single payment system is required, otherwise it will not be possible to process the payments associated with monetary policy. Target is the name of the system that is now under construction and which will link all national interbank systems - in Sweden our so-called RIX system - into a common network. A payment from one bank, say in Stockholm to another bank in Copenhagen or in Milan, should normally be made in a matter of seconds. Today, this takes a whole day at best. The main purpose of TARGET is to enable the ECB to conduct monetary policy, but at the same time the new system establishes a new "motorway" for commercial transactions as well. How much banks and companies will use the system is likely to be determined by the price. What it will cost to exploit is still under discusssion. However, the principle is that full cost recovery should be achieved, and that pricing policy should be in line with the EU's competition principles. The central banks of all EU countries should be able to join Target whether they are in the monetary union or not. Discussions on the design of the system clearly show that there is a significant risk that countries outside the euro area will be less able to use TARGET, for example through restrictions on borrowing in euros during the day, which is important in order to be able to fend off fluctuations in payment flows. Among other things, it has been discussed that the so-called outsbanks should close the system early-re. The Riksbank has worked vigorously to prevent this type of possible discrimination, but decisions on this issue, as in some others, have been postponed and will now be taken by the countries that are members of EMU from the start. Target will be tested by the summer and will be ready for full use by 1 January 1999. 3. The laws Everyone must be able to trust that the euro has a solid legal basis on which to stand. Economic values in, for example, contracts, bank accounts and pension contracts must be guaranteed during the period between 1999 and 2002, when we have both the euro and national currencies in circulation. Businesses and individuals must be sure that the contracts concluded in kros also apply when we have received euros, i.e. contract continuity will prevail. This and much more is regulated in the so-called. the euro regulations. This legislation must be directly applicable in all Member States and therefore applies in Sweden if we become members. It is also likely that we will have to amend our national legislation. One such national legal issue concerns the role of the Riksbank. The Maastricht Treaty stipulates that the Riksbank must be made more independent in law. This means, among other things, that the position of the Governor of the Riksbank must be clarified. He or she should only be able to be removed if there are exceptional reasons such as gross misconduct, etc. The Riksbank should also not be able to receive directives, other than by law, from someone else, such as the government. In our Riksbank Council there are also members of parliament represented according to Swedish tradition. This is against the traditions that exist in Central Europe where our order is seen as a risk to political control of monetary policy. The effects of EMU on the financial sector and the securities market Emu is usually discussed and evaluated from a macroeconomic perspective, not least because the convergence criteria are about this. But EMU is more than macroeconomics - it is also about new infrastructures, increased competitiveness and structural change. These, if you like, microeconomic effects will work in all industries and all parts of the economy. This is also where the EU's growth-enhancing potential lies - and there are probably reasons to assume that it is greater than many imagine. Since a new currency touches on one of the hearts of every financial system, the financial sector will, of course, be particularly affected. Some developments Several of the developments we will see after the introduction of the euro are ones that we are already seeing to a large extent today and that we would probably see emu before. The overall trends are thus also driven by other factors and are linked to the liberalisation of markets and the general internationalisation that began in the mid-80s. Examples of these include information technology and the internationalisation of savings. The tendencies point to a continued rapid development of the financial markets, with new instruments, industry shifts and concentration of certain specialist functions. Competitive pressures in traditional banking are likely to continue to intensify at the same time as long-term demand for financial services is increasing and knowledge - whether we are talking about companies, municipalities or households - is becoming increasingly demanding. The number of "full-service" banks has already declined while their big-game is increasing. It is also likely that there will be continued growth of niche banks or financial companies focused on just a few services or distribution channels. The trend towards traditional bank deposits and loans is decreasing, while the supply and demand for market-based instruments is likely to continue. There is also reason to assume that some products on the financial markets will disappear while new ones come into being. Examples of products that may disappear are e.g. intra-European currency futures, intra-European currency swaps. In addition, internal risk management and intra-European currency risk management systems will not be needed after the changeover to the euro according to ISMA (International Securities Market Association). At the same time, new products can be created, such as euro options, euro futures, euro area stock indices and euro-designed settlement systems. In detail, we cannot know what will happen, the market will largely control developments in this area. How great the importance of EMU will prove to be for this whole process of transformation is debatable and difficult to delimit and measure in advance - and perhaps not even in hindsight. One could, of course, and rightly so, argue that it is primarily governed by the global integ ration and by the EU's internal market. However, it is very likely that EMU will accelerate and accentuate these developments. Today's European capital markets are fragmented. Domestic banks and insurance companies dominate in most countries and Sweden is no exception. The basis for this is not only that there are different currencies in Europe, but probably even more the tendency of customers to stick to banks they know in combination with the banks' long-acquired knowledge of credit risks and local markets. With the exception of the disappearance of the various currencies, the arguments for nationally based activities remain even after EMU has been formed. Combined with language difficulties and cultural differences, this suggests that the development of the financial "retail trade" and its structure will be driven by essentially factors other than EMU. In the long term, however, the constituent countries can be expected to grow ever closer to each other and thus also to the financial structures. However, when it comes to services aimed at companies - especially larger companies - there is reason to believe that the ef-effects can become quite large quite soon. When we wrote our progress report on the changeover to the euro, we also contacted a number of housing institutions to get an idea of what the changeover would mean for the housing loan market. However, opinions were divided and the matter had not yet been investigated to any great extent. In the case of old loans disbursed before 1 January 1999, several institutions considered that conversion was not necessary. Until new banknotes and coins are put into circulation, notification would therefore be made in sek. As for the time thereafter, the conversion will occur at one point, but physical rewrites of home loan agreements are likely only as terms change. However, the opinion also emerged that the conversion could already take place during the transition period, so opinions seem to be divided. With regard to new loans, however, the view seemed to be that the demand for crown loans might fall drastically as early as 1 January 1999. These issues are worthy of further discussion. Credit risk is increasing in importance In general, due to economic convergence between countries and a common anti-inflationary monetary policy, monetary union will lead to a convergence of interest rates in high-interest and low-interest rate countries. This also means that the currency risk premium disappears completely because in EMU there is only one currency. What will remain, even after the transition process is fully implemented, is above all liquidity and credit risks. In the case of so-called risk-free securities, such as government securities, interest rates on at least short paper may converge almost fully. This is supported by, among other things, the requirements for good public finances. As currency risk disappears and investment decisions will be more about credit risks, there is much to suggest that well-developed European markets may form across national borders for different types of bonds such as corporate, residential and municipal bonds. This is likely to be accompanied by an interest on the part of investors in spreading their risks by diversifying their portfolios to several countries in order to limit loss risks in the event of asymmetric shocks in any country. The interesting thing to note is that the rating of the companies could thus differ from the rating of the home country. A company, say Volvo, could have a higher rating than the Kingdom of Sweden. Larger and more liquid markets Today, we have about 9 million potential investors in Sweden. There are a total of just over 370 million in the EU. In addition, investors from other countries in Europe and from the rest of the world can be expected to seek out this new large market. The euro, along with the dollar and yen, will become one of the three major reserve currencies. A larger market normally leads, through rising competition, to lower costs, better loan opportunities and increased liquidity. It is difficult to see anything other than that this will be beneficial for the mortgage bond market as well. It is therefore likely that, with monetary union, borrowers will have a larger market to operate in. There will also be more investors and as the currency risk disappears, it will be cheaper for them to diversify their portfolios. This should mean good conditions for borrowers to get hold of attractive financing via, among other things, the bond market. With regard to the housing sector and housing finance, there is also particular reason to point to the effects of the lower and more stable interest rates that EMU, all other things being equal, will entail. The result should be higher property prices, increased housing construction and thus an increased demand for financing. What is probably very important, when it comes to borrowing in this new European market, is that borrowers quickly adapt to international market standards in terms of accounting for their finances and financial position. In this also lies acquiring an international rating. Those borrowers who can handle this are likely to have one advantage over others. As always, it is borrowers with a stable economy who can take advantage over others. In this competition, the creditworthiness of the home country will also come into play. Foreign lenders are already increasingly targeting Sweden. Among other things, the recently established French Municipal Bank (Credit Locale de France) is a good example of this. But other banks, both Norwegian, Danish, Finnish, English, and American banks, are also strengthening their positions in Sweden. In combination with the fact that banks in EMU countries can lend to Swedish borrowers without exchange rate risk, this leads to increased competition in Sweden and thus also to generally better loan terms. overgangsprocessen As far as the transition process itself is concerned, it is partly a question of converting the financial instruments and partly of 'converting' the infrastructure in which the instruments are managed. Starting with the instruments, the countries joining EMU can, and should, carry out new issues of their euro-denominated sovereign debt. Other issuers - not least housing institutions - should also quickly start issuing in the new currency. If any Member State wants to convert its outstanding debt into euros, it may also do so. When it comes to infrastructure, institutions such as the stock exchange, VPC and OM are particularly affected when it comes to the securities and banks and the Riksbank when it comes to money and payment processing. As far as the securities side is concerned, the companies mentioned have clearly advocated a "big bang solution", i.e. a quick and comprehensive transition from sek to euro already at the turn of the year 1998/1999, in order to avoid "double systems" that are partly operationally cumbersome and expensive and partly risk fragmenting liquidity in the market, which would make Sweden less attractive as an international financial place. VPC is also actively involved in discussions with its European counterparts on building a common network where securities can be transferred across borders in a similar way to money in the central banks' Target system. This is both technically and legally a complicated work that will not be finished on this side of the century, but it is gratifying that the work has started. With regard to payment systems, I have previously mentioned the TARGET system, the common network of central bank-based interbank systems. At the Riksbank, we are working intensively to make our Rix system compatible with Target. However, the major adjustment work lies in the banking sector - this is where the large account stocks and large transaction volumes are located. Between 1999 and 2002, the banks will handle both euros and kronor. Therefore, somewhere in the system there must be a conversion mechanism, a "shell" that converts from crowns to euros and, conversely, according to the established, fix rate. Customers of banks will be able to receive euros and pay out crowns and vice versa, without having to make currency transactions. After all, currencies are not really two va-lutes, but only two ways of expressing exactly the same value - you could say that the relationship between the euro and the krona will be the same as between a 100-crown banknote and five 20-crown banknotes. A "scale function" must thus be in place almost immediately. On the other hand, there will be no need for banks to immediately and at the same time change their internal systems following the introduction of the euro - this can be done when it is best suited for each bank during the transition phase. Another advantage is that this can help avoid too much of the bottleneck problem in terms of access to data and programming expertise.. If Sweden is outside Sweden may end up in a situation where, for various reasons, we are not part of monetary union from January 1999. In a formal sense, this means an essentially unchanged situation compared to today - the RIX system works in sek (although we are also building a parallel system in Euro), monetary policy is conducted in sek and government securities are issued in sek. The currency risk remains, of course, if you choose to borrow from investors in the euro area and thus also the costs of hedging. But in a real sense, this means deterioration for the Swedish financial system in several ways: the ability to handle payments via the TARGET system is likely to be worse. Since the euro will nevertheless be a major currency in all respects, for example, it cannot be ruled out that several of the major Swedish industrial giants will switch to the Euro as a group currency - this will mean that the financial companies will be forced to invest in and operate parallel infrastructures. Moreover, if it cannot be assumed with any degree of certainty that there will be a short-term 'out' period, these decisions will have to be taken under great uncertainty, and probably also in the context of a financial market of declining international importance. Admittedly, it can be said that we will in any case have to live with "double systems" in the period 1999-2002 even if we are in EMU, but there is a difference between "double system" and "double system" - if we are in EMU, it is firstly about about dealing with two expressions for the same currency, not two different currencies, secondly, it is a clearly defined period of time. The interest of Swedish investors in turning to the market in euros is likely to be less than if Sweden is a member of the Union. However, an increase in placements within the EMU block compared to today may take place. This would then mean that the scope for investments in Sweden may decrease, something that would be negative, among other things, for the housing finance market. Another disadvantage of not joining the currency union from the beginning is that the diversification to different sectors, borrowers and countries that foreign investors may implement, then Sweden will not benefit. When Sweden, as I assume at a later date, enters the currency union, the big train has gone and the interest in investing in Sweden will then probably be less because the investors have then already diversified their portfolios. Summary and conclusions Today, there is every reason why economic and monetary union will get under way as planned on 1 January 1999. For Sweden, the question is whether we should be involved from the beginning, wait a while or try to stay out for good. My hope is that in the future we will have an increased debate on this very important decision. The discussion leading up to this position should not then concentrate solely on the question of monetary policy independence. It is not just a question of economics, although we believe that the economic arguments speak in favour of membership. It is also about the fact that EMU is an important part of the European development cooperation in which Sweden now participates. -- Exclusion makes demands Sometimes in the discussion one gets the impression that in the event of exclusion there is an easy way for Sweden to go. Outside of this European cooperation, we would be spared all the adaptation requirements that are imposed. That's not the case. In any case, we must continue to work on reorganising the state's finances and creating long-term confidence in the stability of the Swedish economy. It will hardly be easier outside EMU. If we are left out, we will be put on the line and then, as it is usually called, we must be "holier than the Pope" so as not to get into trouble. The possibility of trying to solve the unemployment problems of inflationary economic policies and devaluations does not exist within the framework of EMU, but it does not exist outside EMU either. -- The world will not be the same A 'no' to EMU does not mean the status quo. By creating a pre-cis monetary union beyond our borders, the world will not be the same. Both individuals and businesses will feel the introduction of the euro, whether we are involved or not. In our work to inform the financial sector about EMU, we see that preparations have gone a long way. We also see a strong desire from the parties involved to be involved as quickly as possible so as not to be left behind. - EMU and the Swedish financial sector EMU will contribute to increased pressure for structural change and thus to greater efficiency in all parts of the economy. This also applies to a large extent to the financial sector, including the part facing the housing sector. We get a completely different range of players on both the borrower and investor side. The market is focused on credit risks and becomes more transparent, more diversified, more competitive and more efficient. It seems quite clear that exclusion of a "for the time being" nature would affect the Swedish financial sector in a negative way. Duplication of infrastructures would create increased costs, and this, together with uncertainty about future developments, would reduce the competitiveness of individual companies and the Swedish financial market as a whole would become less interesting for both Swedish and foreign players. Added to this are the risks of more or less pronounced discrimination, for example in access to the TARGET system. -- Further preparations Regardless of the political discussion, practical preparations must continue. The EMI will continue to resolve the issues on which it has not yet taken a position. We will continue to participate in that work. Here at home, the Government Offices will continue to provide information on their level and we will continue our cooperation with the financial sector. In the autumn, we have the ambition to write a new report on emu preparations. After the Riksdag has taken a position on Swedish participation or not, we will also have the opportunity to give clearer and more clear information about what preparations will be needed. We are facing a dynamic process both in the world around us and here at home.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Konsekvenserna fr Sverige om vi gr med i EMU Datum: 1997-04-17 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Stefan Ingves Plats: Sparbankens Bofinanssymposium i Kpenhamn Till att brja med vill jag att tacka fr att jag ftt komma hit och tala om EMU och om de effekter EMU kan innebra fr den svenska finansiella marknaden. Det hr r frgor som intresserar och engagerar allt fler - helt naturligt bde drfr att vi nrmar oss den stipulerade starten fr EMU och fr att det framstr som alltmer sannolikt att det hela verkligen ocks blir av. Det senaste mtet mellan fi-nansministrarna och centralbankscheferna i Holland gav ju ytterligare en bekrf-telse p detta. Vad jag kommer att tala om hr idag r dels att rekapitulera hur tidtabellen ser ut fr EMU, vilka frndringar vi redan idag vet kommer att intrffa och vilka prak-tiska frberedelser Riksbanken bedriver infr EMU. Jag kommer ocks att dis-kutera vilka konsekvenserna kan bli fr den finansiella sektorn i Sverige av - bde i det fall vi deltar och i det fall vi inte deltar. Ingen kan idag p ett exakt stt bedma hur stora och hur snabba effekterna blir av ett infrande av en gemensam europeisk valuta. EMU-projektet r faktiskt nnting unikt - det finns inget att jmfra med och just inga erfarenheter att luta sig mot, i varje fall inte i modern tid. Dessutom r det ju s att det frvisso handlar om ekonomi - men lngifrn enbart om eko-nomi. Det hr hindrar inte att man nd kan ha en ganska vlgrundad uppfattning om i vilken riktning och ungefrligen med vilken kraft olika effekter kommer att verka. Utifrn detta r det ocks, menar jag, mjligt att ta stllning. Varfr EMU och varfr br Sverige vara med ? Valutaunion eller ej ? Sannolikheten r hg att valutaunionen frverkligas enligt planerna - den po-litiska viljan r stor och den manifesteras gng p gng nr motsttningar och tvivel ser ut att hota processen. Att diskutera om projektet i princip och i strsta allmn-het r bra eller mindre bra har drfr mist en del av sin aktualitet. Vad frgan i praktiken gller r nu om vi vill vara med p det tg som sannolikt lm-nar perrongen den 1 januari 1999, om vi ska vnta p nsta avgng eller om vi ska g hem igen. Sverige br delta frn starten Grundtanken med EMU r ganska enkel. En gemensam valuta ger effektivitetsvinster, och kad effektvitet innebr vxande resurser och kat vlstnd. Transaktionskostnaderna minskar nr vxlingskostnaderna frsvinner. Frnvaro av vxelkursvariationer underlttar handel och investeringar. Prisjmfrelser och ekonomiska kalkyler blir enklare, inte minst fr hushll och mindre fretag. Nr prisbilden blir transparent ver hela Euro-omrdet kommer konkurrensen att skrpas och priserna pressas till gagn fr konsumenterna. Vad gller Riksbankens syn p om Sverige br delta i valutaunionen har vrt full- mktige dragit slutsatsen att vi br vara med, och vara med frn starten 1999. Vi tror att de ekonomiska och de politiska vinsterna av att g med i unionen under-skattats, bl. a. i den s.k. Calmforska utredningen, samtidigt som de stabiliseringspo-litiska kostnaderna verdrivits. Lt mig frklara nrmare. Ett av de vanligaste argumenten mot valutaunionen r att man anser att vi mste ha kvar mjligheten att devalvera fr att klara av s.k. asymmetriska chocker, dvs. strningar i ekonomin som ensidigt drabbar Sverige. Vid en sdan strning i ekonomin r risken stor fr en kning av arbetslsheten, och fr att hindra detta mste vi kunna anpassa vxelkursen. Detta argument brukar ocks kallas frskringsargumentet. I en valutaunion med lsta vxelkurser har vi inte denna "frskring" : i EMU kan inte Sverige devalvera sig ur ekonomiska problem. Hr skiljer sig vr syn p den ekonomiska politiken frn de som sger nej till unionen. Vi kan inte anvnda penning- och valutapolitiken fr att lsa problem som i praktiken ofta berott p den frda ekonomiska politiken och p kvardrjande strukturella problem som vi sjlva skapat, snarare n p ngra asymmetriska chocker. De problem som EMU -ut-redningen lyft fram, t.ex. risken fr kad arbetslshet, frtjnar naturligtvis att tas p strsta allvar. Men lsningen p arbetslshetsproblemen ligger inte i penning- eller valutapolitiken, utan frmst i frndringar av arbetsmarknadens stt att fungera. De politiska konsekvenserna De ekonomiska effekterna av EMU r naturligtvis viktiga att diskutera. Vad som ocks spelar roll r de politiska effek-terna av att vara med eller st utanfr. Hr delar vi EMU-utredningens uppfattning - att st utanfr unionen innebr politiska kostnader. Vi kommer vid ett utanfr-skap att vara utanfr den innersta kretsen av lnder som skall fra Europa in i framtiden. Vr mjlighet att pverka viktiga beslut reduceras frmodligen ocks p andra omrden n penningpolitiken. Skulle Sverige stlla sig utanfr valutaunio-nen fr gott finns en risk att vi marginaliseras som ett "uteland". Vi skall ocks vara medvetna om att de lnder som gr med i EMU frn start kommer att ha ett strre inflytande ver hur den nya europeiska centralbanken, ECB, kommer att utvecklas under de frsta viktiga ren d man skall finna formerna fr sitt arbete. Vad vi br gra r att stlla frgan vad r det fr Europa vi vill skall utvecklas, och hur kan vi delta och bidra till den processen. Vi kan naturligtvis ocks vlja att st vid sidan av och se p nr de andra lnderna gr vidare i detta samarbete. Men vi ska i s fall vara medvetna om att det r ett val vi gr. Att Sverige i lngden skulle vilja st utanfr ett fungerande EMU har jag svrt att se. Europas ekonomier och lnder kommer att vxa samman. Frgan r drmed inte om utan nr Sverige br g med. Det var ocks slutsatsen i EMU-utredningen. Nr frgestllningen formuleras s avdramatiseras debatten en del. Lt mig nu verg till de mer praktiska aspekterna av detta projekt. Vad kommer att hnda ? Sverige och konvergensvillkoren Nr det gller konvergensvillkoren innebr dessa ingen ny inriktning av den ekonomiska politiken i Sverige. Tre av kriterierna berr direkt Riksbankens omrde, nmligen inflationskriteriet, kriteriet fr den lnga rntan och vxelkurskriteriet. Fr tillfllet har Sverige Europas lgsta inflation och vi frvntar oss att Sverige uppfyller kriteriet betrffande inflationen ven under 1997. Vi uppfyller sannolikt ven rntekriteriet. Kring vxelkurskriteriet har det diskuterats mycket. Vissa anser att ett land mste deltaga i vxelkurssamarbetet inom ERM under minst tv r fre prvningen infr EMU fr att kvalificera sig, medan andra hvdar att det r valu-tans stabilitet i praktiken som r det vsentliga. Frn svensk sida ansluter vi oss till den senare uppfattningen. Betrffande de terstende kriterierna r prognosen att budgetunderskottet hller sig nra 3 procent fr 1997. Regeringen har uttalat att den r beredd att vidta tgrder om underskottet utvecklas i ofrmnlig riktning. Dremot kommer vi nog inte att klara att nedbringa relationen statsskuld/BNP, som idag ligger kring 80 procent, till angivna 60 procent redan till 1997. Maastrichtfrdraget ger dock utrymme fr en flexibel tolkning p denna punkt. Exempelvis kan det godtas att ett land ligger ver 60 procent i skuldkvot om det uppvisar en tillfredsstllande snabb och stabil minskningstakt. Sammantaget ser drfr lget ut som att vi faktiskt kommer att uppfylla konvergensvillkoren. Detta gr det naturligtvis nnu mer intressant att brja frberedelserna ven fr dem som tidigare varit tveksamma. Vad hnder d framver? "Krschemat" fr EMU r i korthet: Om nstan precis ett r, under ett veckoslut i slutet av April eller brjan av Maj 1998, beslutar ministerrdet vilka lnder som ska delta i unionen. Beslutet grundas p vilka lnder som uppfyllt konvergensvillkoren p basis av statis-tiken frn 1997. Den frsta januari 1999 lses vxelkurserna och den europeiska centralbanken, ECB, vertar penningpolitiken. Euron infrs som egen valuta och alla penningpolitiska transaktioner sker i euro. Fram till senast 1 januari 2002 kommer bde euro och kronor att existera parallellt. I laglig mening kommer det dock att vara en valuta. Det r inte konstigare n att svenska kronor kan ut-tryckas bde som ren och kronor. Men vi kommer inte att ha euro i plnboken under denna tid utan frst senast den 1 januari 2002 kommer euro att finnas som sedlar och mynt. Nr eurosedlar och cent stts i omlopp brjar ett stort utbyte av sedlar och mynt under sex mnader. Senast 1 juli 2002 kommer kronor att mista status som lagligt betalningsmedel, men Riksbanken kommer naturligtvis ven ef-ter detta datum att byta in kronor mot euro. Frberedelserna i Sverige Det r Riksdagen som beslutar om Sveriges medlemskap i EMU. Riksbankens uppgift r att bidra till att Sverige verkligen kan g med om Riksdagens majoritet s nskar. Det r drfr frberedelser behvs redan nu. Svl Finansdepartementet som Riksbanken har sina egna organisationer fr det praktiska infrandet av euron. En grundlggande princip i detta arbete r att frivillighet skall rda. Det r allts upp till varje organisation att sjlv bestmma vilka omstllningar man vill gra. Alla inblandade parter mste ocks sjlva lsa de eventuella problem de stlls infr till fljd av EMU. Ett resultat av arbetet hittills r rapporten "Euron i den svenska finansiella sek-torn en lgesrapport", som publicerades i brjan av februari. Rapporten har utar-betats tillsammans med representanter frn finansiella sektorn och speglar drfr bde vr syn p vergngsfrgorna och ytterligare 12 organisationers syn via bilagda yttranden. Det r den frsta rapporten dr en versyn och sammanstllning gjorts ver EMU-frberedelserna i det svenska finansiella systemet. I rapporten drar vi slutsatsen att frberedelsearbetet i den svenska finansiella sektorn har kommit en bra bit p vg. Tidsplaner och lmpliga lsningar har tagits fram p flertalet omrden. Riksbankens bedmning blir drfr att den finansiella sektorn klarar en omstllning till euro 1 januari 1999. Vi ser ocks att ett senare medlemskap kan i vissa fall underltta och i andra fall frsvra frberedelsearbetet. Det smsta alternativet r en lng period av oskerhet om vi skall delta eller inte, det vi brukar kalla fr ett "mjukt nej". Dubbla kostsamma system kommer d att bli en realitet p flera omrden. Vi har ocks sett en oro inom den finansiella sektorn ver kade kostnader, konkurrensnackdelar och risk fr olika former av diskrimi-nering av att st utanfr EMU. Detta ppekas bde i vr lgesrapport och i vrt remissvar p EMUutredningen. Vrt arbetet med frberedelserna kommer att g vidare under vren. Vad kommer att frndras? Hur kommer vi att mrka av EMU? Vilka frndringar kommer att vara av strst betydelse fr det finansiella systemet? Vad kommer vi som medborgare att mrka? Jag tnker kortfattat g igenom en del av de frndringar vi vet kommer att intrffa fr ett antal viktiga omrden. 1. Penning- och valutapolitiken En enda valuta frutstter en gemensam penningpolitik. Denna kommer i EMU att bestmmas av ECB. Riksbanken och de andra nationella centralbankerna roll blir att genomfra denna penningpolitik. Fr svenska banker och finansinstitut blir den praktiska skillnaden sannolikt inte s stor. Troligen kommer Riksbanken ven i fortsttningen att vara den finansiella sektorns motpart. Den strsta skillnaden jmfrt med idag fr svenska banker r att dagslnemarknaden kommer att vara betydligt strre och att motparterna kommer att finnas i hela Europa. Hur penningpolitiken i alla detaljer kommer att bedrivas r nnu inte klart. Frst 1998 nr ECB bildats fattas de slutgiltiga besluten. Det blir allts de lnder som gr med frn brjan som kommer att kunna pverka vilken politik som frs och hur arbetet skall organiseras i den nya europeiska banken. Det finns tendenser till att de som tillhr den "tilltnkta" krnan av medlemslnder har strre inflytande ver processen redan idag. 2. Betalningssystem Fr att kunna bedriva en gemensam penningpolitik krvs ett gemensamt betalningssystem, annars gr det inte att hantera de betalningar som sammanhnger med penningpolitiken. Target heter det system som nu r under uppbyggnad och som kommer att lnka samman alla nationella interbanksystem - i Sverige vrt s.k RIXsystem - till ett gemensamt ntverk. En betalning frn en bank, sg i Stockholm till en annan bank i Kpenhamn eller i Milano skall normalt ske inom loppet av ngra f sekunder. I dag tar detta i bsta fall en hel dag. Syftet med Target r frmst att ECB ska kunna bedriva penningpoli-tik, men det nya systemet innebr samtidigt att en ny "motorvg" etableras ven fr kommersiella transaktioner. Hur mycket banker och fretag kommer att anvnda sig av systemet avgrs troligen av priset. Vad det kommer att kosta att utnyttja r fortfarande under diskusssion. Principen r dock att full kostnadstckning skall r-da, och att prispolitiken ska ligga i linje med EUs konkurrensprinciper. Alla EU-lnders centralbanker skall kunna ansluta sig till Target vare sig de r med i valutaunionen eller inte. Diskussionerna om systemets utformning visar klart att det finns en betydande risk att lnder utanfr euro-omrdet kommer att f smre mjligheter att anvnda Target, genom t.ex. begrnsningar att lna i euro under dagen vilket r viktigt fr att kunna parera svngningar i betalningsfldena. Det har bl.a. diskuterats att de s kallade outsbankerna skall stnga systemet tidiga-re. Riksbanken har med kraft arbetat fr att hindra denna typ av eventuell diskriminering, men beslut i denna frga, liksom i en del andra, har skjutits p och kommer nu att fattas av de lnder som r med i EMU frn starten. Target kommer att testkras till sommaren och skall vara frdigt att anvndas fullt ut 1 januari 1999. 3. Lagarna Alla mste kunna lita p att euron har en stabil laglig grund att st p. Ekonomiska vrden i t.ex. kontrakt, bankkonton och pensionsavtal mste garanteras under perioden mellan 1999 och 2002, d vi har bde euron och nationella valutor i omlopp. Fretag och privatpersoner mste vara skra p att de kontrakt som ingicks i kro-nor ven gller nr vi har ftt euro dvs. kontraktskontinuitet skall rda. Detta och mycket annat regleras i de sk. euro-frordningarna. Denna lagstiftning skall vara direkt tillmplig i alla medlemsstater och gller drfr i Sverige om vi blir med-lemmar. Troligen kommer vi ocks att behva ndra i vr nationella lagstiftning. En sdan nationell rttslig frga rr Riksbankens roll. Maastrichtfrdraget inne-br att Riksbanken i lag mste gras mer oberoende. Det hr innebr bl.a. att Riksbankschefens stllning mste tydliggras. Han eller hon skall bara kunna avsttas om det finns synnerliga skl som grov missktsel etc. Riksbanken ska inte heller kunna ta emot direktiv, annat n genom lag, frn ngon annan t.ex. regeringen. I vrt Riksbanksfullmktige finns ocks riksdagsmn representerade enligt svensk tradition. Detta r emot de traditioner som finns i Centraleuropa dr vr ordning ses som en risk fr politisk styrning av penningpolitiken. EMU's effekter p den finansiella sektorn och vrdepappers-marknaden Oftast brukar EMU diskuteras och vrderas utifrn ett makroekonomisk perspektiv, inte minst beroende p att konvergenskraven ju handlar om detta. Men EMU r mer n makroekonomi - det handlar ocks om nya infrastrukturer, kad konkur-rens och strukturomvandling. Dessa, om man s vill, mikroekonomiska effekter kommer att verka inom alla branscher och alla delar av ekonomin. Det r ocks hr som EMUs tillvxtfrstrkande potential finns - och det finns nog skl att anta att den r strre n mnga frestller sig. Eftersom en ny valuta berr ngot av hjrt-punkten i varje finansiellt system kommer naturligtvis finanssektorn att berras sr-skilt ptagligt. Ngra utvecklingstendenser Flera av de utvecklingstendenser vi kommer att f se efter Eurons infrande r sdana som vi i stor utstrckning ser redan idag och som vi troligen skulle f se ven EMU frutan. De vergripande tendenserna drivs allts ven av andra faktorer och sammanhnger med den avreglering av marknader och den allmna internationalisering som inleddes i mitten p 80-talet. Exempel p sdana r bland annat informationsteknologin och sparandets internationalisering. Tenden-serna pekar mot en fortsatt snabb utveckling av de finansiella marknaderna, med nya in-strument, branschglidningar och koncentration av vissa specialistfunktioner. Konkurrenstrycket inom den traditionella bankverksamheten lr fortstta att skr-pas samtidigt som den lngsiktiga efterfrgan p finansiella tjnster kar och kun-derna - vare sig vi talar om fretag, kommuner eller hushll - blir alltmer krvande. Antalet "full-service" banker har redan minskat samtidigt som deras stor-lek kar. Troligt r ocks en fortsatt tillvxt av s k nischbanker eller finansiella fre-tag inriktade p bara ngra tjnster eller distributionskanaler. Tendensen att tradi-tionell inlning och utlning i bank minskar, samtidigt som utbudet och efterfr-gan p marknadsbaserade instrument kar torde fortstta. Det finns ocks anledning att anta att vissa produkter p de finansiella marknaderna kommer att frsvinna medan nya kommer till. Exempel p produkter som kan komma att frsvinna r t.ex. intra-europeiska valutaterminer, intra-europeiska "currency swap". Dessutom kommer inte intern riskhantering och system fr hantering av intra europeisk valutarisk att behvas efter vergngen till euro enligt ISMA (International Securities Market Association). Samtidigt kan nya produkter skapas t.ex. euro optioner, euro terminer, aktieindex fr euroomrdet och eurodesignade avvecklingssystem. I detalj kan vi inte veta vad som kommer att hnda, marknaden kommer i stor utstrckning att styra utvecklingen p detta omrde. Hur stor just EMU's betydelse kommer att visa sig vara fr hela denna omvandlingsprocess kan diskuteras och lter svrligen avgrnsas och mtas p frhand - och kanske inte ens i ef-terhand. Man kan givetvis, och med rtta, hvda att den i frsta hand styrs av integ-rationen globalt och av EU's inre marknad. Dock r det mycket sannolikt att EMU kommer att pskynda och accentuera denna utveckling. Dagens europeiska kapitalmarknader r fragmenterade. Inhemska banker och frskringsbolag dominerar i de flesta lnder och Sverige r inget undantag. Grunden fr detta r inte bara att det r olika valutor i Europa utan antagligen n mer kundernas tendens att hlla sig till banker de knner i kombination med bankernas sedan lnge frvrvade kunskaper om kreditrisker och lokala marknader. Med undantag fr att de olika valutorna frsvinner kvarstr argumenten fr natio-nellt baserade verksamheter ven sedan EMU bildats. I kombination med sprksvrigheter och kulturella skillnader talar detta fr att utvecklingen i den finansiella "detaljhandeln" och dess struktur kommer att styras av i huvudsak andra faktorer n EMU. P sikt kan dock de ingende lnderna frvntas vxa allt nrmare var-andra och drmed ven de finansiella strukturerna. Nr det gller tjnster riktade mot fretag - srskilt strre fretag - finns det dock anledning att tro att ef-fekterna kan bli rtt stora rtt snart. Nr vi skrev vr lgesrapport om vergngen till euro kontaktade vi ven ett antal bostadsinstitut fr att f en uppfattning om vad vergngen skulle innebra fr bostadslnemarknaden. Uppfattningarna var dock delade och man hade nnu inte utrett frgan i ngon strre omfattning. Nr det gllde gamla ln som utbetalats fre 1 januari 1999 ansg flera institut att konvertering inte var ndvndig. Fram till dess att nya sedlar och mynt stts i omlopp skulle drfr avisering ske i kronor. Nr det gller tiden drefter kommer konverteringen att ske vid ett tillflle, men fysiska omskrivningar av bostadslnavtal sannolikt frst i takt med att villkoren ndras. Dock framkom ven sikten att konverteringen redan skulle kunna ske under vergngsperioden, s uppfattningarna tycks delade. Vad gller nya ln tycktes dock uppfattningen vara att efterfrgan p kronln kan komma att minska drastiskt redan 1 januari 1999. Dessa frgor tl att ytterligare diskuteras. Kreditrisken kar i betydelse Valutaunionen kommer generellt sett - p grund av ekonomisk konvergens mellan lnderna och en gemensam inflationbekmpande penningpolitik - att leda till att rnteniverna i hgrntelnderna och lgrntelnderna konvergerar. Fr detta ta-lar ven att valutariskpremien helt frsvinner eftersom det i EMU endast finns en valuta. Det som kommer att finnas kvar, ven efter vergngsprocessen r helt ge-nomfrd, r framfr allt likviditets- och kreditrisker. Nr det gller s k riskfria vrdepapper, typ statspapper, kan rnteniverna p tminstone korta papper komma att konvergera i stort sett fullt ut. Fr detta talar bland annat kraven p goda statsfinanser. I och med att valutarisken frsvinner och placeringsbesluten mera kommer att handla om kreditrisker talar mycket fr att det kan komma att bildas vl utvecklade europeiska marknader ver landgrnserna fr olika typer av obligationer som exempelvis fretags- bostads- och kommunobligationer. Till detta bidrar sannolikt ett intresse frn placerarnas sida att sprida sina risker genom att diversifiera sina portfljer till flera lnder fr att begrnsa frlustriskerna i hndelse av asymmetriska chocker i ngot land. Inressant att notera r att rating fr fretagen drmed skulle kunna skilja sig frn hemmalandets rating. Ett fretag, sg Volvo, skulle kunna ha hgre rating n Konungariket Sverige. Strre och mer likvida marknader Idag har vi i Sverige ca 9 miljoner potentiella placerare. Inom EU finns totalt drygt 370 miljoner. Drutver kan man rkna med att investerare frn andra lnder i Europa och frn resten av vrlden sker sig till denna nya stora marknad. Euron kommer, tillsammans med dollarn och yenen, att bli en av de tre stora reservvalutorna. En strre marknad leder normalt, genom stigande konkurrens, till lgre kostnader, bttre lnemjligheter och en kad likviditet. Det r svrt att se annat n att detta kommer att vara till frdel ven fr bostadsobligationsmarknaden. Det r allts troligt att lntagare i och med valutaunionen fr en strre marknad att verka p. Placerarna kommer ocks att bli flera och d valutarisken frsvinner blir det billigare fr dessa att diversifiera sina portfljer. Detta br inne-bra goda frutsttningar fr lntagare att f tag i en attraktiv finansiering via bland annat obligationsmarknaden. Nr det gller bostadssektorn och bostadsfinansieringen finns det ocks srskild anledning att peka p effekterna av den lgre och stablilare rnteniv som EMU, allt annat lika, kommer att innebra. Resultatet br bli hgre fastighetspriser, ett kat bostadsbyggande och drmed en kad efterfrgan p finansiering. Vad som sannolikt r mycket viktigt, nr det gller upplning p denna nya europeiska mark-nad r att lntagarna snabbt anpassar sig till internationell marknadsstandard nr det gller redovisning av sin ekonomi och finansiella stllning. I detta ligger ocks att skaffa sig en internationell rating. De lntagare som kan hantera detta kommer sannolikt att ha ett frsteg framfr andra. Som alltid r det lntagare med en stabil ekonomi som kan dra frdelar framfr andra. I denna konkurrens kommer ven hemlandets kreditvrdighet att spela in. Utlndska lngivare riktar sig redan i en kad utstrckning mot Sverige. Det r bland annat den nyligen etablerade franska kommunbanken (Credit Locale de France) ett gott exempel p. Men ven andra banker, bde norska, danska, finlndska, engelska, och amerikan-ska banker frstrker sina positioner i Sverige. I kombination med att banker i EMU-lnder kan lna ut till svenska lntagare utan valutakursrisk, leder detta till en kad konkurrens i Sverige och drmed ocks till generellt sett bttre lnevillkor. vergngsprocessen Nr det gller sjlva vergngsprocessen handlar det dels om att konvertera de finansiella instrumenten, dels om att "konvertera" den infrastruktur som instrumen-ten hanteras i. Fr att brja med instrumenten kan, och br, de lnder som gr med i EMU genomfra nyemissioner av sina statspapper i euro. ven andra emittenter - inte minst bostadsinstituten - torde ocks snabbt brja emittera i den nya valutan. Om ngot medlemsland vill konvertera sin utestende skuld till euro s fr landet ocks gra detta. Nr det gller infrastrukturen s pverkas framfr allt institutioner som brsen, VPC och OM nr det gller vrdepapperen och bankerna och Riksbanken nr det gller penning- och betalningshanteringen. Vad gller vrdepappersidan har de nmnda fretagen klart frordat en "big bang-lsning", dvs en snabb och samlad vergng frn kronor till euro redan vid rsskiftet 1998/1999, fr att undvika "dubbelsystem" som dels r operativt besvrliga och dyrbara, dels riskerar splittra likviditeten i marknaden, vilket sammataget skulle gra Sverige mindre attraktivt som internationell finansplats. VPC deltar ocks aktivt i diskussioner med sina europeiska motsvarigheter om att bygga upp ett gemensamt ntverk dr vrdepapper kan fras ver grnserna p liknande stt som pengar i centralbankernas Targetsystem. Detta r bde tekniskt och juridiskt ett komplicerat arbete som inte kom-mer att vara frdigt p denna sidan sekelskiftet, men det r gldjande att arbetet kommit igng. Nr det gller betalningssystem har jag tidigare nmnt Target-systemet, det gemensamma ntverket fr de centralbanksbaserade interbanksystemen. I Riksbanken arbetar vi intensivt med att gra vrt Rix-system kompatibelt med Target. Det stora omstllningsarbetet ligger dock i banksektorn - det r ju hr de stora kontostockar-na och de stora transaktionsvolymerna finns. Bankerna kommer mellan 1999 och 2002 att hantera bde euro och kronor. Det mste drfr ngonstans i systemet finnas en konverteringsmekanism, ett "skal" som rknar om frn kronor till euro och omvnt enligt den faststllda, fixa kursen. Bankernas kunder kommer att kunna ta emot euro och betala ut kronor och tvrtom, utan att behva gra valutaaffrer. Valutorna r ju egentligen inte tv va-lutor utan bara tv stt att uttrycka exakt samma vrde - man kan sga att frhllan-det mellan euron och kronan blir detsamma som mellan en 100-kronors sedel och fem 20kronors sedlar. En "skalfunktion" mste allts finnas p plats i princip omedelbart. Dremot kom-mer det inte att finnas ngot behov fr bankerna att omedelbart och samtidigt lgga om sina interna system med anledning av infrandet av euron - detta kan ske nr det bst passar varje bank under vergngsfasen. En annan frdel r att detta kan bidra till att undvika alltfr mycket av flaskhalsproblem nr det gller tillgng p data- och programmeringsexpertis.. Om Sverige str utanfr Sverige kan komma att hamna i en situation dr vi av olika skl inte r med i valutaunionen frn januari 1999. Detta innebr i formell mening en i huvudsak ofrndrad situation jmfrt med idag - RIX-systemet arbetar i kronor (ven om vi ven bygger ett parallellsystem i Euro), penningpolitiken bedrivs i kronor och statpapperen emitteras i kronor. Valutarisken kvarstr givetvis om man vljer att lna frn placerare i euro-omrdet och drmed ocks kostnader fr kursskring. Men i reell mening innebr det p flera stt frsmringar fr det svenska finan-siella systemet: mjligheterna att hantera betalningar via Target-systemet kommer troligen att bli smre. Eftersom Euron likvl kommer att bli en i alla avseenden stor valuta exempelvis kan man inte utesluta att flera av de stora svenska industriskoncer-nerna vergr till Euro som koncernvaluta - kommer det att innebra att de fi-nansiella fretagen tvingas investera i och driva parallella infrastrukturer. Om man inte med ngorlunda skerhet kan utg ifrn att det blir frga om en kortvarig "ute"-period, kommer dessutom dessa beslut att f fattas under stor oskerhet, och sannolikt ocks inom ramen fr en finansiell marknad med minskande internationell betydelse. Visserligen kan man sga att vi i alla hndelser fr leva med "dubbelsystem" under perioden 1999-2002 ven om vi r med i EMU, men det r skillnad p "dubbelsystem" och "dubbelsystem" - om vi r med i EMU handlar det fr det frsta om att hantera tv uttryck fr en och samma valuta, inte tv olika valutor, fr det andra handlar det om en klart avgrnsad tidsperiod. Intresset fr svenska placerare att vnda sig till marknaden i euro blir sannolikt mindre n om Sverige r med i unionen. En kning av placeringarna inom EMUblocket jmfrt med idag kan dock komma att ga rum. Detta skulle d innebra att utrymmet fr placeringar i Sverige kan komma att minska, ngot som skulle vara negativt bl.a. fr bofinansmarknaden. En annan nackdel med att inte komma med i valutaunionen frn brjan r att den diversifiering till olika sektorer, lntagare och lnder som utlndska placerare kan komma att genomfra, d inte kommer Sverige till del. Nr sedan Sverige, som jag utgr ifrn vid ett senare tillflle, gr in i valutaunionen har det stora tget gtt och intresset att placera i Sverige kommer d sannolikt att vara mindre eftersom placerarna d redan har diversifierat sin portfljer. Sammanfattning och slutsatser Det mesta talar idag fr att den ekonomiska och monetra unionen kommer igng som planerat den 1 januari 1999. Fr svensk del r frgan om vi ska vara med frn brjan, vnta ett tag eller frska hlla oss utanfr fr gott. Min frhoppning r att vi framver kommer att f en kad debatt om detta mycket viktiga beslut. Diskussionen infr detta stllningstagande br d inte bara koncentrera sig p fr-gan om penningpolitisk sjlvstndighet. Det handlar inte bara om ekonomi, ven om vi anser att de ekonomiska argumenten talar fr medlemskap. Det handlar ocks om att EMU r en viktig del i det europeiska utvecklingssamarbete dr Sverige nu deltar. -- Ett utanfrskap stller krav Ibland fr man i diskussionen intrycket av att det vid ett utanfrskap finns en enkel vg fr Sverige att g. Utanfr detta europasamarbete skulle vi slippa alla de anpassningkrav som stlls. S r det inte. Vi mste under alla omstndigheter arbeta vidare med att sanera statens finanser och att skapa en lngsiktig tilltro till stabiliteten i svensk ekonomi. Det blir knappast lttare utanfr EMU. Om vi str utanfr blir vi ppassade och d mste vi, som det brukar heta, vara "heligare n Pven" fr att inte rka i problem. Mjligheten att frska lsa arbetslshetsproblemen med inflationistisk ekonomisk politik och devalveringar finns inte inom ramen fr EMU men den finns inte heller utanfr EMU. -- Vrlden blir inte densamma Ett nej till EMU innebr inte status quo. Genom att det skapas en valutaunion pre-cis utanfr vra grnser kommer vrlden inte att vara sig lik. Bde privatpersoner och fretag kommer att knna av eurointroduktionen oavsett om vi r med eller inte. I vrt arbete med att informera den finansiella sektorn om EMU ser vi att fr-beredelserna gtt lngt. Vi ser ocks en stark nskan frn inblandade parter att f vara med s snabbt som mjligt fr att inte hamna p efterklken. - EMU och den svenska finanssektorn EMU kommer att bidra till ett kat strukturomvandlingstryck och drmed till kad effektivitet i alla delar av nringslivet. Detta gller i hg grad ocks finanssektorn, inklusive den del som vetter mot bostadssektorn. Vi fr ett helt annt utbud av aktrer bde p lntagar- och placerarsidan. Marknaden fokuseras p kreditrisker och blir mer transparent, mer diversifierad, mer konkurrensutsatt och mer effektiv. Det framstr rtt klart att ett utanfrskap av "tills-vidare"-karaktr skulle pverka den svenska finansiella sektorn p ett negativt stt. Dubblering av infrastrukturerna skulle skapa kade kostnader, och detta i frening med oskerhet om den framtida utvecklingen skulle minska de enskilda fretagens konkurrenskraft och den sven-ska finansmarknaden som helhet skulle bli mindre intressant fr bde svenska och utlndska aktrer. Till detta kommer riskerna fr mer eller mindre uttalad diskriminering, t. ex vad gller tillgngen till Target-systemet. -- Fortsatta frberedelser Oavsett den politiska diskussionen mste de praktiska frberedelserna fortstta. Inom EMI kommer man att fortstta att lsa de frgor man inte tagit stllning till nnu. Vi kommer att fortstta att delta i det arbetet. Hr hemma kommer rege-ringskansliet att fortstta att informera p sitt plan och vi kommer att fortstta vrt samarbete med den finansiella sektorn. Till hsten har vi ambitionen att skriva en ny rapport om EMU-frberedelserna. Efter att riksdagen tagit stllning till ett svenskt deltagande eller ej kommer vi ocks att ha mjlighet att ge klarare och en-tydigare besked om vilka frberedelser som kommer att behvas. Vi str infr en dynamisk process bde i vr omvrld och hr hemma.
