Title: How do you liquidate a bank in crisis?
text: Nyberg: How do you wind up a bank in crisis? Date: 2011-04-01 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg Location: Swedbank, Stockholm On Friday, April 1, Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg gave a speech at Swedbank in which he gave his view on how banks in crisis should be wound up. He began by stating that in practice it is difficult to allow banks, especially if they are large and important to the financial system, to go bankrupt like ordinary companies. This was shown not least during the crisis when a number of banks in the world came to be saved for continued lives and in several countries taxpayers had to contribute significant amounts. After all, in an ordinary bankruptcy, first the shareholders and then the creditors suffer the losses. But if the bank is saved from bankruptcy, the creditors and, in fact, sometimes also the shareholders, are saved. Instead, taxpayers suffer. It's obviously crazy," Nyberg said. What is needed, then, is legislation for banks that cannot be put into bankruptcy like ordinary companies, but which nevertheless leaves the shareholders and creditors to foot the bill if the bank is poorly managed and ends up insolvent. What such legislation should look like is one of the hot topics of the spring both in Sweden and internationally, Nyberg said. Nyberg then described why banks cannot go bankrupt like ordinary companies. But, Nyberg asked, if the traditional bankruptcy legislation is not suitable for banks, what should a functioning legislation look like? In fact, he continued, some kind of consensus is beginning to emerge around this in the international discussion. He then outlined the elements that he believes should be contained in such legislation. Firstly, the state needs to be able to intervene early in order for the bank to be kept alive. By early is meant before that the bank is formally insolvent. This intervention then needs to be followed by a quick process. Secondly, the state needs to have special tools to bring about an orderly settlement. These tools must enable the authorities to sell and restructure a bank, for example by dividing the bank into a good and a bad part. As a last resort, there is also a need to have the possibility of a state takeover of a bank. This is a sensitive issue in some parts of the world, but sometimes it is necessary. Then it is better that there are rules for how this should be done than that the opportunity is denied, Nyberg said. The best thing, of course, would be to avoid the state taking over banks. But then other ways must be found to improve the capital situation of the failing bank if it is to live on. What one could do is write down some debts or convert them into shares. This is referred to in the international discussion as "bail-in". Nyberg then described how bail-in can be designed in slightly different ways, but he also said that there are still some problems around "bail-in" to solve. After this account of what should be included, Nyberg switched to talking about what is happening in reality. He briefly talked about the regulations in the US and in the UK and what is going on in the EU. He compared these with the components that he believes should be in legislation and with the Swedish support law. Nyberg found that all the regulatory structures can deal with the most important problem, namely winding up a bank so that it is primarily the owners who are affected, not the taxpayers. But there are differences and he pointed to three of them, namely how creditors are treated, how views differ when it comes to government takeovers and how to treat small banks. When it comes to the latter, the treatment of small banks, it is we in Sweden who deviate, Nyberg noted. In contrast to the US and the UK, in Sweden there are no special rules for banks that are not systemically important, instead the usual bankruptcy procedure applies. Nyberg argued for a general legislation that can be applied to all banks. An important reason for this is that in real life situations it is very difficult to determine whether a bank is systemically important or not and each assessment contains a large degree of arbitrariness. It feels uneasy, Nyberg said, that the consequences for many people should unnecessarily be so dependent on assessments that are far from obvious. Read the full speech in the pdf file.

Datum: 2011-04-01 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg Plats: Swedbank, Stockholm Fredagen den 1 april hll vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg ett tal hos Swedbank i vilket han gav sin syn p hur banker i kris ska avvecklas. Han inledde med att konstatera att det i praktiken r svrt att lta banker, srskilt om de r stora och viktiga fr det finansiella systemet, att g i konkurs som vanliga fretag. Detta visade sig inte minst under krisen d ett antal banker i vrlden kom att rddas till fortsatt liv och i flera lnder fick skattebetalarna bidra med betydande belopp. I en vanlig konkurs drabbas ju frst aktiegarna och sedan fordringsgarna av frlusterna. Men rddas banken frn konkurs s rddas ocks fordringsgarna och faktiskt ibland ocks aktiegarna. I stllet drabbas skattebetalarna. Det r uppenbarligen tokigt, sade Nyberg. Vad som behvs r allts en lagstiftning fr banker som inte kan sttas i konkurs som vanliga fretag, men som nd lter aktiegarna och fordringsgarna st fr notan om banken skts dligt och hamnar p obestnd. Hur en sdan lagstiftning ska se ut r ett av vrens heta mnen bde i Sverige och internationellt, menade Nyberg. Nyberg beskrev sedan varfr banker inte kan g i konkurs som vanliga fretag. Men, frgade Nyberg, om den traditionella konkurslagstiftningen inte r lmplig fr banker, hur ska d en fungerande lagstiftning se ut? Faktiskt, fortsatte han, brjar det vxa fram ngon form av konsensus kring detta i den internationella diskussionen. Han redogjorde sedan fr de komponenter som han anser br finnas i en sdan lagstiftning. Fr det frsta s behver staten kunna gripa in tidigt fr att banken ska kunna hllas vid liv. Med tidigt menas fre det att banken formellt r p obestnd. Detta ingripande behver sedan fljas av en snabb process. Fr det andra behver staten ha srskilda verktyg fr att kunna f till stnd en ordnad avveckling. Dessa verktyg mste ge myndigheterna mjligheter att slja och omstrukturera en bank, exempelvis genom att dela upp banken i en bra och en dlig del. Man behver ocks som en sista utvg ha en mjlighet till ett statligt vertagande av en bank. Detta r en knslig frga p sina hll i vrlden, men ibland r det ndvndigt. D r det bttre att det finns regler fr hur det ska ske n att mjligheten frnekas, sade Nyberg. Det bsta vore naturligtvis om man kunde undvika att staten tar ver banker. Men d mste man hitta andra stt att frbttra den krisande bankens kapitalsituation om den ska leva vidare. Vad man skulle kunna gra r att skriva ner en del skulder eller konvertera dem till aktier. Detta kallas i den internationella diskussionen fr bail-in. Nyberg beskrev sedan hur bail-in kan utformas p lite olika stt, men han sade ocks att det terstr en del problem runt bail-in att lsa. Efter denna redogrelse fr vad som br ing gick Nyberg ver till att prata om vad som hnder i verkligheten. Han berttade kortfattat om regelverken i USA och i Storbritannien och vad som r p gng inom EU. Han jmfrde dessa med de komponenter som han anser br finnas i en lagstiftning och med den svenska stdlagen. Nyberg fann att alla regelstrukturerna kan hantera det viktigaste problemet, nmligen att avveckla en bank s att det i frsta hand r garna som drabbas, inte skattebetalarna. Men det finns skillnader och han pekade p tre av dem, nmligen hur fordringsgare behandlas, hur synen skiljer sig nr det gller statligt vertagande och hur man behandlar sm banker. Nr det gller det sistnmnda, behandlingen av sm banker, r det vi i Sverige som avviker, konstaterade Nyberg. I motsats till USA och Storbritannien s finns det i Sverige inga srskilda regler fr banker som inte r systemviktiga, istllet gller det vanliga konkursfrfarandet. Nyberg argumenterade fr en generell lagstiftning som kan tillmpas p alla banker. Ett viktigt skl fr detta r att det i verkliga situationer r mycket svrt att avgra om en bank r systemviktig eller inte och varje bedmning innehller ett stort mtt av godtycke. Det knns olustigt, sade Nyberg, att konsekvenserna fr mnga mnniskor i ondan ska vara s beroende av bedmningar som r lngtifrn sjlvklara. Ls hela talet i pdf-filen. Title: Households increase their debt and house prices continue to rise
text: Nyberg: Households are increasing their debts and house prices continue to rise Date 2005-08-25 "Developments since last spring show that households continue to increase their debt at a rapid pace. The latest single-family house barometer for July also shows continued rising house prices. Somewhere there is reasonably a limit to how long this development can continue". This was highlighted by Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg today at a conference organized by the National Land Survey. "The fact that house prices have risen over a long period can largely be explained by traditional demand and supply factors. The supply of new housing has been low for many years, while demand has increased as household incomes have improved and more and more people have moved to big cities. But supply and demand can change. A lot of housing is currently being built in the big cities and the supply is gradually increasing as these are completed. Demand usually follows the economic picture. Right now, the Swedish economy is strong, but when the economy eventually slows down, it is reasonable for the demand for housing to follow as well," Nyberg noted. "Of course, the low interest rates have also helped to keep the demand for loans and housing up. In addition, competition in the mortgage market has increased, reducing the margins that mortgage institutions charge for their lending, but also making them accept higher loan-to-value ratios and longer amortization periods. One factor behind this development is likely to be that mortgages will become more profitable for banks and their housing institutions with the new capital adequacy rules (Basel II)," Nyberg continued. "These supply and demand factors go a relatively long way to explain price and debt developments in Sweden. The speculative elements of the housing market are likely to be small. One reason for this is that Swedish households, unlike households in a number of other countries, buy homes to live in and not to assimilate an increase in value. You do not buy your home just to be able to sell it a few years later and make a capital gain. Therefore, prices do not go up in the same way as they can in a financial bubble, like the one we saw in the stock market not so long ago," Nyberg said. However, Nyberg emphasized that this in no way excludes future price falls. "Demand can decrease and supply can increase as a natural part of the business cycle, just as I described earlier. For households, it is probably immaterial whether we economists choose to talk about a bubble or not, if prices were to fall. Significant price falls are quite possible even if it is not a bubble, something that households should take into account in their calculations. However, prices should not fall as much and as quickly as if the development were primarily speculation-driven." "Recently, we have seen new products in the mortgage market that have allowed new categories of households to borrow. One example is mortgage pension - a form of loan that allows older people to take part in the increase in the value of their homes by mortgaging them. Another is what in English-speaking countries is usually called "sub-prime lending" - loans that, for example, are given without the requirement of ongoing income, but in return is a little more expensive," Nyberg said. "This type of loan has existed in other countries for a long time. It is fundamentally good for consumers that competition is increasing in the market and it is not wrong that borrowers who really pose a higher risk to the lender also pay a higher interest rate. Of course, this presupposes that the interest rate is a fair compensation for the increased risk. As always when it comes to new and unknown products, however, it is important that they are sold with such care, that customers are aware of how they work. Here, both the banks and the new companies that appear on the market have a great responsibility". "There may also be reasons to periodically ask ourselves what kind of competition is desirable and what the changes that have taken place mean. So far, the increased competition and new products have mostly been about increasing credit volumes, but I would like to see more of the innovations aimed at helping households manage the risks that arise. It would be good for everyone involved," Nyberg said. "The Riksbank is closely monitoring both the development of house prices and household indebtedness. It is not because we fear any crisis in the financial system. Households can generally afford their mortgages and Swedish banks are well capitalised. But experience shows that individual households can incur more debt than they can handle in the longer term, and there is reason to warn about this. In addition, the development of house prices affects households' decisions regarding savings and consumption, which in turn affects production and employment in Sweden. It is therefore obvious that these issues are also central to the discussion on monetary policy," Nyberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Nyberg: Hushllen kar sina skulder och bostadspriserna fortstter att stiga Datum 2005-08-25 Utvecklingen sedan i vras visar att hushllen fortstter att ka sina skulder i snabb takt. Den senaste smhusbarometern fr juli mnad visar ocks p fortsatt stigande bostadspriser. Ngonstans finns rimligen en grns fr hur lnge denna utveckling kan fortg. Detta framhll vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg idag vid en konferens anordnad av Lantmteriet. Att bostadspriserna har stigit under en lng period kan till stor del frklaras av traditionella efterfrge- och utbudsfaktorer. Utbudet av nya bostder har varit lgt under mnga r samtidigt som efterfrgan kat i takt med att hushllens inkomster frbttrats och allt fler flyttat till storstderna. Men utbud och efterfrgan kan frndras. Det byggs fr nrvarande mycket bostder i storstderna och utbudet kar successivt allteftersom dessa blir frdiga. Efterfrgan brukar flja konjunkturbilden. Just nu r den svenska ekonomin stark, men nr konjunkturen s smningom mattas av, r det rimligt att efterfrgan p bostder ocks fljer med konstaterade Nyberg. Sjlvklart har ocks de lga rntorna bidragit till att hlla efterfrgan p ln och bostder uppe. Dessutom har konkurrensen p bolnemarknaden kat, vilket minskat marginalerna som bolneinstituten tar fr sin utlning, men ocks ftt dem att acceptera hgre belningsgrader och lngre amorteringstider. En faktor bakom den utvecklingen r sannolikt att boln blir mer lnsamma fr bankerna och deras bostadsinstitut med de nya kapitaltckningsreglerna (Basel II) fortsatte Nyberg. Dessa utbuds- och efterfrgefaktorer rcker frhllandevis lngt fr att frklara prisoch skuldutvecklingen i Sverige. De spekulativa inslagen p bostadsmarknaden r sannolikt sm. Ett skl till detta r att de svenska hushllen, till skillnad frn hushll i en rad andra lnder, kper bostder fr att bo i och inte fr att tillgodogra sig en vrdestegring. Man kper inte sin bostad enbart fr att kunna slja den ngot r senare och gra en reavinst. Drfr trissas inte priserna upp p samma stt som de kan gra i en finansiell bubbla, likt den vi sg p aktiemarknaden fr inte s lnge sedan, ansg Nyberg. Nyberg understrk dock att detta inte p ngot stt utesluter framtida prisfall. Efterfrgan kan minska och utbudet ka som en naturlig del av konjunkturfrloppet, precis som jag beskrev tidigare. Fr hushllen r det nog ovsentligt om vi ekonomer vljer att tala om en bubbla eller inte, om nu priserna skulle falla. Betydande prisfall r fullt mjliga ven om det inte rr sig om en bubbla, ngot som hushllen br beakta i sina kalkyler. Priserna br emellertid inte falla s mycket och s snabbt som om utvecklingen frmst vore spekulationsdriven. Den senaste tiden har vi sett nya produkter p bolnemarknaden som gjort det mjligt fr nya kategorier av hushll att lna. Ett exempel r hypotekspension - en lneform som gr det mjligt fr ldre mnniskor att ta del av vrdestegringen p sina bostder genom att belna dessa. Ett annat r vad som i engelsksprkiga lnder brukar kallas sub-prime lending - ln som exempelvis ges utan krav p lpande inkomst, men i gengld r lite dyrare, sade Nyberg. Denna typ av ln finns sedan lnge i andra lnder. Det r i grunden bra fr konsumenterna att konkurrensen kar p marknaden och det r inte fel att lntagare som verkligen innebr en hgre risk fr lngivaren ocks betalar en hgre rnta. Title: Households' growing debt burden is not a problem for banks
text: Nyberg: Households' growing debt burden is not a problem for banks Date 2005-02-11 "Households now have average debts of 125 percent of annual income, almost as much as just before the 1992 real estate crisis. On the other hand, interest payments are less than half of what they were then, about 4 percent of income," deputy riksbank governor Lars Nyberg said at a breakfast meeting in Malmo today. "The fact that households borrow more, in Sweden and in many other countries, is linked to the fact that inflation and thus interest rates have fallen. It can be said that households' growing debt burden is partly a natural consequence of the successful inflation targeting policy pursued over the past decade," Nyberg continued. "Households also appear to have high confidence that both inflation and interest rates will remain low. They borrow to a large extent with short fixed interest periods. However, it is reasonable to expect interest costs to increase over a business cycle. The fact that interest rates can be twice as high as today when the loans are to be traded is something that every household should take into account when assessing the risks in their loan calculation," Nyberg said. Nyberg also noted that the supply of household credit has increased. "The new capital adequacy rules, Basel II, will give mortgages a lower risk weight. This makes it interesting for many banks to already increase their home lending. Competition has increased in the mortgage market, which has pushed down interest rates and created more favorable loan terms. However, the repayment capacity requirements that banks place on their mortgage customers appear to have been tightened." "Households are borrowing extensively to buy homes and that has led to rising prices in the housing market. In 2003 prices rose by 7% and in 2004 by 9%. Here and there in the country, where development has been particularly fast, I think there may be room for price drops. At the same time, we do not see the speculative trends that exist in several other countries, where households buy several homes to sublet and sell when prices have risen further. When prices are governed by expectations of future price rises rather than by normal demand and supply conditions, there is always a significant risk of a sharp fall in prices if expectations are breached. But in Sweden, we still buy homes to live in ourselves, not primarily to sell when prices rise," Nyberg said. "When you see that household lending has become as large as in the early 1990s and that housing prices have risen as they have, there is reason to ask whether the development may not be dangerous for the stability of the banking system. But even during the crisis of the early 1990s, it was not households that caused the banks serious problems. Instead, it was the lending secured by commercial real estate that caused problems. And when it comes to commercial real estate, neither lending nor prices have risen in this economic upturn," Nyberg continued. "Studies by the Riksbank show that even significant increases in interest rates or sharp falls in the price of housing would not cause the banks extensive losses. I am not concerned that household lending and house prices will threaten the stability of the banking system. However, the situation for individual households can become difficult if, with their large debt burden, they become too sensitive to changes in interest rates and house prices," Nyberg concluded.

Title: The economy and the real estate market
text: Nyberg: The economy and the real estate market Date 2008-03-04 In several countries, housing prices have slowed down recently and in some countries prices are even falling. The same applies to prices for commercial real estate. Prices in Sweden have so far not moderated to the same extent as in parts of the world around us. But a declining international economy and higher financing costs as a result of the financial crisis may also have effects on the Swedish real estate market. These are some of the messages from Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg, who today speaks at a real estate seminar in Karlstad. He also discusses the background to the decision to raise the repo rate to 4.25 percent at the last monetary policy meeting. "Just as in Sweden, with a few exceptions, house prices in the rest of the world have risen sharply over the past ten years. However, in a number of countries, prices are now increasing at a slower pace than in the past. This applies, for example, to Denmark, France, the United Kingdom and Spain. In the U.S. and Ireland, home prices are falling." "Housing is not a commodity that is traded across national borders. But changes in the outside world can still affect the Swedish housing market. When the international economy falters, the demand for Swedish goods decreases and eventually also the willingness and ability of Swedish households to pay for new or better housing. Swedish housing institutions are also dependent on borrowing on the international capital market. And here interest rates have risen as a result of the financial crisis. Higher interest rates are helping to reduce demand for housing and to slow the pace of price increases." "Until last autumn, pricing in the covered bond market in Europe was markedly homogeneous. But since September, there have been significant price differences depending on who issues the bonds. For Swedish housing institutions, the domestic market has worked well. Since the beginning of the year, they have again started issuing on the international market, although interest rates have been higher than before. For credit institutions in other European countries, things have gone significantly worse. Bonds issued in the UK and Spain have in many cases been met with suspicion in the market, which has been reflected in higher interest rate demands from investors. " "Commercial property prices have also risen in many countries in recent years. However, in some of these countries, including Ireland, the United Kingdom and Sweden, rents have not increased to the same extent. The fact that prices have nevertheless risen indicates that investors have demanded less and less for the risk they take. Risk premia has thus decreased. However, as a result of the turbulence in financial markets, investors have now reassessed their view of risk and are again demanding higher compensation. All other things being equal, it puts downward pressure on commercial property prices. This is most evident in the UK where prices were ten per cent lower in January compared to the same time last year." "Rising risk premia also has a negative impact on prices in the Swedish market. But the outlook in the rental market seems in the opposite direction. Employment in the services sector has increased significantly since 2006, which has meant that vacancy rates in the office market are currently low. This speaks for a positive rental trend and higher prices going forward. How the Swedish economy develops will also be decisive for the price development of the commercial real estate market." "In the international financial markets, performance has deteriorated rather than improved in recent months and uncertainty has increased. The risk premia that investors demand to buy bank bonds have risen. And the stock prices of financial institutions have fallen overall. In part, this is related to expectations that the US economic downturn appears to be deeper than previously expected. The economic downturn increases credit losses and amplifies the financial crisis. At the same time, the financial crisis is amplifying the economic downturn, as banks tighten the terms of their lending when they receive less capital. I don't think we've seen the end of this development yet. There are many indications that uncertainty in the financial markets will persist for a longer period of time." "In Sweden, we have mainly been able to regard the financial crisis as spectators. Swedish banks have not had any direct exposures to the troubled subprime market, and we have not seen the negative development in the real estate market that is experiencing in the US and several European countries. Nor do we see the falling economy that is the basis for the unrest in the United States. On the contrary, the economy in Sweden is still good, although we expect it to moderate somewhat in the coming year. Cost pressures are high and inflation is above the 2% target. In addition, inflation expectations have risen in both the short and long term. "This was mainly the background when we in the Riksbank's Executive Board had to take a position on the repo rate just over a couple of weeks ago. The monetary policy trade-off was unusually difficult. At the same time as the financial crisis entailed risks of a significantly weaker development in the rest of the world and thus in Sweden, domestic developments spoke quite unequivocally in favour of an increase in the repo rate. For me, the risks associated with the financial crisis were outweighed and I therefore wanted to hold off on a rate hike."

Title: Interest rates, real estate prices and monetary policy
text: Nyberg: Interest rates, real estate prices and monetary policy Date: 1999-12-15 Speaker: Deputy Governor lars Nyberg Location: Sveriges Trahusfabrikers Riksforbund Introduction At the outset, I would like to thank you for the invitation to the Swedish Association of Wooden House Factories. It feels particularly interesting to be here and talk because the slow pace of construction and the rising property prices - especially here in Stockholm - are something that has received a lot of attention recently. I intend to return to property prices and other asset prices later, as well as to what the Riksbank can do if these prices tend to develop too quickly. However, I would like to start by talking about the link between inflation and mortgage rates. Will the interest rate rise? A week ago, the Riksbank published this year's fourth inflation report. It noted, among other things, that both domestic and foreign demand are growing rapidly and that monetary policy may need to be adjusted in a tightening direction next year. How, then, can such austerity affect mortgage rates? By changing the repo rate, the Riksbank can influence other Swedish market interest rates. These, in turn, affect economic activity in the economy, such as business investment and household consumption, and thus, by extension, price developments. If the Riksbank raises interest rates, economic activity will slow and inflation will be held back. However, the Riksbank's actions do not have the same impact on all interest rates. Interest rates with the shortest maturities are controlled more or less directly via the repo rate, while interest rates with longer maturities are largely determined by factors that are beyond the Riksbank's direct control. Long-term interest rates are mainly internationally determined and are primarily influenced by the remuneration that large international capital investors require to buy Swedish government securities. The capital comes largely from pension funds all over the world, where the managers want to invest part of the fund's wealth in Europe. They often turn to German government and residential securities because these are considered safe and because they are easy to buy and sell in large quantities on the market. If you are going to invest in Swedish government securities, you want a little better interest than you get in Germany. If Swedish inflation is high, they want compensation for the risk of the krona falling in value. If government finances are weak, Sweden can be considered a worse credit risk, and then it would like compensation for it. Therefore, long-term interest rates are also affected by how the Riksbank manages monetary policy and how the government handles fiscal policy and government debt policy. The difference between the German and Swedish five-year yields is currently about 0.6 percentage points. In the mid-1990s, the difference was close to 5 percentage points. Mortgage lenders have to pay slightly higher interest rates than the state if they are to sell their Bonds. The surcharge on the government bond rate  the so-called mortgage spread  is due to several factors, including the fact that mortgage institutions are naturally considered to have higher credit risk than the government and that liquidity in the market is usually worse for mortgage bonds than for government securities. The mortgage spread, like the difference between the German and Swedish interest rates, has varied considerably over time. A change in the repo rate will have a rapid impact on variable mortgages and loans with short maturities. Mortgages with longer maturities are certainly affected by a change in the repo rate, but not to the same extent as variable loans. In this context, it may be worth noting that an increasing part of new lending is done at variable interest rates, which means that a change in the repo rate has a faster effect on household finances today than a couple of years ago (OH). The Riksbank's 0.35 percentage point repo rate hike on 11 November was the first in a long time. With one exception, the repo rate has been reduced since July 1995, a total of 5.7 percentage points. Monetary policy has long stimulated economic activity, which has been natural in the light of high unemployment and weak demand developments. Now that the economy has turned around and monetary policy is starting to tighten again, it is from a historically very low level of interest rates. Hopefully, a gradual adjustment of monetary policy will help us to achieve a period of good growth and growing employment. If the adjustment is gradual, we can avoid, as so many times before, having an overheated economy that requires greater tightening of monetary and fiscal policy than would have been necessary if the tightening had taken place at an earlier stage. The Riksbank's stated target is to keep inflation in the range of 1-3 per cent with 2 per cent as the benchmark. The repo rate will be adjusted with this target in mind. By keeping inflation at a low level, the Riksbank is helping to create confidence in economic policy and, in the longer term, to keeping interest rates down. Rising property prices I am now going to leave interest rates and move on to discussing price developments in the real estate market. As is well known, after the recession in the early 1990s, there has been a sharp rise in prices in this market. Prices of apartment buildings in metropolitan areas rose by over 20 per cent in the first half of this year alone and prices of detached houses are now at a higher level than before the fall in the early 1990s (OH). However, it should be emphasized that the development mainly concerns the metropolitan regions. Price developments in the rest of the country are subdued. This is an important difference from the 1980s when we saw sharp price increases across the country. One of the reasons why property prices have risen recently is certainly the historically low nominal interest rates. Another reason is the slow pace of construction. In this context, you usually follow the ratio between what an existing house costs and what it costs to build a new one. In economic literature, that ratio is called "Tobin's q" after Nobel laureate James Tobin, who studied, among other things, real estate prices. If Tobin's q is equal to one, it means that the cost of buying an existing house and building a new one is equal. If house prices rise so that the market value is higher than the replacement value, it will pay to build new, since every krona invested is valued at more than a dime by the market. If you study Tobin's q at present, you will see that there is a marked difference between large cities and the rest of the country (OH). In the metropolitan regions, we have a Tobin's q that clearly exceeds one, i.e. it is cheaper to build new than to buy an existing property. This is different from other regions where it is cheaper to buy an existing property. Despite the fact that, by this measure, it would pay to build new buildings in the metropolitan regions, housing construction is still at a very low level. One explanation for this may be that the price increase has occurred quickly and it takes time to gather resources for a more extensive construction. The shortage of construction workers in big cities points in that direction. The low pace of construction combined with increased demand and low interest rates has thus led to property prices rising significantly in metropolitan regions. This development brings to mind developments in the late 1980s. We all remember how it ended that time, when the price rises resulted in a bubble that eventually burst with a serious banking crisis as a result. So what is the current situation? Do we have reason to fear that the same thing may happen again? Let me first take a brief historical look back and then describe the current situation. One of the contributing factors to the rise in property prices in the 1980s was the deregulation of the credit market. There was a large pent-up need for loans and lending increased very sharply. High inflation in the wake of expansionary fiscal policies and tax rules that allowed for high deductions for interest payments made it profitable to borrow. The amortizations were quick in real terms. Taking into account tax effects, the real interest rate was even negative for long periods (OH). In this environment, with expansionary fiscal policy and a monetary policy focused on maintaining the fixed exchange rate, property prices and credit lending were driven up. When the policy was shifted to low inflation in 1991, while the tax reform reduced the deductibility of interest payments, the real interest rate on loans rose sharply, which in turn led to a fall in prices. Prices of commercial real estate in metropolitan regions halved over a period of 4 years and the financial crisis was a fact. So what does it look like at the moment? To get an idea of the price expectations in the real estate market, one can compare the dividend yield with the return on a risk-free investment, such as a government bond (OH). During the late 1980s, the bond yield was well above the dividend yield, reflecting strong expectations of an upturn in property prices. The dividend yield for residential properties has fallen in recent years and it cannot be ruled out that this may reflect expectations of rising prices. However, conversion to condominiums and expectations of a relaxation of the utility value system make the situation difficult to assess. In commercial real estate, price developments are more subdued and the same expectation picture cannot be discerned as for residential real estate. Can households and businesses cope with falling property prices? If today's relatively high real estate prices are speculation-driven, this will reasonably eventually be corrected more or less vehemently. An important question is how households and businesses would cope with such a situation. If you compare the current situation with what prevailed in the 1980s, there are major differences. The objective of monetary policy is no longer a fixed exchange rate but a stable monetary value and a low level has also been established for both inflation and inflation expectations. The real interest rate is stable and positive, which has reduced the incentives to borrow. At the same time, the adjustment processes following the currency and credit market deregulations and the tax reform have largely been completed. In addition, banks and other financial institutions have learned from the experience of the early 1990s and hopefully become better at assessing risks in lending. However, some similarities exist with the situation in the 1980s. Indebtedness has increased, but we are not seeing the same dramatic development as in the late 1980s, when debts peaked at 135% of disposable income. The new savings are low. However, households' disposable income can be expected to increase in the coming years, partly as a result of a more expansionary fiscal policy and partly due to lower unemployment as the economy has now turned around. In the corporate sector, lending growth is calmer. The annual growth rate of loans to companies from banks and housing institutions was 1.4% (excl. repos) in October, which must be described as rather low during an economic upturn. Debt is also low at present. A large part of lending to companies goes to the real estate sector. The situation in real estate companies today is satisfactory, with a low debt/equity ratio and a high interest coverage ratio for the sector as a whole. Thus, there is hardly any cause for concern that a correction in prices in the real estate market would bring about any serious disruptions in the economy. The sharp increases in the price of real estate are concentrated in the metropolitan areas, mainly Stockholm. Borrowing is not bothersomely high, especially among companies. It is worth recalling that it was companies that accounted for about 95% of credit losses during the banking crisis. The asset market where prices have risen the most in recent years is not the real estate market, but the stock market. Indices in the stock market have risen by over 50 percent this year alone. Here, of course, there may be a price correction. However, Swedish households' shareholdings are under leveraged, which is why a fall in share prices need not pose an immediate threat to financial stability. It looks different in the United States. The prolonged boom with sharply rising asset prices has meant that U.S. households have increased their consumption significantly faster than their incomes have risen. As a result, the U.S. household savings rate has fallen to historically low (OH) levels. Indebtedness has increased in recent years. Large shareholdings and high debt make U.S. households vulnerable to falls in asset prices, and a U.S. stock market collapse could therefore have serious consequences for the U.S. economy  and thus for the world economy. Unlike in Sweden, debt in the US corporate sector has also increased. What will the Riksbank do if asset prices rise? The implication of what I have said so far is that we cannot rule out that there may be incipient "bubble tendencies" in the Swedish asset markets. Should the Riksbank then act if asset prices change? The answer to this question depends on whether the development of asset prices threatens the inflation target, as formulated by the Riksbank, or financial stability, for which the Riksbank also has a responsibility. Let me start with how the evolution of asset prices can affect financial stability. Moderate fluctuations in asset prices will always occur. New information and changes in the underlying macroeconomic environment naturally lead to changes in asset prices and this is not something a central bank should be concerned about. If, on the other hand, asset prices have risen to such levels that one might suspect that it is a bubble, the situation may end up in a different situation. A bursting bubble can wreak havoc on the financial markets and thus threaten the stability of the financial system. It cannot be ruled out that such a situation can and should provoke an adjustment of monetary policy. Identifying a bubble is unfortunately a difficult, if not impossible task. As the US Federal Reserve Governor Alan Greenspan has pointed out, there is a fundamental problem here: 'You have to know something that the market does not know'. If you still succeed in the art of identifying a bubble, you risk causing more harm than good if you try to pierce it. The dominant strategy of central banks, therefore, is not to try to directly influence asset prices, but instead to try to quickly restore stability at the relatively few times when asset markets collapse. For example, the US Federal Reserve acted in the autumn of 1998 to mitigate the effects of the Asian crisis and to deal with the acute crisis that arose when Long Term Capital Management ran into problems. Let me again take a brief historical look back here. In October 1929, New York- the stock market, which was the prelude to the crisis that propagated across the world's financial markets and triggered a world depression. Instead of easing monetary policy in such a situation, it tightened. This was done for fear that the speculative attacks would pick up again and to defend the gold standard. This austerity had devastating effects on the entire real economy. A wave of bankruptcies swept across the country, not least in the banking sector, unemployment skyrocketed and great uncertainty spread among households. Activity in the economy almost completely stopped. In the period 1929-33, GDP fell by over 30 percent. Sweden was also affected by the depression, but fared better than many other countries and was able to quickly get out of the crisis. One reason that has been highlighted to explain this is that Sweden abandoned the gold standard, introduced a price stability objective and let the value of the krona be determined by the market, which meant that the krona was depreciated and competitiveness strengthened. The next stock market crash of significance occurred in 1987. On Monday, October 19, 1987, the Dow Jones index fell over 20 percent in one day. Wisely from the experience of 1929, monetary policy was eased this time on a broad front in the world. The FED increased liquidity in the financial system, causing short-term interest rates to fall, and it made it clear that it would act as a "lender of last resort" if necessary. Similar measures were taken in Sweden, the rest of Western Europe and Japan. Overall, the effects of the 1987 stock market crash were small on growth, inflation and unemployment. Thus, the lower interest rates resulting from the easing of monetary policy seemed to compensate to some extent for the fall in share prices. Asset prices and the inflation target How, then, is the Riksbank's second target, the inflation target, affected by changes in asset prices? It is usually said that it takes place in three ways; by influencing fortunes, by the granting of credit and by changes in the ratio of new and old capital  i.e. by Tobin's q. This time let's assume that asset prices are falling. The wealth effect means that when the value of the home/shareholding falls, households feel poorer and consume less. A household may have saved in shares and when assets suddenly decrease in value, you see your savings disappear and have to start saving more. How vulnerable an economy is to falling asset prices naturally depends on how much exposure to asset markets is. A household or company that has a large portion of its assets invested in stocks or real estate is reasonably more sensitive to falling asset prices than those that have their assets placed in the bank. In addition, if the assets are largely leveraged, the consequences of a fall in prices will be even more serious. The wealth effect has reasonably gained in importance in Sweden in recent years as a result of the stock market's development, but as has been pointed out, the shareholdings are only to a limited extent leveraged. The credit effect means that when a security (e.g. a property) falls in value, it cannot be leveraged as high and at the same low interest rate as before. A decline in asset values reduces the value of collateral and hinders potential borrowers' access to credit. When credit is not forthcoming, investment or consumption decreases, which has a negative impact on activity in the economy. The third effect occurs if asset prices fall so that the market value is lower than the replacement cost, i.e. if tobin's q, which I have spoken about earlier, is less than one. Then it will pay to buy existing capital rather than build new, which means that activity in the economy decreases. However, when assessing the impact on inflation, it must be taken into account that falling investment in real capital not only reduces demand in the economy, but also reduces overall production capacity. Thus, changes in supply prices affect inflation through effects on production capacity and demand in society. In this regard, they are not unique. If asset prices, together with other factors affecting the inflation assessment, indicate that inflation is falling below target, the Riksbank may lower interest rates. If they point in the opposite direction, the interest rate can be raised. Conclusion Let me conclude by summarising the Riksbank's view regarding price bubbles in the asset markets and the stability of the financial system. If there is reason to suspect that a bubble is building up, the Riksbank should not normally intervene with direct policy measures, unless the development of asset prices threatens its inflation target. This is because it is often difficult to first identify and then puncture a bubble. However, it must be kept open to the fact that the risks of a disruption to financial stability will be so great that the Riksbank chooses to act after all. However, the Riksbank is putting a lot of effort into regularly reporting its assessment of the risks in the financial system. This is primarily done in the financial stability report, which is published twice a year, the latest in October. An important idea behind the stability reports is to help ensure that the risks of, for example, rising asset prices and increasing borrowing are discussed openly. An open discussion can, in turn, help market participants to be more cautious in their risk-taking. Expectations of the Riksbank's actions are also important in this context. A transparent central bank with a clear and credible commitment to reach the inflation target means that financial actors expect higher interest rates if rising asset prices threaten to overheat the economy. The awareness that the Riksbank will act may in this way reduce the likelihood of bubbles forming. If asset markets are subjected to severe shocks in the form of large and sudden price falls and this poses a threat to financial stability, the Riksbank's monetary policy can be adjusted with the aim of trying to restore stability. Monetary policy easing during a period of drastically falling asset prices means making it easier for operators to pay the debts incurred, reducing the vulnerability of the economy to further shocks. However, this should not be interpreted as meaning that it is the Riksbank that is responsible for sorting out all crises once they have arisen. The Riksbank, like the Federal Reserve in the autumn of 1998, can help limit the spread of a crisis in the financial system. Responsibilities and costs always fall mostly on market participants, who have contributed to the build-up of a price bubble.

Om dessutom tillgngarna till stor del r lnefinansierade blir konsekvenserna av ett prisfall nnu allvarligare. Frmgenhetseffekten har rimligen ftt kad betydelse i Sverige under senare r till fljd av brsens utveckling, men aktieinnehaven r som ppekats endast i begrnsad utstrckning belnade. Krediteffekten innebr att nr en skerhet (t.ex. en fastighet) sjunker i vrde kan den inte belnas lika hgt och till samma lga rnta som tidigare. En nedgng i tillgngsvrdena reducerar skerheternas vrde och hindrar potentiella lntagares tillgng till kredit. Nr krediterna uteblir minskar investeringar eller konsumtion, vilket pverkar aktiviteten i ekonomin negativt. Den tredje effekten uppstr om tillgngspriserna faller s att marknadsvrdet blir lgre n teranskaffningsvrdet, dvs. om Tobins q som jag tidigare talat om, r mindre n ett. D kommer det lna sig att kpa existerande kapital snarare n att bygga nytt, vilket innebr att aktiviteten i ekonomin minskar. Vid en bedmning av effekterna p inflationen mste man dock beakta att fallande investeringar i realkapital inte bara minskar efterfrgan i ekonomin utan ocks minskar den samlade produktionskapaciteten. Frndringar i tillgngspriserna pverkar sledes inflationen genom effekter p produktionskapacitet och efterfrgan i samhllet. I detta avseende r de inte unika. Om tillgngspriserna jmte vriga faktorer som pverkar inflationsbedmningen pekar p att inflationen faller under mlet kan Riksbanken snka rntan. Om de pekar t motsatt hll s kan rntan hjas. Avslutning Lt mig avslutningsvis sammanfatta Riksbankens syn nr det gller prisbubblor p tillgngsmarknaderna och stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet. Om det finns anledning att misstnka att en bubbla hller p att byggas upp br Riksbanken normalt sett inte ingripa med direkta policytgrder, annat n om utvecklingen av tillgngspriserna hotar inflationsmlet. Detta eftersom det ofta r svrt att frst identifiera och sedan punktera en bubbla. Man mste dock hlla ppet fr att riskerna fr en strning av den finansiella stabiliteten blir s stora att Riksbanken trots allt vljer att agera. Riksbanken lgger emellertid ned ett ett stort arbete p att regelbundet redovisa sin bedmning av riskerna i det finansiella systemet. Det sker i frsta hand i rapporten Finansiell Stabilitet som publiceras tv gnger per r, den senaste i oktober. En viktig tanke bakom stabilitetsrapporterna r att bidra till att riskerna med t.ex. stigande tillgngspriser och kande belning diskuteras ppet. En ppen diskussion kan i sin tur medverka till att marknadsaktrerna blir mer frsiktiga i sitt risktagande. Frvntningarna om Riksbankens agerande r ocks viktiga i sammanhanget. En transparent centralbank med en tydlig och trovrdig utfstelse att n inflationsmlet gr att de finansiella aktrerna frvntar sig hjda rntor om stigande tillgngspriser hotar att verhetta ekonomin. Medvetandet om att Riksbanken kommer att agera kan p detta stt minska sannolikheten fr att bubblor bildas. Om tillgngsmarknader utstts fr kraftiga chocker i form av stora och pltsliga prisfall och detta utgr ett hot mot den finansiella stabiliteten kan Riksbankens penningpolitik anpassas med syfte att frska terskapa stabilitet. En penningpolitisk lttnad under en period med drastiskt fallande tillgngspriser innebr att man underlttar fr aktrerna att betala de skulder som uppkommit, vilket reducerar ekonomins srbarhet fr ytterligare chocker. Detta skall dock inte tolkas som att det r Riksbanken som ansvarar fr att reda ut alla kriser nr de vl uppkommit. Riksbanken kan, liksom Federal Reserve under hsten 1998, medverka till att begrnsa spridningen av en kris i det finansiella systemet. Title: The Riksbank's monetary policy strategy
text: Nyberg: Riksbank's monetary policy strategy Date 2006-05-19 Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg spoke on Friday at a meeting organised by Nordea. The theme of the speech was the Riksbank's monetary policy strategy. "There has been a discussion for some time about what our monetary policy targets are. There are those who have expressed that we should have several goals while others believed that we are already pursuing too many goals and that this creates ambiguity. During the spring, we have in various speeches described the Riksbank's view of which principles guide how monetary policy is conducted, and today we have published a special document in which we report on this. I will therefore begin by, with this document as a background, say a few words about the Riksbank's goals and strategies and then give my view on the monetary policy situation," Nyberg began. "The document clearly states that the Riksbank has a statutory objective for monetary policy: to maintain a fixed monetary value. We have defined it as the annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) to be 2 percent with a tolerance range of 1 percentage point. Often, monetary policy is also guided by other measures of inflation, especially UND1X, i.e. CPI excluding interest costs for own homes, indirect taxes and subsidies. Monetary policy normally focuses on achieving the inflation target within a two-year period. This horizon is justified by the fact that monetary policy operates with some delay, but also by a desire to dampen fluctuations in the real economy. By not having the ambition to return inflation to its target as soon as possible, the Riksbank will have room to take into account, in addition to inflation developments, how the real economy, such as growth and employment, develops. At the same time, the two-year horizon and the tolerance range set a limit on how large deviations from the target can normally be allowed. This flexibility can only be used as long as there is a high level of confidence in inflation targeting policies. Otherwise, we would have to change interest rates more often and in larger steps and not have the same opportunities to take into account the development of the real economy," Nyberg stressed. "However, there may be situations when we may need even greater flexibility than the two-year perspective allows. For example, if the economy were to suffer an unexpectedly large supply disruption, it may be necessary to allow it to take longer than two years for inflation to return to target. Otherwise, there is a risk that the strain on the real economy will be too great. In order for this flexible application of the inflation target to be possible and not perceived as arbitrary, it is important that we state openly and clearly why inflation is expected to deviate from the target within the normal time horizon. We do this in inflation reports, press releases, minutes of our meetings and in speeches from executive board members," Nyberg said. "Since the third inflation report last year, the Riksbank has switched to making its forecasts under the assumption that the repo rate will develop in line with market expectations, as reflected in the so-called implicit futures rates. Previously, we based our forecasts on the assumption that the repo rate would remain unchanged during the forecast period. One advantage of basing forecasts on more realistic repo rate assumptions is that it becomes easier to make consistent forecasts on, for example, exchange rates and long-term interest rates, which depend to a large extent on expectations of short-term interest rate developments. Another advantage is that it will be easier to evaluate the forecasts and to compare our forecasts with the forecasts made by other forecasters. The new interest rate assumption means that the old rule of action for monetary policy, which said that if the inflation forecast deviated from the target over a couple of years' time, the interest rate would normally change, is no longer applicable. The inflation forecast is now based on interest rates developing in line with market expectations. Given this path of interest rates, inflation is expected to be close to the target in a two-year horizon, market expectations about future monetary policy can normally be considered reasonable. But to determine it more firmly, we need to take into account what the entire trajectory of inflation and the real economy looks like. The monetary policy decisions and how we view market expectations are then based on an overall valuation of these," Nyberg said. "The Riksbank has not yet taken the step fully and itself has presented its own forecast for interest rate developments. But it is an opportunity that there is reason for us on the Executive Board to discuss," Nyberg continued. "Since the turn of the year, the Riksbank has been moving monetary policy in a somewhat less expansionary direction in the sense that the repo rate has been raised by a total of 0.5 percentage points. The main reason for the increases is that we foresee a continued economic upturn and rising resource utilisation, which means that interest rates must gradually be raised to secure inflation in line with the two-year target. In addition, it should be borne in mind that household indebtedness and house prices have continued to grow at a rate that is hardly sustainable in the long term. If this trend continues, it risks leading to a situation further down the line where there is a sudden downward adjustment in house prices with major repercussions on domestic demand and inflation as a result," Nyberg continued. "A gradual rise in interest rates increases the chances of a calmer deceleration in the pace of housing price growth and thus reduces the risk of large fluctuations in the real economy. This should not be interpreted as meaning that the Riksbank has any specific target for how much house prices and borrowing should increase. On the other hand, monetary policy decisions should take these aspects into account insofar as they involve risks of large fluctuations in the real economy and inflation. As far as financial stability is concerned, there are no signs that house prices and household indebtedness currently pose a threat," Nyberg noted. "Let me conclude by briefly commenting on the decision at the last monetary policy meeting to keep the repo rate unchanged. In the rest of the world, growth looks somewhat stronger. It is particularly interesting to note that cyclical indicators have now also clearly strengthened in the euro area. The new information received since February confirms the favourable economic picture that was drawn for Sweden in the Inflation Report. With regard to the inflation outlook, the Inflation Report estimated that inflation would rise to approach 2% over a couple of years' time, provided that the repo rate is gradually raised over the forecast period. This picture is quite correct, even if inflation is slightly higher than expected in the short term. Let me also say something about the turmoil of the last few days in the financial markets. We have had a long period of very low volatility in most financial markets. It is not surprising if this volatility would increase slightly. This does not necessarily mean that we are facing a prolonged stock market downturn. Measures of the P/E ratios, for example, are not abnormally high," Nyberg said. "At the last monetary policy meeting, we chose to leave the repo rate unchanged. However, it was not an obvious decision. Monetary policy remains very expansionary, which is reflected, among other things, in continued rapid credit growth and the rate of increase in housing prices, which now also seem to have spread to the commercial real estate market. In my opinion, the economic and inflation outlook suggests that it will soon be time to take the next step towards a less expansionary monetary policy. It is also in line with market expectations," concluded Nyberg.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Nyberg: Riksbankens penningpolitiska strategi Datum 2006-05-19 Vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg talade under fredagen p ett mte anordnat av Nordea. Temat fr anfrandet var Riksbankens penningpolitiska strategi. Det har under en tid frts en diskussion om vilka ml vi har fr penningpolitiken. Det finns de som uttryckt att vi borde ha flera ml medan andra menat att vi redan strvar efter fr mnga ml och att detta skapar otydlighet. Under vren har vi i olika tal beskrivit Riksbankens syn p vilka principer som r vgledande fr hur penningpolitiken bedrivs och idag har vi publicerat ett srskilt dokument dr vi redogr fr detta. Jag tnker drfr inleda med att, med detta dokument som bakgrund, sga ngra ord om Riksbankens ml och strategier fr att drefter ge min syn p det penningpolitiska lget, inledde Nyberg. Av dokumentet framgr tydligt att Riksbanken har ett lagstadgat ml fr penningpolitiken: att upprtthlla ett fast penningvrde. Vi har definierat det som att den rliga frndringen av konsumentprisindex (KPI) ska vara 2 procent med ett toleransintervall p  1 procentenhet. Ofta vgleds penningpolitiken ocks av andra mtt p inflationen, framfrallt UND1X, dvs. KPI exklusive rntekostnader fr egna hem, indirekta skatter och subventioner. Penningpolitiken inriktas normalt p att uppn inflationsmlet inom en tvrsperiod. Denna horisont motiveras av att penningpolitiken verkar med viss frdrjning men ven av en nskan att dmpa svngningar i den reala ekonomin. Genom att inte ha ambitionen att terfra inflationen till mlet s fort som mjligt fr Riksbanken ett utrymme att vid sidan av inflationsutvecklingen ven ta hnsyn till hur den reala ekonomin, till exempel tillvxt och sysselsttning, utvecklas. Tvrshorisonten och toleransintervallet stter samtidigt en grns fr hur stora avvikelser frn mlet som normalt kan tilltas. Denna flexibilitet kan bara utnyttjas s lnge som det finns ett stort frtroende fr inflationsmlspolitiken. I annat fall skulle vi vara tvungna att ndra rntan oftare och i strre steg och inte ha samma mjligheter att ta hnsyn till realekonomins utveckling, betonade Nyberg. Det kan dock uppst situationer nr vi kan komma att behva en nnu strre flexibilitet n vad tvrsperspektivet medger. Om till exempel ekonomin skulle drabbas av en ovntat stor utbudsstrning kan det vara ndvndigt att lta det ta lngre tid n tv r fr inflationen att komma tillbaka till mlet. Risken r annars att pfrestningarna p den reala ekonomin blir allt fr stora. Fr att denna flexibla tillmpning av inflationsmlet ska vara mjlig och inte uppfattas som godtycklig r det viktigt att vi ppet och tydligt redovisar varfr inflationen vntas avvika frn mlet inom den normala tidshorisonten. Detta gr vi i inflationsrapporter, pressmeddelande, protokoll frn vra sammantrden och i tal frn direktionens ledamter", sa Nyberg. Sedan den tredje inflationsrapporten frra ret har Riksbanken vergtt till att gra sina prognoser under antagandet att reporntan utvecklas i linje med marknadens frvntningar, s som de speglas i de s kallade implicita terminsrntorna. Tidigare baserade vi vra prognoser p antagandet att reporntan skulle vara ofrndrad under prognosperioden. En frdel med att basera prognoserna p mer realistiska antaganden om repornteutvecklingen r att det blir lttare att gra konsistenta prognoser p till exempel vxelkurs och lngrntor, som i hg grad beror p frvntningar om kortrnteutvecklingen. En annan frdel r att det blir lttare att utvrdera prognoserna och att jmfra vra prognoser med de prognoser som andra prognosmakare gr. Det nya rnteantagandet innebr att den gamla handlingsregeln fr penningpolitiken, som sade att om inflationsprognosen avvek frn mlet p ett par rs sikt skulle rntan normalt ndras, inte lngre r tillmplig. Inflationsprognosen baseras numera p att rntan utvecklas i linje med marknadens frvntningar. Om inflationen givet denna rntebana vntas vara nra mlet i ett tvrigt tidsperspektiv kan marknadens frvntningar om den framtida penningpolitiken normalt betraktas som rimliga. Men fr att avgra det mer bestmt mste vi ta hnsyn till hur hela utvecklingsbanorna fr inflationen och den reala ekonomin ser ut. De penningpolitiska besluten och hur vi ser p marknadens frvntningar baseras sedan p en samlad vrdering av dessa, sa Nyberg. Riksbanken har nnu inte tagit steget fullt ut och sjlv redovisat en egen prognos fr rnteutvecklingen. Men det r en mjlighet som det finns anledning fr oss i direktionen att diskutera, fortsatte Nyberg. Riksbanken har sedan rsskiftet frt penningpolitiken i en ngot mindre expansiv riktning i den meningen att reporntan hjts med sammanlagt 0,5 procentenheter. Huvudmotivet till hjningarna r att vi ser framfr oss en fortsatt konjunkturuppgng och ett stigande resursutnyttjande som gr att rntan gradvis mste hjas fr att skra en inflation i linje med mlet p tv rs sikt. Drtill finns det anledning att beakta att hushllens skuldsttning och huspriserna fortsatt att ka i en takt som knappast r lngsiktigt hllbar. Om denna utveckling fortstter riskerar det att leda till en situation lngre fram dr det sker en pltslig anpassning nedt i huspriserna med stora terverkningar p inhemsk efterfrgan och inflation som fljd, sade Nyberg vidare. En gradvis hjning av rntan kar mjligheterna fr en lugnare uppbromsning av priskningstakten p bostder och minskar drmed risken fr stora svngningar i den reala ekonomin. Det ska inte tolkas som att Riksbanken har ngot speciellt ml fr hur mycket huspriserna och upplningen br ka. Dremot finns det i de penningpolitiska besluten skl att beakta dessa aspekter i den mn de inrymmer risker fr stora fluktuationer i realekonomin och inflationen. Vad gller den finansiella stabiliteten finns det inga tecken p att huspriserna och hushllens skuldsttning fr nrvarande utgr ngot hot, konstaterade Nyberg. Lt mig avslutningsvis kort kommentera beslutet vid det senaste penningpolitiska sammantrdet att hlla reporntan ofrndrad. I omvrlden ser tillvxten ngot starkare ut. Det r srskilt intressant att notera att konjunkturindikatorerna nu ven har strkts tydligt i euroomrdet. Den nya information som inkommit sedan i februari bekrftar den gynnsamma konjunkturbild som tecknades fr Sverige i inflationsrapporten. Nr det gller inflationsutsikterna var bedmningen i inflationsrapporten att inflationen skulle stiga fr att p ett par rs sikt nrma sig 2 procent, under frutsttning att reporntan successivt hjs under prognosperioden. Den bilden str sig rtt vl ven om inflationen r ngot hgre n vntat p kort sikt. Lt mig ocks sga ngot med anledning av de senaste dagarnas oro p de finansiella marknaderna. Vi har haft en lng period av mycket lg volatilitet p de flesta finansiella marknaderna. Det r inte frvnande om denna volatilitet skulle ka ngot. Det behver inte betyda att vi str infr en lngvarig brsnedgng. Mtt p P/E-talen r till exempel inte onormalt hga, sade Nyberg. Vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet valde vi att lmna reporntan ofrndrad. Det var dock inget sjlvklart beslut. Penningpolitiken r alltjmt mycket expansiv vilket bland annat kommer till uttryck i en fortsatt snabb kredittillvxt och priskningstakt p bostder, som nu ocks tycks ha spritt sig till marknaden fr kommersiella fastigheter. Enligt min uppfattning talar konjunktur- och inflationsutsikterna fr att det snart r tid att ta nsta steg mot en mindre expansiv penningpolitik. Det r ocks i linje med marknadens frvntningar, avslutade Nyberg. Title: Sweden's economic development
text: Nyberg: Sweden's economic development (press release) Date: 2004-01-28 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg Location: Share meeting arranged by Aktiespararna Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg spoke today at a share meeting arranged by Aktiespararna about the Riksbank and the current situation "As you know, the goal of monetary policy is to maintain a fixed monetary value, which the Riksbank has defined as the rate of change in the CPI to reach 2 percent with a permissible deviation of /- 1 percentage point. In order to achieve this goal, it is important that there is confidence in monetary policy. This requires transparency and clarity on our part. Therefore, it is an important part of our business to explain monetary policy and the inflation assessment on which it is based. At the beginning of February, we will meet in the Executive Board of the Riksbank to discuss the recent economic development, its implications for the inflation outlook and thus the design of monetary policy. It is around my view of this that I will primarily dwell today," Nyberg said. "Recent statistics broadly confirm the picture of international and domestic economic developments outlined in the latest Inflation Report and the recovery appears increasingly stable. Developments in the financial markets also indicate a continued economic upturn. Looking at the U.S. economy, the signals have been generally positive both in the household sector and business. However, the dollar has continued to weaken, which can be assumed to be due to developments in the current account deficit, combined with increasing government budget deficits. However, the depreciation has taken place from a level that was generally judged to be far too high. In the euro area, newly emerging statistics essentially support the picture drawn in the Inflation Report. However, the strong development of the euro may mean that exports will be weaker than expected and thus also growth," Nyberg said. "In Sweden, the outcome statistics for the third quarter of 2003 indicate that the economic upturn will continue. Other indicators, such as retail sales growth and the barometers of the National Institute of Economic Research, also speak for this. However, the picture is not yet completely unambiguous. Industrial output has developed relatively weakly and new orders have declined. In addition, recent estimates of public finances suggest that public consumption this year may be slightly weaker than assumed in December. This suggests weak employment growth in the public sector, while an upturn in private sector employment is not yet discernible. Inflation has so far developed about as expected, on the margin slightly weaker at the end of last year. The weak labour market situation has been reflected in surprisingly strong productivity developments. This may have contributed to the somewhat more favourable inflation trend. Whether the good productivity growth will last for a longer period of time is still uncertain, but the development so far gives reason to look somewhat more optimistically at the Swedish supply conditions. What the overall effect of all this will be on the outcome of the salary negotiations remains to be seen, but there are currently, as I see it, reasons to be cautious optimistic," Nyberg said. "The debt burden on Swedish households has grown throughout the economic slowdown. Low interest rates and rising disposable incomes have meant that households have gradually borrowed more and debt is now at a high level with what they did in the early 1990s, before the great real estate crisis. In addition, the trend towards higher borrowing appears to be continuing. The prices of housing have also risen, despite the economic slowdown. We share this experience with many other countries where inflation has fallen and stabilised at a low level. It is possible that the increased propensity of households to borrow is a natural adaptation to an environment of low inflation and low interest rates. After all, the difference from the years before the crisis and the introduction of the inflation targeting regime is that interest costs in relation to income are lower, which makes the high debts bearable. Nevertheless, there is reason to be vigilant about developments. In any case, the increased debt burden has made households more sensitive to rising interest rates and falling house prices," Nyberg said. "Overall, the real economic development both abroad and in Sweden has been approximately as we expected in December. However, the weak development of the labour market has continued. The low inflation has meant that even small nominal wage increases can lead to increased real wages, which, as I see it, has reduced the risk that wage movement will disrupt the inflation picture. In addition, productivity figures have continued to surprise positively, which may mean that the economic upturn can probably last for some time without inflation rising. I also think that we have reason to be a little less worried that high electricity prices would spread and have a lasting impact on price developments in other sectors of the economy. All this suggests that inflationary pressures will be somewhat more subdued than we estimated in December. This could thus suggest that some further reduction in the repo rate is possible, especially since the inflation outlook was already quite favourable already in December. While we foresee an economic upturn that will sooner or later lead to monetary policy having to be tightened again, there is no indication that the upturn would be so strong and rapid that it would speak against a lighter monetary policy at present. In my opinion, this is the situation ahead of the Executive Board meeting on 5 February. The decision next week will of course, as usual, be made in light of all the information that then exists", Nyberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Nyberg: Sveriges ekonomiska utveckling (pressmeddelande) Datum: 2004-01-28 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg Plats: Aktietrff arrangerad av Aktiespararna Vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg talade idag p en aktietrff arrangerad av Aktiespararna om Riksbanken och det aktuella lget "Som ni vet r mlet fr penningpolitiken att upprtthlla ett fast penningvrde, vilket Riksbanken har definierat som att frndringstakten i KPI ska uppg till 2 procent med en tillten avvikelse p +/- 1 procentenhet. Fr att uppn det mlet r det viktigt att det finns frtroende fr penningpolitiken. Det stller krav p ppenhet och tydlighet frn vr sida. Drfr r det en viktig del av vr verksamhet att frklara penningpolitiken och den inflationsbedmning som den grundar sig p. I brjan av februari sammantrder vi i Riksbankens direktion fr att nyo resonera om den senaste tidens ekonomiska utveckling, dess implikationer fr inflationsutsikterna och drmed penningpolitikens utformning. Det r kring min syn p detta som jag framfrallt kommer att uppehlla mig idag", sade Nyberg. "Nyinkommen statistik bekrftar i stort den bild av den internationella och inhemska konjunkturutveckling som tecknades i den senaste inflationsrapporten och terhmtningen tycks alltmer stabil. ven utvecklingen p de finansiella marknaderna indikerar en fortsatt konjunkturuppgng. Ser vi till den amerikanska ekonomin har signalerna varit verlag positiva bde vad gller hushllssektorn och nringslivet. Dollarn har dock fortsatt att frsvagas, vilket kan frmodas bero p utvecklingen av bytesbalansunderskottet, i kombination med kande underskott i statsbudgeten. Deprecieringen har emellertid skett frn en niv som allmnt bedmdes som alldeles fr hg. I euroomrdet stdjer nyinkommen statistik i allt vsentligt den bild som tecknades i inflationsrapporten. Den starka utvecklingen av euron kan emellertid medfra att exporten blir svagare n vntat och drmed ven tillvxten", sade Nyberg. "I Sverige tyder utfallsstatistiken fr tredje kvartalet 2003 p att konjunkturuppgngen fortstter. Fr detta talar ocks andra indikatorer, exempelvis detaljhandelstillvxten och konjunkturinstitutets barometrar. Bilden r dock nnu inte helt entydig. Industriproduktionen har utvecklats relativt svagt och orderingngen minskat. Nya berkningar av de offentliga finanserna tyder dessutom p att den offentliga konsumtionen i r kan bli ngot svagare n vad som antogs i december. Detta talar fr en svag sysselsttningsutveckling i den offentliga sektorn samtidigt som en uppgng i sysselsttningen i den privata sektorn nnu inte kan sknjas. Inflationen har hittills utvecklats ungefr som vntat, p marginalen ngot svagare under slutet av frra ret. Det svaga lget p arbetsmarknaden har terspeglats i en verraskande stark produktivitetsutveckling. Det kan ha bidragit till den ngot mer gynnsamma inflationsutvecklingen. Huruvida den goda produktivitetstillvxten kommer att hlla i sig en lngre tid r dock fortfarande oskert men utvecklingen hittills ger skl att se ngot mer optimistiskt p de svenska utbudsfrhllandena. Vad den sammantagna effekten av allt detta blir p utfallen av lnefrhandlingarna terstr att se, men det finns i dagslget s som jag ser det skl till att vara frsiktigt optimistisk", sade Nyberg. "De svenska hushllens skuldbrda har vuxit under hela konjunkturavmattningen. Lga rntor och stigande disponibla inkomster har gjort att hushllen gradvis lnat mer och skulderna ligger nu i hjd med vad de gjorde i brjan av 1990-talet, innan den stora fastighetskrisen. Utvecklingen mot hgre belning frefaller dessutom fortstta. Priserna p bostder har ocks stigit, konjunkturavmattningen till trots. Vi delar dessa erfarenheter med mnga andra lnder dr inflationen fallit och stabiliserats p en lg niv. Det r mjligt att hushllens kade bengenhet att lna r en naturlig anpassning till en milj med lg inflation och lga rntor. Skillnaden mot ren fre krisen och infrandet av inflationsmlsregimen r ju att rntekostnaderna i frhllande till inkomsterna r lgre, vilket gr de hga skulderna mjliga att bra. Inte desto mindre finns det anledning att vara vaksam ver utvecklingen. Under alla omstndigheter har den kade skuldbrdan gjort hushllen mer knsliga fr stigande rntor och fallande bostadspriser", sade Nyberg. "Sammantaget har den realekonomiska utvecklingen bde utomlands och i Sverige varit ungefr som vi frvntade i december. Den svaga utvecklingen p arbetsmarknaden har emellertid fortsatt. Den lga inflationen har gjort att ven sm nominella lnelyft kan ge hjda reallner, vilket, som jag ser det, minskat risken att lnerrelsen ska stra inflationsbilden. Dessutom har produktivitetssiffrorna fortsatt att verraska positivt, vilket kan gra att konjunkturuppgngen antagligen kan pg nnu en tid utan att inflationen stiger. Jag tror ocks att vi har skl att vara lite mindre oroliga fr att hga elpriser skulle sprida sig och varaktigt pverka prisutvecklingen i andra sektorer av ekonomin. Allt detta talar fr att inflationstrycket kommer att vara ngot mer dmpat n vi bedmde i december. Detta skulle drmed kunna tala fr att en viss ytterligare snkning av reporntan r mjlig, srskilt som inflationsutsikterna redan i december redan var ganska gynnsamma. Vi ser visserligen framfr oss en konjunkturuppgng som frr eller senare kommer att leda till att penningpolitiken ter mste stramas t, men inget tyder p att uppgngen skulle bli s stark och snabb att den skulle tala mot en lttare penningpolitik i dagslget. S ser enligt min mening situationen ut infr direktionssammantrdet den 5 februari. Beslutet nsta vecka kommer vi frsts som vanligt att fatta mot bakgrund av all information som d finns", avslutade Nyberg.
