Title: Challenges in monetary policy
text: Nyberg: Challenges in monetary policy Date 2007-05-25 Deputy Governor Lars Nyberg spoke today in Stockholm at a meeting organised by Nordea. Among other things, he discussed the monetary policy situation and his position at the previous monetary policy meeting. "The fact that the economy is currently very favourable can hardly have escaped anyone. International development is very strong. While some signs of weakness linked to the housing and automotive markets can be discerned in the US, on the other hand, European economies are growing somewhat faster than expected. Most indications are that growth internationally will develop overall in line with the Riksbank's forecasts. To this positive picture can be added a renewed optimism in the stock markets after a downturn earlier this year and an increased willingness of financial market participants to take risky positions," Nyberg began. "Growth in Sweden is also currently high. During the spring, the Government has proposed new tax cuts that increase households' disposable income. This, together with higher wage increases, could contribute to faster consumption growth in the future. Government expenditure increases can also contribute to increased public consumption and production in the economy. Several wage agreements have been reached in recent times and the outcome of these so far looks to be higher than what is consistent with the salary forecast that was laid in February. The improved labour market situation with lower than expected open unemployment also suggests that, overall, there are reasons to adjust the forecast for wage increases in the coming years upwards," Nyberg noted. "Inflation so far this year has become higher than in the February forecast largely due to oil prices rising. In addition to oil prices, some other prices have also risen more than expected, including the prices of fruits and vegetables, which can sometimes fluctuate relatively sharply. House prices continue to increase at a rapid pace although there has been some moderation in the rate of increase. With the higher prices in the real estate market also comes rapid credit growth to households," Nyberg pointed out. "We in the Executive Board concluded in February that the repo rate needs to be raised further in the future in order for inflation to develop in line with the target and for real economic developments to be balanced. At the meeting on 3 May, we all agreed that the path of interest rates needed to be shifted up a bit, but opinions on how quickly this should happen differed marginally. I believed that the developments that have taken place recently justified that we should proceed somewhat more quickly and therefore advocated an increase in the repo rate. The majority of my colleagues did not think so, which is why I chose to reserve my position," Nyberg said. "My position is based on a concern about the development of several important factors, which I touched on above. The outcome of the wage round so far indicates that costs for companies will rise, which in turn risks leading to higher than expected inflation. To this can be added that the development of the labour market remains strong. Even if the balance of the market overall looks reasonable, you cannot ignore the fact that bottlenecks in certain industries may further increase wage costs. Household consumption may also grow more than expected, partly as a result of the tax cuts announced by the government. Finally, the development of property prices and the associated rapid credit expansion is a cause for concern, in Sweden as well as in other countries," Nyberg pointed out. "The major challenges in monetary policy right now are, in my opinion, tied to two issues. The first question is about how quickly the rising demand will have an effect on inflation, which in turn has to do with how long we can expect continued good growth without encountering capacity caps in various industries. In other words, this question is strongly linked to how productivity develops. The second question concerns what effect credit growth can have on inflation in the short term, and here, unfortunately, knowledge is rather small. Although there is great uncertainty on both issues, my assessment is that the risks to both inflation and real economic developments are currently clearly on the upside," Nyberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Nyberg: Utmaningar inom penningpolitiken Datum 2007-05-25 Vice riksbankschef Lars Nyberg talade idag i Stockholm p ett mte anordnat av Nordea. Han diskuterade bland annat det penningpolitiska lget och sitt stllningstagande vid det frra penningpolitiska mtet. Att konjunkturen fr nrvarande r mycket gynnsam kan knappast ha undgtt ngon. Den internationella utvecklingen r mycket stark. I USA kan man visserligen sknja vissa svaghetstecken knutna till bostads- och fordonsmarknaderna, men  andra sidan vxer de europeiska ekonomierna ngot snabbare n vntat. Det mesta tyder p att tillvxten internationellt totalt sett utvecklas i linje med Riksbankens prognoser. Till den positiva bilden kan lggas en frnyad optimism p aktiemarknaderna efter en nedgng tidigare i r och en kad vilja hos aktrerna p de finansiella marknaderna att ta riskfyllda positioner, inledde Nyberg. ven i Sverige r tillvxten fr nrvarande hg. Under vren har regeringen freslagit nya skattesnkningar som kar hushllens disponibla inkomster. Detta kan tillsammans med hgre lnekningar bidra till en snabbare konsumtionstillvxt framver. ven offentliga utgiftskningar kan bidra till kad offentlig konsumtion och produktion i ekonomin. Flera lneavtal har trffats under senare tid och utfallen av dessa ser s hr lngt ut att vara hgre n vad som r frenligt med den lneprognos som lades i februari. Det frbttrade arbetsmarknadslget med en lgre ppen arbetslshet n vntat talar ocks fr att det sammantaget finns skl att justera upp prognosen fr lnekningarna de kommande ren, konstaterade Nyberg. Inflationen hittills i r har blivit hgre n i februariprognosen till stor del beroende p att oljepriserna har stigit. Frutom oljepriserna har ven en del andra priser stigit mer n vntat, bland annat priserna p frukt och grnsaker, som ibland kan fluktuera relativt kraftigt. Huspriserna fortstter att ka i snabb takt ven om en viss dmpning av kningstakten har skett. Med de hgre priserna p fastighetsmarknaden fljer ocks en snabb kredittillvxt till hushllen, ppekade Nyberg. Vi i direktionen konstaterade i februari att reporntan behver hjas ytterligare framver fr att inflationen ska utvecklas i linje med mlet och att den realekonomiska utvecklingen ska bli balanserad. Vid mtet den 3 maj var vi alla verens om att rntebanan behvde skiftas upp en aning, men sikterna om hur snabbt det borde ske skiljde sig marginellt. Jag menade att den utveckling som gt rum under den senaste tiden motiverade att vi borde g ngot snabbare fram och frordade drfr en hjning av reporntan. Det tyckte inte majoriteten av mina kollegor, och drfr valde jag att reservera mig, sade Nyberg. Mitt stllningstagande grundar sig p en oro fr utvecklingen av flera viktiga faktorer, som jag berrt ovan. Utfallen av avtalsrrelsen s hr lngt tyder p att kostnaderna fr fretagen kommer att stiga, vilket i sin tur riskerar att leda till hgre inflation n vntat. Till detta kan lggas att utvecklingen p arbetsmarknaden r fortsatt stark. ven om balansen p marknaden totalt ser rimlig ut, s kan man inte bortse frn att flaskhalsar inom vissa branscher kan komma att ka lnekostnaderna ytterligare. Hushllens konsumtion kan ocks komma att vxa mer n vntat, delvis till fljd av de skattesnkningar som har aviserats av regeringen. Slutligen r utvecklingen av fastighetspriserna och den drtill knutna snabba kreditexpansionen en klla till oro, i Sverige lika vl som i andra lnder, ppekade Nyberg. De stora utmaningarna inom penningpolitiken just nu r enligt min mening knutna till tv frgor. Den frsta frgan handlar om hur snabbt den stigande efterfrgan fr effekter p inflationen, vilket i sin tur har att gra med hur lnge vi kan frvnta en fortsatt god tillvxt utan att stta p kapacitetstak i olika branscher. Den frgan r med andra ord starkt knuten till hur produktiviteten utvecklas. Den andra frgan gller vilken effekt kredittillvxten p lite sikt kan f p inflationen, och hr r kunskaperna dessvrre ganska sm. ven om oskerheten r stor nr det gller bda frgorna s r min bedmning att riskerna fr bde inflationen och den realekonomiska utvecklingen fr nrvarande r tydligt p upptsidan, avslutade Nyberg. Title: Current monetary policy
text: oberg: The current monetary policy Date 2007-04-18 Deputy Governor Svante oberg spoke today in Stockholm at a meeting organized by Barclays Capital. "I would like to start by thanking you for the invitation to come and talk about the current monetary policy. Being able to talk about it today suits me very well because I had a slightly different view of monetary policy than my colleagues in the Riksbank's Executive Board at the last monetary policy meeting on March 29. This is also evident from the minutes that became public on Monday," oberg began. "My assessment is that the policy rate should have been raised by 0.25 percentage points and that the future interest rate path should have been revised in an upward direction. I therefore had reservations about the decision to keep the repo rate unchanged," oberg continued. "There are three reasons I made reservations. The first is that economic development is very strong both internationally and in Sweden. The second is that the development is stronger than we predicted at the monetary policy meeting in February. The third is that the contract negotiations seem to result in higher wage increases than we have anticipated. I will elaborate on these three reasons today," oberg explained. "Thus, the first reason is that economic development is very strong. I am thinking here of developments in a more long-term perspective. In its latest report, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects GDP growth for the world economy of about 5 percent per year during the five years 2004- 2008. It is not common to have such a strong development for several years in a row. The strong international development is also very well spread geographically. The OECD area is growing by in the order of 3 percent per year, while the rest of the world, which accounts for about half of the world's GDP, is growing by in the order of 7 percent per year," oberg said. "Growth in Sweden is also unusually strong, with GDP growth of 4.4 per cent last year and up to four per cent this year and rapidly rising employment. In this strong economic situation, both fiscal and monetary policy are expansionary. Households' real disposable income is projected to increase sharply this year, interest rates remain low and credit expansion is strong," oberg pointed out. "A general experience from the last 10 to 15 years is that real developments do not have the same impact on inflation as before. The short-term so-called Phillips curve is flatter. This is linked to the increased credibility of monetary policy. Inflation expectations are close to the inflation target of 2%, which in turn affects price and wage formation. The variations in inflation around the target are significantly smaller than before. But this does not exclude that the strong real development will still eventually bring with it an increase in inflation that needs to be met with interest rate hikes. In that case, it is most likely that the inflation process will pick up speed as wage costs begin to rise at a faster pace," oberg continued. "The second reason for my reservation is that economic development is stronger than we anticipated at the February monetary policy meeting. National Accounts for the fourth quarter of 2006 was slightly stronger than expected. At the same time, previous quarters were revised down so that the annual average for 2006 was still in line with the forecast," oberg noted. "But if you look at how we have revised our forecasts for a little longer, the direction has been consistently upwards. Since the beginning of last year, we have gradually revised up the forecasts for GDP growth in 2006 from 3.5% to 4.4% and the forecasts for 2007 from 2.8% to 3.5%. The latest information suggests that we need to revise up the forecast further. The Nier Institute's latest forecast for GDP growth in 2007 is 3.9 per cent and the government expects GDP growth of 3.7 per cent in the spring economic bill in 2007," oberg continued. "The NiER's business cycle barometer for February and March showed continued strong development. The industrial economy has continued to improve and the construction economy is record strong. Retail sales continue to increase and demand in the private service industries is rising. The nier institute's new barometer indicator is at a high level. All in all, this means that the economy is developing much stronger than normal," oberg continued. "The labour market has also developed stronger compared to the assessment we made in February. The Labour Force Surveys (LFSs) in January and February showed faster growth in employment and a larger than expected decrease in unemployment. Employment is now rising at an annual rate of about 100,000 people. In the three-month period December to February, the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 per cent and was thus 0.9 percentage points lower than in the corresponding period last year. The number of latent job seekers has also now begun to decline. In addition, other labour market indicators also show a strong development," oberg pointed out. "Despite the strong real momentum, inflation remains low. The consumer price index rose by 1.9 per cent in March this year compared with the same month last year, which is slightly more than we expected in February. Underlying inflation is lower. The UND1X excluding energy inflation rate was just 1.1 percent in March, marginally higher than our forecast. But the important thing is how the increasingly strong economy will affect wage growth and inflation in the slightly longer term," oberg said. "The third reason for my reservation is that, in my opinion, the contract negotiations look set to result in higher wage increases than we have anticipated. Crucial for future inflation and monetary policy is how the strong real development affects wage formation and, in particular, how it can be handled in the spring contract negotiations. From this point of view, the wage round has not started very well. It looks like it will result in higher wage growth rates than we have anticipated. The first three-year agreement in industry is reported to mean a 10.2 percent wage increase and the agreement in the area of trade 12.6 percent in wage growth over a three-year period," oberg said. "In February, we expected hourly wages to increase by 3.9 percent next year when the full-year effect of the agreements concluded this year has taken effect. The National Institute of Economic Research's report, which was published recently, instead expects an hourly wage increase of 4.4 percent, and then they would not have taken into account the agreement in the area of trade. The government also expects higher wage increases than we did in February," oberg noted. "My assessment in the past was that the contract negotiations would result in agreements in a reasonable time, at levels that were consistent with the inflation target and without major conflicts. At the same time, my assessment was that the risks were on the upside, that despite the good experiences of recent years, the contract negotiations could become significantly more difficult and that market forces could also pull up wage growth rates to higher levels," oberg said. "This risk scenario now looks set to materialise. Coordinated three-year agreements with a moderate level of wage growth could have been compatible with low and stable inflation. What now looks set to be the case is instead weaker coordinated three-year agreements with higher wage increases than we have previously anticipated. In addition, there is a continued strong strengthening the labor market that risks resulting in an increased wage slide", oberg pointed out. "At the same time, it cannot be ruled out that there have been structural changes in the economy that contribute to inflationary pressures remaining low. Productivity and import prices could continue to hold down inflation even in the longer term. An important question for future development is therefore to what extent the strong productivity development is cyclical and to what extent it is structural. But that question is difficult to answer before a few years have passed," oberg said. "The uncertainty about future economic developments means that we have to try our hand at monetary policy. My assessment is that upside risks are now stronger than downside risks. In a situation like the current one when strong forces are driving economic development, we should raise the policy rate to a more neutral level. This is important not least to anchor inflation expectations," oberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE berg: Den aktuella penningpolitiken Datum 2007-04-18 Vice riksbankschef Svante berg talade idag i Stockholm p ett mte anordnat av Barclays Capital. Jag vill brja med att tacka fr inbjudan att f komma och tala om den aktuella penningpolitiken. Att f prata om den just idag passar mig mycket bra eftersom jag hade en lite annan syn p penningpolitiken n mina kollegor i Riksbankens direktion vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet den 29 mars. Det framgr ocks av protokollet som blev offentligt i mndags, inledde berg. Min bedmning r att styrrntan borde ha hjts med 0,25 procentenheter och att den framtida rntebanan borde ha reviderats i upptgende riktning. Jag reserverade mig drfr mot beslutet att hlla reporntan ofrndrad, fortsatte berg. Det finns tre skl till att jag reserverade mig. Det frsta r att den ekonomiska utvecklingen r mycket stark bde internationellt och i Sverige. Det andra r att utvecklingen r starkare n vad vi frutsg vid det penningpolitiska mtet i februari. Det tredje r att avtalsfrhandlingarna ser ut att resultera i hgre lnekningar n vi har rknat med. Jag ska idag utveckla dessa tre skl, frklarade berg. Det frsta sklet r sledes att den ekonomiska utvecklingen r mycket stark. Jag tnker d p utvecklingen i ett mer lngsiktigt perspektiv. Internationella valutafonden (IMF) rknar i sin senaste rapport med en BNP-tillvxt fr vrldsekonomin p ca 5 procent per r under de fem ren 2004 - 2008. Det r inte vanligt med en s stark utveckling flera r i rad. Den starka internationella utvecklingen r ocks mycket vl spridd geografiskt. OECD-omrdet vxer med i storleksordningen 3 procent per r medan vriga vrlden, som svarar fr ungefr hlften av vrldens BNP, vxer med i storleksordningen 7 procent per r, sade berg. ven tillvxten i Sverige r ovanligt stark med en BNP-tillvxt p 4,4 procent i fjol och uppemot fyra procent i r och en snabbt stigande sysselsttning. I detta starka konjunkturlge r bde finans- och penningpolitik expansiv. Hushllens reala disponibla inkomster berknas ka kraftigt i r, rntorna r fortfarande lga och kreditexpansionen r stark, ppekade berg. En allmn erfarenhet frn de senaste 10  15 ren r att den reala utvecklingen inte har samma genomslag p inflationen som tidigare. Den kortsiktiga s kallade Phillipskurvan r flackare. Det hnger samman med att penningpolitiken har ftt en kad trovrdighet. Inflationsfrvntningarna ligger nra inflationsmlet 2 procent, vilket i sin tur pverkar pris- och lnebildningen. Variationerna i inflationen omkring mlet r betydligt mindre n tidigare. Men det utesluter inte att den starka reala utvecklingen nd till sist drar med sig en kad inflation som behver mtas med rntehjningar. Det mest troliga r i s fall att inflationsprocessen stter fart genom att lnekostnaderna brjar stiga i en snabbare takt, fortsatte berg. Det andra sklet till min reservation r att den ekonomiska utvecklingen r starkare n vad vi frutsg vid det penningpolitiska mtet i februari. Nationalrkenskaperna fr det fjrde kvartalet 2006 blev ngot starkare n vntat. Samtidigt reviderades tidigare kvartal ned s att rsgenomsnittet fr 2006 nd lg i linje med prognosen, konstaterade berg. Men ser man till hur vi har reviderat vra prognoser under en lite lngre tid har riktningen varit konsekvent uppt. Sedan brjan av frra ret har vi successivt reviderat upp prognoserna fr BNP-tillvxten 2006 frn 3,5 till 4,4 procent och prognoserna fr 2007 frn 2,8 till 3,5 procent. Den senaste informationen tyder p att vi behver revidera upp prognosen ytterligare. Konjunkturinstitutets senaste prognos fr BNP-tillvxten 2007 r 3,9 procent och regeringen rknar i den ekonomiska vrpropositionen med en BNP-tillvxt p 3,7 procent 2007, fortsatte berg. Konjunkturinstitutets konjunkturbarometer fr februari och mars visade p en fortsatt stark utveckling. Industrikonjunkturen har fortsatt att frbttras och byggkonjunkturen r rekordstark. Detaljhandeln fortstter att ka sin frsljning och efterfrgan i de privata tjnstenringarna stiger. Konjunkturinstitutets nya barometerindikator ligger p en hg niv. Sammantaget innebr det att ekonomin utvecklas mycket starkare n normalt., fortsatte berg. ven arbetsmarknaden har utvecklats starkare jmfrt med den bedmning vi gjorde i februari. Arbetskraftsunderskningarna (AKU) i januari och februari visade p en snabbare kning av sysselsttningen och en strre minskning av arbetslsheten n vntat. Sysselsttningen stiger nu med ca 100 000 personer i rstakt. Under tremnadersperioden december till februari sjnk arbetslsheten till 4,9 procent och var drmed 0,9 procentenheter lgre n vid motsvarande period i fjol. ven antalet latent arbetsskande har nu brjat minska. Drtill visar ocks andra arbetsmarknadsindikatorer p en stark utveckling, framhll berg. Trots den starka reala utvecklingen r inflationen fortfarande lg. Konsumentprisindex steg i mars i r med 1,9 procent jmfrt med samma mnad ifjol, vilket r ngot mer n vi rknade med i februari. Den underliggande inflationen r lgre. Inflationstakten enligt UND1X exklusive energi var bara 1,1 procent i mars, marginellt hgre n vr prognos. Men det viktiga r hur den allt starkare konjunkturen kommer att pverka lneutvecklingen och inflationen p lite lngre sikt, sade berg. Det tredje sklet till min reservation r att avtalsfrhandlingarna enligt min mening ser ut att resultera i hgre lnekningar n vad vi har rknat med. Avgrande fr den framtida inflationen och penningpolitiken r hur den starka reala utvecklingen pverkar lnebildningen och srskilt hur den kan hanteras i vrens avtalsfrhandlingar. Avtalsrrelsen har ur den synvinkeln inte brjat srskilt bra. Den ser ut att resultera i hgre lnekningstakter n vi har rknat med. Det frsta trersavtalet inom industrin uppges innebra 10,2 procent i lnekning och avtalet p handelns omrde 12,6 procent i lnekning p tre rs sikt, sade berg. I februari rknade vi med att timlnerna skulle komma att ka med 3,9 procent nsta r nr helrseffekten av de avtal som sluts i r har slagit igenom. I Konjunkturinstitutets rapport, som publicerades nyligen, rknar man istllet med en timlnekning p 4,4 procent och d hade de inte tagit hnsyn till avtalet p handelns omrde. Regeringen rknar ocks med hgre lnekningar n vad vi gjorde i februari, konstaterade berg. Min bedmning var tidigare att avtalsfrhandlingarna skulle komma att resultera i avtal i rimlig tid, p niver som var frenliga med inflationsmlet och utan strre konflikter. Samtidigt var min bedmning att riskerna fanns p uppsidan, att avtalsfrhandlingarna trots de senaste rens goda erfarenheter skulle kunna bli betydligt svrare och att marknadskrafterna ocks skulle kunna dra upp lnekningstakterna till hgre niver, sade berg. Detta riskscenario ser nu ut att infrias. Samordnade treriga avtal med en mttlig niv p lnekningarna hade kunnat vara frenliga med en lg och stabil inflation. Det som nu ser ut att bli fallet r istllet svagare samordnade treriga avtal med hgre lnekningar n vi tidigare har rknat med. Till det kommer en fortsatt kraftig frstrkning av arbetsmarknaden som riskerar att resultera i en kad lneglidning, ppekade berg. "Samtidigt kan det inte uteslutas att det har skett strukturella frndringar i ekonomin som bidrar till att inflationstrycket frblir lgt. Produktiviteten och importpriserna skulle kunna fortstta att hlla nere inflationen ven p lngre sikt. En viktig frga fr utvecklingen framver r drfr i vilken utstrckning den starka produktivitetsutvecklingen r cyklisk och i vilken utstrckning den r strukturell. Men den frgan r svr att svara p innan det gtt ngra r, sade berg. Oskerheten om den framtida ekonomiska utvecklingen gr att vi mste prva oss fram i penningpolitiken. Min bedmning r att upptriskerna nu r starkare n nedtriskerna. I ett lge som det nuvarande nr starka krafter driver p den ekonomiska utvecklingen br vi hja styrrntan till en mer neutral niv. Det r viktigt inte minst fr att frankra inflationsfrvntningarna, avslutade berg. Title: Monetary policy and the state of the Swedish economy
text: oberg: Monetary policy and the state of the Swedish economy Date 2008-05-08 Deputy Governor Svante oberg spoke on Thursday at a seminar organized by TCO. In the speech, oberg presented his view of the economic situation. He saw risks that GDP growth in the US will be weaker than the Riksbank expects in its monetary policy follow-up. Growth is also slowing in Sweden, but the slowdown will not be so sharp. At the same time, there is a risk that inflation will be higher both in the rest of the world and in Sweden. - Economic development in the United States has continued to deteriorate in recent months. This is largely linked to the problems in the financial markets. GDP growth has largely stagnated, employment has started to fall and unemployment has started to rise. The future expectations of American companies and households are very pessimistic. It is hard to believe that a recovery can get underway until a better picture has been created of where the losses in the financial system are and before the fall in house prices has been stopped. There is a risk that the slowdown in the US will be more protracted than we expect in the monetary policy follow-up, oberg began. - Europe has so far fared better than the US. This is partly due to the fact that the origins of the financial crisis are in the United States and that the turbulence in the financial markets has not been as strong in Europe. But in light of the slowdown in the US and the turmoil in the financial markets, it is reasonable to expect a slowdown in Europe as well, oberg said. In emerging and developing countries, on the other hand, GDP growth remains high. The strong growth in the world in recent years has brought with it rising prices for energy, raw materials and food. This has led to rising inflation both in the emerging market economies and in more developed countries. The most likely thing is that inflation will moderate next year. Normally, inflation tends to slow down when growth slows down, even if with some lag. But there is a risk that the inflation process will be more protracted. Overall, therefore, I saw downside risks to global GDP growth, but upside risks to inflation at the last monetary policy meeting," oberg continued. "Growth is also slowing down in Sweden. In the monetary policy follow-up, we expect GDP growth of just over 2 1/2% this year and just under 2% next year. Exports are negatively affected by the weaker development in the rest of the world. Household consumption is being dampened by weaker developments in real disposable income, weaker real wealth growth and subdued expectations for the future, oberg said. "At the same time, there are several factors that suggest that the attenuation will not be so strong. Hard data for the Swedish economy does not yet show a significant slowdown. Furthermore, it should be noted that the current account and government finances are strong, which puts us in a good position to deal with a weaker economy. In addition, the financial sector in Sweden has fared relatively well in the international financial turbulence, which reduces the risk of a severe credit crunch. It The latest economic barometer for April shows that sentiment in the Swedish economy is largely unchanged from the month before and that the situation in the Swedish economy is stronger than normal, oberg continued. " The slowdown in growth means that employment is likely to develop weaker than in recent years. I broadly agree with the picture of economic development in Sweden presented in the monetary policy follow-up, but on this point my assessment differs slightly. I believe in a somewhat more protracted process with a continued increase in employment during the year and a continued tendency towards an increase in the number of hours worked per person employed. The March figures from the Labour Force Surveys (LFSs) were also slightly stronger than forecast in the follow-up, oberg continued. "Wage increases have so far been moderate after the last round of contract negotiations last year. The rate of wage growth was 3.9% in January and February, according to preliminary statistics from the Mediation Institute. However, wage and salary increases may be underestimated due to the fact that not all wage and salary increases have been included in the preliminary statistics, the rapid growth of the number of employed persons and the partial replacement of the sample of enterprises in the wage and salary statistics. It is important to clarify the significance of the latter factor and to produce data on the accuracy of estimates of wage developments, oberg said. "Prior to the 2007 agreement negotiations, I was quite optimistic in the sense that they would essentially be implemented well in advance of the old agreements, that they would be implemented without more extensive conflicts and that they would result in wage increases that were consistent with the Riksbank's inflation target. But as the agreements began to be finalized, optimism waned. The levels of agreed wage increases were significantly higher than in previous contract negotiations. The possibilities of pursuing a relatively expansionary monetary policy with low interest rates and still meeting the inflation target decreased. I therefore advocated a faster increase in the Riksbank's key interest rate last year," oberg continued. "What has happened since last spring is that economic development has become worse than we expected at the time. The turbulence in the financial markets has brought with it a sharp economic slowdown in the United States, which has a dampening effect on economic development in other countries and also in Sweden. This, in turn, may have made companies more cost-conscious and less likely to hire new employees and to raise wages more than under the agreements. Nevertheless, my assessment is that wages may well increase more than foreseen in the follow-up. Capacity utilisation is high and unemployment is low, oberg noted. "Inflation has risen and is now significantly above the Riksbank's target. Inflation as measured by the CPI was 3.4% in March 2008. Inflation expectations are also above the inflation target, both over two and five years. One explanation for the high inflation is our own interest rate hikes. Another explanation is the rise in the price of energy, raw materials and food. A third explanation is the cost trend in Sweden. Wages are projected to grow faster than in recent years and productivity to slow down. This means that unit labour costs are increasing significantly faster than before, oberg said. "The Riksbank's Executive Board decided at the April monetary policy meeting that the repo rate would remain at 4.25%, and we estimated that it is most likely to remain at that level for the rest of the year. I supported both the interest rate decision and the forecast for the repo rate. But my view was that there is a slightly higher probability of an increase in the policy rate during the year than of a cut. The risk is that the inflation process will be more protracted both in the rest of the world and in Sweden, oberg concluded.

Title: The Riksbank and the agreement movement
text: oberg: The Riksbank and the wage round Date 2006-12-18 Deputy Governor Svante oberg spoke today in Vasteras at a meeting organized by LO Vastmanland. "Next year, a large part of the wage agreements in the labor market will be renegotiated. The Riksbank is not a party to the wage movement. The negotiations are the responsibility of the social partners. On the other hand, there are links between wage formation and monetary policy. The Riksbank's task is to ensure that inflation remains at a low and stable level. This is an important prerequisite for wage negotiations and their outcome. At the same time, both the actual and the expected development of wages play a major role in inflation. Everyone concerned is aware that these links are important. This applies to employees and employers as well as the Riksbank," oberg began. "Over the past ten years, things have gone well for Sweden. Growth has been high and inflation low. General government finances have been strong and surpluses in trade with foreign countries large. Employment has increased and unemployment has fallen, although not to such an extent that it corresponds to the ambitions of the state authorities. Despite moderate nominal wage growth, real wages have risen significantly. And thanks to a high rate of productivity growth, firms' labour costs have been held back and competitiveness improved. The contrast with the major economic problems of the 1970s and 80s is striking," oberg continued. "Most indications are that we can look forward to a round of collective bargaining next year that is consistent with continued good economic development. There are three reasons in particular that speak for this," oberg said. "Firstly, the financial conditions for next year's contract negotiations are good. Wages have increased moderately in recent years. Although it is to be expected that the rate of wage growth will rise slightly in the coming years as the labour market situation improves, as we noted in the latest Inflation Report, there is a large amount of spare resources in the labour market. The existence of large labour reserves should hold back wage and price increases. At the same time, the labor market is improving at a rapid pace and there is of course a risk that the wage round will become more problematic and result in higher wage increases than we expected," oberg continued. "Secondly, wage formation has improved since the crisis of the early 1990s. The Rehnberg Commission, the Industrial Agreement and the Mediation Institute are important parts of this change. Over the past ten fifteen years, national agreements have contained wage levels that have been well compatible with low and stable inflation. The contract negotiations have started well in advance of the expiry of the old agreements. The competitive sector has normally made up first and set the mark for other parts of the economy. The contracts have normally been three years. They no longer contain compliance clauses that cause wages and prices to chase each other in an upward spiral. At the same time, wage formation within the national framework has allowed for significant variations between companies and individuals. The number of conflicts in the labor market has been lower than before," oberg continued. "Thirdly, the monetary policy framework has improved and thus the conditions for low and stable inflation. The change began at the end of 1992 with the abandonment of the fixed exchange rate in favour of a floating exchange rate. In January 1993, it was decided that monetary policy would have an inflation target from 1995 onwards. A decision by the Riksdag at the end of the 1990s meant that the price stability objective was laid down in law and that the Riksbank became independent. This has meant new conditions for monetary policy. The Riksbank currently has a high level of credibility in that the public's expectations are set for inflation to end up at the inflation target's two per cent per year," oberg said. "In short, the stability of the Swedish economy has increased. Well-functioning wage formation hand in hand with a well-functioning monetary policy has produced tangible and positive results. The Swedish economy now works much better than in the 1970s and 80s. That's something we should be very concerned about. Although the good development has a good chance of continuing in the coming years, it is not something we can take for granted. My job and that of my colleagues is to steer interest rates so that we reach our goal of low and stable inflation. In this way, we can contribute to the stability of the economy. A stable economy, in turn, increases the chances of good economic development," oberg concluded.

Title: A combination of measures most effective to support the economy
text: Ohlsson hearing in the Finance Committee: A combination of measures most effective in supporting the economy Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson today participated in this year's second hearing on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. There, they commented on, among other things, the measures the Riksbank has put in place to mitigate the economic consequences of the corona pandemic. Date: 2020-10-20 10:00 Speaker: Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson Place: Finance Committee, Swedish Parliament Henry Ohlsson highlighted the effects of the corona pandemic on the economy in his introduction. As a result of the crisis, unemployment has risen rapidly both in Sweden and in the rest of the world. "Now we are seeing rapid improvements in economic activity. But if history gives us guidance, the improvements in the labor market will take longer," Ohlsson said. "There are therefore now good opportunities to increase labour productivity through training and other skills-enhancing measures. Such efforts would have long-term positive effects on both employment and inflation," Ohlsson said. text: Ohlsson: No obvious decision Date: 2016-02-18 Speaker: Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson Location: Nordea, Malmo On Thursday, Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson will visit Malmo where he talks about the Riksbank's latest interest rate cut, which took place in light of the fact that inflation is expected to be lower in 2016 compared to the previous forecast. At Nordea's lunch meeting in Malmo, Ohlsson notes that the Swedish economy is now strong and that inflation and inflation expectations are rising. At the same time, there is great uncertainty about the outside world. "The inflation target is important at the same time as inflation and inflation expectations have long been below target," says Ohlsson. In connection with the monetary policy reports, the members of the Executive Board carry out visits to various locations in Sweden and abroad to present the conclusions of the monetary policy decisions. The members then give lectures and, depending on the occasion, they meet financial market participants, the business community, municipal representatives, the media and / or representatives of higher education institutions at the relevant location.

Title: Towards the goal in an orderly manner
text: Ohlsson: Towards the goal in an orderly manner Date: 2015-10-12 Speaker: Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson Location: Mediation Institute, Stockholm "The division of labour is clear, the Riksbank is responsible for monetary policy and the social partners determine wages." This is emphasized by Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson when he speaks today at the Mediation Institute's seminar on the socio-economic conditions for wage formation. The inflation target is an important benchmark in price and wage formation and, since its introduction, has contributed to more stable wage developments and greater purchasing power for wage earners. "It is important to safeguard this cornerstone of economic policy," says Ohlsson. "That's why we're pursuing such an expansionary monetary policy." And the policy has an effect. The low interest rate environment is an important explanation for the fact that the Swedish economy is developing well and that there is a clear upward trend in inflation since last year. "It is important that inflation continues to rise towards our target. But it must be done in an orderly manner, so that production and employment are not threatened. What we can do is give credibility to the inflation target, so that it can serve as a starting point for the negotiations," concludes Ohlsson. Title: Monetary policy and wage formation
text: Ohlsson: Monetary policy and wage formation The division of labour is clear, the Riksbank is responsible for monetary policy and the social partners determine wages, said Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson when he spoke today at the Mediation Institute's seminar "Socio-economic conditions for wage formation" in Stockholm. Date: 2017-10-16 09:00 Speaker: Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson Location: 2017-10-16 09:00 Ohlsson described the Riksbank's work to ensure the role of its inflation target as an anchor for price and wage formation. "After a long period of below-target inflation, inflation has come up and we have a strong economy in Sweden. Monetary policy has contributed to this development," says Ohlsson. However, he stressed the need for an expansionary monetary policy in order for inflation to remain close to 2 percent in the future. The Riksbank recently decided to make CPIF a formal target variable for monetary policy and to use a variation band for the outcomes of CPIF inflation. The band should remind that inflation cannot be exactly 2 every single month. However, Ohlsson emphasizes: "I want it to be crystal clear to the social partners that it is 2 percent inflation that is the goal of monetary policy. The Riksbank will always aim there, regardless of whether inflation is inside or outside the band." Title: Monetary policy
text: Monetary policy Date: 1996-10-09 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars Heikensten Location: SNS Business Cycle Day Let me begin by thanking you for being able to come here and talk about monetary policy. My intention today is to dwell mainly on two themes. First, I will talk about monetary policy over the last year. What has happened since we last saw each other here and why? Next, I intend to look to the future. What does the Riksbank expect from the coming year and how might it affect monetary policy? Before I go into this, however, I will say a few words about how I see the need for transparency and clarity in monetary policy. The ambition to be open and clear should be a fundamentally reasonable starting point for every central bank. It's hard to see factual motives for mystery and smokescreens. Transparency is particularly important when the power and independence of central banks increase. It is all the more important, then, that citizens should be able to understand how the Central Bank works and that they should be able to evaluate their actions and demand accountability. In Sweden, such an attitude is especially important for several reasons. Our democratic traditions - and the transparency of the state apparatus in general - make it difficult to apply any other approach. We are also only at the beginning of building understanding and support for the Riksbank's goals and actions and, as I see it, our openness is important in this process. Transparency and clarity are also natural prerequisites for the smooth functioning of a market-conforming monetary policy. If market participants do not understand the Riksbank's actions or if they feel deceived by the measures we are taking, monetary policy will be less effective. In addition, the need for clarity in action is particularly great when a new monetary policy regime is to be established. The monetary policy debate is easily characterised by the sometimes short-term views of market participants. In the market, it is important whether the interest rate is lowered one week and not the next or whether it is reduced by 10 basis points or 20. But this is not so important from a larger socio-economic perspective. Perhaps it is possible, with clear action, to shift the debate in the direction of the larger monetary policy issues - at least that is our hope. Monetary policy is being reoriented So it's time to get into what's happened over the past year. There is no doubt that the conditions for monetary policy have changed significantly. By this time last year, the krona had strengthened from its low in TCW terms at index 136.50 on April 24, 1995 to about 124. (Figure 1.) At the same time, the expected inflation had been due to two years' time, according to, for example, the United States. Aragon's measurements came down from levels around 4 percent in the winter of 1995 to around 3 percent for most groups. Inflation in the current twelve-month figure was 2.7 per cent. In the latter part of 1995, this pattern was reinforced. The crown first rose further and then dropped back, but on the whole kept the new levels. In parallel, inflation expectations gradually crept down. (Figure 2.) We were approaching the point where it should be possible to turn monetary policy in a more expansionary direction and lower the repo rate. However, we did not yet calculate that inflation could be lower than two per cent and thus there was no reason to change policy. The debate on monetary policy was intense around Christmas 1995. Most observers then believed that we should lower interest rates. This applied to several of our more frequent economic policy debaters, but also to foreign brokerage houses, etc. At this time, we made a compilation of different actors' inflation forecasts, which I have previously shown in some for a. (Table 1) It follows that none of the more established assessors of the Swedish economy expected that we would meet the target in 1996. In the Riksbank, there was a gradual reassessment of developments in late autumn 1995. The inflation forecast in our main scenario was revised down. At the same time, the likelihood of an alternative with weaker economic development and with this subsequent lower inflation increased. The latter, too, was something we had reason to weave into our decision. Normally, monetary policy decisions are not based on a single point estimate of future inflation. We work with several options and our decisions are based on an assessment of the probability of the different options. In this perspective, we judged in January that it was time to start lowering interest rates. In this context, it may be worth recalling that As recently as the beginning of February, Urban Backstrom was criticized by the Economic Association - by our own adviser on academic issues Lars Svensson, by Assar Lindbeck and by Anders Vredin - for the Riksbank not sticking to the rules of the game but lowering before, in their opinion, the forecast for inflation came down to 2 percent. The situation we faced at the beginning of this year can perhaps be described as going out into uncharted waters. The direction of travel must then be clear. At the same time, there were reasons to avoid drastic maneuvers that could disrupt the picture. We would like to see a continued decline in long-term interest rates and some further strengthening of the exchange rate. The market should then ideally feel at home in the new waters and share our view of the economy and inflation. It is easy to forget today that the situation in January 1996 was anything but stable. An example of the concern was the market reaction to the so-called Persson plan. The krona fell and long-term interest rates rose. Many market commentators then questioned whether the Riksbank could proceed with cuts. We chose to do that. Decisive for the action was the fundamental inflation picture. Moreover, our confidence in budgetary developments was obviously greater than that of the market. Surely a central bank must "listen" to the market. But it is still primarily important to have a clear picture and stand for it. Inflation picture better than expected The policy during the spring and summer has been successful in that the repo rate has been able to be reduced by almost four percent without weakening the krona or negatively affecting long-term interest rates. In fact, the opposite has been true; the krona is stronger than in January and long-term interest rates are significantly lower. Even more evident is the strong long-term interest rate development measured as a difference with German long-term interest rates. (Figure 3) Behind this development are many different factors. The international environment has been good. A large part of the past year has been characterized by increased belief that EMU will take place, which has benefited interest rate developments in Europe's high interest rate countries. The fact that monetary policy has remained expansionary in both Europe and Japan, while there has been no increase in the key interest rate in the US, is also part of the picture. At least as important, however, is what has happened in Sweden. The budget trend has been significantly better than most people expected a year ago. The same applies to the inflation picture. Our relative position in Europe today is in these respects significantly better than it was one year ago. since. In addition, the policy follows established plans (convergence programmes, etc.). The tactic we chose was to initially advance in relatively large steps (25 points initially) at reasonably regular intervals. The influx of new positive information on inflationary pressures led us to gradually revise our view of how far down the repo rate could go. The new information could possibly have justified reductions in larger increments, but we refrained from that; we didn't want to risk the market committing bigger rate cuts than we were sure to be able to implement ourselves. The sequence of roughly equal reductions thus came to be relatively long. If we had had the picture of the day completely clear to us from the beginning, it might have been natural to make a couple of major cuts in the spring. At the same time, it should be stressed that we are not then - nor now - bound by any particular pattern. The tactic is always subordinate to our quest to achieve the inflation target and new information about inflationary pressures in the economy can always justify a rethinking of the chosen tactic. On the whole, our action seems to have been comprehensible. During the spring and summer, the market has changed its picture of how much interest rates could be reduced at about the same rate as we ourselves have done. A picture of how the reduction potential has shifted can be obtained by combining the development of the repo rate during the period with the expectations of the overnight interest rate at different times. This shows, for example, that the market at the end of March expected that the repo rate could be reduced to just over 6 percent. There somewhere we were also at that time. (Figure 4) Another way to describe the development is to compare the actual development of the repo rate during the period with the overnight rate expected by the market three months earlier. (Figure 5) On this time horizon, pricing has well come to reflect the actual outcome. If anything, over the past six months, the repo rate has been lowered faster than expectations were set. It is also noteworthy that the market seems to have predicted relatively well the timing of the policy change. The picture will be different if the repo rate is related to the assessment the market made of the overnight interest rate a whole year earlier. (Figure 6) Then the deviation is significantly greater. The repo rate has thus been able to be taken down more than the market expected a year earlier. Reasonably, this is essentially due to an influx of new information. Gradually, during the winter and spring, the image of Sweden as a country seriously focused on low inflation and orderly government finances was consolidated. All in all, we can thus state that over the past year there has been a radical reassessment of the Swedish economy in a more positive direction, a shock of confidence if you like. Just like previous shocks in the opposite direction, this has significantly changed the conditions for monetary policy, mainly through the sharp strengthening of the krona that has followed. Among other things, it is this that is behind the reports in recent months of inflation developments that would be below the lower bound. It is my guess - and hope - that such dramatic fluctuations in the crown's rate will prove rare in the future. Weak inflationary pressures With this, I am ready to go ahead and say something about how we view inflation conditions going forward. I will largely start from the inflation report published about three weeks ago. When assessing future inflation, we focus primarily on two factors; the relationship between demand and supply conditions in the economy (the output gap in the broad sense) and inflation expectations. In most simple economic models for the determination of inflation, it is precisely these factors that are highlighted. In addition, the exchange rate is worth mentioning, among other things, because it has a direct influence on inflation via import prices and on demand in the economy. It is also an indicator of inflation expectations. Unfortunately, the world is not so simple that there are unambiguous measures of the output gap and expected inflation, which can only be "plugged into" an equation and give us inflation in a year or two. On the contrary, the overall knowledge of how the relationship between the output gap and inflation expectations on the one hand and actual inflation on the other is incomplete. This is not least due to the fact that the Swedish economy has undergone extensive structural changes in recent times. We are also working on a new monetary policy regime, with a variable exchange rate, which makes it extra difficult to have faith in historical patterns. The output gap as a unifying concept of demand and supply conditions is important in our analyses. If demand tends to exceed supply in the economy, the output gap is positive. Then the risk of accelerating inflation is great. The opposite is true when supply is greater than demand. Normally, there are therefore reasons to tighten monetary policy if the output gap is positive and to shift it in a more expansionary direction when the gap is negative. This is provided that inflation expectations do not show a different picture, because then the situation can be significantly more complicated. The Riksbank has long worked to develop measures of the output gap in the economy as a whole. The results have varied greatly with the method chosen. In the latest Inflation Report, we present three different estimates. They show that the gap today varies between 0.5 and 2.5 percent of GDP. (Figure 7) All in all, this suggests that inflationary pressures today should be low. The uncertainty that characterizes estimates of output gaps at national level makes it almost self-evident to work with a wide range of indicators of demand and supply conditions. One possibility to approach the issue of capacity utilization in the economy is to study more disaggregated information. As a result of the two-fold division that has characterized the Swedish economy, the picture has in recent years been significantly divided. (Figure 8) This is also true today, albeit not quite as significantly. However, even this information suggests that the output gap in a broad sense is not the end. As a result, inflationary pressures should be weak. Wage increases worrying The question of the wide size of the output gap and of inflationary pressures becomes substantially more complicated when wage developments are brought into the picture. Over the past year, wages in the economy have increased by about 6 percent, according to Statistics Sweden. These are numbers that have been questioned. However, we estimate that the rate of wage growth for the economy as a whole is hardly lower than five percent, after we have made adjustments for structural factors (layoffs of lower paid e.g.), varying contract lengths, etc. In the longer term, this is not an acceptable rate of wage growth, as developed, among other things, by the so-called 'Wage And Salary Increase'. Edin Group, with representatives of the social partners. A pessimistic interpretation is that the rate of wage growth even when new agreements are concluded may be too high. Wage growth has been high across the economy, not only in sectors where demand and profit levels were driven up when the agreements were concluded in 1995 (trade is the best-known example). Wage increases are also a consequence of wage slippage, which has continued despite a slump in the economy. There is a close correlation between the so-called equilibrium unemployment rate (the level of unemployment at which inflation starts to rise) and the concept of the output gap. If the rate of wage growth is not slowed, it means that the equilibrium unemployment rate is substantially higher than most academic studies have shown so far, which would also suggest a smaller output gap. However, there are good arguments for a more optimistic assessment. Wage agreements were concluded at a time when inflation expectations were still high in the labour market, capacity utilisation was increasing rapidly in industry and profit levels were extreme. Inflation expectations for the next few years averaged around 3.5-4 percent among labor market organizations, compared with about 2 percent in September this year. (Table 2) International experience also appears - although not entirely unambiguous - to show that it takes a few years for wage formation to adapt to an economy with low inflation. Against this background, we assume that a decline in the rate of wage growth will gradually occur as the current agreements expire. The process may be lengthy and costly in terms of unemployment, but it will happen. If, on the other hand, it goes faster, the result will be better employment growth. In this context, let me point out an important difference compared to the latter part of the 80s, which also illustrates well the interaction between monetary and fiscal policy. This year, real wages are increasing more than expected, driven by high nominal wage increases and low inflation. However, the effect of the real wage increase on demand will be less than in the 80s. A major reason for this is the tight fiscal policy. (This year, for example, real wages will increase by around 4-5 percent, while disposable income will grow by only about 1 percent.) Thus, tight fiscal policy is not only necessary in the longer term, in order to secure a lower debt-to-GDP ratio, it also contributes greatly to reducing inflationary pressures from wages. This increases the Riksbank's monetary policy room for manoeuvre. There is no direct coordination of monetary and fiscal policy, but in practice inflation targeting is taken into account when monetary policy is determined. Conclusions for monetary policy When the Riksbank weighed up the various arguments in the Inflation Report, the conclusion was that there was an output gap in the economy. Overall, economic growth in 1996-1997 was estimated at 3-4%, with the centre of gravity at the upper end of the range. The new information added in recent weeks fits well with this picture. If anything, the new data suggests a marginal upward revision of growth. At the same time, we estimate that the potential growth in the economy is just over 2 percent. Against this background, we do not believe in any major inflationary pressures over the next two years, even if demand pressures turn out to be slightly higher than in the main scenario of the Inflation Report. Moreover, as inflation expectations have come down to par with the Riksbank's target, the report concluded that inflation in 1996 would be around one per cent and in 1997 and also in the first half of 1998 in line with the 2 per cent target. Inflation may develop more favourably than in the main scenario of the Inflation Report. This mainly indicates the low inflation expectations and that the propensity for inflation may have fallen. A larger than projected output gap means that inflation in 1997 and beyond will be lower. On the other hand, stronger developments in private consumption may drive up the pass-through of rising wage costs at the consumer price level. In the longer term, wage formation that has not adapted to the new conditions poses a threat to the reconciliation of price stability with a high level of employment. The next "round of agreements" is important for the future organisation of monetary policy. Already at the turn of the year, the contracts expire for the financial sector and the pulp and paper industry. Our assessment from mid-September - which stands today - was that the available information suggested some remaining room to lower the repo rate. However, it is not always to be expected that monetary policy will follow a certain pattern going forward. Crucial for further development is incoming information and how it relates to the analysis in the Riksbank's latest inflation report. Vi arbetar med flera alternativ och vra beslut utgr frn en bedmning av sannolikheten fr de olika alternativen. I detta perspektiv bedmde vi i januari att det var dags att brja snka rntan. Det kan i detta sammanhang vara vrt att pminna om att Urban Bckstrm s sent som i brjan av februari fick kritik p nationalekonomiska freningen - av vr egen rdgivare i akademiska frgor Lars Svensson, av Assar Lindbeck och av Anders Vredin - fr att Riksbanken inte hllit sig till spelreglerna utan snkt innan enligt deras uppfattning prognosen fr inflationen kommit ner till 2 procent. Den situation vi stod infr i brjan av detta r kan kanske beskrivas som att vi skulle ut p oknda vatten. Frdriktningen mste d vara tydlig. Samtidigt fanns det skl att undvika drastiska manvrar som kunde stra bilden. Vi ville grna se en fortsatt nedgng i de lnga rntorna och en viss ytterligare frstrkning av vxelkursen. Marknaden borde d helst knna sig hemma i de nya vattnen och dela vr syn p ekonomin och inflationen. Det r ltt att idag glmma att situationen i januari 1996 var allt annat n stabil. Ett exempel p oron var marknadsreaktionerna p den s.k. Perssonplanen. Kronan fll och de lnga rntorna steg. Mnga marknadskommentatorer ifrgasatte d om Riksbanken skulle kunna g vidare med snkningar. Det valde vi att gra. Avgrande fr agerandet var den grundlggande inflationsbilden. Vr tilltro till budgetutvecklingen var dessutom uppenbarligen strre n marknadens. Visst mste en centralbank "lyssna" p marknaden. Men det gller nd i frsta hand att sjlv ha en tydlig bild och st fr den. Inflationsbilden bttre n vntat Politiken under vren och sommaren har varit framgngsrik p s vis att reporntan har kunnat tas ner med nstan fyra procent utan att kronan frsvagats eller att de lnga rntorna pverkats negativt. I sjlva verket har ju motsatsen gllt; kronan r starkare n i januari och de lnga rntorna vsentligt lgre. n tydligare r den starka lngrnteutvecklingen mtt som differens mot de tyska lnga rntorna. (Diagram 3) Bakom denna utveckling ligger mnga olika faktorer. Den internationella miljn har varit god. En stor del av det senaste ret har prglats av en kad tro p att EMU blir av, vilket gynnat rnteutvecklingen i Europas hgrntelnder. Det faktum att penningpolitiken varit fortsatt expansiv i svl Europa som Japan samtidigt som ngon hjning av styrrntan inte skett i USA r ocks en del av bilden. Minst lika viktigt r dock vad som hnt i Sverige. Budgetutvecklingen har blivit vsentligt bttre n de flesta rknade med fr ett r sedan. Detsamma gller inflationsbilden. Vr relativa position i Europa r i dag i dessa avseenden betydligt bttre n fr ett r sedan. Dessutom fljer politiken fastlagda planer (konvergensprogram etc.). Den taktik vi valde var att frn brjan g fram i relativt stora steg (25 punkter inledningsvis) med ngorlunda jmna mellanrum. Infldet av ny positiv information om inflationstrycket gjorde att vi gradvis reviderade vr uppfattning om hur lngt ner reporntan skulle kunna komma. Den nya informationen skulle mjligen kunna ha motiverat snkningar i strre steg, men det avhll vi oss ifrn; vi ville inte riskera att marknaden intecknade strre rntesnkningar n vi sjlva var skra p att kunna genomfra. Sekvensen av i stort sett lika stora snkningar kom drmed att bli relativt lng. Om vi haft dagens bild helt klar fr oss frn brjan hade det kanske varit naturligt att gra ett par strre snkningar under vren. Samtidigt finns det skl att betona att vi inte d - och inte heller nu - r bundna av ngot srskilt mnster. Taktiken r alltid underordnad vr strvan att uppn inflationsmlet och ny information om inflationstrycket i ekonomin kan alltid motivera en omprvning av den valda taktiken. Vrt agerande frefaller p det hela taget ha varit begripligt. Marknaden har under vren och sommaren frndrat sin bild av hur mycket rntan skulle kunna tnkas snkas i ungefr samma takt som vi sjlva gjort. En bild av hur snkningspotentialen frflyttats kan man f genom att sammanfra reporntans utveckling under perioden med frvntningarna om dagslnerntan vid olika tillfllen. D framgr t.ex. att marknaden i slutet av mars rknande med att reporntan skulle kunna snkas till drygt 6 procent. Dr ngonstans befann vi oss ocks vid den tiden. (Diagram 4) Ett annat stt att beskriva utvecklingen r att jmfra den faktiska utvecklingen av reporntan under perioden med den dagslnernta som frvntades av marknaden tre mnader tidigare. (Diagram 5) P denna tidshorisont har prissttningen vl kommit att spegla det faktiska utfallet. Om ngot har reporntan under det senaste halvret snkts snabbare n frvntningarna var instllda p. Det r ocks anmrkningsvrt att marknaden relativt vl frefaller ha frutsett tidpunkten fr omlggningen av politiken. Annorlunda blir bilden om reporntan relateras till den bedmning marknaden gjorde av dagslnerntan ett helt r tidigare.(Diagram 6) D r avvikelsen betydligt strre. Reporntan har allts kunnat tas ner mer n marknaden rknat med ett r tidigare. Rimligen beror detta i allt vsentligt p ett inflde av ny information. Gradvis under vintern och vren befstes bilden av Sverige som ett land serist inriktat p lg inflation och ordnade statsfinanser. Sammantaget kan vi allts konstatera att det under det senaste ret skett en radikal omvrdering av svensk ekonomi i mer positiv riktning, en frtroendechock om ni s vill. Precis som tidigare chocker i motsatt riktning har denna ptagligt frndrat villkoren fr penningpolitiken frmst genom den kraftiga kronfrstrkning som fljt. Det r bl.a. denna som ligger bakom de senaste mnadernas rapporter om en inflationsutveckling som skulle ligga under den nedre bandgrnsen. Det r min gissning - och frhoppning - att s dramatiska fluktuationer i kronans kurs ska visa sig sllsynta i framtiden. Svagt inflationstryck Med detta r jag frdig att g vidare och sga ngot om hur vi ser p inflationsfrutsttningarna framver. Jag kommer i stor utstrckning att utg frn den inflationsrapport som publicerades fr ca tre veckor sedan. Nr vi bedmer den framtida inflationen fokuserar vi framfrallt p tv faktorer; relationen mellan efterfrge- och utbudsfrhllandena i ekonomin (produktionsgapet i vid mening) och inflationsfrvntningarna. I de flesta enkla nationalekonomiska modeller fr inflationens bestmning r det just dessa faktorer som lyfts fram. Vxelkursen r drutver vrd att nmna bl.a. drfr att den har ett direkt inflytande p inflationen via importpriserna och p efter-frgan i ekonomin. Den r ocks en indikator p inflationsfrvntningarna. Tyvrr r vrlden inte s enkel att det finns entydiga mtt p produktionsgapet och den vntade inflationen, som bara kan "pluggas in" i en ekvation och ge oss inflationen om ett r eller tv. Tvrtom, r det s att den samlade kunskapen om hur sambanden mellan produktionsgapet och inflationsfrvntningarna  den ena sidan och den faktiska inflationen  den andra sidan r ofullstndig. Detta beror inte minst p att den svenska ekonomin genomgtt omfattande strukturella frndringar p senare tid. Vi arbetar ocks med en ny penningpolitisk regim, med rrlig vxelkurs, som gr det extra svrt att hysa tilltro till historiska mnster. Produktionsgapet som ett samlande begrepp fr efterfrge - och utbudfrhllandena r viktigt i vra analyser. Om efterfrgan tenderar att verstiga utbudet i ekonomin r produktionsgapet positivt. D r risken fr accelererande inflation stor. Motsatsen gller nr utbudet r strre n efterfrgan. Normalt finns det drmed skl att strama t penningpolitiken om produktionsgapet r positivt och att lgga om den i mer expansiv riktning nr gapet r negativt. Detta under frutsttning att inflationsfrvntningarna inte visar p en annan bild, fr d kan situationen vara betydligt mer komplicerad. Riksbanken har lnge arbetat med att ta fram mtt p produktionsgapet i ekonomin som helhet. Resultaten har varierat starkt med den metod som valts. I den senaste inflationsrapporten redovisar vi tre olika skattningar. De visar att gapet idag varierar mellan 0,5 och 2,5 procent av BNP. (Diagram 7) Sammantaget antyder detta att inflationstrycket idag borde vara lgt. Den oskerhet som prglar skattningar av produktionsgap p nationell niv gr att det r nrmast sjlvklart att arbeta med ett brett spektrum av indikatorer p efterfrge - och utbudsfrhllandena. En mjlighet att nrma sig frgan om kapacitetsutnyttjandet i ekonomin r att studera mer disaggregerad information. Till fljd av den tudelning som prglat svensk ekonomi har bilden under senare r varit ptagligt splittrad. (Diagram 8) Detta gller ocks idag, om n inte fullt lika markant. ven denna information tyder dock p att produktionsgapet i vid mening inte r slutet. Drmed borde inflationstrycket vara svagt. Lnekningarna oroande Frgan om produktionsgapets i vid mening storlek och om inflationstrycket blir vsentligt mer komplicerad nr lneutvecklingen frs in i bilden. Under det senaste ret har lnerna i ekonomin enligt SCB kat med ca 6 procent. Det hr r siffror som ifrgasatts. Vi bedmer dock att lnekningstakten fr ekonomin som helhet knappast r lgre n fem procent, sedan vi gjort justeringar fr strukturella faktorer (uppsgningar av lgre betalda t.ex.), varierande avtalslngder etc. P lngre sikt r detta inte en godtagbar lnekningstakt, ngot som bl.a. utvecklats av den s.k. Edingruppen, med representanteter fr arbetsmarknadens parter. En pessimistisk tolkning r att lnekningstakten ocks nr nya avtal sluts kan bli fr hg. Lnekningarna har varit hga i hela ekonomin, inte bara i sektorer dr efterfrgan och vinstniver var uppdrivna nr avtalen slts 1995 (handeln r det mest knda exemplet). Lnekningarna r ocks en fljd av lneglid-ning, som fortsatt trots en svacka i konjunkturen. Mellan den s.k. jmviktsarbetslsheten (den arbetslshetsniv vid vilken inflationen brjar stiga) och produktionsgapsbegreppet freligger ett nra samband. Om lnekningstakten inte dmpas innebr det att jmviktsarbetslsheten r vsentligt hgre n de flesta akademiska studier hittills visat, vilket ocks skulle tala fr ett mindre produktionsgap. Det finns dock goda argument fr en mer optimistisk bedmning. Lneavtalen slts i ett lge nr inflationsfrvntningarna nnu var hga p arbetsmarknaden, kapacitetsutnyttjandet kade snabbt inom industrin och vinstniverna var extrema. Inflationsfrvntningarna fr de nrmaste ren lg i genomsnitt kring 3,5- 4 procent hos arbetsmarknadens organisationer jmfrt med ca 2 procent i september i r. (Tabell 2) Internationella erfarenheter synes ocks - ven om de inte r helt entydiga - visa att det tar ngra r innan lnebildningen har anpassat sig till en ekonomi med lg inflation. Mot den hr bakgrunden utgr vi ifrn att en nedgng i lnekningstakten gradvis kommer till stnd nr nuvarande avtal lper ut. Processen kan bli lngdragen och kostsam i termer av arbetslshet, men den kommer att ske. Om den  andra sidan gr snabbare blir resultatet en bttre sysselsttningstillvxt. Lt mig i detta sammanhang pongtera en viktig skillnad jmfrt med senare delen av 80-talet som dessutom vl skdliggr samspelet mellan penning - och finanspolitiken. Innevarande r kar reallnerna mer n vntat, till fljd av hga nominella lnelyft och lg inflation. Effekten av reallnelyften p efterfrgan blir dock mindre n under 80-talet. En viktig orsak till detta r den strama finanspolitiken. (Innevarande r kar reallnerna exempelvis med runt 4-5 procent samtidigt som de disponibla inkomsterna vxer med bara ca. 1 procent.) Den strama finanspolitiken r allts inte bara ndvndig i ett lngre perspektiv, fr att skra en lgre skuldkvot, den bidrar ocks i hgsta grad till att minska inflationstrycket frn lnerna. Drmed kar Riksbankens penningpolitiska manverutrymme. Ngon direkt koordinering av penning - och finanspolitiken frekommer inte, men med inflationsmlsstyrning tas i praktiken hnsyn till finanspolitiken nr penningpolitiken lggs fast. Slutsatser fr penningpolitiken Nr Riksbanken i inflationsrapporten vgde ihop de olika argumenten blev slutsatsen att det fanns ett produktionsgap i ekonomin. Den ekonomiska tillvxten berknades under 1996-1997 sammantaget uppg till 3-4 procent, med tyngdpunkten i den vre delen av intervallet. Den nya information som tillkommit under de senaste veckorna stmmer vl med denna bild. Om ngot talar den nya informationen fr en marginell upprevidering av tillvxten. Samtidigt bedmer vi att den potentiella tillvxten i ekonomin r lite drygt 2 procent. Mot denna bakgrund tror vi inte p ngot strre inflationstryck under de nrmaste tv ren, ven om efterfrgetrycket skulle visa sig bli ngot hgre n i inflationsrapportens huvudscenario. Eftersom inflationsfrvntningarna dessutom kommit ner i niv med Riksbankens ml blev slutsatsen i rapporten att inflationen under 1996 skulle bli runt en procent samt under 1997 och ven under frsta hlften av 1998 i linje med mlet p 2 procent. Inflationen kan utvecklas gynnsammare n i inflationsrapportens huvudscena-rio. Fr detta talar frmst de lga inflationsfrvntningarna och att inflationsbengenheten kan ha fallit. Ett strre produktionsgap n berknat innebr att inflationen 1997 och drefter blir lgre.  andra sidan kan en starkare utveckling av den privata konsumtionen driva upp genomslaget frn de stigande lnekostnaderna i konsumentprisledet. I ett lngre perspektiv utgr en lnebildning som inte anpassats till de nya frutsttningarna ett hot mot mjligheterna att frena prisstabilitet med hg sysselsttning. Nsta "avtalsrunda" r viktig fr penningpolitikens framtida upplggning. Redan vid rsskiftet lper avtalen ut fr finanssektorn och massa- och pappersindustrin. Vr bedmning frn mitten av september - som str sig idag - var att den tillgngliga informationen talade fr ett visst terstende utrymme att snka reporntan. Dremot kan man inte alltid frvnta sig att penningpolitiken framver kommer att flja ett visst mnster. Avgrande fr den fortsatta utvecklingen r inkommande information och hur den frhller sig till analysen i Riksbankens senaste inflationsrapport.
