Title: The Riksbank's role in an electronic payment system
text: The riksbank's role in an electronic payment system Date: 1996-08-28 Speaker: Deputy Governor Stefan Ingves Location: IIR's conference Credit card, 28-29 August 1996 Berns Congress Introduction First of all, let me clarify the concept of the heading somewhat. The Riksbank has long been involved in electronic payments by operating the RIX system for clearing and settlement large payments. This system has a turnover of "electronic" payments worth approximately SEK 300 billion per day. During a working week, this means that amounts equivalent to Sweden's GDP pass the Riksbank's computers in terms of value. What the title refers to is the payment system that we usually associate with the everyday purchases of newspapers, parking services, public transport, etc. That is, small payments. Experience shows that the small everyday cash payments account for about 10% of the traded value, while the volume of these small payments accounts for about 90% of the number of daily completed transactions. Small value transactions cost money Traditionally, these small payments have been made using banknotes and coins provided by the Riksbank. Of the outstanding volume of banknotes in December 1995, smaller denominations (up to SEK 100) accounted for only about 18% of the total value of the banknote stock in circulation. If we also count the banknotes of SEK 500, this corresponds to about 50% of the banknote stock in circulation, which means that about 50% of the value of the banknote stock in circulation was represented by SEK 1000 banknotes, which are unlikely to be used for the smaller transactions to any great extent. The development that is now underway is thus aimed at eventually replacing primarily the need for small denominations of banknotes and coins (up to SEK 500). For banks as well as for outlets of various kinds, the handling of banknotes and coins as a result of small-value transactions is rather costly. Against this background, it is not surprising that new technologies are being developed aimed at reducing the management costs of small value transactions. In a broader sense, it is desirable that more and more transactions take place by electronic means, as this means that today's expensive paper-based handling can be further reduced. In Sweden, this development is still somewhat sluggish compared to many other industrialized countries. Demand for banknotes and coins To get an idea of the importance of banknotes and coins in the Swedish economy, I have calculated the banknote stock's share of GDP for the years 1950 to 1995 As can be seen from the following picture, the value of the banknotes and coins in circulation relative to the value of GDP has more than halved over the period under consideration. The explanation for this is, among other things, that more and more transactions take place in the form of electronic money transfers. An important event that contributed to this development was the transition from cash-paid salaries to wages deposited in salary accounts in a bank or postal giro. One should be wary of trends, but if the trend of this development continues, the use of banknotes will completely cease in 20 years...! From the Riksbank's point of view, this development is something that we have to live with and that we cannot oppose. At the outset, I mentioned that the Riksbank is already heavily involved in large-value transactions, which are not very numerous, but all the more significant, as a basis for the monetary policy it conducts. From this point of view, a possible loss of demand for lower denominations of banknotes and coins is of minor importance. The main tasks of the Riksbank The riksbank's main tasks are, firstly, to conduct monetary policy and, secondly, to promote a safe and efficient payment system. As is well known, the objective of monetary policy is that the value of the Swedish krona must not be eroded by domestic inflation. The goal is more concretely set at a price change rate per year of 2% with a tolerance of - 1%. Supplying the Swedish economy with banknotes and coins of sufficient size is another important task, but this does not mean that this is an end in itself for the bank. Therefore, if the costs of small value transactions can be reduced, it is not something we are opposed to. The Riksbank's responsibility for the previously mentioned RIX system contributes to achieving the goal of promoting a secure and efficient payment system. The stability of the pay system Something that can harm the payment system is, for example, if counterfeit notes and coins come into circulation. In order to make counterfeiting more difficult, the Swedish banknotes and coins have been equipped with various security features that make them almost impossible to counterfeit. Of course, bad copies can always be achieved, but these are discovered with today's technology with relatively great ease. Since the Riksbank has a statutory monopoly on the issuance of banknotes and coins, and the Riksbank cannot, by definition, go bankrupt, no user holder of banknotes and coins needs to feel any concern that these will become worthless. This is, of course, one of the reasons why they are still popular and attractive to hold. From the Riksbank's perspective, electronic money, or more precisely, electronic unit of value carriers for small value transactions, are of interest primarily from the point of view of payment systems. Electronic money, old instrument  new technology In future, let me define electronic money or electronic small-value transactions as such that are carried out using so-called prepaid cards (smart cards). The introduction of electronic money does not imply that a new means of payment in itself Arisen. Paper-based prepaid payment instruments such as travellers' cheques and postal drafts already exist in the past. The former are in many cases issued by non-banks as travel companies etc, the latter however mainly by banks. Characteristic of these instruments is high credibility and therefore great usefulness. A prepaid card can similarly replace cash in the form of banknotes and coins. By transferring a sum of money from a bank account or other deposit account to a computer chip in a plastic card, this can be equated to withdrawing money from an account and receiving cash in the form of banknotes and coins. The difference to the cash withdrawal case is legally that in the chip case the claim remains against the bank/issuer institution and the chip holder has received a promise from the issuer to ""redeem""" these electronic commitments, upon request, for money. In the case of a payment to a third party, a means of payment that definitively extinguishes a claim is not transferred, but what is transferred is a claim on the issuer. Banknotes and coins are legal tenders, which does not apply to electronic units of value. Electronic money  deposits or not? Technically, a "withdrawal document" means that the account holder debits his account - withdraws money - and lends it to the issuer against the security of electronic devices stored on the computer chip on the plastic card. The issuer incurs a debt towards the chip card holder. Formally legally, however, the transaction should be considered to involve the account holder's claim on the bank/issuer changing form from an account claim to a claim in the form of a chip card. For this "lending"" to the issuer, the cardholder does not normally receive any compensation. For the issuer, this is equivalent to an interest-free loan. Normally, this should not be a problem, but if the issuer should get into payment difficulties before our cardholder has had time to spend their electronic money or the recipient of the electronic money has had time to "redeem" these and enter the ""real" value in their account, problems arise. The holder of the plastic card with ""prepaid money"" or the one who received, but did not redeem the electronic money, assumes a risk that depends on the issuer of the solvency of the electronic host. This problem is to be equated with the risk that exists when someone deposits money with ICA or KF. The advantage of depositing money in a bank is that these deposits are subject to special legislation and now also to a deposit guarantee. Neither legislation nor guarantee covers deposits outside the banking system. Recommendations of the EMI Within the EMI, this problem has been addressed and the EMI has decided to recommend to member states to limit the right to issue electronic money to banks, if the electronic money can be used for payment without restrictions. The background to this proposal is that the EMI believes that banks are under extensive supervision, which is why the risk of an uncontrolled suspension of payments is limited, and that if this were to happen, smaller creditors such as small savers are covered by the depositor account. Developments in Sweden; account in non-banks; As I mentioned earlier, there is a certain similarity in terms of the basic problem, with, for example, the ICA account. In Sweden, a law was passed in 1994 that allows non-banks to also be allowed to receive deposits (prepayments) without special requirements for supervision. However, it was decided that the proceeds of such an account could not amount to more than the equivalent of half a basic amount. One of the reasons for this was that parliament and the government wanted to promote competition for depositors' money and allow a lot of transactions to be carried out outside the banking system. It was hoped that the transaction costs could thus be reduced and thus benefited to consumers. The risk taken by depositors by depositing the funds with unsupervised companies was assumed to be outweighed by the benefits that could be achieved in the form of higher interest rates and smoother transactions. Who is allowed to issue electronic money? From this aspect and with the experience gained so far from this system, I do not believe that the right to issue prepaid data-chip cards needs to be limited to banks, as long as the value that can be stored on the card is low. For natural reasons, interest in storing large values on the card will be limited as long as no compensation is provided to the holders of the electronic money. The profit made by the issuer/issuer of electronic money is matched by the interest profit he makes on his interest-free loan from the cardholder. This merit is reminiscent of the one that the Riksbank currently has on its banknotes and coins in circulation. This Riksbank income, the seignoraget or banknote issuance privilege, is normally passed on to the Riksbank's owner, the Riksdag, and thus takes on the character of a tax on the means of payment. Legislation and technological developments The technical development in chip technology in particular is fast and the opportunities created are great. In this context, it is important to recall that it is the combination of law and technology that determines which financial products can be launched. Technology alone is not enough. Against this background, there may be an interest in clarifying certain basic provisions applicable to electronic money. However, it is important that laws and regulations are not designed in such a way as to hamper further development, rather they should reinforce the same in a favourable direction. One problem that is already being dealt with in detail is the issue of anonymity. After all, notes and coins have the characteristic of the holder that a payment cannot be traced afterwards. A transaction in a data chip allows the transaction to be saved and thus enables a payment to be followed. This possibility is valuable from a socio-economic point of view, mainly when criminal transactions are to be traced, but on the other hand can be questionable for the individual. Other aspects are the previously mentioned regarding the legal status of electronic money. What happens to electronic money when a issuer of the same can no longer redeem the electronic devices for "real" money? It is likely that these and other issues can be dealt with acceptable by means of the existing legislation adapted to the new conditions. Another problem area may be cross-border payments using prepaid cards. The problem that may arise here is almost statistical. It may be more difficult to follow cross-border transactions with prepaid cards than with banknotes. However, given that transactions are carried out using computers, this problem should also be solved by means of common rules on reporting, etc. E-money and security/credibility Security issues have been touched upon before and are of course important to monitor. For banknotes and coins, these have become increasingly difficult to copy. Conversely, for a computer chip, it is fairly easy to copy, which is why it must be surrounded with other security procedures. Technological development has also advanced strongly here and, according to information from the chip manufacturers, today protocols were used for the data transfer that utilize such advanced encryption technology that it would likely take at least 100 years to reveal the encryption with today's capabilities on computers. This emerges from an investigation and analysis of data security issues, carried out on behalf of the BIS. The investigation further showed that security is likely to be higher for electronic transactions than for transactions using banknotes. Electronic money in the future Future developments in the field of electronic payments will take place not only by card, but also in various computer networks, of which the Internet is one. What is likely to be the next step is communication between different, today closed systems. By staging values on, for example, your own PC, opportunities to transfer money from one system to another can be created. From the point of view of the individual consumer, this means that she is no longer tied to a system, for example within a bank, but can, using her own hard drive, move money from one bank to another. These developments are likely to promote competition and thus the development of the future payment systems. Let me summarize The Riksbank essentially welcomes the trend towards an increasing number of electronic transactions. This will increase the efficiency of payment intermediation, transaction costs will fall and security will increase in comparison to more traditionally paper-based transactions. My opinion is that it is not necessary to restrict the right to issue prepaid cards or other prepaid instruments in the form of electronic money to the credit institutions (banks). Important in this context, however, is that the public is made aware of the differences that arise if electronic money is issued by credit institutions or other companies. Credit institutions are under the supervision of the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the rules and balances on accounts in these institutions are covered by the general deposit guarantee. Electronic money issued by undertakings other than credit institutions is not subject to the same supervision and guarantees. I believe that current legislation, both banking and consumer legislation, with some adaptations, is sufficient to regulate the issuance of electronic money. Some issues related to the reporting of major transactions in connection with presumed money laundering may remain to be addressed. From the Riksbank's point of view, the primary concern is that the technology used is secure and that the transaction registration systems are sound. I see the move towards prepaid data chip cards ("smart cards") as a first step in a possibly comprehensive change in the payment system that is likely to lead to changes in the financial market for payment services. Money and payment processing will always include societal protection interests, which is why the Riksbank both welcomes the development as such and wishes it to hurry slowly. What is happening now on the part of the authorities to pursue the issue further and gradually work out an appropriate regulatory framework for electronic payments - given what I said earlier about avoiding going in and regulating too hard and too soon? I now think it is appropriate for the Riksbank, together with the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority - since we both have interests to monitor when it comes to the development of these new means of payment - to sit down and formulate a letter to the government. One option is to propose supplementary directives to the work of the Banking Law Committee. In my opinion, it is reasonable to bring these issues together with the rest of the work of this committee, because electronic payments should be seen in the context of other payment services and not as a specific, separate activity. This has, of course, been one of the most important messages in my speech.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Riksbankens roll i ett elektroniskt betalningssystem Datum: 1996-08-28 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Stefan Ingves Plats: IIRs konferens Kontokort, 28-29 augusti 1996 Berns Congress Inledning Lt mig till att brja med reda ut rubrikens begrepp ngot. Riksbanken r sedan lng tid tillbaka engagerad i elektroniska betalningar genom att banken driver RIXsystemet fr clearing och avveckling av stora betalningar. Detta system omstter """elektroniska""" betalningar till ett vrde av ca 300 miljarder svenska kronor per dag. Under en arbetsvecka innebr detta att belopp motsvarande Sveriges BNP passerar Riksbankens datorer vrdemssigt. Vad rubriken avser r det betalningssystem som vi vanligtvis frknippar med de vardagliga inkpen av tidningar, parkeringstjnster, lokaltrafik etc. Det vill sga sm betalningar. Erfarenhetsmssigt str de sm vardagliga kontantbetalningarna fr ca 10% av det omsatta vrdet, medan volymen av dessa sm betalningar svarar fr ca 90% av antalet dagligen genomfrda transaktioner. Smvrdestransaktioner kostar pengar Traditionellt har dessa sm betalningar skett med hjlp av sedlar och mynt som tillhandahlls av Riksbanken. Av den utestende sedelmngden i december 1995 svarade mindre valrer (tom 100 SEK) endast fr ca 18 % av den utelpande sedelstockens samlade vrde. Om vi ven rknar med 500 kronors sedlarna motsvarar det ca 50% av den utelpande sedelstocken, vilket innebr att ca 50% av den utelpande sedelstockens vrde representerades av 1000 kronors sedlar, vilka sannolikt inte anvnds fr de mindre transaktionerna i ngon strre utstrckning. Den utveckling som nu pgr syftar sledes till att p sikt erstta frmst behovet av sm valrer av sedlar och mynt (upp till 500 SEK). Fr banker svl som fr frsljningsstllen av olika slag r hanteringen av sedlar och mynt som resultat av smvrdestransaktioner tmligen kostsam. Mot denna bakgrund r det inte frvnande att ny teknik utvecklas vilken syftar till att nedbringa hanteringskostnaderna fr smvrdestransaktioner. I en vidare mening r det nskvrt att allt fler transaktioner sker p elektronisk vg d drigenom dagens dyra pappersbaserade hantering kan reduceras ytterligare. I Sverige gr denna utveckling nnu ngot trgt jmfrt med mnga andra industrilnder. Efterfrgan p sedlar och mynt Fr att f en uppfattning om sedlarnas och myntens betydelse i den svenska ekonomin har jag berknat sedelstockens andel av BNP fr ren 1950 till 1995 Som framgr av fljande bild har vrdet av de utelpande sedlarna och mynten relativt BNP-vrdet mer n halverats under den redovisade perioden. Frklaringen till detta r bland annat att allt fler transaktioner sker i form av elektroniska penningverfringar. En viktig hndelse som bidragit till denna utveckling var vergngen frn kontantutbetalda lner till lner insatta p lnekonton i bank eller postgiro. Man skall vara frsiktig med trender men om trenden fr denna utveckling hller i sig kommer sedelanvndningen att helt upphra om 20 r...! Ur Riksbankens synvinkel r denna utveckling ngot som vi har att leva med och som vi inte kan motstta oss. Inledningsvis nmnde jag att Riksbanken redan r starkt involverad i storvrdestransaktionerna, vilka inte r srskilt mnga, men desto mer betydelsefulla, som bas fr den penningpolitik banken bedriver. Ur den synvinkeln r en eventuell frlust av efterfrgan p lgre valrer av sedlar och mynt av mindre betydelse. Riksbankens huvuduppgifter Riksbankens huvuduppgifter r fr det frsta att bedriva penningpolitik och fr det andra att frmja ett skert och effektivt betalningsvsende. Penningpolitikens ml r som bekant att vrdet p den svenska kronan inte fr urholkas av inhemsk inflation. Mlet r mer konkret satt till en prisfrndringstakt per r om 2% med en tolerans p + - 1%. Att frse den svenska ekonomin med sedlar och mynt av tillrcklig omfattning r en annan viktig uppgift, men detta innebr ju inte att detta r ett sjlvndaml fr banken. Om drfr kostnaderna fr smvrdestransaktioner kan minskas r det inte ngot vi motstter oss. Riksbankens ansvar fr det tidigare omnmnda RIX-systemet bidrar till att mlet att frmja ett skert och effektivt betalningsvsende kan uppns. Stabiliteten i betalningssystemet Ngot som kan skada betalningsvsendet r exempelvis om falska sedlar och mynt kommer i omlopp. Fr att frsvra frfalskningar har de svenska sedlarna och mynten frsetts med olika skerhetsdetaljer som gr dem i det nrmaste omjliga att frfalska. Dliga kopior kan sjlvfallet alltid stadkommas, men dessa upptcks med dagens teknik med relativt stor ltthet. Genom att Riksbanken har lagstadgat monopol p utgivningen av sedlar och mynt, och Riksbanken per definition inte kan bli bankrutt, behver inte ngon anvndareinnehavare av sedlar och mynt knna ngon oro fr att dessa skall bli vrdelsa. Detta r sjlvfallet en av frklaringarna till att de fortfarande r populra och attraktiva att inneha. Ur Riksbankens perspektiv r elektroniska pengar, eller mer egentligt, elektroniska vrdeenhetsbrare fr smvrdestransaktioner, intressanta ur frmst betalningsvsendesynvinkel. Elektroniska pengar, gammalt instrument  ny teknik Lt mig i fortsttningen definiera elektroniska pengar eller elektroniska smvrdestransaktioner som sdana vilka genomfres med hjlp av s kallade frbetalda kort (smarta kort). Introduktionen av elektroniska pengar innebr inte att ett nytt betalningsmedel i sig uppkommit. Redan tidigare frekommer pappersbaserade frbetalda betalningsinstrument som resecheckar och postvxlar. De frra utges i mnga fall av icke banker som resefretag etc, de senare dock frmst av banker. Knnetecknande fr dessa instrument r hg trovrdighet och drmed stor anvndbarhet. Ett frbetalt kort kan p samma stt erstta kontanter i form av sedlar och mynt. Genom att fra ver en summa pengar frn ett bankkonto eller annat deponeringskonto till ett datachip i ett plastkort, kan detta jmstllas med att ta ut pengar frn ett konto och erhlla kontanter i form av sedlar och mynt. Skillnaden gentemot kontantuttags fallet r rent juridiskt att i chipfallet finns fordran kvar mot banken/utgivarinstitutet och chipinnehavaren har erhllit ett lfte frn utgivaren att """lsa""" in dessa elektroniska taganden, vid anmodan, mot pengar. Vid en betalning till tredjeman verlts inte ett betalningsmedel som definitivt utslcker en fordran utan vad som verlts r en fordran p utgivaren. Sedlar och mynt r legala betalningsmedel, vilket inte gller elektroniska vrdeenheter. Elektroniska pengar  inlning eller ej? Tekniskt sett innebr en """uttagshandling""" att kontoinnehavaren debiterar sitt konto -tar ut pengar- och lnar ut dessa till utgivaren mot skerhet i elektroniska enheter som lagras p datachipet p plastkortet. Utgivaren iklr sig en skuld gentemot chipkort innehavaren. Formellt juridiskt torde transaktionen emellertid f anses innebra att kontohavarens fordran p banken/utgivaren ndrar form frn kontofordran till en fordran i form av ett chip-kort. Fr denna """utlning""" till utgivaren fr inte kortinnehavaren normalt ngon ersttning. Fr utgivaren motsvarar detta ett rntefritt ln. Normalt skall detta inte vara ngot problem, men om utgivaren skulle komma i betalningssvrigheter innan vr kortinnehavare hunnit spendera sina elektroniska pengar eller mottagaren av de elektroniska pengarna hunnit """lsa in""" dessa och fra in """riktigt""" vrde p sitt konto, uppkommer problem. Den som innehar plastkortet med """frbetalda pengar""" eller den som mottagit, men inte lst in de elektroniska pengarna, tar p sig en risk som beror av utstllaren av elektroniska vrdens soliditet. Denna problematik r att jmstlla med den risk som finns d ngon deponerar pengar hos ICA eller KF. Frdelen med att deponera pengar i en bank r att dessa depositioner omfattas av srskild lagstiftning och numera ven av en insttargaranti. Varken lagstiftning eller garanti omfattar insttningar utanfr banksystemet. EMI:s rekommendationer Inom EMI har detta problem behandlats och EMI har beslutat rekommendera medlemslnderna att begrnsa utgivningsrtten av elektroniska pengar till banker, om de elektroniska pengarna kan anvndas fr betalning utan begrnsningar. Bakgrunden till detta frslag r att EMI menar att banker str under omfattande tillsyn, varfr risken fr en okontrollerad betalningsinstllelse r begrnsad, samt att om s skulle ske mindre fordringsgare som smsparare omfattas av insttargrantin. Utvecklingen i Sverige; konto i icke banker Som jag tidigare nmnde finns en viss likhet vad gller grundproblematiken, med exempelvis ICA-konto. I Sverige antogs en lag 1994 som medger att ven icke banker skulle f rtt att ta emot insttningar (frbetalningar) utan srskilda krav p tillsyn. Dock bestmdes att behllningen p ett sdant konto inte fick uppg till mer n motsvarande ett halvt basbelopp. Ett av sklen till detta var att riksdagen och regeringen ville frmja konkurrensen om insttarnas pengar och medge att en mngd transaktioner skulle kunna genomfras utanfr banksystemet. Frhoppningen var att transaktionskostnaderna hrigenom skulle kunna nedbringas och drmed komma konsumenterna tillgodo. Den risk som insttarna tar genom att medlen deponeras hos fretag som inte str under tillsyn, antogs uppvgda av de frdelar som kunde uppns i form av hgre rntersttning och smidigare transaktioner. Vem fr ge ut elektroniska pengar? Utifrn denna aspekt och med de erfarenheter som hittills erhllits frn detta system anser jag inte att utgivningsrtten till frbetalda data-chip kort behver begrnsas till banker, s lnge som det vrde som kan lagras p kortet r lgt. Av naturliga skl kommer intresset av att lagra stora vrden p kortet att vara begrnsat s lnge som ingen ersttning lmnas till innehaven av de elektroniska pengarna. Den frtjnst som utstllaren/utgivaren av elektroniska pengar gr motsvaras av den rntevinst denne gr p sitt rntefria ln frn kortinnehavaren. Denna frtjnst pminner om den som Riksbanken idag har p sina utelpande sedlar och mynt. Denna Riksbanksinkomst, seignoraget eller sedelutgivningsprivilegiet, levereras normalt vidare till Riksbankens gare, riksdagen, och fr drmed karaktren av en skatt p betalningsmedlen. Lagstiftning och teknisk utveckling Den tekniska utvecklingen inom frmst chip-tekniken gr fort och de mjligheter som skapas r stora. Det r i detta sammanhang viktigt att pminna om att det r kombinationen av juridik och teknik som bestmmer vilka finansiella produkter som kan lanseras. Enbart tekniken rcker inte. Mot denna bakgrund kan det finnas intresse av att klargra vissa grundlggande bestmmelser som r tillmpliga p de elektroniska pengarna. Det r emellertid viktigt att lagar och regler inte fr en sdan utformning att de hmmar den fortsatta utvecklingen, de br snarare frstrka densamma i gynnsam riktning. En problematik som redan nu behandlas ingende r frgan om anonymitet. Sedlar och mynt har ju den egenskapen fr innehavaren, att en betalning inte kan spras i efterhand. En transaktion i ett data-chip medger att transaktionen sparas och drmed mjliggr att en betalning kan fljas. Denna mjlighet r ur samhllsekonomisk synvinkel vrdefull, frmst d kriminella transaktioner skall spras, men kan  andra sidan vara tveksam fr individen. Andra aspekter r de tidigare nmnda kring de elektroniska pengarnas legala status. Vad hnder med elektroniska pengar d en utgivare av desamma inte lngre kan lsa in de elektroniska enheterna mot "riktiga" pengar? Sannolikt kan dessa och andra frgor ges en godtagbar behandling med hjlp av den existerande lagstiftningen anpassad till de nya frutsttningarna. Ett annat problemomrde kan vara grnsverskridande betalningar med hjlp av frbetalda kort. Det problem som hr kan uppkomma r nrmast statistiskt. Det kan bli svrare att flja grnsverskridande transaktioner med frbetalda kort n med hjlp av sedlar. Men med tanke p att transaktionerna genomfres med hjlp av datorer torde ven detta problem kunna lsas med hjlp av gemensamma regler om rapportering etc. E-pengar och skerhet/trovrdighet Skerhetsfrgorna har berrts tidigare och r naturligtvis viktiga att bevaka. Fr sedlar och mynt gller att dessa ju blivit allt svrare att kopiera. Fr ett datachip gller det omvnda att det r tmligen enkelt att kopiera varfr det mste omges med andra skerhetsrutiner. Den tekniska utvecklingen har ven hr gtt starkt framt och enligt uppgift frn chip-tillverkarna anvndes idag protokoll fr dataverfringen som utnyttjar s avancerad krypteringsteknik att det sannolikt skulle ta minst 100 r att avslja krypteringen med dagens kapacitet p datorer. Detta framkommer i en utredning och analys av dataskerhetsfrgor, som genomfrts p uppdrag av BIS. Utredningen visade vidare att skerheten sannolikt r hgre fr elektroniska transaktioner n fr transaktioner med hjlp av sedlar. Elektoniska pengar i framtiden Den framtida utvecklingen inom omrdet elektroniska betalningar kommer att ske inte bara med kort utan ven inom olika datantverk, varav Internet r ett. Det som sannolikt kommer att bli nsta steg r kommunikation mellan olika, idag slutna system. Genom att mellanlagra vrden p t.ex den egna PC:n kan mjligheter att verfra pengar frn ett system till ett annat skapas. Ur den enskilde konsumentens synvinkel innebr detta att hon inte lngre r bunden till ett system, exempelvis inom en bank, utan kan med hjlp av den egna hrddisken flytta pengar frn en bank till en annan. Denna utveckling befrmjar sannolikt konkurrensen och drmed utvecklingen av de framtida betalningssytemen. Lt mig sammanfatta Riksbanken vlkomnar i allt vsentligt utvecklingen mot allt fler elektroniska transaktioner. Detta kommer att ka effektiviteten i betalningsfrmedlingen, transaktionskostnaderna kommer att sjunka och skerheten att ka i jmfrelse med mer traditionellt pappersbaserade transaktioner. Min sikt r att det inte r ndvndigt att begrnsa utgivningsrtten av frbetalda kort eller andra frbetalda instrument i form av elektroniska pengar till kreditinstituten (bankerna). Viktigt i detta sammanhang r emellertid att allmnheten uppmrksammas p de skillnader som uppkommer om elektroniska pengar ges ut av kreditinstitut eller andra fretag. Kreditinstituten str under Finansinspektionens tillsyn och regler och behllning p konton i dessa institut omfattas av den allmnna insttargarantin. Elektroniska pengar utgivna av andra fretag n kreditinstitut omfattas inte av samma tillsyn och garantier. Jag tror att nuvarande lagstiftning, svl banklagstiftning som konsumentlagstiftning, med vissa anpassningar, r tillrcklig fr att reglera utgivningen av elektroniska pengar. Vissa frgor kring rapportering av strre transaktioner i samband med frmodad penningtvtt kan terst att behandla. Ur Riksbankens synvinkel r det primra att den anvnda tekniken r sker och att systemen fr transaktionsregistrering r sunda. Jag ser utvecklingen mot frbetalda data-chip kort ("smart cards") som ett frsta steg i en mjligen omfattande frndring av betalningsystemet vilken sannolikt kommer att leda till frndringar i den finansiella marknaden fr betaltjnster. Pengar och betalningshantering kommer alltid att innefatta samhlleliga skyddsintressen varfr Riksbanken bde vlkomnar utvecklingen som sdan och nskar att den skyndar lngsamt. Vad sker nu frn myndigheternas sida fr att driva frgan vidare och gradvis arbeta fram ett lmpligt regelverk fr elektroniska betalningar - givet vad jag tidigare sagt om att man skall undvika att g in och reglera fr hrt och fr tidigt? Jag tycker nu att det r lmpligt att Riksbanken tillsammans med Finansinspektionen - eftersom vi bda har intressen att bevaka nr det gller utvecklingen av dessa nya betalningsmedel - stter sig ned och formulerar ett brev till regeringen. Ett alternativ r att fresl tillggsdirektiv till arbetet i Banklagskommittn. Enligt min mening r det rimligt att sammanfra dessa frgor med det vriga arbetet i denna kommitt eftersom elektroniska betalningar br ses i samband med vriga betalningstjnster och inte som ngon srskild, avskild, aktivitet. Detta har ju varit ett av de viktigaste budskapen i mitt anfrande. Title: Current monetary policy
text: Rosenberg: The current monetary policy Date 2007-02-05 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg gave a speech at the Royal Institute of Technology on Monday. Rosenberg began by talking about the Riksbank's goals and strategy and then presented his view of the current monetary policy situation. "The Riksbank has a statutory objective for monetary policy: to maintain a fixed monetary value. We have defined it as the annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) to be 2 percent with a tolerance range of b1 1 percentage point. Monetary policy normally focuses on achieving the inflation target within a two-year period. That's because monetary policy operates with some delay. But it is also because the Riksbank wants to dampen fluctuations in the real economy, such as GDP growth and employment," Rosenberg said. "In some situations, we may even need to let the adaptation take longer than two years. This could be the case, for example, if the economy were to suffer an unexpectedly large disruption. Otherwise, there is a risk that the pressures on the real economy will be too great. But in order for us to be so flexible with the inflation target at all, there must be confidence in monetary policy. This, in turn, requires us to openly and clearly report why inflation deviates from the target and how we view the development going forward. We do this in inflation reports, press releases, minutes of our meetings and in speeches from executive board members," Rosenberg said. "Open and clear communication is important for the Riksbank. Many believe that we are already among the most open and clear central banks in the world. But there's always more to do. Therefore, we have continued the work of developing our analysis and how we present it. In connection with the next monetary policy meeting on February 14, some changes will take place. The most important one is that we will publish our own forecast for the repo rate. Since the autumn of 2005, we have based our forecasts on the repo rate developing in line with market expectations. The fact that we are now making our own forecast for the repo rate will be an even clearer guide for the public on how the Riksbank views developments in the Swedish economy and how the repo rate may change. At the same time, I would like to emphasize that our own forecast for the development of interest rates is not a promise on the part of the Riksbank, it is precisely a forecast. As in the past, economic developments will determine how we will change the repo rate in the future," Rosenberg stressed. "Another change we are making is to rename the Inflation Report to 'Monetary Policy Report'. This is partly because the report will include not only a forecast for inflation but also a monetary policy message by publishing our own interest rate forecast. There will be a clear link between the projections and the monetary policy considerations directly in the report. Our hope is also that the report will be more educational," Rosenberg said. "I would like to conclude by saying a few words about how I see economic development and what it means for monetary policy. The development in the Swedish economy is very positive. Output and employment are growing rapidly at the same time as inflation remains at a low level. At the last monetary policy meeting on 14 December, we raised the repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.0 per cent. The Executive Board also announced that we saw further hikes ahead of us, at about the rate expressed at the time in market participants' expectations," Rosenberg said. "In my opinion, the new information that has come does not give reason to change the assessment from December to any great extent. Both the international and Swedish economic conditions have continued to develop favourably. The global economy has developed in line with both the forecast in the October Inflation Report and the assessment made ahead of the December monetary policy meeting. Overall, the Swedish economy has developed somewhat stronger than we expected in October, but in line with what we assessed in December. The same goes for the labor market and employment," Rosenberg continued. "Despite the rapid growth, there is much to suggest that there will continue to be forces holding back inflation. Not only demand, but also supply in the economy is growing rapidly. Productivity growth is strong and it cannot be ruled out that labour force growth will be higher in the coming years than we previously expected, partly as a result of the government's proposals for tax and labour market policy reforms. In addition, the price of oil has fallen. Inflation therefore looks set to remain subdued," Rosenberg said. "All in all, therefore, I see no reason today to move faster with interest rate hikes than markets expected in the weeks before the December monetary policy meeting despite the continued strong upturn in the economy. But as usual, we will take a position on all the new information that has come since our previous meeting when we in the Riksbank's Executive Board take our next decision on monetary policy on February 14," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Den aktuella penningpolitiken Datum 2007-02-05 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg hll under mndagen ett tal p Kungliga Tekniska hgskolan. Rosenberg inledde med att tala om Riksbankens ml och strategi och redogjorde drefter fr sin syn p det aktuella penningpolitiska lget. Riksbanken har ett lagstadgat ml fr penningpolitiken: att upprtthlla ett fast penningvrde. Vi har definierat det som att den rliga frndringen av konsumentprisindex (KPI) ska vara 2 procent med ett toleransintervall p  1 procentenhet. Penningpolitiken inriktas normalt p att uppn inflationsmlet inom en tvrsperiod. Det beror p att penningpolitiken verkar med viss frdrjning. Men det beror ocks p att Riksbanken vill dmpa svngningar i den reala ekonomin, som till exempel BNP-tillvxt och sysselsttning, sade Rosenberg. I vissa situationer kan vi till och med behva lta anpassningen ta lngre tid n tv r. Det kan till exempel vara fallet om ekonomin skulle drabbas av en ovntat stor strning. Risken r annars att pfrestningarna p den reala ekonomin blir alltfr stora. Men fr att vi verhuvudtaget ska kunna vara s flexibla med inflationsmlet s mste det finnas ett frtroende fr penningpolitiken. Det stller i sin tur krav p att vi ppet och tydligt redovisar varfr inflationen avviker frn mlet och hur vi ser p utvecklingen framver. Detta gr vi i inflationsrapporter, pressmeddelanden, protokoll frn vra sammantrden och i tal frn direktionens ledamter", sade Rosenberg. ppen och tydlig kommunikation r viktig fr Riksbanken. Mnga anser att vi redan idag tillhr de mest ppna och tydliga centralbankerna i vrlden. Men det finns alltid mer att gra. Drfr har vi fortsatt arbetet med att utveckla vr analys och hur vi presenterar den. I samband med nsta penningpolitiska mte den 14 februari sker ngra frndringar. Den viktigaste r att vi kommer att publicera vr egen prognos fr reporntan. Sedan hsten 2005 har vi byggt prognoserna p att reporntan utvecklas i linje med marknadens frvntningar. Att vi nu gr vr egen prognos fr reporntan blir en nnu tydligare vgledning fr allmnheten om hur Riksbanken ser p utvecklingen i svensk ekonomi och p hur reporntan kan komma att ndras. Samtidigt vill jag understryka att vr egen prognos fr rntans utveckling inte r ngot lfte frn Riksbankens sida, den r just en prognos. Precis som tidigare kommer den ekonomiska utvecklingen att avgra hur vi kommer att frndra reporntan i framtiden, betonade Rosenberg. En annan frndring som vi gr r att byta namn p inflationsrapporten till Penningpolitisk rapport. Det beror bland annat p att rapporten inte bara kommer att inkludera en prognos fr inflationen utan ocks ett penningpolitiskt budskap genom att vi publicerar vr egen rnteprognos. Det kommer att finnas en tydlig koppling mellan prognoserna och de penningpolitiska vervgandena direkt i rapporten. Vr frhoppning r ocks att rapporten ska bli mer pedagogisk, sade Rosenberg. Jag vill avsluta med att sga ngra ord om hur jag ser p den ekonomiska utvecklingen och vad den innebr fr penningpolitiken. Utvecklingen i svensk ekonomi r mycket positiv. Produktion och sysselsttning kar snabbt samtidigt som inflationen hller sig kvar p en lg niv. Vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet den 14 december hjde vi reporntan med 0,25 procentenheter till 3,0 procent. Direktionen meddelade ocks att vi sg ytterligare hjningar framfr oss, ungefr i den takt som d kom till uttryck i marknadsaktrernas frvntningar, sade Rosenberg. Enligt min mening ger den nya information som kommit inte anledning att ndra bedmningen frn i december i ngon strre utstrckning. Bde den internationella och den svenska konjunkturen har fortsatt att utvecklas gynnsamt. Den globala ekonomin har utvecklats i linje med svl prognosen i inflationsrapporten frn oktober som den bedmning som gjordes infr det penningpolitiska mtet i december. Den svenska ekonomin har p det hela taget utvecklats ngot starkare n vad vi frvntade i oktober, men i linje med vad vi bedmde i december. Detsamma gller arbetsmarknaden och sysselsttningen, fortsatte Rosenberg. Produktivitetstillvxten r stark och det kan inte uteslutas att arbetskraftens tillvxt kommer att bli hgre de kommande ren n vi tidigare frvntat oss bland annat till fljd av regeringens frslag p skatte- och arbetsmarknadspolitiska reformer. Dessutom har oljepriset sjunkit. Inflationen ser drfr ut att bli fortsatt dmpad, sade Rosenberg. Sammantaget ser jag drfr idag inga skl att g snabbare fram med rntehjningar n vad marknaderna frvntade sig veckorna innan det penningpolitiska mtet i december trots den fortsatt starka uppgngen i ekonomin. Title: The current economic situation
text: Rosenberg: The current economic situation Date 2006-11-28 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke on Tuesday about the current economic situation and monetary policy at business administration day 2006. "The Inflation Report published at the end of October states that GDP growth in both Sweden and the rest of the world has remained high during the first half of this year and stronger than expected. Growth is also expected to be relatively strong during the rest of the year and next year. Gradually, however, the economy enters a calmer phase. Inflation in the rest of the world is expected to be relatively moderate," Rosenberg began. "The high growth in the Swedish economy is expected in the Inflation Report to continue for the rest of the year, albeit at a slightly lower pace. In the coming years, there will be a gradual slowdown in growth as a result of slower productivity growth as well as demand from the rest of the world. In the labour market, there has been a clear improvement during the year and most indications are that employment will continue to rise. As productivity growth slows and wages rise faster, domestic cost pressures are expected to increase. The strong economic development is also reflected in the fact that companies and households have increased their borrowing relatively much in recent years from a historical perspective. At the same time, house prices have risen rapidly and household wealth has increased further," Rosenberg continued. "Inflation has gradually risen from a low level since the beginning of 2005 and is expected to be moderate in the coming years despite good economic developments. The low inflation in recent years is largely due to favourable supply conditions such as strong productivity growth and international price pressures. These factors are expected to continue to dampen inflation. Inflation is also expected to be held down over the forecast period by low rates of increase in energy prices," Rosenberg said. "The Inflation Report estimates that the risks of inflation being higher than in the main scenario are slightly greater than the risks of it being lower. Over a two-year horizon, risk-adjusted inflation measured by UND1X is expected to be 1.7 per cent. The fact that inflation is expected to be slightly below the two-year inflation target is largely due to the fact that energy prices are then expected to temporarily dampen inflation. When this effect fades, inflation will rise and is expected to be in line with the target after just over two years. Real economic developments are expected to be strong over the projection horizon. In order to ensure inflation in line with the target and contribute to a balanced real economic development, the Riksbank's Executive Board decided to raise the repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2.75 per cent at the last monetary policy meeting in October," Rosenberg said. "The new statistics that have been published since then broadly confirm the economic picture that was drawn in the Inflation Report. The preliminary GDP outcome for the third quarter in the US was slightly weaker than expected, which suggests slightly lower growth there going forward. In Sweden, inflation figures for the month of October have been published. The outcome for both CPI and UND1X was in line with our forecast. New national accounts statistics show that GDP growth in 2004 and 2005 was stronger than previously estimated. But productivity growth was also faster, helping to contain cost pressures and inflation. The krona has strengthened unexpectedly much on more recently and this is probably largely related to a general weakening of the dollar. Experience shows that exchange rates can fluctuate rapidly both up and down. It is now too early to comment on whether the krona appreciation will be permanent and what consequences this may have for the Swedish economy. The labour market statistics for October show continued strong labour market developments, if slightly stronger than forecast in the Inflation Report. Other indicators also show that the labour market situation continues to improve. The latest indicators from the Business Cycle Barometer and the Purchasing Managers' Index indicate continued good economic development, but there has nevertheless been some moderation compared to the strong development during the first half of the year," Rosenberg noted. "In the October Inflation Report, inflation was assessed to be in line with the target over a two-year horizon provided that the repo rate is gradually raised approximately in the way expected in the market. The new information that has come, as I see it, so far does not speak for any major changes in the assessments presented at the time. But there are a few weeks left until our next monetary policy meeting and, as usual, my colleagues and I will have to decide on the overall information that is then available," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Det aktuella ekonomiska lget Datum 2006-11-28 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade under tisdagen om det aktuella ekonomiska lget och penningpolitiken vid Fretagsekonomidagen 2006. Efterhand gr dock konjunkturen in i ett lugnare skede. Inflationen i omvrlden vntas bli relativt mttlig, inledde Rosenberg. Den hga tillvxten i svensk ekonomi frvntas i inflationsrapporten fortstta under resten av ret, om n i ngot lgre takt. De kommande ren sker en successiv avmattning av tillvxten till fljd av att produktiviteten kar lngsammare liksom efterfrgan frn omvrlden. Den starka ekonomiska utvecklingen avspeglas ocks i att fretag och hushll under senare r kat sin upplning relativt mycket sett i ett historiskt perspektiv. Samtidigt har huspriserna stigit snabbt och hushllens frmgenhet kat ytterligare, fortsatte Rosenberg. P tv rs sikt vntas den riskjusterade inflationen mtt med UND1X vara 1,7 procent. Att inflationen vntas vara ngot under inflationsmlet p tv rs sikt beror till stor del p att energipriserna d tillflligt vntas dmpa inflationen. Nr den effekten klingar av stiger inflationen och vntas vara i linje med mlet efter drygt tv r. Den realekonomiska utvecklingen vntas vara stark under prognosperioden. Fr att skerstlla en inflation i linje med mlet och bidra till en balanserad realekonomisk utveckling beslutade Riksbankens direktion att hja reporntan med 0,25 procentenheter till 2,75 procent vid det senaste penningpolitiska mtet i oktober, sade Rosenberg. Utfallet fr bde KPI och UND1X var i linje med vr prognos. Ny nationalrkenskapsstatistik visar att BNP-tillvxten 2004 och 2005 var starkare n tidigare berknat. Men ven produktivitetstillvxten var snabbare, vilket bidrar till att hlla ned kostnadstrycket och inflationen. Kronan har strkts ovntat mycket p senare tid och detta hnger troligen till stor del samman med en allmn frsvagning av dollarn. Erfarenheterna visar att valutakurser kan svnga snabbt bde upp och ned. I inflationsrapporten i oktober bedmdes inflationen ligga i linje med mlet p drygt tv rs sikt frutsatt att reporntan gradvis hjs ungefr p det stt som frvntades p marknaden. Title: Changes in monetary policy communication
text: Rosenberg: Changes in monetary policy communication Date 2007-05-11 First Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke today at a meeting at stockholmdjurge5rden Rotary club. In his speech, Rosenberg presented, among other things, some changes in monetary policy communication, which the Riksbank's Executive Board decided on at its meeting on 10 May. "Ever since the introduction of its inflation target, the Riksbank has tried in various ways to increase the transparency and clarity of monetary policy. The decision to start publishing the Riksbank's own interest rate forecasts is the latest expression of this ambition. At our meeting yesterday, the Executive Board decided to take some further steps towards greater clarity in monetary policy communication," Rosenberg began. "Firstly, press conferences will be held in the future after every monetary policy meeting, regardless of the interest rate decision taken. So far, there have only been press conferences if the repo rate has changed or if an inflation report has been published. But information about why the repo rate has remained unchanged is just as important for understanding the structure of monetary policy as information about why the repo rate has changed. By publishing its own interest rate forecasts and by holding press conferences after each monetary policy meeting, the Riksbank provides more detailed and more regular information about the Executive Board's considerations," Rosenberg stressed. "Secondly, the Executive Board has decided to make some changes in terms of monetary policy signalling. By signaling, I mean, simply put, how we convey our monetary policy intentions. The Executive Board has come to the conclusion that there is normally no reason to indicate in speeches and press releases before the monetary policy meetings how the repo rate will be set. We believe that it is sufficient to clearly signal our intentions in connection with the seven monetary policy meetings held per year. In connection with three of these meetings, we publish our own interest rate forecast in the monetary policy report. On other four occasions, we present a qualitative assessment of how the latest published interest rate forecast relates to the new information received. The need to signal between meetings has thus decreased," Rosenberg continued. "One reason why, in exceptional cases, signalling between two monetary policy meetings may still be justified could be that something happens that radically changes the economic situation, while at the same time it is a long way to the next meeting. It should then be clear whether the message comes from an individual member or from a majority of the Executive Board," Rosenberg said. "It may be worth pointing out that individual members of the Executive Board should, of course, be able to express their own views in public in the future as well. But it is above all a matter of clarifying and explaining in retrospect the personal considerations made in connection with the monetary policy meetings. Differences of opinion within the Executive Board will also, as in the past, be evident in the minutes," Rosenberg noted. "That brings me to the third change we decided on. In the Minutes, we will also name members in the ongoing discussion, not just if they have reservations about the interest rate decision. This facilitates forecasting of how monetary policy will be conducted. It will also be easier to examine the motives behind monetary policy decisions. Names in the protocols will thus be another step towards increased transparency and clarity," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Frndringar i den penningpolitiska kommunikationen Datum 2007-05-11 Frste vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade idag vid ett mte p StockholmDjurgrden Rotaryklubb. I sitt anfrande presenterade Rosenberg bland annat ngra frndringar i den penningpolitiska kommunikationen, som Riksbankens direktion fattade beslut om vid sitt mte den 10 maj. nda sedan inflationsmlet infrdes har Riksbanken frskt att p olika stt ka ppenheten och tydligheten i penningpolitiken. Hittills har det bara hllits presskonferenser om reporntan ndrats eller om det publicerats en inflationsrapport. Genom att publicera egna rnteprognoser och genom att hlla presskonferenser efter varje penningpolitiskt mte ger Riksbanken mer detaljerad och mer regelbunden information om direktionens vervganden, framhll Rosenberg. Direktionen har kommit till slutsatsen att det i normalfallet inte finns skl att fre de penningpolitiska mtena i tal och pressmeddelanden indikera hur reporntan kommer att sttas. Vi bedmer att det r tillrckligt att tydligt signalera vra intentioner i samband med de sju penningpolitiska mten som hlls per r. Vid vriga fyra tillfllen redovisar vi en kvalitativ bedmning av hur den senaste publicerade rnteprognosen frhller sig till den nya information som kommit in. Ett skl fr att det i undantagsfall nd kan vara motiverat med signalering mellan tv penningpolitiska mten skulle kunna vara att det intrffar ngot som radikalt ndrar det ekonomiska lget, samtidigt som det r lngt till nsta mte. Det br d tydligt framg om budskapet kommer frn en enskild ledamot eller frn en majoritet i direktionen, framhll Rosenberg. Det kan vara vrt att ppeka att de enskilda direktionsledamterna naturligtvis ska kunna uttrycka sin egen uppfattning offentligt ven i fortsttningen. Det leder mig ver till den tredje frndringen vi beslutat om. I protokollen kommer vi att namnge ledamterna ven i den lpande diskussionen, inte bara om de reserverat sig mot rntebeslutet. Title: Continued strong economy and low inflation
text: Rosenberg: Continued strong economy and low inflation Date 2005-02-24 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke on Thursday at a meeting arranged by Handelsbanken about the work of developing the monetary policy analysis basis and about the current economic situation. "Let me start by highlighting an improvement in the monetary policy analysis underpinnings that we are introducing in the upcoming Inflation Report. In addition to our main scenario, we will present forecasts for inflation where the forecast horizon is longer than it has been so far and with the assumption that the repo rate develops in line with so-called implicit forward rates that reflect the expectations that exist in the financial market about future interest rate policy," Rosenberg said. "The new calculations are presented as a supplementary basis, while the forecast in our main scenario is made in the same way as before. The hope is that this more robust basis will make it easier to understand how we in the Executive Board reason, for example, in situations when inflation is affected by temporary factors. In the past, we have sometimes cleared our measure of inflation of temporary factors that we do not want to affect monetary policy. By extending the forecast horizon, we can now more clearly show that these factors are fading and better justify the design of monetary policy," Rosenberg explained. "At the turn of the year 2002-03 when energy prices rose sharply, we supplemented the analysis with a measure of inflation that was adjusted for energy prices. This led some observers to believe that we had changed our inflation target and led to a debate about which measure of inflation was most relevant to monetary policy and when we would again include energy prices in that measure. I think it would have been clearer how we wanted to deal with the energy price fluctuations if we had then also shown inflation developments in a slightly longer time perspective, just in the way we will now," Rosenberg continued. "The fact that we will at the same time make the forecasts under an alternative assumption for the repo rate is something I also want to highlight. To assume that the repo rate is unchanged, as we usually do in our main scenario, clarifies how inflation develops compared to the target of current monetary policy, but is of course not realistic if the market is set for a rapid change in interest rates. An interest rate assumption closer to market expectations makes it easier to compare our forecasts with those of other analysts who do not normally assume unchanged interest rates. It also improves the ability of our clients and various external assessors to evaluate our forecasts and how we manage," Rosenberg said. "The changes are about making it easier to understand how the Executive Board and the Riksbank reason. So it is not a question of changing the way monetary policy is conducted. Let me also emphasize that an interest rate development in line with futures rates should not be interpreted as the assumption for monetary policy that we in the Riksbank consider most likely," Rosenberg stressed. "When it comes to the current economic situation, I think that the economic picture we drew in connection with last year's last inflation report and when we last took a position on the repo rate in January roughly stands. It's also been that way for more than a year now; although there has been some uncertainty about the economy, it has actually rolled on with good force. Developments since our Interest Rate meeting in January do not provide any reason to make any major revisions to the assessments. The forecast that the euro area will develop somewhat worse than we expected in December seems to be holding up. In Sweden, growth conditions remain good. Ki's Business Cycle Barometer for February certainly shows weaker industrial order growth in recent months, but the order situation is nevertheless good and companies are optimistic about output growth going forward. The construction economy is on the rise and most service industries have a positive view of the future. The same applies to households, which are showing great confidence in the coming year. All in all, this may mean that in the short term we may even need to write up our Swedish GDP forecast a little," Rosenberg continued. "In the labour market, development remains rather sluggish, although there are some signs that a brightening is on the way. For example, the number of newly registered vacancies continues to improve and the number of notices is lower than a year ago. The weak development of employment while gdp growth has been strong is due to rapid productivity growth. Companies have been able to produce more without having to hire new employees. However, if demand in the economy continues to increase as we expected, companies will be forced to increase their workforce. Employment is therefore likely to pick up in 2005," Rosenberg said. "Finally, let me say a few words about the monetary policy decision-making situation. High growth leads to gradually increasing resource utilization. For much of the next two-year period, inflation is still expected to be below the 2% inflation target. Against this background, one could argue for lowering the policy rate further. But there are also reasons against a reduction. The drivers of low inflation, rapid productivity growth and low imported inflation are supply factors that in themselves act as a stimulus to growth. Growth is already high and exceeds what is considered to be sustainable in the long term. In addition, monetary policy is expansionary at present, which contributes, among other things, to a rapid increase in household borrowing and housing prices. Investments in the business sector also turned clearly upwards last year and we expect continued growth at a decent pace during the rest of the forecast period. Against this background, I have made and continue to believe that demand does not need to be further stimulated by monetary policy. At the same time, as always, it deserves to be emphasized that this assessment applies today and under the conditions that now prevail. For example, if we were to see a clearly weaker economy, the assessment could be different," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Fortsatt stark konjunktur och lg inflation Datum 2005-02-24 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade under torsdagen vid ett mte ordnat av Handelsbanken om arbetet med att utveckla det penningpolitiska analysunderlaget samt om det aktuella ekonomiska lget. Lt mig brja med att lyfta fram en frbttring i det penningpolitiska analysunderlaget som vi infr i den kommande inflationsrapporten. Vi kommer att vid sidan av vrt huvudscenario redovisa prognoser fr inflationen dr prognoshorisonten r lngre n den hittills varit och med antagandet att reporntan utvecklas i linje med s kallade implicita terminsrntor som avspeglar de frvntningar som finns p finansmarknaden om den framtida rntepolitiken, sa Rosenberg. De nya berkningarna redovisas som ett kompletterande underlag samtidigt som prognosen i vrt huvudscenario grs p samma stt som tidigare. Frhoppningen r att detta mer fylliga underlag ska gra det lttare att frst hur vi i direktionen resonerar till exempel i situationer nr inflation pverkas av tillflliga faktorer. Tidigare har vi ibland rensat vrt inflationsmtt fr tillflliga faktorer som vi inte vill ska pverka penningpolitiken. Genom att strcka ut prognoshorisonten kan vi nu tydligare visa att dessa faktorer klingar av och bttre motivera utformningen av penningpolitiken, frklarade Rosenberg. Vid rsskiftet 2002-03 d energipriserna steg kraftigt kompletterade vi analysen med ett inflationsmtt som var rensat fr energipriserna. Det fick en del bedmare att tro att vi bytt inflationsml och ledde till en debatt om vilket inflationsmtt som var mest relevant fr penningpolitiken och nr vi terigen skulle komma att inkludera energipriserna i det mttet. Jag tror att det tydligare hade framgtt hur vi ville hantera energiprissvngningarna om vi d ocks hade visat inflationsutvecklingen i ett ngot lngre tidsperspektiv, just p det stt vi nu kommer att gra, fortsatte Rosenberg. Att vi samtidigt kommer att gra prognoserna under ett alternativt antagande fr reporntan r ngot jag ocks vill lyfta fram. Att anta att reporntan r ofrndrad, som vi brukar gra i vrt huvudscenario tydliggr hur inflationen utvecklas jmfrt med mlet vid nuvarande penningpolitik, men r frsts inte realistiskt om marknaden r instlld p en snabb frndring av rntan. Ett rnteantagande nrmare marknadsfrvntningarna gr det lttare att jmfra vra prognoser med andra bedmares som normalt inte frutstter ofrndrad rnta. Det frbttrar dessutom mjligheterna fr vra uppdragsgivare och olika externa bedmare att utvrdera vra prognoser och hur vi skter oss, sa Rosenberg. Frndringarna handlar om att det ska bli lttare att frst hur direktionen och Riksbanken resonerar. Det handlar allts inte om att sttet att bedriva penningpolitiken ndras. Lt mig ocks understryka att en rnteutveckling i linje med terminsrntor inte ska tolkas som det antagande fr penningpolitiken som vi i Riksbanken anser mest sannolikt, betonade Rosenberg. Nr det gller det aktuella ekonomiska lget tycker jag att den konjunkturbild vi tecknade i samband med fjolrets sista inflationsrapport och nr vi sist tog stllning till reporntan i januari i grova drag str sig. S har det ocks varit i mer n ett r nu; ven om det funnits en del oskerhet kring konjunkturen har den faktiskt rullat p med god kraft. Utvecklingen sedan vrt rntemte i januari ger inte skl att gra ngra strre revideringar av bedmningarna. Prognosen att euroomrdet kommer att utvecklas ngot smre n vi rknade med i december verkar st sig. I Sverige r tillvxtfrutsttningarna fortsatt goda. KI:s Konjunkturbarometer fr februari visar visserligen en svagare ordertillvxt i industrin de senaste mnaderna, men orderlget r trots det gott och fretagen r optimistiska om produktionstillvxten framver. Byggkonjunkturen r p vg uppt och de flesta tjnstebranscherna ser positivt p framtiden. Detsamma gller hushllen, som uppvisar en stor tillfrsikt infr det kommande ret. Det hr kan sammantaget gra att vi i det korta perspektivet kanske till och med behver skriva upp vr svenska BNP-prognos en aning, fortsatte Rosenberg. P arbetsmarknaden r utvecklingen fortsatt ganska trg ven om det finns vissa tecken p att en ljusning r p vg. Till exempel fortstter antalet nyanmlda lediga platser att frbttras och antalet varsel r lgre n fr ett r sedan. Att sysselsttningen utvecklats svagt samtidigt som BNP-tillvxten varit stark beror p den snabba produktivitetstillvxten. Fretagen har kunnat tillverka mer utan att behva nyanstlla. Om efterfrgan i ekonomin fortstter att ka som vi rknat med kommer fretagen dock att tvingas ka arbetsstyrkan. Sysselsttningen vnder drfr troligen upp under 2005, sa Rosenberg. Lt mig slutligen sga ngra ord om den penningpolitiska beslutssituationen. Hg tillvxt ger gradvis stigande resursutnyttjande. Under en stor del av den kommande tvrsperioden vntas inflationen nd bli lgre n inflationsmlet p 2 procent. Mot den bakgrunden skulle man kunna argumentera fr att snka styrrntan ytterligare. Men det finns ocks skl som talar emot en snkning. Drivkrafterna bakom den lga inflationen, den snabba produktivitetstillvxten och den lga importerade inflationen, r utbudsfaktorer som i sig verkar stimulerande p tillvxten. Tillvxten r redan hg och verstiger vad som bedms vara lngsiktigt hllbart. Penningpolitiken r dessutom expansiv i dagslget, vilket bl.a. bidrar till att hushllsupplningen och priserna p bostder stiger i snabb takt. Investeringarna i nringslivet vnde ocks tydligt uppt i fjol och vi rknar med en fortsatt kning i hygglig takt under resten av prognosperioden. Mot den bakgrunden har jag gjort och gr ven i dagslget bedmningen att efterfrgan inte behver stimuleras ytterligare med penningpolitiken. Samtidigt frtjnar det som alltid att understrykas att denna bedmning gller idag och under de frutsttningar som nu rder. Om vi exempelvis skulle se en tydligt svagare konjunktur skulle bedmningen kunna bli en annan, avslutade Rosenberg.
