Title: Inflation lower than expected
text: Rosenberg: Inflation lower than expected Date 2004-03-24 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke at SBAB's annual general meeting about household debt and price developments in the housing market. She also commented on the economic situation and monetary policy Households' debt situation "Household debt has increased at a steady pace in recent years despite stock market swings and a weak economy. At the same time, single-family house prices have continued to rise, albeit there are significant regional differences. The discussion about Swedish household indebtedness has been fuelled by developments in many other countries, for example in the UK, the US and Australia, where debt build-up has increased significantly more than here. This has raised the question of whether development is sustainable or whether there is a risk that households will go into too much debt and that property price bubbles will build up in different countries. The Riksbank constantly monitors households' ability to pay in order to assess the stability of the financial system. Swedish household debt as a share of disposable income is certainly approaching the levels that prevailed before the financial crisis in the early 1990s. But the low interest rates mean that household interest costs as a share of income have largely halved since then and are now at a historically low level," Rosenberg noted. "The development of single-family house prices also seems to be reasonably explained by fundamental factors such as interest rates, incomes and new construction in relation to developments in housing demand. This speaks against there being any single-family house price bubble under way, at least at national level. At present, we do not see any major problems for the household sector as a whole to meet its commitments. We also see no problems for the banks and the stability of the financial system. However, this does not prevent problems for individual households from arising when interest rates start to rise sooner or later. At today's low interest rates, it is therefore especially important for borrowers to include this in their calculations and carefully consider how much debt they can handle," Rosenberg said. "Of course, household indebtedness also plays a role in monetary policy decisions to the extent that it has an impact on the inflation assessment. With rising debt-to-GDP ratios, households' sensitivity to interest rate changes is also increasing. This effect will be stronger the greater the proportion of borrowings at variable interest rates. But the purpose of policy rate changes is precisely to affect interest rate-sensitive demand, and therefore these are factors that are included in our analyses and that come into account in our consumption forecasts, among other things," Rosenberg noted. Economic situation and monetary policy "In essence, recent statistics have confirmed the external development we saw ahead of us in December. But in some countries and regions, the upturn seems to be a little faster than expected. This is particularly true of developments in the United States, but also in Asia, Eastern and Central Europe and Latin America. Growth has also surprised positively in the UK and Norway, both of which are important export countries for Sweden. However growth in the euro area is sluggish and it looks set to be somewhat weaker going forward than we expected in December. International price pressures on processed goods are low. At the same time, the rise in the price of raw materials is very sharp. The rapid growth in China is likely to be a major contributor to this," according to Rosenberg. "In Sweden, too, the economic upturn is now strengthening, broadly in line with the December forecast. However, the composition of growth looks to have been slightly different from what we thought in December. The upturn in investment has been further delayed, but this has been offset by slightly stronger private consumption and exports. There is reason to expect slightly higher exports in the coming year than in the previous inflation report. A slightly stronger development in disposable income, lower interest rates and rising asset prices also mean that there is reason to be a little more optimistic about future consumption growth. At the same time, it is worth recalling that there seem to be a lot of free resources in the initial situation. Even if the economy strengthens as expected, there will also be spare resources for most of the forecast period," Rosenberg said. "The labour market has developed weaker than we expected in the December forecast. This probably means that wage cost increases may be slightly lower than expected in December. The wage agreements that have just been concluded in the field of industry and trade are in line with this. Productivity has also developed relatively strongly. Although we believe that the upturn in productivity can to some extent be explained by cyclical developments, there also seem to be more lasting elements. One interpretation is that this may partly be related to the fact that previous investments in new technology are starting to yield results outside the IT and telecommunications sectors as well. It is therefore likely that productivity can increase a little faster even in the next few years. Unit labour costs may therefore be slightly lower. We partially took that into account in February, but since then the picture has become clearer and reinforced," according to Rosenberg. "The fact that inflation is now so low is largely due to the fact that, as expected, electricity prices have fallen sharply. But inflation has developed weaker in recent months than we predicted in December. This is due to several factors. Imported inflation has become weaker than expected, partly in the wake of the krona's strengthening in recent years, but also as a result of continued low international price pressures. Domestic prices have also risen less than expected. This is probably partly due to the fact that wage costs have increased a little more slowly and that productivity growth has become higher than previously assumed. Lower cost pressures, both internationally and domestically, are expected to continue to contribute to a more subdued increase in inflation compared with the assessment in February. This means that inflation will be significantly below target in both one and two years' time. In light of this, I see room for a clearly more expansionary monetary policy," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Inflationen lgre n vntat Datum 2004-03-24 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade p SBAB:s bolagsstmma om hushllens skuldsttning och prisutvecklingen p bostadsmarknaden. Hon kommenterade ocks det ekonomiska lget och penningpolitiken Hushllens skuldsituation "Hushllens skulder har kat i stadig takt de senaste ren trots brssvngningar och svag konjunktur. Samtidigt har smhuspriserna fortsatt att stiga, lt vara att det finns betydande regionala skillnader. Diskussionen om de svenska hushllens skuldsttning har ftt nring av utvecklingen i mnga andra lnder t.ex. i Storbritannien, USA och i Australien dr skulduppbyggnaden kat betydligt mer n hr. Detta har vckt frgan om utvecklingen r hllbar eller om det finns risk att hushllen skuldstter sig fr mycket och att det byggs upp fastighetsprisbubblor i olika lnder. Riksbanken fljer stndigt hushllens betalningsfrmga fr att kunna bedma stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet. De svenska hushllens skulder som andel av de disponibla inkomsterna nrmar sig visserligen de niver som rdde infr finanskrisen i brjan av 1990-talet. Men de lga rntorna innebr att hushllens rntekostnader som andel av inkomsten i stort sett har halverats sedan dess och nu ligger p en historiskt lg niv", konstaterade Rosenberg. "Utvecklingen av smhuspriserna ser ocks ut att hyggligt kunna frklaras med fundamentala faktorer som rntor, inkomster och nyproduktion i relation till utvecklingen i bostadsefterfrgan. Det talar emot att det skulle vara ngon smhusprisbubbla under uppsegling, i varje fall p nationell niv. I dagslget ser vi inga strre problem fr hushllssektorn som helhet att klara av sina taganden. Vi ser heller inga problem fr bankerna och stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet. Det hindrar dock inte att det kan uppst problem fr enskilda hushll nr rntan frr eller senare brjar stiga. Vid dagens lga rntor r det drfr srskilt viktigt fr lntagarna att ta med detta i sina kalkyler och noga vervga hur stor skuldsttning man klarar av", sade Rosenberg. "Hushllens skuldsttning har givetvis ocks betydelse fr de penningpolitiska besluten i den mn den inverkar p inflationsbedmningen. Med stigande skuldkvot kar ocks hushllens knslighet fr rntefrndringar. Den effekten blir starkare ju strre andel av upplningen som sker till rrlig rnta. Men syftet med styrrntefrndringar r just att pverka den rnteknsliga efterfrgan och drfr r det hr faktorer som finns med i vra analyser och som kommer in bl.a. i vra konsumtionsprognoser", konstaterade Rosenberg. Det ekonomiska lget och penningpolitiken "I allt vsentligt har den senaste tidens statistik bekrftat den omvrldsutveckling vi sg framfr oss i december. Men i ngra lnder och regioner tycks uppgngen g lite snabbare n vntat. Det gller srskilt utvecklingen i USA men ocks i Asien, st- och Centraleuropa och i Latinamerika. ven i Storbritannien och Norge, som bda r viktiga exportlnder fr Sverige, har tillvxten verraskat positivt. Dremot gr tillvxten i euroomrdet trgt och den ser ut att bli ngot svagare framver n vad vi rknade med i december. Det internationella pristrycket p bearbetade varor r lgt. Samtidigt r prisuppgngen p rvaror mycket kraftig. Den snabba tillvxten i Kina r sannolikt en viktig bidragande orsak till detta", enligt Rosenberg. "ven i Sverige frstrks nu konjunkturuppgngen, i stort sett i linje med decemberprognosen. Tillvxtens sammansttning ser dock ut att ha varit ngot annorlunda n vad vi trodde i december. Uppgngen i investeringarna har frdrjts ytterligare men detta har motverkats av en ngot starkare privat konsumtion och export. Det finns anledning att rkna med en ngot hgre export under det nrmaste ret n i den frra inflationsrapporten. En ngot starkare utveckling av disponibelinkomsterna, lgre rntor och stigande tillgngspriser medfr ocks att det finns anledning att vara lite mer optimistisk om den framtida konsumtionstillvxten. Samtidigt r det vrt att pminna om att det frefaller finnas en hel del lediga resurser i utgngslget. ven om konjunkturen strks som frvntat kommer det ocks under strre delen av prognosperioden att finnas lediga resurser", sade Rosenberg. "Arbetsmarknaden har utvecklats svagare n vad vi rknade med i decemberprognosen. Det innebr troligen att lnekostnadskningarna kan bli ngot lgre n frvntat i december. De lneavtal som just slutits p industrins och handelns omrde r i linje med detta. Produktiviteten har ocks utvecklats frhllandevis starkt. ven om vi tror att uppgngen i produktiviteten till viss del kan frklaras av konjunkturutvecklingen tycks det ocks finnas mer varaktiga inslag. En tolkning r att detta delvis kan sammanhnga med att tidigare investeringar i ny teknologi brjar ge resultat ven utanfr IT- och telekommunikationssektorerna. Det r drfr troligt att produktiviteten kan ka lite snabbare ven de nrmaste ren. Enhetsarbetskostnaderna kan drfr komma att bli ytterligare ngot lgre. Det tog vi delvis hnsyn till i februari men sedan dess har bilden blivit tydligare och frstrkts", enligt Rosenberg. "Att inflationen nu r s lg beror till stor del p att elpriserna som vntat gtt ned kraftigt. Men inflationen har utvecklats svagare de senaste mnaderna n vad vi frutsg i december. Detta beror p flera faktorer. Den importerade inflationen har blivit svagare n vntat bl.a. i spren av kronans frstrkning de senaste ren men ocks till fljd av ett fortsatt lgt internationellt pristryck. De inhemska priserna har ocks stigit mindre n vntat. Det beror sannolikt delvis p att lnekostnaderna har kat lite lngsammare och p att produktivitetstillvxten blivit hgre n tidigare antagits. Ett lgre kostnadstryck, svl internationellt som inhemskt, bedms ven framver bidra till att inflationsuppgngen blir mer dmpad jmfrt med bedmningen i februari. Det hr innebr att inflationen kommer att ligga ptagligt under mlet bde p ett och tv rs sikt. Mot bakgrund av detta ser jag utrymme fr en tydligt mer expansiv penningpolitik", avslutade Rosenberg. Title: The inflation target and CPI
text: Rosenberg: Inflation target and CPI Date: 2004-04-04 Speaker: Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg Location: KPI Board's 50th anniversary, Norra Latin The speech in its entirety Let me begin by thanking you for the invitation to this anniversary seminar. I have previously participated in the KPI board for a period of time, so I have some insight into the issues that the board has wrestled with over the years. Today, as is well known, my role is different and it is from it, as monetary policymakers, that I today intended to contribute with some reflections on the CPI's role as a target variable for monetary policy. In January 1993, a few months after the Riksbank had been forced to give up defending the fixed exchange rate, a monetary policy strategy was introduced that was rather untested, not only in Sweden but also internationally: monetary policy was to be geared towards achieving a quantified target for inflation. The rate of price increase would stabilise at 2% per annum with a tolerance range of 1 percentage point. From the outset, the target was specified in terms of the rate of increase in the CPI, although other measures were also included in the discussion. There were several reasons why the KPI was chosen as the target variable. What perhaps weighed most heavily was that the CPI with its long history is the most famous measure of price development in Sweden. This was considered particularly important in a context of rapid public confidence in the new monetary policy regime. It was also considered reasonable to try to stabilise the value of money in terms of a "basket of goods" that is of great importance to the average citizen. Additional advantages that are usually highlighted are that CPI is published regularly and relatively frequently and that CPI inflation is not normally revised. When you look back at the more than ten years that have passed since the inflation targeting policy was introduced, you can see that the CPI has worked relatively well as a target variable. When the target was introduced, there were probably many who regarded it as unrealistic. But inflation has averaged close to 2 percent over these years. The credibility of the target is also high today, judging by the inflation expectations of households and other actors. I do not think it is an exaggeration to say that with the new policy with a target for the CPI growth rate as anchors, combined with the successful consolidation of public finances, we have essentially succeeded in achieving what we hoped for. Sweden has gone from being a high-inflation economy, characterized by recurring cost crises and unstable economic development, to becoming an economy with low and relatively stable price and wage increases, where the risk of periods of overheating and subsequent recessions has been significantly reduced. The journey has not been entirely problem-free and the experiences we have had along the way have forced us to make some changes in practical policy, or perhaps rather in terms of how policy is communicated to the public. We have also needed to change and improve our analysis of inflation in various respects. I was going to say something here today about the problems we've encountered along the way and how we've tried to deal with them. Clear communication is important What problems in defining the inflation target in terms of the change in CPI have we encountered? To illustrate this, I first need to say something about the principles that form the basis for the Riksbank's interest rate setting decision. The Riksbank, like other central banks working with inflation targets, has taken as its starting point that monetary policy affects inflation developments with a certain delay; it is usually expected that they will take one to two years before a change in interest rates has a full impact on inflation. Against this background, and as part of clarifying how we are trying to achieve our goal, we have formulated a simple rule of action for policy: if the inflation forecast exceeds 2 percent in one to two years' time, the repo rate should normally be raised and if the forecast is below 2 percent, the repo rate should normally be lowered. In a slightly different wording, but where the spirit is much the same, the rule means that monetary policy should normally be aimed at achieving the inflation target of 2 percent CPI inflation over one to two years' time. The fact that we use the inflation forecast primarily over one to two years as a kind of intermediate target for the actual target of actual inflation being 2% means that temporary disturbances that affect inflation in the next year alone do not usually affect interest rates. It is conceivable that with drastic changes in interest rates it would be possible to return inflation to the target faster than in one to two years' time. But the consequences of such a policy would probably be large, undesirable fluctuations in both the real and financial economies. Against this background, it could be said that we normally deliberately allow the target deviations resulting from temporary disturbances to inflation that arise and subside over the next year. Sometimes, however, there are temporary effects on inflation that do not have time to subside in the coming year. These effects will then be visible in the inflation forecast, measured by the CPI, over one to two years' time. However, if the effects are expected to dissipate fairly soon thereafter, there may be reasons to refrain from counteracting them with scratch rate changes. In other words, in some situations there is reason to deviate from the rule that the repo rate should be changed if the forecast for CPI inflation deviates from the 2 percent target over one to two years. In such situations, great demands are placed on us to communicate that we intend to deviate from the ordinary rule of action and pedagogically explain the underlying motives. One way in which the Riksbank has chosen to handle the issue is to highlight "cleared" inflation measures at different times, as indicators of longer-term inflation developments. I was going to illustrate this here with a few examples. The first example concerns the period of monetary easing and a sharp decline in general interest rates in the second half of the 1990s. Between autumn 1995 and spring 1999, the repo rate was reduced from just under 9 per cent to below 3 per cent. At the same time, long-term interest rates also fell sharply. The repo rate cuts were aimed at stimulating the economy via the traditional demand channels, thereby helping to raise CPI inflation, but these effects only came with some delay. The immediate effects on the CPI of the repo rate cuts and the decline in general interest rates went in the opposite direction, via falling interest costs for single-family homes. This meant that CPI inflation initially fell very sharply. The fact that the change in general interest rates was both large and protracted meant that the CPI was affected for a significantly longer period than one to two years. Since the low CPI inflation was largely a result of its own interest rate cuts and was therefore considered to be transitory, the Riksbank considered that there was no reason to counteract it with further easing of monetary policy. During this period, however, the Riksbank was often asked why the repo rate was not lowered even though inflation was below target, which showed that there was a need for a clearer explanation of the policy. As part of this, a new index was highlighted as an important measure of inflation, namely UND1X, which, among other things, excludes interest costs for single-family homes. In e.g. Inflation Report 1999:2 illustrates how UND1X was used to clarify the structure of monetary policy. When the repo rate on this occasion was left unchanged, the assessment that UND1X inflation would be close to 2% towards the end of the forecast period, while CPI inflation was expected to fall significantly below the inflation target. The monetary policy communication problems that arose in connection with the sharp interest rate cuts in the second half of the 1990s were also an important reason why the Riksbank published a clarification in 1999 on the structure of monetary policy and the application of the inflation target. (1) This clarification specified, inter alia, the occasions on which there may be reason to deviate from the simple rule of action that monetary policy should be geared towards achieving the target of 2% CPI inflation over one to two years' time. My discussion today is based on exactly the same reasoning as in that clarification. The second example is taken from spring 2001. Increases in food and energy prices due to foot-and-mouth disease and mad cow disease, as well as supply disruptions in energy production, caused CPI inflation to rise sharply. The price increases were considered temporary and the Riksbank therefore chose not to raise the repo rate. Since price increases were projected to fall out of CPI inflation relatively quickly, in this case no deviation from the simple rule of action for monetary policy needed to be made. However, there was a need to clearly illustrate in the external communication the assessment that it was mainly price increases of a temporary nature that were the reason why CPI inflation was so high above target. For this purpose, the Inflation Report 2001:2 therefore presented a measure of inflation that was adjusted for the price increases that were deemed temporary. At that time, no forecast was presented for the cleared measure. The third and most closely related example is when the Riksbank last year chose to highlight UND1X excluding energy as a particularly important index for assessing the more lasting inflationary pressures. Energy prices had risen sharply around the turn of the year 2002/2003. We assessed that this upturn was temporary and that energy prices would fall back again. This meant that inflation rates would be affected for quite a long period by these temporary fluctuations in energy prices. At its monetary policy meeting in April 2003, the Riksbank estimated that inflation would fall slightly below its inflation target towards the end of its forecast period if the repo rate were kept unchanged. If the simple rule had been strictly applied, the repo rate would have been lowered, but since temporary fluctuations in energy prices were the main reason why the inflation forecast ended up below 2 percent, the Riksbank chose to leave the repo rate unchanged. In order to make it clear that the Riksbank did not want to bring inflation back to its target within the normal two-year horizon, the Riksbank chose in that situation to highlight a measure of inflation that was not so strongly affected by fluctuations in energy prices. How has the strategy worked? How, then, has this strategy worked, i.e. to highlight indices other than CPI at different times as a way of illustrating that there may sometimes be reasons to deviate from the rule that CPI inflation should be 2 percent in one to two years' time? In retrospect, it can be stated that although we have tried to be clear in our communication, we do not seem to have reached all the way in all respects. Admittedly, the strategy appears to have been successful in that we have not been asked very often, especially in recent years, why the repo rate has not changed even though the inflation forecast has fallen above or below target. On the other hand, the interpretation has sometimes, and especially for a couple of months in the autumn of 2003, been that the Riksbank "changed its target variable". However, that hasn't really been the case; the inflation target is and has always been defined in terms of the rate of increase in the CPI, although we have often made it clear that policy in the current time perspective has been based more on some other index, mainly UND1X. Let me go back to last year's discussion on energy prices to illustrate what I think may be one of the problems. As I mentioned, the repo rate was not lowered in April 2003, although forecasts indicated that CPI inflation would fall short of the two-year target. The reason was that the forecast for CPI inflation was pushed down by energy price effects that were judged to be temporary and expected to fade just beyond the forecast horizon. By contrast, the measure that was better considered to reflect longer-term cyclical inflation, UND1X excluding energy, was considered to be in line with the inflation target at the end of the projection horizon. An interpretation that is perhaps close at hand, and which obviously many did, was that although the Riksbank has not departed from its rule of action that interest rates should be changed if inflation deviates from the target, the target variable itself has changed. Since the new presumed target variable was in line with the inflation target, there was no reason to change the interest rate. However, our intention was rather the opposite, i.e. to point out, by highlighting UND1X excluding energy, that fluctuations in CPI inflation were largely driven by temporary fluctuations in energy prices, even a bit beyond the normal two-year horizon, and that this was therefore a time when there were reasons to deviate from the rule. It is possible that at such times it would be useful to show, as a complement, the expected CPI inflation in a time perspective that is long enough for all temporary effects to fully subside. It then becomes clearer that the analysis of inflation developments in terms of various purged measures is done for educational reasons. The risk of interpretations that we "changed the target variable" should thus be avoided. Such an approach would also be well in line with the clarification from 1999, which states that the Riksbank should clarify in advance how much deviation from the inflation target defined in terms of CPI can be justified in one to two years' time. One could clearly illustrate both the size of the target deviation over the normal forecast horizon and the fact that inflation is expected to be back on target not too long thereafter. Let me illustrate the line of thought with a picture. Suppose something happens that causes the inflation rate after 1.5 years to rise from 2 to 3 percent. The disturbance is believed to be such that, after it occurs, it affects inflation for only one year. An example of a disruption with such a time profile is an expected VAT increase, which raises the price level permanently but only affects the twelve-month change in the CPI one year in the future. Another example is an increase in some excise duty, such as the tobacco tax. With a forecast covering only the first two years, it would not appear that inflation will eventually be back in line with the target. If the forecast horizon is instead extended slightly, so that both the ups and downs in inflation are evident, it will be more clear that the Riksbank makes the assessment that the disruption will not have a lasting effect on inflation. Against this background, there could therefore be a case for presenting forecasts, where appropriate, also in a slightly longer perspective in order to illustrate how we view these temporary effects. An advantage of this procedure would be that the monetary policy discussion could thereby focus more clearly on the target variable CPI. In summary, I think it can be stated that the CPI has worked well in the new role it was given just over 10 years ago - as a target variable for monetary policy. To the extent that problems have arisen, there have been relatively limited educational complications in those situations when the Riksbank has made the assessment that it is appropriate to depart from the simple rule of action for how interest rates are usually set. My assessment is that these problems are no more serious than that they can be dealt with by the Riksbank sticking to its ambition to constantly strive to make monetary policy as clear as possible. Footnote: 1) See Heikensten, L, "The Riksbank's inflation target - clarifications and evaluation", Monetary and exchange rate policy No. 1, 1999
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Inflationsmlet och KPI Datum: 2004-04-04 Talare: Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg Plats: KPI-nmndens 50-rsjubileum, Norra Latin Talet i sin helhet Lt mig brja med att tacka fr inbjudan till detta jubileumsseminarium. Jag har tidigare under en period deltagit i KPI-nmnden, s jag har en viss inblick i de frgor som nmnden har brottats med genom ren. Idag r min roll som bekant en annan och det r utifrn den, som penningpolitisk beslutsfattare, som jag idag tnkte bidra med ngra reflektioner kring KPI:s roll som mlvariabel fr penningpolitiken. I januari 1993, ngra mnader efter att Riksbanken hade tvingats ge upp frsvaret av den fasta vxelkursen, introducerades en penningpolitisk strategi som var tmligen oprvad, inte bara i Sverige utan ocks internationellt: Penningpolitiken skulle inriktas p att uppn ett kvantifierat ml fr inflationen. Priskningstakten skulle stabiliseras p 2 procent per r med ett toleransintervall p 1 procentenhet. Redan frn brjan specificerades mlet i termer av kningstakten i KPI, ven om ocks andra mtt fanns med i diskussionen. Det fanns flera skl till att KPI valdes som mlvariabel. Det som kanske vgde tyngst var att KPI med sin lnga historia r det mest knda mttet p prisutvecklingen i Sverige. Detta bedmdes vara srskilt viktigt i ett lge dr man snabbt ville skapa ett frtroende hos allmnheten fr den nya penningpolitiska regimen. Det bedmdes ocks rimligt att frska stabilisera penningvrdet i termer av en "varukorg" som har stor betydelse fr den genomsnittlige medborgaren. Ytterligare frdelar som brukar framhllas r att KPI publiceras regelbundet och frhllandevis ofta samt att KPI-inflationen normalt inte revideras. Nr man blickar tillbaka p de drygt tio r som har gtt sedan inflationsmlspolitiken introducerades kan man konstatera att KPI fungerat frhllandevis vl som mlvariabel. Nr mlet infrdes fanns det nog mnga som betraktade det som orealistiskt. Men inflationen har under de hr ren i genomsnitt varit nra 2 procent. Trovrdigheten fr mlet r ocks idag hg att dma av hushllens och andra aktrers inflationsfrvntningar. Jag tycker inte att det r ngon verdrift att sga att vi med den nya politiken med ett ml fr KPI-kningstakten som ankare, i kombination med en framgngsrik konsolidering av statsfinanserna, i allt vsentligt lyckats stadkomma vad vi hoppades p. Sverige har gtt frn att ha varit en hginflationsekonomi, som knnetecknades av terkommande kostnadskriser och en instabil ekonomisk utveckling, till att bli en ekonomi med lga och frhllandevis stabila pris- och lnekningar, dr risken fr perioder av verhettning och efterfljande recessioner har reducerats betydligt. Resan har inte varit helt problemfri och de erfarenheter vi gjort under vgen har tvingat oss till vissa frndringar i den praktiska politiken, eller kanske snarare nr det gller hur politiken kommuniceras till allmnheten. Vi har ocks behvt frndra och frbttra vr analys av inflationen i olika avseenden. Jag tnkte hr idag sga ngot om vilka problem vi har sttt p under resans gng och hur vi har frskt att hantera dem. Viktigt med tydlig kommunikation Vilka problem med att definiera inflationsmlet i termer av frndringen i KPI har vi d sttt p? Fr att illustrera detta behver jag frst sga ngot om de principer som ligger till grund fr Riksbankens rntesttningsbeslut. Riksbanken har, liksom andra centralbanker som arbetar med inflationsml, tagit som utgngspunkt att penningpolitiken pverkar inflationsutvecklingen med en viss frdrjning; man brukar rkna med att de tar ett till tv r innan en rntendring ftt fullt genomslag p inflationen. Mot denna bakgrund, och som ett led i att tydliggra hur vi frsker uppn vrt ml, har vi formulerat en enkel handlingsregel fr politiken: om inflationsprognosen p ett till tv rs sikt verstiger 2 procent ska reporntan normalt hjas och om prognosen understiger 2 procent ska reporntan normalt snkas. Med en ngot annorlunda formulering, men dr andemeningen r ungefr densamma, innebr regeln att penningpolitiken normalt ska inriktas p att uppn inflationsmlet om 2 procents KPI-inflation p ett till tv rs sikt. Att vi anvnder inflationsprognosen p i frsta hand ett till tv rs sikt som ett slags mellanliggande ml fr det egentliga mlet att den faktiska inflationen ska vara 2 procent innebr att tillflliga strningar som pverkar inflationen enbart under det nrmaste ret i regel inte pverkar rntesttningen. Det r tnkbart att det med drastiska rntefrndringar skulle vara mjligt att terfra inflationen till mlet snabbare n p ett till tv rs sikt. Men konsekvenserna av en sdan politik skulle antagligen bli stora, onskade fluktuationer i svl den reala som den finansiella ekonomin. Mot den hr bakgrunden skulle man kunna sga att vi normalt sett medvetet tillter de mlavvikelser som r ett resultat av tillflliga strningar till inflationen som uppkommer och klingar av under det nrmaste ret. Ibland uppstr emellertid tillflliga effekter p inflationen som inte hinner klinga av under det nrmaste ret. Dessa effekter blir d synliga i inflationsprognosen, mtt med KPI, p ett till tv rs sikt. Men om effekterna frvntas frsvinna ganska snart drefter kan det finnas skl att avst frn att motverka dem med reporntefrndringar. Med andra ord finns det i vissa lgen anledning att avvika frn regeln att reporntan ska ndras om prognosen fr KPI-inflationen avviker frn 2-procentsmlet p ett till tv rs sikt. I sdana situationer stlls stora krav p att vi kommunicerar att vi avser att avvika frn ordinarie handlingsregel och pedagogiskt frklarar de bakomliggande motiven. Ett stt p vilket Riksbanken valt att hantera frgan r att vid olika tidpunkter lyfta fram "rensade" inflationsmtt, som indikatorer p den mer lngsiktiga inflationsutvecklingen. Jag tnkte hr illustrera detta med ngra exempel. Det frsta exemplet gller perioden med penningpolitiska lttnader och kraftig nedgng i det allmnna rntelget under andra hlften av 1990-talet. Mellan hsten 1995 och vren 1999 snktes reporntan frn knappt 9 procent till under 3 procent. Samtidigt fll ven de lnga rntorna kraftigt. Reporntesnkningarna syftade till att stimulera ekonomin via de traditionella efterfrgekanalerna fr att drigenom bidra till att hja KPI-inflationen, men dessa effekter kom frst med viss frdrjning. De omedelbara effekterna p KPI av snkningarna av reporntan och nedgngen i det allmnna rntelget gick i motsatt riktning, via sjunkande rntekostnader fr egnahem. Detta innebar att KPI-inflationen till en brjan fll mycket kraftigt. Det faktum att frndringen i det allmnna rntelget var bde stor och utdragen innebar att KPI pverkades under en betydligt lngre tid n ett till tv r. Eftersom den lga KPI-inflationen till stor del var ett resultat av de egna rntesnkningarna och drfr bedmdes vara vergende, ansg Riksbanken att det inte fanns skl att motverka den med ytterligare lttnader i penningpolitiken. Under denna period fick Riksbanken emellertid ofta frgor om varfr reporntan inte snktes trots att inflationen lg under mlet, vilket visade att det fanns ett behov av en tydligare frklaring av politiken. Som ett led i detta lyftes ett nytt index fram som ett viktigt inflationsmtt, nmligen UND1X, som bl.a. exkluderar rntekostnader fr egnahem. I t.ex. Inflationsrapport 1999:2 illustreras hur UND1X anvndes fr att tydliggra penningpolitikens upplggning. Nr reporntan vid detta tillflle lmnades ofrndrad gjordes bedmningen att UND1X-inflationen skulle ligga nra 2 procent mot slutet av prognosperioden medan KPI-inflationen frvntades hamna vsentligt lgre n inflationsmlet. De penningpolitiska kommunikationsproblem som uppstod i samband med de kraftiga rntesnkningarna under andra hlften av 1990-talet var ocks ett viktigt skl till att Riksbanken 1999 publicerade ett frtydligande om penningpolitikens upplggning och tillmpningen av inflationsmlet.(1) I detta frtydligande preciserades bl.a. vid vilka tillfllen det kan finnas anledning att avvika frn den enkla handlingsregeln att penningpolitiken ska inriktas p att uppn mlet om 2 procents KPI-inflation p ett till tv rs sikt. Min diskussion idag bygger p precis samma resonemang som i det frtydligandet. Det andra exemplet r hmtat frn vren 2001. Hjda livsmedels- och energipriser till fljd av mul- och klvsjukan och galna kosjukan samt utbudsstrningar i energiproduktionen medfrde d att KPI-inflationen steg kraftigt. Priskningarna bedmdes vara temporra och Riksbanken valde drfr att inte hja reporntan. Eftersom priskningarna relativt snabbt berknades falla ur KPI-inflationen behvde i detta fall inget avsteg gras frn den enkla handlingsregeln fr penningpolitiken. Det fanns dock ett behov att i den externa kommunikationen tydligt illustrera bedmningen att det i huvudsak var priskningar av tillfllig karaktr som var sklet till att KPI-inflationen lg s hgt ver mlet. Fr detta syfte redovisades i Inflationsrapport 2001:2 drfr ett mtt p inflationen som var rensat fr de priskningar som bedmdes vara tillflliga. Vid det tillfllet presenterades inte ngon prognos fr det rensade mttet. Det tredje och i tiden mest nrliggande exemplet r nr Riksbanken under fjolret valde att lyfta fram UND1X exklusive energi som ett srskilt viktigt index fr bedmningen av det mer varaktiga inflationstrycket. Energipriserna hade stigit kraftigt runt rsskiftet 2002/2003. Vi bedmde att denna uppgng var tillfllig och att energipriserna skulle falla tillbaka igen. Detta innebar att inflationstakten skulle komma att pverkas under en ganska lng period av dessa tillflliga svngningar i energipriserna. Vid det penningpolitiska mtet i april 2003 gjorde Riksbanken bedmningen att inflationen mot slutet av prognosperioden skulle hamna ngot under inflationsmlet om reporntan hlls ofrndrad. Om den enkla regeln hade tillmpats strikt skulle reporntan ha snkts, men eftersom tillflliga fluktuationer i energipriserna var det frmsta sklet till att inflationsprognosen hamnade under 2 procent valde Riksbanken att lta reporntan vara ofrndrad. Fr att tydliggra att Riksbanken inte ville fra inflationen tillbaka till mlet inom den normala tvrshorisonten valde Riksbanken i det lget att lyfta fram ett inflationsmtt som inte var s starkt pverkat av fluktuationerna i energipriserna. Hur har strategin fungerat? Hur har d denna strategi fungerat, dvs. att vid olika tidpunkter lyfta fram andra index n KPI som ett stt att illustrera att det ibland kan finnas skl att frng regeln att KPI-inflationen ska vara 2 procent p ett till tv rs sikt? Man kan i efterhand konstatera att trots att vi frskt vara tydliga i vr kommunikation s tycks vi inte i alla stycken ha ntt nda fram. Strategin frefaller visserligen ha varit framgngsrik stillvida att vi inte srskilt ofta, i synnerhet inte under de senaste ren, ftt frgan varfr reporntan inte har ndrats trots att inflationsprognosen hamnat ver eller under mlet. Dremot har tolkningen ibland, och i synnerhet under ett par mnader under hsten 2003, varit att Riksbanken "bytt mlvariabel". S har dock egentligen inte varit fallet; inflationsmlet r och har alltid varit definierat i termer av kningstakten i KPI, ven om vi ofta gjort klart att politiken i det aktuella tidsperspektivet utgtt mer frn ngot annat index, frmst UND1X. Lt mig g tillbaka till fjolrets diskussion om energipriserna fr att illustrera vad jag tror kan vara ett av problemen. Som jag nmnde snktes reporntan inte i april 2003 trots att prognoserna pekade p att KPI-inflationen skulle komma att underskrida mlet p tv rs sikt. Sklet var att prognosen fr KPI-inflationen pressades ner av energipriseffekter som bedmdes vara tillflliga och vntades klinga av strax bortom prognoshorisonten. Det mtt som bttre ansgs avspegla den mer lngsiktiga konjunkturrelaterade inflationen, UND1X exklusive energi, bedmdes dremot vara i linje med inflationsmlet i slutet av prognosperioden. En tolkning som kanske ligger nra till hands, och som uppenbarligen mnga gjorde, var att Riksbanken visserligen inte frngtt sin handlingsregel om att rntan ska ndras om inflationen avviker frn mlet, men att mlvariabeln i sig ndrats. Eftersom den nya frmodade mlvariabeln var i linje med inflationsmlet fanns ju ingen anledning att ndra rntan. Vr avsikt var dock snarast den motsatta, dvs. att genom att lyfta fram UND1X exklusive energi peka p att fluktuationerna i KPI-inflationen i hg grad drevs av tillflliga variationer i energipriserna, ven en bit bortom den normala tvrshorisonten, och att detta drfr var ett tillflle d det fanns skl att avvika frn regeln. Det r mjligt att det vid sdana hr tillfllen skulle vara bra att som komplement visa den vntade KPI-inflationen i ett tidsperspektiv som r tillrckligt lngt fr att samtliga tillflliga effekter fullt ut ska hinna klinga av. Det blir d tydligare att analysen av inflationsutvecklingen i termer av olika rensade mtt grs av pedagogiska skl. Risken fr tolkningar att vi "bytt mlvariabel" br drigenom kunna undvikas. Ett sdant angreppsstt skulle ocks vara vl i linje med frtydligandet frn 1999 som sger att Riksbanken i frvg ska klargra hur stor avvikelse frn inflationsmlet definierat i termer av KPI som kan vara motiverad p ett till tv rs sikt. Man skulle ju tydligt kunna illustrera svl storleken p mlavvikelsen under den normala prognoshorisonten som det faktum att inflationen vntas vara tillbaka p mlet inte alltfr lng tid drefter. Lt mig skdliggra tankegngen med en bild. Anta att ngot intrffar som gr att inflationstakten efter 1,5 r berknas komma att stiga frn 2 till 3 procent. Strningen antas vara sdan att den, efter det att den intrffat, pverkar inflationen under endast ett r. Ett exempel p en strning med en sdan tidsprofil r en vntad momshjning, som hjer prisnivn varaktigt men bara pverkar tolvmnadersfrndringen av KPI ett r framt i tiden. Ett annat exempel r en hjning av ngon punktskatt, t.ex. tobaksskatten. Med en prognos som omfattar enbart de frsta tv ren skulle det inte framg att inflationen s smningom ter kommer att vara i linje med mlet. Om prognoshorisonten istllet frlngs ngot, s att bde upp- och nedgngen i inflationen framgr, blir det mer tydligt att Riksbanken gr bedmningen att strningen inte fr ngon varaktig effekt p inflationen. Mot den hr bakgrunden skulle det allts kunna finnas skl att nr s r lmpligt redovisa prognoser ocks i ett lite lngre perspektiv fr att p s vis skdliggra hur vi ser p dessa tillflliga effekter. En frdel med detta frfarande skulle vara att den penningpolitiska diskussionen drigenom p ett tydligare stt kunde fokusera p mlvariabeln KPI. Sammanfattningsvis tycker jag att man kan konstatera att KPI fungerat vl i den nya roll som det fick fr drygt 10 r sedan - som mlvariabel fr penningpolitiken. I den mn problem har uppsttt har det handlat om frhllandevis begrnsade pedagogiska komplikationer i de lgen nr Riksbanken gjort bedmningen att det r lmpligt att frng den enkla handlingsregeln fr hur rntan vanligen stts. Min bedmning r att dessa problem inte r allvarligare n att de kan hanteras genom att Riksbanken hller fast vid ambitionen att hela tiden strva efter att gra penningpolitiken s tydlig som mjligt. Title: Some questions about monetary policy
text: Rosenberg: Some questions about monetary policy Date 2006-03-16 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg gave the opening speech on Thursday at the Association of Swedish Sawmillmen's annual meeting in Stockholm. The theme of the speech was the current monetary policy. "After our recent decisions in January and February to raise the repo rate by a total of 0.5 percentage points, the debate on monetary policy has continued. It is quite natural when we raise the repo rate for the first time in several years. Today I would like to address three issues that seem to recur in the discussion of current monetary policy. I hope it can contribute to a better understanding of how we conduct monetary policy," Rosenberg began. "The first question is whether the Riksbank cares too much, or just, about inflation. How do we take into account general economic developments and, for example, developments in the labour market when deciding on changes to the repo rate? According to the law, the Riksbank has one goal and that is to keep inflation at a low and stable level - 'to maintain a fixed monetary value' as stated in the legal text. We are trying to achieve this by ensuring that the increase in the consumer price index is 2% per annum. As long as the credibility of the inflation target is not threatened, the Riksbank also has the opportunity to take into account how the real economy, such as production and employment, develops. In its main features, we have this strategy in common with many other central banks," Rosenberg noted. "Taking into account the real economy may mean that inflation is allowed to deviate from the target for a period of time. Of course, the deviations must not be as large as possible, and therefore the Riksbank has made it clear that b1 1 percentage point around the inflation target of 2 percent can normally be tolerated. Nor can we allow the anomalies to persist for too long. For this reason, the Riksbank follows the principle of normally ensuring that inflation returns to its target within two years when a deviation has occurred. This means that we have the opportunity to bring inflation back to the target gradually," Rosenberg continued. "A fundamental example of how this flexibility can be used is when the economy is subjected to a disruption that causes inflation to go in one direction and production and employment in the opposite direction. It could be a change in the price of raw materials or food or some other disruption on the so-called supply side of the economy. In such a situation, changing interest rates so much that inflation is in line with the target as soon as possible could have far too much impact on the real economy. Our approach with the principle that inflation should normally be in line with the two-year target gives us room to take into account the real economy and instead change interest rates gradually. The Riksbank has also pointed out that, exceptionally, in the event of major disruptions, it may be necessary to allow it to take longer than two years for inflation to return to target in order not to make the fluctuations in the economy unnecessarily large. All in all, such a way of working provides better conditions for us to have a stable development of production and employment and to be able to avoid large fluctuations," Rosenberg explained. "The second issue I would like to raise is the one that recurs most often in the discussion of current monetary policy. Why is the Riksbank raising interest rates now that inflation is low and the labour market has not yet started in earnest? What should be borne in mind is that the decisions we take must be based on forecasts of future developments. It takes time for the economy to fully adjust to a change in the repo rate and, as I mentioned earlier, our principle is to normally bring inflation back to target within two years. When we make decisions about the repo rate, we do so primarily to influence inflation over a couple of years' time. If we only assumed how inflation is expected to be in the very near future, interest rate policy would be far too jerky and have a negative impact on the real economy," Rosenberg continued. "The Riksbank's view of economic development going forward is presented in the Inflation Report published in connection with the interest rate decision in February. The statistics that have come in recently largely support that assessment. In the Inflation Report, we note that the Swedish economy is in the midst of an economic upturn. Growth is currently high and we anticipate that it will remain good. International demand for Swedish goods and services looks set to grow steadily going forward. Household consumption is expected to grow at a rapid pace and business investment is also expected to continue to rise. The labour market situation will gradually improve as the demand for labour increases. Resource utilisation and cost pressures will gradually increase. We therefore anticipate that inflation will also rise, which suggests that monetary policy needs to become less expansionary," Rosenberg continued. "I think this picture of the economic outlook also looks much the same with basically all forecasters, although some details obviously differ. Most forecasts indicate that the economic upturn will continue, inflationary pressures will increase and interest rates will need to be raised from today's very low level. What is debatable is the pace at which it should happen," Rosenberg noted. "Our forecasts in the Inflation Report were based on the assumption that the interest rate would be raised by another 0.25 percentage points in the first quarter and then continue upwards gradually over the next few years. With such a profile of interest rate developments, inflation was projected to be close to the two-year target, but it was also clear that inflation would be below target for much of the forecast period. While we in the Executive Board thought that this indicated that it should be possible to aim for a somewhat more expansionary monetary policy than that on which the forecast in the Inflation Report was based, but at the same time we agreed that there were factors that made an increase in interest rates in February the best option. Let me explain why," Rosenberg continued. "In recent years, inflation has been held down by weak import price developments and strong domestic productivity developments. Output has been able to grow rapidly without inflationary pressures rising. Inflation has thus been held down by favourable factors on the supply side of the economy, which have affected it for a longer period of time than the Riksbank and other forecasters predicted. I mentioned earlier that changes of this type can lead to difficult trade-offs about how quickly inflation should be brought back to the target, e.g. it can be difficult to know how lasting such factors are. In recent years, the Riksbank has lowered its repo rate to a record low level in order to bring inflation up to its target. It has stimulated the economy and contributed to the rapid growth. But there are risks in continuing to pursue a very expansionary monetary policy at a time when the economy is already growing so strongly," Rosenberg noted. "For example, the very low level of interest rates has contributed to the fact that house prices and lending to households - which have already increased rapidly over a succession of years - have continued to rise at a pace that is not sustainable in the long term. If this trend continues, we in the Executive Board think that there is a risk that a situation could build up where a sharp deceleration of house price development later on makes households feel that the debt burden will be too high and that they are therefore increasing their savings at a rapid pace. As a result, demand in the economy may falter sharply and inflation may also become too low. It strengthened us in our assessment that there were reasons to make monetary policy less expansionary in January and February," Rosenberg said. "That brings us to the third question: does this mean that monetary policy now has a goal for the development of house prices? I have worded the question a little pointedly, but what I am looking for is that it has sometimes been interpreted as concern about house prices and growing household debt that has been the main motive for the rate hikes. That is not the case, I can assure you. The main motive, as I mentioned earlier, is that we envision a development in which the economy will continue to rise and inflation will rise. So it is primarily the inflation outlook over a couple of years' time that is why we do not want to continue to stimulate the economy as strongly as we have done recently. That's why we've raised interest rates," Rosenberg pointed out. "As always, there are also various risks we consider when making our monetary policy decisions. In our trade-offs, the risks linked to house price developments and household indebtedness have been an argument for not pushing an increase forward for a few months. This does not mean that we have any particular target for how much house prices and borrowing should increase. Nor does it mean that monetary policy was guided by concerns that household borrowing would jeopardise the stability of the financial system. How the housing market develops is of course also important in this perspective, but the Riksbank sees no signs that house prices and debt would pose any threat to the banking system. Rather, it is the risks associated with future real stability that we have highlighted," Rosenberg continued. "The Riksbank has now raised its repo rate to 2 per cent. With inflation expectations between 1.5 and 2 percent, this means that the real interest rate is close to zero. Monetary policy is thus still very expansionary, something I think is often forgotten in the debate about our latest interest rate decisions," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Ngra frgor om penningpolitiken Datum 2006-03-16 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg hll under torsdagen inledningsanfrandet p Freningen Svenska Sgverksmns rsmte i Stockholm. Temat fr anfrandet var den aktuella penningpolitiken. "Efter vra senaste beslut i januari och februari att hja reporntan med sammanlagt 0,5 procentenheter har debatten om penningpolitiken fortsatt. Det r ganska naturligt nr vi fr frsta gngen p flera r hjer reporntan. Idag vill jag ta upp tre frgor som verkar terkomma i diskussionen om den aktuella penningpolitiken. Jag hoppas det kan bidra till en kad frstelse fr hur vi bedriver penningpolitik", inledde Rosenberg. "Den frsta frgan r huruvida Riksbanken alltfr mycket, eller bara, bryr sig om inflationen. Hur tar vi hnsyn till den allmnna ekonomiska utvecklingen och t.ex. utvecklingen p arbetsmarknaden d vi beslutar om frndringar av reporntan? Riksbanken har enligt lagen ett ml och det r att hlla inflationen p en lg och stabil niv  att upprtthlla ett fast penningvrde som det str i lagtexten. Det frsker vi stadkomma genom att se till att kningen i konsumentprisindex r 2 procent per r. S lnge trovrdigheten fr inflationsmlet inte hotas har Riksbanken ocks mjligheter att ta hnsyn till hur den reala ekonomin, t.ex. produktion och sysselsttning, utvecklas. I sina huvuddrag har vi den hr strategin gemensam med mnga andra centralbanker", konstaterade Rosenberg. "Hnsyn till den reala ekonomin kan innebra att inflationen under en period tillts att avvika frn mlet. Avvikelserna fr givetvis inte bli hur stora som helst och drfr har Riksbanken gjort det tydligt att  1 procentenhet kring inflationsmlet p 2 procent normalt kan tolereras. Vi kan heller inte tillta att avvikelserna bestr alltfr lnge. Av den anledningen fljer Riksbanken principen att i normala fall se till att inflationen ska komma tillbaka till mlet inom tv r d en avvikelse har intrffat. Det hr innebr att vi har mjlighet att fra tillbaka inflationen till mlet gradvis", fortsatte Rosenberg. "Ett principiellt exempel p hur den hr flexibiliteten kan utnyttjas r d ekonomin utstts fr en strning som fr inflationen att g t ett hll och produktion och sysselsttning i motsatt riktning. Det skulle kunna rra sig om en prisndring p rvaror eller livsmedel eller ngon annan strning p ekonomins s.k. utbudssida. Att i ett sdant lge ndra rntan s mycket att inflationen snarast mjligt r i linje med mlet skulle kunna pverka den reala ekonomin i alldeles fr stor utstrckning. Vrt arbetsstt med principen att inflationen i normala fall ska vara i linje med mlet p tv rs sikt ger oss utrymme att ta hnsyn till den reala ekonomin och istllet ndra rntan gradvis. Riksbanken har ocks pongterat att det undantagsvis, vid stora strningar, kan vara ndvndigt att lta det ta lngre tid n tv r fr inflationen att komma tillbaka till mlet fr att inte svngningarna i ekonomin ska bli ondigt stora. Sammantaget medfr ett sdant stt att arbeta bttre frutsttningar fr att vi ska f en stabil utveckling av produktion och sysselsttning och kunna undvika stora svngningar", frklarade Rosenberg. "Den andra frgan jag skulle vilja ta upp r den som oftast terkommer i diskussionen om den aktuella penningpolitiken. Varfr hjer Riksbanken rntan nu nr inflationen r lg och arbetsmarknaden nnu inte kommit igng p allvar? Det man br tnka p r att de beslut vi fattar mste baseras p prognoser om den framtida utvecklingen. Det tar tid fr ekonomin att helt anpassa sig till en frndring av reporntan och som jag nmnde tidigare r vr princip att normalt fra tillbaka inflationen till mlet inom tv r. D vi fattar beslut om reporntan gr vi det allts i frsta hand fr att pverka inflationen p ett par rs sikt. Om vi bara utgick frn hur inflationen bedms bli den allra nrmaste tiden skulle rntepolitiken bli alldeles fr ryckig och pverka realekonomin negativt", fortsatte Rosenberg. "Riksbankens syn p den ekonomiska utvecklingen framver presenteras i inflationsrapporten som publicerades i samband med rntebeslutet i februari. Den statistik som kommit in den senaste tiden stdjer i stort den bedmningen. I inflationsrapporten konstaterar vi att den svenska ekonomin r inne i en konjunkturuppgng. Tillvxten r hg fr nrvarande och vi ser framfr oss att den kommer att vara fortsatt god. Den internationella efterfrgan p svenska varor och tjnster ser ut att vxa stabilt framver. Hushllens konsumtion frvntas ka i snabb takt och fretagens investeringar vntas ocks fortstta att stiga. Lget p arbetsmarknaden kommer att frbttras successivt i takt med att efterfrgan p arbetskraft kar. Resursutnyttjandet och kostnadstrycket kommer efterhand att ka. Vi ser drfr framfr oss att inflationen ocks kommer att stiga, vilket talar fr att penningpolitiken behver bli mindre expansiv", fortsatte Rosenberg. "Den hr bilden av de ekonomiska utsikterna tror jag ocks ser ut ungefr p samma stt hos i princip alla prognosmakare, ven om vissa detaljer givetvis skiljer sig t. De flesta prognoser pekar p att konjunkturuppgngen kommer att fortstta, inflationstrycket kommer att ka och rntan kommer att behva hjas frn dagens mycket lga niv. Det som kan diskuteras r i vilken takt det br ske", konstaterade Rosenberg. "Vra prognoser i inflationsrapporten var baserade p antagandet att rntan skulle hjas med ytterligare 0,25 procentenheter under frsta kvartalet och sedan fortstta uppt gradvis under de nrmsta ren. Med en sdan profil p rnteutvecklingen hamnade inflationen enligt prognosen nra mlet p tv rs sikt, men det stod ocks klart att inflationen skulle vara under mlet under en stor del av prognosperioden. I direktionen tyckte vi visserligen att detta tydde p att man borde kunna sikta p en ngot mer expansiv penningpolitik n den som prognosen i inflationsrapporten utgick frn, men vi var samtidigt verens om att det fanns faktorer som gjorde att en hjning av rntan i februari nd var det bsta alternativet. Lt mig frklara varfr", fortsatte Rosenberg. "Under de senaste ren har inflationen hllits ned av en svag importprisutveckling och en stark inhemsk produktivitetsutveckling. Produktionen har kunnat vxa snabbt utan att inflationstrycket stigit. Inflationen har allts hllits ned av gynnsamma faktorer p ekonomins utbudssida, och som pverkat den under en lngre tid n vad Riksbanken och andra prognosmakare frutsett. Jag var tidigare inne p att frndringar av den hr typen kan medfra svra avvgningar om hur snabbt inflationen ska fras tillbaka till mlet, t.ex. kan det vara svrt att veta hur varaktiga sdana faktorer r. Riksbanken har under de senaste ren snkt reporntan till en rekordlg niv fr att f upp inflationen mot mlet. Det har stimulerat ekonomin och bidragit till den snabba tillvxten. Men det finns risker med att fortstta bedriva en mycket expansiv penningpolitik i ett lge nr ekonomin redan vxer s starkt", konstaterade Rosenberg. "Den mycket lga rntenivn har t.ex. bidragit till att huspriser och utlningen till hushll  som redan kat snabbt under en fljd av r  har fortsatt att stiga i en takt som inte r lngsiktigt hllbar. Om denna utveckling fortstter tycker vi i direktionen att det finns en risk att en situation kan byggas upp dr en kraftig inbromsning av husprisutvecklingen lngre fram fr hushllen att knna att skuldbrdan blir fr hg och att de drfr kar sitt sparande i snabb takt. Det kan leda till att efterfrgan i ekonomin viker kraftigt och att inflationen ocks kan bli alltfr lg. Det strkte oss i vr bedmning att det fanns skl att gra penningpolitiken mindre expansiv i januari och februari", menade Rosenberg. "Det fr oss fram till den tredje frgan: innebr detta att penningpolitiken nu har ett ml fr utvecklingen av huspriserna? Jag har formulerat frgan lite tillspetsat, men det jag r ute efter r att det ibland har tolkats som om det r oro fr huspriserna och hushllens vxande skuldsttning som varit huvudmotivet till rntehjningarna. S r det inte, det kan jag frskra. Huvudmotivet r, precis som jag nmnde tidigare, att vi ser framfr oss en utveckling dr konjunkturen kommer att fortstta uppt och inflationen kommer att stiga. Det r allts i frsta hand inflationsutsikterna p ett par rs sikt som r anledningen till att vi inte vill fortstta stimulera ekonomin lika kraftigt som vi gjort den senaste tiden. Det r drfr vi har hjt rntan", pongterade Rosenberg. "Som alltid finns det ocks olika risker vi beaktar nr vi fattar vra penningpolitiska beslut. I vra avvgningar har riskerna kopplade till husprisutvecklingen och hushllens skuldsttning varit ett argument fr att inte skjuta en hjning framt ngra mnader. Det betyder inte att vi har ngot speciellt ml fr hur mycket huspriser och upplning br ka. Det betyder inte heller att penningpolitiken styrts av en oro fr att hushllens upplning skulle ventyra stabiliteten i det finansiella systemet. Hur bostadsmarknaden utvecklas r givetvis viktigt ven i det perspektivet, men Riksbanken ser inga tecken p att huspriser och skuldsttning skulle utgra ngot hot mot banksystemet. Det r snarare riskerna kopplade till den framtida reala stabiliteten som vi lyft fram", fortsatte Rosenberg. "Riksbanken har nu hjt reporntan till 2 procent. Med inflationsfrvntningar mellan 1,5 och 2 procent innebr det att realrntan r nra noll. Penningpolitiken r allts fortfarande vldigt expansiv, ngot jag tycker ofta glms bort i debatten om vra senaste rntebeslut", avslutade Rosenberg. Title: Surprisingly weak growth dampens inflation outlook
text: Rosenberg: Surprisingly weak growth dampens inflation outlook Date 2005-06-15 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke on Wednesday about the economic situation and current monetary policy at a meeting organized by Handelsbanken. "The development of the world economy in recent years has generally been very good. Growth has been high, which last year benefited the Swedish economy as demand for our exports was very strong. Increased international competition has contributed to low global inflation, despite the sharp rise in oil prices. This has contributed to weak inflation impulses from the outside world in recent years," Rosenberg began. "In our latest inflation report in March, we expected the economy in the rest of the world to enter a calmer phase this year partly as a result of a less expansionary economic policy. However, growth was expected to remain good in the coming years. Our assessment was also that the economic recovery in the Swedish economy would continue, but that the pace of output growth would slow somewhat. Exports were no longer expected to grow as fast, but instead we expected domestic demand to grow stronger," Rosenberg said. "When we did our monetary policy reconciliation in April, we noted that the economic picture in the rest of the world appeared more uncertain than before. Various indicators gave a fragmented picture of developments in the United States, while figures for the euro area had come in that more clearly indicated a weaker than expected development in output. In Sweden, there were signs that the industrial economy and goods exports were not developing as strongly as predicted. The indicators of domestic demand in Sweden, on the other hand, suggested an increase roughly in line with the March forecast. However, no really clear signs of a turnaround in the Swedish labour market could still be seen and this contributed to us feeling an increased uncertainty about the strength of the Swedish economy," Rosenberg continued. "In the U.S., there seems to have been no more than a temporary slowdown. There again, it looks as if growth continues at a good pace and resource utilisation is rising," Rosenberg continued. "In the euro area, however, developments appear to be weaker than we expected in March. For Sweden, the slowdown in the euro area means a slower development of export markets overall, since such a large part of our exports go to the euro area countries. The low interest rate environment and a low-valued krona partly counteract the effects of the slowdown in demand in Swedish export markets, but there is still reason to revise down the outlook for Swedish exports," Rosenberg noted. "Now that the first outcome figures are available for the first quarter of this year, we can also state that Swedish GDP growth at the beginning of the year was significantly lower than all the forecasts I have seen so far. Exports slowed down surprisingly quickly. But households' consumption and consumption in the public sector were also weaker than Expected. Fixed investments in the business sector, on the other hand, increased strongly, roughly in line with our previous forecast. Of course, as usual, there is uncertainty as the first preliminary picture of developments in the first quarter may be revised as new data is collected and processed. Still, I hardly think, based on what we know now, that 2005 will be characterized as a year of rising resource utilization," Rosenberg said. "The difficulty now is to determine whether the fairly clear slowdown in growth that occurred in the first quarter constitutes the beginning of an economic downturn or whether it is rather a temporary slowdown. Most of it speaks so far for the latter. To a large extent, the development reflects a decline in production in the public sector, especially in municipalities. Production in the business world was not as weak. There are also special circumstances that make it difficult to assess the underlying strength of demand developments in the first quarter. Demand has in all likelihood been affected by calendar effects, i.e. differences in the number of holidays and working days between the first quarters of last year and this year. It is likely that the calendar differences will contribute to the fact that private consumption and foreign trade in particular look excessively weak in the first quarter. Nevertheless, the weak GDP outcome means, in my opinion, that the forecast for GDP growth this year will have to be revised down quite properly. For 2006, on the other hand, with the information we have today, only a minor downward adjustment is justified. The financial position of households and enterprises has strengthened. This suggests that both private and public consumption and investments can develop relatively favorably in the years to come. While the labour market situation is still weak, the number of job vacancies is increasing and notices are decreasing, and there are therefore still signs that an improvement may be on the way," Rosenberg said. "Finally, let me touch on the monetary policy decision-making situation. At our April meeting, just as in March, we chose to leave the repo rate unchanged at 2 percent. We then had some difficult trade-offs to make. Inflation was expected to fall below the 2% inflation target for most of the projection horizon, partly driven by supply-side factors but in line with its target over a couple of years' time. At the same time, the growth we predicted was higher than what can be considered sustainable in the long term. This was expected to contribute to an increase in resource utilisation, resulting in a gradual rise in inflationary pressures. Furthermore, household borrowing and house prices increased strongly for several years, partly as a result of the already expansionary stance of monetary policy. All in all, in our judgment, this suggested some caution in the design of monetary policy," Rosenberg said. "Inflation so far this year has been slightly higher than we expected in March. This is partly due to higher oil prices, but also because some domestic prices have not fallen as expected. This suggests that the inflation forecast will be slightly higher in the short term. At the same time, the weak growth at the beginning of the year means that resource utilisation has probably not risen but rather fallen so far this year. Even if growth becomes stronger again in the coming years, which I think there are reasons to believe, this suggests that resource utilisation will be lower throughout the forecast period than in our previous assessment. As a result, both the cost pressures and the price increases, as I see it, will be weaker further ahead than we expected before. All in all, this reasonably means that inflation, even if it gradually rises, will remain significantly below target over both one and two years' time. While there are still risks associated with the rapid growth in household borrowing and house prices, household consumption demand is likely to be weaker, especially this year, than we expected in March. Against this background, I, for my part, see room for a more expansionary monetary policy. How big this space is, we in the Executive Board will consider next week when we meet," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: verraskande svag tillvxt dmpar inflationsutsikterna Datum 2005-06-15 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade under onsdagen om det ekonomiska lget och den aktuella penningpolitiken vid ett mte anordnat av Handelsbanken. Utvecklingen i vrldsekonomin har de senaste ren verlag varit mycket god. Tillvxten har varit hg vilket under fjolret gynnade den svenska ekonomin genom att efterfrgan p vr export var mycket stark. kad internationell konkurrens har bidragit till att den globala inflationen varit lg, trots den kraftiga uppgngen i oljepriserna. Det har medverkat till svaga inflationsimpulser frn omvrlden de senaste ren, inledde Rosenberg. I vr senaste inflationsrapport i mars rknade vi med att konjunkturen i omvrlden skulle g in i en lugnare fas i r delvis till fljd av en mindre expansiv ekonomisk politik. Tillvxten vntades nd bli fortsatt god de kommande ren. Vr bedmning var ocks att konjunkturterhmtningen i den svenska ekonomin skulle fortstta, men att takten i produktionstillvxten skulle dmpas ngot. Exporten vntades inte lngre ka lika snabbt, men istllet rknade vi med att den inhemska efterfrgan skulle vxa starkare, sa Rosenberg. Nr vi gjorde vr penningpolitiska avstmning i april, noterade vi att konjunkturbilden i omvrlden framstod som mer osker n tidigare. Olika indikatorer gav en splittrad bild av utvecklingen i USA, medan det fr euroomrdet hade kommit in siffror som mer tydligt pekade p en svagare utveckling av produktionen n vntat. I Sverige fanns tecken p att industrikonjunkturen och varuexporten inte utvecklades s starkt som frutsett. Indikatorerna fr den inhemska efterfrgan i Sverige talade dremot fr en kning ungefr i linje med marsprognosen. Ngra riktigt tydliga tecken p en vndning p den svenska arbetsmarknaden kunde dremot fortfarande inte ses och det bidrog till att vi knde en kad oskerhet om styrkan i den svenska ekonomin, fortsatte Rosenberg. I USA tycks det inte ha skett mer n en tillfllig uppbromsning. Dr ser det nu ter ut som om tillvxten fortstter i god takt och resursutnyttjandet stiger, fortsatte Rosenberg. I euroomrdet verkar utvecklingen dock bli svagare n vi rknade med i mars. Fr Sveriges del innebr dmpningen i euroomrdet en lngsammare utveckling av exportmarknaderna totalt sett, eftersom en s stor del av vr export gr till eurolnderna. Det lga rntelget och en lgt vrderad krona motverkar delvis effekterna av uppbromsningen av efterfrgan p de svenska exportmarknaderna, men det finns nd anledning att revidera ned utsikterna fr den svenska exporten, konstaterade Rosenberg. Nr nu de frsta utfallssiffrorna finns fr det frsta kvartalet i r, kan vi ocks konstatera, att den svenska BNP-tillvxten i brjan av ret blev betydligt lgre n alla de prognoser jag hittills sett. Exporten saktade in verraskande snabbt. Men ven hushllens konsumtion och konsumtionen i den offentliga sektorn blev svagare n vntat. De fasta investeringarna i nringslivet dremot kade starkt, ungefr i linje med vr tidigare prognos. Naturligtvis finns det som vanligt en oskerhet i och med att den frsta preliminra bilden av utvecklingen under frsta kvartalet kan komma att revideras allteftersom nya data samlas in och bearbetas. nd tror jag knappast, p basis av vad vi vet nu, att 2005 kommer att kunna karakteriseras som ett r med stigande resursutnyttjande, sa Rosenberg. Svrigheten r nu att avgra om den ganska tydliga dmpningen av tillvxten som skett under frsta kvartalet utgr brjan p en konjunkturnedgng eller om det snarare r en tillfllig inbromsning. Det mesta talar s hr lngt fr det senare. Till stor del speglar utvecklingen en nedgng i produktionen i den offentliga sektorn, srskilt i kommunerna. Produktionen i nringslivet var inte lika svag. Det finns ocks speciella omstndigheter som gr det svrt att bedma den underliggande styrkan i efterfrgeutvecklingen under frsta kvartalet. Efterfrgan har med all sannolikhet pverkats av kalendereffekter, det vill sga skillnader i antalet helgdagar respektive arbetsdagar mellan frsta kvartalen i fjol och i r. Det troliga r att kalenderskillnaderna bidrar till att framfr allt den privata konsumtionen och utrikeshandeln ser verdrivet svag ut under frsta kvartalet. Inte desto mindre innebr det svaga BNP-utfallet enligt min mening att prognosen fr BNP-tillvxten i r mste justeras ned ganska ordentligt. Fr 2006 r dremot med den information vi har idag bara en mindre nedjustering motiverad. Den finansiella stllningen har strkts svl i kommunsektorn som bland hushllen och i fretagen. Det talar fr att bde privat och offentlig konsumtion och investeringarna kan utvecklas frhllandevis gynnsamt ren framver. Lget p arbetsmarknaden r visserligen fortfarande svagt, men antalet lediga platser kar och varslen minskar och det finns drfr nd tecken p att en frbttring kan vara p vg, menade Rosenberg. Lt mig slutligen ngot berra den penningpolitiska beslutssituationen. Vid vrt aprilmte valde vi, precis som i mars, att lta reporntan vara ofrndrad p 2 procent. Vi hade d en del svra avvgningar att gra. Inflationen vntades under strre delen av prognosperioden understiga inflationsmlet p 2 procent delvis till fljd av faktorer av utbudskaraktr men vara i linje med mlet p ett par rs sikt. Den tillvxt vi frutsg var samtidigt hgre n vad som kan betraktas som lngsiktigt hllbart. Det vntades bidra till att resursutnyttjandet skulle komma att ka med ett gradvis stigande inflationstryck som fljd. Vidare kade hushllens upplning och bostadspriserna sedan flera r tillbaka starkt, delvis som ett resultat av penningpolitikens redan expansiva inriktning. Sammantaget talade detta enligt vr bedmning fr en viss frsiktighet i utformningen av penningpolitiken, sa Rosenberg. Inflationen har hittills i r blivit ngot hgre n vi rknade med i mars. Delvis beror det p hgre oljepris men ven p att vissa inhemska priser inte fallit som berknat. Det talar fr att inflationsprognosen blir ngot hgre p kort sikt. Den svaga tillvxten i brjan av ret gr samtidigt att resursutnyttjandet troligen inte stigit utan snarast fallit hittills i r. ven om tillvxten blir starkare igen de kommande ren, vilket jag tycker det finns skl att tro, talar det fr att resursutnyttjandet kommer att vara lgre under hela prognosperioden n enligt vr tidigare bedmning. Drmed blir bde kostnadstrycket och prisstegringarna som jag ser det svagare lngre fram n vi rknat med tidigare. Sammantaget innebr detta rimligen att inflationen, ven om den gradvis stiger, kommer att ligga ptagligt under mlet bde p ett och tv rs sikt. ven om det fortfarande finns risker med den snabba kningen av hushllens upplning och bostadspriserna blir troligen hushllens konsumtionsefterfrgan svagare, framfr allt i r, n vi rknade med i mars. Mot den bakgrunden ser jag, fr min del, utrymme fr en mer expansiv penningpolitik. Hur stort detta utrymme r kommer vi i direktionen att ta stllning till nsta vecka nr vi sammantrder, avslutade Rosenberg.
