Title: Monetary policy and prices of raw materials and energy
text: Rosenberg: Monetary policy and commodity and energy prices Date 2008-03-03 How should central banks respond to rising prices of raw materials and energy? First Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg discussed this issue when she spoke today at the "Commodities, Energy and Finance" workshop in Vienna. "The prices of energy and raw materials have risen rapidly in recent years. This is very much linked to the fact that emerging countries such as China and India have increasingly integrated into the world economy  what is often referred to when talking about globalisation. At the same time, globalisation has brought with it low prices for imported products from emerging countries and, through increased competition, has helped to curb the rise in the price of import-competing products in developed countries. This has made it easier for central banks to maintain price stability. For a long time, the economic discussion focused on the inflation-dampening effect of globalization. The challenge for some central banks, such as the Riksbank, which I represent, was rather how monetary policy could stimulate economies to drive inflation up towards the target," Rosenberg began. "But now globalization seems to have instead begun to create upward pressure on inflation, as increasing demand from emerging countries drives up world market prices not only for energy and metals, but also for food commodities. Perhaps it is only now that the low-inflation policies that have seemingly been pursued so successfully in many countries are beginning to be put to the test in earnest," Rosenberg continued. "How, then, is inflation affected by rising energy and commodity prices and how should monetary policy deal with such price changes? The principles for this are basically simple in so-called flexible inflation targeting. It means that the central bank tries to stabilise inflation around the inflation target and, provided that confidence in the inflation target is maintained, also places some emphasis on stabilising output and employment. Another and more concrete way of describing this is for the central bank to try to find a path for the key interest rate that means that the forecast for inflation ends up reasonably close to the target while the real economy develops in a balanced way. These principles are universal and can be applied regardless of the disruption hitting the economy. In this sense, one could say that an upturn in energy and commodity prices is not a particular problem from a monetary policy point of view  it is very much about 'business as usual'," Rosenberg said. "But while the principles of how monetary policy should be conducted are, in theory, simple, its practical implementation is far from simple. An assessment must be made of how the rise in energy and commodity prices will affect the economy, not only inflation but also the real economy. An increase in the prices of energy and raw materials can affect the economy in different ways. Price increases have a direct effect by including, for example, energy and food in the measure of inflation. But the real economy is also affected by indirect means. Raising energy prices works much like a tax increase for households and dampens domestic demand," Rosenberg continued. "A faster increase in the price of energy and raw materials means that production costs are increasing. The effect can be likened to that resulting from a fall in productivity. It tends to dampen production and growth. At the same time, the rise in energy prices in recent years has been significantly more pronounced than the upturns of the 1970s and 1980s driven by strong demand on the world market rather than by supply-side disruptions. The negative effects on the real economy of the rapid rise in energy prices have then been offset in whole or in part by favourable price developments in other areas and strong international growth. Thus, it is not possible to give a standard answer as to how monetary policy should respond to an increase in energy and commodity prices. Each disorder must be analyzed separately and what policy is appropriate must be determined on a case-by-case basis," Rosenberg noted. "Characteristic of energy and commodity prices is that they tend to fluctuate sharply during the economic cycle. Periods of rapid price increases can be followed by periods of significantly calmer development or often even price falls. These fluctuations are also propagating to the consumer level. Such rapid shifts in inflationary impulses are often impossible to predict and cannot be immediately countered by monetary policy. That's because monetary policy operates with delay. In the monetary policy analysis, it is therefore common for central banks, in addition to the more comprehensive measures of inflation, to also study measures of inflation that exclude short-term effects in energy and commodity prices. In my view, this is not about the fact that there are reasons to ignore the prices of energy and raw materials when balancing monetary policy. Instead, what it comes down to is trying to separate out which price impulses risk producing lasting effects on inflation and which are temporary and will ebb without strong monetary policy countermeasures," Rosenberg said. "How practical monetary policy should relate to rising energy and commodity prices is an issue that the Riksbank, like many other central banks, is currently grappling with. In Sweden, rising prices of energy and food contributed to a rapid increase in inflation in the autumn of 2007. Inflation measured by the CPI is today more than one percentage point above the target of 2 percent. Especially for energy, but also largely for food, the rapid rise in prices reflects a sharp rise in world market prices. The assessments that must be made in such a situation are therefore partly about how lasting the effects will be. On the one hand, they're about how much of the price increases have to do with increased demand and changes in supply," Rosenberg said. "In the forecast presented in connection with the monetary policy meeting of the Riksbank in mid-February, the assessment was that world market prices will not continue to rise at the same rapid pace in the future. Inflation impulses are therefore considered to be partly temporary and inflation is therefore expected to fall back again in a year or so. But to some extent, these are also effects on inflation that risk becoming more lasting and that should be counteracted with monetary policy," Rosenberg noted. "It is also very important that confidence in monetary policy and the inflation target is maintained. The fact that inflation exceeds the target must be regarded as a temporary departure. The inflationary impulse cannot be allowed to take hold in the economy and drive up inflation permanently. In this context, it is important to be particularly vigilant about the evolution of inflation expectations. In Sweden, we continuously follow through special surveys how inflation expectations develop in different groups in society and with different time horizons. These show that inflation expectations have risen recently, not only in the short term but also in the longer term. This was an important reason that, in addition to still good growth and high cost pressures, justified the decision to raise the repo rate in February," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Penningpolitik och priser p rvaror och energi Datum 2008-03-03 Hur br centralbanker frhlla sig till stigande priser p rvaror och energi? Den frgan diskuterade frste vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg nr hon idag talade p workshopen Commodities, Energy and Finance i Wien. Priserna p energi och rvaror har stigit snabbt de senaste ren. Detta hnger i hg grad samman med att tillvxtlnder som Kina och Indien alltmer integrerats i vrldsekonomin  det man ofta syftar p nr man talar om globalisering. Samtidigt har globaliseringen frt med sig lga priser p importerade produkter frn tillvxtlnderna och via kad konkurrens bidragit till att dmpa priskningarna p importkonkurrerande produkter i industrilnderna. Detta har underlttat fr centralbankerna att upprtthlla prisstabilitet. Lnge fokuserade den ekonomiska diskussionen p den inflationsdmpande effekten av globaliseringen. Utmaningen fr en del centralbanker, som till exempel Riksbanken som jag representerar, blev snarast hur man med penningpolitiken kunde stimulera ekonomierna fr att driva upp inflationen mot mlet, inledde Rosenberg. Men nu tycks globaliseringen istllet ha brjat skapa ett tryck uppt p inflationen, nr kande efterfrgan frn tillvxtlnderna driver upp vrldsmarknadspriserna inte bara p energi och metaller utan ven p livsmedelsrvaror. Kanske r det frst nu som den lginflationspolitik som till synes bedrivits s framgngsrikt i mnga lnder brjar sttas p prov p allvar, fortsatte Rosenberg. Hur pverkas d inflationen av stigande energi- och rvarupriser och hur ska penningpolitiken hantera sdana prisndringar? Principerna fr detta r i grunden enkla vid s kallad flexibel inflationsmlsstyrning. Den innebr att centralbanken frsker stabilisera inflationen kring inflationsmlet och, frutsatt att frtroendet fr inflationsmlet upprtthlls, ocks lgger viss vikt vid att stabilisera produktion och sysselsttning. Ett annat och mer konkret stt att beskriva detta r att centralbanken frsker hitta en bana fr styrrntan som innebr att prognosen fr inflationen hamnar rimligt nra mlet samtidigt som realekonomin utvecklas balanserat. De hr principerna r allmngiltiga och kan tillmpas oavsett vilken strning som trffar ekonomin. I den meningen skulle man kunna sga att en uppgng i energi- och rvarupriserna inte r ngot speciellt problem ur penningpolitisk synvinkel  det handlar i mngt och mycket om business as usual, sade Rosenberg. Men ven om principerna fr hur penningpolitiken br bedrivas i teorin r enkla, r det praktiska genomfrandet lngtifrn enkelt. En bedmning mste gras av hur uppgngen i priserna p energi och rvaror kommer att pverka ekonomin, inte bara inflationen utan ven den reala ekonomin. En kning av priserna p energi och rvaror kan pverka ekonomin p olika stt. Priskningarna fr en direkt effekt genom att till exempel energi och livsmedel ingr i inflationsmttet. Men ven den reala ekonomin pverkas via indirekta vgar. Hjda energipriser fungerar ungefr som en skattehjning fr hushllen och dmpar den inhemska efterfrgan, fortsatte Rosenberg. En snabbare priskning p energi och rvaror innebr att produktionskostnaderna kar. Effekten kan liknas vid den som fljer av ett fall i produktiviteten. Det tenderar att dmpa produktion och tillvxt. Samtidigt har de senaste rens uppgng i energipriserna i betydligt hgre grad n uppgngarna p 1970- och 1980-talen varit driven av stark efterfrgan p vrldsmarknaden snarare n av strningar p utbudssidan. De negativa effekterna p realekonomin av den snabba uppgngen i energipriserna har d helt eller delvis motverkats av en gynnsam prisutveckling p andra omrden och stark internationell tillvxt. Det gr allts inte att ge ngot standardmssigt svar p hur penningpolitiken br reagera p en kning av energioch rvarupriserna. Varje strning mste analyseras fr sig och vilken politik som r lmplig mste avgras frn fall till fall, konstaterade Rosenberg. Karakteristiskt fr energi- och rvarupriser r att de tenderar att svnga kraftigt under konjunkturfrloppet. Perioder av snabba prishjningar kan fljas av perioder med avsevrt lugnare utveckling eller ofta till och med prisfall. Dessa svngningar fortplantas ocks till konsumentledet. Sdana snabba skiften i inflationsimpulser r ofta omjliga att frutse och kan inte omedelbart motverkas med penningpolitik. Det beror p att penningpolitiken verkar med frdrjning. I den penningpolitiska analysen r det drfr vanligt att centralbanker vid sidan av de mer heltckande inflationsmtten ocks studerar mtt p inflationen som exkluderar kortsiktiga effekter i energi- och rvarupriser. Enligt min syn handlar detta inte om att det finns skl att bortse frn priser p energi och rvaror nr penningpolitiken avvgs. Vad det handlar om r istllet att frska skilja ut vilka prisimpulser som riskerar att ge varaktiga effekter p inflationen och vilka som r tillflliga och kommer att ebba ut utan kraftfulla penningpolitiska mottgrder, sade Rosenberg. Hur den praktiska penningpolitiken br frhlla sig till stigande energi- och rvarupriser r en frga som Riksbanken liksom mnga andra centralbanker brottas med fr nrvarande. I Sverige bidrog stigande priser p energi och livsmedel till att inflationen kade snabbt under hsten 2007. Inflationen mtt med KPI r idag mer n en procentenhet ver mlet p 2 procent. Srskilt fr energi, men ven till stor del nr det gller livsmedel, speglar den snabba prisuppgngen att vrldsmarknadspriserna stigit kraftigt. De bedmningar som mste gras i ett sdant lge handlar allts dels om hur varaktiga effekterna kommer att bli. Dels handlar de om hur stor del av prishjningarna som har att gra med kad efterfrgan och frndringar i utbudet, sade Rosenberg. I den prognos som presenterades i samband med det penningpolitiska mtet i Riksbanken i mitten av februari var bedmningen att vrldsmarknadspriserna inte kommer att fortstta att stiga i samma snabba takt framver. Inflationsimpulserna bedms drfr delvis vara tillflliga och inflationen vntas drfr falla tillbaka igen om ngot r. Men till viss del rr det sig ocks om effekter p inflationen som riskerar att bli mer varaktiga och som br motverkas med penningpolitiken, konstaterade Rosenberg. Det r ocks mycket viktigt att frtroendet fr penningpolitiken och inflationsmlet upprtthlls. Att inflationen verstiger mlet mste betraktas som ett tillflligt avsteg. Inflationsimpulsen kan inte tilltas f fste i ekonomin och driva upp inflationen permanent. I det sammanhanget gller det att vara srskilt vaksam p hur inflationsfrvntningarna utvecklas. I Sverige fljer vi genom srskilda enkter lpande hur inflationsfrvntningarna utvecklas i olika grupper i samhllet och med olika tidshorisont. Av dessa framgr att inflationsfrvntningarna stigit den senaste tiden, inte bara p kort utan ven p lngre sikt. Detta var ett viktigt skl som, vid sidan av en fortfarande god tillvxt och ett hgt kostnadstryck, motiverade beslutet att hja reporntan i februari, avslutade Rosenberg. Title: Monetary policy and the economic situation
text: Rosenberg: Monetary policy and the economic situation Date 2006-01-13 Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg spoke on Friday at Handelsbanken's lunch meeting in Ve4stere5s. "In the latest inflation report published in early December, the Riksbank drew a relatively bright picture of economic development both in Sweden and internationally. We found that growth in the world economy was high and that it could be expected to remain good over the next few years. For the Swedish economy, we expected that the economy would continue to strengthen. The information received since December indicates that economic development both globally and in Sweden has become somewhat stronger than expected," Rosenberg began. "In the US, the development looks to be consistent with the picture drawn in December. While retail sales data through November suggests that U.S. household consumption has been slightly weaker than expected in the fourth quarter, consumer confidence has quickly strengthened again after the slump earlier in the fall. The purchasing managers' index for December fell back, but from a high level and other economic indicators suggest that the stable development will continue. For the euro area, the third-quarter data confirmed a pick-up in GDP growth. On the positive side, it is now a larger group of countries that are contributing to the improvement in the economic cycle in the euro area. Both domestic demand and exports grew at a good pace. Available indicators, mainly from various barometer surveys, point to continued good development in the fourth quarter. For Asia, too, there have mainly been positive signals about the economy. All in all, the growth outlook for the rest of the world thus looks somewhat stronger than in December. With regard to price developments, we can state that the price of oil looks set to increase somewhat faster than previously estimated. Consumer prices, on the other hand, fell back in November in the United States. Even in the euro area, inflation has moderated somewhat," Rosenberg continued. "For the Swedish economy, our assessment in the previous inflation report was that the development would remain favourable: growth was expected to be good and the situation on the labour market to brighten with a clear turnaround in 2006. The expansionary economic policy was expected this year to contribute to raising both public sector and household consumption. At the same time, a weak krona together with strong growth in the Swedish export markets were expected to provide a good development of exports. Due to good growth conditions in the Swedish economy and large current account surpluses, the exchange rate was expected to strengthen gradually. However, we saw a risk that it could take longer than assumed before these fundamental factors would have an impact on the krona exchange rate, which could provide stronger inflation impulses partly via import prices and partly via stronger export development. As a result, our Analysis in December also included an upside risk to inflation," Rosenberg said. "Since December, the krona has strengthened roughly in line with forecasts. This is probably partly due to the fact that expectations of the future repo rate have shifted up slightly since our December meeting. The new statistics that have become available suggests that some upward revision of the forecast for growth in the Swedish economy may be justified. National accounts for the third quarter of 2005 show that strong domestic demand and high export growth, as expected, drove up GDP growth. The growth in consumption growth that began in the second quarter of last year continued in the third quarter, and retail sales statistics through November indicate continued good growth in household consumption. According to the latest business cycle barometer, Swedish companies are optimistic about the near future. It is mainly the construction industry and trade that are doing well. The construction economy is strengthening more and more and order intake has increased in recent months. The manufacturing industry also continues to experience strong export order growth. The survey on households' purchasing plans breathes optimism for the future both in terms of sweden's economic development and its own economy," Rosenberg pointed out. "New information on the labour market also suggests a relatively good development. According to LFSS, employment and the number of people in the labour force have increased roughly as we expected. The number of newly registered vacancies has continued to rise and the number of notices has decreased. The latest business cycle barometer shows continued positive employment plans in the construction industry and parts of the private service industries. However, according to the national accounts for the third quarter, employment developments measured by the number of hours worked were weaker than expected and productivity growth in the business sector was therefore significantly stronger than projected. This suggests that, despite the high growth, cost pressures going forward will be contained," Rosenberg continued. "Inflation in Sweden has been low and below target since the end of 2003. According to the latest statistics, which refer to the month of December 2005, the annual rate of price rise as measured by the CPI and UND1X was 0.9% and 1.2% respectively. It is above all the rapid increase in productivity that has dampened inflation. But imported inflation has also been surprisingly low for some time. It has been held down by strong competitive pressure and the previous strengthening of the krona. In the latest Inflation Report, we assessed that inflation would rise gradually and move closer to its target as resource utilisation and domestic and international cost pressures rise. However, inflation was expected to fall below 2 percent for most of the forecast period," Rosenberg said. "It is important to bear in mind that the December inflation assessment was based on the assumption of a gradual increase in the repo rate in line with expectations in financial markets as reflected in the implied forward rates. As I mentioned earlier, these expectations have shifted upwards slightly since the December report. The fact that GDP growth in Sweden is now expected to be stronger could mean that inflation will also be higher in the future. But at the same time, productivity has again risen more than expected, helping to dampen domestic cost pressures. The krona has also strengthened and how this affects price development is difficult to assess. Overall, therefore, I do not currently think there is any reason to revise the view of the future inflation outlook: inflation can be expected to rise gradually towards the 2% target as resource utilisation increases in the wake of strong growth," Rosenberg said. Given the strong demand development, we see a relatively moderate upturn in inflation ahead of us. This is something that we have also emphasised earlier. However, as I pointed out earlier, this presupposes a gradual increase in the repo rate. Therefore, in my opinion, with the information available today, there is reason to now take a first step towards normalizing the level of the repo rate and thus make monetary policy somewhat less expansionary. It would also mean that the stimulating impact on the housing market is somewhat diminished," Rosenberg said. "Let me conclude by reminding you that what we had slightly different views on in the Executive Board at the last monetary policy meeting in December, was exactly when a rate hike should take place. At the same time, we basically agreed that the repo rate needs to be raised, something that most other forecasters also seem to agree with and that the financial markets have taken to heart. Next week, the Executive Board will meet again to take a position on monetary policy. Then we'll see what trade-offs are made and how my colleagues reason," Rosenberg concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Rosenberg: Penningpolitiken och det ekonomiska lget Datum 2006-01-13 Vice riksbankschef Irma Rosenberg talade under fredagen vid Handelsbankens lunchmte i Vsters. I den senaste inflationsrapporten som publicerades i brjan av december tecknade Riksbanken en relativt ljus bild av den ekonomiska utvecklingen svl i Sverige som internationellt. Vi konstaterade att tillvxten i vrldsekonomin var hg och att den kunde vntas bli fortsatt god under de nrmaste ren. Fr den svenska ekonomin rknade vi med att konjunkturen skulle fortstta att frstrkas. Den information som inkommit sedan i december tyder p att den ekonomiska utvecklingen svl globalt som i Sverige blivit ngot starkare n vntat, inledde Rosenberg. I USA ser utvecklingen ut att vara frenlig med den bild som tecknades i december. Detaljhandelsstatistik till och med november tyder visserligen p att de amerikanska hushllens konsumtion blivit ngot svagare n vntat fjrde kvartalet, men konsumentfrtroendet har snabbt strkts igen efter svackan tidigare under hsten. Inkpschefsindex fr december sjnk tillbaka, men frn en hg niv och andra konjunkturindikatorer talar fr att den stabila utvecklingen hller i sig. Fr euroomrdet bekrftade statistiken fr tredje kvartalet att BNP-tillvxten tilltagit. Positivt r att det nu r en strre grupp lnder som bidrar till konjunkturfrbttringen i euroomrdet. Bde den inhemska efterfrgan och exporten kade i god takt. Tillgngliga indikatorer, frmst frn olika barometerunderskningar, pekar mot en fortsatt god utveckling under fjrde kvartalet. ven fr Asien har det i huvudsak kommit positiva signaler om konjunkturen. Sammantaget ser tillvxtutsikterna fr omvrlden drmed ngot starkare ut n i december. Nr det gller prisutvecklingen kan vi konstatera att oljepriset ser ut att ka ngot snabbare n tidigare berknat. Konsumentpriserna sjnk dremot tillbaka i november i USA. ven i euroomrdet har inflationen dmpats ngot, fortsatte Rosenberg. Fr den svenska ekonomin var vr bedmning i den frra inflationsrapporten att utvecklingen skulle vara fortsatt gynnsam: tillvxten vntades bli god och situationen p arbetsmarknaden allt ljusare med en tydlig vndning under 2006. Den expansiva ekonomiska politiken vntades i r bidra till att hja bde den offentliga sektorns och hushllens konsumtion. En svag krona tillsammans med en stark tillvxt p de svenska exportmarknaderna bedmdes samtidigt ge en god utveckling av exporten. Till fljd av goda tillvxtfrutsttningar i den svenska ekonomin och stora verskott i bytesbalansen vntades vxelkursen strkas successivt. Vi sg dock en risk fr att det skulle kunna ta lngre tid n vad som antagits innan dessa fundamentala faktorer skulle sl igenom p kronkursen, ngot som skulle kunna ge starkare inflationsimpulser dels via importpriserna, dels via en starkare exportutveckling. Drmed fanns i vr analys i december ocks en upptrisk fr inflationen, sa Rosenberg. Kronan har sedan i december strkts ungefr i linje med prognosen. Det hnger troligen delvis samman med att frvntningarna om den framtida reporntan har skiftat upp ngot sedan vrt decembermte. Den nya statistik som blivit tillgnglig tyder p att en viss upprevidering av prognosen fr tillvxten i svensk ekonomi kan vara motiverad. Nationalrkenskaperna fr tredje kvartalet 2005 visar att en stark inhemsk efterfrgan och en hg exporttillvxt som vntat drev upp BNP-tillvxten. Den kning i konsumtionstillvxten som pbrjades andra kvartalet i fjol hll i sig under det tredje kvartalet och detaljhandelsstatistik till och med november tyder p en fortsatt god tillvxt i hushllens konsumtion. Enligt den senaste konjunkturbarometern r svenska fretag optimistiska om den nrmaste framtiden. Frmst r det byggbranschen och handeln som gr bra. Byggkonjunkturen strks alltmer och orderingngen har kat de senaste mnaderna. Ocks tillverkningsindustrin har en fortsatt stark exportordertillvxt. Underskningen om hushllens inkpsplaner andas framtidsoptimism svl nr det gller den ekonomiska utvecklingen fr Sverige som den egna ekonomin, framhll Rosenberg. Ny information om arbetsmarknaden talar ocks fr en relativt god utveckling. Sysselsttningen och antalet personer i arbetskraften har enligt AKU kat ungefr som vi rknat med. Antalet nyanmlda lediga platser har fortsatt att stiga och antalet varsel har minskat. Den senaste konjunkturbarometern visar p fortsatt positiva anstllningsplaner inom byggindustrin och delar av de privata tjnstenringarna. Enligt nationalrkenskaperna fr tredje kvartalet var emellertid sysselsttningsutvecklingen mtt i antalet arbetade timmar svagare n vntat och produktivitetstillvxten i nringslivet drfr betydligt starkare n berknat. Det talar fr att kostnadstrycket framver trots den hga tillvxten kommer att hllas nere, fortsatte Rosenberg. Inflationen i Sverige har varit lg och understigit mlet sedan slutet av 2003. Enligt den senaste statistiken, som avser december mnad 2005, uppgick den rliga prisstegringstakten mtt med KPI och UND1X till 0,9 respektive 1,2 procent. Det r framfr allt den snabba kningen av produktiviteten, som dmpat inflationen. Men ocks den importerade inflationen har under en lngre tid varit verraskande lg. Den har hllits nere av ett starkt konkurrenstryck och den tidigare frstrkningen av kronan. I den senaste inflationsrapporten gjorde vi bedmningen att inflationen skulle stiga gradvis och nrma sig mlet i takt med att resursutnyttjandet och det inhemska och internationella kostnadstrycket stiger. Inflationen vntades dock understiga 2 procent under strre delen av prognosperioden, sa Rosenberg. Det r viktigt att hlla i minnet att inflationsbedmningen i december byggde p antagandet om en gradvis hjning av reporntan i linje med frvntningarna p de finansiella marknaderna som de avspeglades i de implicita terminsrntorna. Som jag nmnde tidigare har dessa frvntningar skiftat uppt ngot sedan decemberrapporten. Att BNP-tillvxten i Sverige nu bedms bli starkare skulle kunna innebra att ocks inflationen blir hgre framver. Men samtidigt har produktiviteten terigen stigit mer n vntat, vilket bidrar till att dmpa det inhemska kostnadstrycket. Kronan har dessutom strkts och hur det pverkar prisutvecklingen r svrbedmt. Sammantaget tycker jag drfr fr nrvarande inte att det finns ngon anledning att revidera synen p de framtida inflationsutsikterna: inflationen kan vntas stiga gradvis mot mlet p 2 procent nr resursutnyttjandet kar i spren av den starka tillvxten, sa Rosenberg. Med hnsyn till den starka efterfrgeutvecklingen r det en frhllandevis mttlig uppgng i inflationen vi ser framfr oss. Detta r ngot som vi ocks framhllit tidigare. Men som jag tidigare ppekade frutstter det att reporntan gradvis hjs. Drfr finns det enligt min mening, med den information som finns idag, anledning att nu ta ett frsta steg mot en normalisering av nivn p reporntan och drmed gra penningpolitiken ngot mindre expansiv. Det skulle ocks innebra att den stimulerande inverkan p bostadsmarknaden minskar ngot, sa Rosenberg. Lt mig avslutningsvis pminna om att det vi hade lite olika sikter om i direktionen vid det frra penningpolitiska mtet i december, var exakt nr en rntehjning borde ske. Samtidigt var vi i grunden verens om att reporntan behver hjas, ngot som de flesta andra prognosmakare ocks verkar hlla med om och som de finansiella marknaderna tagit till sig. Nsta vecka samlas direktionen igen fr att ta stllning till penningpolitiken. D fr vi se vilka avvgningar som grs och hur mina kollegor resonerar, avslutade Rosenberg. Title: The Riksbank and monetary policy
text: Rosenberg: The Riksbank and monetary policy Date: 2005-09-29 Speaker: Deputy Governor Irma Rosenberg Location: Danske Bank I would like to start by thanking you for the invitation to come here and talk about the Riksbank and monetary policy. Over the past year, the discussion on monetary policy has been lively. The background is, among other things, the surprisingly low inflation and the weak labor market, but the rapid increase in household debt and rising house prices have also been in the picture. Discussion of monetary policy is important and something that the Riksbank cherishes. This means that we constantly have reason to test our policies, our arguments and our working methods. Not least, it encourages us to constantly review our forecasting work and how we explain our monetary policy decisions. These are precisely the aspects I initially intended to talk a little about here today. Over the years, the forecasts in the main scenario in the Riksbank's inflation reports have been based on the assumption that the repo rate will remain unchanged during the forecast period. In the context of the Inflation Report in March this year, we supplemented the analysis with new alternative forecasts, based on the assumption that the repo rate develops in line with so-called implicit forward rates, which in principle reflect market expectations about future monetary policy. At the same time, we slightly stretched the time perspective in these forecasts. Such alternative projections were also included in the June Inflation Report alongside the main scenario, which was, as usual, based on the assumption of a constant repo rate. Starting with the next inflation report to be published on 20 October, the forecasts in the main scenario will instead be based on the assumption that interest rate developments follow the implied forward rates, while a forecast based on constant repo rate will be included as an alternative scenario in a special box. Let me underline right now that this does not mean any change in the monetary policy strategy. Rather, as we have pointed out earlier, it is primarily about increasing the understanding of how the Riksbank reasons and at the same time making it easier to evaluate our forecasts. In this way, we can also create better conditions for a constructive monetary policy debate. (1) I would like to end my talk by saying a few words about the current situation. The monetary policy strategy Since 1993, monetary policy has been guided by an inflation target of 2% as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) with a tolerance range of plus/minus 1 percentage point. As monetary policy affects inflation with some delay, monetary policy decisions must be based on a forecast of inflation for the next two years. The forecasts in the Inflation Report have been based on the assumption that the repo rate kept unchanged. To explain how the inflation forecast affects decisions on the repo rate, the Riksbank has referred to a simple rule of action: if inflation, under this assumption, deviates from the target in one to two years' time, the Riksbank should normally raise or lower interest rates. At the same time, we have made it clear that this simple rule of action should be seen primarily as a guide to how monetary policy can be expected to be designed on average. In its simplicity, it cannot describe all the considerations on which monetary policy decisions are based. There are a number of different circumstances that justify deviations from this simple rule, which was also specified in a clarification in 1999. (2) One such is when inflation has been affected by effects that are considered temporary but that do not have time to fully subside within the two-year horizon. These are the reasons why we have often chosen to let the inflation measure UND1X, which is adjusted for interest costs for single-family homes (which are strongly affected by changes in the repo rate) and indirect taxes and subsidies, form the basis for our monetary policy decisions. The Riksbank has sometimes also chosen to let monetary policy be guided by measures of inflation that are cleared of other types of temporary effects. For example, for most of 2003 and early 2004, we chose to start from a measure of inflation adjusted for energy price developments, as energy price changes gave rise to sharp but temporary fluctuations in inflation. In this context, it may be worth pointing out that during such periods we had anticipated in advance that CPI inflation would not be at its target for one to two years, but that there was no reason to take monetary policy measures to bring it back to its target. The second case that justifies a deviation from the rule is when inflation has for some reason deviated significantly from the target and when a monetary policy aimed at a rapid return to the target is expected to have major negative effects on output and employment. For example, a sharp rise in oil prices can lead to large cost increases for companies, which in turn can lead to both higher prices and reduced production. In such situations, we have made it clear that a more flexible policy approach that provides for somewhat slower adjustment towards the inflation target may be justified in order to avoid excessive fluctuations in the real economy. Although we have sometimes chosen to highlight measures of inflation other than CPI, I want to be clear that there is no single inflation index that, on the one hand, always captures all the effects relevant to monetary policy and, on the other hand, always weeds out the inflation impulses that monetary policy should not counteract. A disadvantage of using different measures of inflation in different situations is that it can create uncertainty about how the inflation target is defined, although we try to be very clear about why a particular inflation measure at a given time is judged to give the best picture of the underlying price pressures and thus the development of inflation in the short term. However, there is a way to reduce the need to use several different measures of inflation that also clarify the trade-offs that monetary policy may face. It is to make forecasts for more than two years, i.e. slightly extend the forecast horizon. With a longer forecast horizon, it is possible to illustrate more clearly when various disturbances have effects that are temporary and how they fall away over time without lasting affect inflation. It can thus help to improve pedagogy and hopefully also reduce the uncertainty about the direction of monetary policy that can sometimes arise among market players. This does not mean, and I want to be clear about this, that we are changing our view of the normal target horizon. We intend to continue to normally bring inflation back to target within two years when there has been a deviation. But it may be easier to explain the trade-offs the policy faces if you extend the time horizon of the forecasts somewhat. Let me also highlight some aspects that speak in favour of a main scenario based on a more realistic assumption of the repo rate. Advantages of the assumption that the repo rate develops in line with the implicit terminsrantorna Basing the forecasts in the main scenario on the assumption of a constant policy rate has long been the practice among countries that have chosen to let an inflation target guide monetary policy. This assumption makes it easy to justify changes in policy; if the forecasted inflation deviates from the target at an unchanged repo rate, it shows that there are reasons to consider a change in the repo rate. This arrangement has worked well and has been justified for educational reasons. It has provided a clarity of communication that has been particularly important in the establishment phase of the new monetary policy regime. At the same time, there are some problems with an inflation forecast based on an assumption of unchanged repo rate. If you want to make forecasts in a slightly longer time perspective, as I have just described, the assumption of an unchanged repo rate becomes more unrealistic. Even in some other contexts, it can be complicated to make consistent forecasts based on this assumption. This applies, for example, if there are market expectations of significant policy rate changes. Then it can be difficult to reconcile an assumption that the repo rate is kept constant with reasonable forecast paths for, for example, long-term interest rates and exchange rates that largely depend on expectations about the development of short-term interest rates. The assumption that the repo rate will develop according to the implicit forward rates means that the Riksbank's forecast takes into account that market participants actually make assessments of how the Riksbank conducts monetary policy over the economy and adjusts its actions accordingly. This is something that is not taken into account in forecasts based on the assumption of constant repo rate. The methods in the analysis and forecasting work have gradually been developed and our assessment is now that the approach used so far in the main scenario has come to be perceived as too strong a restriction, in some respects also for pedagogy. Knowledge of how monetary policy is normally conducted is now also so established that the benefits of making forecasts based on a more realistic interest rate path than the assumption of a constant repo rate outweigh the possible risks of changing interest rate assumptions from a communication point of view. Another disadvantage of an inflation forecast based on an assumption of an unchanged repo rate is that it is difficult to compare the Riksbank's forecasts with other analysts' forecasts that are not based on the same assumption. Since in most cases it is also unlikely that the repo rate will remain unchanged in a two-year perspective, it will also be difficult to make meaningful evaluations of the inflation forecast afterwards. If the repo rate has not been left unchanged throughout the two-year period, our forecasts should not normally come in. This is an important reason why the main scenario is still not based on the assumption that the repo rate will remain unchanged, but instead on the assumption that it will develop in line with market expectations. It is worth mentioning that Norges Bank and the Bank of England have recently made similar changes to their inflation reports. Choice of interest rate path There are a few different methods that can be used to illustrate a more realistic interest rate path than unchanged policy rates. One is that the central bank itself is trying to set an interest rate path that, at the time of the current forecast, it considers to provide the best target achievement. One option is to base the forecasts on market expectations about the repo rate. Information about these can be obtained through survey studies or indirectly through implicit forward rates that can be deduced from the so-called yield curve for interest-bearing securities with different maturities. In the new main scenario, we have chosen to base the inflation forecast on implicit forward rates, primarily because this is a relatively manageable way of reading market expectations and of producing a reasonable assumption for future monetary policy. However, for the monetary policy conclusions, in the most cases, it is not decisive whether the inflation forecast is based on market expectations according to survey studies, implicit futures rates or on a central bank-specified interest rate path. It should also be pointed out that the implied forward rates do not exactly reflect market expectations of future repo rates due to the presence of maturity premiums and other forms of risk adjustments, but they should nevertheless provide a good approximation. (3) In most circumstances, the implied forward rates are a more realistic assumption for monetary policy than the constant repo rate. The importance for the monetary policy strategy I would like to stress once again that the changes in forecasting that I have now described do not represent a fundamental change in the monetary policy strategy. Monetary policy will normally focus on bringing inflation to its target within a two-year period. The need for a slower adjustment to the target in the event of major deviations with the risk of large negative real economic effects will continue to be taken into account in monetary policy considerations, as in the past. The same applies to temporary fluctuations in inflation that do not need to be countered by monetary policy measures. It is important to realise that the assumption that the repo rate develops like the implied forward rates does not constitute a commitment from the Riksbank that this will happen any more than the assumption of a constant repo rate has been. Moreover, the transition to a main scenario based on the implied forward rates does not have any implications for the monetary policy strategy. Decisions on when to change the repo rate and by how much will continue to depend on a variety of assessments of how inflation and the real economy are expected to develop in the future. As usual, the Executive Board's analysis and conclusions on monetary policy will be presented in press releases and in the minutes of monetary policy meetings. The current monetary policy situation Let me now turn to how I see the current monetary policy situation. The upturn in the outside world continues despite oil and hurricanes In June, our assessment was that growth in the rest of the world would be good both this year and the next two years. But we felt an uncertainty due to the tendencies towards a slowdown that existed during the spring. In the United States, the signs of weakness noted in June looked temporary, while growth in the euro area had moderated more than expected. We therefore revised down the euro area assessment but still felt some concern that developments could become even weaker. The flow of information during the summer then mainly spoke in favor of a rather favorable development in the outside world. This meant that at our monetary policy meeting in August, we felt less uncertain about the assessment we made in June. The slowdown in the spring was temporary and growth in the rest of the world would continue at a good pace. As so many times before in recent years, oil prices have become significantly higher than we expected. This means that supply disruptions of various kinds easily create nervousness in the market with rising oil prices as a result. Over the past month, it is, among other things, the ravages of hurricanes in the Gulf of Mexico that have caused concern and caused the prices of oil and oil products to skyrocket. The reason, of course, is that a large part of US oil production and refining capacity is located in the area and there have been great fears that a significant part of that capacity would be wiped out for a longer period of time. It is still too early to fully assess the damage, but it seems that the oil sector has not been hit as hard as many feared. As in most cases with natural disasters of this kind, the consequences are primarily about great human suffering and also material losses for the inhabitants of those affected areas. Most macroeconomic analysts so far seem to expect that there will be no lasting effects on growth in the U.S. or the rest of the world from the events in the Gulf of Mexico. The assessment that the effects on growth will be temporary was also the basis for the US Federal Reserve's decision last week to raise its key interest rate by another 25 basis points to 3.75 percent. Growth in the US is likely to be lower in the second half of this year but is expected to rise again in the first half of next year, as reconstruction efforts pick up activity. Inflationary pressures in the rest of the world have so far been low, despite the fact that growth has been stronger than in many years. Good productivity growth and relatively ample spare resources have so far held back cost pressures in many countries, and the increase in low-cost countries' share of world trade has further helped to slow down the pace of price appreciation. However, the high oil prices have meant that inflation has become slightly higher recently than we expected and we will therefore in all likelihood have to adjust the forecast for international price developments slightly this year and next year when we set our next inflation report in just under a month' s time. Good growth in Sweden In Sweden, too, there was a slowdown in growth at the beginning of the year and it was new information that showed that growth in the Swedish economy was significantly weaker in the first quarter than we had expected before, which was the main reason why the Executive Board decided to reduce the repo rate by 0.5 percentage points at the monetary policy meeting in June. Although we assessed it as a temporary slowdown, this still resulted in us having to lower our forecast for growth and resource utilisation relatively much going forward and our forecast for inflation was thus below target throughout the forecast period. Even for the Swedish economy, the new information that then became available during the summer looked to confirm that the low growth in the first quarter of this year was a temporary slowdown. Growth strengthened in the second quarter and was then fully in line with our assessment in the June Inflation Report. At the same time, the growth figures for the first quarter were revised up slightly. This has led some observers to question whether we took in too much when we cut interest rates in June. But despite the fact that the start of the year was not quite as weak as it looked in June, our assessment is still that growth and resource utilisation this year will be significantly lower than we expected at the beginning of this year. Therefore, even if we had had access to the revised figures for the first quarter back in June, it would not, in my opinion, have changed the basis for the decision on the repo rate that we made at the time. At our August meeting, we chose to leave the repo rate unchanged. Swedish GDP growth was expected to be slightly higher in the coming years compared with the assessment we expected in the June Inflation Report, which was partly related to the reduction in the repo rate. Together with the rising oil prices, it justified some upward adjustment of the inflation forecast. Inflation was expected to return to its inflation target over a couple of years. As can be seen from the minutes of our August meeting, we in the Executive Board then agreed to leave the repo rate unchanged. Last year, it was exports that drove up growth. This year, exports will develop significantly weaker, but instead domestic demand will become more important as a driving force. In particular, consumption, both private and public, looks set to be stronger than we expected in June, which is partly a result of economic policy being more expansionary than was in our calculations in June. Business investment also continues to increase. The budget proposal presented on 20 September has a more expansionary fiscal stance than we expected in June. There are proposals for measures in both the area of taxation and expenditure to stimulate both private and public consumption and demand for labour in the private sector. Examples include increased ceilings in health and parental insurance, increased child benefit, a employment package over two years that provides the opportunity for a job, education or internship for 55000 people and an increase in the number of college places. The final stage of compensation for the general pension contribution is also taken. Most of the stimulus measures will be introduced in 2006 and, compared with our calculations in June, they can be estimated to result in some weakening of public finances and an increase in demand growth in 2006. Public consumption, especially municipal consumption, has developed weakly so far this year, while municipal finances appear to be strengthening sharply. This suggests that there may be a fairly strong development in municipal consumption in the future, especially next year. The situation on the labour market is difficult to assess. The change of method in the Labour Force Survey makes it unusually difficult to interpret the employment statistics. But now there are still signs that the labour market may be on the verge of brightening. According to National Accounts, the number of hours worked grew in the second quarter. At the same time, average working hours increased, which may explain the fact that there was no significant increase in the number of people employed regularly. As production increases, companies can initially do so by having already employed people working more, but sooner or later employment will also have to follow upwards. The fact that the number of vacancies is increasing indicates that companies have now begun to attract new employees. Another positive sign is that the notices are going down. In the second quarter, the number of hours worked increased above all in the construction and services sectors. The NIER's quarterly barometer indicates that there are continued plans to increase employment in these sectors. The high productivity growth in the Swedish economy in recent years has contributed to the weak development of the labour market, despite the fact that growth has been good. In the second quarter of this year, however, productivity growth slowed somewhat. There is reason to expect productivity to grow somewhat more slowly in the coming years for economic reasons than in recent years, as we move further along in the economic cycle. The contribution to growth from the export sector will then have less weight, while the contribution will increase from more domestically oriented service sectors with lower productivity growth. At the same time, there are signs that there was a more lasting increase in the growth rate of productivity during the 90s, which may have to do with, for example, IT technology and increased competition. Nevertheless, there are reasons to expect an increase in regular employment in the coming years. Resource utilisation provides an important basis for assessing inflation developments in the future. In June, we expected that the weaker growth would mean that resource utilisation would fall this year as soon as possible and then rise slowly in the coming years. This picture is likely to stand up quite well, although resource utilisation can now be expected to be slightly higher when growth in the future becomes somewhat stronger. It also allows inflation to rise slightly more than june forecasts assumed. When we discussed monetary policy in the Executive Board in recent years, the rapid growth in household borrowing and house prices has been part of the picture. One reason for the Riksbank to closely monitor the development of house prices and household indebtedness is that house prices affect households' saving and consumption decisions and thus also production and employment. This is something we must try to take into account when making our forecasts for growth and inflation. One question we then also have reason to ask is whether the development is sustainable in the long term or whether there is a risk that it will spiral away too quickly. The latter could lead to a more drastic adjustment down the line, driving the economy into a deeper and more protracted slump that will be difficult for economic policy to manage. These are risks that we must take into account when making our decisions on monetary policy. Our assessment so far is that the prices of single-family houses and also the increase in household borrowing can mainly be explained by traditional demand and supply factors. The low interest rate environment and increased competition in the mortgage market have helped to keep up credit growth. Demographics and migration patterns also play a role. The speculative elements of the Swedish single-family house market, which could contribute to the emergence of a house price bubble, are considered to be small. But this does not exclude that there may be future price drops. Ordinary cyclical fluctuations can affect demand and supply conditions in such a way that the prices of small houses fall. Our assessment is that households are generally able to cope with amortisation and interest expenditure even if the interest rate level were to be raised from the current level. But that doesn't stop there being many individual households that have incurred excessive debt. It is important to be clear that interest rates are now historically low, which suggests that sooner or later they can be expected to rise. As a borrower, you have to make sure that your own finances can withstand this. All in all, the more expansionary economic policy contributes to the fact that demand can be expected to be somewhat stronger over the next two years than we expected in June. This, together with the information that has come in since our last monetary policy meeting in August, suggests that, as then, there are reasons to believe in slightly higher inflation than in the previous inflation report in June. Inflation is currently very low, but the inflation outlook going forward suggests that it will rise. Recently, inflation has become higher than expected and this is mainly due to the price of oil. Adjusted for this type of temporary effect, there are still reasons to expect an upturn in inflation as the economy strengthens. However, good productivity and high competition will continue to dampen price increases. How these different factors will be weighed together into an inflation forecast and a monetary policy assessment, I will devote a large part of my time to until the Riksbank's next monetary policy meeting on 19 October. Det aktuella penningpolitiska lget Lt mig nu g ver till hur jag ser p det aktuella penningpolitiska lget. Som i de flesta fall med naturkatastrofer av det hr slaget handlar konsekvenserna i frsta hand om stort mnskligt lidande och ven materiella frluster fr invnarna i de drabbade omrdena. De flesta makroekonomiska bedmare verkar s hr lngt rkna med att det inte kommer att bli ngra varaktiga effekter p tillvxten i USA eller resten av vrlden av hndelserna i Mexikanska Golfen. Bedmningen att effekterna p tillvxten blir tillflliga lg ocks till grund fr den amerikanska centralbankens beslut i frra veckan att hja styrrntan med ytterligare 25 punkter till 3,75 procent. Tillvxten i USA blir troligen lgre andra halvret i r men vntas stiga igen under frsta halvret nsta r, nr teruppbyggnadsarbetet drar upp aktiviteten. Inflationstrycket i omvrlden har hittills varit lgt trots att tillvxten varit starkare n p mnga r. God produktivitetstillvxt och relativt gott om lediga resurser har hittills hllit tillbaka kostnadstrycket i mnga lnder och att lgkostnadslnderna kat sin andel av vrldshandeln har ytterligare bidragit till att hlla ned prisstegringstakten. De hga oljepriserna har emellertid medfrt att inflationen har blivit ngot hgre den senaste tiden n vi rknat med och vi fr drfr med all sannolikhet justera upp prognosen fr den internationella prisutvecklingen ngot i r och nsta r nr vi lgger fast vr nsta inflationsrapport om knappt en mnad. God tillvxt i Sverige ven i Sverige skedde en uppbromsning i tillvxten i brjan av ret och det var ny information som visade att tillvxten i den svenska ekonomin var betydligt svagare under frsta kvartalet n vi hade rknat med tidigare, som var det viktigaste sklet till att direktionen beslutade att snka reporntan med 0,5 procentenheter vid det penningpolitiska mtet i juni. ven om vi bedmde att det var en tillfllig avmattning resulterade detta nd i att vi fick snka vr prognos fr tillvxten och resursutnyttjandet framver relativt mycket och vr prognos fr inflationen understeg drmed mlet under hela prognosperioden. ven fr den svenska ekonomin sg den nya informationen som sedan blev tillgnglig under sommaren ut att bekrfta att den lga tillvxten under frsta kvartalet i r var en tillfllig avmattning. Tillvxten frstrktes under andra kvartalet och lg d helt i linje med vr bedmning i inflationsrapporten i juni. Samtidigt reviderades tillvxttalen fr frsta kvartalet upp ngot. Det har ftt ngra bedmare att ifrgastta om vi tog i fr mycket nr vi snkte rntan i juni. Men trots att inledningen av ret inte blev fullt s svag som det sg ut i juni r vr bedmning fortfarande att tillvxten och resursutnyttjandet i r blir betydligt lgre n vad vi rknade med i brjan av det hr ret. ven om vi hade haft tillgng till de reviderade siffrorna fr frsta kvartalet redan i juni hade det drfr, enligt min mening, inte ndrat grunderna fr det beslut om reporntan som vi d fattade. Vid vrt augustimte valde vi att lta reporntan vara ofrndrad. Den svenska BNPtillvxten bedmdes bli ngot hgre de kommande ren jmfrt med den bedmning som vi rknade med i inflationsrapporten i juni, vilket delvis sammanhngde med snkningen av reporntan. Tillsammans med de stigande oljepriserna motiverade det en viss uppjustering av inflationsprognosen. Inflationen vntades terg till inflationsmlet p ett par rs sikt. Som framgr av protokollet frn vrt augustimte var vi i direktionen d verens om att lmna reporntan ofrndrad. I fjol var det exporten som drev upp tillvxten. I r utvecklas exporten betydligt svagare, men istllet blir den inhemska efterfrgan viktigare som drivkraft. Framfrallt konsumtionen, bde den privata och den offentliga ser ut att bli starkare n vi rknade med i juni, vilket delvis r ett resultat av att den ekonomiska politiken r mer expansiv n vad som lg i vra berkningar i juni. Fretagens investeringar fortstter ocks att ka. Budgetpropositionen som presenterades den 20 september har en mer expansiv finanspolitisk inriktning n vi rknade med i juni. Det finns frslag till tgrder p bde skatte- och utgiftsomrdet fr att stimulera svl privat som offentlig konsumtion och efterfrgan p arbetskraft i den privata sektorn. Som exempel kan nmnas hjda tak i sjuk- och frldrafrskringen, hjda barnbidrag, ett sysselsttningspaket ver tv r som ger mjlighet till jobb, utbildning eller praktik fr 55000 personer och en kning av antalet hgskoleplatser. Det sista steget i kompensationen fr den allmnna pensionsavgiften tas ocks. Huvuddelen av stimulanserna infrs 2006 och jmfrt med vad som ingick i vra berkningar i juni kan de uppskattas ge en viss frsvagning av de offentliga finanserna och en kning av efterfrgetillvxten 2006. Den offentliga konsumtionen, srskilt den kommunala, har utvecklats svagt hittills i r samtidigt som kommunernas finanser ser ut att strkas kraftigt. Det talar fr att det kan bli en ganska stark utveckling av den kommunala konsumtionen framver, srskilt under nsta r. Lget p arbetsmarknaden r svrbedmt. Metodbytet i arbetskraftsunderskningen gr att det r ovanligt besvrligt att tolka statistiken ver sysselsttningen. Men nu finns det nd tecken p att det kan vara p vg att ljusna p arbetsmarknaden. Antalet arbetade timmar kade enligt nationalrkenskaperna under andra kvartalet. Samtidigt kade medelarbetstiden, vilket kan frklara att det inte skedde ngon ptaglig kning av antalet reguljrt sysselsatta personer. Nr produktionen kar kan fretagen till att brja med klara det genom att redan anstllda arbetar mer, men frr eller senare mste ocks anstllningarna flja efter uppt. Att antalet lediga platser kar talar fr att fretagen nu har brjat dra till sig nya medarbetare. Ett annat positivt tecken r att varslen gr ned. Under andra kvartalet var det framfr allt i bygg- och tjnstesektorerna som antalet arbetade timmar kade. Konjunkturinstitutets kvartalsbarometer tyder p att det finns fortsatta planer p att ka sysselsttningen i dessa sektorer. Den hga produktivitetstillvxten i den svenska ekonomin under de senaste ren har bidragit till att arbetsmarknaden har utvecklats svagt trots att tillvxten varit god. Under andra kvartalet i r dmpades emellertid produktivitetstillvxten ngot. Det finns anledning att rkna med att produktiviteten av konjunkturskl vxer ngot lngsammare de kommande ren jmfrt med de senaste ren, nr vi kommer lngre fram i konjunkturfrloppet. Bidraget till tillvxten frn exportsektorn fr d mindre tyngd samtidigt som bidraget kar frn mer inhemskt orienterade tjnstesektorer med lgre produktivitetstillvxt. Samtidigt finns det tecken p att det skedde en mer varaktig stegring i produktivitetens tillvxttakt under 90-talet, som kan ha att gra med till exempel IT-teknologin och kad konkurrens. nd finns det skl att rkna med en kning av den reguljra sysselsttningen de nrmaste ren. Resursutnyttjandet utgr viktigt underlag fr att bedma inflationsutvecklingen framver. I juni rknade vi med att den svagare tillvxten skulle innebra att resursutnyttjandet snarast faller i r fr att sedan stiga lngsamt de kommande ren. Den bilden lr st sig rtt vl ven om resursutnyttjandet nu kan vntas bli ngot hgre nr tillvxten framver blir ngot starkare. Det gr ocks att inflationen kan stiga ngot mer n juniprognoserna frutsatte. Nr vi diskuterat penningpolitiken i direktionen de senaste ren har den snabba kningen av hushllens upplning och bostadspriserna varit en del i bilden. Ett skl fr Riksbanken att noga flja utvecklingen av huspriserna och hushllens skuldsttning r att huspriserna pverkar hushllens sparande- och konsumtionsbeslut och drmed ocks produktionen och sysselsttningen. Det r ngot vi mste frska beakta nr vi gr vra prognoser fr tillvxten och inflationen. En frga vi d ocks har anledning att stlla r om utvecklingen r lngsiktigt hllbar eller om det finns risk att den skenar ivg alltfr snabbt. Det senare skulle nmligen kunna leda till en mer drastisk anpassning lngre fram som driver ned ekonomin i en djupare och mer utdragen svacka som blir svr att hantera fr den ekonomiska politiken. Det r risker som vi mste vga in nr vi fattar vra beslut om penningpolitiken. Vr bedmning r s hr lngt att priserna p smhus och ocks den kade hushllsupplningen i huvudsak kan frklaras av traditionella efterfrgeoch utbudsfaktorer. Det lga rntelget och kad konkurrens p bolnemarknaden har bidragit till att hlla uppe kredittillvxten. Demografi och flyttmnster spelar ocks en roll. De spekulativa inslagen p den svenska smhusmarknaden, som skulle kunna bidra till uppkomsten av en husprisbubbla, bedms vara sm. Men detta utesluter inte att det kan komma framtida prisfall. Vanliga konjunktursvngningar kan pverka efterfrge- och utbudsfrhllandena p ett sdant stt att priserna p smhus faller. Vr bedmning r att hushllen verlag klarar av amorteringar och rnteutgifter ven om rntenivn skulle hjas frn nuvarande niv. Men det hindrar inte att det kan finnas mnga enskilda hushll som har dragit p sig fr stora skulder. Det r viktigt att ha klart fr sig att rntorna nu r historiskt lga vilket talar fr att de frr eller senare kan vntas stiga. Det mste man som lntagare se till att den egna ekonomin tl. Sammantaget bidrar den mer expansiva ekonomiska politiken till att efterfrgan kan vntas bli ngot starkare de kommande tv ren n vi rknade med i juni. Detta tillsammans med den information som kommit in sedan vrt senaste penningpolitiska mte i augusti talar enligt min mening fr att det precis som d finns skl att tro p en ngot hgre inflation n i den frra inflationsrapporten i juni. Inflationen r idag mycket lg men inflationsutsikterna framver talar fr att den kommer att stiga. Den senaste tiden har inflationen blivit hgre n vntat och det beror frmst p oljepriset. Rensat fr den typen av tillflliga effekter finns nd skl att vnta sig en uppgng i inflationen i takt med att konjunkturen frstrks. God produktivitet och hg konkurrens kommer dock att dmpa priskningarna ven framver. Hur dessa olika faktorer ska vgas samman till en inflationsprognos och en penningpolitisk bedmning kommer jag att gna en stor del av min tid t fram till Riksbankens nsta penningpolitiska mte den 19 oktober.
