Title: The real estate market and economic development in Sweden
text: Srejber: The real estate market and economic development in Sweden Date: 2001-05-09 Speaker: Second Deputy Governor of the Riksbank Eva Srejber Location: SABO Byggnadsforsakrings AB Introduction To begin with, I would like to thank you for the invitation and the opportunity to talk about the Swedish real estate market. For the Riksbank, there is reason to follow developments in the Swedish real estate market both from a monetary policy perspective and from a financial stability perspective. From a monetary policy perspective, the real estate market is interesting, among other things, because house prices and the value of households' real estate holdings affect household consumption and savings. Just over 1/3 of households' wealth consists of single-family house properties. For households, savings in horrors are the single largest asset class. Real estate also serves as a pledge to loans, which is why, for example, rising real estate prices increase the loan space for households and thus demand in the country is affected. A functioning housing market is also important for mobility in both the housing and labor markets, which in turn is important so as not to hamper economic growth. From a financial stability perspective, the development of the real estate market is important because the banks, which have a central role in the payment system, are exposed to the real estate sector partly through lending with real estate as collateral and partly through lending directly to the property management companies. The report provided by the large Swedish banking groups on their credit portfolios shows that approximately 20% of lending to the public consists of lending to property management companies and the construction industry. If you add to that mortgages, lending to the real estate sector accounts for almost half of the large banking groups' lending to the public. These circumstances, as well as the fact that banking crises around the world have often been preceded by rapidly rising real estate prices combined with strong credit expansion, justify a special analysis of the real estate sector. As is well known, the real estate market consists of several submarkets. In addition to the single-family house market, we have the market for apartment buildings consisting of condominiums or rental apartments as well as the market for commercial properties consisting of retail and office space. Although apartment buildings and commercial properties have completely different types of tenants, price and rental developments in these two markets can serve as examples to illustrate the difference between a market with market-determined rents and a market with regulated rents. Rents in the housing market are regulated by utility-value-determined rents and the Rent Negotiation Act. Utility-value-determined housing rents and large subsidies for housing construction have been the main means of state housing policy's goal that everyone should have access to housing of a certain desirable minimum standard. Since regional growth in metropolitan areas is a dominant part of the growth of the entire economy and since price and rent developments in the real estate market have fluctuated most strongly in these regions, production continues to focus on these regions. Price and rental trends The price of a property reflects the present value of the property's expected return consisting of a net operating income and an expected future change in value discounted by a nominal required rate of return. Net operating income consists of the difference between rental income and operating expenses. An increase in the property price today can thus be caused by increased net operating income, increased expected future property price level or reduced nominal return requirement. Although rent levels evolve in line with property prices, expectations of future property price changes or changes in nominal return requirements can trigger corrections in property prices. Real price and rental developments for apartment buildings and commercial properties between 1987 and 2000 show that real estate prices for both apartment buildings and commercial properties significantly exceeded rental trends until the real estate crisis occurred in 1990. Extensive subsidies to the real estate market in the form of housing subsidies, interest subsidies, generous deduction opportunities for nominal interest costs and lower construction VAT combined with strong growth led to sharply rising property prices and increased expectations of future property price rises. Something akin to a price bubble had emerged in the real estate market. Between 1990 and 1993, there is a sharp adjustment in property prices. At the same time as the Swedish economy enters a recession, a comprehensive tax reform is being implemented that, among other things, entails reduced subsidies to the real estate market. During this period, GDP growth will decrease by between -1.1 to -1.8 percent per year, while subsidies for housing construction will decrease and construction VAT will increase from 13 to 25 percent. This leads to it becoming more expensive to build and use the properties and that the demand for both residential and commercial properties decreases. Prices for apartment buildings as well as commercial properties are falling. Market-determined rents in commercial properties are also falling, while utility-value-regulated rents in apartment buildings are increasing. As a result of the use-value regulation, the increase in costs will have a full impact on residential rents, while the reduction in demand will have no impact at all. However, property prices and market-determined rents in commercial real estate are immediately corrected. From 1993 onwards, the economy is slowly recovering and GDP growth is again showing positive growth rates. Demand is rising and property prices for both apartment buildings and commercial properties are increasing again, as are market-determined rents in commercial properties. By contrast, the use-value-determined rents of apartment buildings do not react to the increase in demand and develop at an unchanged pace. This reflects the steady long-term development of utility-value rents over the business cycle, while market-determined rents show temporary deviations from the long-term level due to demand-side or cost-side disruptions. Although the use-value principle has contributed to a level of rents levelling out over the business cycle, it has also contributed to the fact that apartment buildings with rental apartments are increasingly being transferred to tenant-owner associations in connection with the conversion of rental apartments into tenant-owner apartments. Since the utility value system limits the income that a rental property can generate, the market value of rental properties is also limited and both the owner of the rental property and the prospective condominium owners benefit from the property being transferred at a price somewhere between the market value of the rental properties and the market value of the condominiums. The value of condominium properties can be considered as the sum of the transfer prices for the condominiums included in the property. These transfer prices are market-determined and reflect the present value of the expected future change in the value of the condominium and the net present value between the value of using the condominium and the costs associated with the ownership of the condominium by the individual condominium owner. The cost of the condominium consists partly of the individual tenant-owner's share of the tenant-owner association's common costs for the management of the condominium property covered by the fee to the association, and partly of costs that are individual for the individual tenant-owner. The costs common to the tenant-owner association include, for example, property tax and operating and maintenance costs for the property. Interest costs after tax to finance the condominium purchase are borne by the individual condominium owner as well as certain operating and maintenance costs associated with the condominium. Thus, price and rent developments for metropolitan areas indicate that the increase in the price of commercial real estate from 1993 onwards has developed in line with rent increases, while the rise in the price of apartment buildings exceeds the rental trend according to the use value. The price development of apartment buildings does not reflect changes in income streams from the rental of apartments, since the sales of apartment buildings consist mainly of sales in connection with the conversion of rental properties into tenant-owner associations. Today's price level for commercial real estate is in real terms about 25 percent lower than the current price level in 1990, which was the year immediately before the real estate crisis. At the same time, today's rent level for commercial real estate in real terms is about 14 percent above the peak level of rents that was also noted in 1990. This indicates that the strong increase in the price of commercial real estate from 1994 onwards appears to be justified on the basis of fundamental factors and that the price level has developed in balance with rent increases. This is a significant difference compared to the four years before the real estate crisis in 1990 when the price level for commercial properties doubled while rents rose by only about 20 percent. Divided into the three major cities Of Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmo, Stockholm shows the strongest fluctuation in real prices for commercial real estate. Today's price levels represent about 70 percent of the peak level before the real estate crisis in 1990. The corresponding figures for Gothenburg and Malmo are 80 and 90 percent, respectively. A picture of whether the price development in the real estate market is sustainable in the long term can be obtained by studying how investors' nominal return requirements relate to the properties' dividend yield. A property's dividend yield indicates how large operating surpluses  the difference between rental income and operating costs  that a property is expected to generate relative to the property's value. The difference between an investment's total return and dividend yield can be assumed to consist of the compensatory increase in value that an investor requires to carry out a real estate investment at a given market price. By comparing the property's dividend yield with the investors' return requirements, a rough measure of investors' expectations of the properties' future increase in value can thus be obtained. A look at how the yield for commercial real estate developed over time in metropolitan areas shows that dividend yields fell relatively sharply in the face of the real estate crisis of 1990 as a result of, as we have previously seen, sharply rising property prices and largely unchanged rent levels. After that, dividend yields rise during the real estate crisis in line with falling property prices. In recent years, the real estate market has recovered again and the dividend yield has also shown a slight decrease during this period property prices have shown a higher growth rate than net operating income. The dividend yield for commercial properties based on the Swedish Property Index was on average 5.8 percent in 2000. The dividend yield for commercial real estate, calculated by SVEFA, in January 2001 was between 6.25 and 7 percent in Stockholm, between 6.5 and 9.5 percent in Gothenburg and between 6 and 8.5 percent in Malmo depending on the location. Better location means lower dividend yield, which indicates higher price level in relation to the rental level for the properties in the more attractive locations. The expected future change in the value of commercial real estate required for the property's total return to be in line with investors' return requirements is currently relatively low, indicating that investors do not base their investment decisions on exaggerated expectations of future property price increases. New production of real estate A look at investment in real estate in relation to GDP, the gross capital formation ratio in real estate, indicates that investment in the real estate sector lags behind the development of the rest of the economy. The gross capital formation rate for both dwellings and other real estate remains at unchanged low levels since 1994, despite the growth of the economy as a whole. After the real estate crisis in 1990, investments in real estate decreased sharply, especially investments in housing. Since then, construction has remained at an unchanged low level. The construction of rental housing in growth regions such as Stockholm has largely come to a complete standstill. The new construction of housing that is nevertheless coming into being consists largely of condominiums. The situation is well illustrated in Bengt Turner's article in the second issue of Economic Debate this year. The demand surplus for housing in Stockholm is reflected, among other things, by the rising housing prices. In 2000, the average price for tenant-owner apartments in Stockholm's inner city was around SEK 32,000 square metre, which is 33 per cent higher than in the previous year, despite the fact that new tenant-owned apartments were added by converting around 4,000 rental apartments into tenant-owner association-owned apartments. With a population increase of about 20,000 individuals in 2000 in Stockholm (net immigration about 14,000 individuals), the demand for housing increases. Despite rising house prices, only 1,074 dwellings were completed in apartment buildings in Stockholm municipality, of which 185 were leased in 1999. Cost and demand changes are allowed, as we have said before, to take effect on the market-determined rents for commercial real estate. Increased growth and increased demand have led to rising rent levels for this category of properties and new production of commercial properties is increasing throughout the country and especially in Stockholm. At the same time, the number of building permits granted is increasing, which is an indicator that new production is likely to continue to increase. Here, however, the downwardly revised forecasts of economic growth are likely to have some dampening effect on new production. To some extent, granted construction projects will not be implemented or postponed until uncertainty about economic development has decreased. The level of investment in commercial real estate is still well below the levels prevailing in the late 1980s and early 1990s. At that time, the maximum number of commercial space was 1.2 million square metres per year in the whole country, compared with just under 600,000 square metres in 2000. An indication that the real estate market is healthier today than it was before the real estate crisis in 1990 is that construction projects today in the Stockholm area will only begin when between 50 to 75 percent of the surfaces are contracted with tenants. Conclusion In conclusion, I would just like to say that this was a taste of our analysis of the real estate market. Anyone who wants to read about the real estate market from a financial stability perspective can read in our report on financial stability that will come in a couple of weeks.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Srejber: Fastighetsmarknaden och konjunkturutvecklingen i Sverige Datum: 2001-05-09 Talare: Andre vice riksbankschef Eva Srejber Plats: SABO Byggnadsfrskrings AB Inledning Till att brja med vill jag tacka fr inbjudan och mjligheten att tala om den svenska fastighetsmarknaden. Fr Riksbankens del finns det anledning att flja utvecklingen p den svenska fastighetsmarknaden bde ur ett penningpolitiskt perspektiv och ur ett finansiellt stabilitetsperspektiv. Ur penningpolitiskt perspektiv r fastighetsmarknaden intressant bland annat drfr att huspriser och vrdet av hushllens fastighetsinnehav pverkar hushllens konsumtion och sparande. Drygt 1/3 av hushllens frmgenhet utgrs av smhusfastigheter. Fr hushllen r sparande i fasigheter det enskilt strsta tillgngsslaget. Fastigheter tjnar dessutom som pant till ln, varfr t ex stigande fastighetspriser kar lneutrymmet fr hushllen och drmed pverkas efterfrgan i landet. En fungerande bostadsmarknad r dessutom viktig fr rrligheten p bde bostads- och arbetsmarknaden vilket i sin tur r viktigt fr att inte hmma den ekonomiska tillvxten. Ur finansiell stabilitetsperspektiv r utvecklingen p fastighetsmarknaden viktig drfr att bankerna, som har en central roll i betalningssystemet, r exponerade mot fastighetssektorn dels genom utlning med fastigheter som skerhet och dels genom utlning direkt till fastighetsfrvaltningsfretagen. Av den redovisning som de stora svenska bankkoncernerna lmnar betrffande sina kreditstockar framgr att ca 20 procent av utlningen till allmnheten bestr av utlning till fastighetsfrvaltningsfretag och byggnadsindustri. Lgger man drtill boln s utgr utlningen till fastighetssektorn nstan hlften av de stora bankkoncernernas utlning till allmnheten. Dessa omstndigheter samt att bankkriser runt om i vrlden ofta fregtts av snabbt stigande fastighetspriser i kombination med kraftig kreditexpansion motiverar en srskild analys av fastighetssektorn. Fastighetsmarknaden bestr som bekant av flera delmarknader. Frutom smhusmarknaden har vi marknaden fr flerbostadshus som bestr av bostadsrtter eller hyresrtter samt marknaden fr kommersiella fastigheter som bestr av butiksoch kontorslokaler. ven om flerbostadshus och kommersiella fastigheter har helt olika typer av hyresgster kan pris- och hyresutvecklingen p dessa tv marknader tjna som exempel fr att illustrera skillnaden mellan en marknad med marknadsbestmda hyror och en marknad med reglerade hyror. Hyrorna p bostadsmarknaden r reglerade genom bruksvrdesbestmda hyror och hyresfrhandlingslagen. Bruksvrdesbestmda bostadshyror och stora subventioner till bostadsbyggandet har varit de frmsta medlen i den statliga bostadspolitikens ml att alla skall f tillgng till en bostad av en viss nskvrd minimistandard. Eftersom den regionala tillvxten i storstadsregionerna utgr en dominerande del av hela ekonomins tillvxt och eftersom pris- och hyresutvecklingen p fastighetsmarknaden fluktuerat kraftigast i dessa regioner fokuseras framstllningen fortsttningsvis p dessa regioner. Pris- och hyresutvecklingen Priset p en fastighet terspeglar nuvrdet av fastighetens frvntade avkastning bestende av ett driftnetto och en frvntad framtida vrdefrndring som diskonteras med ett nominellt avkastningskrav. Driftnettot bestr av skillnaden mellan hyresintkter och driftskostnader. En kning av fastighetspriset idag kan sledes orsakas av kat driftnetto, kad frvntad framtida fastighetsprisniv eller minskat nominellt avkastningskrav. ven om hyresniverna utvecklas i takt med fastighetspriserna s kan frvntningar om framtida fastighetsprisfrndringar eller ndrade nominella avkastningskrav utlsa korrigeringar i fastighetspriserna. Av den reala pris- och hyresutvecklingen fr flerbostadshus och kommersiella fastigheter mellan 1987 och r 2000 framgr att fastighetspriserna fr svl flerbostadshus som kommersiella fastigheter kraftigt versteg hyresutvecklingen fram till dess fastighetskrisen intrffade 1990. Omfattande subventioner till fastighetsmarknaden i form av bostadsbidrag, rntebidrag, genersa avdragsmjligheter fr nominella rntekostnader och lgre byggmoms i kombination med en stark tillvxt ledde till kraftigt stigande fastighetspriser och kade frvntningar om framtida fastighetsprisstegringar. Ngot som kan liknas vid en prisbubbla hade uppsttt p fastighetsmarknaden. Mellan 1990 och 1993 sker en kraftig anpassning av fastighetspriserna. Samtidigt som den svenska ekonomin trder in i en lgkonjunktur s genomfrs en omfattande skattereform som bland annat medfr minskade subventioner till fastighetsmarknaden. Under denna period minskar BNP tillvxten med mellan -1,1 till -1,8 procent per r samtidigt som subventionerna till bostadsbyggandet minskar och byggmomsen kar frn 13 till 25 procent. Detta leder till att det blir dyrare att bygga och nyttja fastigheterna och att efterfrgan p bde bostder och kommersiella fastigheter minskar. Priserna p svl flerbostadshus som kommersiella fastigheter faller. De marknadsbestmda hyrorna i kommersiella fastigheter faller likas medan de bruksvrdesreglerade hyrorna i flerbostadshusen kar. Till fljd av bruksvrdesregleringen slr kostnadskningen igenom fullt ut p bostadshyrorna samtidigt som efterfrgeminskningen inte fr ngot genomslag alls. Fastighetspriserna och de marknadsbestmda hyrorna i kommersiella fastigheter korrigeras dock omedelbart. Frn och med 1993 brjar ekonomin lngsamt terhmta sig och BNP-tillvxten uppvisar terigen positiva tillvxttal. Efterfrgan stiger och fastighetspriserna p svl flerbostadshus som kommersiella fastigheter kar igen liksom de marknadsbestmda hyrorna i kommersiella fastigheter. De brukvrdesbestmda hyrorna i flerbostadshus dremot reagerar inte p efterfrgekningen utan utvecklas i ofrndrad takt. Detta terspeglar att bruksvrdeshyrorna hller en jmn lngsiktig utveckling ver konjunkturcykeln medan de marknadsbestmda hyrorna uppvisar tillflliga avvikelser frn den lngsiktiga nivn till fljd av strningar p efterfrgeeller kostnadssidan. Bruksvrdesprincipen har visserligen bidragit till att hyresnivn jmnats ut ver konjunkturcykeln men den har ocks bidragit till att flerbostadshus med hyreslgenheter i allt hgre utstrckning verlts till bostadsrttsfreningar i samband med ombildning av hyresrtter till bostadsrtter. Eftersom bruksvrdessystemet begrnsar de inkomster som en hyresfastighet kan generera begrnsas ven marknadsvrdet fr hyresfastigheter och bde garen av hyresfastigheten och de blivande bostadsrttsgarna tjnar p att fastigheten verlts till ett pris ngonstans mellan marknadsvrdet fr hyresfastigheter och marknadsvrdet fr bostadsrtterna. Vrdet p bostadsrttsfastigheter kan betraktas som summan av verltelsepriserna fr de bostadsrtter som ingr i fastigheten. Dessa verltelsepriser r marknadsbestmda och terspeglar nuvrdet av frvntad framtida vrdefrndring fr bostadsrtten och nuvrdet av nettot mellan vrdet av att nyttja bostadsrtten och de kostnader den enskilde bostadsrttsgaren har frknippad med gandet av bostadsrtten. Kostnaden fr bostadsrtten bestr dels av den enskilde bostadsrttsgarens andel av bostadsrttsfreningens gemensamma kostnader fr frvaltningen av bostadsrttsfastigheten som tcks av avgiften till freningen, dels av kostnader som r individuella fr den enskilde bostadsrttsgaren. Till de kostnader som r gemensamma fr bostadsrttsfreningen hr exempelvis fastighetsskatten samt drifts- och underhllskostnader fr fastigheten. Rntekostnader efter skatt fr att finansiera bostadsrttskpet brs av den enskilde bostadsrttsgaren liksom vissa drifts- och underhllskostnader knutna till bostadsrtten. Pris- och hyresutvecklingen fr storstadsomrdena indikerar sledes att priskningen fr kommersiella fastigheter frn och med 1993 utvecklats i takt med hyreskningarna medan prisuppgngen p flerbostadshus dremot verstiger hyresutvecklingen enligt bruksvrdet. Prisutvecklingen fr flerbostadshus terspeglar inte frndringar i inkomststrmmar frn uthyrning av lgenheter eftersom frsljningarna av flerbostadshus huvudsakligen utgrs av frsljningar i samband med ombildning av hyresfastigheter till bostadsrttsfreningar. Dagens prisniv fr kommersiella fastigheter r i reala termer omkring 25 procent lgre n den gllande prisnivn 1990 vilket var ret nrmast fre fastighetskrisen. Samtidigt ligger dagens hyresniv fr kommersiella fastigheter i reala termer ca 14 procent ver toppnivn fr hyrorna som ocks noterades 1990. Detta indikerar att den starka priskningen fr kommersiella fastigheter frn och med 1994 frefaller vara motiverad utifrn fundamentala faktorer och att prisnivn har utvecklats i balans med hyreskningarna. Detta r en avsevrd skillnad jmfrt med de fyra r som fregick fastighetskrisen 1990 d prisnivn fr kommersiella fastigheter frdubblades samtidigt som hyrorna endast steg med ca 20 procent. Uppdelat p de tre storstderna Stockholm, Gteborg och Malm uppvisar Stockholm den starkaste fluktuationen i reala priser fr kommersiella fastigheter. Dagens prisniver utgr ca 70 procent av toppnivn innan fastighetskrisen 1990. Motsvarande siffror fr Gteborg och Malm r 80 respektive 90 procent. En bild av huruvida prisutvecklingen p fastighetsmarknaden r lngsiktigt hllbar kan erhllas genom att studera hur investerarnas nominella avkastningskrav frhller sig till fastigheternas direktavkastning. En fastighets direktavkastning anger hur stora driftsverskott - skillnaden mellan hyresintkter och driftskostnader - som en fastighet frvntas generera i frhllande till fastighetens vrde. Skillnaden mellan en investerings totalavkastning och direktavkastning kan antas utgras av den kompenserande vrdekning som en investerare krver fr att genomfra en fastighetsinvestering till ett givet marknadspris. Genom att jmfra fastighetens direktavkastning med investerarnas avkastningskrav kan man drmed erhlla ett grovt mtt p investerarnas frvntningar om fastigheternas framtida vrdekning. En titt p hur direktavkastningen fr kommersiella fastigheter utvecklats ver tiden i storstadsomrdena visar att direktavkastningen sjnk relativt kraftigt infr fastighetskrisen 1990 till fljd av, som vi tidigare har sett, kraftigt stigande fastighetspriser och i stort sett ofrndrade hyresniver. Drefter stiger direktavkastningen under fastighetskrisen i takt med fallande fastighetspriser. Under senare r har fastighetsmarknaden terhmtat sig igen och direktavkastningen har ocks uppvisat en svag minskning under denna period fastighetspriserna har uppvisat en hgre tillvxttakt n driftnettot. Direktavkastningen fr kommersiella fastigheter baserat p Svenskt fastighetsindex var under r 2000 i genomsnitt 5,8 procent. Direktavkastningen fr kommersiella fastigheter, berknade av SVEFA, uppgick under januari 2001 till mellan 6,25 och 7 procent i Stockholm, mellan 6,5 och 9,5 procent i Gteborg och mellan 6 och 8,5 procent i Malm beroende p lge. Bttre lge medfr lgre direktavkastning vilket indikerar hgre prisniv i frhllande till hyresniv fr fastigheterna i de mer attraktiva lgena. Den frvntade framtida vrdefrndring fr kommersiella fastigheter som krvs fr att fastighetens totala avkastning skall vara i niv med investerarnas avkastningskrav r i dag frhllandevis lg, vilket indikerar att investerarna inte baserar sina investeringsbeslut p verdrivna frvntningar om framtida fastighetsprisstegringar. Nyproduktionen av fastigheter En titt p investeringar i fastigheter i frhllande till BNP, bruttoinvesteringskvoten i fastigheter, indikerar att investeringar i fastighetssektorn efterslpar utvecklingen i den vriga ekonomin. Bruttoinvesteringskvoten fr svl bostder som vriga fastigheter ligger kvar p ofrndrat lga niver sedan 1994 trots att ekonomin som helhet har vxt. Efter fastighetskrisen 1990 minskade investeringar i fastigheter kraftigt och d framfrallt investeringar i bostder. Sedan dess har byggandet legat p en ofrndrat lg niv. Byggandet av hyresbostder i tillvxtregioner som Stockholm har i stort sett avstannat helt. Den nyproduktion av bostder som ndock kommer till stnd utgrs i stort sett av bostadsrtter. Situationen belyses vl i Bengt Turners artikel i andra numret av Ekonomisk Debatt detta r. Efterfrgeverskottet p bostder i Stockholm terspeglas bland annat av de stigande bostadsrttspriserna. Genomsnittspriset fr bostadsrttlgenheter i Stockholms innerstad lg under r 2000 p omkring 32 000 kronor kvadratmetern vilket r 33 procent hgre n ret innan, trots att nya bostadsrtter tillkommit genom att omkring 4 000 hyresbostder omvandlats till bostadsrttsfreningsgda lgenheter. Med en befolkningskning p ca 20 000 individer r 2000 i Stockholm (nettoinflyttning cirka 14 000 individer) kar efterfrgan p bostder. Trots stigande bostadspriser frdigstlldes i Stockholms kommun endast 1 074 bostder i flerbostadshus, varav 185 upplts med hyresrtt under 1999. Kostnads- och efterfrgefrndringar tillts, som vi tidigare har sagt, sl igenom p de marknadsbestmda hyrorna fr kommersiella fastigheter. kad tillvxt och kad efterfrgan har lett till stigande hyresniver fr denna kategori fastigheter och nyproduktionen av kommersiella fastigheter kar i hela riket och framfrallt i Stockholm. Samtidigt kar antalet beviljade bygglov vilket r en indikator p att nyproduktionen sannolikt kommer att fortstta ka. Hr kommer dock troligtvis de nedreviderade prognoserna betrffande den ekonomiska tillvxten att ha en viss dmpande effekt p nyproduktionen. Beviljade byggprojekt kommer i viss utstrckning inte att genomfras eller skjutas p framtiden till dess oskerheten om den ekonomiska utvecklingen minskat. Investeringsnivn fr kommersiella fastigheter ligger fortfarande lngt under de niver som rdde i slutet av 1980-talet och i brjan av 1990-talet. D producerades som mest omkring 1,2 miljoner kvadratmeter kommersiell yta per r i hela riket mot strax under 600 000 kvadratmeter under r 2000. En indikation p att fastighetsmarknaden r sundare idag n vad den var infr fastighetskrisen 1990 r att byggprojekt idag i Stockholmsomrdet pbrjas frst nr mellan 50 till 75 procent av ytorna r kontrakterade med hyresgster. Avslutning Avslutningsvis vill jag bara sga att det hr var ett smakprov p vr analys av fastighetsmarknaden. Den som vill lsa om fastighetsmarknaden ur ett finansiellt stabilitetsperspektiv kan lsa i vr rapport om finansiell stabilitet som kommer om ett par veckor. Title: Low interest rates and tight credit spreads  a possible conflict?
text: Srejber: Low interest rates and tight credit spreads  a possible conflict? Date: 2005-10-05 Speaker: First Deputy Governor Eva Srejber Location: Nordea, Uppsala Let me begin by thanking you for the invitation to address you here today. I would like to take this opportunity to talk about the risks in the international financial system and I will do so by addressing a very specific aspect, namely the simultaneous existence of low long-term interest rates and narrow credit spreads. The reason why I have chosen this particular aspect is that, depending on how one looks at this combination, diametrically opposed conclusions are arrived at about the inherent risk in the financial system. But first, let me say a few words about how credit spreads normally tend to develop over time. Credit spreads reflect the premium that investors demand to buy risky assets instead of risk-free government bonds. The lower the quality of a security, the greater the compensation should be in the form of higher returns. Credit spreads are changing in line with the economic outlook. When times are good, companies' balance sheets are strong and the perceived financial risk is low, credit spreads tend to narrower. But when times are bad, corporate performance is pointing downwards and there may be financial turbulence, the differences in returns increase, as both the actual and the perceived risk are then higher. Larger credit spreads simply reflect the higher premium that investors require to take on risks. There seems to be what you might call a spread cycle. So what does this have to do with today's low long-term interest rates? Falling long-term interest rates are often seen as a signal from financial markets that economic growth is on the decline. This reasoning is based on the idea that the risk of inflation due to strained resources decreases during an economic downturn. This in turn means that the premium that investors require to invest in bonds with longer maturities to cover inflation risk will be lower. But if this hypothesis is correct, the same financial markets seem to be giving completely different signals at the same time through the historically narrow credit spreads. As I said earlier, credit spreads tend to widen when the economic outlook gets gloomier. That's obviously not the case here. Instead, spreads seem to be stuck at historically low levels. The downgrade of Ford and General Motors in May seemingly had no deeper impact on investors' risk appetite, as the risk bond market has since recovered. If you start from the credit spreads to get an indication of the future, the economy seems to be in as good shape as ever before. So how are we actually going to interpret these contradictory signals? Lasting effects One interpretation is that the low long-term interest rates do not at all signal an impending economic downturn(1). Instead, they are the result of effects on central banks and globalisation. Over the past 15-20 years, we have seen the emergence of independent central banks that have a clear mandate to achieve low and stable inflation. The Swedish Central Bank is one example. There is compelling empirical evidence that such banks have been successful. This definitely supports the argument that the equilibrium level of long-term interest rates may be lower than it was in the past. The globalization argument is mainly about markets being opened up to tougher competition, which, combined with China's and India's entry into the global goods markets, has pushed down consumer prices. We have also seen how technology, deregulation and institutional changes have had profound effects on the financial market. They have all contributed to lower transaction costs and created a plethora of new opportunities to share financial risks, leading to lower investment costs. These changes have certainly affected the inflation-related risk premium demanded by investors and have thus led to lower nominal and real long-term interest rates. The fact that countries such as China and India are now part of the global market economy may also have led to more stable global growth. In the past, the global economy had three engines: the United States, Europe and Japan. As new countries have entered world markets, the risk of a global economic downturn due to "engine stalling" has probably decreased. This, in turn, means that the risk of a decline in demand for goods and services has also become less, which may have made it less risky to lend money to the corporate sector as a whole, although the tougher competition means that the risk of an individual company having problems does not have to have decreased. Overall, developments may have contributed to lowering the risk premium and thus to lower real interest rates. Transient effects There is undoubtedly a lot in these arguments. On the other hand, low interest rates, at least to some extent, can also be the result of more short-term effects. The low U.S. interest rates, for example, are partly due to the strong demand for U.S. Treasuries from central banks in Asia and oil-exporting countries. If this demand were to fall, this would naturally affect interest rates in the opposite direction. In addition, it has been pointed out that pension funds have come to be more concerned with debt than asset management. The reason for this is said to be the underfunding of pension plans that have forced pension funds and insurance companies to increase the share of long-term bonds in their portfolios. Once these portfolio shifts are completed, the effects are likely to fade. Another possible short-term effect has to do with the sharp cost savings that companies implemented after the stock market's sudden decline from the high levels of 2000. As business investment declined, an important source of competition for capital disappeared. When there are fewer securities to invest in, but the demand for portfolio investments at the same time remains unchanged, interest rates will fall. Sooner or later, however, the corporate sector will have to make new real investments. Then competition for capital will again increase, which will lead to higher interest rates. In any case, if the impact of the structural changes resulting from central bank inflation targets and globalisation is strong enough, it is no problem to reconcile low long-term interest rates with narrow credit spreads. But there is also another possible explanation based on what Alan Greenspan, among others, has called the "pursuit of returns"(2). This concept is somewhat misleading because you have to take for granted that market participants are always chasing returns, but what it is trying to capture is the idea that investors have for some reason come to underprice financial risks. A global abundance of savings The interpretation based on the theory of the "pursuit of returns" is usually based on the increase in private savings that took place in developing and emerging economies in the wake of the financial crises of the 1990s in, for example, Mexico and East Asia. Because the outflow of capital had been devastating to many of the crisis-hit countries, some of them began to build up huge foreign exchange reserves as a buffer against future outflows. Foreign exchange interventions aimed at promoting export-led growth further fuelled the rapid accumulation of reserves in some countries. The change was reflected in rapidly growing current account surpluses. The rise in oil prices, for its part, led to growing surpluses in the oil-producing countries. These developments transformed many developing and emerging economies from net importers to net exporters of financial capital. As a result, there was what Ben Bernanke during his time at the Federal Reserve called "a global saving glut," which can perhaps most closely translate to a global abundance of savings. This saving was accommodated by the United States and some other industrialized countries. Rising demand for these countries' sovereign debt securities pushed down risk-free interest rates. But the most important event according to this interpretation was the stock boom. From the mid-1990s until the bursting of the technology bubble in 2000, stock markets played an important balancing role in international financial markets. As shareholders in developed countries watched their fortunes grow, they reduced their savings, leading to rising current account deficits. The stock crash and the resulting reduced investment opportunities could have put an end to this development, but this was not the case. As companies began cutting their costs to clean up their balance sheets, their demand for investment capital declined. To balance the market for global savings, real interest rates fell, causing house prices to rise sharply and triggering a search for returns. Low compensation for risks As government bond yields were already low, many investors, according to this interpretation, began to chase returns by investing in riskier assets such as commodities and composite credit products(3), without requiring full compensation for the increased risks. This development may have been fostered by the success of quantitative risk models such as the Value at Risk (VaR) model, which is based on the historical volatility of returns and correlations between different asset classes. Corporate bonds have had low volatility for years and since these bonds and risk-free assets are far from perfectly correlated, they are often a logical option to include in a diversified portfolio. Thus, there seem to be at least two possible explanations for the simultaneous occurrence of low long-term interest rates and narrow credit spreads that we can see today. The interesting difference between the two explanatory models is, at least from a central bank perspective, that they lead to diametrically different conclusions about the current systemic risks in global financial markets. The first interpretation, according to which low long-term interest rates are mainly due to structural changes that have led to a lower inflation premium, is that the situation is stable. According to the second interpretation, low long-term interest rates may in fact signal an impending economic downturn. The fact that credit spreads have not widened is due to the intense pursuit of returns that has led investors to underprice financial risks. Those who advocate the second explanatory model see the activities of pension funds, insurance companies, venture capital companies and hedge funds as symptoms. I will say a few words about the latter. Hedgefondsektorns expansion Hedge funds are normally valuable players in financial markets. Their search for arbitrage opportunities makes markets more efficient as it helps to correct any mispricings. By helping other financial institutions to get rid of some of the risks, hedge funds create important opportunities for risk transfers and risk diversification. But this time, the contribution of hedge funds to the efficiency of markets, at least according to the theory of interpretation based on the pursuit of returns, has perhaps been partially counteracted. Indeed, the huge expansion of the hedge fund sector may have amplified the mispricing that has manifested itself in historical low credit spreads. According to Hennessee Group, a global advisor to hedge fund investors, the number of hedge funds has doubled since 2000 and now stands at 8,000. Over the same period, the value of the funds controlled by these funds has tripled to 1 trillion. And as the Bank of England pointed out in its stability report, inflows into hedge funds have continued at a record pace, despite recent returns being relatively modest. To generate returns in the low interest rate environment, the fiercely competing funds may have increased their engagements in less liquid markets and in new asset classes, such as commodities and energy. In addition, many hedge funds seem to finance an increasing proportion of their investments with short-term loans. This is worrying. Assets with low liquidity along with a high loan-to-value ratio could prove to be a dangerous combination should interest rates rise or credit spreads widen. Potential triggers There are currently a number of potential factors that could widen credit spreads. One such potential factor is whether the large US current account deficit is adjusted by a sharp adjustment in the exchange rate of the dollar (4). If this were to happen, investors would demand compensation for the currency risk. This compensation would take the form of higher interest rates on U.S. bonds. There are so far no obvious signs of a steady decline in capital flow to the US. But it seems clear that financing the country's current account deficit depends in part on central banks being willing to accumulate additional dollar assets (5). A clear signal that central bank dollar appetite is declining would, of course, be a strong incentive for other investors to reduce their dollar holdings. The effects of a sharp depreciation of the dollar would not only affect the pursuit of returns, but in all likelihood also have a negative impact on global economic growth through adjustments to international trade patterns. A higher rate of investment worldwide would probably also lead to higher interest rates by shrinking the current "abundance of savings". This seems highly likely. After years of cost savings, the need for investment may be on the rise in both the private and public sectors. Increasing inflationary pressures could also be the trigger. This can lead not only to higher long-term interest rates, but also to higher policy rates. Financial markets appear to have largely anticipated a moderate and gradual tightening of monetary and exchange rate policy in the United States, while the ECB is expected to maintain its key interest rates for some time to come. If higher prices for oil and other commodities were to make an impact on consumer prices, this rather calm scenario could quickly change. However, it is not certain that the negative impact on credit spreads would come solely from rising interest rates. If rising oil and commodity prices do not affect inflation, they will break through into companies' production costs and weaken their financial base. An increase in U.S. savings, perhaps caused by falling home prices, or a marked economic downturn in the Chinese economy, would also negatively affect global growth and thus corporate profits. As market expectations for corporate profits are adjusted downwards, spreads will widen. If this in turn were to lead to business downgrades, credit spreads would widen further. Higher long-term interest rates and wider credit spreads would also affect the figures obtained through quantitative risk models. If this were to lead to a reversal of financial positions based on expectations of low or slowly rising interest rates, we would probably see corrections in many asset markets. This would be particularly problematic in a market with a high loan-to-value ratio. Closing discussion Today's combination of historically low long-term interest rates and tight credit spreads may well be due to central banks' successful inflation control and a favourable macroeconomic climate. Unfortunately, however, there may also be another, less pleasant, explanation that gives cause for concern about the financial risks that are accumulating. This explanatory model assumes that there is an intense hunt for returns in the sense that market participants underprice financial risks, thereby pushing interest rates and credit spreads down to unsustainable levels. The rapid expansion of the hedge fund sector in recent years can be seen as a symptom of this hunt. The increasingly fierce competition between the funds, combined with the limited opportunities for high returns, may have weakened the funds' role as gardeners clearing out mispricing from financial markets. Instead, there is some evidence to suggest that hedge funds may have contributed to such mispricing by increasing their presence in less liquid markets. Many globally operating banks also seem to have developed new business areas due to the low margins in more established financial markets. Thus, the expanded market for structured credit products and an increasing interest in prime brokerage activities, as well as in energy and commodity trading, may be due to the fact that the hunt for returns has escalated. These activities may have increased vulnerability to unexpected market developments, a problem that may have been further exacerbated by the widespread use of quantitative risk models such as the VaR models. VaR models normally estimate the likely market risk based on the assumption that historical volatilities and correlation patterns will continue to apply in the future. Less volatile assets or assets that are not closely correlated reduce risk in a portfolio. More recently, volatility in many financial markets has been below its historical average. These volatility figures feed directly into the models and can therefore influence the valuation of the perceived risk borne by companies and give them the green light to take on additional financial risks. The problem is that in a financial crisis, volatility increases while correlations tend to move towards one. The latter means that the prices of different assets change in the same direction more or less simultaneously. It also means that when you most need the risk-lowering effect of diversification, it may not be there. It highlights the need to conduct serious stress tests, such as what happens to the risk in a financial portfolio if the correlation coefficient between assets is 1. It is also important to remember that these models were originally designed to limit trading risks, meaning that they estimate the risks over very short time horizons of no more than a couple of days. Today, however, they are often used by company management to calculate risks for an entire financial year. This is done by scaling up the values obtained for very short time horizons, which are not always relevant for longer periods. In addition, most VaR models are based on a simplification of statistical assumptions. The essence of this is that they do not take into account the risk of very bad outcomes. One can only hope that decision-makers at different levels are well aware of these weaknesses if it turns out that the current combination of low long-term interest rates and tight credit spreads is a consequence of the riskier of the two interpretations I have discussed here today. Footnotes: 1) For a general discussion of business cycles, see imf's World Economic Outlook, April 2002. 2) See, for example, Alan Greenspan's statements at the International Monetary Conference in China in June this year (published on the Federal Reserve's website). 3) The development of the structured credit products market was discussed in the BIS Quarterly Review, June 2005. 4) For a discussion of how extensive such a change could be, see "Obstfeld, M & Rogoff, K, Global Current Account Imbalances and Exchange Rate Adjustments," May 16, 2005. 5) Denna fraga diskuteras i Roubini, N & Setser, B: "Will the Bretton Woods System 2 System Unravel Soon? The Risk of a Hard Landing in 2005  2006", februari 2005.

Datum: 2005-10-05 Talare: Frste vice riksbankschef Eva Srejber Plats: Nordea, Uppsala Lt mig brja med att tacka fr inbjudan att tala infr er hr i dag. Jag vill ta tillfllet i akt att tala om riskerna i det internationella finansiella systemet och jag skall gra det genom att ta upp en mycket specifik aspekt, nmligen den samtidiga frekomsten av lga lngrntor och snva kreditspreadar. Anledningen till att jag har valt just denna aspekt r att man beroende p hur man ser p denna kombination kommer fram till diametralt motsatta slutsatser om den inneboende risken i det finansiella systemet. Men lt mig frst sga ngra ord om hur kreditspreadar normalt brukar utvecklas ver tiden. Kreditspreadar speglar den premie som placerarna krver fr att kpa riskfyllda tillgngar i stllet fr riskfria statsobligationer. Nr tiderna r goda, fretagens balansrkningar starka och den upplevda finansiella risken lg brukar kreditspreadarna bli snvare. Men nr tiderna r dliga, fretagens resultat pekar nedt och det kanske rder finansiell turbulens kar skillnaderna i avkastning, eftersom bde den faktiska och den upplevda risken d r hgre. Strre kreditspreadar speglar helt enkelt den hgre premie som placerarna krver fr att ta p sig risker. Det tycks finnas vad man skulle kunna kalla en spreadcykel. Det hr resonemanget bygger p idn att risken fr inflation p grund av anstrngda resurser minskar under en konjunkturnedgng. Men om denna hypotes stmmer verkar samma finansmarknader samtidigt ge helt andra signaler genom de historiskt snva kreditspreadarna. Som jag sade tidigare brukar kreditspreadarna vidgas nr de ekonomiska utsikterna blir dystrare. S r uppenbarligen inte fallet hr. I stllet verkar spreadarna ligga fast p historiskt lga niver. Varaktiga effekter En tolkning r att de lga lngrntorna inte alls signalerar en annalkande konjunkturnedgng(1). De r i stllet resultatet av effekter som rr centralbanker och globaliseringen. Under de senaste 15-20 ren har vi sett oberoende centralbanker vxa fram som har ett tydligt mandat att uppn en lg och stabil inflation. Den svenska riksbanken r ett exempel. Det finns vertygande empiriska bevis fr att sdana banker har varit framgngsrika. Detta ger definitivt std fr argumentet att lngrntornas jmviktsniv kan vara lgre n den var tidigare. Globaliseringsargumentet handlar frmst om att marknader har ppnats upp fr hrdare konkurrens, vilket i kombination med Kinas och Indiens intg p de globala varumarknaderna har pressat ned konsumentpriserna. Vi har ocks sett hur teknik, avregleringar och institutionella frndringar har ftt djupgende effekter p finansmarknaden. De har alla bidragit till lgre transaktionskostnader och skapat en uppsj nya mjligheter att dela finansiella risker, vilket har lett till lgre investeringskostnader. Dessa frndringar har skerligen pverkat den inflationsrelaterade riskpremie som placerarna krver och har drmed lett till lgre nominella och reala lngrntor. Att lnder som Kina och Indien nu r en del av den globala marknadsekonomin kan ocks ha lett till en mer stabil global tillvxt. Frr hade den globala ekonomin tre motorer: USA, Europa och Japan. I och med att nya lnder har trtt in p vrldsmarknaderna har risken fr en global konjunkturnedgng p grund av "motorstopp" frmodligen minskat. Detta innebr i sin tur att risken fr en nedgng i efterfrgan p varor och tjnster ocks har blivit mindre, vilket kan ha gjort det mindre riskfyllt att lna ut pengar till fretagssektorn som helhet, ven om den tuffare konkurrensen gr att risken fr att ett enskilt fretag ska f problem inte behver ha minskat. P det hela taget kan utvecklingen ha bidragit till att snka riskpremien och drmed till lgre realrntor. vergende effekter Det ligger utan tvivel mycket i dessa argument.  andra sidan kan lga rntor, tminstone till viss grad, ocks vara resultatet av mer kortsiktiga effekter. De lga amerikanska rntorna beror till exempel delvis p den starka efterfrgan p amerikanska statspapper frn centralbanker i Asien och oljeexporterande lnder. Om denna efterfrgan skulle sjunka skulle detta naturligtvis pverka rntorna i motsatt riktning. Det har dessutom ppekats att pensionsfonder har kommit att gna sig mer t skuld- n tillgngsfrvaltning. Sklet till detta sgs vara underfinansieringen av pensionsplaner som har tvingat pensionsfonder och frskringsbolag att ka andelen lngfristiga obligationer i sina portfljer. Nr dessa portfljomplaceringar r avslutade torde effekterna att klinga av. En annan mjlig kortsiktig effekt har att gra med de kraftiga kostnadsbesparingar som fretagen genomfrde efter aktiemarknadens pltsliga nedgng frn de hga niverna r 2000. Nr fretagens investeringar minskade frsvann en viktig klla till konkurrensen om kapital. Nr det finns frre vrdepapper att placera i, men efterfrgan p portfljinvesteringar samtidigt r ofrndrad, kommer rntorna att sjunka. Frr eller senare kommer dock fretagssektorn att behva gra nya realinvesteringar. D kommer konkurrensen om kapital terigen att ka, vilket kommer att leda till hgre rntor. Om effekten av de strukturfrndringar som r en fljd av centralbankernas inflationsml och globaliseringen r tillrckligt stark r det hur som helst inget problem att f lga lngrntor att g ihop med snva kreditspreadar. Men det finns ocks en annan mjlig frklaring som bygger p vad bl.a. Alan Greenspan har kallat "jakten p avkastning"(2). Detta begrepp r ngot vilseledande eftersom man ju mste ta fr givet att marknadsdeltagarna alltid jagar avkastning, men vad det frsker fnga r tanken att investerarna av ngon anledning har kommit att underprisstta finansiella risker. Ett globalt verfld av sparande Den tolkning som baseras p teorin om "jakten p avkastning" brukar utg frn den kning av det privata sparandet som gde rum i utvecklingslnder och tillvxtekonomier i klvattnet av 1990-talets finanskriser i till exempel Mexiko och Ostasien. Eftersom utfldet av kapital hade varit frdande fr mnga av de krisdrabbade lnderna brjade en del av dem bygga upp enorma valutareserver som en buffert mot framtida utflden. Valutainterventioner i syfte att frmja en exportledd tillvxt spdde ytterligare p den snabba ackumuleringen av reserver i en del lnder. Frndringen mrktes i snabbt vxande bytesbalansverskott. Oljeprisernas uppgng ledde  sin sida till vxande verskott i de oljeproducerande lnderna. Denna utveckling omvandlade mnga utvecklingslnder och tillvxtekonomier frn nettoimportrer till nettoexportrer av finansiellt kapital. Fljden blev att det uppstod vad Ben Bernanke under sin tid p Federal Reserve kallade "a global saving glut", vilket kanske nrmast kan versttas med ett globalt verfld av sparande. Detta sparande ackommoderades av USA och en del andra industrilnder. Den stigande efterfrgan p dessa lnders statsskuldpapper pressade ned de riskfria rntorna. Men den viktigaste hndelsen enligt denna tolkning var aktieboomen. Frn mitten av 1990-talet fram till dess att teknikbubblan sprack r 2000 hade aktiemarknaderna en viktig utjmnande roll p de internationella finansmarknaderna. Nr aktiegare i de utvecklade lnderna sg sina frmgenheter vxa minskade de sitt sparande, vilket ledde till stigande bytesbalansunderskott. Aktiekraschen och de minskade investeringsmjligheter som den resulterade i kunde ha satt stopp fr denna utveckling, men s blev inte fallet. Nr fretagen brjade skra i sina kostnader fr att sanera sina balansrkningar minskade deras efterfrgan p investeringskapital. Fr att balansera marknaden fr det globala sparandet sjnk realrntorna, vilket dels fick bostadspriserna att stiga kraftigt, dels utlste en jakt p avkastning. Lg kompensation fr risker Eftersom rntorna p statsobligationer redan var lga brjade mnga investerare, enligt denna tolkning, jaga avkastning genom att placera i mer riskfyllda tillgngar som rvaror och sammansatta kreditprodukter(3), utan att krva full kompensation fr de kade riskerna. Denna utveckling kan ha frmjats av framgngarna fr kvantitativa riskmodeller som till exempel VaR-modellen (Value at Risk), vilka utgr frn avkastningars historiska volatilitet och korrelationer mellan olika tillgngsklasser. Fretagsobligationer har i flera r haft en lg volatilitet och eftersom dessa obligationer och riskfria tillgngar r lngt ifrn perfekt korrelerade r de ofta ett logiskt alternativ att ha med i en diversifierad portflj. Det verkar allts finnas minst tv mjliga frklaringar till den samtidiga frekomst av lga lngrntor och snva kreditspreadar som vi kan se i dag. Den intressanta skillnaden mellan de tv frklaringsmodellerna r, tminstone ur ett centralbanksperspektiv, att de leder till diametralt olika slutsatser om de nuvarande systemriskerna p de globala finansmarknaderna. Den frsta tolkningen, enligt vilken lga lngrntor frmst beror p strukturfrndringar som har lett till en lgre inflationspremie, r att situationen r stabil. Enligt den andra tolkningen kan de lga lngrntorna i sjlva verket signalera en annalkande konjunkturnedgng. Att kreditspreadarna inte har vidgats beror p den intensiva jakt p avkastning som har ftt placerarna att underprisstta de finansiella riskerna. De som fresprkar den andra frklaringsmodellen ser pensionsfonders, frskringsbolags, riskkapitalbolags och hedgefonders aktiviteter som symptom. Jag skall sga ngra ord om de sistnmnda. Hedgefondsektorns expansion Hedgefonder r normalt vrdefulla aktrer p finansmarknaderna. Deras skande efter arbitragemjligheter gr marknaderna effektivare eftersom det bidrar till att korrigera eventuella felprissttningar. Genom att hjlpa andra finansinstitut att gra sig av med en del av riskerna skapar hedgefonder viktiga mjligheter till riskverfringar och riskspridning. Men den hr gngen har hedgefondernas bidrag till marknadernas effektivitet, tminstone enligt den tolkningsteori som baseras p jakten p avkastning, kanske delvis motverkats. Hedgefondsektorns enorma expansion kan i sjlva verket ha frstrkt den felprissttning som yttrat sig i historiskt lga kreditspreadar. Enligt Hennessee Group, en global rdgivare till placerare i hedgefonder, har antalet hedgefonder frdubblats sedan r 2000 och uppgr nu till 8 000. Under samma period har vrdet p de medel som dessa fonder kontrollerar tredubblats till 1 biljon dollar. Och infldet till hedgefonder har, som Bank of England ppekat i sin stabilitetsrapport, fortsatt i rekordtakt, trots att avkastningen p senare tid har varit frhllandevis blygsam. Fr att generera avkastning i det lga rntelget kan de hrt konkurrerande fonderna ha kat sina engagemang p mindre likvida marknader och inom nya tillgngsklasser, som rvaror och energi. Mnga hedgefonder verkar dessutom finansiera en allt strre del av sina investeringar med kortfristiga ln. Detta r oroande. Tillgngar med lg likviditet tillsammans med en hg belningsgrad kan visa sig vara en farlig kombination om rntorna skulle stiga eller kreditspreadarna g isr. Potentiella utlsande faktorer Det finns fr nrvarande ett antal potentiella faktorer som skulle kunna f kreditspreadarna att vidgas. En sdan potentiell faktor r om det stora amerikanska bytesbalansunderskottet anpassas genom en kraftig justering av dollarns vxelkurs (4). Om detta skulle hnda skulle placerarna krva kompensation fr valutarisken. Denna kompensation skulle ske i form av hgre rntor p amerikanska obligationer. Det finns n s lnge inga uppenbara tecken p ngon stadig minskning av kapitalfldet till USA. Men det verkar st klart att finansieringen av landets bytesbalansunderskott delvis hnger p att centralbankerna r villiga att ackumulera ytterligare dollartillgngar (5). En tydlig signal om att centralbankernas dollaraptit minskar skulle naturligtvis vara ett starkt incitament fr andra investerare att minska sina dollarinnehav. Effekterna av en kraftig depreciering av dollarn skulle inte bara pverka jakten p avkastning, utan med all sannolikhet ven ha en negativ inverkan p den globala ekonomiska tillvxten genom anpassningar av internationella handelsmnster. En hgre investeringstakt vrlden ver skulle frmodligen ocks leda till hgre rntor genom att krympa det nuvarande "verfldet av sparande". Detta verkar hgst sannolikt. Efter r av kostnadsbesparingar kan behovet av investeringar vara p vg att ka inom bde den privata och den offentliga sektorn. Ett tilltagande inflationstryck skulle ocks kunna vara utlsande faktor. Detta kan inte bara leda till hgre lngrntor, utan ocks till hgre styrrntor. Finansmarknaderna verkar i stor utstrckning ha rknat med en mttlig och gradvis tstramning av penning- och valutapolitiken i USA, medan ECB frvntas behlla sina styrrntor en tid framt. Om hgre priser p olja och andra rvaror skulle sl igenom i konsumentpriserna kan detta tmligen lugna scenario snabbt komma att frndras. Det r dock inte skert att den negativa inverkan p kreditspreadarna enbart skulle komma frn stigande rntor. Om stigande priser p olja och rvaror inte pverkar inflationen kommer de att sl igenom i fretagens produktionskostnader och frsvaga deras finansiella bas. Ett kat amerikanskt sparande, kanske orsakat av sjunkande bostadspriser, eller en markant konjunkturnedgng i den kinesiska ekonomin, skulle ocks pverka den globala tillvxten och drmed bolagsvinsterna negativt. D marknadsfrvntningarna p fretagens vinster justeras ned, kommer spreadarna att ka. Om detta i sin tur skulle leda till nedgraderingar av fretag skulle kreditspreadarna ka ytterligare. Hgre lngrntor och bredare kreditspreadar skulle ven pverka de siffror som erhlls genom kvantitativa riskmodeller. Om detta skulle leda till en reversering av finansiella positioner som grundats p frvntningar om lga eller lngsamt stigande rntor, skulle vi frmodligen f se korrigeringar p mnga tillgngsmarknader. Detta skulle vara srskilt problematiskt p en marknad med en hg belningsgrad. Avslutande diskussion Dagens kombination av historiskt lga lngrntor och snva kreditspreadar kan mycket vl bero p centralbankernas framgngsrika inflationsbekmpning och ett gynnsamt makroekonomiskt klimat. Men det kan tyvrr ocks finnas en annan, inte lika angenm, frklaring som ger anledning till oro ver de finansiella risker som hller p att ackumuleras. Denna frklaringsmodell utgr frn att det frekommer en intensiv jakt p avkastning i den meningen att marknadsdeltagarna underprisstter finansiella risker och drmed pressar ned rntor och kreditspreadar till ohllbara niver. Hedgefondsektorns snabba expansion p senare r kan ses som ett symptom p denna jakt. Den allt hrdare konkurrensen mellan fonderna kan i kombination med de begrnsade mjligheterna till hg avkastning ha frsvagat fondernas roll som trdgrdsmstare som rensar ut felprissttningar frn finansmarknaderna. I stllet finns det vissa tecken som tyder p att hedgefonderna kan ha bidragit till sdana felprissttningar genom att ka sin nrvaro p mindre likvida marknader. Mnga globalt verksamma banker verkar ocks ha utvecklat nya affrsomrden p grund av de lga marginalerna p mer etablerade finansmarknader. Den expanderade marknaden fr strukturerade kreditprodukter och ett allt strre intresse fr prime brokerage-aktiviteter, liksom fr energi- och rvaruhandel, kan allts bero p att jakten p avkastning har trappats upp. Dessa aktiviteter kan ha kat srbarheten fr en ovntad marknadsutveckling, ett problem som kan ha frvrrats ytterligare av den utbredda anvndningen av kvantitativa riskmodeller som VaR-modellerna. VaR-modeller skattar normalt den sannolika marknadsrisken utifrn antagandet att historiska volatiliteter och korrelationsmnster kommer att glla ven i framtiden. Mindre volatila tillgngar eller tillgngar som inte r nra korrelerade gr att risken i en portflj minskar. P senare tid har volatiliteten p mnga finansmarknader legat under sitt historiska genomsnitt. Dessa volatilitetstal matas direkt in i modellerna och kan drfr pverka vrderingen av den uppfattade risk som brs av fretag och ge dem grnt ljus att ta p sig ytterligare finansiella risker. Problemet r att i en finanskris kar volatiliteten medan korrelationer tenderar att g mot ett. Det sistnmnda betyder att priserna p olika tillgngar frndras i samma riktning mer eller mindre samtidigt. Det innebr ocks att nr man som mest behver den risksnkande effekten av diversifiering kanske den inte finns dr. Det belyser behovet av att gra serisa stresstester, exempelvis vad som hnder med risken i en finansiell portflj om korrelationskoefficienten mellan tillgngarna r 1. Det r ocks viktigt att komma ihg att dessa modeller ursprungligen konstruerades fr att begrnsa tradingrisker, vilket innebr att de skattar riskerna ver mycket korta tidshorisonter p hgst ett par dagar. I dag anvnds de dock ofta av fretagsledningar fr att berkna risker under ett helt rkenskapsr. Det sker genom uppskalning av de vrden som fs fram fr mycket korta tidshorisonter, vilka inte alltid r relevanta fr lngre perioder. De flesta VaR-modellerna bygger dessutom p en frenkling av statistiska antaganden. Krnan i detta r att de inte tar hnsyn till risken fr mycket dliga utfall. Man kan bara hoppas att beslutsfattare p olika niver r vl medvetna om dessa svagheter om det visar sig att den nuvarande kombinationen av lga lnga rntor och snva kreditspreadar r en fljd av den mer riskfyllda av de bda tolkningar jag diskuterat hr i dag. Title: Unusual developments for market interest rates
text: Srejber: Unusual development for market interest rates Date 2005-04-14 First Deputy Governor of the Riksbank Eva Srejber spoke on Thursday at the Annual Meeting of the Association of Finance Companies at grand hotel in Stockholm. "Let me start by noting that despite the fact that growth has gradually risen since 2001 in both Sweden and the rest of the world, long-term interest rates have fallen to low levels in several OECD countries," Srejber began. "The fact that the fiscal situation in the US and in several countries in the EU has been weak at the same time for a number of years, and in some countries has become increasingly poor, makes the development of bond yields seem unusual. Weak fiscal policy usually leads to higher government interest rates, partly because the supply of government securities increases and partly because the risk for lenders is greater the worse the state financial situation is. At the same time, the crowding-out effect normally leads to higher interest rates even for private borrowers. Possibly the fact that, after several years of rationalisation, companies are well settled at cash and therefore do not yet need to borrow for investments to any great extent may partly explain the fact that the crowding-out effect has so far not been achieved," Srejber continued. "The low long-term interest rates are partly a result of monetary policy. International resource utilisation and inflationary pressures have been low. Central banks have tried to avoid inflation that is too low by lowering their key interest rates to historically low levels, and key interest rates are expected by markets to remain at a historically low level for a while in continental Europe and Scandinavia. This is also a factor behind the low bond yields," Srejber said. "Another factor that may have contributed to the falling long-term interest rates is that inflation expectations have fallen. Internationally, the trend towards more independent central banks and a clearer focus on price stability has continued. One consequence of this is that inflation in the world has fallen sharply since the early 1990s. Higher credibility for long-term low inflation reduces the risk premium in the bond market. In addition, the financial markets have continued to develop, which has led to higher liquidity and improved risk management, among other things. The combined effect of these factors could be slightly lower long-term equilibrium interest rates globally," Srejber said. "An additional aspect that is likely to have influenced global interest rate developments is asian central bank purchases of us dollars to their foreign exchange reserves, which have been invested in US government securities which has driven up the price of these papers and thus driven down the interest rate on them. However, it is worth recalling that of the total inflow of capital to the United States, the private sector accounts for the bulk. It is not the case that Asian central banks finance the bulk of the US current account deficit, but the purchases have still likely had an effect on interest rate developments in the US, which also affects other markets. A contributing factor to the fact that private investors are nevertheless interested in longer investments may be that in recent years there have been some regulatory changes for financial institutions, changes that, among other things, mean that liabilities should be marketed to a greater extent in the same way as assets. Similarly, several players have an increased focus on better matching the asset and debt side. The result is a greater demand for long-term investments," Srejber said. "Thus, there are a number of explanations for the historically somewhat unusual situation that long-term government bond yields have fallen to such low levels in recent years, despite the fact that growth has recovered at an increasingly rapid pace. It is worth noting that last year, global growth was the highest in about 30 years," Srejber continued. "But it's not just the government bond yield that's low given growth and the economic situation. The same applies to the premium companies need to pay to borrow compared to the risk-free government borrowing. This applies not least to bonds with high risk, partly on the corporate side and partly to bonds issued by emerging countries. The development of interest rates on emerging countries' bonds is interesting, among other things, in view of the fact that few fundamental economic factors have changed in these countries. For example, the debt burden of emerging countries as a share of GDP has not decreased significantly. Nor have there been major structural changes indicating that the rates of supply in these countries would be clearly higher in the future. All in all, this could indicate that financial markets are currently putting a historically low price on risk," Srejber said. "Interest rates are thus such that it is reasonable to ask whether risk is currently underpriced in financial markets. I don't have a clear answer, but there are some signs that lenders and investors historically tend to be slightly over-optimistic in good times when aggregate growth is good, bankruptcies are low and more and more companies are getting better and better ratings on their borrowing," Srejber said. "As the economy continues to strengthen and employment picks up, it is reasonable to believe that both long-term and short-term interest rates will return to historically more normal levels. How long this will take is uncertain, but the Riksbank estimates in the latest inflation report that real economic development internationally will continue to be strong and growth good, even if it has peaked. The picture for Sweden was similar. Recent information since the publication of the Inflation Report on March 15 suggests a development that is broadly in line with the picture drawn in the Inflation Report," Srejber explained. "Overall, I think there is reason to assume that long-term interest rates will rise from today's low levels to more normal levels in the long run, both in terms of risk-free government borrowing becoming more expensive and in terms of the premium for loans with risk rising," Srejber concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Srejber: Ovanlig utveckling fr marknadsrntor Datum 2005-04-14 Frste vice riksbankschef Eva Srejber talade under torsdagen vid Finansbolagens frenings rsmte p Grand Hotel i Stockholm. Lt mig brja med att konstatera att trots att tillvxten gradvis stigit sedan 2001 i svl Sverige som i omvrlden, har de lnga rntorna fallit till lga niver i flera OECD-lnder, inledde Srejber. Att den statsfinansiella situationen i USA och i flera lnder i EU samtidigt har varit svag i ett antal r, och i vissa lnder blivit allt smre, gr att obligationsrntornas utveckling framstr som ovanlig. Svag finanspolitik brukar allt annat lika leda till hgre statliga rntor dels drfr att utbudet p statspapper kar, dels genom att risken fr lngivarna r strre ju smre den statsfinansiella situationen r. Samtidigt brukar normalt undantrngningseffekten leda till hgre rntor ven fr privata lntagare. Mjligen kan det faktum att fretagen efter flera rs rationaliseringar r vl stadda vid kassa och drfr nnu inte behver lna till investeringar i ngon strre utstrckning, delvis frklara att undantrngningseffekten hittills uteblivit, fortsatte Srejber. De lga lnga rntorna r delvis ett resultat av penningpolitiken. Det internationella resursutnyttjandet och inflationstrycket har varit lgt. Centralbankerna har frskt undvika alltfr lg inflation genom att snka sina styrrntor till historiskt lga niver och styrrntorna frvntas av marknaderna ligga kvar p en historiskt sett lg niv nnu ett tag i Kontinentaleuropa och i Skandinavien. Detta r ocks en faktor bakom de lga obligationsrntorna, sade Srejber. En annan faktor som kan ha bidragit till de fallande lnga rntorna r att inflationsfrvntningarna sjunkit. Internationellt har utvecklingen mot mer sjlvstndiga centralbanker och tydligare fokus mot prisstabilitet fortgtt. En fljd av detta r att inflationen i vrlden har fallit kraftigt sedan brjan av 1990-talet. Hgre trovrdighet fr lngsiktigt lg inflation minskar riskpremien p obligationsmarknaden. Drtill kommer att de finansiella marknaderna har fortsatt att utvecklas vilket bland annat lett till hgre likviditet och frbttrad riskhantering. Den sammantagna effekten av dessa faktorer skulle kunna vara ngot lgre lngsiktiga jmviktsrntor globalt sett, sade Srejber En ytterligare aspekt som sannolikt har pverkat den globala rnteutvecklingen r asiatiska centralbankers kp till sina valutareserver av amerikanska dollar, som investerats i amerikanska statspapper vilket har drivit upp priset p dessa papper och drmed drivit ner rntan p dem. Det r dock vrt att erinra sig att av det totala kapitalinfldet till USA str den privata sektorn fr huvuddelen. Det r inte s att asiatiska centralbanker finansierar huvuddelen av det amerikanska bytesbalansunderskottet, men kpen har nd sannolikt haft en effekt p rnteutvecklingen i USA, vilket ven pverkar andra marknader. En bidragande orsak till att privata placerare trots det r intresserade av lngre placeringar kan vara att det under senare r skett vissa regelfrndringar fr finansiella institutioner, frndringar som bland annat innebr att skulder i strre utstrckning ska marknadsvrderas p samma stt som tillgngar. Likas finns hos flera aktrer ett kat fokus p att bttre matcha tillgngs- och skuldsidan. Resultatet r en strre efterfrgan p lnga placeringar, sade Srejber. Det finns sledes ett antal frklaringar till den historiskt ngot ovanliga situationen att de lnga statsobligationsrntorna har fallit till s lga niver under senare r, trots att tillvxten terhmtat sig i en allt snabbare takt. Det r vrt att notera att frra ret var den globala tillvxten den hgsta p cirka 30 r, fortsatte Srejber. Men det r inte bara rntan p statsobligationer som r lg givet tillvxten och konjunkturlget. Detsamma gller den premie fretagen behver betala fr att lna jmfrt med den riskfria statliga upplningen. Det gller inte minst obligationer med hg risk, dels p fretagssidan, dels obligationer utstllda av tillvxtlnder. Utvecklingen vad gller rntor p tillvxtlndernas obligationer r intressant bland annat mot bakgrund av att f fundamentala ekonomiska faktorer har ndrats i dessa lnder. Till exempel har tillvxtlnders skuldbrda som andel av BNP inte minskat ptagligt. Inte heller har det skett stora strukturfrndringar som indikerar att tillvttakterna i dessa lnder skulle bli tydligt hgre framver. Sammantaget kan detta indikera att finansmarknaderna fr nrvarande stter ett historiskt lgt pris p risk, sade Srejber. Rnteniverna r sledes sdana att det r rimligt att frga sig om risk fr nrvarande r underprissatt p finansmarknaderna.
