Title: Saving and inflation
text: Srejber: Savings and Inflation Date: 2003-11-19 Speaker: First Deputy Governor of the Riksbank Eva Srejber Location: Framtidsbyggets, Sparbanken Uplands and Ff6reningsSparbankens konferens. University Building, Uppsala Introduction I would like to start by thanking you for the invitation to come here and speak at framtidsbyggets, Sparbanksstiftelsen Uplands and Ff6reningssparbanken's annual conference. In my speech today, I intend to talk about the regulations for stabilization policy, what it has looked like, especially over the past 30 years, but also about the challenges that an aging population may pose to the regulations we now have. In particular, I will dwell on questions about the role of saving in this context. From the magazine Lyckoslanten's cartoon characters Save and Waste, we learned that in all situations it was better to save than to spend. Of course, it is not that simple, but we can at least state that during the 1970s and 1980s we lived beyond our means. For that we have had to pay dearly, as everyone who has been through the crisis years of the 1990s is well aware of. New challenges for stabilization policy also await in the future, for example in connection with the ageing of our population and the increase in the dependency ratio of society. An important question is whether we are saving enough today to reduce the burden on future generations? Will the public sector be able to cope with the dependency ratio in the future? And is private savings today, both quantitatively and qualitatively, adapted to future stresses as the proportion of pensioners increases? The deregulations that have taken place in the financial markets, the changes in the tax system and the regime change in stabilization policy have radically changed and improved the conditions for both savings and resource allocation to take place in a socio-economically more efficient way. However, the imbalances that built up during the 1970s and 80s contributed to the fact that the adjustments to the necessary structural changes led to large socio-economic costs. It is only in recent years that the economy is less characterised by processes of adaptation to the major structural shifts. But the change in the direction of stabilization policy has not yet been subjected to any really great strain. The adjustment to low inflation made in the 1990s has taken place during a period of relatively low resource utilisation and would of course have been more difficult if resource utilisation had instead been high. A major challenge for the political system and for low-inflation policy will be to cope with the adaptation to the fact that Sweden's population, just as in many other countries, for example in the rest of Europe and in Japan, is getting older. With such demographic developments, in which the proportion of the working-age population is becoming smaller and smaller, we must succeed in increasing productivity sufficiently to avoid lower potential growth in the long term. An important task of the political system is therefore to take measures to reduce the pressures of demographic development in the future. Without sufficient efforts, there may be a risk that the achievements we have made in maintaining price stability will again be lost and the costs of adapting to demographic change will thus be unnecessarily high. History horrifies History shows that the political system has previously been inclined to deal with situations of reduced consumption space in a way that has led to inflation picking up. The consequences of the inflationary stabilization policies of the 1970s and 80s are discouraging and are still relatively fresh in the memory. It is true that politicians have often learned lessons from past mistakes and periods of hyperinflation have been followed, for example, by periods in which economic policies have prioritised and achieved price stability. However, the various systems created to maintain such a development have generally not held up when they have been subjected to really severe stresses. One could liken the economic policy regulatory framework or system to a corset. It works well as long as you stay in shape, exercise regularly and eat just the right amount. If you suspect that the corset can be stretched out a little and fall for the temptation to skip the jog to instead sit on the couch and put in too much good food for a longer period, well then the corset will eventually burst! The gold standard, which was temporarily abandoned during World War I, was reintroduced after a period of high inflation in many countries, in May 1925. However, the system collapsed in the early 1930s in connection with the Depression. An important factor was that the reintroduction had chosen to link the currencies to the exchange rates against gold that prevailed before the war, despite large differences in price developments during the period of floating exchange rates. The under- and overvaluation of the various currencies contributed to overheating in some countries and unemployment in others, and the fiscal and monetary policy situation was not managed. Another example is the Bretton Woods system, which had "anchors" in the form of gold via the US dollar's connection to gold, and was introduced after World War II and with the problems of the 1920s and 30s in relatively recent memory. This "corset" also broke down, partly because the US sought to partly finance its budget deficit via the printing presses. But experiences that lie some way back in time have had a tendency to fall into oblivion and when the economy has been subjected to new stresses, the political system has again chosen solutions where inflation has had to take care of the necessary redistributions and adjustments. For the individual citizen, there is a strong interest in preserving the value of money. A high and variable price development creates uncertainty about the future - both for households and companies. Unexpectedly high inflation erodes the purchasing power of saved funds. The economy as a whole works less efficiently because the signals of the price system become less clear, which in turn leads to a poorer allocation of resources. It is not surprising that, before the introduction of democracy, those in power chose to finance war via the banknote presses. The population certainly became poorer but the king was able to continue to rule. But even democratically elected governments, even in peacetime, have for long periods pursued policies that have led to high and variable inflation. One such example is the Swedish bridging policy in the 1970s and 80s. The reason, of course, is that it has been all too tempting to "reap" political gains by driving the economy into overdrive in order to achieve short-term employment gains and introducing reforms with spending increases that could not be financed from the budget. For Sweden, the mistakes of the 1970s and 80s led to a change in stabilization policy. Gradually, we gained a stable monetary value and sound government finances, expenditure ceilings and balance targets for fiscal policy, and credibility around the inflation target of monetary policy. Demographic developments can be a challenge for the political system. A major challenge to the political system, as I mentioned earlier, comes from labour supply and population structure over the next few decades. Roughly speaking, two trends can be distinguished when it comes to population development in Sweden. On the one hand, we have fewer and fewer children per family. On the one hand, we are living longer and longer. Compared to about 100 years ago, life expectancy in Sweden today is about 20 years higher for men and almost 25 years higher for women on average! The development has been rapid even in the last 50 years. Life expectancy in the years 1951-1960 was about 70.9 for men and 74.1 for women compared to 77.7 years for men and 82.1 years for women in 2002. In the 1990s alone, life expectancy increased by over 1 year for women and by more than 2 years for men. Statistics Sweden's forecast for population development up to 2050 shows a shift upwards in the age structure where almost one in four citizens are 65 years or older by the middle of the century! The redistribution system Sweden has today was created during a period with a relatively large proportion of the population in the labor force and with a high employment rate. In Sweden, a large part of pensions in the coming decades will still be financed from public budgets. In order to cope with the burdens of increased pension expenditure, the government and parliament must, among other things, ensure that the public sector keeps down other expenses and ensure that tax bases grow. The so-called surplus target, i.e. a surplus of 2 per cent on average over a business cycle, reduces government debt as a share of GDP and the interest burden. The surplus is invested in the AP Funds, which increases the scope for future pension payments as a percentage of GDP. In order for the tax bases to grow, demands are placed on the labor supply and that growth is kept up. Thus, in order for the state to be able to meet its pension obligations in the future, it is necessary to maintain both the budget target and continued growth, although the burden could be alleviated by reforms such as raising the retirement age. But then what can we say about the need for private savings in the coming years? It is likely that increased savings will lead to lower real interest rates and thus higher investments. However, in well-developed and internationalized markets, savings will be channeled into objects with the highest real return regardless of the country in which the investments are made. For an individual country, this may mean that expenditure on consumption and investment is below the income from production in a given period and that the country shows a current account surplus. If the age composition differs greatly between the countries of the world, it is reasonable for part of the savings in a country with an aging population to be channeled to investments in countries with an opposite population development, since the propensity to save is probably lower in a country with a population that is getting younger on average. This could suggest that Sweden and countries with the same population structure need to have a current account surplus during the years when the propensity to save increases and that savings are channeled to economies with a population that is getting younger. Current account surpluses, i.e. saving in other countries, mean that in future we could take up some of the external - probably emerging markets and the USA - production via current account deficits. We can state that since the mid-1990s we have had an annual current account surplus of about 4% of GDP. Household and central government gross savings have partly been channelled into real investments within Sweden, but to a much greater extent to financial savings abroad. The question is to what extent an unfavorable investment climate in Sweden has contributed to dampening investment in our country? Another but related question is, of course, whether households' consumption and saving decisions were based on reasonable assumptions about the future? Here, confidence in the state's ability to meet its pension obligations and commitments on, for example, health and social care plays an important role. Reforms have increased resource allocation efficiency and created favourable conditions for growth Although many questions remain regarding saving, it is clear that deregulation and the reorientation of stabilisation policies have contributed to more effective savings decisions. The choice between consumption, savings and investment is influenced by a variety of factors. History shows that market economy solutions where tax systems and other regulations do not control resource allocation provide better conditions for growth and prosperity. In general, predictability is also beneficial for investments. Here, of course, price stability is an important factor. Well-developed capital markets also allow savers and investors to quickly find each other at low costs. There, risks are also assessed and disseminated so that those who save do not have to take greater risks than necessary. The greater the risks of not getting back your saved funds plus the real return you want for postponing your consumption, the greater the compensation you require to lend your money. The same applies if you are forced to tie up your money for a long time without having the opportunity to use it. Lower inflation expectations thus reduce the compensation requirement for those who lend their money. Until the mid-1980s, virtually none of these growth-promoting conditions were in place in Sweden. Until then, both borrowing and lending rates were set by the state while there were restrictions on how much and for what purposes the banks could give credit. Exchange regulation also limited the ability to save and borrow in foreign banks or on foreign securities markets. The breathing hole of the companies was that they could reinvest their earnings. Foreign investors were also not allowed to freely buy Swedish securities. At the same time, the tax system favored borrowers over savers. During parts of the 1980s, the system of interest deductions contributed to people being paid in practice to borrow but having to pay to save. And last but not least - high and variable inflation made it unsafe to save because one could not be sure how the purchasing power of the saved funds would develop. This held back savings and also the willingness to invest. During the 1980s and early 1990s, changes were implemented that radically improved conditions in the capital market. First, the credit market was deregulated, then currency regulation was abolished and the tax system changed. And last but not least, the stabilization policy was changed with the aim of clear regulations and price stability. As we know, neither the financial sector, nor the public, nor the authorities were prepared for the effects of the changes that took place in the 1980s, although lessons were learned in terms of the time sequence of changes in other countries. Monetary policy was tied to defending the fixed exchange rate. Nevertheless, fiscal policy, which had full responsibility for stabilisation policy at the time, was not sufficiently adjusted to mitigate the overheating caused by credit deregulation. In the late 1980s and early 1990s, unemployment was very low while inflation in 1990 reached over 10 percent! In addition, there is the search for market share by financial institutions, combined with the fact that supervision was not sufficiently well developed. As we know, the adjustment costs were high because very large imbalances had been building up over such a long period of time. We clearly remember both the banking and currency crises of the early 1990s and the recession that followed. Overall unemployment was between 9-12 percent in 1993, depending on how you measure. The negative experience of the hyperinflationary economy led, after the crises, to a new regulatory framework for fiscal policy and a monetary policy geared towards price stability. At the same time, the banking crisis meant that regulatory frameworks, supervision and crisis management to reduce the risks of new crises have developed in a favourable way. After the large and socio-economically costly adjustments, it now seems that the low-inflation economy has been established in earnest. The Riksbank's independence and a statutory price stability target, as well as a balance target and expenditure ceiling for fiscal policy, have contributed to this. The framework built up for both fiscal and monetary policy should also ensure more stable developments going forward. EU membership has also been important in this context. The conditions for households to make decisions about savings in a socio-economically efficient way should therefore now be significantly better than before. Liberalised and efficient capital markets should thus have contributed to the channelling of resources in a way that is more efficient from a socio-economic perspective. Savings have been strongly affected by the structural changes that have taken place The structural changes in the Swedish economy over the past 20 years have been very clearly reflected in financial saving in various sectors. Since I want to highlight the role of savings in the economy today, I want to give a look back at how savings have developed over the past 20-30 years. In the long term, it is reasonable to assume that a country must adjust its expenditure to the income it receives for what it produces. The age composition of the population, as I mentioned, can justify current account surpluses or deficits during a transitional period, which can sometimes also be quite long. The desire to keep one relatively even consumption during one's lifetime means that you need to save during your working life in order to then be able to use the money as a pensioner. An alternative to this is that we commit ourselves via taxes to support our elderly during the period we work towards ourselves being supported when we become pensioners. Then the private savings may be lower. However, problems arise with this system if the age composition of the population varies greatly over time. This applies, for example, to the united states. Sweden because we have an aging population. During periods with a large proportion of pensioners, the burden on those who work will be very onerous. To avoid this, each generation should save for its own old age and ensure that savings are capitalized in a good way. This can be done either through private or state-organized pension savings. The stabilization policy's focus on short-term employment during the 1970s and 80s was one of the factors that led to the swedish economy's savings being negative for a long time. During these years, we consumed too much relative to the production space, resulting in high inflation, continuous current account deficits and growing external debt. This is despite the fact that the population structure was such that the burden on future generations would be heavy if we did not save enough. During the overheating period in the late 1980s, financial saving in the private sector was sharply negative - this applied to both firms and households. While this was compensated to some extent by the rise in general government savings as a result of overheating, it was not sufficiently compensated to avoid large current account deficits. In part, the negative development of financial saving was due to an increase in real investment, but in the second half of the 1980s investments were largely made in commercial real estate, which was characterised by overproduction. Such investments hardly increased our ability to pay interest on our foreign loans or created future consumption opportunities. Even in the past, large misinvestments had been made due to the fact that regulated markets, recurrent devaluations and the design of the tax system meant that resources were not channelled in a socio-economically efficient way. In conclusion, it can thus be said that we neither saved enough nor invested in such a way that we fully improved our production capabilities. During the crisis years of the early 1990s, both companies and households raised their savings sharply. This was due both to the need for consolidation after the loan carousel, but also to increased uncertainty about the future. At the same time, real interest rates after tax were very high, largely due to the fact that it took time to sweep up the traces of the poorly managed stabilization policy and establish credibility for low-inflation policies. The picture is that high inflation expectations made it difficult to quickly lower interest rates, despite the fact that low capacity utilisation dragged down actual inflation. Of course, the high real interest rates also stimulated savings. The very weak growth of the economy, combined with the high interest burden on the state, caused public finances to deteriorate dramatically during these years. The current account therefore continued to show a deficit in the early years of the 1990s, despite the strong upward trend in private sector savings. The turnaround came in the mid-1990s. The international economy brightened and central government finances improved. This was partly a result of the turnaround in the economy, but also of the savings measures taken by the state. The so-called consolidation programme, which was presented in 1994 and then implemented between 1995 and 1998, included a total increase in public savings of approximately SEK 125 billion. The budget process was also later tightened and fiscal policy was provided with two overarching targets - a spending cap that limits government spending and a target for general government financial savings that should lead to a surplus of 2 percent on average over a business cycle. This, together with the stance of monetary policy, contributed to a fall in inflation expectations and a fall in interest rates. Private sector savings were thus very high after the crisis years, and as central government finances improved, the current account also started to show a surplus. Since in the mid-1990s, the current account has shown a stable surplus of around 4% every year! Although the private sector has cut its savings sharply, it is still significantly higher than in the late 1980s - a weak deficit was reported only one year, in 2001. In part, the decrease in the private financial saving surplus is partly explained by the rise in the investment ratio, but to a very small extent. Households have had a positive financial saving throughout the period. At the same time as private sector savings have decreased, public sector savings have risen. All in all, the Swedish economy has thus had positive savings in recent years. This means that we have given up public and private consumption in order to obtain income through net exports to pay the debts of the previous overconsumption. Sweden has thus significantly reduced its external debt since the early 1990s and our net position to foreign countries has improved. At the end of 2002, the statistics on Sweden's total net external position showed a Swedish net debt of SEK 553 billion, which corresponded to 24 per cent of GDP compared with net debt of around 43.7 per cent of GDP in 1993. The development means that the interest burden has been reduced. The fact that the interest burden has thus decreased means that a larger part of what we produce can be used for consumption in the future. However, given our age structure, it is probably not enough that we have managed to halve the old consumer debts. We probably would have needed - and need - to "collect more in the barns" when we have the chance. The challenges of the future. As I have already spoken about, history shows that there is a risk that frameworks built up for stabilisation policies aimed at price stability and stable demand developments will crumble if the political system is faced with situations where consumption opportunities are shrinking and policies are thus again tempted to be focused too short-term. The right choices are so difficult when the situation is urgent,. Admittedly, thankfully, the system seems robust at the moment, but no real tests have yet been put to it after the 1990s crisis. The fact that the age structure of the population is equally problematic in large parts of the EU means that the same risk exists for the common intergovernmental acquis, including the Stability Pact. The EU's Economic Policy Committee recently published a study on how demographic developments will affect member states' public finances. The study also provided estimates of how demographic change - including its effects on the labour market and capital intensity - will affect potential growth in the EU in the future. The calculations indicate that the demographic effect means that potential growth will fall compared to the average in the 1990s, to an average of 1.3 percent in the period 2000-2050. All other things being equal, this means that almost a third of the consumption space would fall away if no other measures are taken or enough savings are invested abroad. The desired consumption can be obtained through the disposal of savings invested in other countries. A net worth abroad means that we have a claim on future production in the outside world. When those who retire no longer contribute to production and it is then not enough for the desired consumption, it can, somewhat simplified, be replaced by imports financed by the sale of the shares and bonds we own abroad. When we start using our savings abroad, it will of course lead to a current account deficit. This in itself is hardly something to be concerned about, since for Sweden it has been preceded by surpluses for many years. If the savings invested abroad are not enough to maintain the desired consumption for Sweden with an older population, what are the ways to keep consumption up? On the one hand, we in Sweden must ensure that we increase our employment rate in the labour force and, on the other hand, we must increase our productivity! According to LU 1999/2000, a general government surplus in the public sector of an average of 2 per cent of GDP until 2015 and an annual growth of an average of 1.9 per cent between 1998-2015 will mean that the state will meet its commitments. Although this in the light of different assessments of the potential growth of the Swedish economy in the current situation does not appear to be an unrealistic scenario, it can be stated that in order to achieve this, private sector productivity must continue to increase, compensating for the low contribution of labour supply resulting from the unfavourable demographic shift. In the light of the above, however, it is desirable that the policy should already be clearly focused on creating the best possible conditions for growth. Even if savings and productivity were to be high enough, we still face major adjustments in the production of goods and services and in the labour market. Demand will shift towards services such as health and social care. The labour market must then be flexible enough to allow the transfer of labour to this service production without inflationary pressures.

Ett sdant exempel r den svenska verbryggningpolitiken p 1970- och 80-talet. Anledningen r frsts att det varit alltfr lockande att "kamma hem" politiska vinster genom att driva ekonomin p vervxel fr att uppn kortfristiga sysselsttningsvinster och infra reformer med utgiftskningar som inte kunnat finansieras ver budgeten. Fr svensk del ledde 1970- och 80-talets misstag till att stabiliseringspolitiken lades om. Vi fick efterhand ett stabilt penningvrde och sunda statsfinanser, utgiftstak och saldoml fr finanspolitiken och trovrdighet kring penningpolitikens inflationsml. Den demografiska utvecklingen kan bli en utmaning fr det politiska systemet. En stor utmaning fr det politiska systemet kommer som jag tidigare nmnde frn arbetskraftsutbudet och befolkningsstrukturen under de nrmaste rtiondena. Grovt sett kan tv trender urskiljas nr det gller befolkningsutvecklingen i Sverige. Dels skaffar vi allt frre barn per familj. Dels lever vi allt lngre. Jmfrt med fr omkring 100 r sedan r medellivslngden i Sverige idag omkring 20 r hgre fr mn och nstan 25 r hgre fr kvinnor i genomsnitt! Utvecklingen har gtt snabbt ven under de senaste 50 ren. Medellivslngden under ren 1951-1960 var ca 70,9 fr mn och 74,1 fr kvinnor jmfrt med 77,7 r fr mn och 82,1 r fr kvinnor r 2002. Bara under 1990-talet kade medellivslngden med ver 1 r fr kvinnor och med mer n 2 r fr mn. SCB:s prognos fr befolkningsutvecklingen fram till 2050 visar en frskjutning uppt i ldersstrukturen dr nstan var fjrde medborgare r 65 r eller ldre vid mitten av seklet! Det omfrdelningssystem Sverige har idag skapades under en period med en relativt stor andel av befolkningen i arbetskraften och med hg sysselsttningsgrad. I Sverige kommer en stor del av pensionerna under de nrmaste rtiondena fortfarande att finansieras ver de offentliga budgetarna. Fr att klara av de belastningar som kade pensionsutgifter innebr mste regering och riksdag bl.a. se till att den offentliga sektorn hller nere andra utgifter och se till att skattebaserna vxer. Det s.k. verskottsmlet, dvs. att den offentliga sektorns finanser ska uppvisa ett verskott p 2 procent i genomsnitt ver en konjunkturcykel, minskar den offentliga skuldsttningen som andel av BNP och rntebrdan. verskottet placeras i AP-fonderna vilket kar utrymmet fr framtida pensionsutbetalningar i procent av BNP. Fr att skattebaserna ska vxa stlls krav p arbetskraftsutbudet och att tillvxten hlls uppe. Fr att staten ska kunna fullgra sina pensionsfrpliktelser i framtiden krvs allts bde att budgetmlet upprtthlls och fortsatt tillvxt, ven om brdan skulle kunna komma att lindras av reformer som t.ex. hjd pensionslder. Men vad kan vi d sga om behovet av privat sparande under de kommande ren? Det r troligt att ett kat sparande leder till lgre realrntor och drmed hgre investeringar. P vlutvecklade och internationaliserade marknader kommer dock sparandet att kanaliseras till objekt med hgst realavkastning oavsett i vilket land investeringarna sker. Fr ett enskilt land kan det innebra att utgifterna fr konsumtion och investeringar underskrider inkomsterna frn produktionen under en given period och att landet uppvisar ett bytesbalansverskott. Om ldersammansttningen skiljer sig t mycket mellan vrldens lnder s r det rimligt att en del av sparandet i ett land med ldrande befolkning kanaliseras till investeringar i lnder med en motsatt befolkningsutveckling eftersom sparbengenheten troligen r lgre i ett land med en befolkning som i genomsnitt blir yngre. Det skulle kunna tala fr att Sverige och lnder med samma befolkningsstruktur behver ha ett bytesbalansverskott under de r som sparbengenheten kar och att sparandet kanaliseras till ekonomier med en befolkning som blir yngre. Bytesbalansverskott, dvs. att vi sparar i andra lnder, innebr i s fall att vi i framtiden skulle kunna ta i ansprk en del av omvrldens - sannolikt emerging markets och USA - produktion via bytesbalansunderskott. Vi kan konstatera att vi sedan mitten av 1990-talet haft rligt bytesbalansverskott p ca 4 procent av BNP. Hushllens och statens bruttosparande har till en del kanaliserats till reala investeringar inom Sverige, men i mycket hgre utstrckning till ett finansiellt sparande utomlands. Frgan r i vilken utstrckning ett ogynnsamt investeringsklimat i Sverige bidragit till att dmpa investeringarna i vrt land? En annan men relaterad frga r frsts om hushllens konsumtions- och sparandebeslut baserats p rimliga antaganden om framtiden? Hr spelar tilltron till statens mjlighet att klara sina pensionstaganden och utfstelser om t.ex. vrd och omsorg en viktig roll. Reformer har gett kad effektivitet i resursallokeringen och skapat gynnsamma frutsttningar fr tillvxt ven om mnga frgor kvarstr vad gller sparandet str det klart att avregleringarna och omlggningen av stabiliseringspolitiken bidragit till effektivare sparandebeslut. Valet mellan konsumtion, sparande och investeringar pverkas av en mngd faktorer. Historien visar att marknadsekonomiska lsningar dr skattesystem och andra regleringar inte styr resursallokeringen ger bttre frutsttningar fr tillvxt och vlstnd. Generellt gller ocks att frutsgbarhet r gynnsamt fr investeringar. Hr r naturligtvis prisstabilitet en viktig faktor. Vlutvecklade kapitalmarknader gr det ocks mjligt fr sparare och investerare att till lga kostnader snabbt hitta varandra. Dr bedms och sprids ocks risker s att de som sparar inte behver ta strre risker n ndvndigt. Ju strre riskerna r fr att man inte fr tillbaka sina sparade medel plus den reala avkastning man vill ha fr att skjuta upp sin konsumtion, desto strre ersttning krver man fr att lna ut sina pengar. Detsamma gller om man tvingas binda sina pengar under lng tid utan att ha mjlighet att anvnda dem. Lgre inflationsfrvntningar minskar drmed ersttningskravet fr dem som lnar ut sina pengar. Fram till mitten av 1980-talet fanns i princip inga av dessa tillvxtbefrmjande frutsttningar p plats i Sverige. Tills dess bestmdes svl in- som utlningsrntor av staten samtidigt som det fanns begrnsningar fr hur mycket och till vilka ndaml bankerna fick ge krediter. Valutaregleringen begrnsade ocks mjligheten att spara och lna i utlndska banker eller p utlndska vrdepappersmarknader. Fretagens andningshl var att de kunde terinvestera sina vinstmedel. Utlndska investerare fick inte heller fritt kpa svenska vrdepapper. Skattesystemet gynnade samtidigt lntagare framfr sparare. Under delar av 1980-talet bidrog systemet med rnteavdrag till att folk i praktiken fick betalt fr att lna men fick betala fr att spara. Och sist men inte minst - hg och varierande inflation gjorde det oskert att spara eftersom man inte kunde vara sker p hur kpkraften fr de sparade medlen skulle komma att utvecklas. Detta hll tillbaka sparandet och ven investeringsviljan. Under 1980-talet och i brjan av 1990-talet genomfrdes frndringar som radikalt frbttrade frutsttningarna p kapitalmarknaden. Frst avreglerades kreditmarknaden, sedan avskaffades valutaregleringen och skattesystemet frndrades. Och sist men inte minst s lades stabiliseringspolitiken om med siktet instllt p tydliga regelverk och prisstabilitet. Vare sig den finansiella sektorn, allmnheten eller myndigheterna var som vi vet frberedda fr effekterna av de frndringar som gde rum under 1980-talet, ven om lrdomar dragits nr det gllde tidsfljden av frndringarna i andra lnder. Penningpolitiken var bunden till att frsvara den fasta vxelkursen. Finanspolitiken som under denna tid hade hela ansvaret fr stabiliseringspolitiken anpassades trots detta inte tillrckligt fr att dmpa den verhettning som kreditavregleringen ledde till. I slutet av 1980-talet och inledningen av 1990-talet var arbetslsheten mycket lg medan inflationen under 1990 ndde ver 10 procent! Drtill kommer de finansiella institutens jakt p marknadsandelar i kombination med att tillsynen inte var tillrckligt vlutvecklad. Anpassningskostnaderna blev som vi vet hga eftersom mycket stora obalanser hade byggts upp under s lng tid. Vi minns tydligt bde bankkriser och valutakris i brjan av 1990-talet och den lgkonjunktur som fljde. Den totala arbetslsheten var mellan 9-12 procent 1993, beroende p hur man mter. De negativa erfarenheterna av hginflationsekonomin ledde efter kriserna till ett nytt regelverk fr finanspolitiken och en penningpolitik inriktad p prisstabilitet. Bankkrisen innebar samtidigt att regelverk, tillsyn och krishantering fr att minska riskerna fr nya kriser har utvecklats p ett gynnsamt stt. Efter de stora och samhllsekonomiskt kostsamma anpassningarna tycks det nu som om lginflationsekonomin har etablerats p allvar. Sjlvstndighet fr Riksbanken och ett lagfst prisstabilitetsml samt saldoml och utgiftstak fr finanspolitiken har bidragit till detta. Det ramverk som byggts upp fr svl finanspolitiken som fr penningpolitiken borde ocks garantera en stabilare utveckling framver. EUmedlemskapet har i sammanhanget ocks varit betydelsefullt. Frutsttningarna fr att hushllen ska fatta beslut om sparandet p ett samhllsekonomiskt effektivt stt torde drfr nu vara betydligt bttre n tidigare. Avreglerade och effektiva kapitalmarknader borde allts ha bidragit till att resurserna kanaliserats p ett stt som r effektivare sett ur ett samhllekonomiskt perspektiv. Sparandet har pverkats starkt av de strukturella frndringar som skett De strukturella frndringarna i den svenska ekonomin under de senaste 20 ren har avspeglats mycket tydligt i det finansiella sparandet i olika sektorer. Eftersom jag idag vill lyfta fram sparandets roll i ekonomin vill jag ge en terblick av hur sparandet utvecklats under de senaste 20-30 ren. P lng sikt r det rimligt att anta att ett land mste anpassa sina utgifter till de inkomster man fr fr det man producerar. lderssammansttningen i befolkningen kan, som jag nmnde, motivera ver- eller underskott i bytesbalansen under en vergngsperiod, som ibland ocks kan vara ganska lng. nskan att hlla en relativt jmn konsumtion under sin livstid gr att man behver spara under sin yrkesverksamma tid fr att sedan kunna anvnda pengarna som pensionr. Ett alternativ till det r att vi via skatter frbinder oss att frsrja vra ldre under den period vi arbetar mot att vi sjlva blir frsrjda nr vi blir pensionrer. D kan det privata sparandet vara lgre. Problem uppstr dock med detta system om lderssammansttningen i befolkningen varierar kraftigt ver tiden. Det gller t.ex. Sverige eftersom vi har en ldrande befolkning. Under perioder med en stor andel pensionrer s kommer ju belastningen p dem som arbetar bli mycket betungande. Fr att undvika detta br varje generation spara fr sin egen lderdom och se till att sparandet kapitaliseras p ett bra stt. Det kan ske antingen genom privat eller statligt organiserat pensionssparande. Stabiliseringspolitikens inriktning mot kortsiktig sysselsttning under 1970-och 80 talet var en av de faktorer som ledde till att sparandet i den svenska ekonomin under lng tid var negativt. Vi konsumerade under dessa r alltfr mycket i frhllande till produktionsutrymmet, vilket resulterade i hg inflation, kontinuerliga bytesbalansunderskott och vxande utlandsskuld. Detta trots att befolkningsstrukturen var sdan att belastningen p kommande generationer skulle bli tung om vi inte sparade tillrckligt. Under verhettningsperioden i slutet av 1980-talet var det finansiella sparandet i den privata sektorn kraftigt negativt - det gllde bde fretag och hushll. Visserligen kompenserades detta i viss mn av att sparandet i den offentliga sektorn steg till fljd av verhettningen, men inte tillrckligt fr att undvika stora bytesbalansunderskott. Till en del berodde den negativa utvecklingen av det finansiella sparandet p att de reala investeringarna steg, men under 1980-talets andra hlft skedde investeringarna i stor utstrckning i kommersiella fastigheter, som prglades av verproduktion. Sdana investeringar kade knappast vra mjligheter att betala rntor p vra utlandsln eller skapade framtida konsumtionsmjligheter. ven tidigare hade stora felinvesteringar genomfrts vilket berodde p att reglerade marknader, terkommande devalveringar och utformningen av skattesystemet gjorde att resurserna inte kanaliserades p ett samhllsekonomiskt effektivt stt. Sammanfattningsvis kan allts sgas att vi varken sparade tillrckligt eller investerade p ett sdant stt att vi frbttrade vra produktionsmjligheter fullt ut. Under krisren i brjan av 1990- talet drog svl fretag som hushll upp sitt sparande kraftigt. Det berodde bde p att det fanns ett konsolideringsbehov efter lnekarusellen, men ocks p kad oskerhet om framtiden. Realrntorna efter skatt var samtidigt mycket hga, vilket till stor del berodde p att det tog tid att sopa igen spren efter den dligt sktta stabiliseringspolitiken och etablera trovrdighet fr lginflationspolitiken. Till bilden hr att hga inflationsfrvntningar gjorde det svrt att snabbt snka rntan, trots att ett lgt kapacitetsutnyttjande drog ned den faktiska inflationen. De hga realrntorna stimulerade frsts ocks sparandet. Den mycket svaga tillvxten i ekonomin i kombination med den hga rntebrdan fr staten gjorde att statsfinanserna frsmrades dramatiskt under dessa r. Bytesbalansen fortsatte drfr att visa underskott de frsta ren p 1990-talet trots att den privata sektorns sparande vnde kraftig uppt. Vndningen kom i mitten av 1990-talet. Den internationella konjunkturen ljusnade och statsfinanserna frbttrades. Det var delvis en fljd av att konjunkturen vnde men ocks av de besparingstgrder som staten vidtog. Det s.k. konsolideringsprogrammet som presenterades 1994 och sedan genomfrdes under ren 1995 till 1998, omfattade en total frstrkning av det offentliga sparandet med omkring 125 miljarder kronor. Budgetprocessen stramades ocks senare upp och finanspolitiken frsgs med tv vergripande ml - ett utgiftstak som begrnsar statens utgifter och ett ml fr den offentliga sektorns finansiella sparande som ska leda till ett verskott p 2 procent i genomsnitt ver en konjunkturcykel. Detta bidrog tillsammans med penningpolitikens inriktning till att inflationsfrvntningarna fll och att rntorna sjnk. Den privata sektorns sparande var allts mycket hgt efter krisren och nr statsfinanserna frbttrades brjade ocks bytesbalansen att visa verskott. Sedan mitten av 1990-talet har bytesbalansen visat ett stabilt verskott p omkring 4 procent varje r! Visserligen har den privata sektorn dragit ner sitt sparande kraftigt men ligger fortfarande betydligt hgre n under slutet av 1980-talet - ett svagt underskott redovisades endast ett r, 2001. Till en del frklaras det minskade privata finansiella sparandeverskottet av att investeringskvoten stigit, men dock i mycket liten utstrckning. Hushllen har haft ett positivt finansiellt sparande under hela perioden. Samtidigt som den privata sektorns sparande minskat s har den offentliga sektorns sparande stigit. Sammantaget har den svenska ekonomin allts haft ett positivt sparande under de senaste ren. Det betyder att vi avsttt offentlig och privat konsumtion fr att genom nettoexport f inkomster fr att betala skulderna fr den tidigare verkonsumtionen. Sverige har allts minskat sin utlandsskuld kraftigt sedan brjan av 1990-talet och vr nettostllning mot utlandet har frbttrats. Statistiken ver Sveriges samlade nettostllning gentemot utlandet visade vid utgngen av 2002 en svensk nettoskuld p 553 miljarder kronor, vilket motsvarade 24 procent av BNP jmfrt med nettoskuld p omkring 43,7 procent av BNP 1993. Utvecklingen innebr att rntebelastningen reducerats. Att rntebrdan allts har minskat innebr att en strre del av det vi producerar kan anvndas fr konsumtion i framtiden. Men med tanke p vr ldersstruktur rcker det frmodligen inte med att vi lyckats halvera de gamla konsumtionsskulderna. Vi hade sannolikt behvt - och behver - "samla mer i ladorna" nr vi har chansen. Framtidens utmaningar. Som jag tidigare talat om visar historien att det finns en risk fr att ramverk som byggts upp fr stabiliseringspolitiken och som syftar till prisstabilitet och stabil efterfrgeutveckling rmnar om det politiska systemet stlls infr lgen d konsumtionsmjligheterna krymper och politiken drmed terigen frestas inriktas alltfr kortsiktigt. De rtta valen r s svra d situationen r akut,. Visserligen verkar systemet tack och lov vara robust just nu, men ngra riktiga tester har det efter 1990-talskrisen nnu inte utsatts fr. Att ldersstrukturen i befolkningen r lika problematisk i stora delar av EU gr ju att samma risk finns fr det gemensamma mellanstatliga regelverket, bl. a. stabilitetspakten. EU:s ekonomisk-politiska kommitt publicerade nyligen en studie ver hur den demografiska utvecklingen kommer att pverka EU-lndernas offentliga finanser. I studien utfrdes ocks skattningar av hur befolkningsstrukturens frndring - inklusive dess effekter p arbetsmarknad och kapitalintensitet - kommer att pverka potentiell tillvxt inom EU framver. Berkningarna indikerar att demografieffekten gr att potentiell tillvxt kommer att falla jmfrt med genomsnittet under 1990-talet, till i genomsnitt 1,3 procent under perioden 2000-2050. Det innebr, allt annat lika, att nstan en tredjedel av konsumtionsutrymmet skulle falla bort, om inga andra tgrder vidtas eller tillrckligt mycket sparande finns placerat i utlandet. Den nskade konsumtionen kan erhllas genom avyttring av sparande placerat i andra lnder. En nettofrmgenhet i utlandet innebr att vi har en fordran p framtida produktion i omvrlden. Nr de som pensioneras inte lngre bidrar till produktionen och den d inte rcker till den nskade konsumtionen s kan ju det, lite frenklat, ersttas med import som finansieras med frsljning av de aktier och obligationer vi ger i utlandet. Nr vi brjar anvnda vrt sparande i utlandet kommer det frsts att leda till ett bytesbalansunderskott. Detta r i sig knappast ngot att vara bekymrad ver eftersom det fr Sveriges del fregtts av verskott under mnga r. Om inte sparandet placerat i utlandet rcker till fr att upprtthlla nskad konsumtion fr Sverige med en ldre befolkning, vad finns det fr vgar att hlla konsumtionen uppe? Dels mste vi i Sverige se till att ka vr sysselsttningsgrad i arbetskraften och dels mste vi hja vr produktivitet! Ett finansiellt sparverskott i den offentliga sektorn p i genomsnitt 2 procent av BNP fram till 2015 och en rlig tillvxt p i genomsnitt 1,9 procent mellan 1998-2015 kommer enligt LU 1999/2000 att innebra att staten klarar sina utfstelser. ven om detta i ljuset av olika bedmningar av den svenska ekonomins potentiella tillvxt i nulget inte frefaller vara ett orealistiskt scenario kan konstateras att fr att detta ska infrias mste produktiviteten i den privata sektorn fortstta att ka och kompensera fr det lga bidraget frn arbetskraftsutbudet som fljer av den ogynnsamma demografifrskjutningen. Mot bakgrund av ovanstende r det dock nskvrt att politiken redan idag tydligt inriktas p att skapa s goda frutsttningar fr tillvxt som mjligt. ven om sparandet och produktiviteten skulle bli hga nog str vi nd infr stora anpassningar inom produktionen av varor och tjnster och p arbetsmarknaden. Efterfrgan kommer att frskjutas mot tjnster som vrd och omsorg. Title: The role of asset prices and credit in an inflation target policy
text: Srejber: The role of asset prices and credit in inflation targeting policies Date 2005-03-16 First Deputy Governor of the Riksbank Eva Srejber spoke on Wednesday at a seminar on the housing market and housing construction arranged by the Construction and Real Estate Economists' Travel Association at the Royal Institute of Technology. It is now more than 10 years since the Riksbank set an explicit inflation target for monetary policy. Price stability policy has been successful. Inflation expectations have been very close to 2% and the rate of price increase has been close to the target, while in the 1970s and 1980s it was around 8% per annum. At the same time, GDP growth has been on average about half a percentage point higher per year in the new regime. However, a monetary policy geared towards keeping inflation on target over the short or medium term does not guarantee against excessive increases in lending and asset prices. We know from experience that strong credit expansion and sharply rising asset prices have often preceded large falls in resource utilisation and inflation rates. However, with the flexible inflation targeting policy pursued by the Riksbank, the risk of such a development can be taken into account when monetary policy is designed. The inflation target is defined as prices measured as CPI increasing 2 percent per year with a tolerance range of plus minus 1 percentage point. Normally, monetary policy is geared towards achieving the inflation target over one to two years. The reason is that interest rate changes are expected to have a full impact on inflation during that period. However, if we assess that target achievement within the normal horizon risks leading to large fluctuations in growth, we can choose to bring inflation measured as CPI back to the target more gradually. In practice, we have therefore often focused on the und1x inflation measure, which does not include the direct effects of indirect taxes and subsidies as well as interest rate changes. In some situations, we have also chosen to study measures of inflation that have been cleared of temporary effects of supply disruptions, for example from the impact of the low water supply on electricity prices. If credit expansion and asset price increases are estimated to create significant risk of strong demand shortfalls and lower inflation rates beyond the normal target horizon, we can take this into account in the design of monetary policy within our flexible inflation targeting policy. If so, it could justify a more restrictive monetary policy than is necessary to keep inflation on target within the normal target horizon. The Riksbank's second objective, financial stability, does not have to be threatened to justify such a monetary policy either. It is enough that growth and inflation risk slowing down sharply in the slightly longer term. However, although our monetary policy framework makes it possible to take into account excessive credit expansion and inflated asset prices, in practice it is not so easy to assess when there are large imbalances in these variables. Knowledge of credit and asset price cycles needs to be developed in order to identify more accurately when lending and asset prices are developing so strongly that they risk leading to disruptions to the macroeconomy down the line. However, the choice is between: prevent or respond only when asset price falls and debt consolidation are already a fact. My assessment is that the costs of waiting may be so great that it is better, with the limited knowledge we have, after all, to try to intervene if we see the build-up of large financial imbalances. The development of prices in the housing market and of household indebtedness is analysed on an ongoing basis by the Riksbank. It is estimated that the rapid increase in both house prices and indebtedness since the mid-1990s has so far not meant that any significant imbalances have built up. Although households have debts that relative to incomes are almost as high as before the real estate crisis in 1992, at the same time the share of interest costs in income is significantly lower than then due to the low nominal interest rates and, unlike many other countries, it does not seem to be common for us in Sweden to buy single-family houses and apartments for purely speculative purposes. This reduces the risk of creating a housing price bubble. Moreover, house price and lending increases started from very low levels after the crisis years when interest rates were still very high. The decline in interest rates since then explains a large part of the increases. Lending rates are now significantly lower than they have historically been and there are many indications that they will rise in the future. The low interest rates are due, firstly, to the expansionary monetary policy in recent years. Secondly, housing institutions' financing costs in the bond market appear to have fallen as a result of a sharp decline in investor compensation claims. Housing institutions have therefore been able to offer their borrowers very low lending rates. This means that lending rates may rise a lot when interest rates normalize. This is hopefully something that both households and banks take into account when making their calculations of future payment burdens. However, there are some worrying signs that this is not happening to a sufficient extent. There are indications that more households are now taking on a payment burden that leaves little room for loss of income or higher interest rates. Of course, it is a risk if lenders and borrowers begin to believe that the current low interest rate environment will last a long time and adjust their behavior to this. This could lead to continued strong credit expansion and excessive house prices. If such behaviour continues for a longer period of time, then, in my opinion, the risk increases that the adjustment to more balanced debt and house price levels will lead to significant drop-offs in demand and thus lower inflation later on.

Det r nu mer n 10 r sedan Riksbanken faststllde ett explicit inflationsml fr penningpolitiken. Prisstabilitetspolitiken har varit framgngsrik. Samtidigt har BNP-tillvxten i genomsnitt varit ungefr en halv procentenhet hgre per r i den nya regimen. En penningpolitik inriktad mot att hlla inflationen p mlet p kort eller medellng sikt utgr dock ingen garanti mot verdriven kning av utlning och tillgngspriser. Av erfarenhet vet vi att stark kreditexpansion och kraftigt stigande tillgngspriser ofta fregtt stora fall i resursutnyttjande och inflationstakt. Med den flexibla inflationsmlspolitik Riksbanken fr kan emellertid risken fr en sdan utveckling beaktas nr penningpolitiken utformas. Inflationsmlet r definierat som att priserna mtt som KPI skall ka 2 procent per r med ett toleransintervall p plus minus 1 procentenhet. Normalt inriktas penningpolitiken p att uppn inflationsmlet p ett till tv rs sikt. Anledningen r att rntefrndringar bedms f fullt genomslag p inflationen under den perioden. Men om vi bedmer att mluppfyllelse inom den normala horisonten riskerar att leda till stora fluktuationer i tillvxten s kan vi vlja att fra inflationen mtt som KPI tillbaka till mlet mera gradvis. I praktiken har vi drfr ofta fokuserat p inflationsmttet UND1X dr de direkta effekterna av indirekta skatter och subventioner samt rntefrndringar inte ingr. I ngra situationer har vi ocks valt att studera inflationsmtt som rensats frn tillflliga effekter av utbudsstrningar exempelvis frn den lga vattentillgngens pverkan p elpriserna. Om en kreditexpansion och tillgngspriskningar bedms skapa betydande risk fr kraftigt efterfrgebortfall och lgre inflationstakt efter den normala mlhorisonten kan vi ta hnsyn till det i utformningen av penningpolitiken inom ramen fr vr flexibla inflationsmlspolitik. Det skulle i s fall kunna motivera en mer restriktiv penningpolitik n vad som krvs fr att hlla inflationen p mlet inom den normala mlhorisonten. Riksbankens andra ml, den finansiella stabiliteten, behver inte heller vara hotat fr att motivera en sdan penningpolitik. Det rcker med att tillvxten och inflationen p lite lngre sikt riskerar att dmpas kraftigt. Men ven om vrt penningpolitiska ramverk gr det mjligt att ta hnsyn till verdriven kreditexpansion och uppdrivna tillgngspriser s r det i praktiken inte s ltt att bedma nr det rr sig om stora obalanser i dessa variabler. Kunskapen om kredit- och tillgngspriscykler behver utvecklas fr att vi med strre exakthet ska kunna identifiera nr utlning och tillgngspriser utvecklas s starkt att de riskerar att leda till strningar av makroekonomin lngre fram. Valet str emellertid mellan att frebygga eller reagera frst nr tillgngsprisfall och skuldkonsolidering redan r ett faktum. Min bedmning r att kostnaderna med att vnta kan bli s stora att det r bttre att med den begrnsade kunskap vi trots allt har, frska gripa in om vi ser uppbyggnaden av stora finansiella obalanser. Utvecklingen av priserna p bostadsmarknaden och av hushllens skuldsttning analyseras lpande av Riksbanken. Bedmningen r att den snabba kningen av bde bostadspriser och skuldsttning sedan mitten av 1990-talet hittills inte inneburit att ngra betydande obalanser har byggts upp. Hushllen har visserligen skulder som relativt inkomsterna r nsta lika hga som fre fastighetskrisen 1992, men samtidigt r rntekostnadernas andel av inkomsterna betydligt lgre n d p grund av de lga nominella rntorna och i motsats till mnga andra lnder frefaller det inte vara vanligt att vi i Sverige kper smhus och lgenheter i rent spekulationssyfte. Det minskar risken fr att det skapas en bostadsprisbubbla. Bostadspris- och utlningskningarna startade dessutom frn mycket lga niver efter krisren d rntan fortfarande var mycket hg. Rntenedgngen sedan dess frklarar en stor del av kningarna. Utlningsrntorna r nu betydligt lgre n vad de historiskt sett varit och mycket talar fr att de kommer att stiga framver. Det r frhoppningsvis ngot som bde hushll och banker beaktar nr de gr sina kalkyler ver framtida betalningsbrda. Men det finns dock vissa oroande tecken p att s inte sker i tillrcklig utstrckning. Det finns indikationer p att fler hushll nu tar p sig en betalningsbrda som lmnar litet utrymme fr inkomstbortfall eller hgre rntor. Det r naturligtvis en risk om lngivare och lntagare brjar tro att det nuvarande lga rntelget kommer att vara lnge och anpassar sitt beteende till detta. Det kan leda till fortsatt stark kreditexpansion och verdrivna bostadspriser. Title: Governor Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: Hearing on financial stability
text: Governor Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: Hearing on financial stability "The economic vulnerabilities have become even greater during the pandemic/ Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves said today when he participated in the annual open hearing of the Riksdag Committee on Finance, which dealt with vulnerabilities in the light of increasing debts among households and commercial property companies. In addition to the Riksbank Governor, others taking part in the hearing included Minister for Financial Markets Max Eiger, Finansinspektionen's Director-General ErikThedeen, and Swedish National Debt Office Director-General Karolina Ekholm. Date: 01/02/2022 09:00 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Place: Sveriges Riksdag, Andrakammarsal (Second Chamber) or Online Published 01/02/2022 Mr Ingves emphasized that prices of a variety of assets have increased during the pandemic. At the same time, the debts of both households and property companies have risen. The price trend in the housing market has been particularly noteworthy, said Mr Ingves, and pointed out at the same time that a number of new trends affect the risk spectrum in the commercial property market. The transition from physical trading to e-commerce has been accelerated during the pandemic, and increased teleworking can lead to changes in the way companies use office space. These trends may in turn affect the demand for such premises and could ultimately lead to more vacancies, lower rent levels and falling property values, Mr Ingves pointed out. The focus must now be on addressing growing imbalances Mr Ingves underlined that overall economic policy needs to focus more on counteracting the risks of growing indebtedness. The most appropriate approach is to use targeted structural measures, well designed financial regulation and macroprudential policy. "Resolving the fundamental problems linked to the housing market and high household indebtedness will requires broad reforms in housing and tax policy", commented Stefan Ingves. If they are not implemented to the necessary extent, the need for macroprudential policy measures will increase. It is also important that the banks properly account for the risks associated with lending to commercial properties.

Title: Ingves at Riksdag Committee on Finance: The geopolitical uncertainty makes it more difficult to assess inflation
text: Ingves at Riksdag Committee on Finance: The geopolitical uncertainty makes it more difficult to assess inflation The Riksbank is closely following developments and is prepared to deal with possible effects on the financial markets as a result of Russia's invasion of Ukraine. "We are continually evaluating the consequences for the Swedish economy," said Governor Stefan Ingves in his introduction on monetary policy, when he and Deputy Governor Anna Breman took part in the first hearing of the year at the Riksdag Committee on Finance. Date: 03/03/2022 10:00 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Published 03/03/2022 "Back when we presented our assessment of inflation prospects in our latest Monetary Policy Report on 10 February, we said that inflation was uncertain. Recent developments in Ukraine further reinforce that impression," said Mr Ingves. At the moment, inflation in Sweden is higher than the target, but according to the Riksbank's latest forecast from February, it is expected to fall back over the year. For inflation to be close to the target a little further ahead requires continued support from monetary policy. "But we are continually assessing how the Swedish economy is developing and how sustainable the higher inflation is and we will adjust our monetary policy if necessary," said Mr Ingves. Ms Breman also stressed the need to follow developments in financial markets and in the Swedish and global economies. The direct effects on the Swedish economy are expected to be small, as Sweden's trade with Ukraine and Russia is limited and Swedish banks have little exposure to these countries. However, the consequences can be more tangible if the war escalates, or causes greater unrest in financial markets. The prices of energy and intermediate goods increased sharply even before Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and many companies may need to raise prices in the light of the fact that energy prices are now rising further. "The war will affect economic and inflation prospects in Sweden, as well as abroad. We need to be prepared to adjust monetary policy if necessary," said Ms Breman.

Title: Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: Hearing regarding Account of Monetary Policy 2021
text: Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: Hearing regarding Account of Monetary Policy 2021 On Tuesday, the entire Executive Board of the Riksbank participated in the annual hearing of the Committee on Finance on the monetary policy conducted the previous year. Governor Stefan Ingves began the hearing by summarising the monetary policy year 2021, a year marked by a rapid economic recovery and the pandemic. The fall in GDP was recovered and the employment rate rose to pre-pandemic levels. Several of the crisis measures implemented by the Riksbank at the beginning of the crisis could be phased out during the year. Date: 10/05/2022 10:00 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Place: Committee on Finance, Sveriges Riksdag Published 10/05/2022 After being very low in 2020, inflation rose rapidly in the second half of 2021. In Sweden, the upturn in inflation was driven by sharply rising energy prices. Excluding these, cost pressures remained moderate during the year. Monetary policy was aimed at supporting the economic recovery and bringing inflation back to the target of 2 per cent. "Given the extraordinary disturbances that the world economy underwent during the pandemic, target attainment should be considered acceptable," said Stefan Ingves. Christina Nyman, Handelsbanken and John Hassler, Stockholm University, gave their views on the Account of Monetary Policy and the policy conducted. After this, First Deputy Governor Cecilia Skingsley commented on the views of the opponents.

Title: Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: We are safeguarding the inflation target
text: Ingves at the Riksdag Committee on Finance: We are safeguarding the inflation target The high inflation creates problems. It erodes purchasing power- especially for the least well-off - and makes it difficult for both households and businesses to plan their finances. Therefore, the Riksbank, which has been given the task by the Riksdag of keeping inflation low and stable, must now act to bring inflation down. Low and stable inflation provides a foundation for good economic development. This was the message from Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Per Jansson when they took part in a hearing on current monetary policy at the Riksdag Committee on Finance. Date: 20/10/2022 09:00 Speaker: Governor Stefan Ingves Place: Committee on Finance, Sveriges Riksdag Published 20/10/2022 Inflation is too high - monetary policy has to act At the end of last year, inflation excluding energy prices was still low. But over the course of the year, inflation has spread widely in the economy. "Today, almost all prices are rising in Sweden, and rising fast," said Stefan Ingves. To dampen the high inflation, the Riksbank has raised its policy rate three times this year and the Executive Board's forecast is that it will need to be raised further in the next six months. "Inflation is far too high, and we must therefore use our monetary policy. A higher policy rate slows down economic activity. If we do not act now, it could lead to even more severe and negative effects later on. The inflation-targeting policy is now being put to the test," said Stefan Ingves. At the same time, he pointed to the considerable uncertainty in the Riksbank's forecasts and mentioned in this context the high price of electricity, the geopolitical situation and the interaction between fiscal and monetary policy in various parts of the world. "If the conditions change, we need to adjust monetary policy accordingly. We will do what is necessary to bring inflation back to the target."

Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Stefan Ingves in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2015-03-05 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament. Why do we have negative interest rates? How is the Swedish economy developing? These are some of the questions that Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and First Deputy Governor Kerstin af Jochnick will answer when they begin the first hearing of the year on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee on Thursday. Stefan Ingves presents the background to the decision to lower the repo rate to a historically low -0.10 percent and to buy government bonds for SEK 10 billion. He talks about the fact that the Swedish economy has developed relatively well and that there are signs that low inflation has bottomed out. But he also points out that uncertainty in the world around us has increased. "The measures we have taken, which can be scaled up if necessary, can be seen as insurance against the risk of lower inflation and inflation expectations. We show in action that we are defending the inflation target", says Ingves. Ingves also highlights the problems in the housing market. The fact that both house prices and lending for home purchases are increasing is a side effect of the low interest rate. "It is urgent that other policy areas address these risks," Ingves stresses. Kerstin af Jochnick also points out how important it is for inflation to rise towards the target and gives her perspective on the debate on monetary policy in recent years. The criticism has now clearly changed character, says af Jochnick. From having previously been about the Riksbank stimulating more, that debt does not pose a risk and that the inflation target must be prioritized, the criticism now boils down to the fact that the Riksbank should stimulate less, that debt is a significant risk and that the inflation target is less important. af Jochnick believes that the previous criticism took too lightly the risks of high household indebtedness, while the new criticism underestimates the importance of the inflation target for stable economic development. "The policy we pursue is not a new type of policy, it is a reaction to a change in the conditions for monetary policy", says af Jochnick, pointing out that inflation in recent years has become lower than expected and that inflation expectations have fallen. The Governor of the Riksbank and one of the Deputy Governors of the Riksbank are questioned about monetary policy by the Parliamentary Finance Committee three times a year.

Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Stefan Ingves in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2015-09-24 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament How is the Swedish economy doing? Why do we have negative interest rates? What can be done to curb rising household indebtedness? These are some of the questions that Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Cecilia Skingsley will answer when they begin the second hearing of the year on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee on Thursday. Stefan Ingves presents the latest monetary policy decision from the beginning of September, when the Riksbank's Executive Board decided to leave the repo rate unchanged at -0.35 percent in order to provide continued necessary support for the rise in inflation. The Riksbank's expansionary monetary policy, with negative interest rates and purchases of government bonds, is an important explanation for the stable development of growth in Sweden, the fact that unemployment is falling and that there is a clear upward trend in inflation. Inflation has risen from 0.5% to 1.4% over the past year, excluding interest rate effects and volatile energy prices. But the rise in inflation may be jeopardised by developments in the rest of the world, and the Riksbank therefore remains highly prepared to act if the outlook for inflation deteriorates. At the same time, Ingves emphasizes the importance of further measures from the government, parliament and the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority to mitigate the risks of high household indebtedness. An amortisation requirement is a welcome, but not enough, step to calm down the development of the mortgage market, says Ingves. "We are behind schedule in solving these problems in Sweden, but there is an opportunity to act, there are more measures to take. If nothing more is done, there are obvious risks of very poor economic development down the line." Cecilia Skingsley discusses in her introduction the effects of digitalisation on inflation and believes that these have contributed to dampening price developments. But they are not the main explanation for the low inflation rate in recent years. The recovery in the rest of the world has been slow, the krona strengthened sharply after the financial crisis, energy prices have fallen and in the uncertain environment after the crises, it has been difficult for companies to raise prices. "But monetary policy is having an effect. Inflation is now rising from low levels. This shows that it is possible to raise inflation despite digitalisation." Skingsley also addresses discussions about whether central bank targets should be changed. She points out that in the Swedish debate, arguments have mainly been put forward for lowering the inflation target, while the international discussion is rather about whether the target should be raised. But you don't create confidence by adjusting the target to where inflation is at the moment, skingsley says. "Stable expectations about general price developments mean one less uncertainty factor for both price and wage-setters in our society."

Title: Hearing on monetary policy
text: Stefan Ingves in the Finance Committee. Hearing on monetary policy Date: 2015-11-12 Speaker: Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves Location: Skandiasalen, Swedish Parliament On Thursday, Riksbank Governor Stefan Ingves and Deputy Governor Henry Ohlsson will participate in this year's third hearing on monetary policy in the Riksdag's Finance Committee. Ingves: Sweden must relate to developments in the outside world Stefan Ingves begins the hearing by presenting the latest monetary policy decision from the end of October, when the Riksbank's Executive Board decided to expand purchases of government bonds, leave the repo rate unchanged at -0.35 percent and postpone a first rate hike six months ahead. Ingves points out how dependent the Swedish economy is on developments in the outside world. There is continued uncertainty about the strength of the global economy and monetary policy in the rest of the world. The low interest rate situation in Sweden has contributed to a relatively strong economy with stable GDP growth, falling unemployment and inflation rising since last year. Ingves points out that it is important to maintain the positive trend with low interest rates so that inflation continues to rise towards the target. At the same time, he stresses that the low interest rate environment can increase the risks associated with the housing market and high household indebtedness, and therefore underlines the importance of other policy areas addressing these risks in different ways. Ohlsson: Opportunities and challenges with increased immigration In his introduction, Henry Ohlsson focuses on the opportunities and challenges that increased immigration to Sweden entails. He believes that since a country's growth in the long term largely depends on how its population changes, the increased immigration is a positive and much-needed addition to the Swedish, aging population. But Ohlsson also points to the challenges that increased immigration entails: that it is difficult for vulnerable groups to enter the labor market and that housing construction needs to increase in order to meet the need for housing.
