Title: Monetary policy and interest rate path
text: Svensson: Monetary policy and interest rate path Date 2007-08-22 Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson spoke today at a meeting at Danske Bank in Stockholm. In his speech, Svensson discussed, among other things, some basic principles for a flexible inflation targeting policy and his view of the Riksbank's development of monetary policy with a published interest rate path. "The Riksbank is pursuing what is usually called a 'flexible' inflation targeting policy. This means that we are trying to both stabilise inflation around the inflation target and stabilise resource utilisation. A 'strict' inflation targeting policy would mean that we only stabilise inflation around its target regardless of what it entails for resource utilisation. We would then try to reach the inflation target as quickly as possible. This would require many major changes in interest rates as soon as new information suggests that the inflation forecast is above or below the inflation target. This, in turn, would lead to large fluctuations in resource utilisation and thus production and employment. In economic research, it is sometimes assumed that the central bank pursues a strict inflation targeting policy, but this is never more than a simplistic pedagogical assumption. In practice, all central banks with inflation targets pursue flexible policies and also try to stabilise resource utilisation," Svensson began. "But how much the central bank chooses to stabilize resource utilization may vary over time. When the inflation target is new and it is important to establish credibility for the target, it is natural that the central bank devotes itself most to keeping inflation close to the target and cares less about fluctuations in resource utilisation. When credibility has been built up and the central bank has become warm in its clothes, it is natural that the bank attaches greater importance to stabilizing resource utilization as well. But the importance of stabilizing resource utilisation must never be so great that the credibility of the inflation target is threatened," Svensson continued. "It is also important to remember that the only thing monetary policy can do is stabilize resource utilisation around its average level. Monetary policy, on the other hand, cannot influence this average level. Thus, it does not make sense to have a monetary policy target for the average resource utilisation. On the other hand, it makes the utmost sense to have a monetary policy target for inflation," Svensson continued. "Normally, it takes time for inflation and resource utilisation to react to changes in interest rates. Milton Friedman used the expression 'long and variable lags'. It may take a year for production and another year for inflation to react. Therefore, an effective inflation targeting policy must be based on forecasts, even though these forecasts are always uncertain (and more uncertain the longer the forecast horizon). The Riksbank's interest rate decision is therefore based on forecasts for inflation and resource utilisation on a 1-3 year horizon," Svensson said. "In addition, the repo rate in the coming weeks itself plays an insignificant role in future production and inflation. What matters instead is what companies, households and market participants think about the repo rate later in the future, in one or more years. These expectations influence long-term interest rates, which have a greater bearing on decisions about production, consumption, investment, prices, wages, etc. central bank decisions on interest rates in the coming weeks are almost solely a role in that they affect expectations. In fact, monetary policy consists mainly of influencing expectations, the 'management of expectations', as economist Michael Woodford has put it," Svensson continued. "With a flexible inflation targeting policy, the central bank must choose an interest rate path that makes the forecast for inflation and resource utilisation 'look good'. By looking good is meant inflation in line with the target and a normal resource utilization over a 2-3 year period, or that inflation approaches the target and resource utilization approaches normally at an appropriate pace. The Riksbank also uses the expression 'balanced' monetary policy for this. In my research, I have called this way of using forecast targeting forecasts, because it involves choosing the path of interest rates so that the forecasts are right, i.e. look good. You might be able to call it 'forecasting' in Swedish (unless you misunderstand the expression and think it amounts to wishful thinking or other misleading manipulation of the forecast)," Svensson said. "The forecasts for interest rates, inflation and resource utilisation are a natural trinity. It is not possible to determine a forecast of inflation and resource utilisation without having a forecast or assumption about the path of interest rates at the same time. Therefore, all central banks that strive to stabilize inflation, including the ECB and the Fed, also have an interest rate forecast or an interest rate assumption somewhere in their decision-making basis, even when they do not publish these," Svensson continued. "It is against this background that the Riksbank's decision to publish an interest rate path should be seen. Monetary policy operates through the expectations of the path of interest rates that it gives rise to. It is the entire path of interest rates that matters for future inflation and resource utilisation, not the level of interest rates in the coming weeks. The Riksbank has therefore come to the conclusion that the only straightforward thing is to explicitly discuss the interest rate path itself and to choose a certain interest rate path as the main forecast, but also to publish and justify this interest rate path. This is, in my opinion, the most effective way of conducting monetary policy. Not discussing and choosing a particular interest rate path as the main forecast would be an incomplete decision-making process. Not to publish the interest rate forecast would be to darken the most material information," Svensson said. "The Riksbank is not the first with this monetary policy innovation. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand began back in 1997. Several researchers, including myself, have been arguing for years for more central banks to publish their own interest rate forecasts. I was therefore very happy when Norges Bank started doing this in 2005, and I was even happier when the Riksbank started doing the same thing in February this year. The publication of interest rate paths is now widely discussed around the world in both research and central bank circles. I won't be surprised if more central banks start publishing their own interest rate forecasts going forward," Svensson said. "There has been a lot of discussion about the two interest rate forecasts that the Riksbank has published so far in February and June. Many market participants felt that the February interest rate forecast was too low. On the contrary, in connection with the June forecast, there were players who were surprised by how much we adjusted the interest rate forecast upwards. But I don't think it's strange that some observers have been surprised by our forecasts for interest rates. It is natural that it takes time for the new system to settle down, including the interplay between the interest rate, inflation and resource utilisation forecast. It is only natural that the interest rate forecast can be revised when new information has come in. The interest rate path we publish is a forecast that is based on the information available at the time and is thus not a promise! After all, it is in fact a probability distribution and is also published in the form of an average with a significant uncertainty interval and with alternative scenarios. Even when the system has settled down, there will be room for different interpretations of new information and what change in the interest rate path this justifies," Svensson continued. "Forecast control, the method of steering with forecasts that I have described, also shows how monetary policy with inflation targets should take into account new information about the economy, the business cycle and the outside world. This new information has implications for monetary policy only if, at unchanged interest rate path, it affects the forecast for: inflation and resource utilisation. Thus, if the new information does not affect the forecast in any particular way, it has no impact on monetary policy. If the new information shifts up the forecast for inflation or resource utilisation (or both), it is justified to adjust up the path of interest rates. If the forecast for inflation or resource utilisation shifts down, it is instead justified to adjust the interest rate path down. If the new information shifts the forecast for inflation and for resource utilisation in different directions, it will be a more complicated trade-off. For market participants and analysts who want to predict how the Riksbank will act on new information in the next monetary policy decision, it is therefore important to analyse how this new information affects the forecasts for inflation and resource utilisation," Svensson continued. "The main scenario's forecast for interest rates, inflation and resource utilisation in the February report presented what the Riksbank then considered to be a well-balanced monetary policy with regard to the information available at the time. The information received between the February and June reports suggested that wage increases would be greater, productivity lower and fiscal policy more expansionary than the Riksbank expected in February. At unchanged interest rates, this information shifted up the inflation and output forecasts, and inflation and resource utilisation risked being too high in our assessment. We therefore needed to adjust the path of interest rates upwards, which then shifted back the inflation and output forecasts, so that they showed a better development for inflation and resource utilisation. The interest rate path that we in the Executive Board agreed on for the June report ended up being higher than the alternative high-wage scenario published in the February report. This is consistent with the fact that the new information also included lower productivity and more expansionary fiscal policy, both of which increase inflationary pressures," Svensson said. "After the June report, new information has come in. I myself am not interested in and do not think it is very effective to interpret week by week how this information possibly shifts the forecast for inflation and resource utilisation and possibly justifies changing the path of interest rates. Instead, I prefer to take a comprehensive approach to the new situation ahead of the next monetary policy meeting in September. With regard to the turmoil that has arisen in the financial markets, we are, of course, following developments closely. Through our continuous monitoring of the financial markets, we have good information about the situation. For Sweden, the Swedish money market and financial systems are working well," Svensson said. "Let me conclude by saying a few more words about the use of resources. As has been shown, I believe that resource utilisation is an important variable in monetary policy. It can be measured in several ways. Research on monetary policy suggests that the gap between actual output and 'potential' output, the so-called output gap, is an appropriate measure of resource utilisation in monetary policy. But there is considerable uncertainty, both theoretically and empirically, about how potential production should be estimated and forecasted. Consequently, the measures of potential output used by central banks are quite uncertain. There are thus strong reasons for the Riksbank and other central banks to deepen their analyses in this area," Svensson concluded.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Svensson: Penningpolitik och rntebana Datum 2007-08-22 Vice riksbankschef Lars E.O. Svensson talade idag vid ett mte p Danske Bank i Stockholm. I sitt anfrande diskuterade Svensson bland annat ngra grundlggande principer fr en flexibel inflationsmlspolitik och sin syn p Riksbankens utveckling av penningpolitiken med publicerad rntebana. Riksbanken bedriver vad som brukar kallas en flexibel inflationsmlspolitik. Med det menas att vi frsker att bde stabilisera inflationen runt inflationsmlet och stabilisera resursutnyttjandet. En strikt inflationsmlspolitik skulle innebra att vi enbart stabiliserar inflationen runt sitt ml oavsett vad det medfr fr resursutnyttjandet. Vi skulle d frska n inflationsmlet s snabbt som mjligt. Detta skulle krva mnga och stora rntefrndringar s fort ny information tyder p att inflationsprognosen ver- eller underskrider inflationsmlet. Detta skulle i sin tur leda till stora fluktuationer i resursutnyttjandet och drmed produktionen och sysselsttningen. Inom den nationalekonomiska forskningen antas ibland att centralbanken fr en strikt inflationsmlspolitik, men det r aldrig mer n ett frenklande pedagogiskt antagande. I praktiken bedriver alla centralbanker med inflationsml en flexibel politik och frsker ocks stabilisera resursutnyttjandet, inledde Svensson. Men hur mycket centralbanken vljer att stabilisera resursutnyttjandet kan variera ver tiden. Nr inflationsmlet r nytt och det r viktigt att etablera trovrdighet fr mlet r det naturligt att centralbanken gnar sig mest t att hlla inflationen nra mlet och bryr sig mindre om fluktuationer i resursutnyttjandet. Nr trovrdigheten byggts upp och centralbanken blivit varm i klderna r det naturligt att banken fster strre vikt vid att stabilisera ven resursutnyttjandet. Men vikten p stabilisering av resursutnyttjandet fr aldrig bli s stor att trovrdigheten fr inflationsmlet hotas, fortsatte Svensson. Det r ocks viktigt att komma ihg att det enda penningpolitiken kan gra r att stabilisera resursutnyttjandet kring dess genomsnittliga niv. Penningpolitiken kan dremot inte pverka denna genomsnittliga niv. Det r allts inte meningsfullt att ha ett penningpolitiskt ml fr det genomsnittliga resursutnyttjandet. Dremot r det hgst meningsfullt att ha ett penningpolitiskt ml fr inflationen, fortsatte Svensson. Normalt tar det tid innan inflation och resursutnyttjande reagerar p frndringar av rntan. Milton Friedman anvnde uttrycket long and variable lags. Det kan ta ett r fr produktionen och ytterligare ett r fr inflationen att reagera. Drfr mste en effektiv inflationsmlspolitik bygga p prognoser, trots att dessa prognoser alltid r oskra (och mer oskra ju lngre prognoshorisonten r). Riksbankens rntebeslut bygger drfr p prognoser fr inflation och resursutnyttjande p 1-3 rs horisont, sade Svensson. Dessutom spelar reporntan de nrmaste veckorna i sig en obetydlig roll fr framtida produktion och inflation. Vad som spelar roll r istllet vad fretag, hushll och marknadsaktrer tror om reporntan lngre fram i tiden, om ett eller flera r. Dessa frvntningar pverkar lnga rntor, som har strre betydelse fr beslut om produktion, konsumtion, investeringar, priser, lner, osv. I sjlva verket spelar centralbankers beslut om rntan de nrmaste veckorna nstan enbart en roll genom att de pverkar frvntningarna. Penningpolitik bestr faktiskt huvudsakligen i att pverka frvntningar, management of expectations, som nationalekonomen Michael Woodford har uttryckt det, fortsatte Svensson. Med en flexibel inflationsmlspolitik mste centralbanken vlja en rntebana som gr att prognosen fr inflationen och resursutnyttjandet ser bra ut. Med att se bra ut menas en inflation i linje med mlet och ett normalt resursutnyttjande p 2-3 rs sikt, eller att inflationen nrmar sig mlet och resursutnyttjandet nrmar sig normalt i en lmplig takt. Riksbanken anvnder ocks uttrycket vl avvgd penningpolitik fr detta. I min forskning har jag kallat detta stt att utnyttja prognoser fr forecast targeting, eftersom det innebr att vlja rntebanan s att prognoserna ligger rtt, dvs. ser bra ut. Man kanske kan kalla det prognosstyrning p svenska (om man inte missfrstr uttrycket och tror att det innebr nsketnkande eller annan missledande manipulation av prognosen), sade Svensson. Prognoserna fr rntan, inflationen och resursutnyttjandet r en naturlig treenighet. Det gr inte att bestmma en prognos fr inflationen och resursutnyttjandet utan att samtidigt ha en prognos eller ett antagande om rntebanan. Drfr har alla centralbanker som strvar efter att stabilisera inflationen, inklusive ECB och Fed, ngonstans i sitt beslutsunderlag ocks en rnteprognos eller ett rnteantagande, ven nr de inte publicerar dessa, fortsatte Svensson. Det r mot denna bakgrund som Riksbankens beslut att publicera en rntebana br ses. Penningpolitiken verkar genom de frvntningar om rntebanan som den ger upphov till. Det r hela rntebanan som spelar roll fr framtida inflation och resursutnyttjande, inte rntenivn de nrmaste veckorna. Riksbanken har drfr kommit fram till att det enda raka r att explicit diskutera sjlva rntebanan och att vlja en viss rntebana som huvudprognos, men ocks att publicera och motivera denna rntebana. Detta r enligt min mening det mest effektiva sttet att bedriva penningpolitik. Att inte diskutera och vlja en viss rntebana som huvudprognos vore en ofullstndig beslutsprocess. Title: Practical monetary policy: Why has the Riksbank's repo rate path been so high and why has this not hindered the recovery?
text: Svensson: Practical monetary policy: Why has the Riksbank's repo rate path been so high and why has this not hindered the recovery? Date: 2011-09-17 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson Location: National Conference in Economics, Uppsala University On Saturday, Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson gave the lecture "Practical Monetary Policy: Why Has the Riksbank's Policy-Rate Path Been So High, and Why Did This Not Prevent the Recovery?" at the National Conference in Economics at Uppsala University. Svensson believed that the Riksbank's interest rate path has been too high and that this was due, among other things, to an excessively high forecast for foreign policy rates and to an overestimation of and too high a forecast for resource utilisation. He also claimed that the recovery in the Swedish economy has benefited from the market implementing low long-term interest rates and financial conditions that have been much more expansionary than those that have been consistent with the high interest rate path. He also noted that "a simple and transparent monetary policy framework brings significant benefits to both policymakers and external evaluators of monetary policy". The lecture was based on an essay on monetary policy in Sweden and the United States that Svensson presented at a conference arranged by the Brookings Institute in Washington, USA on September 15, 2011. The thesis is available for download on the Brookings Institute's website. See the presentation material from the lecture and read the summary of Svensson's lecture in the pdf file.

Title: Challenges for the Riksbank  monetary policy, financial stability and asset management
text: Svensson: Challenges for the Riksbank  monetary policy, financial stability and asset management Date: 2011-11-17 Speaker: Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson Location: School of Business, Economics and Law, University of Gothenburg On Thursday, Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson Felix Neubergh gave the lecture "Central-banking challenges for the Riksbank  monetary policy, financial stability policy and asset management" at the School of Business, Economics and Law at the University of Gothenburg. In his lecture, Svensson discussed challenges that the Riksbank faces in its basic tasks. The first challenge, Svensson said, is to ensure that monetary policy is clearly and unambiguously and clearly focused on stabilizing inflation and resource utilisation and not on anything else. A closely related challenge, Svensson argued, is the risk of a conceptual and practical confusion between monetary policy and policy to promote financial stability. The third and final challenge he discussed concerned the need to ensure that the Riksbank's asset management is efficient and eliminates unnecessary risks  including the large currency risk. Title: What have economists learned about monetary policy over the past 50 years?
text: Svensson: What have economists learned about monetary policy over the past 50 years? Date 2007-09-21 Deputy Governor Lars E.O. Svensson spoke today at the conference "Monetary Policy over Fifty Years" in Frankfurt held on the occasion of the Bundesbank's 50th anniversary. In his speech, Svensson presented his personal view of how research on monetary policy has developed over the past 50 years. The speech was given in English. "In economic research, it is a 50-year-long time. Since I will begin in 1967, with Milton Friedman's speech before the American Economic Association, I will in fact only be talking about the last 40 years. I will present my very personal view of the lessons economists have learned since Friedman's speech that are of greatest importance for practical monetary policy. So I will be selective, eclectic and perhaps controversial," Svensson began. Friedmans klassiska anforande The role of monetary policy "Friedman's speech was titled 'The role of monetary policy' and remains a classic in the development of the monetary policy framework. He discussed what monetary policy cannot do, what it can do and how it should be conducted. As for what monetary policy cannot do, he noted that in the long run it cannot control real variables such as unemployment and GDP. It can only control nominal variables such as exchange rates, price level and measures of money supply. At the time, these insights were not obvious, but today they are 'conventional wisdom'," Svensson continued. "In terms of what monetary policy can do, Friedman emphasized three things: First, monetary policy can avoid giving rise to serious disruptions. It should avoid major mistakes. Secondly, monetary policy can create stable conditions for the economy, preferably by achieving price stability. And, finally, it can help to counteract serious disruptions in the economic system emanating from other sources. On the last point, Friedman stressed the danger of being overambitious: ' '[T]he potentiality of monetary policy in offsetting other forces making for instability is far more limited than is commonly believed. ... In this area particularly the best is likely to be the enemy of the good. Experience suggests that the path of wisdom is to use monetary policy explicitly to offset other disturbances only when they offer a clear and present danger' ", sade Svensson. "Controlling the money supply  controlling the price level is too difficult" "With regard to how monetary policy should be conducted, Friedman set out two demands: The first requirement is that central banks only control variables that they can control, such as the use of monetary policy. exchange rate, price level or a measure of money. Friedman believed that an exchange rate target would be inappropriate for the United States, as it involves aligning with the average of policies pursued by monetary policy authorities in the rest of the world. He stated that the best thing in principle is to control the price level, but at the same time stressed that the control of the price level is too inadequate because the impact of monetary policy measures on the price level is uncertain and with long and variable lags. His recommendation was therefore that central banks should control a measure of the money supply, as they have greater control over the money supply and the backlog is smaller. The second requirement is that central banks should avoid major fluctuations in their policies. He therefore recommended that central banks create steady but moderate growth in a given monetary aggregate  which growth rate and which measure is chosen is less important provided they have been clearly announced and adopted. Friedman said, 'That is the most that we can ask from monetary policy at our present state of knowledge,'" Svensson continued, emphasizing Friedman's caveat "at our present state of knowledge." Money supply management failed but inflation targeting has worked well "Money supply targets were tried in several countries in the 1970s and 1980s but consistently failed, leading to their abandonment. However, when inflation targeting policy, which is best practice in today's monetary policy, was introduced in the 1990s in New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, Sweden, Finland, Australia and later in many other countries, it worked well. The big exception to the failure of the money supply targets seems to be the outstanding results achieved in Germany by the Bundesbank, which kept inflation low and stable when in other countries it became high and variable," Svensson said. "However, a closer examination and numerous studies of the Bundesbank's monetary policy have shown that the bank actually pursued inflation targeting in secret: As soon as there was a conflict between the target of monetary growth and the inflation target (which was called 'inevitable inflation', 'price norm' or 'medium-term price assumption'), the Bundesbank consistently prioritised the inflation target and was prepared to miss the money supply target. In fact, the Bundesbank's outstanding performance is due to successful inflation targeting and not to money supply management  although in this case the inflation targeting management was not very transparent," Svensson added. "Friedman actually changed his mind in light of later findings. A few years ago, at a conference at the San Francisco Fed, I myself had the opportunity to ask him whether the success of inflation targeting policy could lead him to revise his recommendation that central banks should control the money supply instead of directly targeting inflation and price levels. He replied that he had revised his recommendation. In an interview with the Financial Times in June 2003, Friedman also admitted that the money supply policy had not been successful," Svensson continued. "In practice, inflation targeting policies are always flexible, that is, they aim not only to stabilize inflation around an inflation target, but also the real economy. Moreover, as monetary policy measures affect inflation and resource utilisation with a significant backlog, it is necessary to rely on forecasts. The flexible inflation targeting policy therefore ends up being what I usually call 'forecast targeting', which involves choosing and applying an interest rate path that makes the forecasts for inflation and the measures of resource utilisation 'look good'. By "to look good" is meant inflation that approaches the target and resource utilisation that approaches normal levels at an appropriate pace," Svensson continued. Better knowledge of the transmission mechanism "Why has inflation targeting policy worked so well? I think central banks today have a better understanding of the transmission mechanism of monetary policy than 40 years ago. This gives them the opportunity to produce useful forecasts for inflation and resource utilisation that are conditioned on alternative interest rate paths  forecasts that are a necessary prerequisite for forecast management policy," Svensson said. "The conventional wisdom when it comes to the transmission mechanism  with the aggregate demand and the aggregate supply and phillips curves  is still relevant. But it has improved significantly with more transmission channels and, above all, with a much better understanding of the importance of expectations. Today, it is more generally accepted that monetary policy operates primarily through private actors' expectations of future interest rates and inflation that central banks' actions and statements give rise to. These expectations play a much bigger role than interest rates today. As Michael Woodford has put it: monetary policy is 'the management of expectations', that is, 'influencing expectations'. Some central banks  the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Norges Bank, Sveriges Riksbank and Sedlabanki Islands  now choose and publish what can be interpreted as an optimal interest rate path or interest rate plan, as they consider it a more efficient and transparent way to conduct their monetary policy. I think this will eventually become common practice. Among other things, the Czech Central Bank has announced that it will do this from 2008," Svensson said. "While theoretical research on the transmission mechanism has progressed, the empirical methods have been improved, for example with kalman filtering, vector autoregression and Bayesian estimation methods. Today's front line in monetary policy research seems to be the development within several central banks of empirical, Bayesian DSGE (dynamic, stochastic general equilibrium models) to be used for analyses, forecasts and simulations. The Riksbank already has such a model called RAMSES, which is used operationally," Svensson continued. Monetary aggregates play little role in monetary policy "I also think we've learned that monetary aggregates play a small or even non-existent role in monetary policy. Credit aggregates, on the other hand, can play a role. But economic theory has not been able to demonstrate a separate transmission channel from money supply to prices. A significant amount of empirical research has confirmed that the money supply provides little or no information about future inflation beyond other explanatory variables, both for short- and long-term fluctuations," Svensson said. "I further believe that Friedman's statement that 'inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon' is often misunderstood. It refers to a correlation between endogenous variables, inflation and money supply growth, but does not say anything about causality, that is, which variable determines the other. Instead, the direction of causation is determined by the monetary policy regime. More specifically, endogenous variables are determined by exogenous variables in general equilibrium and which variables are exogenous and endogenous, respectively, depend on the monetary policy regime. With a strict monetary supply target, money growth becomes, in reality, an exogenous variable. Inflation then becomes an endogenous variable determined by money growth. With a strict inflation target, inflation becomes in reality an exogenous variable. Money supply growth then becomes an endogenous variable determined by inflation. With a fixed exchange rate, both inflation and monetary growth become endogenous variables, both of which are determined by exogenous domestic and foreign variables, including the monetary policies of other countries," Svensson said. The importance of the institutional framework "We have also learned how important the institutional framework is for a stable and successful monetary policy. The Bundesbank has been the starting point for recent institutional developments. A good and stable monetary policy is now considered to rest on three pillars: 1) a mandate, where the emphasis is on price stability but where some weight is also given attaches to the stabilisation of the real economy, 2) independence, to avoid short-term political interference and enable the central bank to fulfil its mandate, and 3) accountability, which is promoted by transparency, gives the central bank an incentive to fulfil its mandate and ensures that this important institution is under democratic control. Today, there is also a much greater understanding of the importance of credibility and transparency, and a good institutional structure contributes to making the monetary policy regime credible," Svensson continued. Taylor rules are robust but overemphasized and often misunderstood "Taylor rules, which involve setting interest rates mechanically as a simple, linear function of current inflation and output, are often mentioned in today's monetary policy analyses. I believe that the Taylor rules are often overemphasized and misunderstood. In many research papers, monetary policy is described as if central banks are committed to a Taylor rule and Taylor rules are often treated as a structural equation. However, no central bank has made such a commitment and central banks pursuing inflation targeting policies take into account much more information than just today's inflation and output. In empirical analyses, Taylor rules turn out to have a limited accuracy: I don't know of any regression where R-square for rate changes is higher than about 2/3. This means that 1/3 of the variance in interest rate changes has its explanation in factors other than the Taylor rule. Taylor rules are, in fact, empirical and simplified reduced forms, not structural equations. They are not optimal and they lack micro-foundations," Svensson said. "However, Taylor rules are quite robust in the sense that they almost never work very poorly in reasonable models. Why is that? The reason is that an optimal instrument rule takes into account all the factors that determine the forecasts of the target variables (inflation and resource utilisation). Inflation and production today are important determinants of inflation and production in the future. Therefore, to consider only today's inflation and production is not so bad, but really a rather robust policy. If the central bank doesn't know much about the economy and the transmission mechanism but can at least observe today's inflation and production, there are far worse things it can do than follow a Taylor rule. But since the central banks that currently pursue an inflation targeting policy have access to significantly more information and know more about the transmission mechanism, they do not have to settle for a Taylor rule. They therefore consider more information and deviate quite significantly from a Taylor rule," Svensson said. What knowledge gaps are there? "What knowledge gaps are there and in what areas should we try to make progress in future research? I think it is desirable for the flexible inflation targeting policy to become more explicit. This requires working more with measures of resource stabilization and potential production, which gives rise to difficult but important conceptual and empirical questions. I also believe that flexible inflation targeting policies would benefit from an increased use of explicit loss functions to evaluate different monetary policy options and determine which is optimal. Norges Bank seems to be ahead of other central banks here. Anyone who works with monetary policy knows that there is always model uncertainty and it is sometimes very large. We would definitely benefit from better methods of integrating model uncertainty into forecasts. It would also be desirable to have better descriptions of the credit channel, the labour market and of financial markets and how the yield curve and exchange rate are determined in the existing empirical DSBE models for the transmission mechanism," Svensson continued. "In terms of the ongoing discussion about the role of asset prices in monetary policy, I think we know enough to be able to conclude that monetary policy should not have targets for asset prices. As long as their development does not threaten financial stability and the payment system, they are only relevant to monetary policy as indicator variables, that is, only insofar as they contain any information on the future target variables (inflation and resource utilisation). However, if the development of credit or asset prices would threaten financial stability or the payment system, this may place restrictions on the normal way of conducting monetary policy and may also require special measures", Svensson concluded.

Friedman sade:  That is the most that we can ask from monetary policy at our present state of knowledge, fortsatte Svensson och betonade Friedmans frbehll at our present state of knowledge. Penningmngdsstyrning misslyckades men inflationsmlsstyrning har fungerat bra Penningmngdsml prvades i flera lnder p 1970- och 1980-talen men misslyckades genomgende, vilket ledde till att de vergavs. Nr inflationsmlspolitiken, som r bsta praxis inom dagens penningpolitik, infrdes p 1990-talet i Nya Zeeland, Kanada, Storbritannien, Sverige, Finland, Australien och senare i mnga andra lnder fungerade den dremot bra. Det stora undantaget nr det gller penningmngdsmlens misslyckande tycks vara de enastende resultat som uppnddes i Tyskland av Bundesbank, som hll inflationen lg och stabil nr den i andra lnder blev hg och varierande, sade Svensson. En nrmare granskning och mnga studier av Bundesbanks penningpolitik har emellertid visat att banken faktiskt bedrev inflationsmlsstyrning i det frdolda: S snart det uppstod en konflikt mellan mlet fr pennningmngdstillvxten och inflationsmlet (som kallades oundviklig inflation, prisnorm eller prisantagande p medellng sikt) prioriterade Bundesbank konsekvent inflationsmlet och var beredd att missa penningmngdsmlet. Egentligen beror Bundesbanks enastende resultat allts p framgngsrik inflationsmlsstyrning och inte p penningmngdsstyrning  ven om inflationsmlsstyrningen i det hr fallet inte var srskilt transparent, tillade Svensson. Friedman ndrade faktiskt uppfattning i ljuset av senare rn. Fr ngra r sedan fick jag i samband med en konferens p San Francisco Fed sjlv tillflle att frga honom om inflationsmlspolitikens framgngar kunde f honom att revidera sin rekommendation om att centralbanker ska styra penningmngden i stllet fr att direkt rikta in sig p inflation och prisniv. Han svarade att han hade reviderat sin rekommendation. I en intervju med Financial Times i juni 2003 medgav Friedman ocks att politiken med penningmngdsml inte hade varit framgngsrik, fortsatte Svensson. Inflationsmlspolitik r i praktiken alltid flexibel, det vill sga den syftar inte bara till att stabilisera inflationen kring ett inflationsml utan ocks den reala ekonomin. Eftersom penningpolitiska tgrder pverkar inflation och resursutnyttjande med en betydande efterslpning r det dessutom ndvndigt att frlita sig p prognoser. Den flexibla inflationsmlspolitiken blir drfr i slutndan vad jag brukar kalla prognosstyrning (forecast targeting) som gr ut p att vlja och tillmpa en rntebana som fr prognoserna fr inflationen och mtten p resursutnyttjande att se bra ut. Med att se bra ut menas en inflation som nrmar sig mlet och ett resursutnyttjande som nrmar sig normal niv i lmplig takt, fortsatte Svensson. Bttre kunskaper om transmissionsmekanismen Varfr har inflationsmlspolitiken fungerat s bra? Jag tror att centralbankerna idag har bttre kunskaper om penningpolitikens transmissionsmekanism n fr 40 r sedan. Det ger dem mjligheten att ta fram anvndbara prognoser fr inflation och resursutnyttjande som r betingade p alternativa rntebanor  prognoser som r en ndvndig frutsttning fr prognosstyrningspolitiken, sade Svensson. Den konventionella visdomen nr det gller transmissionsmekanismen  med den aggregerade efterfrgan och det aggregerade utbudet och Phillipskurvorna  r fortfarande relevant. Men den har frbttrats avsevrt med fler transmissionskanaler och, framfrallt, med en mycket bttre frstelse av frvntningarnas betydelse. Idag r det mer allmnt vedertaget att penningpolitiken i frsta hand verkar genom privata aktrers frvntningar om framtida rntor och inflation som centralbankernas agerande och uttalanden ger upphov till. Dessa frvntningar spelar en mycket strre roll n rntorna idag. Som Michael Woodford har uttryckt det: penningpolitik r the management of expectations, det vill sga att pverka frvntningar. Ngra centralbanker  Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Norges Bank, Sveriges riksbank och Sedlabanki Islands  vljer och offentliggr numera vad som kan tolkas som en optimal rntebana eller rnteplan, eftersom de anser det vara ett mer effektivt och transparent stt att bedriva sin penningpolitik. Jag tror att detta s smningom kommer att bli gngse praxis. Bland annat har den tjeckiska centralbanken meddelat att man kommer att gra detta frn och med 2008, sade Svensson. Samtidigt som den teoretiska forskningen om transmissionsmekanismen har gtt framt har de empiriska metoderna frbttrats, till exempel med kalmanfiltrering, vektor-autoregression och bayesianska skattningsmetoder. Dagens frontlinje i den penningpolitiska forskningen verkar vara utvecklingen inom flera centralbanker av empiriska, bayesianska DSGE-modeller (dynamiska, stokastiska allmnjmviktsmodeller) som ska anvndas fr analyser, prognoser och simuleringar. Riksbanken har redan en sdan modell kallad RAMSES som anvnds operativt, fortsatte Svensson. Penningmngdsmtt spelar liten roll fr penningpolitiken Jag tror ocks att vi har lrt oss att penningmngdsmtten spelar en liten eller till och med obefintlig roll fr penningpolitiken. Kreditaggregat kan dremot spela en roll. Men nationalekonomisk teori har inte kunnat pvisa ngon separat transmissionskanal frn penningmngd till priser. En betydande mngd empirisk forskning har bekrftat att penningmngden ger lite eller ingen information om den framtida inflationen utver andra frklaringsvariabler, bde fr kort- och lngsiktiga fluktuationer, sade Svensson. Jag tror vidare att Friedmans uttalande om att inflation alltid och verallt r ett monetrt fenomen ofta missfrsts. Det hnvisar till en korrelation mellan endogena variabler, inflation och penningmngdstillvxt, men sger inget om kausaliteten, det vill sga vilken variabel som bestmmer den andra. Riktningen p kausaliteten bestms i stllet av den penningpolitiska regimen. Mer specifikt bestms endogena variabler av exogena variabler i allmn jmvikt och vilka variabler som r exogena respektive endogena beror p den penningpolitiska regimen. Med ett strikt penningmngdsml blir penningmngdstillvxten i realiteten en exogen variabel. Inflationen blir d en endogen variabel som bestms av penningmngdstillvxten. Med ett strikt inflationsml blir inflationen i realiteten en exogen variabel. Penningmngdstillvxten blir d en endogen variabel som bestms av inflationen. Med en fast vxelkurs blir bde inflationen och penningmngdstillvxten endogena variabler, som bda bestms av exogena inhemska och utlndska variabler, dribland andra lnders penningpolitik", sade Svensson. Vikten av det institutionella ramverket Vi har ocks lrt oss hur viktig det institutionella ramverket r fr en stabil och framgngsrik penningpolitik. Bundesbank har varit utgngspunkten fr den senare institutionella utvecklingen. En bra och stabil penningpolitik anses numera vila p tre pelare: 1) ett mandat, dr tyngdpunkten ligger p prisstabilitet men dr viss vikt ven fsts vid stabilisering av den reala ekonomin, 2) oberoende, fr att undvika kortsiktig politisk inblandning och gra det mjligt fr centralbanken att fullgra sitt mandat, och 3) ansvarighet, vilket frmjas av ppenhet, ger centralbanken ett incitament att fullgra sitt mandat och skerstller att denna betydelsefulla institution str under demokratisk kontroll. Idag finns det ocks en mycket strre frstelse fr hur viktigt det r med trovrdighet och ppenhet, och en bra institutionell struktur bidrar till att gra den penningpolitiska regimen trovrdig, fortsatte Svensson. Taylor-regler r robusta men verbetonas och missfrsts ofta Taylor-regler, som innebr att rntan stts mekaniskt som en enkel, linjr funktion av nuvarande inflation och produktion, nmns ofta i dagens penningpolitiska analyser. Jag anser att Taylor-reglerna ofta verbetonas och missfrsts. I mnga forskningsrapporter beskrivs penningpolitiken som om centralbanker har tagit sig att flja en Taylor-regel och Taylor-regler behandlas ofta som en strukturell ekvation. Ingen centralbank har dock gjort ngot sdant tagande och centralbanker som fr en inflationsmlspolitik beaktar mycket mer information n bara dagens inflation och produktion. I empiriska analyser visar sig Taylor-regler ha en begrnsad trffskerhet: jag knner inte till ngon regression dr R-kvadrat fr rntefrndringar r hgre n ca 2/3. Det innebr att 1/3 av variansen i rntefrndringar har sin frklaring i andra faktorer n Taylor-regeln. Taylor-regler r i sjlva verket empiriska och frenklade reducerade former, inte strukturella ekvationer. De r inte optimala och de saknar mikrofundament, sade Svensson. Taylor-regler r emellertid ganska robusta i den meningen att de nstan aldrig fungerar mycket dligt i rimliga modeller. Vad beror det p? Sklet r att en optimal instrumentregel beaktar alla de faktorer som bestmmer prognoserna fr mlvariablerna (inflation och resursutnyttjande). Inflationen och produktionen idag r viktiga bestmningsfaktorer fr inflationen och produktionen i framtiden. Att enbart beakta dagens inflation och produktion r drfr inte s dumt, utan egentligen en ganska robust politik. Om centralbanken inte vet s mycket om ekonomin och transmissionsmekanismen men tminstone kan observera dagens inflation och produktion finns det betydligt vrre saker den kan gra n att flja en Taylor-regel. Men eftersom de centralbanker som idag fr en inflationsmlspolitik har tillgng till betydligt mer information och vet mer om transmissionsmekanismen behver de inte nja sig med en Taylor-regel. De beaktar drfr mer information och avviker ganska rejlt frn en Taylor-regel, sade Svensson. Vilka kunskapsbrister finns det? Vilka kunskapsbrister finns det och inom vilka omrden br vi frska gra framsteg i framtida forskning? Jag tycker det r nskvrt att den flexibla inflationsmlspolitiken blir mer explicit. Detta krver att man arbetar mer med mtt p resursstabilisering och potentiell produktion vilket ger upphov till svra men viktiga begreppsmssiga och empiriska frgestllningar. Jag anser ocks att den flexibla inflationsmlspolitiken skulle dra nytta av en kad anvndning av explicita frlustfunktioner fr att utvrdera olika penningpolitiska alternativ och faststlla vilket som r optimalt. Norges Bank verkar hr ligga fre andra centralbanker. Alla som arbetar med penningpolitik vet att det alltid finns modelloskerhet och den r ibland mycket stor. Vi skulle definitivt ha nytta av bttre metoder fr att integrera modelloskerheten i prognoserna. Det vore ocks nskvrt att ha bttre beskrivningar av kreditkanalen, arbetsmarknaden och av finansiella marknader och hur avkastningskurvan och vxelkursen bestms i de befintliga empiriska DSGEmodellerna fr transmissionsmekanismen, fortsatte Svensson. Nr det gller den pgende diskussionen om tillgngsprisernas roll i penningpolitiken tror jag att vi vet tillrckligt fr att kunna sl fast att penningpolitiken inte br ha ml fr tillgngspriser. S lnge deras utveckling inte hotar den finansiella stabiliteten och betalningssystemet r de bara relevanta fr penningpolitiken i egenskap av indikatorvariabler, det vill sga bara i den mn de innehller ngon information om de framtida mlvariablerna (inflation och resursutnyttjande). Men om utvecklingen av krediter eller tillgngspriser skulle hota den finansiella stabiliteten eller betalningssystemet kan detta lgga restriktioner p det normala sttet att bedriva penningpolitik och kan ven krva srskilda tgrder, avslutade Svensson. Title: Sweden and EMU
text: Sweden and EMU Date: 1997-10-22 Speaker: Governor Urban Be4ckstrf6m Location: Annual Meeting of the Swedish Bankers' Association in Stockholm Mr President, let me first thank you for the invitation to speak about EMU at the Annual Meeting of the Bankers' Association. We have now heard the Finance Minister describe the political situation in Sweden and we have heard the Governor of the Finnish Central Bank talk about the situation of a country that wants to join monetary cooperation from its inception. I would now like to give my picture of the situation for the Riksbank. A situation that can be likened to being both outside and inside. There are a number of areas where we as a central bank must "join" even though Sweden as a nation has chosen not to participate fully in the third stage of the EMI from the beginning. In the event of exclusion, we will, of course, be excluded from the major step in EMU, that of introducing the new currency. Nor will we leave monetary policy to the ECB. But despite this, Sweden is a member of the EU and has full access to the internal market. We are also now participating in the second stage of EMU and we will become members of the ESCB, the European System of Central Banks. The Riksbank must also be prepared for a possible later entry. How the Riksbank will handle this situation in the future is what I intend to dwell on here today. Sweden, member of the EU but outside EMU EMU will mean major changes for all countries within the EU. All in all, I believe that Sweden is well equipped to meet these changes. Our economy has achieved an ever better foundation on which to stand. From the economic crisis of the early 1990s and the major setback after the inflationary economy, today we have a situation characterized by low inflation and favorable growth. The ambitions to strengthen public finances and achieve a balance in the 1998 budget have contributed to strengthening public confidence in Swedish politics. This is reflected in the fact that the krona has appreciated in recent years and long-term interest rates have converged more and more towards European levels - although in both these areas we have some way to go. However, one area remains in this extensive work, namely the labour market. Unemployment is still very high. Let me also say something about Sweden's role in Europe. Since 1995, we have been full members of the EU. Being part of this cooperation in a number of socio-economic and political areas with fourteen other EU countries has meant a new situation for us in Sweden. The EU-related work has increased continuously and I think that most of us have experienced it as positive to be involved and influence developments in Europe in a more clear way than we could outside the EU. Even if we do not participate in monetary union, this cooperation will continue. For example, we will be bound to treat our economic and monetary policies as a matter of 'common interest'. Developments in the Swedish economy will be examined and monitored. Convergence programmes shall be presented annually. However, the development ahead is not just about Europe, we are today seeing extensive globalization and continued integration of markets around the world. Especially in the financial field, over the past decade there have been dramatic developments in terms of integration, harmonisation and technological development. Great demands will be placed on the financial sector and the banking system in Sweden if we want to compete in the new open world market for financial services. We can already see today how the Stockholm Stock Exchange is preparing to list shares in currencies other than sek, we see that the traditionally oriented major banks through mergers and acquisitions have decreased in number and at the same time increased in size, but we also see an increase in the number of niche banks. These are all signs that the financial sector in Sweden is adapting to face a new situation. The Riksbank is also affected by the new developments. The demands for credibility and discipline in monetary policy have increased markedly in recent years. Furthermore, the requirements for financial stability have increased. Also when it comes to more practical things, we adapt. The Riksbank has decided to approve certain foreign securities as pledges in the RIX system. It is a step in increasing the efficiency of our payment system, among other things. The Riksbank's role in the ESCB As I have previously mentioned, the Riksbank will also be part of the European System of Central Banks as an outdoor country. We will not be part of the ECB's main decision-making body, the Governing Council, but we will participate in the ECB's General Council. This Council will include the governors of the central banks of all EU countries together with the President and Vice-President of the ECB. The General Affairs Council has no influence on monetary policy in the euro area, but will nevertheless have a number of important tasks. The most important task will be to take over the functions of the EMI, which must continue to be carried out as long as there are countries which do not participate in monetary union. This means, among other things, monitoring the convergence process in the non-participating EU countries. It will also coordinate monetary policy between the euro area and the EU countries not participating in monetary union and the new exchange rate system, ERM2, will be administered. It is also for the General Affairs Council to prepare for countries entering monetary union later. By participating in the General Affairs Council, we will also gain insight into the activities of the Governing Council when the President of the ECB informs the General Council of the decisions it has taken. EMI currently has about 30 committees and working groups where we participate. We do not know exactly what the committee structure of the ECB will look like today. Some workgroups may disappear and others come into being. Nor do we know what the representation for us as an outside country will be like in these new groups. Participation is likely to be limited to certain areas. But since most issues will continue to affect the outside countries as well, it is likely that our representation in the upcoming committee work will be extensive in the future as well. This will continue to be an important activity for the Riksbank. In addition to continuing to work at European level, there are also areas here at home that we must monitor. The Riksbank will continue with preparatory work. Of course, we in the Riksbank have asked ourselves how we should relate to euro preparations in the light of the fact that Sweden is initially outside the currency union. A decision to actively continue the preparatory work involves extensive work at the bank, where all relevant economists, lawyers, computer technicians and statisticians must acquire an in-depth knowledge and understanding of how the planned systems are intended to work, even if monetary policy is fundamentally similar to the one the Riksbank conducts today. We have come to the conclusion that even if Sweden is not to participate in the currency union from the start, the Riksbank will have to be highly prepared for a later entry. We do not want to risk ending up in a situation where decisions on participation are changed and the Riksbank does not have time for the changes needed to be able to participate in EMU. To be clear on this point, we have said that the Riksbank will be able to join the Union within a year. Thus, from the time it is clear that Sweden will participate, it will take a maximum of one year for the Riksbank to cope with the transitions needed to: participate in the single monetary policy. In order for the Riksbank to be able to maintain this one-year limit and for a number of other reasons, to which I will return, the Riksbank's preparations for meeting the euro are progressing. We will continue our work to consult with and inform the Swedish financial sector and we will prepare internally. I would like to mention some important areas for this preparatory work. Statistics One concrete area where preparations are also continuing for outdoor countries is the collection of statistics. In order to conduct the single monetary policy in EMU, an analytical basis based on harmonised statistics for the entire EMU area will be needed. Firstly, it is a question of compiling a harmonised balance sheet for the financial institutions that are important for the exercise of monetary policy. Secondly, it is important that the ECB has a good picture of the Union's relations with surrounding economies, for example in terms of currency flows and securities trading. It takes a long time to transform statistical systems so that they deliver the basis needed for the single monetary policy. This long preparation time is also the reason why the statistical area is one of the areas in which Sweden and the Riksbank participate, regardless of membership in the currency union. It follows that the Riksbank is continuing the statistical transitions despite the fact that Sweden does not participate in EMU from the start. I would like to take this opportunity to thank you for the extensive work that you and your colleagues in the banks are putting into this. An improved statistical basis is of course valuable for the Riksbank even in the event of exclusion. The control system We already know what the monetary policy system will look like in principle when EMU is formed. Going forward, the NCBs themselves will be active in the further work of adapting technology and internal procedures so that they can effectively operate with a single monetary policy. EMI's role in this work is to coordinate and supervise and the central banks then have the ultimate responsibility for implementing the necessary changes. The Riksbank has chosen to continue to participate in the preparatory work in step with the other central banks. Our policy going forward is that, as a starting point, we participate fully in the preparatory work, but at the same time we reserve the right, as the work progresses and issues arise, to test and evaluate whether it makes sense to carry out these particular preparations and to do so right now instead of later. Some preparations may prove to incur unnecessary costs if they are carried out now. Such changes, of course, should not be made. This may apply, for example, to computer systems that become obsolete within a couple of years and thus have to be continuously replaced. Similarly, there is still uncertainty on some points about how the ECB will actually conduct its monetary policy. In these cases, there may be reasons to wait with preparations to avoid unnecessary work. However, it is impossible to make a full assessment at this stage of which of these preparations we should refrain from. Therefore, today we are working on preparation across the field and will reduce our involvement only when we see clear reasons for it. THE TARGET system An important task of the EMI is to build up the European payment system, TARGET. Through this system, the payment systems of the fifteen EU countries are linked to a system that is already being tested. Target will be responsible for the swift and secure processing of payments related to monetary policy operations, but the system will also handle commercial payments. Participation in TARGET is formally open to all EU countries, not just those that will participate in EMU. Target is therefore as important a project for the 'single market' as it is for EMU. The requirements for this system must therefore be imposed both on the basis of its role in the single monetary policy and on the principles on which the internal market is based, i.e. fair and open competition and non-discrimination. Unfortunately, however, these good principles do not seem to have been fully applied, and I regret that. As is well known, there is a risk that EU countries outside EMU may be de facto discriminated against when it comes to accessing so-called intraday credit in the system. These are credits that provide the necessary liquidity readiness to fend off fluctuations in payment flows on an ongoing basis, thus preventing bottlenecks and lock-ins in payment flows. We do not know for sure today whether any such restrictions will actually be imposed, and if so, how they will be applied. It is therefore important that both the Riksbank and the banks prepare to deal with such a situation - and this is certainly already happening. If Swedish banks do not have access to intraday credit in the ESCB, the options for the banks are essentially three: to outsource payment processing in euros to a branch or subsidiary bank in the EMU area, to borrow euros on the market, or if possible to find ways to "bring home" euro liquidity to Sweden. As for the intermediate option, it is very likely that a market for intraday liquidity in euros will emerge. The issue is complicated by the fact that the problem actually has two dimensions: firstly, there is the pure 'access issue', which I have touched on, and secondly, Sweden, as an outside country, will also be able to have problems with regard to the collateral for euro borrowing, which applies even if we were to have the fundamental right to borrowing. What is at issue is that the securities that will be accepted as collateral within the ESCB must meet certain criteria, be able to be proposed by the national central banks and finally approved by the ECB. The problem for us as an 'out-of-town bank' is that we will not be part of the circle of central banks that can propose collateral, let alone be involved in making these decisions. If Swedish krona-denominated government and housing securities are to be used as collateral for intraday loans in euros, they must therefore be proposed and "listed" by a central bank within EMU. This must then be approved by the ECB. We thus become highly dependent on the benevolence of others. The issue of intraday credit is a difficult one and we continue to work with it within the EMI to bring about sensible solutions from a Swedish point of view. But we have also asked ourselves whether we in the Riksbank can contribute more effectively to facilitating the banks' supply of euro liquidity during the day, without, however, engaging in any form of subsidized lending. What we have looked at is the possibility of using the euro part of our foreign exchange reserves. We believe that this is technically possible to cope with and it may be a possibility, given that it is accepted by the ECB. However, this would entail costs for the Riksbank that we would have to charge the banks. How big these would be and whether this will be a financially attractive solution for the banks, it is difficult to have an exact idea of today. However, we believe there is value in this possibility being carefully explored, as an alternative or a complement to the avenues and methods the banks themselves will to follow. In summary, it can thus be said that the banks will find different ways to deal with the Target problem, and we as the Riksbank will contribute as constructively as possible. But whatever solutions we choose, we are not likely to get away from the fact that this will cost - exclusion has a price and this is part of it. The design of the target system will also affect the Swedish financial market in other ways. One such thing concerns the opening hours of the system. EMI's focus is for Target to be open every day except Christmas Day and New Year's Day, as well as Saturdays and Sundays. This will not mean any compulsion for individual countries to stay open all other holidays - if we in Sweden want to keep the store closed on, for example, Midsummer's Eve and instead devote ourselves to herring with its accessories, no one will force us to stay open. However, it is quite clear that we will see a market-driven process towards an increasingly "standardized" opening hours, where we will probably have to get used to the idea that more and more functions will be kept open for more and more days. From the Riksbank's side, we will take the initiative to start a discussion on these issues. This issue and many others need to be resolved in the future. Eu work has not stopped in Sweden, despite the fact that we will not participate in EMU from the start.
text_original: UTSKRIFT FRN WWW.RIKSBANK.SE Sverige och EMU Datum: 1997-10-22 Talare: Riksbankschef Urban Bckstrm Plats: Svenska Bankfreningens rsmte i Stockholm Lt mig frst tacka fr inbjudan att tala om EMU p Bankfreningens rsmte. Vi har nu hrt finansministern beskriva det politiska lget i Sverige och vi har hrt den finlndska centralbankschefen tala om lget fr ett land som vill g med i valutasamarbetet frn dess start. Jag vill nu ge min bild av situationen fr Riksbanken. En situation som kan liknas vid att vara bde ute och inne. Det finns nmligen ett antal omrden dr vi som centralbank mste "g med" fast Sverige som nation valt att inte delta fullt ut i EMUs tredje etapp frn brjan. Vid ett utanfrskap kommer vi sjlvklart att st utanfr det stora steget i EMU, det att introducera den nya valutan. Vi kommer inte heller att verlta penningpolitiken till ECB. Men oaktat detta r Sverige medlem i EU och har fullt tilltrde till den inre marknaden. Vi deltar ocks nu i den andra etappen av EMU och vi kommer att bli medlemmar i ECBS, det europeiska centralbankssystemet. Riksbanken mste ocks hlla beredskap fr ett eventuellt senare intrde. Hur Riksbanken skall hantera denna situation framver r vad jag tnker uppehlla mig kring hr idag. Sverige, medlem i EU men utanfr EMU EMU kommer att innebra stora frndringar fr alla lnder inom EU. Sammantaget tror jag att Sverige str vl rustat fr att mta dessa frndringar. Vr ekonomi har uppntt en allt bttre grund att st p. Frn den ekonomiska krisen i brjan av 1990talet och det stora bakslaget efter inflationsekonomin har vi idag en situation som prglas av lg inflation och gynnsam tillvxt. Ambitionerna att strka statsfinanserna och n balans i budgeten 1998 har medverkat till att det allmnna frtroendet fr den svenska politiken har strkts. Det kommer till uttryck i att kronan har apprecierat de senaste ren och den lnga rntan har konvergerat allt mer mot europaniver - ven om vi p bda dessa omrden har en bit kvar. Ett omrde terstr dock i detta omfattande arbete, nmligen arbetsmarknaden. Fortfarande r arbetslsheten mycket hg. Lt mig ocks sga ngot om Sveriges roll i Europa. Sedan 1995 r vi fullvrdiga medlemmar i EU. Att ing i detta samarbete p ett flertal samhllsekonomiska och politiska omrden med fjorton andra EU-lnder har inneburit en ny situation fr oss i Sverige. Det EU-relaterade arbetet har kat kontinuerligt och jag tror att de flesta av oss upplevt det som positivt att f vara med och pverka utvecklingen i Europa p ett mer tydligt stt n vad vi kunnat utanfr EU. ven om vi inte deltar i valutaunionen kommer detta samarbete att fortstta. Vi kommer exempelvis att vara bundna att behandla vr ekonomiska politik och valutapolitik som en frga av "gemensamt intresse". Utvecklingen i den svenska ekonomin kommer att granskas och vara freml fr vervakning. Konvergensprogram skall presenteras rligen. Men, utvecklingen framver handlar inte bara om Europa, vi ser idag en omfattande globalisering och fortsatt integration av marknader runt om i vrlden. Speciellt p det finansiella omrdet har det under de senaste decenniet skett en dramatisk utveckling vad gller integration, harmonisering och teknisk utveckling. Stora krav kommer att stllas p den finansiella sektorn och banksystemet i Sverige om vi vill vara med och konkurrera p den nya ppna vrldsmarknaden fr finansiella tjnster. Vi kan redan idag se hur Stockholms fondbrs frbereder sig fr att notera aktier i andra valutor n kronor, vi ser att de traditionellt inriktade storbankerna genom fusioner och uppkp minskat i antal och samtidigt kat i storlek, men vi ser ocks en kning av antalet nischbanker. Allt detta r tecken p att den finansiella sektorn i Sverige anpassar sig fr att mta en ny situation. ven Riksbanken pverkas av den nya utvecklingen. Kraven p trovrdighet och disciplin i penningpolitiken har kat markant under senare r. Vidare har kraven p finansiell stabilitet kat. Ocks nr det gller mer praktiska saker anpassar vi oss. Riksbanken har fattat beslut om att godknna vissa utlndska vrdepapper som pant i RIX-systemet. Det r ett steg i att ka effektiviteten bl.a. i vrt betalningssystem. Riksbankens roll i ECBS Som jag tidigare nmnt kommer Riksbanken att ing i det europeiska centralbanksystemet ven som uteland. Vi kommer inte att ing i ECBs viktigaste beslutande organ, ECB-rdet, men vi kommer att delta i ECBs allmnna rd. I detta rd kommer centralbankscheferna fr samtliga EU-lnder att ing tillsammans med ECBs ordfrande och vice ordfrande. Det allmnna rdet har inget inflytande ver penningpolitiken i euro-omrdet men kommer nd att ha ett flertal viktiga uppgifter. Den viktigaste uppgiften blir att verta de funktioner som EMI haft och som fortsatt mste utfras s lnge det finns lnder som inte deltar i valutaunionen. Det innebr bland annat att man skall vervaka konvergensprocessen i de EU-lnder som inte deltar. Man skall ocks samordna penningpolitiken mellan euro-omrdet och de EUlnder som inte deltar i valutaunionen och man kommer att administrera det nya vxelkurssystemet, ERM2. Det r ocks allmnna rdet som skall frbereda fr lnder som intrder senare i valutaunionen. Genom att vi deltar i allmnna rdet kommer vi ven att f inblick i ECB-rdets verksamhet d ECBs ordfrande skall underrtta allmnna rdet om de beslut man fattat. EMI har idag ett 30-tal kommitter och arbetsgrupper dr vi deltar. Exakt hur kommittstrukturen i ECB kommer att se ut vet vi inte idag. Vissa arbetsgrupper kanske frsvinner och andra kommer till. Hur representationen fr oss som uteland kommer att bli i dessa nya grupper vet vi inte heller. Troligen blir deltagandet begrnsat till vissa omrden. Men d flertalet frgor fortsatt kommer att berra ven utelnderna s r det troligt att vr representation i det kommande kommittarbetet blir omfattande ven i framtiden. Detta blir en fortsatt viktig verksamhet fr Riksbanken. Frutom att vi fortstter att arbeta p europeisk niv finns det ocks omrden hr hemma vi mste bevaka. Riksbanken fortstter med frberedelsearbete. Naturligtvis har vi i Riksbanken stllt oss frgan hur vi skall frhlla oss till eurofrberedelser i ljuset av att Sverige inledningsvis str utanfr valutaunionen. Ett beslut om att aktivt fortstta frberedelsearbetet innebr ett omfattande arbete p banken, dr alla berrda ekonomer, jurister, datatekniker och statistiker mste skaffa sig en ingende kunskap och frstelse fr hur de planerade systemen r tnkta att fungera ven om penningpolitiken i grunden liknar den Riksbanken bedriver idag. Vi har kommit fram till att ven om Sverige inte skall delta i valutaunionen frn start kommer Riksbanken att vara tvungen att ha hg beredskap fr ett senare intrde. Vi vill inte riskera att hamna i en situation dr beslut om deltagande ndras och Riksbanken inte hinner med de omstllningar som behvs fr att kunna delta i EMU. Fr att vara tydliga p den hr punkten har vi sagt att Riksbanken skall klara ett intrde i unionen inom ett r. Allts, frn det att det str klart att Sverige skall delta skall det ta hgst ett r fr Riksbanken att klara de omstllningar som behvs fr att medverka i den gemensamma penningpolitiken. Fr att Riksbanken skall kunna hlla denna ettrsgrns och p grund av ett antal andra orsaker, som jag terkommer till, fortskrider Riksbankens frberedelser fr att mta euron. Vi kommer att fortstta vrt arbete med att samrda med och informera den svenska finansiella sektorn och vi kommer att frbereda oss internt. Jag vill nmna ngra viktiga omrden fr detta frberedelsearbete. Statistik Ett konkret omrde dr frberedelserna fortstter ven fr utelnder r statistikinsamling. Fr att bedriva den gemensamma penningpolitiken i EMU kommer det att behvas ett analysunderlag som r grundat p en harmoniserad statistik fr hela EMU-omrdet. Fr det frsta gller det att sammanstlla en harmoniserad balansrkning fr de finansiella institut som har betydelse fr utvandet av penningpolitiken. Fr det andra r det viktigt att ECB har en god bild av unionens relationer till omkringliggande ekonomier, t. ex. vad gller valutaflden och vrdepappershandel. Det tar lng tid att stlla om statistiksystem s att de levererar det underlag som behvs fr den gemensamma penningpolitiken. Denna lnga frberedelsetid r ocks sklet till att just statistikomrdet r ett av de omrden dr Sverige och Riksbanken deltar oavsett medlemskap i valutaunionen. Av detta fljer att Riksbanken driver statistikomstllningarna vidare trots att Sverige inte deltar i EMU frn starten. Jag vill passa p tillfllet att tacka fr det omfattande arbete som ni och era kollegor ute i bankerna lgger ned p detta. Ett frbttrat statistikunderlag r givetvis vrdefullt fr Riksbanken ven vid ett utanfrskap. Styrsystemet Vi vet redan hur det penningpolitiska styrsystemet i princip skall se ut nr EMU bildas. Framver kommer de nationella centralbankerna sjlva att vara aktiva i det fortsatta arbetet med att anpassa tekniken och de interna rutinerna s att de i praktiken kan fungera med en gemensam penningpolitik. EMIs roll i detta arbete r att samordna och vervaka och centralbankerna har sedan det yttersta ansvaret fr att de ndvndiga frndringarna genomfrs. Riksbanken har valt att fortstta att delta i frberedelsearbetet i takt med vriga centralbanker. Vr policy framver r att vi som utgngspunkt deltar fullt ut i frberedelsearbetet, men att vi samtidigt frbehller oss rtten att i takt med att arbetet fortskrider och frgor aktualiseras, prva och utvrdera om det r vettigt att genomfra just dessa frberedelser och att gra det just nu i stllet fr senare. Vissa frberedelser kan visa sig frorsaka ondiga kostnader om de genomfrs redan nu. Sdana frndringar br naturligtvis inte gras. Det kan glla t.ex. datasystem som redan inom ett par r blir frldrade och drmed kontinuerligt mste bytas ut. Likas rder det p ngra punkter fortfarande oskerhet om hur ECB faktiskt kommer att bedriva sin penningpolitik. I dessa fall kan det finnas skl att avvakta med frberedelser fr att undvika ondigt arbete. Det r dock omjligt att redan nu gra en fullstndig bedmning av vilka av dessa frberedelser vi skall avst ifrn. Drfr arbetar vi idag med frberedelser ver hela fltet och kommer att minska vrt engagemang frst nr vi ser tydliga skl till det. TARGET-systemet En viktig uppgift fr EMI r att bygga upp det europeiska betalningssystemet, TARGET. Genom detta system kopplas de femton EU lndernas betalningssystem ihop till ett system som redan nu testkrs. Target skall svara fr en snabb och sker hantering av de betalningar som sammanhnger med de penningpolitiska operationerna, men systemet kommer ven att hantera kommersiella betalningar. Deltagandet i Target r i formell mening ppet fr alla EU-lnder, inte bara fr de som kommer att delta i EMU. Target r drfr ett lika betydelsefullt projekt fr den "inre marknaden" som fr EMU. Kraven p detta system mste drfr stllas utifrn svl dess roll i den gemensamma penningpolitiken som utifrn de principer som den inre marknaden grundas p, d v s rttvis och ppen konkurrens och icke-diskriminering. Men tyvrr verkar dessa goda principer inte tillmpats fullt ut, och jag beklagar det. Som bekant finns en risk att EU-lnder utanfr EMU kan komma att de-facto diskrimineras nr det gller att f tillgng till s.k. intradagskrediter i systemet. Det rr sig om krediter som ger den ndvndiga likviditetsberedskapen fr att lpande parera svngningar i betalningsfldena och p s stt frhindrar flaskhalsar och lsningar i betalningsstrmmarna. Vi vet inte idag med skerhet om ngra sdana begrnsningar verkligen kommer att infras, och hur de i s fall kommer att tillmpas. Det r drfr viktigt att svl Riksbanken som bankerna frbereder sig p att hantera en sdan situation - och s sker frvisso redan. Om svenska banker inte fr access till intradagskredit i ECBS, r alternativen fr bankerna i huvudsak tre: att utlokalisera betalningshanteringen i euro till en filial eller dotterbank inom EMU-omrdet, att lna upp euro p marknaden, eller att om mjligt finna vgar att "hmta hem" euro-likviditet till Sverige. Nr det gller mellan alternativet, r det mycket troligt att en marknad fr intradagslikviditet i euro kommer att uppst. Frgan kompliceras av att problemet egentligen har tv dimensioner: dels finns den rena "access-frgan", som jag berrt, dels kommer Sverige som utanfrstende land att kunna f problem ven nr det gller skerheterna fr euro-upplningen, ngot som gller ven om vi skulle f den principiella rtten till upplning. Vad det handlar om r att de vrdepapper som kommer att godtas som skerhet inom ECBS skall uppfylla vissa kriterier, kunna fresls av de nationella centralbankerna och slutligt godknnas av ECB. Problemet fr oss som "utecentralbank" r att vi inte kommer att vara med i den krets av centralbanker som kan ge frslag p skerheter och n mindre kommer vi att vara med och fatta dessa beslut. Skall svenska krondenominerade stats- och bostadspapper kunna anvndas som skerhet fr intradagsln i euro, mste de allts fresls och "listas" av en centralbank inom EMU. Detta skall sedan godknnas av ECB. Vi blir allts i hg grad beroende av andras vlvilja. Frgan om intradagskredit r besvrlig och vi fortstter att arbeta med den inom EMI fr att f till stnd frn svensk synpunkt vettiga lsningar. Men vi har ocks stllt oss frgan om vi frn Riksbankens sida mer handgripligt kan bidra till att underltta bankernas frsrjning av euro-likviditet under dagen, utan att fr den skull gna oss t ngon form av subventionerad kreditgivning. Det vi tittat p r mjligheten att anvnda euro-delen av vr valutareserv. Vi tror att detta r tekniskt mjligt att klara av och det kan vara en mjlighet, givet att det accepteras av ECB. Det skulle dock innebra kostnader fr Riksbanken som vi mste ta ut av bankerna. Hur stora dessa skulle bli och huruvida detta blir en ekonomiskt attraktiv lsning fr bankerna, r det svrt att ha en exakt uppfattning om idag. Dock tror vi det finns ett vrde i att den hr mjligheten undersks noga, som ett alternativ eller ett komplement till de vgar och metoder bankerna sjlva kommer att flja. Sammanfattningsvis kan allts sgas att bankerna kommer att finna olika vgar att hantera Target-problematiken, och vi ska frn Riksbanken sida bidra s konstruktivt som mjligt. Men vilka lsningar vi n vljer lr vi inte komma ifrn att detta kommer att kosta - utanfrskapet har ett pris och detta utgr en del. Utformningen av target-systemet kommer att pverka den svenska finansmarknaden ocks p andra stt. En sdan sak gller ppettiderna i systemet. EMIs inriktning r att Target skall vara ppet alla dagar utom juldagen och nyrsdagen, samt lrdagar och sndagar. Det hr kommer inte att innebra ngot tvng fr enskilda lnder att hlla ppet alla vriga helgdagar - om vi i Sverige vill hlla butiken stngd p exempelvis midsommarafton fr att istllet gna oss t sillen med dess tillbehr, r det ingen som kommer att tvinga oss att hlla ppet. Dock r det ganska klart att vi kommer att f se en marknadsstyrd process mot ett allt mer "standardiserat" ppethllande, dr vi nog fr vnja oss vid tanken att allt fler funktioner kommer att hllas ppna under allt fler dagar. Frn Riksbankens sida kommer vi att ta initiativ till att f igng en diskussion kring dessa frgor. Denna frga och mnga andra behver finna sin lsning framver. EU-arbetet har inte avstannat i Sverige, trots att vi inte kommer att delta i EMU frn start.
